reviews.transcript_full:
This evening, we'll be flying with 
Peach Airlines on their longest flight   connecting Osaka and Singapore. From 
our experience flying domestically,   Peach is not a bad little budget carrier. But 
does this carry over to their longest flight?   We'll also check out their brand renewal and see 
what this means for the airline going forward.   Is flying this budget carrier a decent way to 
get from A to B? Come along and let's find out.   We are beginning at Kansai airport in Osaka, one of five island airports in the country. Serving   over 30 million passengers a year and being on 
an island, the train station is definitely a buzz   while you're trying to gather your bearings. The 
airport has two terminals with Terminal 2 being   dedicated to the budget airlines. And judging by 
this map, we got to first hightail it over to the   bus, which will then take us over to the terminal. 
  EE: This was later in the day after my JR BUS trip from Tokyo! If there's one thing about budget airlines,  it's sure the prices can be cheap, but 
that comes at a cost in other manners.   In our case, it first means factoring in the 
additional time to even get to the terminal. EE: And waiting for this bus should you miss it. I had to spring for the last bit to make it >.< All said and done, it's another 20 minutes. 
Once we arrive, you can see another way to   keep costs down. The terminal is only one level. 
No fancy elevators nor escalators here. Inside   is equally as no-frills. The building itself 
is bare bones. Pretty much one big warehouse   with no fancy lighting, fancy seating, 
or other ambiance-enhancing items. Today,   we'll be flying on MM773, Peach Airlines' 
once-daily flight to Singapore departing at   6:25 p.m. They operate their longest flight using 
the A321 long-range aircraft. I visited the kiosk   to print out the boarding pass, which was quick 
enough. Should you have baggage to drop off,   you're going to want to add on extra time as well, 
as this is done without machines. After check-in,   there's not much to do here other than consume the 
remainder of the very dangerous water and complete   the security and passport check. You know, 
when it comes to the low-cost carrier world,   there really is no such thing as a free lunch. 
I mean, look at this terminal, for example.   There's only a couple of places to grab a bite to 
eat. There's one drugstore. There's a duty-free,   and that's about it. There's not even any windows 
to plane spot. Also, when it comes to the flights,   sure, they're cheap, but they run at odd hours 
of the day. We leave at 6:25 p.m., not too late,   but we do arrive in Singapore past midnight 
after the trains and buses stop running. So,   you do have to plan a little bit after the 
flight as well. And for the flight itself,   you got to figure out if you want to bring snacks 
or buy something on board. So, yes, the flights   are cheap, but a little bit of planning beforehand 
is going to help you out in the long run. Today,   we're departing from gate 89, which lies 
beyond these mysterious doors. I did manage   to find a quiet corner to pass the time, do some 
editing, and recharge the batteries. Nowadays,   more and more airlines are banning the use of 
portable chargers, and having access to power on   board is really hit or miss. Once the mysterious 
doors opened, it was time to head to the gate. And   calling these gates might be a bit of a stretch. 
It's just a lot of walking. Oh, and there's no   washroom past the main building. And yeah, it is a 
lot of walking. This clip is sped up seven times,   and there's still another clip I didn't include of 
another minute of walking. So, it's about four or   five minutes just to reach the end. The end is 
just a door with a small workstation for staff   to scan boarding passes and to check passports. 
There's no chairs or seating or anything like   that, and then we head out and walk to the plane. 
Perhaps the best perk of a budget airline. And as   we walk to the plane, I'll take this moment 
to welcome you viewers to the channel, and I   invite you to subscribe for continued aviation and 
travel-related content. Or you can check out my   flight with Jeju Air, a budget carrier based out 
of Korea, which has a very delicious menu. Yum. If you can, hyping the video is a great way to 
help the channel gain traction on the platform.   Doesn't cost a thing and takes only a few clicks. 
Many thanks. Today, we'll be seated in 35A at the   rear of the plane. Once everyone was on board, 
we made a quick taxi to 06 Left and headed on our   way. This is, of course, one of Peach Airlines' 
A321 long-range aircraft, one of three in their   fleet. The long-range variant extends the range 
by about 900 km, give or take, compared to the   A321. The interior is configured in a single 
cabin with 218 seats and three lavatories on   board. Our aircraft is just over five years old, 
being delivered to the airline in December 2021. It'll take just over 6 hours to cover the 
4,800 km to reach Singapore this evening. One difference between Peach's in-flight 
service on international versus domestic   is the opportunity to pre-order meals. And you can 
bet your britches I took full advantage of it. The   options for this flight were a chicken curry—not 
bad—spaghetti—okay—basil chicken, or is it basil?   And okonomiyaki, an Osaka favourite. Since Peach 
is an Osaka-based airline, I, of course, had to go   with the okonomiyaki. Batteries not included. Some 
assembly required. And it looks pretty good. But   in the words of any government official, there's 
still more work to be done. I got down to business   by applying the okonomiyaki sauce, followed by the 
mayo. We then added the shaved bonito katsuobushi,   followed by a little baggie of seaweed to top it 
off. The dish was a solid   call. Works well for airplane food. Very savoury, 
great flavours, nice piece of crispy bacon,   just a perfect taste of Osaka, and I had no 
problem finishing the whole thing. There's   also the on-board menu for smaller items, drinks, 
cup noodles, things of that nature that are very   reasonably priced. And the reverse side has some 
stationery and some other items to take home. The hard product is Peach's older original design 
which we have seen in the past. Though many   aspects are the same, there are some differences 
compared to their A320 aircraft. And inquiring   minds can check out the link for more. The seats 
are one thing that remains unchanged. Budget   carrier style seats, and they're nothing to write 
home about and not my preferred seats for a 6-hour   flight. But the seat pitch is advertised as 30 to 
32 in. We're getting 30 in the rear of the plane,   more than on their domestic aircraft, 
which is nice to have. And the A321s do   have the USB outlets. And again, on the A320, 
they're not installed. As mentioned earlier,   Peach is undergoing a brand renewal. And you 
can see this on some of the screenshots already   throughout the video. Visually, they're going 
with more of a peachy, softer logo and colours,   moving away from the purples, and they already 
have started to install their new product on   three of their A320 aircraft. I'm looking forward 
to sharing their new product with you when it's   implemented further throughout their fleet. There 
are a couple washrooms on board, and they have a   little counter space. Though this one, the soap 
dispenser was inoperative. I didn't see any soap   bottles in lieu of this, and a good reminder 
to have some hand sanitizer while travelling.   Like any ultra-low-cost carrier, everything 
comes for a fee, but they do tend to have really   good sales. I purchased the minimum plan, which 
allows for 7 kg of carry-on baggage, though at   no time throughout this trip was my bag weighed, 
though it has been done in the past. From there,   you put in your information, and then you can 
select the seat should you desire. Then you can   choose a meal if the flight offers it and any 
other options. It's pretty simple and easy to   follow.And 6 hours later, we reached Singapore. 
And you know, I really enjoyed this flight. It   was quiet and relaxing, and I was really impressed 
with the okonomiyaki. It really does well on the   airplane. Yeah, sure, the seat is not the best, 
but that comes with a budget carrier, and I knew   I was getting into that, but I'm sure the new 
iteration of the seat will add further comfort.   Having the USB charging and extra seat pitch on 
these planes was a good call by the airline as it   adds to the experience, and having some content 
downloaded is a good call before boarding as   there's no Wi-Fi or internet.When it was all said 
and done, the cost of this one-way flight came out   to 18,100 yen. Under 200 bucks to get from Japan 
to Singapore. I call that a steal of a deal,   even with the added time and budgetiness of 
the airport. Thanks for watching. Let me know   your thoughts on Peach's longest international 
flight, and I'll catch you in the next video.

reviews.transcript_full: Today, come fly Qatar Airways business class with me — 3 different aircraft! My route: Amsterdam, Netherlands → Busan, South Korea I booked a Business Lite fare on Qatar's official website, and the round trip came to €2,561 (about $2,800) Since it's Business Lite, lounge access isn't included! Here's the meal and wine menu You can pick a starter, a main, and a dessert It was a 6-hour flight with one meal service The wines are handpicked by sommeliers Honestly, I barely drink... so it's a pass on the wine haha Open the armrest and there's a hidden drawer Inside: a plush, cushioned headset and a bottle of water The cabin gets super dry, so make sure you drink that water... This is Amsterdam Schiphol Airport The in-flight amenity kit is all Diptyque products Honestly, I hate that my brain does this, but I immediately start adding up how much all this costs haha There are socks and an eye mask (so good!) Shall we open the amenity kit together? Ooh, body lotion Face mist haha It's a scented spray, so sensitive skin types might want to skip Great as a perfume or body spray though As I'm rummaging around with my camera, the flight attendant brought the mocktail I'd ordered Lip balm Phew, filming is not easy Ta-da! There's even a miniature Eau de Toilette It even comes with a little instruction booklet No wonder the pouch felt heavy The scent I got is called Eau Rose The inside of the pouch looks like this, with a little handle It's all complimentary, so you can just take it home Right after boarding, the crew took my order — an apple mint mocktail I always keep my seatbelt fastened tight — it gives me peace of mind Qatar business class even gives you pajamas I flew during World Cup season, so these were World Cup edition If I were rich, I'd fly business just to collect the pajamas... Total case of the tail wagging the dog, I know haha The pajamas are loose-fit and super comfy On Qatar business class, your dedicated flight attendant comes by before takeoff to introduce themselves Mine just stopped by to say hello It's these little touches that make the service feel so good The Amsterdam to Doha flight was nearly empty The cabin is spacious to begin with, but it was practically deserted There are charging ports right next to the seat Gotta finish my drink before takeoff They collect everything right before departure In business class, there's no time to just sit around doing nothing haha A storage compartment on the other side of the seat The doors are closing... are we finally off? A prayer plays, almost like asking for a safe flight... I'm genuinely curious — if you know what it is, tell me in the comments haha Suddenly, Kevin Hart appears It felt a bit like watching a comedy... Until the very end, no one sat next to me or behind me Maybe it's because of the whole war situation? Anyway, now we're really off The Netherlands is a dairy country full of green fields, so from above, you see endless flat green landscapes Honestly, I used to wonder why anyone would pay €2,500+ for a flight — seemed like such a waste But this? This is pure living-like-royalty From the moment I boarded, I thought... I wish this flight were longer Qatar Airways offers satellite Wi-Fi, so you can watch TV and browse the internet mid-flight But I never connect to public Wi-Fi — security risks, you know I had cybersecurity training at work once haha Right after takeoff: non-alcoholic wine and potato chips Zero alcohol, yet I'm somehow tipsy on the vibes Dinner is still coming and I'm already full Let me show you the bathroom The mist and hand cream in here are Diptyque too Size-wise, it's about the same as a regular economy lavatory Changed into the pajamas — done! Just a regular cotton-poly blend, but light and comfy Toothbrushes and toothpaste are stocked in the bathroom It was an evening flight, and when I came back the lighting had changed A burgundy-pink glow? Not bad at all... hehe They started setting up my meal Pre-dinner bread (cold and hard, lol) and even a little candle — the attention to detail It's literally a restaurant opening in the sky There were even several kinds of olive oil to choose from The appetizer was a meat dish And an asparagus cream soup It was a light, creamy soup — pretty tasty The main was Angus beef tenderloin (fillet) with mushroom sauce I was so excited I took photos from every angle For airplane food, I was honestly satisfied The plating looked fine-dining, though the meat quality was a little underwhelming It wasn't that juicy steak you'd get at a restaurant I think this was rooibos tea — I liked it When I got back from brushing my teeth, they'd made up my bed I could already tell I'd sleep like a baby Let's recline it 180 degrees into a full-flat bed A super comfy flat bed, coming right up It feels like being in a luxury hotel Oh right — the amenity kit also had 3M earplugs, and I loved them... 3M is the best! I slept 3 out of the 6 hours I woke up as morning broke One of those moments where the flight itself feels surreal... Every time I fly, I'm reminded how magnificent nature is So much happens up in the sky. (You'll see later in the video) If you're enjoying my travel vlog, don't forget to subscribe and like! We're landing in about 40 minutes Can't skip the morning coffee, right? They brought coffee and chocolate cookies Tastes like coffee from an illy or Nescafé machine As you approach Qatar, the grand desert landscape unfolds Just 6 hours of flying, and the scenery is completely different Qatar mornings are a total natural-light paradise The sunlight streams into the cabin so beautifully I've flown countless times, but this view is unforgettable Seatbelt on tight haha, time to land A view that makes me grateful to be alive Arrived at Doha Airport, Qatar There was no line at the economy transfer checkpoint, so I just went through the economy lane and transferred... haha Wait, is this a jungle? The quality of this airport is insane Is this what happens when capitalism meets nature?.. Why do I feel like I walked into a theme park lol All those spaces down below are airport rest areas Head down and you'll find tons of seats and chargers War tensions? The departure board shows nothing but Qatar Airways flights Though the airport felt way too peaceful for that I could honestly live in this airport for like 3 days This genuinely shocked me The airport ceiling? They clean it like THAT? It was so impressive and fascinating Next up: from Doha, Qatar to Bangkok, Thailand Flight time: 6 hours 55 minutes This cabin has a 2-2-2 layout Heads up — a stranger might sit next to you The cushions and blankets are the same as on the Airbus A350-900 I flew first This time I ordered the signature mocktail right after boarding (mango orange) Definitely an older aircraft — the classic layout feels a bit more spacious On the first aircraft, the legroom tapered off toward the end It was private, but my feet felt a bit boxed in The headset and amenities were pretty much identical I didn't even check the menu, assuming it'd be the same Nope — completely different! (I'll show you soon) This time I got the pajamas in a small (to give to my mom...) The pouch was a different design too >< One trip, two Diptyque pouches (total win) The actual amenity products are the same Still, shall we unbox it together? The perfume was a different scent! Not Eau Rose this time — Eau Duelle It had a more Middle Eastern vibe The lip balm, cream, and mist smell the same as before The refreshment towel you get at boarding — way too nice for a disposable Quick bathroom tour — let's go! Pretty similar to before, right? The finish and materials feel a bit more... economy? It's only 6 hours, but the pajamas are going on anyway The menu is completely different, so I'm speed-reading it It's a morning departure, so the menu is breakfast-focused The tea menu is the same as the drinks menu I didn't show earlier A little bummed I never got to try the traditional Middle Eastern Karak tea The seat controls look like this — a bit old-school, right? The crew is always so kind, even during the pre-takeoff rush Kevin Hart is back on the safety video... one watch and he feels like an old friend haha The legroom is seriously generous, right? I prefer this kind of remote over a touchpad Pulling out the life vest (don't pull the tab!) While I was busy filming everything, we took off in no time A Qatar Airways plane at a desert airport — something grand about it The desert gets me every time... so cool You might think Qatar is nothing but desert, but Doha is surrounded on three sides by the Persian Gulf The water is this emerald-blue color Isn't it just gorgeous? Seriously, I bring this cream on every single flight My skin is extremely dry — I can't survive without it Hands, face, even inside my nostrils... it goes everywhere This is the tomato shake they served after takeoff Looks like a chocolate latte, but it tastes 100% like a tomato shake! This remote has such clicky buttons — so satisfying to use I'd asked to be served right after takeoff, so they got my breakfast ready Quite a few people skipped the meal and went straight to sleep The Doha to Bangkok flight was completely full They served jam and bread before the meal. Cold again... Maybe the fruit is because we're flying to Bangkok? The fruit quality was great — delicious! And I ordered the shrimp dumpling noodle soup Wow, these dumplings are actually amazing The portion was generous and the noodles had a nice bite Ordering the noodles was definitely the right call The dumplings were stuffed full of filling After the meal, the flight attendant asked what else I wanted to drink They really look after you non-stop This time I went with a simple cappuccino I was full, but I couldn't pass up another good nap Full-flat seat, so I was about to turn it into a bed and doze off when the flight attendant asked if I'd like some tea So... yes, I ordered chamomile tea haha I woke up after about 4 hours of sleep As you approach arrival, they hand out another warm towel Honestly, even with someone sitting next to you, it's not that bothersome Probably because the seats are wide apart and there are privacy dividers Flying over Thailand now Just moments ago, the sky was crystal clear We were cruising along so peacefully Then suddenly the clouds rolled in and we flew into this vast sea of clouds One of the most mysterious sights I've ever seen It was magnificent Suddenly turbulence hit and the plane was shaking like crazy It seriously felt like riding a roller coaster The plane plunged through the swirling clouds I thought I was in Mad Max The footage looks steadier thanks to image stabilization, but I was genuinely scared we might go down... The flight attendant swore that would never happen, so I relaxed... ^^ Is this what it feels like to be helpless in front of Mother Nature? It was terrifying and mesmerizing at the same time They say turbulence over Bangkok gets rough during rainy season How many times in your life do you witness a scene like this? Anyway, we pushed through the thunder and lightning Like the eye of a typhoon — as we descended into Bangkok, it turned bright and clear again The night view was fantastic After all that turbulence, the landing was buttery smooth Made it to Bangkok safely! ...or so I thought. Then came a problem Right after landing, a Qatar Airways staff member came looking for me They looked genuinely apologetic and rushed My luggage couldn't be checked through to my Jeju Air flight So I had to leave the transit area and actually enter Thailand then collect my bags and check in all over again from scratch I rushed to fill out the online arrival form Even the staff didn't seem sure how this kind of transfer worked To be fair, it was a pretty unusual routing (Amsterdam → Doha → Bangkok) But then another problem — no matter how long I waited, my bag never came out I asked several airport staff for help, and finally found my bag in the oversized luggage area I figured my Qatar business ticket would get me priority check-in But my last leg was booked in economy — no business check-in with Jeju Air In the end, I stood in the regular line for almost an hour Thankfully, I made it onto the flight without further issues If you're transferring between different airlines: - Check the seat class for each leg - Confirm your luggage is checked through to your final destination - Check whether you need to enter the transit country - And leave yourself plenty of transfer time After 12 hours in business class + 5 hours in economy, I finally arrived in Korea Maybe it's because Busan is a city by the sea, but you see rivers and ocean everywhere I didn't get to travel around Korea this time, so I only filmed food... Still debating whether to turn that into a video Back at Incheon Airport for my flight to the Netherlands Finally — the legendary Qatar Airways Qsuite! Qsuite is basically first class Every seat has its own closing door It's a 1-2-1 layout, and the middle seats can apparently convert into a 4-person pod facing each other The wine selection was the same across all three aircraft Once again, the meal menu was completely different Seoul to Doha is a 10-hour flight, so you get two meal services The foot area is enclosed, but it's quite roomy Pretty sure two people could fit in here And here come the Diptyque amenities again! I asked for the same apple mint mocktail I had on the way to Korea The storage, drink holder, and headset space are all combined Okay, this is where it gets embarrassing — this remote is so hard to use So confused... how do I even work this??? Some kid had spilled snacks all over the seat Ah, maybe I should've kept my door closed But the crew cleaned it all up perfectly Another quick bathroom tour Got the pajamas in a large for my husband haha The suite door has to stay open for takeoff and landing It smells like a pretty new plane There's a card reader here — no clue how to use it though Safety video time with our friendly instructor Kevin Hart A safety video I'd happily watch again It's a midnight departure, so they kept the pink mood lighting on Right after takeoff, they dimmed all the lights Beautiful night view I think the Qsuite screen is the biggest of the three aircraft The flight attendant's pick: TWG vanilla tea — so good For dinner, I ordered the Korean-style braised beef with rice As if to prove it's business class, it came out like a fancy health meal A Western-Korean fusion of sorts — but in a comforting, nourishing way It suited my taste perfectly The braised beef was tender and delicious Morning came of the war, but once again, Doha Airport was busy and perfectly peaceful Apparently (according to AI), Qatar Airways flies its own exclusive route This is the Boeing 777-300ER with Qsuite The seats feel a bit worn, but otherwise it's nearly identical to the last one Just some scratches on the door frame — that's about the only difference They served Qatari dates and traditional coffee For the remote alone, I prefer the Boeing Qsuite Ahhh~ I had the Qatari breakfast with pita bread This was the best meal I had on Qatar Airways The pita bread came out nice and warm I had no idea how to eat in Amsterdam They say rich people buy time with money But it's not just time — it's time filled with precious experiences Feeling that in my bones (since I'm not quite rich yet), I'll wrap up this trip here If you want to see my Netherlands travels too, subscribe :)) See you next time!

messing! I asked about a food menu, and the   crew member explained it would be a snack. That 
lowered my expectations! Cold towels and welcome   drinks from the menu were served, and there was a 
coaster to add to my collection, making it four! There was loads of leg room and

হলো যে দুপুর 12 টা বাংলাদেশে তার মানে ফুল একদিন এক রাত চলে যাবে আমার এই অসাধারণ জার্নি শুরু করার আগে আপনাদেরকে বলে রাখি আমার মনে হয় আমরা একটু ফ্ল্যাশব্যাকে যাই ফ্ল্যাশব্যাকে যাওয়ার আগে চলেন সাইনাস আদন সম্পর্কে আপনাদেরকে কিছু তথ্য শেয়ার করি দেন আমরা আপনাদের সাথে শেয়ার করব হযরত শাহজালাল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দর থেকে এখান পর্যন্ত আসা বাই দা ওয়ে এয়ারফেয়ার সহ সবকিছু শেয়ার করার চেষ্টা করবো আপনাদেরকে। তো চ্যানেলটি সাবস্ক্রাইব করে আমাদের সাথে যুক্ত হয়ে যান এবং দেখতেই থাকুন আজকের এই ব্লগ। আজ আমরা ঢাকা থেকে চীনের গোয়াংজ হয়ে পাপুয়া নিউগিরির পোট মোড় সবাই যাচ্ছি চাইনা সাউদন এয়ারলাইন্সে। চলুন যাত্রার পাশাপাশি এই বিশাল এয়ারলাইন্স সম্পর্কে কিছু মজার এবং শিক্ষামূলক তথ্য জেনে নেওয়া যাক। চাইনা সাউদন এয়ারলাইন্সে। আধুনিক যাত্রা শুরু হয় 1991 সাল থেকে। এর প্রধান কার্যালয় চীনের গুয়াংজু শহরে এবং গুয়াংজু বায়ুন আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দর এয়ারলাইন্সটির সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ হাব। তাদের বিমানের লেজে যে নীল রঙের উপর লাল ফুল দেখা যায় সেটি হচ্ছে কাপুক ফুল। গুয়াংজু শহরের প্রতীকী ফুল। এটি শুধু চীনের একটি সাধারণ এয়ারলাইন্স নয়। যাত্রী বহর হিসেবে বিশ্বের অন্যতম বড় বিমান গোষ্ঠীর একটি। চাইনা সওদাউনের মূল প্রতিষ্ঠান জানিয়েছে 2025 সালের শেষে তাদের পুরা গ্রুপে যাত্রীবাহী এবং কার্গো বিমান সহ মোট বহর ছিল 1005 টি। একই বছরে তারা প্রায় 17 কোটি 40 লাখ যাত্রী পরিবহন করেছে। অর্থাৎ বাংলাদেশের মোট জনসংখ্যার কাছাকাছি সংখ্যক মানুষ এক বছরে তাদের বিমান যাতায়াত করছে। ভাবা যায় 2025 সালে চাইনা সাউদার্ন এয়ারলাইন্স গ্রুপের মোট অপারেটিং রাজস্ব ছিল 182.256 বিলিয়ন চীনা ইউয়ান। আগের বছরের তুলনায় এটি প্রায় 4.6 শতাংশ বেশি। আর এই আয়ের সবচেয়ে বড় অংশ আসছে হলো যে যাত্রী পরিবহনের থেকে পাশাপাশি কার্গো মেল, গ্রাউন্ড সার্ভিস, ক্যাটারিং এবং অন্যান্য বিমান সংশ্লিষ্ট সেবা থেকে। এয়ারলাইন্সটির বহরে স্বল্প এবং দীর্ঘ দূরত্বের জন্য বিভিন্ন ধরনের বিমান আছে। তার মধ্যে এয়ারবাস এ320, এ350 এবং বোইং 7377 এবং 787 ড্রিমলাইনার অন্যতম। দেশীয়ভাবে তৈরি চীনা সিন19 বিমান ও তাদের বহরও যুক্ত আছে। 2025 সালের আগস্ট পর্যন্ত চাইনা সাওদাউন সিও বিমানগুলোর প্রায় 4 লাখ600 যাত্রী বহন করছে। সেবার মানের দিক থেকে আন্তর্জাতিক বিমান রেটিং সংস্থা সকাই ট্র্যাক্স চাইনা সাউদনকে একটি ফোর স্টার রেটিং দেয়। যা এয়ারলাইন্সের হিসেবে স্বীকৃত দিয়েছে। আসন্ন খাবার বিনোদন পরিচ্ছন্নতা কেবিন ক্রু এবং বিমানবন্দরের সেবা মূল্যায়ন করে এই রেটিং দেওয়া হয়। 2025 সালে স্কাই ট্র্যাক্স বিশ্ব এয়ারলাইন্স তালিকায় এটি 33 তম স্থানে ছিল যা আগের বছর ছিল 36 তম। আমাদের এই যাত্রার সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অংশ হচ্ছে গুয়াংজু থেকে পুট মোর সবাই রোড। চাইনা সাউদন 2023 সালের ডিসেম্বরে গুয়াংজু ও পুট মোর সবাইয়ের মধ্যে সরাসরি নিয়মিত যাত্রী ফ্লাইট চালু করে। প্রাতিষ্ঠানিক ভাষ্য অনুযায়ী দক্ষিণ প্রশান্ত মহাসাগরীয় দ্বীপঞ্চলের সঙ্গে এটি তাদের প্রথম নিয়মিত সরাসরি বাণিজ্যিক যাত্রী রোড। এই সংযোগের কারণে বাংলাদেশ সহ দক্ষিণ-পূর্ব এশিয়ার যাত্রীরা গুয়াংজু ট্রানজিট ব্যবহার করে পাপনগিনি যেতে পারে। আরেকটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বিষয় হলো চাইনা সাওদাউন এসকাই টিমের জোটের সাবেক সদস্য ছিল। 2019 সালে তারা জোটটি ছেড়ে বর্তমানে বিভিন্ন আন্তর্জাতিক এয়ারলাইন্সের সঙ্গে কুড শেয়ারু অংশধারিত্বের মাধ্যমে বিশাল নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনা করতেছে। আজকের ব্লগে আমরা দেখবো ঢাকার চেকিন প্রক্রিয়া বিমানের ভেতরের আসন খাবার সেবা গুঞ্জ বিমানবন্দরের টার্জিট ব্যবস্থা এবং দীর্ঘ যাত্রার পর পুট মোড় সবাই পৌঁছানোর সম্পূর্ণ অভিজ্ঞতা। তাহলে চলুন সাইনাস সাউডনের সঙ্গে যাত্রা শুরু করা যাক। ঢাকা থেকে পাপু এগিনীর এই অসাধারণ বিমান যাত্রা। আপনাদেরকে স্বাগত জানাচ্ছি হযরত শাহজালাল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দরে। বোর্ডিং এমাত্র কমপ্লিট করলাম এবং বোর্ডিং এক্সপেরিয়েন্স যদি বলি খুবই সুন্দর, খুবই নিখুত এবং তাদের ব্যবহার সবকিছু ওকে সিরিয়াল নেই। তবে একটা জিনিস আমি আশা করছিলাম সেটা কি জানেন যে বড় বিমান হবে না বিমান ছোট। আই থিংক বোইং 737 ম্যাক্স যেটা আছে এটা হবে। এবং হলো যে আপনাদেরকে দেখাই সিরিয়াল একবারে নেই চাইনা সাউদনে তাদেরকে আমি প্রশ্ন করলাম যে লোকজন এত কম কেন কয় দিনের বেলা লোক কম থাকে তাই ছোট বিমান এবং রাতের বেলা বড় বিমান থাকে হোয়াট এভার আজকে আপনাদের সাথে আমি শেয়ার করব বিশেষ করে গুয়াংজু এয়ারলাইন্সের অভিজ্ঞতা আমার যাত্রার শুরুটা হচ্ছে কোথায় থেকে হযরত শাহজালাল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দর থেকে এবং প্রথম ইম্প্রেশন ছিল মাশআাল্লাহ অসাধারণ এবং এখন সময় বাজে হলো যে দুপুর আমি একটু ওয়েট একলা মানুষ তো ভিডিও করতে এই জিনিসটা একটু প্রবলেম হয়। ওকে সময় বাজে এখন 10টা বেজে 50। যেহেতু আমার দুপুর 1টা বাজে ফ্লাইট এর মানে হাতে আর বেশিক্ষণ সময় নেই। ইমিগ্রেশনটা এখন শেষ করব। শেষ করে হলো যে আপনাদের সাথে আমার অভিজ্ঞতা শেয়ার করব। দেন আমি চলে যাব কোথায়? লাউঞ্জের এক্সেস নিতে। আলহামদুলিল্লাহ সুন্দরভাবে ইমিগ্রেশন কমপ্লিট করলাম। এই ইমিগ্রেশনে এসে এক মজার গল্প আপনাদের সাথে শেয়ার করি। সেটা হলো যে প্রথমে আমি চলে যাই কোথায় জানেন? যিনি ভিসা ভেরিফিকেশন করে আপনারা প্রশ্ন করতে পারেন ওখানে প্রথমে কেন গেলাম ইমিগ্রেশনের আগে। কারণ আমি জানি বারবার গেলে ওখান থেকে ফেরত পাঠাই। কারণ এসব দেশের নাম ওরা জীবনেও শুনে নাই। অনেক ইমিগ্রেশন অফিসার সম্পর্কে বলতেও পারে না। টিমুল লেসনিও এরকম হইছে আরো অনেক দেশ নিয়ে। যার কারণে গেলাম উনি আমার আমি লাইন ধরে গেলাম। উনি বলল যে কয়টা দেশ? 38 টা। চলে যান আপনার আর কিছু লাগবে না। আমি ওয়াও এটা তো খুব ভালো জিনিস। কিন্তু আমি যখন ইমিগ্রেশন লাইন সিরিয়াল ধরে খাড়াইছি আল্লাহু আকবার বিশ্বাস করবেন না আধা ঘন্টা টাইম কেন যাইতেছি কি হইছে আপনি ভেরিফিকেশন করেন আমি বললাম যে না আমার ভেরিফিকেশন ডান তারপরও আমার কথা বিশ্বাস করতেছে না তারপর ওই ব্যক্তি আইসা বলে উনাকে ছেড়ে দেন তারপর উনি পাপ নিয়গিনর ভিসা নাম্বার খুঁজে পাচ্ছে না কারণ পাপনিগিনরম সিল মানে ভিসা হয় আর কি যেটা হল যে আপনার কিছুটা ব্রুনাইের ভিসার মত সটাম মেরে দেই এখন এইখানে এটা নিয়ে আরো খুশ গল্প পরে আমার দুইজন ভক্ত আসছে ইমিগ্রেশন অফিসার ওখান থেকে আরে রোহান ভাই আপনার তো মায়ানমারের ব্লগ দেখছি আমিও খুশি হয়ে গেলাম খুব সুন্দরভাবে কথাবার্তি বললাম বলে তারপরে ওই পুলিশ অফিসার বলতেছে আপনি ঘুরেন আমি ক হ্যা পরে চ্যানেলের নামটা জগলে অনেক কিছু করে ফাইনালি আমাকে রিলিজ করল যাক আমি এখন এসকাই লাউঞ্জে ঢুকি দাড়ান ক্যামেরাটা অফ করে নেই আমি এখন চলে আসলাম লাউঞ্জে বিকজ চেকইন স্টার্ট হতে হতে আরো এক ঘন্টার মত টাইম আছে মোটামুটি ভালো একটা টাইম নিয়ে আমি আসছি। 12:45 এ হলো যে আমার হলো যে আপনার হলো যে গেট ওপেন হয়ে যাবে। সরি অনেকদিন পর ক্যামেরা ধরছি তো তাই কথা বলতে একটু থমত খেয়ে যাচ্ছি। হোয়াট এভার আপনারা এটা ক্ষমা দৃষ্টিতে দেখবেন। এখন লাউঞ্জে এসে খাবার তো আনলিমিটেড। কি কি খাবার নিলাম আপনাদেরকে একটু দেখাই। এই যে দেখুন পরোটা। এর সাথে হলো যে গাজরের হালুয়া। এবং এইখানে হলো যে আপনার এটাকে বলা হল যে আপনার সোনার ডাইল বলি আমরা। অনেকে এটাকে বুড়ের ডাইলো বলে। আর সাথে আছে হলো যে আপনার পানিও এক বোতল পানি এন্ড [নাক ডাকা] অপেল জুস। আপনারা হয়তো জানেন লাউঞ্জের এক্সেস ইবিএল আমি সকাই লাউঞ্জ আসছি ইবিএল এর কার্ড নিয়ে। এছাড়া এখানে আরো অনেকগুলো লাউঞ্জ আছে। বলা আছে। তারপর আপনার হল যে সিটি ব্যাংকার আছে। আমার কাছে এইটাই ভালো লাগে। খাবার দাবার শুরু করে নিই। শুরু করার কথা হচ্ছে। চেকইন কমপ্লিট। আলহামদুলিল্লাহ কোন ধরনের হ্যাসেল হয় নাই। বিকজ এই চেকিনে এসে অনেক ঝামেলা হয়। অন্যান্য সময় কি কি কারণে ঝামেলা হয় তা যদি আপনাদেরকে বলি স্পেসিফিকভাবে ডলারগুলো চেক করে ব্যাগ ক্যামেরা এত গ্যাজেট কেন? এগুলো নিয়ে আবার কোন প্রশ্নই নেই। মানুষজন খুবই কম এবং মনে হচ্ছে এই যাত্রায় একটা খালি এয়ারলাইন্স পাবো। হোয়াট এভার এখন হলো যে গোয়াংজু যেহেতু যাচ্ছি ওখানে গিয়ে চেষ্টা করব আপনাদেরকে ওখানকারও পরিবেশটা দেখানোর জন্য। বিশেষ করে এয়ারপোর্টের কোন ব্রিজ দেয় নাই। আমাদের যেতে হবে হলো যে বাসে করে সামনে হলো মানুষজন আছে। তাই আমি ক্যামেরাটা অফ করে দেব। যেহেতু পাবলিক ট্রান্সপোর্টেশন সবার ফুটেজ নিচ্ছি না। বন্ধুরা আমাদেরকে বাস দিয়ে আনছে বিশ্বাস করবেন না এসি ডেসি কিছু নাই। গরমের ভিতর অবস্থা খুবই খারাপ হয়ে গেছে। এখন এই সার্ভিসটা আমার কাছে খুবই খারাপ লাগলো। এক কথা হল যে আপনার ওরা ব্রিজ দেয় নাই। দ্বিতীয়ত বাসে করে আনছে। ভালো কথা। অন্ততপক্ষে হল যে এই সিডিসিতে থাকতে পারতো। বিমান দেখা যাচ্ছে। এটা কি বোইং মনে হয় সম্ভবত। এয়ারবাস হলে ওদের ঢাকনাগুলো একটু চেপটা থাকতো। যাই হোক ভিতরে ঢুকি। আমরা বিমানের ভিতরে ঢুকি। আমার সিট নাম্বার হলো 59 এ। দেখি আমাদের ফাস্ট থ্যাংক ইউ। আফার লং টাইম অনলি চারটা হল যে বিজনেস ক্লাস লিখতো >> আমরা এসে বসে গেলাম বিমানের ভিতরে আমার সিট নাম্বার হলো 59 এইচ বের হচ্ছে না ভয়ে। যদিও আমি যতটুকু শুনছি টার্বুলেন্স এটা ওদের রেগুলার বিষয়। এবং এটা একটা বিমানের রেগুলারই অংশ। এত কিছু বোঝার পরেও কিন্তু মনকে সান্ত্বনা দেওয়া যায় না। যত কিছুই বলি ভিতরে কিন্তু আমার খুবই কাপনি ধরে গেছে। এই টোরটা দিয়ে আসি আমার এই মনে মানে যখনই টোরগুলো করি মনে মনে শুধু বলি কি এটা আমার লাস্ট টোর আর দেব না। এত পরিমাণের ভয় লাগে। আলহামদুলিল্লাহ কাপনি একটু কমছে। এভাবে যদি স্বাভাবিক গতিতে যাই তাহলে মানে আর কোন টেনশনই লাগে না। কিন্তু টারবুলেন্সটা হলেই ভিতরে কাপনি ধরে যায়। হোয়াট এভার টাইমিং এর দিক দিয়ে ওরা খুবই পাংচুয়াল এবং বিমান যখন ট্যাক্সি রানওয়েতে দাড় হওয়া ছিল তখন তারা এসি ফুল স্পিডে রাখছিল। অনেক সময় অনেক এয়ারলাইন্স এসি ছাড়ে না। গরমে অনেকের অবস্থা খুবই নাজেহাল হয়ে যায়। এদিক দিয়ে কিন্তু ওরা খুবই প্রফেশনাল। তবে হ্যা আমাদেরকে আনার সময় যে বাসগুলো ইউজ করছে এগুলার অবস্থা খুবই পাই নাই তবে চায়না সাউথনের এইসব জিনিসগুলো খুবই মানে আমার কাছে খুবই ভালো লাগে এয়ারলাইন্সের এই গুণগুলা আমাদের খাবার দাবার চলে আসছে। এখন হলো যে আমি আপনাদেরকে দেখাবো ওরা কি কি আইটেম দিছে। আমরা যদি ক্যামেরাটা একটু মুভ করি। এই যে দেখুন এখানে হল যে চিকেন উইথ রাইস এবং নিচে হল যে ফ্রুট সহ স্নক আইটেম দিয়ে দিছে। আমরা ক্যামেরাটা একটু দূরে রাখি। আমাদের পাশে এক ভদ্র লোক আছে ভাইয়া যার হেল্প নিয়ে ভিডিওটা করা হচ্ছে বেসিক্যালি উনার টেবিলে রেখে। সো আমরা আপনাদেরকে আরো কিছু দেখাবো। এটা দেখার জন্য আমরা ক্যামেরা আরেকটা ইউজ করতেছি। ওকে ক্যামেরা ওপেন করে নিলাম। খাবারে কি কি আছে দেখি। পানি না পড়লে চলে। অতিরিক্ত গরম খাবার। ও চিকেনের সাথে হল যে ওরা সবজিও দিয়ে দিছে। গুড। আর এখানে দিয়ে দিছে ওরা একটা কলা। একটা কেক এবং একটা বিস্কিট। এই যে দেখুন গরম গরম দোয়া বের হচ্ছে। এখানে হল যে ব্ল্যাক কফি কলা বাট আমি চামিচ খুজতেছি। ওরা কি চামিজ দেই নাই? ওকে খাবার দাবার স্টার্ট করি আমরা। টিসটা কাজে লাগবে। অনেক সময় সৌদি এয়ারলাইন্স ও কাতার এয়ারলাইন্সে ওরা হল যে [নাক ডাকা] এই জিনিসগুলা ওরা হল যে স্টিলের দেই। দিয়ে গাজর এবংশিম দিয়ে চিকেনটা রান্না করছি। খাবার টেস্ট যদি বুঝি নো স্পাইসি। তবে রাইসটা খাইতে পারি। খুব মিষ্টি খাবার বানাইছে ওরা। ওদের অনুপাতে। আপনি যদি আশা করেন বিমানের খাবার ভালো হবে সম্পূর্ণ। আল্লাহু আকবার। এখন প্রশ্ন প্রথমবার যদি আপনি যান চায়না অথবা চায়না ট্রান্জিট হয়ে টিকেট কাটবেন কিনা আপনাদেরকে বলি নিরাপত্তার দিক দিয়ে 100 তে 100 টার্বন্স কেবিনদের বেহেমিয়ার অসাধারণ মানে টারবো বেশি হচ্ছে reviews.transcript_full: May 05, 2026 Terminal 3, Tokyo Haneda International Airport, Japan I didn't realize that after spending 7 days in Japan, I had to go back home. But this trip was still a memorable experience for me. Because it was my first time trying the flight service from "Singapore Airlines" with Boeing 777-300ER Fleet Heading to the Check-In Counter I boarded from Haneda International Airport, so it's close to the city center. I will fly to Singapore I will sit in Economy class seat Get a 25kg baggage allowance The fleet that transported me was a Singapore Airlines Boeing 777-300ER Livery Star Alliance This airline is allied with Star Alliance, one of the first and largest airline alliances in the world. This plane is about 19 years old Quite old Even though the Boeing 777-300ER fleet is older than other fleets such as the Boeing 787 and Airbus A350, the seats in Economy class are more comfortable. Waiting Room Atmosphere Lufthansa LH714 Munich-Tokyo My flight is scheduled to depart at 08:55 local time. Boarding Preparation Boarding Getting on the Plane Don't forget to take earbuds for entertainment Greeted by friendly cabin crew Business class cabin Hopefully I'll get a chance to try it another time. Premium Economy Class I sat in Economy Class My Seat Number is 58K (Window Seat) Economy Class Seat View on the Boeing 777-300ER Fleet Remote Control Cup Holder Clothes hanger Table Complete with mirror Pillow Blanket Headrest Earbud Air Sickness Bag Safety Instruction Card In-flight Wifi Connection Information Merchandise Sales Menu Each seat gets a universal power outlet USB Port and Earbud Connection Port Glass cover In-Flight Entertainment Screens The flight from Tokyo to Singapore takes about 6 hours. Cabin crew distributes warm towels Earbud Warm Towel 08:52 Pushback Safety Demonstration Video A wave from the ground handling crew signaled our departure from Japan. See you again in Japan. Taxi to Runway 05 Tokyo City View 09:12 Take Off Leaving Japan View of Haneda Airport from Above Tokyo Kota Yokohama The weather was favorable so I could see Mount Fuji from above. Asking for Orange Juice as a drink and get peanut snacks Chubu Centrair Airport and Nagoya City from above Turbulence begins to occur Entering Unfriendly Weather The turbulence is quite strong It feels scary to me Lavatory Inspection This is what we've been waiting for Food Service Roasted Chicken Thigh Stainless Steel Cutlery Crackers Bread Cheese Coffee Creamer Noodle Sauce Japanese Cold Noodle with Noodle Sauce Air Mineral Butter Get Haagen-Dazs Ice Cream Vanilla Flavor Crossing the Philippines Throughout the journey you can ask the cabin crew for snacks. I asked for Chocolate Bar and Popcorn Will arrive in Singapore soon Lowering cruising altitude 16:14 landed at Changi International Airport, Singapore Taxi to Terminal 2 Disembarking I was satisfied on this flight Thank you for watching See You On The Next Flight

reviews.transcript_full: Good morning everyone I'm now at Los Angeles International Airport Today I'll be flying with one of America's largest airlines United Airlines Polaris Business Class From Los Angeles to Hong Kong During this 15-hour journey What will UA's seat, food and service be like? Let's find out together now It's currently during the World Cup LAX is already very busy this morning But security is moving very quickly There's no longer any need to take off your shoes So the process is much faster now Right after security is the United Club But this time it's International Business Class That means access to the Polaris Lounge It's supposed to be a step above the United Club The Polaris Lounge at LAX is quite spacious Besides the regular sofas There are also many semi-private booths The walkways are also quite wide Even though it's busy today It still doesn't feel crowded There's also a separate dining room Where you can sit down and order a meal The salmon sashimi is thick-cut Served with yuzu sauce It takes away the fishy taste The flavor is very light With no fishy taste at all I didn't expect the sashimi here to be decent Coming here to unwind and grab a bite before departure It feels very laid-back Today I'm in seat 1L The first row by the right window Let's see what's at the seat A special 100th anniversary amenity kit A very soft blanket A small memory foam pillow and a large soft pillow There's also a mattress pad Plenty of overnight amenities are provided With US airlines like this Boarding time always seems generous So it doesn't feel rushed You can get settled before takeoff There's also a large storage compartment The reading light is right beside it The headphones are hanging on the door Behind them is a mirror It's nice that they provide a bottle of water It's actually ice cold Below the compartment are the power outlet and USB ports There's also the TV remote The design is simple, but practical The table is made of plastic But the pattern looks like ceramic It gives it a more premium look The menu is already waiting here Let's see what's on it later There's also a table lamp It looks quite premium too This is the older Business Class seat So there's no privacy door United has recently updated its Business Class The new 787 cabins have privacy doors Although this seat is getting old It still looks well maintained The TV screen isn't very large Below it is a space for your phone and a small laptop The USB charging port is right beside it Below that is the tray table It slides out at an angle Once unfolded, it's very large It's also heavy and very sturdy There's plenty of legroom There's also a compartment for your shoes This is where your feet go in bed mode The leather armrest feels nice It's very comfortable to rest your arm on it All the seat controls are on the right There are different seating modes This rotary knob adjusts the seat position And finally, there's a flight mode button Today's flight has been quite smooth So far, we haven't encountered much turbulence Now let's open up the amenity kit and have a look Wow, this is quite interesting There's a 100th anniversary commemorative pen Toothpaste and a toothbrush There's also a separate pack of skincare products Moisturizer, hand cream and eye gel They're all the basic items But they do give you plenty About an hour after takeoff, lunch will be served There are two choices for the salad appetizer One is prosciutto and the other is beet I chose the beet They also gave me a bottle of olive oil But the salad is already dressed It's quite refreshing But the dressing is quite strong It tastes a little like curry After finishing the salad My main course came right after It's a baked steak Let's see if it's too tough The beef comes with potato and broccolini Broccolini is also quite popular in the US these days This one is cooked all the way through It isn't very crisp because it was baked for quite a while The potato isn't overcooked It's quite the opposite of the broccolini The beef is a little dry It's well done But the beef flavor is quite strong The sauce is a little like BBQ sauce But it's not too strong It's a little better than I expected There are three dessert choices Lemon tart, cheese platter, or ice cream Ice cream has many toppings After all, it's a US airline Don't let the small portions fool you You will definitely be full after the meal There was a screen before takeoff United now has Starlink But today's 787 doesn't have it yet You can still access the internet But the speed is a little slow If you want to watch a movie It's easier to select directly on the touchscreen The screen is a little old But the response is actually quite fast Switching between content is already quite smooth There aren't many international movies Especially Asian movies It's more suitable for watching Hollywood movies I didn't realize United also has a midnight snack bar There are quite a lot of choices There's cup noodles, chips and different fruits You can also get some water I also ordered two types of tapas One is chicken, corn and mushroom It also comes with rice The flavor is actually quite good But the rice is quite dry The other one is black bean corn empanadas It looks a bit like dumplings It's fried first and then baked The flavor is sour and spicy It may not suit those who prefer Asian flavors Once converted into a bed, the width is just about right The length is more than enough I have plenty of room to stretch my legs I just woke up I checked the time I slept twice for three hours each Six hours in total The privacy of this seat is better than expected I can't see the passenger next to me It might be because this is the first row near the lavatory So there is a little more noise The cabin temperature is just right It's neither too cold nor too warm Lying down, especially with the memory pillow Sleeping with the large pillow underneath feels great Today's breakfast comes with a bowl of fruit A croissant And a big bowl of congee There are also three shrimp in the congee It smells really good I think the shrimp were added after cooking So the flavors are quite separate But the shrimp are definitely quite big They're pretty tasty too There are about 20 minutes left until landing So let's wrap up this flight experience Although my seat was a little old It was very clean and well maintained And I think the privacy was very good Because I couldn't see the passenger next to me Maybe because I was in the first row There was a little more noise But once the bed was made with the sheet It was actually quite comfortable to sleep in With movies and internet access The 15-hour journey went by very quickly I also found United's service quite warm The crew would actively interact with passengers It made the whole experience feel quite comfortable Have you flown United's Business Class before? What was your experience like? They now have a new generation of Business Class San Francisco to Singapore or London uses the new Business Class If I get the chance I'd also like to unbox the new product with you That's it for today's United Business Class experience I hope you enjoyed this video Don't forget to like, comment and subscribe See you in the next video

reviews.transcript_full: Emirates offers one of the most sought-after premium products in the world. Over the past 7 years, we've had the chance to experience business class with several different airlines. But does Emirates business class really live up to its reputation for luxury, service, and glamour? Today, we're going to find out aboard their brand new Airbus 350, an aircraft that has been in service for only 3 months. The business class cabin features 32 seats in a 1 2 1 configuration, giving every passenger direct aisle access. For window seats, the even-numbered rows are the best choice, as the seats are positioned closer to the window and offer more privacy. In the center, it's the opposite. The seats in the odd-numbered rows are positioned closer together, making them a great choice for couples. Since we're traveling as a couple, today we selected seats 5E and 5F. These two center seats are close together and slightly farther away from the aisles, giving us a little more privacy. If you're traveling alone, I would choose one of the center seats that are positioned farther apart, or an even row window seat for maximum privacy. There are three lavatories. One at the front dedicated to business class, and two more at the rear, shared with premium economy. Now, let's get on board. As soon as we step onto the aircraft, the first impression is excellent, an elegant modern cabin and a warm welcome from the smiling cabin crew. Before departure, we're offered orange juice, booster juice, or champagne. For me, I'll go with the orange juice. Emirates takes things a little further with a small mini bar near the seat, stocked with water, sparkling water, and a few snacks. Is it really necessary? Probably not, especially since you can order something almost anytime during the flight. But personally, I really appreciate this little extra touch. Next to the seat, you'll find everything you need to keep your devices charged. A power outlet, USB port, a fast charging USB-C port, and a built-in wireless charger. Business class is also equipped with a removable tablet that allows you to control the screen and the entire in-flight entertainment system. The amenity kit is very well equipped. It includes a Gillette razor, Bulgari products, earplugs, a toothbrush, a comb, and tissues. Emirates also provides very comfortable pajamas made from a blend of modal and elastane. Additional amenities are also available in the lavatories. Emirates in-flight entertainment system is probably one of the best, if not the best, we've experienced on any airline we've flown. The system is extremely responsive, and the selection of movies, TV shows, music, and other entertainment is simply impressive. In this category, Emirates is very hard to beat. Now, let's take a look at today's onboard menu and wine list. I found the menu quite good, but I was particularly impressed by the quality of the wines, which was excellent compared to what you typically find in business class. About 2 hours into the flight, I start my meal with a traditional Arabic mezze. For the main course, I choose the mixed grill followed by the chocolate pecan cake for dessert. After the meal, I take some time to listen to music and take my magnesium while my partner reads a book before we both try to get a few hours of sleep. After waking up, I take the opportunity to check out the premium economy cabin. And surprisingly, there are only about five passengers in the entire section. The cabin is also very elegant. The seats look comfortable and feature both a footrest and a calf rest. There's one thing to keep in mind, though. When the seat in front of you is fully reclined, the space can feel more restricted, especially if you're tall. To avoid this, I would probably choose the first row. The downside is that the entertainment screen is mounted on the bulkhead in front of you, which is a setup I personally like a little less. So, does Emirates new Airbus 350 business class live up to its reputation? There's no question that Emirates offers a luxurious and elegant cabin, an outstanding entertainment system, and very good service from the cabin crew. But the product isn't perfect. In my opinion, the food is still a step behind some other airlines, particularly Qatar Airways, where you can dine on demand and where the presentation is generally more refined. However, I would give Emirates a slight edge when it comes to the wine list, which I found a little more impressive than Qatar Airways. And of course, Qatar's Qsuites still have a major advantage with their closing doors, providing an extra level of privacy. For these reasons, I would place this new Emirates business class somewhere in the middle of our personal ranking of the business class products we've experienced. Of course, a lot also depends on the price you pay. Interestingly, one of the real sweet spots on the Emirates Airbus 350 might actually be premium economy. The cabin is elegant, the seats offer a respectable amount of recline, and you get both a footrest and a calf rest. On a long flight like Dubai to Montreal, those features can make a significant difference and help you arrive much more rested than you would in economy class. Thanks for watching. If you enjoyed this review, don't forget to subscribe to the channel and leave us a comment below. And let us know if you had to choose between Emirates new Airbus 350 business class and Qatar Airways Qsuite, which one would you pick? See you on our next journey.

Now I'm not going to do a full seat walk through here because I've covered this upper class  seat product in detail in previous reviews. I'll link those below. What I will say is that the A3-330  300 cabin feels noticeably different from the Neo. It's older, the finishes show their age  and you don't have the retreat suite or the loft. But the seat works, the bed is comfortable  and for an 8 hour flight to the Caribbean it does the job. So here's how the morning of the flight  actually went. My car was booked for half past six which meant a quarter to six alarm.  When I woke up and checked the app the flight had already been delayed to 20 past 12 more than  two and a half hours. Now I could see from Friday, the A3-24 that the inbound aircraft had departed  Tampa an hour behind schedule and with a scheduled arrival at Heathrow of 950 there was never any  realistic chance of a 935 departure. Virgin knew this well before I did. The problem was it was too  late to cancel the car so I headed to the airport anyway. Despite arriving at Heathrow at half past  nearly two hours before the original departure time the upper class wing was already well into  its morning. Two cars pulled up immediately ahead of me but I was checked in straight away.  And right there at the desk the agent wished me a happy birthday, first of the day.  The upper class baggage allowance was two checked bags, each weighing up to 32 kilos or 70 pounds  plus one cabin bag and a personal item such as a rucksack. The upper class wing has its own  private security channel and it was through in a matter of minutes with one small exception.  My case was pulled aside because I packed a suntan spray inside one of my shoes. Apparently it  looks suspicious on the scanner. It was fine in the end but consider that a tip. If you're traveling  with aerosols pack them openly in your case rather than tucked inside footwear. It'll save you a few  minutes at security. From security it's a short walk to the Virgin clubhouse and given the delay  this was going to be home for the next four hours. It wasn't particularly busy when I arrived  which made for a relaxed start and at the front desk I was greeted and for the second time  that morning wished a happy birthday. At this point I was starting to wonder quite how prominent the  flag was on my booking. I was then shown to the royal box. A word about the royal box because I  need to be transparent here. The royal box is not something you can book. It's not available to  standard upper class passengers or even gold flying club members. Its invitation only reserved  for celebrities and for wings members which is Virgin Atlantic's hidden tier above gold.  There's no application process and no public acknowledgement that it even exists. I'm a wings member  which is why I was shown there. I mention it because I think it's important you know that the royal  box experience I'm about to describe is not what most upper class passengers will get in the clubhouse  even on a birthday. The royal box is a private room tucked in one corner of the clubhouse  exclusively for one party at a time. Inside three large sofas are arranged around tables that  can be moved around to suit how many of you there are. It's entirely separate from the main clubhouse  floor and the difference in atmosphere is immediate, quieter, more relaxed and with a more personal  level of service. Breakfast was brought to the table and the morning settled into something that  felt considerably more civilised than a three hour delay had any rights to.  Then some clubhouse staff arrived with a birthday cake and a bottle of champagne which at half  past eight in the morning is not something I expected. They also bought a second bottle to take away  on the trip. I'll be honest when you're sitting in the royal box with a glass of champagne and  a birthday cake a delayed flight is a lot easier to absorb. The way the ground experience was handled  meant it barely registered as an inconvenience. That's good hospitality. Around 20 to 12 I headed  down to the gate. The gate for the S185 was gate 27. There were no views of the aircraft from the  gate lounge which is always a slight disappointment when you're waiting to board. At the gate the agent  checked my boarding pass and wished me a happy birthday. I asked if something had flagged on her  screen but no she spotted it on my passport a nice touch and the fourth birthday greeting of the day.  Boarding began at around five to twelve. The aircraft GV-Ray, Miss Sunshine, was an Airbus A330-300  and the upper class cabin was full 246 passengers in total across the aircraft. Shortly after boarding  pre-departure drinks were offered, handled an English sparkling wine, orange juice or water.  Boarding was completed by quarter past twelve and the flight service manager came through the  cabin with personal welcomes and yes a happy birthday along with an apology for the late departure.  The doors closed at 26 minutes past twelve. We pushed back shortly afterwards,  taxiing slowly out to runway 27 left and at one minute past one three and a half hours behind  schedule, VS185 was finally on its way to Barbados. The flight service manager made a cabin  announcement at around five past one confirming the flight time of approximately eight hours to  bridge town. Hot towels followed soon afterwards, a prompt start to the in flight service.  Wi-Fi was another matter, it hadn't worked prior to takeoff or immediately afterwards and needed  to be reset. Once it was up and running it cost £20.99 for the full flight and with a download speed  of just under 10 megabits per second it was perfectly usable. An amenity kit was provided.  It contained an eye mask, socks, hand cream lip balm and facial mist, a toothbrush, toothpaste  and earplugs. On the way back from the washroom I spoke to the flight service manager of the bar,  he offered to make me a drink ahead of the crew coming round to take orders.  Food orders followed shortly afterwards from a friendly and attentive crew member.  On the menu was a choice of two starters, sticky Korean chicken or grilled asparagus.  There were three main courses, stuffed chicken breasts, roasted salmon or pea tortellini.  For dessert there were two choices, a white chocolate and passion fruit bavura,  or toffee pudding and a cheese plate. To get things started I ordered a bloody  merry served with a bowl of savorousness criss made especially for virgin Atlantic.  It's a small touch but it's exactly the kind of detail that makes the upper class experience  feel different. Another option and one worth knowing about is the Bacardi Island Snap,  a cocktail built around spiced rum, very much in keeping with where we were headed.  One of the things that made this like genuinely enjoyable was being able to  dine at the bar rather than at the seat. I want to flight this because it's a finite experience.  Virgin is refitting its dreamliner fleet from 2028 and the bar goes as past that refit.  The A3300s are also being retired as the new A33900 Neos arrive. The current Neos have the  loft seating area but the newer deliveries which will have larger upper class cabins won't even  have the loft. The bar as a social dining space is disappearing from virgin Atlantic altogether.  If that experience matters to you the window is closing faster than you might think.  A place setting was laid at the bar for me. A selection of bread rolls was available.  A linen napkin and metal cutlery were provided. To start I had the Korean chicken, small  important but genuinely tasty. There was an asparagus alternative on the menu, though I stuck with  the chicken. A glass of shardonnay alongside. For main course, panko coated chicken, again pretty good.  I switched to a red wine with the main which worked well with it.  The wine list was curated by Jura Bones. One of London's respected fine wine merchants  and it showed the red I had was a 2019 Chateau Canon Cheong from La L'Ord de Pomora.  2019 was a superb Bordeaux vintage and it was drinking beautifully. At that point the seat belt  signs came on so I had to return to my seat but dessert followed there.  And here the birthday treatment continued. Both dessert options were brought to me.  One was a white chocolate bavura. Very small and set aside once we weren't sure about the nut  content. The other was a toffee pudding which was the better choice. Cheese followed and I'll  be honest the selection and presentation weren't quite up to the standard I'd seen in premium  economy on a recent flight. Port was offered though I still had wine. There was then a long  wait for the table to be cleared, not ideal and probably the one service niggle of the flight.  Ice cream was offered later in the flight. Followed by afternoon tea around two hours prior to  landing, sandwiches, cakes, a scone with clotted cream and jam and a glass of handbooked and  sparking wine to finish. If you're enjoying this kind of in-depth review you can join the  DORST automatic cabin crew to get early access to every video before it goes public. The link is  in the description below. There were two toilets for the upper class cabin, one at the front of  the aircraft and a second next to the upper class bar. They were a standard aircraft size.  Paper towels were provided but premium toiletries from Voltery were on hand.  A baby-changing table folded down from the wall.  The entertainment system on the A330-300 is a solid, if unspectacular offering.  At the time of flying there were just over 200 movies available, around 126 TV series  and close to 750 audio options. There were also 13 games, not that I touched those on an 8 hour  flight to the Caribbean. Preparations for landing began remarkably early, around 90 minutes before  touchdown, which felt excessive. The flight service manager explained it was due to the nature  of the descent, a long, while gradual approach. I'll admit I wasn't entirely convinced by that  explanation. The pilot made a PA around 45 minutes before landing and as I mentioned at the  seat selection stage, the less side of the aircraft pays off on this route. The approach takes you  over the island of Barbados before turning to land at grant liadams and the views are genuinely  spectacular. We landed just before 4 o'clock local time, two and a half hours behind schedule.  So Barbados worth it? Here's where I land. The crew on VS185 were exceptional,  genuinely among the best I've experienced in upper class. The food was good, the service was  attentive and on a personal level the birthday touches were a really nice surprise. But I can't  ignore the context. This was an older aircraft on a route that was supposed to be operated by a  newer one. The flight left more than three hours late and the fare around £2,250 per person  is serious money for a product that isn't Virgin's newest. I'm back on this route in November,  though as it stands that's currently scheduled on another A33300. For now though, the experience  was good enough that I'd do it again. If you've enjoyed this video please do give it a like,  it really helps the channel and if you're not already subscribed hit that button now so you don't  miss the next one. I'll see you on the next flight.

reviews.transcript_full: (Transcribed by TurboScribe. Go Unlimited to remove this message.) Today we're back in Germany to ride the newest train in the country, and one that's not without its controversy. We'll be in first class on board this Taugo ICE-L for this three hour trip from Hamburg up to the unique island of Sylt. I will show you around all the classes, the on-board facilities and the dining car and talk about why this train has caused such a stir for Deutsche Bahn. So come along with me on another epic non-stop Euro trip. This journey starts in Hamburg in northern Germany. This is the second largest city in the country and the sixth largest in the EU with a population of around 2 million people. As far as big German cities go, I quite like it here. Especially as it's home to the world's biggest model railway, which is over 15km of track. Ok, let's head to the station. I was staying at the Ghana Hotel, right outside the eastern entrance. This fabulous station dates back to 1906 and houses 8 mainline, 4 S-Bahn commuter and 8 U-Bahn metro platforms. The entrance to the latter you can see straight ahead here. There is a multitude of different shops and food outlets across two levels. There is also a staff ticket office and travel centre here. I love the design, especially the wrought iron, glass walls and ceilings. The most impressive part however is the arched barrel train shed roof, which spans 70 metres across all mainline platforms. From the first floor balcony, you get wonderful views over Germany's largest unsupported train station canopy. Our train today is the 10.25am ICE 2074, which started in Berlin and is currently 16 minutes delayed. Let's check out the route. We will depart Hamburg and head north-west, making 4 planned intermediate stops on route before crossing the causeway over to the island of Silt. Ok, to the platform. These all have step-free access by lifts, if required. As I am just about to head down to the advertised platform 8, our train is switched over to platform 5. This was announced over the tannoy as well as the departure boards changing. And here comes our train for today, hauled by this Chesky Drahi Siemens Vektron Class 384 electric locomotive. This version has a top speed of 230kmph and a maximum power output of 6,400kW. They were meant to be hauled by DB's own new Talgo Class 105 locomotives, but these have yet to be delivered, just one of the many problems facing these trains' entry to service. Trailing is the brand new 17 coach rake of Talgo 230 ICEL coaches. These feature the iconic Talgo weight-saving design, where a single wheelset is shared between two coaches, but more on that later. There are 562 total seats, of which 477 are second class and 82 are first class, where we'll be travelling today. The rearmost coach is also a control car, which will allow for push-pull operation when they are eventually certified. I do think they look pretty smart though, what do you think? The L in ICEL stands for Low Floor. Level boarding is another Talgo feature, assuming correct platform height, such as here in Hamburg. The door next to the wheelchair spaces has a sliding step too, to bridge the small gap. The first class coaches are laid out in a 2 plus 1 configuration, and despite the greyness of the interior looking quite bland, the lighter coloured head cushions and armrests, along with the wooden tables, make the overall aesthetic quite pleasant. We will check them out in more detail once we get going. Staying connected while all is on the move can be complicated, but Holofly makes it incredibly simple. I am currently using Holofly's Global eSIM, giving me fast and unlimited data, without constantly changing SIM cards or worrying about expensive roaming charges. Coverage has been excellent throughout the past two weeks of this Euro trip, where I visited five countries, with the 4G and 5G seamlessly switching as I cross each international border. Holofly offers eSIMs for more than 200 destinations, including global coverage and over 15 regional packages, so you can choose the one that best suits your trip. Frequent travellers can also benefit from Holofly plans, which covers more than 160 destinations. There are unlimited data and 25GB light options with no contract, and you can cancel at any time. You'll also receive the All Was On benefit, providing 1GB of global backup data every month, from the moment your eSIM is installed. And if you need assistance, Holofly's support team is available 24x7 through web chat or WhatsApp. Use code NONSTOPEUROTRIP to get 5% off any Holofly eSIM, or 10% off a Holofly plans subscription for your first 12 months. Click my link above or in the description below to get connected with Holofly today. In the end we leave 18 minutes after the scheduled departure time at 10.43am. This journey from Hamburg to Esterland on the island of Sylt covers 240km, which is planned to take us 3 hours and 17 minutes of travel time. I booked about two weeks in advance and got my spa price ticket for €48.99, which is pretty good value in my opinion. This included an optional seat reservation fee of €6.90. With hindsight, I definitely didn't need to buy this, but you just never know with German trains. However, if you book earlier, then super spa price tickets start from €35.99 in first class, or from just €26.99 in second class. Various discounts for children up to the age of 14 are also applicable, see on screen now. All onboard announcements are made in both German and English. We warmly welcome you here. Shortly after departure, tickets are checked and the first class host comes around to take food or drinks orders. I passed on this as I want to visit the dining car myself later on. Luggage can be stored on the stacks near to the coach ends or on the overhead racks up above. The seat does look very stylish and although far from the most comfortable I've tried, had okay padding, a reasonable shape and a large winged headrest. There is a reading light built into this too. There are movable padded armrests and the seat can be reclined a bit using this button and sliding the base. Legroom is pretty good with the seat in front featuring an adjustable footrest too. This also has a small netted storage pocket and a large tray table with drinks indent. A small phone holder is at the top of the seat back. There is also a drinks holder in between the two seats and a litter bin down below. Two standard European style power sockets can be found just next to your own seat. Up above are both fixed and movable coat hooks and a very good window blind. Overall a reasonably comfortable first class product. You can scan the QR code on the seat back to connect to the ICE portal which includes free WiFi for all passengers. This was easy to connect to but was woefully slow. As we pick up a bit of speed you can really hear the Talgo ride quality come to light. While it is not as bad as some I have been on, there is just a constant background rattle with occasional big bumps. There are also some other interesting noises that the train makes like these strange hissing sounds. We are now on the approach to Itzyho, where our Czeski 3 Vektron locomotive will be swapped for a Deutsche Bahn bi-mode version for the rest of the route to Silt which is currently un-electrified. There is a scheduled 16 minute stop here for this to take place and we are just over 15 minutes late on arrival. Anyway, after sitting around for another 15 minutes, a man with a high-vis came down outside our coach and after some hands on heads, a few phone calls and a complete train reboot, we are on the move again at 11.54, now 38 minutes late. I have no idea what happened, there were no announcements made. Ok, let's go and check out the rest of the train now. These Talgo coaches are short, around half the length of a normal size train coach and due to this they don't have toilets in every one. There are 11 throughout the 17 coaches, including one which is fully accessible. Here is one of the regular ones. The water, soap and paper towels were all stocked up, as was the toilet roll. The toilet flush works and it was very clean overall. Now let's have a look at second class, which is in a 2 plus 2 layout with a mix of airline style and bay seating around a table. The seats are similar to mine in first class, however come with a reduced width and legroom as you'd expect. All the other amenities are the same with the exception of a shared centre armrest and no reading light. Honestly, if you could guarantee the train is as empty as it is today then I would go for second class every time. Moving through to the wheelchair spaces, of which there are three, all with two accompanying companion seats and all the facilities you get in the other classes. The fully accessible toilet along with baby changing facilities is in the adjacent vestibule, this was also very clean. A bit further and there are lots of amenities for families travelling with children. First, we have this compartment which features two sets of bay seating and a large central space for buggies and prams. More of the latter can be found in the next coach along, as well as plenty more seating dedicated to families which can be identified by the cartoon decorated walls. All of this is absolutely brilliant to see. Right down the far end there are eight vertical bike storage spaces. You must have a bike ticket to bring one on board, which start from €7.50 depending on distance. The bike space reservation is included with this ticket. We're now passing over the Kiel Canal which dates back to 1887. Every year around 32,000 ships use this 98km waterway which links the North and Baltic seas, reducing their transit distance by 460km. Although I am pretty impressed with most of the interior of this new Talgo ICE-L, the bistro dining car is where it's seriously let down. It has just 12 seats for the 17 coach train. There is also a vastly inferior menu to regular ICE services with just three hot options which is very disappointing. I went for the chilli con carne and bread roll along with a warm Coke Zero as they weren't chilled and they had no ICE. Ironic, eh? It wasn't exactly good value either with the total being €16.70. At Heide we pass a southbound service from Westerland to Berlin. This journey takes just over five and a half hours in total. After Hamburg heading eastbound, the train can use the high speed line to get up to its maximum speed of 230kmph. I'm going to have a moan now that Deutsche Bahn have branded this train as an ICE, which is their flagship high speed brand. There is no way that this train is anywhere close to on a par with the recently introduced 320kmph capable ICE3 Neo. I rode this not too long ago and the difference is night and day. I believe they have branded this Talgo set as an ICE to simply allow them to charge higher fares. We are now coming up to the most interesting part of today's route. Our destination at Westerland is on the holiday island of Silt, near to the Danish border in the far north of Germany. This island does not have a road connection to the mainland and as such the only way to reach it is by ferry or rail. And if you want to take your vehicle, then it will be loaded onto one of these auto-rack shuttle trains here at Niebuhr. This is a hugely popular service with holidaymakers, day-trippers and delivery drivers alike, with departures up to every half hour in peak summer season. To take your car over to Silt, prices start from €68 one way or €112 for a return journey which includes all passengers. At most times you can just turn up and go, but booking in advance in peak holiday season is definitely recommended as you can see how busy it gets. As well as these ICEL services, there is also the hourly RE6 regional train from Hamburg to Westerland. One of these trains can be seen over on the far platform here. I was about to say how well we are doing for time now with our delay still hovering around the same as before. However, all is about to go catastrophically wrong in a way only German railways can manage. We come to a rest at Klankspur, the last station on the mainland. We were not scheduled to stop here, which is never a good sign. I thought maybe it was due to some congestion on the single track sections ahead. But no, I will spare you the waiting around, but we were stationary for over 45 minutes while the train was restarted a number of times, with the AC, power sockets and carriage lights going on and off repeatedly during this period. Finally, and with the onboard information screen still not having caught up with our delay, I felt like cheering once we finally started moving again. This next 10 minutes is by far where you will see the best train window views of the journey. Leaving the German mainland, we must first pass through the Rickensbuller Kuge wetland nature reserve, before crossing the Hindenburg Dam, an 11km man-made causeway across to the island of Zilt, which opened in 1927. Dear guests, in a few minutes we have arrived at our last stop, Westerland. Today, 70 minutes delayed. At 40.41 we are there on platform 1. We say thank you and wish you a pleasant afternoon. We finally arrive at Westerland station at 2 .45pm, actually 74 minutes delayed. This entitles me to a 25% refund on my ticket price, which is easily claimed through the DB app. I had the money back to my card three days later. As we alight, let me summarise this journey from Hamburg to Westerland onboard the new DB Talgo ICE-L. Overall, it's a good train internally, well fitted out to a premium finish and quite comfortable. The price I paid was reasonable. It certainly doesn't live up to the ICE name, either in speed, ride quality or even the dining car offering. It's a shame that DB branded it as such, as I think Intercity would have been much more fitting. Have you been on a DB ICE-L in Germany yet? If so, what was your experience like? Let me know in the comments below. I will have a video coming soon on the nearly identical Danish version of this train, so stay tuned for that. Spoiler alert, it was way worse. Don't forget to subscribe. Thanks for watching to the end and I'll see you in the next video.
