reviews.transcript_full:
Six hundred and fifty dollars, one way… Now, 
that's less than a lot of economy fares on the   full-service airlines. So, what's the catch?
Today's flight on this rather tired-looking   Boeing 787 Dreamliner takes me 
from Melbourne to Singapore.  Let's find out whether Scoot 
Plus is too good to be true,   or the best value premium seat 
leaving Australia right now
   I guess we can say Melbourne has beaten 
Sydney to the first project sunrise flight? And yea, that was our first-ever YouTube video. 
It is kind of scary to see how young we were. Back at the airport, I am off to 
find the Scoot check-in counter.  Scoot is Singapore Airlines’ low-cost 
arm and, at the time of recording,   operates 8 weekly flights to Melbourne.
Most of these are afternoon departures. Today’s   Sunday flight is an exception, departing at 9:35pm 
and arriving at an ungodly 4am in Singapore. The Scoot Plus fare includes priority check-in and   30kg of checked baggage. Both 
of which I made full use of. Through immigration and security pretty quickly,   and off to the lounge, I guess…
Except… there isn't one.  Scoot doesn’t provide any form 
of lounge access with its fares. So, I guess I will hang out at the airport. It's almost time to board, so I head 
to my gate — gate 16 today — where I   come face to face with my aircraft, 
a rather weary-looking Boeing 787. Priority boarding is another perk that comes with 
Scoot Plus, and one that was actually enforced Parked right next to us was a 
Singapore Airlines A350, and one that   looked like it had been polished that morning.
Anyway — let's take a look at today's seat map. Scoot has a fleet of 24 Boeing 
787 family aircraft. The Melbourne   flights are operated by the -9 variant.
The type features 375 seats in total.  The Scoot Plus cabin at the front 
has 35 seats in a 2-3-2 layout. So, this is the Scoot Plus cabin.  The 2-3-2 layout does mean a middle seat 
row, which you will probably want to avoid. The seat itself is a leather-covered 
recliner. With a seat width of 19.5”,   it feels reasonably wide, and despite 
its age, the leather still feels solid.  Legroom is outstanding too, 
with 38 inches of pitch.  The recline is generous as well, all 
controlled by these manual levers. And yes, there is no seat-back entertainment. 
All you get is a generous seat pocket.  There are AC power sockets in the centre console,   but you will be out of luck 
if you are after a USB port. Overall, it is a decent hard product that reminds 
me somewhat of the Jetstar business class seat. Pre-departure service was this cup 
of water. And… well, that's it.  Pushback was on time, followed by   a long taxi out to runway 34.
And then we were off.
   Not long after takeoff, the crew came around to 
confirm my pre-selected meal and drink choice.  I was also given this voucher 
for the inflight wifi. It came in handy, because Scoot 
doesn't offer IFE of any sort.  But you're better off downloading something before 
your flight — or paying some fairly ridiculous   prices for their wifi packages.
Fifty-five US dollars for a gigabyte.   The voucher that comes with Scoot Plus 
gives you 200 megabytes, which isn't a lot.  The speed was reasonable for plane 
internet, fine for messages, not much else. About an hour after departure, the meal arrived.  And this is it — the full Scoot 
Plus dining experience, on one tray. The main I preselected was a Curry Chicken 
Biryani Rice, served sealed with a label on   top telling you to peel back with care.
I took that warning very seriously,   considering my past history of spilling food 
on myself and the very dodgy tray table. I pre-selected this meal weeks ago when I booked.   These are some of the other meal choices provided.
Accompanying it was a drink, a chocolate muffin,   a Biscoff biscuit, a wet wipe and 
some plastic cutlery. That's the lot. The curry chicken and biryani rice 
were hot and filling. It was on par   with economy class offerings, 
but nothing more than that.  There's no alcohol included 
unless you paid for it. And that's it in terms of service for the 
flight. No second service, no snack later on,   nothing between here and Singapore.
If you want more, you're paying for   it. Scoot sells combo meals on 
board from around twelve dollars. Service was prompt, friendly and professional. 
Efficient rather than warm, but no complaints. I leaned back into my seat and tried to 
sleep through the rest of the flight.  And if you want a blanket or eye mask, be sure to 
bring your own as none will be provided for free. The rest of the flight was uneventful and some 
hours later, we were on approach to Singapore.  My watch reckoned I had managed 
almost five hours of sleep — broken,   but on an overnight in a recliner, I'll take it. So, time to look back at 
this Scoot Plus experience,   the hard product has a lot going for it.
Th seat’s generous pitch, width and recline   combined to provide a proper seat, almost as 
good as premium economy on other airlines.  The soft product is where it falls short. 
No lounge or inflight entertainment.   Two hundred megabytes of wifi and 
eye-watering prices if you want more.  One pre-selected meal. No blanket or eye mask. Put it next to even Jetstar's business 
class and Scoot gives you noticeably   less. In some ways it's thinner 
than a good premium economy product. But the question is what else six 
hundred and fifty dollars gets you   on this route. And most of the time, the 
answer is a seat down the back in economy.  Against that, this is totally worth it. Yes, 
you're paying for the seat, not the service.   If what you want is to arrive in Singapore 
having slept, that's the part that matters. Let me know what you think about 
Scoot Plus in the comments.  And if you want to see how this stacks 
up against the seat it reminds me of,   the Jetstar business class review is right here!

reviews.transcript_full: Previously After checking out three different oneworld lounges at BKK we continue our journey and finally get to review Cathay Pacific's A350 Business Class and see what it's actually like If you haven't seen the previous episode I recommend giving it a quick watch first But without further ado let's continue our happy little journey Cathay Pacific Business Class Episode 2 of this four-part series Let's... 3 2 1 Take off ✈️ Hello everyone, I'm Ben That's right, we're already at the gate It feels a little weird starting the video here But... that's fine We get to see the plane right away Today's flight is Cathay Pacific Bangkok ✈️ Hong Kong CX704 A350-900 Cathay Pacific is the world's third-largest A350 operator Its fleet currently includes 18 A350-1000s and 30 A350-900s behind only SQ in first place and QR in second Their average age is around 8 years But today's aircraft B-LRI is a little older at almost 10 years old But... none of that matters The sunset today is absolutely gorgeous It looks incredible shining on the plane Business Class passengers happen to be boarding group 2 After passengers requiring assistance and the fancy elite members it's finally our turn to board Let's take a look at this aircraft's layout Cathay's A350-900 only has one seat configuration 38 Business Class seats 28 Premium Economy seats and 214 Economy seats in 1-2-1 2-4-2 and 3-3-3 configurations respectively Hehe~ After flying Cathay so many times I finally don't have to walk all the way to the back Today's seat is 17K The seat itself is the classic reverse herringbone Safran Cirrus III Seat As soon as we get to the seat we can already see a comfy pillow waiting for us and on the side table there's also a physical menu We'll take a closer look at those later Let's look at some numbers first First up, the legroom is pretty insane For reference, I'm comparing this to EVA Air's 777 Business Class because that's... pretty much the only Business Class I've flown that I can compare this to With 45 inches of seat pitch and a seat width of 20.2 inches both are slightly better than EVA Air But honestly... they're all about the same to me My legs can't reach the end anyway But Cathay definitely does feel noticeably more spacious This extra space on the inside for someone who likes sleeping on their side and curling up their legs like me is extremely ergonomic And of course, this compartment opens up too .... Wait a second Isn't this... our old friend Surfshark? (LMAO) Did I just shark you Did I just shark you when you least expected it? Our good friend Surfshark is basically an online teleportation device For someone like me who's constantly traveling around the world like a weird human being it's actually incredibly useful When I'm traveling whether at airports, hotels, or cafés I'm almost always connected to public Wi-Fi It's definitely convenient but public Wi-Fi isn't as safe as you might think But once you turn on Surfshark it encrypts your connection giving you an extra layer of protection Together with its strict no-logs policy you can feel a little more secure when using public Wi-Fi The new email scam checker can also identify emails containing phishing threats giving me all-around online protection And then some websites or streaming platforms have regional restrictions that prevent you from accessing them That's when Surfshark can instantly activate teleportation mode and teleport you to another country With over 140 locations worldwide and more than 4,500 servers wherever you want to go it's pretty much just one click away Plus one account works on unlimited devices and there's 24/7 customer support With all that, what are you waiting for? Just click the link now or use my promo code and you'll get an extra 4 months of Surfshark Yay~ Thank you, everyone~ And thank you to Schrödinger's Surfshark for sponsoring this video So, we... where were we again...? Oh, right Storage Perfect timing Let's take a look at the other storage spaces too The side table is right here Let me show you And if we open this compartment here inside you'll find a bottle of water over-ear noise-cancelling headphones a little mirror that pops up and a small pocket Slightly awkwardly you have to dig everything out before you can find all the ports inside There's USB a universal power outlet and a headphone jack Personally, I don't find this particularly convenient But... it's fine I get to sit up front so who am I to complain? Moving over to the side this is your little control panel a reading light with adjustable brightness the PSP for the entertainment system and... the seat adjustment controls We'll play with those later when I'm being lazy For now, let's look over by the aisle There's a coat hook up top and a literature pocket underneath Inside you'll find the safety card an airsickness bag and the inflight magazine There's not a whole lot in there But at least on both sides your arms each have a comfy little home It's just that the one on my left was ridiculously stuck It took me forever to finally pop it up But... once I got it up it was like I'd unlocked a secret compartment There's a hidden spot for a water bottle underneath I have to say the storage on this seat is genuinely pretty impressive Perfect for people with lots of little things Okay, very nice What else do we have? Let's take a look at this big screen up front The entertainment screen can be stowed away You might need a very long arm to reach it but just push it back like this and there you go It's an 18-inch HD screen running Cathay's latest entertainment system There's really not much to complain about here Although it's still missing a few features found on the new Aria Suite I'll show you those in Episode 4 But Cathay's entertainment system is excellent as always Every time I fly Cathay, I look forward to seeing what new movies they have TV shows news music games shopping the flight map and cameras on the plane's butt and head It's all here Don't worry I think it's basically impossible to get bored on this flight Very nice~ Alright, back to the seat Is there anything else we haven't covered? The seat itself has a headrest that adjusts up, down, left, and right And one thing I really like is there's a small privacy shield on the aisle side It's not as fancy as having a door but honestly, it's a very cost-effective way of providing some privacy And if that little reading light isn't bright enough there are also overhead lights And Cathay is generous enough to let you turn both of them on unlike energy-saving champion EVA Air which only lets you turn on one And that's it That's Cathay Pacific's A350 Business Class seat I really like it At least personally, I think it slightly beats EVA's 777 What do you guys think? The flight attendants were also very attentive As soon as we boarded they came around with hot towels welcome drinks and asked what we'd like for our meal Let's start with a little champagne to ceremoniously kick off this journey Not long after the safety video started playing and we pushed back right on time That's also when I secretly discovered another little light underneath the side table This trip to Bangkok was short but very enjoyable Hopefully I'll be back soon to visit my friends But for now, let's take off It's a little dark but let's still take a moment to enjoy this beautiful engine view See you in a bit~ Okidoki Welcome back~ Once we reached cruising altitude the flight attendant proactively came over to ask if I wanted a blanket I said yes and then she just tucked me right in Peasant Ben had absolutely no idea how to react But anywayz it's time to check out the Wi-Fi After flying Cathay so many times in my life I've finally gotten to use Cathay's Wi-Fi for free When it comes to Cathay this is pretty impressive every aircraft in their fleet has inflight Wi-Fi But if you want to use it for free only First Class Business Class Diamond and Gold status members and members flying Premium Economy are eligible Yep As for the speed it was pretty decent in actual use I'll put my speed test screenshot here too Coverage also seems to be almost worldwide so there's really not much to complain about Hopefully one day in Economy we can at least get free Wi-Fi for messaging Think about it, Cathay~ Alright After playing around with the PSP for a bit next up is of course what I've been looking forward to most meal time! The tray table pulls out from here and as you can see, it folds out You can also easily push it forward so if you need to get out while eating you still have a little room and won't be held hostage by your food Speaking of food what options are on the menu? For drinks alcohol takes up a big part of the menu red wine white wine cocktails whisky beer you can order them all But if you're like me and don't really drink much there's also juice soft drinks coffee and tea plus some special options like Hong Kong milk tea and hot chocolate Now onto the food There are two choices for the main course five-spice chicken with fermented red bean curd and what I chose this time fried tiger prawns with tamarind sauce Ta-da! And here's the food! Look at this~ Don't these colors make it look incredibly appetizing? The bottom-left corner is empty because... the flight attendant soon came by with a basket of warm bread to fill that empty spot Garlic bread—you can't go wrong So let's hurry up and dig in! Okay, first up, the drinks It comes with a glass of water and I ordered the Cathay classic Cathay Delight Don't judge me but this is actually my first time trying it kiwi juice + coconut milk + mint leaves Mmmmm That's pretty good~ Nice and milky No, I'm not swearing but with a refreshing touch to it Delicious! If I had to name one downside I'd say this... isn't the best drink to pair with a meal So next time, I might order this as my welcome drink I think that would work better Next up, the appetizer Thai grilled pork neck salad It doesn't look like much but there's actually quite a lot of meat underneath Drizzle on that sweet and sour Thai dressing Ohhh~ So good Nice and tangy just like the ulcer in my mouth absolutely exploding in there Ughhh Annoying I'll just have to endure it Let's move straight on to today's main course Prawns, rice, and veggies OOOKKAYYY Very generous Five prawns and none of them are particularly small Take a bite and it's packed with meat Very satisfying But I also have to say the flavors are definitely pretty intense Towards the end it got a little spicy, but that's fine because I have absolutely zero spice tolerance But the sauce is also quite salty and oily so you really need to eat it with rice But if you watched the previous episode, you'll know my stomach right now is basically on the verge of exploding So I ended up in this awkward situation where I wanted to eat... but physically couldn't eat anymore The veggies on the side are pickled cabbage with scrambled eggs Pretty interesting It's just a shame that I didn't find it particularly refreshing so this entire main course felt... a little difficult to finish Let's just have some fresh fruit instead This is exactly what I want right now Ohhh~ Cold and sweet Even the pineapple isn't sour at all Very refreshing APPLE-solutely AMAZING! 🤣🤣🤣 But then I got hit with another attack that garlic bread from earlier with some butter CRAPPP So good, but... so fattening 🐷 Whatever, let's not worry about that Let's just enjoy this rare Business Class experience Making myself feel guilty about it would just be unfair to myself And of course how could we finish the meal without Cathay's classic Häagen-Dazs? It was served after everyone had mostly finished eating This time, I got vanilla Nom nom So happy Getting ice cream on a plane is pure happiness I think it's time for a quick summary Overall, I thought the inflight meal was... pretty good Aside from the main course being a bit salty and heavy I really don't have much to complain about They were very generous with the prawns The appetizer fruit bread and drinks were all great The plates and cutlery also made the meal feel quite special I personally really enjoyed it I think the bigger problem was... before I even got on the plane my stomach was already about to explode I... I blame my friend So I think if my stomach had been a little emptier when I ate this meal I might've felt differently Who knows But either way the food is already in my stomach Let's get up and move around and check out Cathay's Business Class bathroom while we're at it Cathay's A350 Business Class has three bathrooms in total shared between 38 passengers That's a great ratio so you rarely have to wait The bathroom is also well stocked with amenities Bamford hand wash body lotion face mist and for some reason, there's also an unbranded hand wash Maybe they want you to use less of the expensive one Then you've got the usual baby changing table two coat hooks a full-length mirror toilet seat covers sanitary pads cups and air vents Not bad It's got everything you need What's more unusual is you can also find a window in the bathroom so you can relieve yourself under the stars I don't even know what I'm saying anymore Anyways, that's about it Let's head back and lie down Before we arrive in Hong Kong let's relax and do absolutely nothing for a bit By the way I noticed the pillowcase actually has a Bamford logo on it so I'll just assume it's a fancy pillow Over on the aisle side there's another section that can pop up but it seemed a little broken so I ended up pulling it up by hand giving you just a tiny bit more room to wiggle around And with my legs fully stretched out my feet reach about here As you can see, there's still plenty of room for me to be a happy little caterpillar Wa wa And that's it From there, we flew all the way back to Hong Kong Sad sad But... it's time to wrap things up When we arrived in Hong Kong I was a little sad The time went by way too quickly But Cathay's A350 Business Class was... really good~ I can't really bring myself to complain much After all, I cherish every chance I get to fly Business Class But the storage is excellent the seat goes fully flat the service is excellent and the food is pretty good Does this seat feel outdated? Of course if you really compare it with the latest Business Class products out there it definitely feels a little dated But is it actually outdated? I think even today with competition this intense it's still a very solid product I think it can easily hold up for a few more years Add in the fast-track service from Bangkok and the lounge experience and overall, it's still a great experience So if you get the chance I'd definitely recommend giving it a try I don't think you'll be disappointed Mhm And that's it That's everything for this episode~ If you enjoy these airline review videos don't forget to like, share, save, and subscribe And once again, thank you to all my lovely supporters for supporting my channel ❤️ If everything goes according to plan the next episode picks up after we arrive in Hong Kong at Hong Kong Airport Cathay's home turf for some lounge hopping We're only halfway through the journey So I'll see you in the next episode~ Biboo

reviews.transcript_full: NNAとJALが羽田を加山線においてお互いのフライト時刻を調整と報道がありました。 皆さんはどう感じたのでしょうか。私が感じたことを話していきたいと思います。 今回の話は、ターンナルNNAとJALが時間をずらすという小さな大変変更に見えますが、 航空業界の共想ルールが一歩変わる可能性があるという点でかなり重要です。 2026年8月17日現在、報道ではNNAとJALが羽田を加山線で大野調整に向けて動いていることが伝えられています。 今回のポイントは、国交省が協語航空会社会の大野調整について、一定の考え方を明確にしたことを受けた動きだという点です。 普通に考えるとNNAとJALはライバルでNNAとJALどちらを選ぼうかなと思いますよね。 ところが航空会社には一般の企業とは少し違う事情があります。 それが、インの時間帯が誘わり過ぎると、利用者にとっても航空会社にとっても法律が悪いという問題が消します。 まずは利用者のメリットを考えてみます。 例えば極端な例ですが、今日のような時刻表になっていたらどう感じますか? 同じような時刻で飛ばさなくてもいいのにと思いますよね。どちらかが1時間ずらしてくれたら便利なのになと思いますよね。 発着時間を分散させることで、どの時間帯でも利用しやすくなります。 次に航空会社のメリットを見ます。 直近の見た時間に2台の飛行機を飛ばすと、上客が分散してどちらのビームを満席になりにくくなります。 時間をずらすことで重要の時間帯を分散でき、結果として路線全体の使い合ってが改善する可能性があります。 航空会社にとって、運知には人数、運行時間などは共想の重要な要素です。 そのため、ライバル関係にあるAMAとJALが自然に話し合い、この時間はAMAが飛ばすので、JALは別の時間にしましょうといった取り決めを行うと、共想を制限するカルテルにつながる恐れがあります。 もし航空会社同士が避速にビンスを得らそう、同じ時間帯には飛ばさないように使用などと決めてしまえば、 利用者が航空会社を選ぶ機会がひり、運知にはサービスの共想も弱まる可能性があります。 その結果、航空会社同士が共想しなくなり、最終的に利用者が振り焼きを受けるのではないこという記念がありました。 ダブルトラックとは同じ航空路線に似射以上の航空会社が参入して運行することです。 例えば、羽田おかやま線をAMAとJALの行動が運行している場合、これがダブルトラックに当たります。 これはAMAとJALが同じ航空会社同士が運知を下げたり、サービスを改善したりする効果を期待したものです。 航空会社には、お互いに話し合ってゆずり合うのではなく、同じ航空線で自由に共想することで利用者により良いサービスを提供することが求められてきました。 そのため、これまでの航空業界では、共合するAMAとJALが運行時間やビンスについて、事前に話し合うことには慎重な姿勢が取られてきました。 AMAとJALが羽田おかやま線のダイヤを調整することが難しかった背景には、羽田空港の発着枠が限られていることがあります。 羽田空港では、飛行機が好きな時間に自由に立着力できるわけではありません。 カスソロや完成などの能力には限界があるため、一日に運行できるビンスには上限があります。 そのため、国土交通省が航空会社に発着枠を配分しています。 国交省の資料では、羽田の国内線発着枠は段階的に増えてきましたが、それでも貴重な資源であることは変わりありません。 羽田の発着枠は限られた責任ようなもの、その責任を共想相手のAMAとJALが勝手に相談して分けると、共想を邪魔する可能性がある。 だから今までは慎重でした。しかし、利用者の利便性を高める目的なら、どこまで調整を認められるのか、そこが今回の大きなポイントになると思います。 結論から言うと、共想を守るだけでは、国内航空ネットワークを一時で気なくなってきたため、一定の条件で共挙を認める方向へ政策を転換したと考えるのが自然です。 なぜ今までダメだったのに、急にAMAとJALの大野調整が認められる方向になったのかを、航空業界そのものの環境変化から見るとわかりやすいと思います。 これまで日本の航空政策では、AMAとJALなど複数の航空会社を同じ路線に参入させ、共想させることが基本でした。 航空会社同士が共想すれば、運勤が下がったり、ビンスが増えたり、サービスが工場したりする。これが利用者にとってもとも望ましいという考え方です。 そのため、共合する航空会社が、この時間はAMA、この時間はJALといった形で自然に大量話し合うことには、独戦金支放状の問題が生じる可能性があり、これまで非常に慎重でした。しかし、近年になって航空業界を取りまく環境が大きく変わりました。 大きなきっかけの一つが、新型コロナウイルスの流行です。コロナカでは、出帳や旅行が大幅に現象しました。その後、旅行需要は回復しましたが、オンライン会議やテレワークが定着したことで、以前のようにビジネス客が飛行機を利用する状態には完全には戻っていません。 特に、地方路線では、以前なら十分な重要があった時間帯でも、状態が集まりにくくなっています。その結果、AMAとJALが同じ時間帯に共想してビーンを飛ばしているけれど、両方とも雑責が生まらないという状況が起こりやすくなりました。 以前は、日車が共想すること時代に大きな意味がありましたが、現在は路線によっては、日車が共想を続けることで、逆に路線全体の再算があっかするという問題が出てきたのです。 その結果、地方路線は徹体という選択肢も出てきました。高空会社にとって再算の悪い路線をいつまでも維持することは簡単ではありません。 AMAとJALが同じ時間帯にビーンを飛ばしていて、どちらも十分な状況を確保できなければ、この路線は再算が合わないという判断につながります。 そして最悪の場合、AMAが徹体する、またはJALが徹体するということになります。 さらに両者とも再算が取れないと判断すれば、二者とも徹体してしまうという可能性もあります。 そうなると、共想どころか地域から高空輪そのものがなくなってしまいます。 国土交通省が2020年5月に公表した国内高空のあり方に関する優式社会議の報告書も、国内高空が厳しい事業環境に置かれていることを踏まえ、 高空外社間の共想を原則として維持しながら、国内高空ネットワークと利用者の利便性を確保する必要があると、国の考え方が変わりました。 これまでは、AMAとJALを共想させることが利用者の利益になるという考え方が中心でした。 しかし現在は、共想させることも重要だが、共想の結果として路線そのものがなくなってしまっては意味がないという問題が出てきました。 そこで国土交通省は2020年5月、一定の条件を見たす場合には高空外社同士の大や調整などを認める考え方をねえ確認しました。 ここが今回の報信展観の確信です。 ただし、今回の制度変更はAMAとJALは自由に話し合っていいという意味ではありません。 むしろ、共想を意地することを基本としながら、路線維持や利用者の利便性向上のために必要な場合に限って一定の強調を認めるというものです。 この報信展観には、人工現象、地方の高空需要の変化、コロナ号のビジネス需要の構造変化、人手不足、高空外社の集液やっかなど、国内高空ネットはあくそのものを意地することが難しくなっている現実があります。 だからこそ国は、共想化、共想化の2社たくいつではなく、共想を基本にしながら必要なところでは共長するという大師さんの選択肢を作ろうとしているのです。 羽田おか山線は全国で初の敵をケースとなります。今後割り可能ような展開が予想されます。 今回の羽田おか山線の取り組みは、他の羽田地方線にも広がる可能性があります。 ただし、すべての路線でNNAとジャルがダイヤを相談するようになるわけではありません。 国交勝の2021年5月の報告書では、国内線の厳しい事業環境を踏まえ、共想を基本としつつ、大や調整や会社環境業などによって国内高空ネットワークを意地する報告が示されています。 今回の羽田おか山線で重要なのは、単純にNNAとジャルが同じ路線を飛ばしていることではなく、2社の輪が同じ時間帯に集中しているケースです。 この場合、輪車が同じ時間帯の上下を奪い合うことになります。時間をずらせば輪車は選べる時間が増える、1輪辺りの登場率を上げやすくなる路線全体の重要を取り込める、 ビンスを維持しながら終益性を改善できるというメリットが期待できます。 今回の羽田おか山線も、金接する輪の時間をずらして強行を関わし、路線の終益力を高める狙いです。 一方でドルバコロ線は必要性が低いと思います。 例えば羽田福岡、新知都線、なはのような非常に重要の大きい路線では、NNAとジャルが同じ時間帯に飛ばしても十分な上下がに込めます。 むしろ利用者からすれば十分後にジャルがあるということ自体が大きなメリットです。 ですから、重要が非常に強い路線まで無理に大量分散させる必要はありません。 今回の仕組みはどちらかというと重要はある。 しかし、二者が同じ時間帯に飛ばす程ではないという路線との相性がよいと考えられます。 羽田福岡もと線のような路線は、地方路線でありながら非常に重要が強くビジネス重要や長久クラス重要も存在します。 そのため、単純に地方路線だからNNAとジャルで大量分散させる必要はならないと思います。 むしろ熊元のような路線では、重要が強い時間帯は両者が共想する価値があるからです。 一方で、特定の時間帯に二者の輪が金接していて、片方の登場率が低いのであれば、そこだけ時間をずらすという可能性は出てきます。 つまり今後は、路線体ではなく時間帯体で共想と共長を使い分けるという考え方が出てくる可能性があります。 今回の羽田を加山線は、たんなる一路線の台や変更ではなく、NNAとジャルが共想しながら必要な部分では強力して地方路線を維持するという新しいモデルケースになる可能性があります。 今後の羽田地方線は、ざっくり言えば、重要が強い路線はNNA、ジャルがしっかり共想、重要が弱くなった路線は必要に応じて大量調整、さらに重要が厳しい路線は、要備運行、機関現備、共同運行など検討というように、路線の重要に応じて共想、調整、協業を使い分ける方向に進む可能性があります。 これは日本の高空業界にとて、かなり大きな変化です。 高校生自身も国内高空ネットワークの以上今回の議論の中心に捨ており、今後は日常を共想させることだけでなく、西野が共想しながら地方の高空ネットワークをどのこすかが重要な政策テーマになっていきそうです。

reviews.transcript_full: What started as a single flight from Melbourne turned into the biggest adventure Joe and I have ever taken. Over 83 days, we traveled through 10 countries, through thousands of kilometers, and experienced everything from Arctic landscapes and ancient cities to incredible food, unforgettable hotels, and some amazing surprises. This is a start of that journey. >> [music] [music] >> Welcome back to Maximo's Travels. Over the coming months, Joe and I are taking you on our biggest adventure yet. 83 days traveling throughout Malaysia, Finland, Estonia, Turkey, Germany, Belgium, England, Scotland, Iceland, and France. Along the way, I'll be sharing honest airline reviews, hotel reviews, airport lounges, train journeys, day trips, local food, and practical travel tips to help you plan your own adventures. Everything you see is completely self-funded, so every review is based on our own experience and honest opinion. Our adventure begins at Melbourne Airport, where we're boarding Malaysian Airlines flight MH148 to Kuala Lumpur aboard one of their newest aircraft, the Airbus A330-900neo. We've chosen extra legroom economy seats, and in this review, I'll show you exactly what the experience is like from check-in and boarding through the seats, meals, entertainment, comfort, and service. But, this isn't just a one-way review. After traveling for 12 weeks, we'll board Malaysian Airlines flight MH129, giving us the perfect opportunity to see whether the experience is just as good on the journey back home. So, how does Malaysia Airlines stack up on one of its flagship routes? Are the extra legroom seats in economy worth paying for? And is it the perfect airline to begin our 83-day adventure around the world? Come with us. Our journey starts now. But first, a little context. Why fly to Malaysia if we intend to fly to Europe? Well, the answer is twofold. Firstly, we wanted to break up the 24-hour plus journey flying from Melbourne to Europe. And secondly, we had accumulated enough Qantas Frequent Flyer points for two business class return trips from Southeast Asia to Europe. It was far, far easier to book a business class flight using points from Southeast Asia on one of Qantas's partners rather than try and book a Qantas flight from Australia to Europe. We'd had one or two bad experiences flying economy on long-haul routes. So, we decided to book Malaysian Airlines and their Airbus A330-900neo, one of their newest aircraft in their fleets. And we decided to book extra legroom seats as well. So, we found ourselves at Melbourne Airport at a very respectable 10:00 a.m. ready to check in for a 1:25 p.m. departure. Malaysian Airlines check-in opened at least 3 hours before departure. However, it did take around 30 minutes to check in. This is largely due to delays in handling luggage at the airport. Although the amount of luggage some of the passengers were carrying might have contributed to the delay somewhat. Malaysian Airlines allows for two 23 kilo bags in economy per passenger or 32 kilos in business class. You're also allowed one cabin bag up to 7 kilos and a personal handbag or other bag. And ours were checked and tagged. The airport didn't appear that busy and I think we cleared customs, immigration, and security in record time and we headed to the nearest airport lounge, the Aspire Lounge. The old lounge on the mezzanine level is under reconstruction. So, we headed to a temporary lounge on the ground floor, which was somewhat hard to find given its temporary nature and lack of adequate signage. Access to this lounge was courtesy of American Express and my Priority Pass membership. Unlike the other lounge that was under reconstruction, this didn't offer a view of the airport tarmac or of the outside world for that matter. There was a limited selection of drinks and spirits available and the food selection was somewhat meager. And unlike other lounges, it didn't offer barista coffee. There was a machine there instead. And whilst the selection was quite limited, the standard of food was quite good. There was something that I was able to eat that was gluten-free and Joe was able to choose one or two things that were vegetarian as well. The original Aspire Lounge will reopen sometime in 2027. And until that time, I think you're better off going to the American Express Lounge if you've got access to that. Or if you're a Priority Pass member, the Marhaba Lounge at Melbourne Airport International Terminal. As you can see, I didn't have that much on my plate, but it was enough to tide me over until lunch was served on our Malaysian Airlines flight in a couple of hours time. The lounge had a couple of shower cubicles, which I couldn't access because they were locked. The men's toilet was clean, functional, but quite small, which was just as well because the lounge wasn't very busy at all. Given the temporary nature of the lounge, there was no Wi-Fi, so I couldn't do a speed test on it. We spent a couple of hours in there and then slowly made our way to the departure gate. Boarding was orderly and relaxed, and it was called in groups. The airline runs up to three daily services between Melbourne and Kuala Lumpur on its new fleet of A330-900 neos. You can tell these are new aircraft from the moment that you step through the door. This newer, small, spacious, and more comfortable aircraft is another one of the reasons why we chose Malaysian Airlines for this particular route. And I was really hoping this aircraft would be much more comfortable than the Airbus A330-200 and 300s that this airline used in the past, as well as the 737-800 that Qantas uses for some of its Southeast Asian long-haul routes between, say, Melbourne and Indonesia, Bali. The interior of the cabin was modern, clean, and somewhat funky. Malaysia Airlines offers 24 extra legroom seats in economy. We were in seats 10H and 10K, and the extra legroom didn't let us down. There was an extra 4 in or 10 cm of legroom, and it made the whole cabin feel quite spacious. They were new Recaro seats and they were quite functional with plenty of storage and offered a tray table that slid out to meet you, as well as a drink cup holder, but I found that I didn't use this. The plane was equipped with Wi-Fi and the entertainment system was pretty good. It offered a 13.3-in high definition 4K screen. It was fast, bright, and offered a fairly decent selection of movies. The touch screen was quite responsive and it didn't take long for movies and TV shows to start loading. Oh, and by the way, if you're planning to visit Malaysia, you need to pre-enter your details in the digital arrival card prior to your departure. It only takes a few minutes via a phone app. The interior seating is configured in a 2-4-2 configuration, which means I got the window seat and Joe avoided the dreaded middle seat. It was quite a comfortable interior. >> [music] >> Staying connected online is a must when traveling. It's always on and you can choose from an individual destination SIM, 15 plus regional eSIMs, or even a global eSIM customized for daily, weekly, or monthly durations. I was provided with a global monthly plan for 3 months and used it extensively in Asia and Europe. One easy setup that took less than 2 minutes and it instantly and seamlessly connected to a local mobile network wherever I traveled. You get to keep your regular SIM, WhatsApp number, contacts, and access to all your other apps. My HolaFly Global eSIM provided me with great, fast, and reliable service up to 5G in all the destinations I visited. reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone and welcome back to my channel! way back to row 76 Walking down the aisle, the layout is mostly a 2-4-2 configuration, tapering off to a 2-3-2 setup towards the very back Today I chose a window seat, seat 62K Let's take a look at the seat Right under the TV screen, there's a handy storage shelf that can hold your phone or small personal items The table is fairly standard, and I particularly love the pop-out cup holder you can use while the table stays closed The headrest is fully adjustable It slides up and down and the sides fold inwards to support your head You'll also find power outlets located under the seat and the headphone jack is right on the armrest In the seatback pocket, you'll find the standard safety card, disposable bag, and the in-flight magazine After a smooth night takeoff with incredible views over Hong Kong, I checked out the entertainment system Headsets were provided for the flight There's a solid library of movies, TV shows, and games I also like the interactive flight map a lot Similar to Starlux, you can zoom in and click on cities to see pictures of points of interest Cathay Pacific also adds some written details for each location, which is a nice touch and a great way to get excited about your trip while in the air Even on this flight under two hours, Cathay Pacific provides meal service Today's meal was chicken, rice, and bok choy The chicken was surprisingly flavorful and delicious I also took a quick look at the bathroom It was pretty standard Please note: the faucet is manual rather than automatic And interestingly, the bathroom featured an air vent inside, which I don't see very often Before long, we were starting our descent into Taipei Here's a quick tip: if you watched my Cathay Pacific business class video, you might remember I also used Qatar Airways Avios Modern naval and aviation sensors are very often infrared, they do not see light, they see heat,  and what they display is not a photograph, it is a map of thermal contrast, rendered in black and  white, with a setting that decides whether hot appears bright or hot appears dark. A thermal camera gives you exactly that kind of image, the property being rendered is heat rather  than colour, and crucially you cannot tell by looking whether the scale has been flipped. reviews.transcript_full: Para que esta bion pueda llevarnos de San Francisco hasta Singapur,  necesita cargar una cantidad de combustible que cuesta de imaginar.  Estamos hablando de decenas de miles de litros de combustible,  solamente para hacer posible un viaje como este.  Y piensen en todo lo demás que tiene que llevar,  cientos de pasajeros, maletas, comida, agua, carga,  y aun así levantar todo ese peso y llevarlo al otro lado del planeta.  Pero lo más increíble es que detrás de un buro como esta  de muchísimas cosas que nosotros como pasajeros ni siquiera vemos.  Y hoy estoy a punto de subirme a uno.  Hola, me jende cómo están bienvenidos a mi canal para aquellos que son no por aquí.  Mi nombre es Luis, el viejero real desde reno elevada como siempre viajando por el mundo  porque si tú no viajas yo no sé realmente qué haces con tu vida.  Y en el día de hoy voy a realizar la aventura más extrema que ha realizado hasta el momento.  Voy a estar hablando desde la ciudad de San Francisco,  Estados Unidos, Asia, Singapur.  Es un vuelo que dura aproximadamente 10 o 8 horas y 10 minutos lo voy a estar haciendo con la  rolinia Singapur, Airlines, que seguramente haces cuchado que es la mejor  rolinia del mundo en clase económica. Pero la gran pregunta es,  ¿Cómo se sobrevive 18 horas aproximadamente en un vuelo en clase económica?  Será realmente que esta rolinia ofrece la mejor clase económica del mundo?  Eso tú y yo lo vamos a comprobar en el día de hoy.  En este video les voy a enseñar todo el despegue desde las ciudades de San Francisco,  la comida, el entretenimiento y todo aquello que la rolinia provea para que el vieja se  sienta más a menú.  Así que acompañan.  Bueno, me jende ya estamos en el aeropuerto de San Francisco y vamos a comenzar por  uno de las primeras cosas que me gustó de la rolinia Singapur, Airlines,  que es el checking. El checking para este vuelo comenzó aproximadamente  cuatro horas antes de la salida y para mí,  ya eso es un punto positivo para la rolinia porque estamos hablando de un vuelo  donde viajan muchísimas personas, cada una con sus maletas,  documentos, conexiones y cuando tienes tanta gente viajando al mismo tiempo,  hacerlo con suficiente anticipación, ayuda muchísimo.  Yo, por ejemplo, llegué súper temprano pensando que quizás me deben encontrar con  tremenda fila o que iba a tener que esperar para poder entregar la maleta,  pero no fue así.  Prácticamente llegué y pude comenzar el proceso súper rápido.  Y otra cosa que tengo que reconocer es la atención del personal.  Fueron súper atentos conmigo y sobre todo rápidos,  revisaron mis documentos y hicieron todo el proceso del cheque,  recibieron mi equipaje y en ningún momento sentí que aquello  estuviera desorganizado o que estuviera demorando ineseciariamente.  Eso se agradece muchísimo porque cuando sabes que tienes por delante un viaje tan largo,  lo último que quieres es empezar la experiencia estresado desde el mostrador.  Ahora algo que también me gustó bastante es el equipaje.  El atarifa de clase económica con la que yo viaje,  tenía incluida una maleta faturada y eso para mí es súper importante mencionarlo  porque cuando uno viaja bastante desde Estados Unidos se acostumbra a ver  muchas tarifas económicas donde la maleta faturada no viene incluida y tienes que  pagarla aparte.  No estoy diciendo que absolutamente todas las arolíneas americanas funcionan igual,  porque depende de la arolínea y la ruta y la tarifa que compres,  pero es algo que vemos muchísimo hoy en día.  Aquí en mi caso ya tenía mi maleta incluida en el boleto,  así que simplemente le entregué durante el checking y listo.  En cuanto a los documentos yo hice todo este viaje utilizando mi pasaporte  americano para entrar a Singapur para una visita corta a los ciudadanos americanos  normalmente no necesitan solicitar una visa previamente,  o sea una visa de turismo,  aunque por supuesto hay que cumplir con lo demás requisitos de entrada correspondientes.  Así que presenté mi pasaporte, verificaron todo y todo el proceso fue bastante sencillo.  Y hasta este momento tengo que decir los Singapur Airlines comenzó bastante bien con  amigo, así con la maleta entregada y el boring pass en la mano ya podemos continuar,  porque todavía falta lo más importante. Continuamos.  Acaba de llegar el avión que dentro de unas horas nos va a llevar hasta Singapur.  Y mientras lo estaba grabando entrando aquí a la puerten San Francisco,  me puso a pensar en algo que normalmente uno no piensa cuando hubo un avión desde una terminal,  porque nosotros lo vemos llegar, bajar pasajeros, limpiar,  cargar las maletas y volver a salir, pero prepararon un avión para un viaje de este tamaño,  es otra historia.  Estamos hablando de un Airbus A350, una máquina diseñada especialmente para vuelos de  larga distancia y para que tengan una idea en una ruta desde San Francisco,  hasta Singapur, esta avión puede consumir alrededor de 120 mil a 125 mil litros de combustible,  unas 97 toneladas solamente en combustible, pero esto solamente es una parte del peso.  Hay que sumar el propio peso del avión, los pasajeros,  todas las maletas, la carga, el agua, las bebidas y toda la comida necesaria para mantener  a cientos de personas durante tantas horas en el aire,  con absolutamente todo preparado para salir.  Este A350 puede alcanzar un peso máximo de despegue de 280 toneladas,  es decir, unos 280 mil kilos aproximadamente y piensen el solo esto por un segundo,  280 toneladas acelerando por una pista y levantándose el suelo impulsada solamente por dos  motores, esto para mí me parece increíble de la aviación.  Faltando aproximadamente 45 minutos para la salida del vuelo,  ya empiezan a llamar a los pasajeros para abordar y aquí vamos nosotros.  Algo que me llamó la atención es que el proceso es bastante rápido,  llen esta parte prácticamente no tienes que estar sacando el pasaporte nuevamente,  porque pasamos por estas puertas automáticas con reconocimiento facial,  verifican tu identidad y seguimos directamente hacia el avión.  Y después de todo el tiempo esperando en el aeropuerto,  ya estamos finalmente caminando hacia la puerta que más yo estaba esperando para subirme a la  avión. Así que vamos avanzando por aquí y cuando estemos un poco más cerca de entrar,  les sigo contando como sigue la experiencia.  Ya estamos prácticamente entrando la avión y aquí hay un detalle que me gustó.  Justo antes de subir, tiene los audífonos para los pasajeros de clase económica,  simplemente pasas, tomas los tuyos y seguimos y ahora sí entramos oficialmente a la avión.  Desde que uno entra la primera impresión es bastante buena, nos recibe la tripulación y como pueden ver,  primero vamos pasando por la zona de business class, obviamente aquí cambia completamente la cosa,  miren el tamaño de esos asientos y el espacio que tiene cada pasajero, pero nosotros seguimos  caminando porque todavía nos queda un poco más para llegar a nuestro siento. Y aquí ya entramos  oficialmente a la clase económica que es donde vamos a viajar nosotros. A primera vista se ve  excelente, la cabina se siente amplia, todo está limpio organizado y algo que me gustó es que  ya tienen preparados en cada siento la almohada y la manta, algo que definitivamente vamos a necesitar en  un vuelo tan largo. Los asientos se ven bastante cómodos para hacer en clase económica y ahora  lo que quiero comprobar realmente es el espacio para las piernas por una cosa es verlo y la otra es  pasar tantas horas sentados aquí. Y ahora les enseño bien que tenemos y cómo es dejar aquí en  el canal. Bueno, estamos oficialmente sentados y vamos a ver qué tenemos aquí para aguantar todas  estas horas hasta Singapur. Lo primero que no es que para hacer clase económica el espacio  entre las piernas está bastante bien, puedo moverme las rodillas no me quedan pegadas a la siento  día adelante y eso es un vuelo tan largo, la verdad que se agradece muchísimo. Aquí tenemos el  bolsillo para guardar nuestras cosas, la mesita y a un lado el puerto USB tenemos conexión para los  audífonos y los controles del asiento. También tenemos un toma corriente que para mí viene genial  porque vengo grabando todo el viaje y la verdad que necesito mantener los equipos cargados. La  rolera también nos dé un almohada en cada siento, vamos a ver dentro de unas horas si es verdad que  ayuda a dormir porque todavía nos queda muchísimo camino por recorrer. El asiento además tiene  apoya cabeza ajustable que puedas acomodar a ser los lados y aquí me ven haciendo mi pequeño  rompecabezas probando una posición después otra acomodando la cabeza mirando para que lado tratando  de encontrar desde ahora cómo voy a poner 2 mil aquí tantas horas. También me gusta la cabina,  se ve bastante limpia, los asientos tienen un diseño sencillo y tenemos esta iluminación ambiental  que le da un ambiente bastante tranquilo a la bien por dentro. Así que por ahora, primera impresión,  estoy cómodo, tengo mi ventana, buen espacio, tengo donde cargar mis equipos y tengo una almohada  preparada para dormir. Ahora falta comprobar lo más importante, si después de tantas horas sentados  aquí sigo sintiendo lo mismo. Y apenas despegamos, llega uno de sus detalles bastante conocidos de  Singapore Airlines, la famosa tualla caliente. reviews.transcript_full: In 1996, a 26-year-old mechanic clocked in at EVA Air's maintenance hanger in Taipei,  Coveralls, Talk Ranch, ramp shift under the belly of a widebody.  17 years later, he sat in that same airline's chairman's seat until three older half-brothers  voted him out of the boardroom while he flew one of its widebodies to Singapore.  Six years after that, he founded a competing carrier that earned a five-star SkyTRAX rating  faster than any airline before it.  The one that fired him needed 27 years, he did it in five.  What sits between those two numbers is what happens when a mechanic learns to fly and a family  will become a business plan.  Every Asian airline startup of the past two decades chased the same segment.  Budget travelers, three abreast economy, race to the bottom on price, Air Asia X, Scoot,  Tiger Air, Vanilla Air.  The regional consensus said the same thing.  Audi launches a premium long-haul carrier from a small island economy that already supports  two established players and certainly not into the teeth of a global pandemic.  Family dynasties do not hand strategic power to fourth-born sons, and boutique brands do  not out-execute Singapore Airlines.  Starlux Airlines was formally registered on 2 May 2018 in Taipei.  Its founder was named Changkwa Way, known across the industry as KW-17 Airbus A-35-0.  Those on order in the largest single Airbus purchase in Taiwanese history, additional  orders for A-330 Nios and A-321 Nios, a market capitalization by mid-2026 of roughly $2  billion US dollars, full year 2025 revenue of $1.41 billion US dollars, and a five-star  SkyTrak's rating earned in five years flat.  But nothing about this should work.  Taiwan is an island of 23 million people already served by two long-haul carriers.  The founder's inheritance was locked in an eight-year court battle, and the airline launched  10 weeks before COVID-Global Aviation.  Industry reports have suggested Cathay Pacific has reservations regarding Starlux joining  one world.  Etihad has signed a strategic partnership and every incumbent Trans-Pacific carrier is  watching a five-year-old boutique undercut their fares by 30%.  So how does a fired chairman with no board, no alliance and no timing build the fastest  rising luxury airline in commercial aviation?  It begins with a will-read in the winter of 2016.  ChangQuo Wei was born in 1970 to the second wife of ChangYongFa, the shipping magnate  who had founded the Evergreen Group in 1968 with a single cargo vessel and turned it into  one of the largest container shipping empires on the planet.  In Taiwan's family business culture, birth order determined succession and being the  fourth-born son of a second marriage placed KW firmly outside the line to the throne.  He did not act accordingly.  In 1996, he joined EVA Air.  The airline his father had launched seven years earlier as a second act to the shipping  business.  He did not join as an executive.  He joined as a maintenance technician.  After the following two decades, he acquired commercial type ratings on the Boeing 777, the  Airbus A321, the Airbus A330, and later the A350.  He earned a United States Federal Aviation Administration aircraft maintenance certificate.  By the time he became chairman of EVA Air in 2013, at the age of 43, he had become the  first airline chairman in Taiwan's history to hold both maintenance licenses and full pilot  type ratings on multiple wide-body aircraft simultaneously.  Under his leadership, EVA Air joined Star Alliance.  He drove the airline's North American expansion.  He turned the Hello Kitty jet livery into a global marketing phenomenon that filled magazine  covers for years, and he flew EVA's own scheduled routes as line captain, sometimes unannounced.  passengers boarding wide-body flights to Los Angeles or Singapore would occasionally discover  the company chairman was at the controls.  That level of operational immersion was almost unprecedented in modern airline management,  and every one of those credentials would matter in ways that only became clear after everything  he had built was taken from him.  Chang Yong-Fah died on the 20th of January 2016.  At the age of 88, his sealed handwritten will opened days after the funeral, named Chang-Kuo  Wei, his fourth-born son from his second marriage, as Soul Air.  The estate was valued at approximately $14 billion new Taiwan dollars, or roughly $433 million  US dollars in cash, stock, and property.  The will also named him as successor to the chairmanship of the entire Evergreen group,  the shipping arm, the hotels, and EVA Air itself.  In a culture where eldest sons run family dynasties, naming a fourth-born son from a second  marriage over three older brothers was to say the least unusual.  The three older half-brothers, or from the founder's first marriage, held the majority of  Evergreen group voting shares.  They rejected the Will's terms.  On 10th March 2016, while KW was piloting an EVA Air-Wide-body flight to Singapore,  the EVA Air Board convened an extraordinary meeting in Taipei.  They voted him out as chairman.  They dissolved the Evergreen group chairmanship.  They installed a new chairman named Stephen Lin.  By the time KW's aircraft touched down at Changi, his executive career at the company his  father had built was finished.  Local media called it a palace coup.  They labeled him Prince Hamlet, a son betrayed by his own family, a named successor stripped  of his throne mid-flight.  The Shakespearean framing wrote itself, and Taiwanese media ran with it for months.  The legal battle over the Will would grind through the courts for eight years before Taiwan's  Supreme Court finally confirmed his inheritance in August 2024.  Most people in his position would have retreated to the yacht deck and the advisory board circuit.  He started ordering aircraft.  Starlux Airlines was formally registered on 2 May 2018.  The name itself is a statement, star for the father who once navigated Evergreen's  shipping fleet by reading the night sky.  Universe, for the son who chose to build his own galaxy.  The formal slogan followed a year later, born with luxury, shining like star.  Every Asian airline launched in the two decades before Starlux had chased the same market,  Air Asia X, Scoot, Tiger Air, Vanilla Air, all racing each other to the bottom of the  price curve.  KW went in the opposite direction.  Starlux would not compete on cost.  It would compete on experience.  A four cabin wide body product on every long haul jet, including first class, on routes  where competitors offered three.  The first class cabin was designed as four private suites with sliding doors, 83 inches  of seat pitch and personal wardrobes.  Business class became 26 lifelapse suites with full privacy doors.  Premium economy sat on Rekaro PL 3530 seats, the same model Emirates chose for its refurbished  A380 fleet.  Economy featured a 31-inch pitch, metal cutlery, and Michelin inspired catering.  Notice what this reveals about the strategy.  Every cabin class was overbuilt for the segment KW was competing in.  In March 2019, Starlux signed the largest single Airbus purchase agreement in Taiwanese  history.  17 A350 XWB wide bodies, later expanded with A330 Nios and A321 Nios.  BMW design works.  The studio behind Rolls Royce interiors was contracted to design the cabin aesthetic.  Ruth Jazz guitarist Peter White composed original in-flight music.  A custom cabin scent was developed by Taiwanese fragrance house P7, wood, leather, and florals.  Taiwanese designer Sean Yin created the crew uniforms.  Read that back.  This was not the specification sheet of a startup trying to win margin.  It was the specification sheet of a founder building the airline he had wanted to build  inside EVA air and had not been permitted to.  Every aesthetic decision was a personality statement.  The competitive axis Starlux was choosing was not the one anyone else was competing on.  Starlux flew its first commercial service on the 23rd of January 2020 flight JX203 from  Taipei, Tau Yuan to Macau.  The captain in the left-hand seat was KW Chang himself.  The first three routes on sale, Macau Penang and Darnang had sold out in 11 minutes when  tickets opened the previous December.  10 weeks later, the world stopped flying.  By March 2020, COVID had grounded global aviation.  Starlux suspended all operations.  When service resumed in June, only three weekly Macau flights remained on the schedule.  The airline was on paper a case study in catastrophic timing.  Aviation analysts began writing Starlux off as a casualty.  A luxury long haul startup with no loyalty program, no alliance, no historical route data,  and no revenue was launching into the worst commercial aviation quarter since the second  World War.  KW did not park the fleet.  He continued accepting aircraft deliveries.  He continued hiring.  He continued training crew.  Spare narrow body passenger aircraft were reconfigured for belly cargo missions and put  to work flying critical semiconductor shipments across the Pacific during the global supply chain  crisis of 2020 and 2021.  While Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines and every major North American carrier were  sending wide bodies to desert storage in Victorville and Alice Springs, Starlux was  quietly adding capacity to its own fleet.  The first Airbus A330 Neo arrived in February 2022.  The first A350-900 landed in Taipei in October of the same year.  KW personally piloted every delivery flight.  Including four years later, the ferry of Starlux's first A350-1000 from Toulouse to Taipei  in January 2026, a 13-hour crossing at the controls of a jet he owned.  The vindication came in April 2023 when Starlux touched down at Los Angeles International  Airport for the first time.  The long haul strategy that had been suspended within weeks of launch was finally operational.  The numerical case for Starlux by mid-2026 has become difficult to argue with.  In October 2024, the airline completed an initial public offering on the Taiwan Stock Exchange,  raising approximately $293 million USD.  KW retained roughly 27.5% of the shares.  Market capitalization by mid-2026 sits at around $2 billion.  Full year 2025 revenue reached $44 billion new Taiwan dollars.  Approximately $1.41 billion USD representing a 24% year-on-year increase.  First half 2025 net profit came in at $12 million USD for an airline barely five years into  commercial operations.  In June 2025, SkyTrak certified Starlux as a five-star airline.  The announcement was made in Paris at the World Air Line Awards.  Only 11 carriers on the planet hold the rating.  Starlux became the fastest airline in the awards history to reach it.  Five years from first commercial flight, EVA Air, the carrier that had fired KW nine  years earlier, needed 27 years to earn the same rating.  In early 2026, Starlux retained the certification for a second consecutive year, landed in the  global top five at the World's Best Airlines Awards, and picked up airline ratings.com's  seven-star plus safety accolade in the organization's first ever evaluation of the carrier.  The honest caveat though is this, net profit margins are thin, sitting near 0.6% on a trailing  12-month basis.  The debt to equity ratio is around 2.86.  Every aircraft in the fleet currently is leased rather than owned outright, reflecting  the capital cost of building a modern wide-body operation from scratch.  The model has not yet been tested through a full economic cycle without pandemic-era supply  chain tailwinds, a sustained fuel spike, a bad demand year, or any escalation in the Taiwan  straight would compress those margins fast.  But here is what the balance sheet alone does not capture.  Starlux is still in build mode.  The dedicated cargo arm has not launched.  Five A35 OF freighters are on order for AI and semiconductor freight out of Sintu.  The Europe route to Prague opens in August 2026.  Milan is expected to follow in late 2026.  Chicago, New York, Washington and Sydney are all in evaluation.  The 1.4 billion in revenue is the floor of the business, not the ceiling.  The structural advantage, Starlux holds over its competition compounds every year.  Every aircraft in the fleet is new, one of the youngest in Asia.  No mixed fleet complexity.  Newer aircrafts generally offer substantially lower fuel burn than older wide-body generations.  Singapore Airlines and Cathay Pacific spend billions annually managing wide-body fleets,  spanning multiple aircraft generations and manufacturers.  SpaceX operates three types, the A350, the A330neo and the A321neo, with an average  fleetage of under four years.  In 2025, the airline recorded an 89.3% on-time performance rate against a cancellation rate  of 0.2%.  The fair position is where the incumbents feel the pressure most directly.  Fair analysis across Trans-Pacific routes through early 2026 shows Starlux consistently  undercutting United, ANA and the North American majors by 20-30% on identical routeings.  An economy round trip from Los Angeles to Ho Chi Minh City via Taipei costs several  hundred dollars less on Starlux than on any of the traditional incumbents flying the  same journey.  That price gap is being achieved on brand new A350s, with an industry-leading premium  economy pitch, Panasonic EX3 in-flight entertainment and cabin service that the CEO of airline ratings.com  publicly called exceptional.  That combination, premium product at discount fairs, has no clean historical precedent in  Long Hall aviation.  The incumbent response tells the rest of the story, a co-chair with Alaska Airlines went  live in March 2023, a strategic co-chair with Etihad Airways followed in September 2025.  American Airlines joined the partnership network in August 2025.  Starlux formally submitted its one-world alliance application in September 2024.  The one carrier not publicly welcoming that application is Cathay Pacific, the Hong Kong  incumbent, whose Trans-Pacific network overlaps almost entirely with Starlux's own.  That opposition by itself is the clearest signal in the industry that a boutique Taipei-based  carrier is now being taken seriously by the largest premium airline in East Asia.  The cargo strategy adds a second front, the incumbents have not fully priced in.  5A35OF freighters are on order with options for 5 more, aimed directly at AI server and  semiconductor shipments out of TSMC's HCINCHU complex.  Starlux's Phoenix Root, launched in January 2026, was timed to TSMC's $165 billion  Arizona investment, the first non-stop service between Arizona and Asia by any carrier.  Prague opens on 1 August 2026, positioning Starlux across the semiconductor corridor that  now runs from SINCHU through Phoenix and Interdresden, Milan, Sydney, Auckland and additional  US East Coast gateways are all in evaluation.  And rumors out of Taipei suggest EVA Air is now planning its own SkyTrak's 5-star bid,  the demonstration effect running in real time.  The half-brothers it seems are watching.  Behind every one of these numbers is KW himself.  He still flies as a line captain on his own airline.  He still personally pilots every delivery flight from the manufacturer.  He still wears the same badge every Starlux employee wears, a small silver pin that reads,  safety is our attitude.  A 5-star SkyTrak's rating earned in 5 years, a 7-star plus safety certification granted  in the airline's first-ever audit, a top 5 global ranking.  $1.4 billion in annual revenue built from a suspended launch during a pandemic, built  by a mechanic turned captain who was voted out of his own family's airline at 35,000  feet, and proof that sometimes the most significant disruptions in aviation don't come from  the incumbents or the discounters or the sovereign wealth funds.  Sometimes they come from the fourth-born son, who was told he wasn't supposed to inherit  anything.  The question isn't whether Starlux can compete with the giants.  The question is whether the industry that dismissed a boutique carrier from a 23 million  person island is really paying attention to what happens next.  If this analysis was useful, subscribe to Plane Files for more.  The algorithms already picked the next one for you.

reviews.title: I Flew One of the World’s Smallest Airlines | Air Cambodia ATR 72-600 (Siem Reap to Saigon)

reviews.transcript_full: In today's video I'm in Siem Reap about to fly over to Saigon with Air Cambodia in their brand new ATR 72-600 I'll show you what the experience with this obscure Southeast Asian airline is like and delve a little bit into how Air Cambodia are currently stuck in a battle of geopolitics and tariffs  between two global superpowers and if you're wondering who I am, my name is Freddie and I make videos reviewing airlines and hotels as a hobby So far I've been to over 50 countries and flown over 70 airlines on my travels and all my trips are completely self-funded, unbiased and professional, or at least I like to think so so if any of that sounds interesting to you then subscribe and stick around! For now though, we need to check-in after arriving at the airport 1.5 hours before departure The queue was quite long and only for our flight as the next Air Cambodia flight was a few hours after ours also, they'd just told us the day before the flight time was being changed to two hours earlier so already off to a slightly shaky start Past security the airport is quite impressive for a city of this size It also still feels quite new having only opened in 2023 and during the 1.5 hours or so I spent here I only saw two aircraft operating, one of which was the one I was flying on so they've clearly built it for future capacity, or should I say, China have built it for future capacity because this airport and the much larger Techo Airport in the capital of Phnom Penh which opened last year were both built and financed by Chinese companies aka, the Chinese government this will become more relevant later in the video for now though, I noticed the terminal already seems to have a bit of a pigeon problem and I saw quite a few flying around like this, it was otherwise spotlessly clean despite the pigeons and very quiet though so I would say overall it's a pretty good little airport and these 8 flights were the only ones operating today They even have 2 outdoor terraces which I went out to hoping to see some planes but at the time literally the only plane at the whole airport was this private jet parked in a lonely spot out on the tarmac So without much to do I just headed to the gate, but they do have a foodhall with a Burger King if you're feeling peckish Here's our plane for today's flight, an ATR 72-600 which had been delivered to Air Cambodia just 4 months earlier and I like how the black paint around the cockpit makes it look like it's wearing sunglasses this plane incidentally is also one of my favourites to fly on It's loud and bumpy and cramped, but something about flying on a propeller plane always makes me happy After filming that little bit of the plane arriving I headed to the gate and after a very quick turnaround it was time to board... but before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight where we departed exactly on time and arrived 20 minutes early in Ho Chi Minh City's Tân Sơn Nhất Airport with a total flight time of 1h 15m  Ho Chi Minh City, aka Saigon, aka thành phố Hồ Chí Minh is the biggest city in Vietnam with over 20 million people in the metropolitan area and a focus city for Air Cambodia being the most served city outside of Cambodia in their network Vietnam Airlines actually own a minority stake in Air Cambodia and they have a codeshare agreement Now that we're onboard I can report this cabin is actually pretty nice and almost has that new plane smell Legroom is nothing special and there's this annoying strut right where your feet want to go but it's quite comfy and has everything else you'd expect from a plane seat you can even recline, which actually isn't that common on ATR 72s There's a proper old-school inflight magazine and I was surprised to learn Air Cambodia is actually a Skytrax 3 star airline I didn't know they gave ratings to airlines with barely 6 aircraft Also to clear up any confusion you might have up to this point, Air Cambodia rebranded in January 2026 so most of their planes including the one I'm on look like this But all of their new planes going forward and branding will look like this: in case you end up wanting to book and find the logo looks different... somewhat related, Air Cambodia currently have a fleet of 6 aircraft, 3 being the ATR72-600 we're on today and they're also brand new with one being delivered in May 2025 and the other two in Jan 2026 they also surprisingly for an airline of their size have 10 Boeing 737MAXs on order and a whopping 20 COMAC C909s on order and not to get too bogged down by geopolitics... which is something I often like to do  both of those orders came during the peak tariff chaos last year which makes me think Cambodia copied a lot of other countries (like Vietnam to name just one) and ordered a bunch of Boeing aircraft to strike a better tariff deal because not long after announcing this deal Cambodia's tariff rate went from one of the highest in the world at 49% to a modest 19% and it just so happens that a certain US President is a big shareholder in Boeing and always goes on about how well he wants the company to do but Cambodia still wants to deepen their relationship with China so not to be outdone they ordered twice  as many Chinese-made COMAC C909s, becoming one of the few airlines outside of China to do so but... I digress there's an inflight magazine with some travel articles and most importantly a route map which I love to see but just to note, almost all of these are Codeshare flights, Air Cambodia actually only fly  This significantly smaller network... On the seat back there's also a QR code for "SkyTV" which I assume is some sort of inflight entertainment for your phone but the link didn't work and there's very limited info online about it so I wasn't sure if it actually exists or not This Bangkok Airways plane was literally the only other airline I saw here I also released a video last week of my flight here from Bangkok with them if you're looking for another video to watch Link in the description below and now for the inflight service, literally just a cup of water Now for the loo review... it's cramped after a relatively short bus ride to the terminal it was on to the infamous Saigon passport control queue which amazingly only took 20 minutes today in the past I've queued here for over 1.5 hours so this was a welcome surprise Vietnam recently started making people fill in a digital arrival card so maybe that's actually helped speed things up and that brings me to my final review, and overall I found Air Cambodia to be a pretty decent airline Their website and overall operations are pretty barebones, but the new ATR 72 was good to fly one and they certainly have an interesting future ahead as they go from the 6 planes they currently operate  to the thirty new planes they've ordered in the last year and with the brand new airports they've built in the last few years with the help of China then who knows maybe they'll end up becoming a real player in the world of Southeast Asian Aviation for now though, I'll put them at a 5/10 on my airline tier list as they really are just a middle of the road airline but that's it for this video, like and subscribe if you enjoyed, leave a comment if any questions and if you enjoy the videos I make then you could even become a channel member no real perks but it would be much appreciated and it would help pay for future videos too thanks a lot for watching and good bye!

The triple-7s in particular have had a somewhat on-again, off-again relationship with, how  shall we say, starting the engines? I can't help but think that these 737s look like if Air China and Delta's delivery from  the 80s and 90s had a baby, a 29-year-old baby.  Air-peace has a habit of announcing expansion plans that are a bit optimistic. Air-peace  has repeatedly signaled intentions to grow long-haul operations, including routes to Europe  to Middle East and even Asia. There have been aircraft orders, partnership discussions,  and plenty of headlines. But translating those into consistent reliable service has proven  much harder.  Operationally, the airline has also faced its share of turbulence. While safety oversight  in Nigeria has improved significantly over the years, I'll give them that.  Air-peace's record has, well, let's just say, it's raised some eyebrows.  For example, last year after a runway excursion, some of the crew allegedly, allegedly, tested  positive for alcohol and a pair of Mary-Janes. Just in the past few years, they've had  burst tire incidents, loss of cabin pressure occurrences, engine failures, and to top it  all off, their CEO was arrested for fraud as well.  The aircraft was half full as we boarded since this was coming in from Legos and continuing  on to Banjul and then Ducar, or so I thought. Business class had recliners in a two by two  configuration with standard 3x3 in economy. These seeds were tight and short, but not as short  as the crew were with passengers.  As I was boarding, I helped a woman in front of me put her carry on in the overhead bin.  In my notes I wrote down, quote, lady mad at me because I helped her with her bag. Other  lady mad at the lady for being mad at me. Flight attendance mad at everyone, unquote.  It just felt like the crew wake up every day and tell themselves, today I will hold nothing  back. Quote It is distracting me from performing my official duties, to which the passenger  quite brilliantly replied, if you don't look at my phone, I promise you it won't distract  you.  I mean, I'll be very honest, I was starting to enjoy all this.  Also, there was no captain announcement at any time. That matters a bit later on. Let's  get in the air.  19 minutes after takeoff, I already had my meal. No choices today, and the breakfast looks  slightly anemic, but it actually tasted fairly good and was well seasoned. We had eggs,  potatoes, beans, and some sort of chicken sausage. 7.3 out of 10.  The same guy that was distracting the crew with his phone ended up not eating anything,  but instead put every single item from that tray, including the paper liner, either in  his pockets or in his backpack.  When the crew came to collect the garbage, that same member of crew questioned where everything  was as he handed back a completely empty tray. To which he snapped back, it is my food.  He's got a point.  I was standing around forever waiting for our inbound aircraft to land. This flight is  operated by a mix of classic 737s and ERJs. When it's in ERJ, you can track the flight.  But these old 737s, black modern ADSB transponders, and instead rely on physical ground radar.  I think I have that right, not exactly my area of expertise. So these flights simply  don't appear on apps like FlightRater24. Comforting, no?  We took off at 8.58. At 10.16, we were told we were starting our descent, and to turn  everything off and put everything away. We didn't actually start our descent though until  58 minutes later. Oh, and they also stored all of the excess beer and drinks in the overhead  bins.  I wanted to use the restroom, but with Mr. HappyPants next to me, I figured I'd just go  when we were on the ground at Banjul. Enjoy the landing.  There's probably like two of you that have caught on already, so we landed. This is not  Banjul. This is Ducca.
