reviews.transcript_full: Some business-class cabins feel closer to first-class, others barely feel worth the upgrade,  and sometimes the biggest difference isn't the seat at all.  Some airlines pour everything into fully enclosed private suites, others bet on service or on food,  dine on demand menus, champagne usually reserved for first-class.  Others focus on the ground, flagship lounges, chauffeur service, spa before you even board.  Two airlines can promise the same flatbed in a private suite and deliver totally different  experiences once privacy, sleep, food, service, and the lounge enter the picture.  This isn't a ranking of the best seat. It's a ranking of the best complete business-class  experience, hard-product, privacy, sleep, food, service, lounges, network, fleet consistency,  and value together. Let's count down the 10 airlines that get the whole experience right.  Number 10, Eddyhade Airways. Business Studios, a new A351,787 suite.  Eddyhade opens the countdown on the strength of one change. It's A351,78710 aircraft  bringing meaningfully refreshed business studio, updated wood accents, and armani kasa textiles,  paired with a genuinely impressive new flagship lounge at Abu Dhabi's Zayed International Terminal A.  The problem is consistency, step onto an older 777, and the product feels noticeably  dated by comparison, so the experience varies depending on aircraft. If you book Eddyhade,  specifically target the A351,000 or a new 78710. Anything older is a downgrade.  Air France ranks just above it. Its Michelin Chef dining program and European connectivity  simply deliver a more dependable experience route-wide. Number 9, Air France new business class suite,  with door. Air France earns its place with one of the strongest combinations of French dining,  wine, and elegant cabin design. The airline partners with Michelin Stard chefs like Anne Sophie  Pick and Regie Smartcone pours an excellent champagne list, and on the newer A35900 and retrofitted  777's, now offers a proper sliding door suite. The catch is that the door isn't fleet wide yet,  and Paris CDG's connections can eat into the experience.  Starlux ranks one spot higher for a simple reason. Hardware consistency. Every Starlux long haul  aircraft carries the same modern suite, so passengers never have to gamble on which product they'll get.  Number 8, Starlux Airlines A350 Business Class Suite  Starlux is the youngest airline here and also one of the most reliable. Nearly its entire fleet runs  the same Collins Elements suite, with a 78-inch bed, a zero-gravity recline, sliding doors,  and a genuinely distinctive Taiwanese soft product. Think premium Taiwanese inspired dining and  drinks, including specialty tea service. What it lacks is scale. The root network is still small,  and lounge access outside Taipei is limited. Emirates ranks above it for exactly that reason.  A much larger global network, complimentary chauffeur service, and the A380's on-board bar.  Social and logistical perks a young airline can't yet replicate.  Number 7, Emirates A380 Business Class and retrofitted 777.  Emirates makes the list almost entirely because of one aircraft. The A380, home to the on-board  lounge and bar that remains business class's most memorable social space.  Pair that with a deep ice entertainment library, Bulgari, amenity kits, and complimentary chauffeur  service, and the A380 experience is hard to beat. The catch is that Emirates is still mid-retrofit.  Older 777s still fly a 2-3-2 layout with a middle seat, even as the newer 121 configuration  keeps expanding across the fleet in 2026. Cathay Pacific ranks just above it, because it doesn't  carry that risk. Every long-haul seat guarantees direct aisle access, full stop.  Number 6, Cathay Pacific Aria Suite Long-haul Business Class  Cathay's case rests on Hong Kong. The pier, the wing, and business lounges are still some of  the best on earth, with T-houses, noodle bars, and premium shower suites, and the new Aria Suite  sliding door, wireless charging, 24-inch 4K screen. Is a real step forward as it rolls out across  the 777 fleet. The rollout won't finish until 2027, though, so plenty of Cathay flights still  carry the older, doerless product, and Legacy A330 regional seats offer no privacy at all.  EVA Air ranks one spot higher purely on soft product, pouring first-class level vintage  champagne, and handing out Jason Wu-designed pajamas in business class is a level of indulgence  Cathay doesn't yet match. Number 5, EVA Air Royal Laurel Class  EVA Air might be the most underrated airline in this ranking. Its Royal Laurel Class,  styled by BMW Designworks, isn't the most technically advanced seat here, but what lands in  the glass is Prestige's champagne often associated with first-class on other airlines,  although the exact label varies by route and season. Alongside pre-order Taiwanese specialties,  such as Shaolong Bao and genuinely rare designer pajamas from Jason Wu. The lounges at  Taipei, Tao Yuan, add real hot meal stations and showers, not just a buffet counter.  Unusually for this list, fleet consistency isn't really a concern. The 787 and 777 products are  close enough in quality that aircraft type barely matters, so booking here is low risk.  What holds EVA back is technology. No sliding door and an entertainment interface that feels  dated next to 4K rivals. Japan Airlines ranks just above it for exactly that reason.  JAL's newest suite adds the door, a personal wardrobe closet, and headrest integrated speakers  that EVA simply doesn't have. Number 4, Japan Airlines, JAL A 351,000 Business Class suite  JAL's new A 351,000 suite is arguably the most technologically ambitious product in business class  right now. Speakers built directly into the headrest let passengers skip headphones entirely.  A world first, and each suite comes with a 52-inch sliding door and its own wardrobe closet,  paired with excellent multi-course Japanese dining and premium bedding.  The problem is availability. This suite is currently concentrated on a handful of flagship routes  out of Hannida, New York, JFK, Dallas, Fort Worth, London, and everywhere else you're flying JAL's  considerably older Sky Suite, a real drop in both privacy and tech. ANA ranks one spot higher on a  simple physical argument, space. The room is measurably wider than JAL's newest suite,  and for passengers who prioritize personal room over gadgets, that wins.  Number 3, All Nippin Airways, ANA, The Room. ANA's The Room is by Sheer Footprint, the widest  business class seat ever built, close to 38 inches at the shoulder, more sofa than airplane seat  with a full sliding door, an electronic lock, and a large 24-inch display.  Multicorce Kyseki dining, a master sommelier socket program, and Hannida's excellent lounges  round out an experience that feels less like flying and more like a private room with wings.  The trade-off is availability and comfort details. The room only flies on a select group of  777-300 ERs, JFK, Heathrow, San Francisco, Los Angeles. While every other route, including most  of ANA's 787 fleet, flies a completely different older staggered product. The cushion is also  firm enough that some passengers add padding and cabins tend to run warm. Singapore Airlines  ranks above it, not because its seat is better, but because it's everywhere. Singapore's book-to-cook  program and famously consistent Singapore Girl Service deliver the same excellent experience  across its entire network, not just a handful of aircraft.  Number 2, Singapore Airlines Long Hall Business Class. Singapore Airlines wins on something  harder to design than a seat, total reliability. Wherever you fly Singapore, you know almost exactly  what you're getting, and it's very good. Book-to-cook lets passengers pre-order dishes like lobster  thermidor up to 24 hours out. The Singapore Girl Service standard is famously consistent,  and the seat itself is one of the widest business class seats in the sky, at up to 30 inches,  practically a couch with a view. The Silver Chris Lounge is at Chongi, round out one of the  smoothest ground experiences anywhere with complimentary Wi-Fi for business class passengers.  The compromises are real though. The current Long Hall fleet still has no sliding privacy door,  and the footwell sits at a corner angle, so sleeping flat means sleeping slightly diagonal. A  retrofit adding doors is underway, but it isn't fleet wide yet. Qatar Airways takes the top spot  for one reason above all others, completeness. Where Singapore is the most consistent airline  in the sky, Qatar is the most complete, enclosed suites, true dine-on-demand, and a lounge in Doha  with no real rival. Number 1, Qatar Airways Q-Suite. Q-Suite, next gen. Qatar Airways takes the  top spot, and it's worth saying plainly that even Qatar isn't perfect. Roughly a quarter of its  Long Hall fleet, mostly older 787-8s in regional A330s still doesn't carry Q-Suite at all,  leading to what frequent flyers call Q-Suite Roulette, an unannounced swap onto a lesser aircraft.  And the rear-facing seats take some passengers a moment to adjust to during takeoff and landing.  So why isn't ANA number 1? Why isn't Singapore number 1? ANA offers more personal space.  Singapore delivers more consistency, but neither offers what Q-Suite does, a 1-2-1 staggered layout  that alternates forward and rear-facing seats, allowing select center seats to convert into a  genuine double bed, or in certain center sections, a shared quad. Something no other business class  product in the sky can do. Every suite gets a full sliding door, dine-on-demand runs around the  clock with Candlelit Table Service, and on the new Q-Suite next-gen, the touchscreen jumps to a  21.5-inch 4K OLED display. The Al-Morjan Business Lounge is arguably one of the finest  business class lounges in the world. Full service dining, water features, spa treatments, quiet rooms.  Award availability is strong, too, through partners like British Airways Avios and American  Advantage, which makes this suite genuinely achievable and not just aspirational.  What earns Q-Suite the number 1 spot isn't perfection in any one category. It's balance.  ANA wins on space. Singapore wins on consistency. EVA wins on what's in the glass.  Emirates wins on spectacle. But across privacy, sleep, dining flexibility, and ground  experience combined, no other airline pulls every category together as completely as Qatar does,  and that's the entire premise of this ranking. If you book it, verify the Q-Suite tag specifically.  It's most reliable on the A350 fleet and mainlines 777-300ER routes through Doha.  Since equipment swaps do still happen. A few airlines narrowly missed the top 10.  Virgin Atlantic's upper class has an excellent Heathrow clubhouse, but older coffin-style seats hurt  fleet consistency. British Airways Club Suite pairs strong door-equipped hardware with a dense  transatlantic network, though service remains more variable. Turkish Airlines may offer the  best food for money in business class, courtesy of Doha and Co-dining and a legendary Istanbul lounge,  but older 777s still fly a 2-2-2 layout without guaranteed aisle access. Delta's Delta-1  suites are a genuine US highlight, backed by new JFK and LAX lounges, but older 767s still carry narrow  low-privacy seats. There's no single best business class. Only the best one for what matters most to  you. The best business class was never simply the one with the biggest seat. It's the airline that  delivers the complete experience, from booking to boarding to the lounge to the seat itself to landing.  So with all of that in mind, which airline would you put at number one?  If breaking down what actually makes a business class experience work is useful to you,  subscribing to Epic Voyage helps this channel keep making videos like this one. And if you made it  this far, a like helps too.

reviews.transcript_full: For more than half a century, the Kuala Lumpur to London route has served as Malaysia's  primary link to Europe. Once flown by the Boeing 707s, then the iconic sample 7,  later the Boeing Juppo 7, and eventually the Double Dacker Abbas A380.  Today, that responsibility belongs to the Abbas A350. A modern-tune engine aircraft operating  one of aviation's most historic Asian long haul routes. But in an era dominated by Gough  Carriors, Ultron Lovers, and fierce competition between Asian Airlines,  where exactly does Malaysia Airlines fit in? After 14 hours on board their flagship flight to  London Heathrow, is this still one of the great ways to fly between Europe and Southeast Asia?  To understand this flight, you first need to understand what this route means to Malaysia Airlines.  The British colonial era of Malaysia meant that there is a continuation of strong diplomatic  educational and business relationships between the two countries, ensuring the months stay strong  despite the independence of Malaysia from Britain in 1963. On top of London, the airline  at one point flew to Paris, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Zurich, Rome, and even Istanbul. But after years  of unfortunate tragedies and events, financial hardships, pricing competition from Gough Carriors,  and changing travel patterns, London became one of the last standing European routes on its network.  Since its founding in 1974, it has never once cut this route, not even during the COVID-19 pandemic.  That means this flight is not just another long haul service, it's effectively Malaysia  Airlines' European flagship service, and in many ways, it carries the identity of the airline  itself on the world stage. And it's safe to say that it Airbus AG50 might be the key to the survival  of this route, more about it later in the video. Our journey actually starts early in the day,  on board MP608 from Singapore. For a 40 minute flight, it's nice to say that they still provide  peanuts, a pack of cookies, and a water bottle for such a short flight. Even Singapore Airlines don't  do the nowadays. We soon docked our call on board international airport, Malaysia Airlines' primary  hub. Even today, KRI still feels heavily designed around the airline, dedicated premium lounge spaces,  and a terminal layer designed for efficient transfers. Built during Malaysia Airlines by  gone global expansion years in the 1990s, there's even a reserve plot of land for our second satellite  terminal, which still sits vacant to this day. Alright, let's make our way to gate C14 at the  satellite terminal, where tonight's aircraft awaits us. Pocked outside is 9 on Mike, Mike Alpha Golf,  a 7.9 year old Airbus AG50 wearing Malaysia Airlines stunning Nagaraguliri. Earlier,  I mentioned why this plane is a crucial factor on why this route survived, so why is it? Before  the AG50, the airline operated the Double Decker Airbus AG80 twice a day on this route,  with a whopping 66 business class and 8 first class seats, along with 412 economy seats. That's  a lot of seats to sell. The idea was simple, flying the premium heavy Airbus AG80 on its  most prestigious route, with three flights from Australia and Southeast Asia helping to fill out  the rest of the seats. But after our operation started in 2012, the airline quickly realized that  it wasn't as easy as a first scene. First of all, the airline needed the AG80 to have consistently  high load factors to break even. Up to 200 tons of fuel buns, a whopping 20 cabin crews,  an aluminum or 4 pilots are needed for a callable to landed flight. And those are very high fixed  costs that Malaysia Airlines need to cover for every single landed H8D flight. Not to mention  the maintenance of these jets. Due to the small fleet, the airline isn't able to take advantage  of the economy's off-scale airlines' half when they operate a large fleet of planes. It's no  problem if the airline is able to consistently fill up planes with high-using passengers in premium  cabins. Just ask Emeralds or Singapore Airlines. But unlike them, Malaysia Airlines doesn't have  a big network to feed onto the twice daily Airbus H8D flights. Which brings us to problem number 2.  Malaysia Airlines could only attract a limited number of high-using passengers at their current state.  This point will be very important later to explain how the H50 saved this route, more  about it in a bit. With the growth of the middle eastern airlines, passengers that will usually fly  Malaysia Airlines shifted their business to Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Etihad, due to the  halo effect of luxury, these airlines project onto their passengers. First class with showers,  business class with an onboard bar, it's clear which airlines' passengers will prefer. And it's  hard for Malaysia Airlines to compete for the deep pocketed passengers that shuttle between Australia  and the UK, or even passengers from their hub in callable itself. Even in the economy,  the airline has to heavily discount flight tickets in order to attempt filling up the 412 economy seats.  And cheap tickets definitely do not help too much in covering the cost of flying the H8D.  The situation was dire, even their most passengers route couldn't make money,  so something had to be done to save the route. So in 2018, after just six years of operations,  Malaysia Airlines decided to cut their losses and remove the H8D from the route,  and the plane that replaced them would be the Airbus H50 they were flying today.  You definitely have heard many times about the efficiency, range, payload capabilities,  and fuel savings of the Airbus H50, so I wouldn't elaborate too much. But to sum up,  the H50 birds a lot less fuel and flies further than other twin engine airliners on long-haul flights,  not to mention the Quadjet H8D. Therefore, solving the first problem,  by helping to lower part of the operating cost of long-haul flights like London.  But what is not mentioned is how the H50 improves the use of the London flights  drastically when compared to the H8D. Remember how I talked about how Malaysia Airlines is only  able to attract a limited number of high-earning passengers, so instead of flying a big plane  with many cheap seats to fill, how about flying a smaller plane that consumes half the fuel needed  and has half the number of seats to fill, and tap more into their strengths.  Which is the flexibility of the twice daily non-stop flights between KL and London  that business and time-sensitive travellers value, and therefore will be willing to pay more  for a premium seat on board. They also took this opportunity to upgrade the hard-and-soft product on  a combination of these strategies, allowing the charged higher prices while having an easier time  filling up the plane. The one major plus to not forget, the free Wi-Fi. For a near 13 hour  journey to Europe, having a complimentary internet access is a huge bonus. It's definitely not  the fastest connection on there, but it's more than sufficient for texting, browsing, and even sending  photos during the flight. And hour after takeoff, the chemical  emerge from the galley with their service cards, signaling the start of the first new service.  But before we begin, did you know Malaysia Airlines allows economy passengers to pre-order  meals on selected long haul routes? Similar in concept, the Singapore Airlines book the cook,  passengers get choose from the wider range of meals via the Malaysia Airlines website before the  departure. For tonight, I pre-selected the beach goulash, and I must say this was definitely one of  the best economy class meals I've ever had. The match potatoes would creamy and smooth,  whether beef itself was juicy, tender, and packed with flavour. Even the side salad was fresh and  enjoyable. With the meal service complete, the crew dimmed the  cabin lights, and that meant one thing, time to get as much sleep as possible for this 13 hour  bearer, don't like to land it.  Imagine the future for an airline that already flies more passengers than any other airline from  Southeast Asia, with the largest fleet of aircraft flying to five continents.  Imagine flying Malaysia Airlines.  Well, it has been a couple of hours and I'm back awake. At the rear galley, the crew had  prepared chicken-brought to eat sandwiches, featuring chicken coated in a Malay-style coconut gravy,  stuffed in bread. Alongside these were crackers with orange juice, apple juice, and water available  The sandwich was surprisingly solid for an in-between snack, and the crew were  proactively handing these out together with drinks throughout the flight. The services where  Malaysia Airlines definitely still stands out, even after multiple restructuring and difficult  years for the airline, the hospitality culture still remains, and as well as the reasons people  continue flying Malaysia Airlines despite fierce competition. Around three hours before arrival  into London, the cabin lights came back on, signaling the second meal service of the flight,  and did not pre-select any meals for this service, going for the onboard offerings instead.  For breakfast, I decided to go with the Asian option, which is a lasian lemak with chicken randang dish.  That lasian lemak was… hmm, lemak. Welcome to London Heathrow, where we arrived nearly an hour ahead of schedule at 4.59 AM  Making us one of the first arrivals of the morning. Considering I only paid $390  Singapore one way, from Singapore to London via Colombo, this was an absolute steal and worth  every penny. Yes, there are imperfections with the onboard product, namely the slightly outdated  heart product in the premium cabin and the lack of economy amenities. But overall,  Malaysia Airlines still offers a very solid experience with comfortable economy seats,  free Wi-Fi, excellent catering and proactive friendly crew. It is an ally I would happily recommend  to anyone looking for value between Southeast Asia and Europe. And with the new cabins now being  introduced on the H-13 year fleet, the future of Malaysia Airlines long haul product looks promising.  Even though the current H-50 fleet has yet to be retrofitted, it remains a very  respectable aircraft to fly on today. Malaysia Airlines today is very different from the  airline in once-was. It's definitely smaller, more cautious and more regionally focused.  But on the Colombo to London route, you still can see glimpses of the airline's golden era. reviews.transcript_full: Hey everyone, Owen here again after an incredible trip to Bangkok. My journey home isn't over yet. From Thailand, I made a quick connection here at Hong Kong where I'll be boarding Cathay Pacific flight 903 to Manila in regional business class on their Boeing 777-300. Although this is only a short regional flight, Cathay Pacific has built a reputation for delivering one of the best premium experiences in Asia. Let's see if they can impress me once again. >> [snorts] >> Since I had a little time before my connecting flight, I decided to explore the airport using the airport's automated people mover. I headed toward the East Hall where you'll find one of my favorite spot inside the terminal. It's the Sky Garden. And even during the busy Christmas travel season, the airport felt remarkably organized. chapters.title: Half a million passengers a day
How American became the world's largest airline
Where American's numbers stop looking impressive
What Qatar, Singapore and JAL do differently
Two airlines running completely different businesses
Why the same problems keep happening
Biggest was never the same project as best

reviews.transcript_full: Every single day, nearly half a million people board an American Airlines flight.  It operates more aircraft than any airline on the planet.  More destinations than almost any competitor. More passengers than almost anyone else in the sky.  So why? After 100 years in business, has American airlines never once been ranked among the world's  best airlines? That contradiction is the whole story. This is how the biggest airline in the world  became one of the lowest ranked, and whether the century-old giant behind it can actually change that.  To understand the size, you have to go back to where it started. American airlines began in 1926  as a scattered patchwork of nearly 80 small aviation companies unified under a single name in 1934.  In its earliest years, the airline partnered directly with Douglas Aircraft to help develop the DC  III, the plane widely credited as the first to prove that flying passengers could actually be  profitable without government mail subsidies propping it up. That partnership put American  at the literal foundation of commercial aviation as an industry. The single biggest leap forward  came in December 2013 when American merged with US Airways in an $11 billion deal,  emerging directly out of American's own bankruptcy. That merger created overnight what was  officially the largest airline in the world. In 2026, the airline marked its 100th anniversary  carrying the youngest fleet among America's legacy carriers by aircraft count, and simultaneously  the largest fleet of any airline on earth. That's the Empire. Now here's the part that Empire couldn't  buy. Imagine asking more than 21 million passengers from over 100 different countries to rate every  single part of their flight, check in, boarding, the seat, the meal, the crew, baggage claim, and  everything in between. That's what SkyTRAX does every year, and its results are treated as the  closest thing the aviation industry has to an Oscar. In 2025, Qatar Airways won it for the ninth  time. Singapore Airlines finished second. Cathay Pacific took third. SkyTRAX's own CEO,  Edward Plasted, explained why the same names keep winning, saying, quote,  as is indicated by so many former winning airlines being present, quality consistency is clearly  well recognized by customers when they vote for these airlines. Consistency, not size,  not fleet count, not route maps. Consistency measured flight after flight by the people actually  sitting in the seats. Here's where Americans numbers stop looking impressive. In SkyTRAX's  full 2025 top 10, every single carrier is based in Asia, the Middle East, or Europe.  Not one American airline appears anywhere in the top 20. Delta comes closest at number 22,  United Lands at 51. American isn't near either of them. Zoom in past the global stage to Americans  own backyard, and it gets worse, not better. The airline quality rating, an independent academic  ranking that's tracked US carriers for decades places American dead last 10 out of 10 major US  airlines in its most recent assessment. The report is specific about why, citing, quote,  the highest consumer complaint rate in the rated group above average baggage mishandling and  below average on-time performance. Every month thousands of passengers file complaints with the  US Department of Transportation. In May 2026, no airline received more of them than American,  1,181 cases in a single month, more than United's and Delta's combined totals for that same period.  JD Powers 2026 Satisfaction Study scored Americans economy cabin at 624 out of 1000,  just under the industry average of 627, a narrow gap on its own, but it's the same story  showing up again in report after report from completely different organizations measuring  completely different things. American also mishandled roughly 0.66 checked bags for every 100  passengers in 2025. The second worst rate of any major US network, trailing only United.  So what does Qatar Airways actually do differently? Its Q-SWITE business class became the industry  benchmark almost the moment it launched, fully enclosed suites, configurable layouts that let  traveling companions merge their space into a shared area mid-flight. Singapore Airlines built  its entire reputation around cabin crew consistency, a factor Sky Tracks explicitly credits it for,  year after year, regardless of aircraft or route. Japan Airlines and ANA, both finishing in the  2025 top 6, are praised repeatedly for operational precision, the kind of on-time reliability that makes  a flight forgettable in the best possible way. Compare that against Americans' own independent  reviews. A 2026 aviation quality analysis described the airline bluntly, calling it a carrier  with quote, genuine strengths and persistent structural weaknesses, and noting that gate agents  had been documented as quote, misleading during delays. Part of this gap isn't just execution,  it's the business itself. Qatar, Singapore, and Emirates are built almost entirely around long  haul international premium travel, backed in some cases by government investment and marketed  explicitly around luxury. American runs a completely different machine, built around domestic  connections, thousands of daily short haul flights, and high-frequency business travel through  massive hub airports. Those are different products solving different problems, and comparing them  head on isn't always fair. But it also doesn't fully explain the gap, because Americans' own hub  structure is where a lot of its specific problems actually start.  American's own second quarter 2025 financial filing revealed a striking number,  a 36% year-over-year increase in disruptive operational events, driven specifically by storm  activity concentrated at its own hubs in Dallas-Fort Worth, Chicago, Washington, D.C., and the Northeast.  Dallas-Fort Worth alone runs more daily departures than any single airport for any airline on the planet,  meaning a single storm cell over Texas can ripple through the airlines' entire national schedule  within hours. That's the trade-off of scale. A bigger network means more places weather, congestion,  and mechanical issues can start a chain reaction, and fewer places to absorb the shock quietly.  American has acknowledged this directly, restructuring hub schedules specifically to reduce overly  dense arrival and departure windows, and rolling out AI-based predictive maintenance meant to catch  mechanical issues before they ground an aircraft entirely.  June 2026 turned that vulnerability into a live case study. A weather system hit multiple major hubs  at once. FAA ground restrictions followed almost immediately. Flights began stacking up on runways  and at gates across the network. Crews started timing out under federal duty limits,  unable to legally fly another leg, even as replacement aircraft sat waiting. Passengers were stranded  for hours and terminals with no clear timeline home. By the end of the day, Delta had recorded  the most cancellations of any airline caught in the disruption. American had recorded the most  delays overall. Financial coverage of the event noted that airlines stocks themselves rarely  move much after a single bad operational day, but the real cost sits elsewhere. In compensation  payouts, customer service strain, and the quiet erosion of trust that shapes which airline  a traveler books next time, especially during the industry's most profitable summer months.  Here's the part most critics skip past entirely. American Airlines has one of the strongest  loyalty programs in the industry. The points guys 2026 airline awards found American narrowly  beat United for the year's best US airline loyalty program driven by a-advantage miles ranking  among the most valuable frequent flyer currencies anywhere in the business. Its admiral's club  network led every domestic competitor in lounge rankings for 2026 ahead of both Delta's Skyclubs  and United's clubs. Its in-flight entertainment library was separately rated the best of any US  carrier. Add in the country's single largest domestic route network and a mileage redemption  system frequent flyers consistently rate above its direct competitors and the picture shifts.  For a specific kind of traveler, someone chasing mile value, lounge access, and route coverage over  raw on-time precision, American isn't the airline the global ranking suggests. It's arguably  the best option in the country. The airline is betting heavily that it can close the gap.  Its new flagship suite business class featuring sliding privacy doors.  Wireless charging and a Shay's lounge recline position is being retrofitted across the entire  47 aircraft Boeing 777-200ER fleet and rolled out on newly delivered Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners.  The Airbus A321XLR, a narrow body capable of true long haul flying,  is bringing that same lifelad flagship suite experience to routes that could never justify  a wide body before. 20 enclosed suites on an aircraft small enough to serve thinner, high-yield  markets directly. American issued a formal request for proposals to both Boeing and Airbus in June  2026 to replace its aging 777-200ER fleet entirely, a wide body decision that will shape its  international network for the next two decades. Free Starlink satellite Wi-Fi is rolling out across  more than 500 narrow body aircraft starting in early 2027. Even the regional fleet,  long the weakest link in the American experience is being retrofitted with what the airline calls  mainline comfort, new business class seating, and upgraded connectivity on smaller jets that  previously felt like a downgrade the moment you boarded. Financial analysts have started calling  2026 American Centennial Pivot, a deliberate shift from chasing volume to chasing premium revenue,  time to land on the airline's 100th birthday. American Airlines didn't become the world's  largest airline by accident. It built an empire, piece by piece, merger by merger, hub by hub,  over a hundred years. But building the biggest airline in the world was never the same project as  building the best one, and the numbers, ranking after ranking, complaint after complaint,  have made that difference impossible to ignore. As passengers keep getting more demanding,  and as competitors keep getting more consistent, that gap is the one thing American can no longer  afford to treat as a footnote to its own size.

reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm finally ticking off two things from my aviation bucket list. I'm flying Austrian Airlines's very first scheduled flight from Vienna, Austria to Bond Delgada, Portugal and the beautiful islands of the Assaurus. I've always wanted to visit this incredible destination and I've also always wanted to experience an inaugural flight. When Austrian announced this new route, it felt like the perfect opportunity to take both off my list at once. Today's flight is operated by Austrian Airlines on board an Airbus A320 Neo. With a flight time of around 5 hours and a distance of 3,770 km, this is one of Austrian's longest narrow body routes and certainly one of the most interesting ones. Our route today takes us west across Austria, southern Germany, and Switzerland before continuing over France, Spain, and Portugal and finally across the Atlantic Ocean towards the Aource. Since this flight departs early in the morning, I decided to spend the night at an airport hotel located just across the street from Vienna airport, which makes getting to the terminal incredibly convenient. One thing I really like about Vienna airport is how efficiently everything usually works from baggage drop off to security. I've rarely experienced long waiting times here. As a business class passenger or Star Alliance Gold member, you can simply drop off your baggage at a dedicated check-in counters. Economy class passengers can also use the self-service kiosks and print their baggage tags before heading to the baggage drop. Security at Vienna airport has recently been upgraded with new scanners, meaning you no longer have to remove liquids or electronics from your hand luggage. You're even allowed to bring drinking bottles again with a combined liquid volume of up to 2 L in your carry-on baggage. While making my way towards the gate, I noticed that the airport was very busy today, most likely because the European summer holiday season just had begun. Our flight today departs from gate F5. Since this is Austrian Airlines's inaugural flight to the Azour, there are a few small celebrations before boarding. Passengers could have commemorative photos taken with their own phones while the ground staff also took Polaroid pictures that everyone could keep as a souvenir. It was a nice little touch that immediately made the flight feel a bit more special. Boarding followed the usual Lufansa group priority system starting with home circle members and passengers requiring assistance followed by business class and star alliance gold members before econass passengers were invited to board. >> While boarding every passenger received a commemorative inaugural flight card together with an Austrian Airlines luggage tag. Another nice souvenir from today's flight. Since the aircraft was parked on a remote stand, we boarded one of the airborne buses. Interestingly, this was the first time I had seen a dedicated business class section inside one of Vienna airports buses, which was a pleasant surprise. after a short drive across the apron, our aircraft finally came into view. Today's aircraft with the registration Sulo Oscar is an Airbus A320 Neo delivered new to Austrian Airlines in 2022, making it just under 4 years old. It is currently powered by Pratt and Whitney tuban engines. Although Austrian plans to gradually replace this aircraft with new leap powered A320 news over the coming years. Whenever the weather cooperates, I try remote stand boarding. It gives you a much better opportunity to admire the aircraft and capture some nice photos before stepping on board. My seat today is 1A which is usually my preferred seat whenever I fly on the Airbus A320 family. Like most European airlines, Austrians business class uses standard economycl class seats with the middle seat blocked creating additional personal space. The aircraft features modern Ricaro slimline seats. While they certainly look more modern than the seats found on Austrian's older Airbus A320 aircraft, I personally find the older seats slightly more comfortable. The new seats are firmer, which becomes more noticeable on a longer flight like this one. >> They also don't feature adjustable headrests. >> The cabin itself, however, looks great. Thanks to Airbus modern airspace cabin, you get larger overhead bins that easily accommodate roller bags standing upright as well as pleasant LED wood lighting, making the cabin feel much brighter and more spacious than the previous generation. The safety demonstration was conducted in English only, while all other announcements throughout the flight were made in German, English, and some announcements also in Portuguese. Today's inaugural flight to Pontto Deada is completely full. So, it's time to get airborne. One thing you immediately notice after takeoff is just how quiet the Airbus A320 Neo is compared to the older A320. The new engines make a noticeable difference and create a much more pleasant cabin environment, especially on longer flights. Another thing worth mentioning is that there is no Wi-Fi or in-flight entertainment available on today's flight. So if you're planning to watch a movie or series, make sure to download it before departure. Austrian and the Lufansza group have already announced that all the aircraft will gradually receive Starlink internet starting later in 2026, which will be a very welcome upgrade. As always, I prefer sitting in the first row whenever I fly on the Airbus A320 family. It offers the most leg room in the cabin, although you do have the bike head wall directly in front of you, and all your hand luggage must be stored in the overhead bins during taxi takeoff and landing. There is a USBA charging port integrated into the armrest, although unfortunately there are no power outlets available. Some of Austrian's newer A320 Neo aircraft have already been fitted with USBC ports as well. Every seat also comes with an individual reading light and personal air vent. Passengers seated outside the first row will find the USB port underneath the seat in front of them. If you're flying in one of Austrian's older Airbus A320 aircraft, however, you won't find USB charging at all. The tray table is stored inside the armrest and simply folds out when needed. It's sturdy enough for working or enjoying a meal, although it's rather small. Since we're departing in the morning, breakfast is served shortly after takeoff. Breakfast has never really been my favorite airline meal, and today's option didn't change my mind. The main course consisted of an omelette with sausages and cottage cheese, a combination that I personally didn't think worked well together. There was also fresh fruit, a small selection of cold cuts and a braid roll accompanied by tea, coffee, and a wide selection of drinks. Passengers traveling in economy class can purchase food and drinks from the onboard menu. Prices are fairly reasonable, although I certainly wouldn't call them cheap. Let's also have a quick look at the lavatory. The front lavatories normally research for business class passengers while the lavatories at the rear of the aircraft are shared with economy class. Inside you will find everything you would expect including soap, paper towels, toilet paper, toilet seat covers and even a changing table. The only thing I noticed was that the floor felt slightly sticky but apart from that everything appeared clean and wellmaintained. The real highlight of today's flight, however, was without a doubt the cabin crew. Business class passengers were personally greeted by name. And throughout the flight, the crew frequently checked whether anyone wanted another drink or anything else. At one point, we even noticed that I looked a little tired and kindly offered me a pillow without me even asking. Small gestures like that really make a difference and show how attentive the crew was throughout the flight. After around 5 hours over Europe and the Atlantic Ocean, the dream coastline of S Miguel finally appeared. The approach into Pontel Gada is absolutely beautiful and a fantastic way to begin a holiday in the Assaurus. I also had the chance to chat with several of the flight attendants and you could really tell how excited they were to be part of Austrian's very first flight to the Assaurus. They really helped make this inaugural flight feel like something special. A special mention also goes to our captain. Rather than simply making the standard announcements, he spoke enthusiastically about the source, sharing some of his personal recommendations on places to visit and restaurants to try. It was refreshing to hear a captain who clearly enjoyed flying this route and was excited to introduce passengers to the destination. Upon arrival, quite a few photographers were already waiting at the apron to capture Austrian's first ever arrival. I was secretly hoping for a traditional water cannon salute, but unfortunately some hopes have to wait for another time. After leaving the airdrop, every passenger received a small welcome kiss from the airport. The terminal itself is quite compact and within just a minute or two you are already standing in the baggage claim area. Immediately outside back at Reclaim are the desks of the various rental car companies. So collecting my rental car only took a few minutes before I was on my way towards my accommodation. Before heading off, let's have a quick look inside the welcome bag. The bag itself is quite nice and something you could easily reuse afterwards. Inside there was a delicious little cake, some tourist information, a miniature bottle of a soran pineapple liquor, and a small keychain. Quite unusually for a European medium hall flight, Austrian also handed out amenity kits on board. I'm sure these were exclusive to today's inaugural flight. The bag itself was much simpler than the ones used on Austrian's long hole flights, but inside you will find the same amenities, including socks, an eye mask, ear plugs, and a toothbrush kit. A week later, it's already time to leave the Assaurus and head back to Vienna. Honda Delgada airport is a relatively small airport, so during busy departure periods, it can get a little crowded. When I arrived, check in hadn't opened yet, so some waiting was unavoidable. Once the count was open, business class check-in was quick and efficient. There was a small queue at the security, but nothing that caused any real delays. The fast track lane was not available this time. After security, you are already inside the compact departure area. There are a few small shops and cafes, but don't expect a huge selection. One thing that's also missing is an airport launch, so business class passengers don't have lounge access before departure. Boarding started right on schedule, beginning with families traveling with young children, passengers requiring assistance, and business class passengers. One thing I really enjoyed here was boarding on foot. There are no track bridges or buses, so you simply walk across the apron to your aircraft. It's only a short walk, but it gives you fantastic views of the aircraft and the surrounding airport. Today's aircraft with the registration Sudo Lenda is another Airbus Escene delivered to Austrian Airlines in 2022. Once again, I'm seated in 1A. Luckily, the seat next to me remained empty, giving me the entire row to myself. However, there is one disadvantage to sitting in the first row. Since the tray table is stored inside the fixed armrests, they can be folded upwards. In the other rows, the movable armrest allows you to stretch out across all three seats if the row is empty, making it very comfortable for a rest. That's unfortunately not possible in row one. Shortly after boarding, refreshing tissues were handed out. >> We are now ready for takeoff. >> To depart from Potter de Gada, aircraft usually have to backtrack along the runway before turning around for takeoff. After waiting for another departing aircraft, it was finally our turn to leave their source behind. Unlike the outbound flight, today's service included lunch. Passengers could choose between a meat and vegetable strudel or a vegetarian option consisting of breaded mushrooms with cauliflower. I went with the first option and while the presentation could have been better, the important part is always the taste. And this meal was very good. I really enjoyed it and found it considerably better than the breakfast served on the outbomb flight. And Austrian's coffee didn't disappoint either. It remains one of my favorite coffees served by any European airline. Let's quickly check the lavatory here as well. Everything essential was available once again, including soap paper, towels, and toilet paper. The overall cleanliness was good, although there were a few stains on the mirror and a slightly sticky floor. Again, nothing major, but worth mentioning. Before landing, the crew handed out Austrian chocolates on both flights. The small tradition that nicely rounds off the onboard service. So, was Austrian Airlines inaugural flight to the Assaurus worth it? Without a question, the highlight of both flights was the outstanding cabin crew. They were enthusiastic, attentive, and incredibly friendly throughout the journey. Visitor's passengers were addressed by name. Drinks were proactively refilled and even small gestures like offering me a pillow without asking made an amazing experience. Combined with the enjoyable conversations I had with a few crew members, this was easily one of the best mediumhole service experience I've had. For me, the cabin crew deserves a well-earned 10 out of 10 points. The food was a bit more mixed. The breakfast on the outbound flight was acceptable, but the combination of flavors simply wasn't for me. I would give the meal a 6 out of 10. The lunch on the return flight, however, was really good and something I would happily order again. That one deserves a solid 8 out of 10. The seat is probably my biggest criticism. Like on most European airlines, business class is simply a standard economic class seat with the middle seat blocked. While the additional space certainly helps, I personally find Austrian's newer recover slimline seats a little too firm for a flight lasting around 5 hours. For shorter flights, they're fine, but on one of Austrian's longest narrow body routes, I started to notice the firmness after a while. For me, the seat gets 4.5 out of 10. Cabin cleanliness was generally good. Apart from the slightly sticky floor and a few stains inside the laboratory on the return flight, I really didn't have anything to complain about. The rest of the cabin was mostly clean and wellmaintained. So, I'll give clean a 7 out of 10. The only other real downside was the lack of onboard Wi-Fi. For a flight of around 5 hours, internet access would certainly have been appreciated. Fortunately, Austrian aircraft will gradually receive stalling internet beginning in the second half of 2026. So, this should improve considerably over the next few years. Finally, let's talk about value for money. I paid €880 for this roundtrip business class ticket. I think it represents good value considering this was Austrian's inaugural non-stop service to their source combined with launch access in Vienna, priority services, excellent cabin crew, and an overall smooth experience. I'm quite happy with what I received for the price. Would I fly this route again? Absolutely. And I also will fly this route again if Austrian keeps the service. For now, this service is only offered during the summer month. Not only because I really enjoyed the flight, but also because the Assaurus turned out to be an incredible destination that I can highly recommend visiting. If you enjoyed this video or found it helpful, I'd really appreciate if you'd left a like and subscribe. Every week I share new travel content, flight reviews, or better reviews from around the world. Thank you very much for watching and I'll see you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: What was once domestic first class on so many airlines is now becoming a standard of high-end economy seating on international flights. ANA, a world-renowned and globally recognized fullervice carrier, is typically celebrated for its service more than its product. So, it's time to see if their premium economy can maintain their reputation. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] [music] >> For your own safety, please. >> Good afternoon on board the People Mover. My name is Devin. I'm currently on my way to the departure gate for [music] an exciting time on board ANA. This train is about to leave and it will arrive at TD. >> Today we're flying from Beijing to Tokyo, Hana on a product meant for flights over 10 hours, but on a flight that lasts just 2 [music] hours and 48 minutes. The fair I booked didn't include free seat [music] selection, so I decided to wait until check-in opened. ANA doesn't sell first class or premium economy on the Beijing to Tokyo route. From what I've heard, those cabins are blocked until check-in and are first made available to ANA status holders. Business class passengers may be able to select seats in the first class cabin, while economy passengers may be able to select seats in premium economy. I don't have status with ANA, so I'm not sure when status holders can actually select those as one cabin up seats. Once check-in begins, any remaining seats become available to all passengers on a first come, first serve basis. So, if you have ANA status or you're simply fast and lucky enough, you might get to enjoy a better cabin. I wasn't fast enough this time, but I was lucky. I checked in a couple of hours after online check and opened and by then there were no window or aisle seats left. I thought why bother selecting a middle seat if it couldn't get really any worse. I arrived at the check-in counter around 3 hours before departure and asked whether there might be a window seat available that I couldn't see online. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back to Indian Nomad. Today we're flying Air France Premium Economy from Mumbai to Paris and back.  But this is more than just a flight review. We'll compare the complete airport and onboard experience,  including check-in, immigration, facilities, food and service.  So which journey comes out on top? Let's find out.  Mumbai's International Airport gets a big advantage with its city centre location.  You can easily reach the airport by Metro, taxi or bus, making it a very convenient choice  for travelers across Mumbai. Clear signage, plenty of counters and a simple premium economy setup.  The separate sky priority line makes check-in quick and efficient.  Immigration at Mumbai was smooth and well-organised with multiple counters and a fairly quick  process. Overall a hassle-free experience.  Once you clear immigration, you enter the international departure area where the airport  really comes alive. With currency exchange, a busy multi-quizine food court, plenty of seating,  bookstores, bars and duty free shopping.  Clear signage, escalators and travel-lators make navigating to the gates effortless.  Mumbai Airport feels modern and world-class, while beautifully showcasing India's rich cultural  heritage throughout the terminal.  When it's time to board, Air France makes things smoother with dedicated sky priority lanes  for business and premium economy passengers and finally it's time for take-off.  As we climb out of Mumbai, the breathtaking city skyline unfolds beneath us before we head out  over the Arabian Sea and begin our journey to Paris.  The premium economy seat is spacious and comfortable with a 19-inch width,  40-inch seat pitch, adjustable headrest, personal reading light,  USB port and dedicated power outlet. The fixed shell design allows you to recline comfortably  without compromising the space behind you and the experience comes with sky priority benefits,  upgraded dining served with real silverware and a complimentary amenity kit.  Air France also provides noise-canceling headphones in premium economy which help reduce the  cabin noise and make the long haul journey more relaxing. They're perfect for enjoying the  in-flight entertainment or simply switching off and getting some rest.  One of the useful perks in premium economy is complimentary Wi-Fi for messaging.  It's enough to stay connected during the flight, whether you want to send messages,  check in with family or keep up with important updates without needing to purchase a full internet  package. About an hour into the flight, the crew served our first meal. Since it was around 2am,  they kept it light, a sandwich and a fresh fruit salad. However, I was surprised that there was  no signature champagne or wine offered with this service, especially in premium economy.  I usually don't sleep on flights. I prefer looking out of the window and enjoying the views along  the way. If you'd like to experience the entire flight through the window, check out the link  in the description. And now, it's time to take a closer look at Air France's in-flight  entertainment. The in-flight entertainment system offers a wide selection of movies,  TV shows, music and other content, with a large, responsive touchscreen that's easy to navigate.  The noise-canceling headphones make the experience even better, while the seats USB and power  options keep your devices charged throughout the flight. Overall, there's plenty to keep you  entertained on this long haul journey. About two hours before landing in Paris, the crew served  breakfast. Unfortunately, it was quite a basic offering, and overall, I wasn't impressed with  the meals on the Mumbai to Paris sector. Even the sandwiches didn't have a non-vegetarian option.  For a premium economy experience, I expected better variety and quality, but don't go anywhere.  Watch till the end to see how the meals on the return flight compare.  After two weeks exploring France from Paris to Normandy, it's time to head back to Mumbai.  Paris, Charles de Gaulle Airport, is located outside the city, but it's well connected by public  transport and road. The terminals are organized by airline and destination, and for our Mumbai  flight, we're departing from Terminal 2E. Air France has a dedicated sky priority section for  premium economy and business passengers, giving the check-in process a more premium and hassle-free  experience. Unfortunately, the ground staff didn't allow me to record the check-in process,  so I'll take you through the rest of the journey instead.  There is a separate sky priority queue for immigration as well. However, with only a limited number  of counters operating, the process can still be quite time consuming, taking away some of the  advantage of the priority line. Once through immigration, CDG has its own metro system to help  passengers reach their gates. Along the way, you'll find plenty of duty-free stores, restaurants,  cafes and even luxury brands. There's also a museum and dedicated play areas to keep curious  little travelers entertained. At the gates, ample seating and modern amenities make waiting for  your flight comfortable and convenient.  Paris, I watched the beautiful city of love slowly fade into the distance, leaving behind memories  that will last a lifetime. And just as I settled into the journey back to Mumbai, the crew arrived  with a welcome glass of champagne. After the disappointing meal service on the outbound flight,  this was a pleasant surprise and I thoroughly enjoyed it. And now for the meal service,  and this time, Air France really stepped it up. The premium economy menu was curated by  Michelin Start, Chef Fredrick Simmoning. We had an asparagus salad with rhubarb vinegret,  followed by a choice of scallops with citrus sauce and asparagus pasta, or trophy pasta with  porcini mushrooms and hazelnuts. Common bear and a lemon tart completed the meal. This was definitely  a much more premium dining experience. The little touches made the return journey even more enjoyable.  The crew surprised us with sweets and premium wine during the flight, adding a lovely touch to  the premium economy experience. Combined with the excellent in-flight entertainment, it made the  journey back to Mumbai relaxed, enjoyable and genuinely memorable. And now it's time to reveal  my personal verdict. Remember, I'm not reviewing just the flight, I'm comparing the complete experience  from airport facilities and immigration to check in, boarding and the premium economy experience  on board. It's a really close contest because both Mumbai and Paris Charles de Gaulle are modern,  well-equipped airports, handling millions of passengers every year. But if I had to pick a winner,  my Paris to Mumbai journey takes the lead albeit marginally. The deciding factor, the noticeably  more premium meal service on board along with the champagne, wine and overall dining experience.  Thank you so much for watching. For more travel adventures, flight experiences and hotel  reviews, follow Indian nomad. And if you enjoyed this video, don't forget to subscribe. I'll see you  in the next adventure. Until then, happy travels.

reviews.transcript_full: Я уже летал по этому маршруту, и это ивя компании, тогда это был Boeing 787 Dreamliner.  А сегодня возвращаюсь до шкентна Airbus A320 Neo, но путешествуюся началось совсем не так, как я ожидал.  Из Гамбурга в Мюнхен не отрался на скоростном пользе ICE.  Он выехал точно про списанию, поэтому причин для волни не было.  Но по дороге, порист начал постепенно отставать графика.  И к моменту прибытия в Мюнхен задержка застаяла почти два часа.  Недовола лишь половины пути.  От главного вокзала мне предстояло пересесть на городскую электричку S-BAN,  который идет прямо в аэропорт.  Интересно, что станция расположена прямо под триминалом на минус первого этажа.  Поэтому после выхода из поезд до зона регистрации остается всего несколько минут из школ.  Правда, сама поездка занимает около 45 минут,  в виде аэропорт Мюнхен находит примерно 40 километров от центра города,  и в моей ситуации каждое минуту была на счету.  В итоге в аэропорте я приехал буквально в последний момент.  Вместо того, чтобы спокойность немать триминалы самолета пришлось быстро проходить в формальности и спешить к выходу на посадку.  Поэтому кадровая аэропорта сегодня будет немного меньше, чем я планировал.  Но самое интересное еще впереди.  Нажстёт обратный рейс в СБК, на Airbus A320 Neo.  Посмотрим, насколько он отличается от моего предыдущего перелета на дремлайн.  Несмотря на спешку, все формальности удалось пройти примерно за 40 минут,  но людей в аэропорту было действительно много.  Особенно запомнились большие группы туристов и страны, иго-восточно Азии.  Пожалуй, больше всего времени занял досмотр.  Сотрудники службы безопасности очень частично проверяли ручную клать,  а некоторые вещи, дополнительные, следовались с помощью специального газа-амальзатора,  который позволяет обнаружить следы взрывчатых пищаст.  Из-за этого, если вы летите международным рейсом из Мюнхена, советую приезжать в аэропорт с хорошим запасом времени.  Здесь лучше немного подождать у выхода на посадку, чем потом переживать из-за людей.  Ирония судьбы заключается в том, что как только я оказался в чистой зоне,  но табло поилу сообщения о задержке моего рейсия еще на 40 минут.  Причина, довольно лаконичная, техническая.  Честно говоря, в этот момент я даже обрадовался.  После такой гонки у меня наконец-то появилось время спокойно по снимать аэропорт,  а посмотреть здесь действительно есть на что.  Мюнхенский аэропорт один из моих любимых в Европе.  Он современный, просторный и при этом очень удобный для пассажиров.  Особенно мне нравится огромный панорамный окна с фидом наперон.  Можно часами набродать за самолетами со всего мира.  И это не удивительно.  Из аэропорта Мюнхена выполняется рейсе в 249 городов более чем 70 стран,  а каждую неделю отсюда проляются пости 3400 рейсов.  Работает аэропорт с двумя параллельными,  взлета посадочными полосами длинной по 4 километра каждое.  Такого запаса хватает даже для самых больших самолетов в мире.  Наконец, в Еввели посадку.  Кстати, приятного утилёкса информация о наш прессе в Мюнхенском аэропорту обидели сразу на трех языках  немецком английском и русском.  Учитывая количество посаживых и стран посредского пространства,  на этом направлении решения в подвелогичное.  Сегодня наш лейс выполняет 7-летний Airbus A320 Neo.  Самолет с момента выпуска завода летает в парке Узбекистрн Эйвейс  и считается одним из самых современных представителей семейства A320.  Задев салон я сразу заметил небольшой сюрприз.  На каждом кресле пассажиров ждали памятные подарочные наборы,  подготовленные в тисфинал очень гантомира по футболу,  в котором должен был состояться или на этот вечер.  Приятная мелочь, которую сразу создает хорошим настроением перед полётом.  Что касается самого салона, то есть здесь всё оказалось на достойном уровне.  Несмотря на то, что Airbus A320 значительно меньше дремлайнер,  место для ног вполне достаточно.  Шаг кресел заставляет 31 дюйн, поэтому даже на таком продолжительном рейсе сидеть был комфортно.  Еще один большой плюс, каждый кресло оборудованно индивидуальным утимедином экрана.  Перед вылитом борд проводники раздали женщинами детям, подушки и преды.  Всё-таки впереди почти шестичасовой перелёт,  и такая казалась бы небольшая деталь, делая путешествие заметно комфортнее.  Тем временем самолёт начали готовить к вылиту.  У нас одуксировали от телетрапа, один за другим запустили двигатели,  и мы отправили с которым он взлёт на посадочной пласты.  В аэропорту мюхина расстояния не маленькие,  поэтому руление занял довольно продолжительное время.  Сейчас предлагаю не надолго войти из без моих комментариев,  просто насладить 10 атмосферу из звуком двигателя Airbus от 320-го,  руление по одному из крупнейших аэропортов Европы и самим взлёта.  На мой взгляд, такие моменты лучше один раз увидеть и услышать,  чем что-либо о них рассказывать.  Разбек оказался довольно коротким и Airbus от 320-го уверенно торвался в земли.  После плавного взлёта на Dreamliner разница ощущается сразу.  Ускофизулятный самолет набирает высоту заметно энергичнее,  и эти ощущения чувствуются буквально с первых секунд.  Закном постепенно открывали живые песные резажи Баварии,  поля небольшие города и из дверистые дороги быстро оставались позади,  пока самолет набирал высоту.  Кстати, сразу после нас в небы поднялся настоящий гигант  двухполобный Airbus от 380 выполняющий рейс Дэнвер.  Этого самолету предстояло провести в воздухе почти 10 часов.  Но вернемся к нашим рейсу, по сравнению с Boeing 787 Dreamliner,  Airbus 320 ощущается совсем иначе.  Борбулентность здесь неустуется сильнее, а особенно если сетить в острову часть салонов,  где находился я.  Если вы не любите тряского время полято, рекоменду выбирать в районе Крыла.  И именно там движение самолет ощущается меньше всего.  А тем кто ценят тушину, лучше присмотреться в местах в передней части салона.  Двигатели расположены под крылом, основная дешевая вибрация распространяется назад.  Из-за этого в носовой части лететь обысь на заметно комфортнее.  Практически сразу после наборов высоты борт проводники начали раздавать пассажирам наушники.  Конечно, аудефильскую качество от не ждать не стоит, но со своей задачей они вполне исправляются.  Посмотрите фильм или послушать музыку в дороге можно без проблем.  В выбор контента в мультиведину системе оказался не самым большим, пока ли стал каталог,  решил остановиться на новом мультфильной про трех богатрии.  Все-таки одна из тех франшизна, которых вырос на целое поколение.  Но, к сожалению, после просмотра впечатления остались не днозначной.  На мой взгляд, современные части уже заметно с допает первым мультфильмом,  и дело не только в сюжете, который стал проще и менее увлекательным, но и в самонимации.  Создалось ощущение, что от тех самых богатрией, которых многие любили много лет назад,  остались разве что знакомые персонажи.  Поэтому там небольшой совет тем, кто спирается лететь этим рейсом.  Если планируйтесь смотреть фильмы в дороге, лучше заранее зарядите планшета или телефон.  Возьмите с собой хорошие наушники, есть качайте несколько фильмов или сериалов, еще то выездовый аэропорт.  Расчитывать только на встроенную мультимедину и системную самолёта, я бы все-таки не стал.  Через несколько минут началось обслуживание пассажиров с начала борпродники,  предложили напитки, выбор оказался довольно большим, соки, газированный на пидке, вода, чай, кофе,  и даже несколько видов и на.  Я как обычно не изменился и традиции выбрал тматный сок с водой.  Вместе с напитками, каждого пассажировала, сдали небольшую упаковку о разе с аэроприятной перекус перед основным блюдом.  Когда напитки были ростаны, настало время горячего питания.  И уже по упаковке было понятно, что кейтринг загружали в мюнхине.  Сразу бросились глаза, характерно немецкой педантичности, но упаковки подробно указано легенды и состав блюда.  На выбор подлагали три варианта, рыбу, курицу и логовядину, я остановился на рыбе и, честно говоря, не пожалел.  Нежная филе с картофельным пюре под сливочным соусом оказалась действительно вкусным.  Но одним горячим дело не граничивалось.  В набор также входили картофельный салат, хлебспорте сливочного масла, сырная, снае нарезка, знаменитый французский сыр Бейби-Белл,  на завершал ужин нежный лимонный шейк.  Торцы получилась очень щедры, концу ужина, я поймала себя на мысли, что кажется немного перееал.  И самое интересное в тот момент я еще не знал, что это только первый раз дачейды.  До посадки оставалось еще несколько часов, и ближе к концу полета пассажировщ стал еще один прием пищи.  Для рейса продолжительности по стишей часов это на мой взгляд большой плюс.  И еще одно подтверждение того, что узбекские авиалини по-опрежнему уделяют питанию на борту особое внимание.  Примерно через пять часов после вылета мы уже прилетали на территории Торпинистана.  До посадки в Ташкенте оставалось чуть больше часа.  В этот момент борт проводники снова начали обслуживание.  Пассажирами еще раз предложили на питке на выбор, а вместе с ним раздали по центру,  и я получил нас на веку Азана.  Сейчас я говорю, что такого плотного обеда я был еще настолько суть, что я уже не хотелось.  Но сон ведь все же взял.  Хотя для того, чтобы показать вам, чем в корме пассажиров перед посадкой.  Приятно, что даже второй прием пищи здесь не ограничивать печенье или небольшим перекосу.  Тем временем за ириминатором началось настоящие представления.  Солнце медленобус колась за горизонт, окрашивая блока взлоты и оранжевые оттенки.  Роди таких моментов я всегда стараюсь брать месту окна.  Медна фотография не способна полностью передать этот атмосферу, когда летишь на высоте 11 километров  и наблюдаешь закат буквально на доблоками.  Пожалуй, это одна из самых красивых частей любого вечернего перелета.  Иногда достаточно просто выключить фильм, убрать телефон и несколько минут молчу смотреть в окно.  Именно такие моменты завымняются намного сильнее, чем сам перелет.  Просадка получилась очень мягкая и спустя несколько секунд мы уже катились в злётно-посарочной плосе аэропорта Шкен.  До места стоянки здесь совсем недалеко, поэтому руление заняла буквально 5 минут.  Что касается самого перелета, то у нас осталось исключительно положительное впечатление.  Несмотря на то, что обратно елете уже не от просторного дремлайдера, а на аэропаса отрицнобации к нему.  Какого-то серьезного вискомфорта я не почувствовал.  Самолец современные салон ухоженные места для ног вполне достаточно даже для шести часов рейсов.  Отдельно хочется отметить работой кипажа.  Всё обслуживание прошло спокойно, профессиональные безспешки.  Питание казалось действительно достойным.  Два приёма пищи, хорошие выборно-киткет и большие порции.  Для европейских рейсов сегодня такой встретишь далеко не у каждой компании.  Если бы меня спросили, плетел бы я эти рейсы мне ещё раз, но этот цвет было бы одно значено.
