reviews.transcript_full: Imagine you're planning the trip of a lifetime. You've decided where you're going, you've picked your dates. Now, there's just one decision left to make. Which airline should you fly? If you're looking for one of the best experiences in the sky, two names almost always rise to the top. Emirates and Singapore Airlines. Both are known around the world for luxury, outstanding service, and some of the most advanced aircraft ever built. But while they may compete for the same passengers, they couldn't be more different. One has built its empire around Dubai, connecting the world through one of the busiest airports on Earth. The other has spent decades perfecting every detail of the passenger experience, earning a reputation that many airlines still try to match. Today, we're putting Emirates and Singapore Airlines head-to-head. Let's get started. Every airline's reputation begins with its fleet, and this is one of the biggest differences between Emirates and Singapore Airlines. Emirates has kept things surprisingly simple. For years, the airline has relied almost entirely on just two aircraft families, the Airbus A380 and the Boeing 777. At first, that might seem like a limitation, but in reality, it's become one of Emirates' biggest strengths. Operating fewer aircraft types makes pilot training, maintenance, and day-to-day operations far more efficient. It also creates a more familiar experience for passengers. If you've flown Emirates before, there's a good chance you'll already know what to expect on your next flight. And then, there's the Airbus A380. No airline has embraced the superjumbo quite like Emirates. With the largest Airbus A380 fleet in the world, the aircraft has become almost inseparable from the Emirates brand. Singapore Airlines has chosen a very different strategy. Rather than relying on just a couple of aircraft, it operates a much more varied fleet. Alongside the Airbus A380, you'll also find the Airbus A350, Boeing 777, Boeing 787 Dreamliner, and Boeing 737 on regional routes. This gives Singapore Airlines far greater flexibility. Smaller aircraft can be used where demand is lower, while larger aircraft operate the airline's busiest long-haul routes. Looking ahead, both airlines are investing billions in the future. Emirates is preparing for the arrival of the Boeing 777X, while introducing the Airbus A350 into its fleet. Singapore Airlines continues expanding with additional Airbus A350s and Boeing 787 Dreamliners as older aircraft are gradually retired. Neither strategy is necessarily better. Emirates focuses on simplicity and consistency. Singapore Airlines prioritizes flexibility and modernization. Having an incredible aircraft means very little if the airline can't take you where you need to go. Fortunately, that isn't a problem for either of these airlines. Emirates has built one of the largest international networks in the world. Nearly every journey passes through one place, Dubai International Airport. Dubai has become one of the world's most important connecting hubs. Singapore Airlines follows a similar model through Singapore Changi Airport. Although its network isn't quite as large as Emirates' is, it connects many of the world's major cities while serving as one of Asia's most important gateways. Singapore Airlines also operates some of the longest non-stop flights ever scheduled, including routes linking Singapore with New York. For passengers, both airlines make long-distance travel remarkably convenient. The difference simply comes down to where you're going. For some destinations, Emirates offers more options. For others, Singapore Airlines provides the more direct route. This is where the vast majority of passengers will spend their journey. And despite the premium reputations of both airlines, the competition here is surprisingly close. Both offer generous baggage allowances on many routes, complimentary meals, seatback entertainment, and friendly cabin crews. Emirates' biggest advantage is its ICE entertainment system with thousands of movies, television shows, music albums, documentaries, podcasts, and even live television on some flights. It's widely considered one of the best entertainment systems in aviation. On ultra-long-haul flights, having that much content can make a huge difference. Singapore Airlines' KrisWorld entertainment system may not offer quite as many titles, but it remains intuitive, responsive, and packed with high-quality content. Food is another area where both airlines perform exceptionally well. Meals are inspired by destinations across their networks, giving passengers a wide variety of international dishes. Where Singapore Airlines often receives praise is consistency. Whether you're flying on an Airbus A350, Airbus A380, or Boeing 777, the experience remains remarkably similar. With Emirates, your experience can sometimes vary depending on whether you're flying on the Airbus A380 or one of the Boeing 777 aircraft. Neither experience is disappointing. They simply feel a little different. For travelers choosing between the two, it really comes down to what matters most. Do you value the massive entertainment library offered by Emirates, or do you prefer the consistency that Singapore Airlines is known for? For years, premium economy was something Emirates simply didn't offer. Singapore Airlines had already established itself as one of the leaders in the cabin, while Emirates focused entirely on economy and business class. That changed in 2022. Emirates introduced an entirely new premium economy product. First on its newest Airbus A380s before gradually expanding it across more aircraft. The difference from economy is immediately noticeable. Passengers get wider seats, significantly more legroom, greater recline, larger entertainment screens, and upgraded dining. The cabin itself also feels quieter and far more spacious. Singapore Airlines has had years to refine its premium economy experience. Its seats are equally spacious, offering generous recline, adjustable leg rests, and thoughtful storage for personal items. Passengers also receive enhanced meals, priority services on many routes, and additional baggage allowances depending on the fare. Perhaps the biggest difference isn't the seat itself. It's availability. Singapore Airlines offers premium economy on a much larger portion of its long-haul fleet. With Emirates, you'll need to check carefully before booking because not every aircraft currently features the cabin. Neither airline disappoints here. Instead, the better choice often depends on which aircraft is operating your flight. Business class has become one of the biggest reasons passengers choose one airline over another. And both Emirates and Singapore Airlines offer products that consistently rank among the best in the world. Let's start with Emirates. If you're lucky enough to board one of the airline's Airbus A380s, you'll immediately notice something very few airlines offer. An onboard lounge. Located at the rear of the upper deck, it's a space where business and first-class passengers can enjoy drinks, light snacks, and stretch their legs while cruising at 37,000 ft. It's become one of Emirates' signature experiences. The seats themselves convert into fully flat beds and include direct aisle access on the Airbus A380. However, not every Emirates business class cabin is identical. Many Boeing 777 aircraft still feature a 2-3-2 seating layout. That means passengers seated by the window may need to step over another passenger to reach the aisle. While Emirates has begun refurbishing these aircraft with a much more modern cabin, it's something travelers should still pay attention to when booking. Singapore Airlines takes a different approach. Rather than offering dramatically different cabins depending on the aircraft, it focuses on consistency. Passengers can generally expect a spacious seat, direct aisle access, and plenty of privacy. The seats are among the widest in commercial aviation, and convert into fully flat beds designed for long-haul comfort. Another feature that frequently receives praise is Singapore Airlines' Book the Cook service. Instead of choosing from only the meals loaded onto the aircraft, eligible passengers can pre-order from an expanded menu before departure. For many frequent flyers, it's one of the airline's standout features. When it comes to onboard dining, both airlines deliver premium multi-course meals, quality beverages, and attentive service. The difference lies in the experience. Emirates creates a sense of luxury through features like the onboard lounge and glamorous cabin design. Singapore Airlines focuses on comfort, privacy, and delivering an experience that's remarkably consistent across its fleet. Neither approach is necessarily better. They're simply designed with different priorities in mind. So, which business class would you rather fly? If business class is impressive, first class is where both airlines showcase everything they're capable of. Emirates has built one of the most recognizable first class products in aviation. On selected Boeing 777 aircraft, passengers are welcomed into fully enclosed private suites featuring floor-to-ceiling doors, virtual windows for the middle seats, personal climate controls, and video call technology that allows passengers to request cabin crew assistance without leaving their suite. It's one of the most technologically advanced first class cabins ever introduced. Then there's the Airbus A380. Alongside spacious private suites, first class passengers also have access to one feature that's become almost legendary, the shower spa. Being able to take a shower while flying at 37,000 ft is something very few people ever experience, and it remains one of Emirates' biggest selling points. Singapore Airlines has taken a different approach. Instead of focusing on technology and unique features, it focuses on space. Its suites aboard the Airbus A380 are among the largest in commercial aviation. Each passenger gets a separate leather armchair and a full-size bed, eliminating the need to convert the seat into a bed before sleeping. For couples traveling together, the center suites can even be combined into a genuine double bed. Combined with exceptional dining and attentive service, it creates an experience that's often described as more like a luxury hotel than an airplane. Emirates impresses with innovation and unforgettable features. Singapore Airlines impresses with comfort, elegance, and space. Both represent the very best of commercial aviation. The question is, which experience would you choose? After comparing every major category, one thing becomes very clear. There isn't a simple answer. Emirates and Singapore Airlines are considered two of the world's best airlines for a reason, but they've reached that position in very different ways. Emirates has built its reputation around bold ideas, the world's largest Airbus A380 fleet, an onboard lounge, a first class shower spa, one of the biggest entertainment libraries in aviation, and a global network that connects almost every corner of the world through Dubai. Singapore Airlines has taken a different path. Rather than focusing on headline-grabbing features, it has built its reputation on consistency, attention to detail, and delivering an exceptional passenger experience across almost every aircraft in its fleet. From economy class to first class, the experience feels refined, polished, and remarkably dependable. So, which airline is actually better? The truth is, that depends entirely on what you value. If unique onboard experiences and iconic features matter most to you, you may find yourself leaning toward Emirates. If consistency, comfort, and understated luxury are your priorities, Singapore Airlines might be the better fit. And that's what makes this comparison so interesting. Neither airline is objectively better than the other. They're simply exceptional in different ways. Now, I'd like to hear from you. If someone handed you two tickets right now, one for Emirates and one for Singapore Airlines, which airline would you choose and why? Let me know in the comments below. If you enjoyed this comparison, don't forget to like the video, subscribe for more aviation content, and I'll see you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: Today, I flew on an Airbus 380 operated by Emirates, the world's premier luxury airline , for just $120 Even those with no interest in airplanes or airlines have likely heard of it at least once. Emirates is considered the undisputed best among the "oil money" Middle Eastern "Big Three " and is the world's largest operator of the A380. Emirates owns 120 of the 251 aircraft produced by Airbus, accounting for nearly half of the total. From the luxury in the skies featuring onboard showers and bars to the ultra-fast in-flight Wi-Fi "Starlink ," Emirates' A380 has a lot to show you today. Let's get started! Hello, this is Manager Woo. This is Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport. Since Bangkok is a top global travel destination, Emirates operates five flights daily; one of them is dedicated to the "Fifth Freedom" route between Bangkok and Hong Kong. EK384 and EK385 depart from Bangkok at 2:15 PM and from Hong Kong at 9:30 PM. I am off to my destination. I booked a one-way economy ticket to Hong Kong on Agoda for $120. Since the lowest fare for this route is in the 110,000 won range on Hong Kong Express, adding 50,000 won to book Emirates is by no means a bad deal. I will proceed with check-in at the S counter. Although there are self-check-in kiosks, I will check in at the counter because the line isn't long. Actually, one of the reasons I checked in at the counter was that I wanted to receive a ticket with this red logo on it. It is convenient because there is an escalator right next to the counter that goes up to the departure hall. Since I have to take a train to get to Gate S today , I will visit the lounge in the main terminal first. This is the Coral Business Lounge located near Gate D1. It has been open for about two years, so I heard the facilities are relatively clean and nice. You can enter using both a PP card and a The Lounge card. There is a shower room here, but it is not free, so if you need a shower, it might be better to go to the Miracle Lounge near Gate D5. Inside, the area is divided into a group space and individual tables. They have a good selection of drinks here, and the bar offers a variety of cocktails. I think this place would be good for people who like to drink, but the food here didn't really suit my taste. Should I say it tasted a bit like stainless steel? It had a slightly strong taste, so since I prioritize food over alcohol, I probably won't visit again. I then came to the Miracle Lounge near Gate D5. Many smokers visit here; you can grab a Zero Coke from the refrigerator right after entering and exit through the side door to smoke on the outdoor terrace. I noticed many people just come here and leave. Now, I will head to the gate. Gates starting with 'S' are located in the satellite terminal, so you have to take a train from the main terminal to get there, just like at Incheon Airport Terminal 1. This is my second time using this place; unlike the Incheon terminal, it is quite large enough to accommodate A380s, and since it hasn't been long since it opened, it is very pleasant. Today's boarding gate is S113. Since this is my first time flying on an Emirates A380, I took some photos of the plane from various angles. It has a sturdy front view with a width of 80 meters, the starboard side on the right where you can feel the height, and the port side on the left where the jet bridge connects. The jet bridge connects first to the upper deck where First and Business Class are located, and then to the main deck on the lower level where Economy is located. Two additional aircraft are being connected. With a wingspan of 36 meters alone, you can immediately feel how massive it is when standing next to a B737, which has a total width of this size. A Qatar Airways A380 had just pulled in at the opposite gate, so I went over to take a picture. Perhaps because its livery is split between gray and white, the all-white Emirates seems to look somehow larger. I have returned to the gate, and the flight attendants are giving a pre-flight briefing. This is a jumbo jet carrying over 20 crew members. Higher classes and membership tiers board first, and economy boarding begins on the lower main deck. That path on the right leads to the upper jet bridge for First and Business, while the Economy main deck is downstairs. Emirates is an airline I have a love-hate relationship with; I applied here several times when I was flying. With the resolve that "I will fly if I get accepted," I used Etihad and Qatar but never flew here, and here I am finally getting to fly it... The A380 is extraordinary starting with its door size, and heading upstairs... I’ll go past the stairs and head to my seat. This is the main deck, filled entirely with economy seats, and the seating arrangement is 3-4-3. The seats are made of fabric in bright pastel tones; to me, they reminded me a bit of the color of a Little Mermaid's fin . My seat today is 50C, an aisle seat in the very back row of the front cabin. The seat width is 18 inches, which is spacious and comfortable. The legroom is ample, even with the pockets packed full . When you recline the seat, the lower seat slides out to create a full recline, yet there is enough room for my knees not to touch the seat. The angle of the backrest is about this much, and the headrest is thick and adjustable up and down. I usually find leather headrests a bit uncomfortable, but since this is fabric, I used it comfortably . Even though it is a flight of less than three hours , headsets, cushions, and blankets are provided as standard. The cabin was so cold that I covered myself with it as soon as I boarded, and the temperature was just right. Now, an announcement is coming on saying, "We are closing the doors, so ground staff, please disembark." I will now verify the aircraft type using the safety card. The safety announcement plays along with the pushback. Over there. The male flight attendant who appeared reminded me a bit of the male lead from the Netflix series 'You.' All the flight attendants here looked like movie stars. 'I guess that's why I didn't make the cut' :(( I briefly had a metacognitive moment. Then an announcement came on saying that Starlink is available. After takeoff, I will check the Starlink speed. Power ports are located next to the monitors in each of the three window seats, excluding the aisle seat. The seat next to me was empty, so I just used it; you can consider there to be two ports for every three seats. Also, there is a USB-A charging port at every seat. Below the monitor is a remote control with a touch screen, and below that is the tray table... no, let's look at the cup holder first. The cup holder here is gimbal-style; the inner holder rotates, so they say it maintains a level position even if you recline the seat in front of you. But when I actually used it, it looked a bit scary. I'll show you later when I get my coffee. Returning to the tray table, it is semi-foldable and adjustable forward and backward. Even though it is a 13-year-old aircraft, the cabin environment and seats are generally clean. We have arrived at the runway, and we will take a look at the A380's heavy takeoff via the tail camera. Because the wings are so big, the landing gear retracting is obscured and hard to see. The overhead control panel is a bit high, so it is difficult to operate while sitting; you have to stand up to operate it, especially on the aisle side. Seat and flight information is displayed at the top of the monitor, and if you press 'I' in the bottom left, you can check the flight details and the aircraft you are currently on. Since the flight is only two hours long, I will diligently capture various things. First, if you go to the in-flight entertainment language settings, you can select from a whopping 14 languages, including Korean. This is the entertainment section, which boasts a vast amount of content that is considered the best in the world. There are sections by genre, and I will go into the latest movies to check for Korean subtitles. I checked 'Project Hale Mary,' but there are no Korean subtitles. Not all content has subtitles, and the content that does have Korean subtitles is... If you go back to the previous step and enter the Korean Movies section at the top, you will find a list. It seems they have separately categorized and stored content that offers Korean dubbing or subtitles. The headset for watching videos is good because it has cushions inside. Now, I will try connecting to Starlink. This is my first time using it, too. If you connect to Emirates Wi-Fi while in airplane mode, the window changes, and once you enter the main screen, the connection is complete. First, let's go into Netflix. I clicked on the "Manager Kim" video, and it loads almost immediately. The playback starting speed is wow... At this rate, it doesn't seem much different from doing it on the ground. Also, when I travel abroad, I usually use A.T. Baro Call; I wonder if it uses data for calls, because it connects as well. Let's check how fast Starlink speeds are at 39,000 feet. Wow , it keeps going up. Let's speed it up a bit. The download speed was 260 megabits per second, and the upload speed was 3.7 megabits per second . You can expect it to take about 30 seconds to download a 1GB video. I also tried connecting with my MacBook. I can watch live broadcasts of CNN, BBC News, and sports matches on the laptop's large screen. However... If I had to point out a downside, since it allows for work, it seems difficult to use the excuse that I can't check emails when flying on a business trip. I was sitting and replying to some emails when the meal cart arrived, so I turned it off immediately. I removed the cushion from my back, adjusted my posture, and will now reverently receive the meal. It is a flight of less than three hours, but the tray is overflowing. A flight attendant at the back even brought me a separate Zero Coke. The main course is chicken, served with cucumber salad for appetizer, blueberry chocolate cake for dessert, and bread. It comes with boiled carrots and mashed potatoes. I was a little disappointed that it wasn't rice, but everything tasted really good. The cabin is tidied up, and now I will go check the restroom. It is decorated luxiously with white and wood patterns, and the space is decent enough not to feel cramped. Even the lid has a wood pattern, and there are disposable toilet seat covers, so you can use it cleanly. Feminine toiletries are also placed under the mirror next to it, but I won't bother opening them. Above the sink, there is an air vent and a call light for the flight attendant, and the faucet below dispenses water automatically with just a touch of the temperature control, keeping it clean. It is set up so you can just wash your hands. Paper towels are right above it, making it convenient to use. Next to the sink, there is hand lotion and an Eau de Toilette spray; these are products from the Noir line by the British lifestyle brand 'The White Company'. The 500ml hand lotion was selling for 30 pounds, which is about 60,000 won in Korean currency. You can tell a lot of money was invested in various details. I came back to my seat and asked for a cup of coffee, but the flight attendant told me not to put it in the cup holder. As I showed you earlier, this holder rotates inward, right? If you insert the coffee, it adjusts the horizontal level like a gimbal, but I was a bit afraid to let go of it. So I just placed it on the table to drink . The monitor tilt works well so you can see the screen when you move over to the seat in front. With about 30 minutes left, the captain's announcement regarding the destination is coming on. The seat next to me is empty, and the legroom is spacious, so I was able to fold my legs and travel comfortably. I didn't show you the remote control; the touch sensitivity of the screen isn't exactly fast, but since I don't really need to use it much, I think it's fine. It is quite large, so when I held my iPhone up to it, [there is] a case It looks like it would be boiling if I took it off. Just like the captain's announcement, it has been raining continuously in Hong Kong , so I can see water passing outside the window. Since we are descending , the water is rising. Seeing the tail camera fog up due to the rain, I thought the rain was really intense. But then, just as the city of Hong Kong started to come into view, the rain stopped again. We are landing at Hong Kong International Airport. An announcement comes on telling us to stand up when the seatbelt lights go off, but everyone is in a hurry . We have about 500 people to disembark from this plane alone, so we really need to get going fast. Today was my first time flying on an Emirates A380, and it was also my first experience with Starlink, so I boarded with a lot of excitement. I have a lot to show you, but time is short, so the three hours seem to have passed in a rush. Actually, for the viewers to enjoy Emirates, you would need to fly Business or First Class to really appreciate it , but this is a small channel that hasn't been around for long, and it’s only fun to start from Economy and work your way up step by step, right?! However, I found Economy class to be excellent as well. I heard that they are currently upgrading the seats on all their aircraft as they add Premium Economy class . I don't know when it will happen, but for my next Emirates review, I plan to move up one class at a time on a retrofitted aircraft. I will not be entering Hong Kong; instead, I will be transferring to Incheon via Hong Kong Express. I will organize the review of the next section well and upload it as well. Thank you for watching the long video until the end.

reviews.transcript_full: I flew thin air from New York to Helsinki and the experience completely surprised me.  As I board, I passed through the business class cabin. If extra legroom is important to you, these seats can make a huge difference on the Trans  Atlantic flight.  thin air's main cabin has one of my favorite configurations.  They use a 242 seating layout on this aircraft, which means windows seat travelers only have  one neighbor instead of two.  Now that's a nice advantage over the more common 333 layout that you'll see on many other  airlines.  Okay, let's look at the entertainment screen.  Each seat comes with its own touchscreen entertainment system and the display is bright,  responsive, totally easy to navigate.  Okay, entertainment options are a plus.  There are plenty of movies and TV shows to choose from, giving you tons of entertainment  to stay busy during the entire flight.  Of course, I ended up watching a couple movies, but one of my favorite features is the  moving flight map.  I probably spend way more time there watching that than I really should.  It's a long haul flight, so meals are included.  The digital menu lets you see exactly what's being served before the meal arrives, which  is a nice touch.  Okay, one of the things that might put people off is the many opportunities to upsell you.  There are a lot of different travel extras that you can go for on this flight.  Things like alcohol and stuff, you can order them all directly right from the entertainment  system.  Okay, let's talk Wi-Fi.  Wi-Fi is available for purchase if you want to stay connected during the flight.  Although whether it's worth paying for, it totally depends on how much you need it.  There are opportunities for a complimentary internet, but those are restricted to first-class  and gold members.  Looking around the cabin, overall, it's modern, clean, and really well-maintained.  One small feature I really appreciated was the built-in phone holder.  It's simple, but surprisingly useful if you're charging your phone or washing something  on your own device.  The screen feature to USB-C port, which is becoming more and more common and makes it really  easy to keep newer devices charged throughout the flight.  The foldable tray table feels sturdy enough and gives you enough space for your meal and  a laptop if you plan on getting some worth done.  The window is a little on the small side compared to the dream line or some other aircraft,  but it still offers great views during the flight. reviews.transcript_full: Join me as I fly United Polaris from San Francisco to Taipei. At SFO, Polaris passengers do get their own dedicated check-in lane, which they share with Global Services and United 1K flyers. United also amazingly had the QR codes for the different countries arrival cards, just in case you're irresponsible like me and forgot to do it beforehand. Make sure you leave enough time for the United Polaris Lounge, which is just located to the right side of security and occupies two entire floors. And my golden rule for the first thing you should always do is check the dining room waitlist, check the shower waitlist. Once you're in the Polaris Lounge, you can enjoy a wide range of seating depending on what your social vibe is. Make sure you stop at the bar to get a drink or two or three or until you can't count anymore. The dining room has an excellent selection of food options to choose from like the ones that you see here, but if you don't have enough time or you spent too long at the bar, the buffet will do just fine. >> [music] >> And please make sure to leave time for a shower where my normal 5-minute showers turn into 30-minute therapy session. Once you get to the gate, as a Polaris passenger, you can board with group one, but if you have United's top-tier 1K or Global Services status, then you can pre-board as they call it. On board the 777-200, we have eight rows of Polaris in the forward cabin and five rows in the rear cabin. My seat is 9L, which is a bulkhead seat in the rear cabin on the right-hand side of the aircraft. In my opinion, the best seat on this aircraft. Waiting for you at your seat is, in my opinion, the best bedding in business class, an amenity kit that's really well stocked with creams and eye masks and pajamas and slippers if you move fast enough. And after getting a feel for my seat, having a little bit of pre-departure champagne, and making sure that my shoulder strap was securely fastened, off we go to Taipei. As far as Wi-Fi goes, United currently charges for Wi-Fi, but Starlink is very much on the way and should be much faster and free once it's here. Once we reach cruising altitude, service began with the hot towels followed by me changing into pajamas and then champagne [music] and warm nuts and a delicious meal consisting of smoked salmon and a very flavorful stir-fried chicken main course. [music] This main course needs to be there on every flight. And our dessert this evening was supposed to be a special 4th of July edition ice cream sundae, but with the blueberry compote missing, it was only red and white on my plate. So, apparently, we were going to be honoring Poland this evening instead of the United States. After the meal finished, I reclined my seat into flatbed mode and fell asleep while watching one of my favorite childhood movies. This is truly a bed in the sky, just with more seat belts. And after getting some quality sleep, I woke up to us flying through a thunderstorm and decided midflight snacks was a good idea. On some of their longer flights, United recently made the midflight snacks into more of a tapas [music] concept. And so, I ordered some herb ricotta, black bean and corn empanadas, and some chicken. The turbulence clearly made me hungry because all three of these were excellent. Then, 1 hour before landing, another hot towel arrived followed by breakfast, which I kept light with a cheese plate. Very restrained of me. One thing is for certain in all of this, you will not go hungry. And if you ever give yourself the chance, you can get a great sleep in as well. So, would you fly Polaris if you had the chance? Let me know in the comments. I'd love to hear your thoughts.

reviews.transcript_full: County weather for St.kah 4 New York City  County State- ville  Hello everyone and welcome back to another flight review.  In today's video I will be flying from Paris to Rally on board Air France's 835900 in  economy class.  Having just arrived in Paris from Florence I had to figure out where my gate was for the  flight to Rally.  The Air France app told me I'd have to navigate to Hall M where the airplane would be.  However the boards in person after I got into the terminal told me Hall K instead.  That being said I had to make my way to passport control in order to enter terminal 2e as  I had arrived in terminal 2f.  It's a little bit confusing as terminal 2e has 3 halls which are K, L and M and each  of the 3 can serve Air France, Delta and many other flights so it can get confusing at  times.  Thankfully Hall K is not too far from where I arrived in terminal 2f so all I had to  do was walk a little bit and then go to passport control.  However in Paris Charles de Gaulle fashion we got to the passport line and it was quite  long which I did not expect as this was during the early morning hours.  Although the process itself is incredibly simple we had to wait for almost an hour  just to get through the line and once you get up to the passport booth since we have  United States passports all they do is scan them and you're good to go which I feel is  a waste of time and they need to have something better set up to make it a lot quicker for  travelers.  Now moving on to the airport itself first is the navigation.  As long as you know where you need to be all you have to do is follow the signs to get  there and you shouldn't get lost or not know where to go.  In my case I knew that my gate was K49 so I followed all the signs to get to Hall K as  well as a specific gate K49.  In terms of the amenities the airport has to offer Charles de Gaulle usually has more  expensive and fashion oriented stores such as Gucci or Saint Laurent.  You will find these stores right before entering the main part of the terminal where the  actual gates are.  In the main part of the terminal there's limited options with a few small stores here  in there, a preta, manjeere and a few other things.  I do enjoy the fact that there's a lot of natural light inside the terminal and also that  there are huge windows where you can see all the on ground movements of aircraft.  There's plenty of seating, close bathrooms and a lot of PS5s, arcade machines and different  activities that you can do as well.  Originally the departure board showed that our gate would be K43 but soon after they  announced that our gate got switched to K49.  Thankfully it was just a short walk to the other gate, however be aware that this is a  possibility whenever you fly out of Paris Charles de Gaulle.  After an hour or two of relaxing in the terminal it was finally time to board.  It's the usual boarding process where they call out zones one by one and once you walk  through the line all you have to do is scan your boarding pass to get through.  Although this was a full flight so much so that we had to check in our carry on bags the  boarding process was very quick.  Make sure that you always have your passport in hand in the case that the gate agents want  to check it.  I noticed that in Paris a lot of the time what they'll end up doing is right when you  enter the line they'll go ahead and check your passport and boarding pass just to make  sure everything matches up and you're good to go.  Now for this flight I was seat 43L which is a window seat on the right side of the airplane.  Before I get into the seat details and further flight details it's time to depart.  To jump right in this economy seat has a width of 17.5 inches.  It's a comfortable width for me and the padding on the seat is more than enough.  The seat was quite comfortable and the headrest was in a nice position.  I am 6 foot and 3 inches tall which is around 190.5 centimeters and despite this there  was still about a fingers width of legroom remaining and I say despite because I'm usually  used to my knees banging on the seat in front of me on other airlines.  However in this case especially if I put my legs out it was quite bearable.  There's a normal nice and big seat pocket with other mini pockets on the front of it.  And within said pockets is a safety card and a waist bag.  The tray table is a pretty decent size and slides out quite far.  Additionally when the tray table is stowed there's a little drink holder that you can pull  down.  At the very top of the IFE there's a clothing hanger and at the very bottom there's a  USB port and headphone jack.  The last detail about the seat is the recline which is about 118 degrees.  This is a fairly decent amount of recline and it felt very relaxing.  Shortly after takeoff we were given a refreshing wet towel which is something that Air France  usually does on their long haul flights.  As for the provided pillow and blanket they were both very comfortable however I wish  the blanket was just a little bit bigger.  Before I get into the meal that this flight had to offer let's take a look at the IFE.  This IFE system is a 13.3 inch 4K ultra high definition touchscreen.  And as you can see whilst I scroll on the screen there are plenty of options to choose from.  There's a massive amount of movies with different genres to explore.  In fact the IFE is very up to date as Project Hail Mary and Michael are both found within  it.  To give context those two movies came out just three months prior to the recording  of this flight review.  There was a very little amount of TV shows as most of them were French.  Other pages on the IFE included Canal Plus, Apple TV, audio games wellness and the Air France channel.  Under the audio section there's numerous podcasts, albums, playlists, radio stations  and more that you can tune into.  The game tab contains the usuals like trivia and sudoku.  However there are also other very well known games such as Uno and Monopoly which I've  never seen on any other flight before.  The flight map operates very smoothly and includes all the details you need to know for  your trip.  There's also many different views that you can choose from.  However my personal favorite option is the tail view camera.  There's also a forward view camera and these camera options are only available if you're  flying on an A350 or A380 and in this case it's an A350.  The last detail is the Wi-Fi.  Air France has two options you can choose from, either Air France Wi-Fi or Air France Connect.  It doesn't really matter which one you choose but for this flight it just wouldn't work  on my phone.  But fortunately it was able to work on another phone so it might have just been an issue  with mine.  It's extremely fast and sometimes even makes you forget your 40,000 feet in the air.  But now almost an hour into the flight it's time for lunch.  The two meal options included chicken with mashed potatoes or a pasta.  I chose the chicken with mashed potatoes which also came with little crackers called  folletes, a unique salad, a roll of bread, a mini raspberry cake, butter and cheese, as  well as a bottle of water and drink of your choice.  I always tend to enjoy meals on Air France and this one definitely stood by that.  Despite the fact that our taste buds are not as effective when you're 30,000 feet  in the air, everything was so flavorful about the meal.  I really don't have any complaints, it was great but I will say I do think I've had  this meal before on another Air France flight that I took.  Not to say that it wasn't good that time but I just like a little more variation.  Now as we continued our trek westward across the Atlantic I decided to do a bathroom review.  This bathroom was in the very back of the aircraft so I expected it to be quite small.  I'm used to having the ceiling of bathrooms almost touch my head due to my height but in  this case it wasn't anywhere close.  The bathroom was very clean, smelled good and included everything you might need from  a baby changing station to two clothing hangers.  I didn't get a chance to check out the bathrooms that are over the wings however I'm sure  there would be more spacious than this one was and I think that goes to show the amazing  quality of these economy bathrooms.  With an hour and 47 minutes remaining the cabin lights became very warm and they served  us some snack baskets.  This included a mini pound cake, cucumber sandwich, yogurt drink and again a drink of your  choice.  In my case I got hot chocolate, again no complaints about this snack basket and it was  just enough to fill me up before landing.  Speaking of which, that's about everything to go through about the inflight details so  now it's time to descend inland into Raleigh.  Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Raleigh.  What is around international importance?  It is 4-14pm local time.  A rival is 18 in 10-0-2.  We would like to offer our sincere apologies for our delayed arrival with a proof of  length, with a false silly issue, pleasant data and so on.  I'm very excited to have a fight.  As you may have heard, our flight did end up landing around 20 minutes behind schedule.  The reasoning for this was the sequencing back in Paris.  We had to wait quite a while to be able to push back and then we had to wait in a long  line of aircraft to be able to take off.  Additionally, after landing, a Copa Airlines 737 max was delayed due to weather so we had  to wait for them to push back from the gate before we could park into our gate.  That itself took around 10-15 minutes to wait for.  Once we parked at the gate, it didn't take too long to be able to debord.  Since we were near the very back of the plane, it wasn't surprising that it took us a little  bit to get out, but it was still a pretty quick process.  All international flights for Raleigh Durham go through terminal 2.  Since we arrived into a dedicated international gate in terminal 2, all you had to do was  take an escalator up to the second floor to head towards passport control.  Once you do that, you need to join whatever line applies to you.  One of the lines is for US citizens in permanent residence, and the other line is for anyone  who doesn't fall under those two categories.  In past years arriving into RDO internationally, the customs process took a very long time.  They would only have two boots open and they'd have to filter through everybody.  However I was pleased to see that they now have a new, quick and easy system.  Unless you are traveling with a baby, all you have to do is get your face scanned and  it'll tell you if you're good to go or not.  After that's done, you head down the escalator to the baggage claim.  Once you grab your bags, you're free to exit right into the Carpool area.  Overall I thought this was a very pleasant flight and definitely up there for one of the  best economy seats I've sat in.  If you want to see more little details about this flight review, check out the description  below.  Thank you all for watching, I hope you enjoyed.  If you haven't already, please hit the like and subscribe button and I'll see you in  the next one.  Bye bye.

reviews.title: Emirates First Class Review | The Ultimate A380 Experience

reviews.transcript_full: Today, we are flying one of the most unique first class routes. Emirates famous freedom flight from Sydney, Australia to Christchurch, New Zealand. In this review, we'll take you inside both the Qantas first class lounge and the Emirates lounge at Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport before stepping on board the iconic Emirates [music] Airbus A380. We'll show you the private suites, the shower spa, the famous on board lounge bar, the dining experience, and everything else that makes Emirates first class one of the most talked about products in commercial aviation. So, come along and experience the journey with us. Let's begin with bag drop. Our check-in is quick and efficient, exactly what you'd expect when traveling first class. Within minutes, our bags are tagged through to Christchurch and we're on our way. Next, we head through security and immigration. Once airside, we take a leisurely walk through Sydney Airport's duty-free precinct before making our way up the escalator to the Qantas first lounge. >> [music] >> As the glass doors open, we're immediately welcomed by the lounge's stunning living green wall, one of the signature design feature, and a beautiful introduction to the experience ahead. >> [music] >> At the top of the escalators sits the classic split flat departures board. It may be old-fashioned, but it brings a timeless charm that reminds you of the golden age of air travel. Looking around, it's easy to see why this is considered one of the finest airline lounges in Australia. [music] Polished marble covers the floors, walls, and bar while floor-to-ceiling windows provide sweeping views across the tarmac [music] where aircraft come and go throughout the day. The open kitchen and marble bar become the centerpiece of the lounge. Fresh coffee made to order, premium teas are available throughout the day, and guests can enjoy champagne, wines, cocktails, and spirits before boarding. One of the best seats in the lounge [music] is right at the bar where you can watch the chefs preparing meals in the open kitchen. The lounge offers plenty of comfortable seating from oversized armchairs perfect for relaxing to full dining tables where guests can enjoy restaurant-quality meals. For travelers needing to work before departure, there is a dedicated business center complete with desks, seating, and printers. Throughout the lounge, you'll also find several self-serve beverage stations making it easy to grab a drink whenever you like. The restrooms continue the same premium design with marble finishes, spacious layouts, and quality amenities all kept immaculately clean. Tucked behind another set of glass doors is the Qantas Spa where eligible first class guests can enjoy a complimentary treatment before they fly. It's one of those little touches that transforms airport waiting time into part of the luxury experience. For breakfast, we decide to make the most of the lounges renowned dining. Today's selection includes a refreshing berry juice, the signature breakfast, fluffy pancakes, a fresh bowl of fruit, and perfectly brewed coffee. The presentation is excellent and it's a wonderful way to begin the journey. With breakfast finished, it's time to compare another premium lounge. We leave the Qantas First Class Lounge, wander through the terminal, and make our way towards the Emirates Lounge. >> [music] >> Walking inside, the atmosphere immediately changes. Behind reception sits an impressive scale model of the Emirates Airbus A380. Warm timber finishes, rich brown tones, and [music] elegant furnishings create the classic Emirates look that's instantly recognizable. >> [music] >> It's an eye-catching display that we'd happily find room for it at home. Compared with the Qantas First Class Lounge, the Emirates Lounge feels much more intimate. There are plenty of lounge chairs and dining tables, although the layout feels notably more compact with less open space. A self-service buffet offers light meals, snacks, and refreshments throughout the day. While the bar provides a selection of wines, spirits, beers, and soft drink. The bathrooms are spacious and include showers, basins, toilets, and premium amenities for guests wanting to freshen up before departure. After a quick look around, it's time to head to our gate. Waiting outside is today's aircraft, the magnificent Emirates Airbus A380. Even after all these years, the A380 remains one of the most impressive passenger aircraft ever built. Boarding begins and one of the great benefits of traveling first class is being invited on board before almost everyone else. >> [music] >> Turning left at door one, we enter the exclusive first class cabin. Today, we're flying in suite 2K. As the flight isn't operating at full capacity, the cabin crew have kindly let us use one of the center suites to demonstrate the bed setup, which we will check out later. It gives you a much better view of how Emirates transforms the suite into a full flat bed. This aircraft features Emirates refreshed first class interiors with elegant cream and brown tones, replacing much of the gold found on earlier cabins. The result feels modern, sophisticated, and quite luxurious. Each private suite is fully enclosed with electronic operated sliding doors, creating your own personal space in the sky. Waiting at every suite is an incredibly comfortable leather seat facing a crisp 32-in 4K entertainment screen powered by Emirates award-winning ice entertainment system. >> You can do here you can do all the seat adjustments right here. >> Beside the seat is a secondary touchscreen, allowing you to control your entertainment, lighting, seating position, privacy door, and window blinds without reaching for the main screen. Storage throughout the suite is excellent with dedicated compartments for shoes, laptops, headphones, and personal belongings. There's also a notebook and Emirates pen waiting for you, a small keepsake you can take home after the flight. A vanity mirror, cosmetic storage, and additional suite accessories are neatly integrated into the design. A personal mini bar sits beside the seat and rises elegantly at the touch of a button. It's one of those features that's both practical and a little bit fun. >> Before long, boarding is complete. The cabin doors close. It's time for pushback and departure. Watching takeoff through the A380's external cameras is one of those experiences that never gets old. The nose camera and tail camera provide a completely different perspective as the giant aircraft lifts gracefully into the sky. >> [music] >> Once airborne, it's time for breakfast. Well, breakfast number two. One of the joys of first class is never having to worry about going hungry. While our meal is being prepared, let's take a closer look at today's menu and drinks selection. Everything is served individually and beautifully presented, allowing guests to dine at at own pace rather than following a fixed service schedule. The quality, presentation, and attention to detail are exactly what you would expect from Emirates First Class. >> [music] >> To finish the meal, we're offered a beautiful selection of luxury chocolates presented in a elegant keepsake box. Next, let's take a look inside the Emirates First Class Bvlgari amenity kit. Inside, you'll find premium skin care products, lip balm, fragrance, aftershave, a dental [music] kit, deodorant, shaving cream, a razor and brush, all beautifully packed inside a luxurious leather style pouch. Now, it's time to visit one of the A380's most iconic features, the Emirates Shower Spa. >> [music] >> For an aircraft bathroom, it's remarkably spacious. Inside, you'll find a large vanity area. >> [music] >> Toilet, premium Voya amenities, heated flooring, and of course, the famous shower. >> [music] [music] >> Each first class passenger receives a dedicated shower booking with approximately 5 minutes of running water available during the session. It's an unforgettable experience and one of the defining features that sets the Emirates A380 apart from almost every other commercial aircraft. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Back at our suite, the cabin crew have transformed the seat next to us into a fully flat bed [music] complete with mattress, duvet, and pillows. >> [music] >> It looks exceptionally comfortable and is easily one of the best sleeping experiences available in commercial aviation. >> [music] >> Now, it's time to visit another signature feature of the Emirates A380, the famous onboard lounge bar. >> [music] >> Reserved exclusively for first and business class passengers, it's a social space unlike anything found on most aircraft. The bar offers premium spirits, cocktails, champagne, wines, and soft drinks [music] alongside a selection of canapés and snacks. A large screen also streams live flight information and selected live sporting events, making it an enjoyable place to stretch your legs during the flight. >> [music] >> On our walk back, we pass through the business class cabin for a closer look at Emirates' latest business class product. It's another beautiful design cabin with direct aisle access for every passenger and a spacious layout that continues Emirates' premium feel throughout the upper deck. Returning to our suite, the cabin lighting has gradually transformed into warm ambient mood lighting, creating a calm and relaxing atmosphere as we continue across the Tasman Sea. Like all good journeys, this one seems to pass far too quickly. Before we know it, the crew begins preparing the cabin for arrival. Seats upright, window shades open, one final look outside. The spectacular landscapes of New Zealand slowly appear beneath the wings as we descend towards Christchurch. So, the Emirates experience, from exceptional lounges and outstanding dining to private suites and onboard shower spa and one of the most iconic bars in the sky, Emirates first class on the Airbus A380 continues to deliver an unforgettable premium travel experience. We booked this flight using our Qantas points and if you're ever wondering whether Emirates first class lives up to its reputation, this journey [music] certainly makes a compelling case. Welcome to Christchurch. From the skies, the seas and everywhere in between, thank you for joining us on another adventure. Please give it a like, hit those subscribe and notification buttons and leave a comment below. Until next time, see you.

reviews.transcript_full: G'day guys and welcome back to another video and today we're going to be flying from  a Shanghai down to Adelaide with China Eastern on their A350-900.  Now it's only been about a week since the inaugural flight from Shanghai here down to Adelaide.  Now they're going to be operating this particular service, MU-781 on Saturdays, Mondays and Thursdays.  It's currently Monday here in Shanghai and I am really looking forward to this flight.  Now this is the first time that there has been a Chinese carrier flying direct nonstop from  Shanghai down to Adelaide. It's going to be seasonal until August the second and then I believe  later in the year in December through to about February 2027 that also going to have another  crack at it then too. So I am really looking forward to tonight's flights. So three times per week  you have an opportunity to get back to Australia and then it's MU-782 heading back up to China  from Adelaide as well. So tonight I'm really looking forward to seeing what the mill is going to be like.  As someone will see that disease I require a gluten free mill so I'm interested to see if I'm  going to be getting my typical fish mill which I usually get up in Asia here or will it be something  different. So I'm interested to see about that. I'm also keen to check out the Wi-Fi  in the situation there and the overall comfort. So anyways let's blabbering on, let's get a silver  to the airport and hop in this flight back home to Adelaide.  As we make our way from the Green Court resident city centre hotel, near People Square,  let's have a chat about costs for tonight's flight. Now I purchased a one-way ticket direct with  China Eastern on their website which set me back about $670 Australian dollars which converts to  about $470 US dollars or about $3,150 Chinese yuan.  The ride from People Square to Pedong International Airport is about an hour depending on traffic.  Sure you can take the subway which I've done many times previously and it is a much cheaper  option but today's ride in a premium vehicle only set me back about $40 Australian dollars.  So for the comfort I feel it was definitely worth it. Now one thing I always find interesting  before a flight is tracking the aircraft for actually be operating the service. So at around 10  40 a.m this morning I jumped on flight radar 24 and found tonight's aircraft about an hour  and 10 minutes away from landing in Tokyo. Earlier in the day it had already completed the long  flight from Madrid to Shanghai before heading straight back out to Japan and after a short  turn around at Tokyo it'll return to Shanghai and that's the aircraft I'll be flying on tonight  down to Adelaide.  So I've just arrived at Shanghai Poudong International Airport which first opened back in 1999  to help take the pressure of Shanghai Hongchiao Airport as the city's international air travel  continue to grow. Fast forward to today and it's become one of the busiest airports in China  and one of the busiest international airports in the world with close to 85 million passengers  passing through last year alone. Now it's the main hub for China Eastern Airlines  so if you're flying with China Eastern from Australia to Europe or even to other parts of China  or Asia there's a pretty good chance you'll be connecting through Shanghai. While China Eastern  does have other hubs around China this is definitely its biggest. In Terminal 1 this afternoon  I have to say immigration and passport control was surprisingly quick especially for a Monday.  Now since my flight departs from Gate 138 which is actually over in satellite Terminal 1  I'm going to have to head downstairs and catch the underground airport train to get there.  It's actually my first time catching this one and by looks of all the signage after two stops  I should be there in about two and a half minutes.  All right so I found my plane earlier and they're just offloading all the cargo  from the flight down from Tokyo just before and now I'm sort of just aimlessly wandering around.  I've got two hours to kill. I've had a look at a few different restaurants but  a lot of them are western and I'm very sure they're going to be crazy expensive for the prices  that I've actually been spending while out here in China. Airport food as we know is never cheap.  Maybe I'll just walk around a little more see if I can find something else and yeah we'll go  from there. So after spending a couple of hours wandering around satellite Terminal 1 it was just  about time to board tonight's flight down to Adelaide, Australia. Now before we hop on board today's  flight I'd like to thank this video sponsor which is Erilo. Now Erilo is a leading EASIN company  which is trusted by over 30 million travelers and can provide EASINs for over 200 destinations.  If you like me and travel internationally quite often one thing I used to hate was hopping off  the plane in a new country and trying to navigate my way through an airport to a store that sold  local SIM cards. Whether it would swap out my Australian SIM for the local one and then I'd have  to safely store my Aussie one in the meantime. However in the last couple of years I have been using  EASINs which have saved me time at the airport and of course stress with how simple the process is.  Now with Erilo it's simple. All we have to do is download the app, create an account,  select the right plan for you depending on your destination, install your EASIN and activate it  when you arrive. Now it doesn't just have to be one place as well. For example on this trip I was  able to download a regional plan that covered up to 18 countries in Asia. So as soon as I landed  in places like Singapore and in China all I had to do was activate the EASIN and I was immediately  connected to the internet. I'd highly recommend downloading the free Erilo app using the link in  the description below and use code loop crisp to get $3 off your first EASIN. Or you can simply  scan the QR code on the screen here to get started. But once again thank you very much for  Erilo for sponsoring today's video but now let's help on board. Boarding was pretty well to  schedule today just after 7pm and with a scheduled departure time at 7.40pm at this stage things  look pretty well on time. Now as I stepped on board I was greeted by a friendly cabin crew member  who actually walked me down the aisle and showed me to my seat. It was a small gesture but it made  for a really welcoming first impression. Now tonight I was originally assigned seat 68A in the  economy cabin however I had to change due to an issue with the seat which I'll explain shortly.  China EASIN's Airbus A35900 features a 333 economy layout which is the configuration the A350  was originally designed around so there's plenty of space to walk around the cabin as passengers  settle in. The seats offer 31 inches of pitch, around 18 inches wide,  so on paper they're fairly typical for a modern long haul economy cabin. Overall in terms of  comfort the seats feel quite comfortable knowing I'll have a long 9 also hour flight tonight down to  Adelaide. Unfortunately once the passenger in front sat down and reclined their seat a little bit  I noticed the seat back literature pocket on one had broken. Now I mentioned this to a crew member  and they were fantastic. They asked me if I wanted another window seat and quickly offered to  move me to seat 65A and even let me know the middle seat beside me was expected to remain empty as  well so overall it's no biggie as it was sort of nice and quick but before we head off tonight  I just wanted to touch on the IFE as well. On this aircraft economy passengers have an 11.6  inch high definition touch screen. The entertainment system is modern and responsive and probably one  of the better system layouts I've seen. The external cameras were great and personally I think the  interactive flight map is one of the best I've come across. You can also check out the layout for  other cabins in the aircraft and learn about the specifications. Something I personally had not seen  before.  Thankfully a crew member came over to confirm a gluten free meal request which gave me confidence  everything had been organized correctly and so far the service has been excellent. The captain  advised we'd be departing around 20 minutes behind schedule tonight due to air traffic control delays.  There was also an announcement inviting passengers to inquire about upgrading to business class.  Now out of curiosity I asked one of the crew members how much it would cost which was 13,000 Chinese  yuan which is about $2,270 Australian dollars or about $1,600 US dollars but for myself I had  mentally prepared for this flight in economy already so I didn't really say the point.  I was definitely keen to get up on the way so I could finally get a meal as I didn't find  anything of interest in the satellite terminal.  Takeoff was at 8.29pm local time tonight so about 50 minutes behind schedule at this stage so we'll  have to see if we can make up the time overnight heading south. And tonight we're expecting a flight  time of 9 hours and 10 minutes to cover about 7,700 kilometres or about 4,790 miles.  Not long after takeoff I could hear the cabin crew jump up and start heating up the meals.  Now at this point I was starving since my last meal was around lunchtime in Shanghai  and as soon as it came over I got the shock of my life. It's not fish and it appears to be a beef  meal as mentioned on the top of the packet here. Now I've possibly mentioned it before I'm not the  biggest fish eater especially with fish meals on planes and the only time I've ever had non fish  gluten free meals in Asia especially way up here in the northeast it's only been on Chinese  carriers. Now as I was about to start my meal there were a few bumps so seatbelt signs came on  so unfortunately for other passengers they were going to have to wait until it cleared before  cabin crew could begin main meal service passengers with non-dietaries. Now overall it doesn't look  too bad I noticed it was no butter for the breads but overall to be completely honest the beef felt  more like water buffalo which I've had in China before it's quite watery although taste buds  are certainly different in the air it wasn't overly beef tasting so we'll give it a 5 out of 10  mainly because it's not a fish meal but it's possible that because the beef has been frozen before  it's just lost some of its taste giving that sort of watery flavor. Other passengers seem to have  beef, rice and potatoes so similar to my meal tonight although they do have salad with prawns  so it's not overly different just apart from some of the sides. Caban crew followed this service  with bread rolls and then finally drinks before dimming down the cabin lighting.  This new non-stop service is about far more than simply giving South Australians another way  to get to China. For the first time Adelaide has a direct link to Shanghai China's largest city  and one of the world's most important financial and logistics hubs. For passengers it's a huge  improvement until now traveling between Adelaide and Shanghai usually meant connecting through Sydney,  Melbourne, Singapore, Hong Kong or Guangzhou and pretty much all those I've had to do myself and  now you can step on board an Adelaide and arrive in Shanghai around 10 hours later making business  trips, holidays and family visits much simpler and the benefits flow in both directions. For Chinese  visitors, international students and business travelers heading to South Australia this new route  removes the need for an additional domestic connection within Australia. Instead of flying into  Sydney or Melbourne before catching another flight to Adelaide they can now travel non-stop to South  Australia making the journey quicker, simpler and far more convenient. The route also compliments  Adelaide's existing non-stop service to Guangzhou rather than relying on a single gateway into  mainland China, South Australia now has direct access to two of the country's most important aviation  hubs. That gives travelers more choice while also creating greater flexibility for freight and  business. Arguably the biggest impact is below the cabin floor. Each flight can carry around 15  tons of cargo, creating a much faster and more efficient route for South Australian exports into  one of the world's largest consumer markets. Fresh seafood, premium beef, cherries, citrus and  South Australia's world-famous wine can now reach Shanghai directly, reducing handling and transit  times before continuing to destinations across China if required. China is already South Australia's  largest trading partner so having direct links into both Shanghai and Guangzhou isn't just convenient,  it's strategically important. Its strengthens business tyres, supports exporters and provides  mortal gateways into one of the world's largest economies. Shanghai is also much more than just  the destination. China Easton's Harbat put on airport offers connections throughout China,  across Asia and to major European cities. That means that this route isn't only about Adelaide  and Shanghai, it also opens up another convenient one-stop option for travelers heading to Europe  alongside the more traditional connections through the Middle East or Southeast Asia.  Competition is always a good thing and another long haul carrier in Adelaide means more choice for  travelers, more opportunities for exporters and stronger international connections for South Australia.  For a city that's worked hard to rebuild its long haul network, this route represents a  significant milestone in progress moving forward.  Breakfast was pretty standard with scrambled eggs, green veggies and potatoes,  overall it wasn't too bad, better than last night's dinner to be honest but not the best breakfast  I've had for a gluten-free meal. Now before we touch down on Adelaide, let's talk the Wi-Fi on this  flight. To connect, all I had to do was enter my seat number and the last four digits of my ID  that I used to book this flight. So in my case, it was my passport. I didn't have to wait until  we got to cruise either, I just gave it a go once over 20,000 feet and then I was connected for the  remainder of the flight. Now overall, the Wi-Fi was fine for socials, although I keep in mind,  I did have a VPN on my phone so I'm not too sure if the Wi-Fi would allow me to connect to these  apps otherwise. The cruise English was excellent and I found all my interactions with them to be  very friendly and to be honest, the only issues I'd ever had with China Eastern is managing flights  when booking them directly on the website. Thankfully on this occasion, I didn't have to organize  too much, a Cindy sort of this for me and organised the window seat and gluten-free meal,  so I didn't need to manage my own booking. Overall, economy seats are comfy, the Wi-Fi was decent,  especially the flight maps. Now if you're looking for a large range of movies and TV shows that are  Western, you'll have to bear with what's available, but overall, there's still a good 14 pages of  international movies, but just not as extensive as I've seen on other airlines. So for $670 for a  one-way flight from Shanghai down to Adelaide, I'm pretty damn happy with how this has turned out.  We touched down at 7.14am, local time in Adelaide, but thank you very much for watching this video.  As usual, if you've liked this video, it would really help me out if you can hit that like button,  and if you're not subscribed, please consider doing so. But thanks for watching this series,  heading up to China via Singapore, and I look forward to getting some more videos out very shortly.  Until then, I'll catch you in the next one and all the best.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back to the Expro State Channel. Today, we're embarking on one of the most exciting  long haul routes in the aviation world. Turkish Airlines Flight 181 Takas, taking us all the way  from Istanbul directly to Mexico City aboard the ultra-modern Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner. After spending  some time at the massive Istanbul Airport, taking advantage of the rest zones and getting a quick  coffee, it was time to board via the apron bus. Watching this massive Dreamliner engine up close  from the tarmac is always a breathtaking way to start a trip. Stepping on board, the cabin set up  immediately feels sleek and spacious. Waiting at our seats was the standard long haul kit, a soft pillow,  a warm blanket, and noise-reducing headphones. One of my favorite features on the 787 is the seat  back entertainment system. Not only is the screen sharp and loaded with hundreds of movies,  series, and live TV, but the exterior belly and tail cameras give you a pilot's eye view of  the runway. Watching our nighttime takeoff over the illuminated streets of Istanbul via the live  feed was absolute magic.  Shortly after reaching cruising altitude, the flight attendants handed out the amenity kits,  a stylish collaboration with La Coss. Inside, you'll find high-quality essentials,  travel socks, an eye mask, ear plugs, lip balm, and a full dental set. It's definitely one of the best  economy class kits out there.  Then came the main event, the first meal service. Turkish Airlines is famous for its catering,  and tonight was no exception. We were served a choice of traditional Turkish musakar baked cheesy  potatoes with grilled vegetables, accompanied by a crisp fresh salad, warm bread, and a delicious  panakata for dessert. The flavors, temperature, and presentation easily score a 10 out of 10 for  economy dining.  During a flight, we also got a small sandwich. Let's talk about a detail every long haul traveler  secretly cares about, the lavatories. On a 14 hour flight, keeping the bathrooms clean is a full-time  job, but Turkish Airlines actually does a fantastic job here. The dreamliner toilets feel surprisingly  modern, featured touchless controls, and, the best part, they stock them with premium hand soaps and  lotions that make you feel like you're in a mini-spaul instead of 35,000 feet in the air. A quick  refresh here halfway through the flight works wonders.  When it comes to killing time, the seat back screen is your best friend.  The Turkish Airlines entertainment lineup on this flight was stacked. We're talking about a  massive selection of the latest Hollywood blockbusters, classic film franchises, international cinema,  and even full seasons of popular TV shows. The touchscreen was super responsive,  and with built-in flight tracking maps and customizable audio channels, you literally cannot get bored,  even if you stay awake the entire flight.  With over 13 hours in the air, getting some sleep is essential. The dreamliner's quiet cabin,  soft mood lighting, and electronically dimmable windows make relaxing so much easier.  About two hours before landing, as the sun began to rise over the horizon,  the cabin filled with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee and a warm breakfast.  We enjoyed fluffy pancakes, side fruits, and hot pastries, the perfect fuel before arriving in  Central America.  The final descent into the Valley of Mexico is spectacular.  Gliding over the rugged mountain ranges and watching the dense, endless urban sprawl of  Mexico City unfold beneath this through the large dreamliner windows was unforgettable.  All in all, Turkish Airlines delivered an incredible long haul experience on 181 Tachas.  From the top tier catering and generous log-cost amenity kit to the comfort of the 787  dreamliner, 14 hours in economy class flew by faster than expected.  If you enjoyed this flight review, don't forget to hit that like button,  subscribe to the channel for more travel adventures, and drop a comment below,  would you survive a 14 hour flight, or do you need a live flat bed to fly this far?  Thanks for watching, and I'll see you in the next one from Mexico.
