reviews.transcript_full: economy, premium economy, business class, and first class. What's the difference in all four cabins on Emirates? And is it worth paying for those more premium cabins? After flying all four, today I'm breaking down what to expect in each class, from the ground experience to the difference in the seats, the onboard dining, drinks, amenities, and the [music] overall experience. I'm going to mainly focus on the experience on board, but let's start briefly on the ground at check-in where you'll find different check-in areas for each class of travel, typically with shorter cues and higher luggage allowances for those higher travel classes. Plus, in business and first class, you'll be able to arrive at the airport via Emirates included chauffeer service. Once through security, business and first class passengers will have access to Emirates lounges. Whilst I've only personally visited outstation lounges of Emirates, their Dubai lounges are massive, spanning most the length of the terminal and feature buffet food and drink, alley dining, and for some flights, direct boarding from the lounge. But let's step on board and check out the differences in the seats. And it's worth noting that in each class, you will find slight seat variations one plane type to the other. So, your seat might not be an exact match to the ones I showed today, but Emirates do have a lot less variation than you'll find on a lot of other airlines, particularly following their Treble 7 refurbishments. We'll start in economy and work our way up. As you'd expect in economy, there's not a lot to get too excited about, but the decor is distinctly Emirates. [music] Leg room here isn't going to be great unless you go for the bulkhead or exo seats. The seat will have a slight recline and an adjustable headrest. Overall comfort is good for economy, but at my size, I do struggle with that lack of leg room and seat width. Each seat has a good size inseat pocket, a foldout tray table that also has a separate drinks holder, inseat power, and an inflight entertainment screen. Thankfully, the version I'm showing here is their worst version, so you will hopefully get a better and more responsive screen than this most of the time in economy. Up in premium economy, the seat is significantly better than economy. A greatl looking [music] seat that provides significantly better comfort, and I personally rank this as one of the best premium economy seats available anywhere. Seats are much more spacious with plenty of leg room and lots of space ahead of you. On the seat back, you'll find a seat pocket, charging ports, and a bigger and better if screen. Down below you have a footrest, a really good and sturdy leg [music] rest, and a storage cubby containing the headphones. In one of the armrests, you'll find a storage cubby, a small drinks table, and controls for the footrest and recline. There's also a foldout tray table, which is a really nice design. The seat has a really comfortable adjustable headrest and also an excellent recline. This does of course mean that when the person in front recines, their seat goes quite far back, but the spacing means it's not as bad as you'll find on some other airlines. In business class, there are a few different seat types, but they mostly now share a similar design. [music] Here on the A380, business class is on the upper deck in the staggered 121 layout. It's not the most private by modern business class standards, but it is very comfortable. A good amount of leg room, although that foot cubby could be a little tight and a goodiz inflight entertainment screen in front. To the side, there's a small table with a mini bar containing soft drinks and snacks. There's a few charging ports, a controller for the inflight [music] entertainment, plus a tablet that can be used both as a controller for the entertainment as well as a second screen. and the tray table slides out from the side console. The A380 also has separate storage to the side which can be great for stashing the bedding that we'll look at later on. [music] You'll also find further document storage space within the foot cubby and underneath the IF screen. And now the really special one, first [music] class. [music] You'll get a beautiful and spacious private suite with a door that closes with the touch of a button. You've got acres of leg room and a seat that's spacious and incredibly comfortable. Ahead, there's a massive IF screen and a sort of desk containing a mirror as well as a few amenities that we'll look at later on. On the side console, there's a tablet to control the inflight entertainment screen since the screen itself is way too far away to be used as a touch [music] screen. This side console also includes another fun gimmick of the seat, the mini bar, which includes water, soft drinks, and snacks. And you've also got the very large and sturdy tray table [music] that deploys from the side, too. Around the seat, you'll find a few conveniences like air vents and charging ports and additional controls. And you also have a small closet area to [music] hang up a jacket. Once settled into your seat, the pre-eparture service can begin. So, what kind of service can you expect pre-eparture in each cabin? Well, in economy, you get nothing apart from a safety video. In premium economy, you'll get a pre-eparture hot towel and a soft drink such as a signature lemon mint drink, orange juice, or water. So, no pre-eparture sparkling wine like you get on some other airlines in premium economy. For that, you'll need to be flying in at least business class in Emirates, where you can receive a glass of mat champagne alongside your hot towel. Up in first, they take it up another notch of a glass of doner, and they'll be happy to top you up before you get going. This will then be followed by Arabic coffee and dates, [music] which they'll also offer top-ups of. Plus, you'll also get a hot towel. Different levels of amenities will also be provided pre-eparture in each cabin. [music] In economy, you'll receive a nice blanket and an unimpressive pillow at your seat alongside some headphones. These headphones are better than you'll get in most airline economy cabins, but you're still probably better off bringing your own. Basic amenity kits are provided only on longer overnight flights that will include basics like a dental kit and eye mask. In premium, you get a nice blanket and a better pillow than economy. But the headphones are unfortunately the same as economy. You'll also have a bottle of water waiting at the seats. And like in economy, the amenity kit is only provided on a longer overnight flight. And in addition to the basics will include a few skincare products like lip balm, moisturizer, and hand cream from Aveda. In business class, you'll find an eye mask and slippers at your seats, which are both excellent quality. The eye mask is really soft and the slippers have a really good stretch fit and are probably the best inflight slippers I've received. Some much improved headphones are also provided as well as pajamas on overnight flights. You'll also get a fantastic amenity kit that is one of the best you can get in business class with separate versions for men and women. In the men's kit, you'll find a Gillette shaving kit, deodorants, tissues, earplugs, a dental kit, comb, and a series of Bulgari products, body lotion, post shave balm, a fragrance, and a lip balm. The women's kit is similar, but it swaps out the shaving kit for a hair bubble and a makeup mirror. Plus, the Bulgari amenities and the deodorant are different versions. In first class, the level of amenities provided is so ridiculous that they even give you an Emirates first [music] class tote bag to carry it all the way in. First off, you'll get the same slippers and eye mask as in business class. There's a drawer with a notebook and pen to take with you, perfect for jotting down travel plans. In the vanity, you'll find a few pampering products like a facial toner, eye cream, sleep oil, and pillow mist. Pajamas are also provided and these are without a doubt the comfiest airline pajamas I've ever received. The pajama bottoms in particular are brilliant and one year after this flight I still wear them. The provided headphones are excellent quality from Bowowers and Wilkins. One of the few things you can't take with you sadly. And then we have the actual amenity kit itself. This contains a lot of the same items as the business class kit with a couple of differentiators like the larger size Bulgari fragrance. Now, let's get up in the sky and see the differences in the onboard service and the food and drink. [music] Once up in the air, that food and drink service can begin. In economy, you receive a menu, something that you don't really get on a lot of airlines in economy. And another thing that Emirates do to stand out here is they do provide metal cutlery in economy. Like most economy services, the food is all served on one tray and drinks are served in plastic cups. A good selection of beer, wine, and spirits is available. Main course portions are light, but typically good quality for economy, and this is served alongside plenty of side dishes and desserts, which I've always find to be good quantity and quality, too. On longer flights, you might get a second meal later in the flight, but on most, it'll just be a light snack. For example, on this one, from the UK to Dubai, I was served ice cream. You won't get many more proactive drink services offered, but the crew have generally been friendly and happy to provide additional drinks when ringing the corbell or heading to the galley. In premium economy, food, drink, and especially the service is much improved compared to economy. The crew will start with a drink service very shortly after takeoff. The main difference in the drinks from economy is an elevated wine selection as well as the fact that drinks are served in proper glassware rather than plastic. [music] The initial drink service is accompanied by a bag of nuts, and the crew offer a very friendly and proactive service, offering top-ups when drinks are low or finished. Meals are much more substantial here and are served on proper crockery, and the cutlery is a better size than what you use in economy, too. Food quality was really excellent as well, with all elements exceeding the economy offerings. Postmeal, there will be tea and coffee service served [music] in Emirates branded cups and served with some chocolate. That Bailey's was an optional touch. The crew come through the cabin very regularly to offer additional drinks and snacks. And before landing on my flight, I received an afternoon tea service, which was lovely quality, aside from the scope, but a very substantial second service. Up in business class, the drink selection is a lot more extensive, nicer wine selection, but more importantly from my perspective, there's a very extensive cocktail menu. I've yet to fly another airline with a cocktail list as long as this in business class. And they get bonus points from me for including Negronis. You'll also find better quality spirits, plus a more extensive soft drink selection than in premium economy. A drink service will start shortly after takeoff. Although worth noting, if you're near the rear of a large A380 cabin, it may take them a while to get to you, but it's worth the wait for that Negroni, and drinks are served along with a dish of warm nuts. For the meal, your tray table will be set with a tablecloth, and the meal is served course by course rather than all one tray. Starters are served alongside bread and a side salad. And it's definitely a step up both in quality and size compared to [music] premium, which is also the case for the main course options, too, which it should be noted can be pre-ordered online. After dessert, the meal is finished off with a small box of chocolates, so you can still order the cheese course without missing out on a sweet finish. Overall, Emirates business class food is very good. I don't think it's quite at the standard of close rivals like Qar, but few are, and Emirates certainly have the better drinks menu. Additional snacks and drinks are served at your seat throughout the flight, but there is somewhere else that you can go if you'd like snacks and drinks, which we'll come on to a bit later. In first class, even the menu itself feels like an event. Rather than a standard menu, this almost feels like a coffee table book that goes into detail about the offerings available, and that includes some very premium options to drink. You can choose from Don Peron champagne, expensive whisies, the same extensive cocktail menu as business class, or to really treat yourself, you can try Hennessy Paradis, which retails for around $1,000 per bottle. You've got to make sure you're getting your money's worth from that first class flight. The food is also impressive, and you can choose to dine at whatever time you'd like. The highlight though has to be the caviar service. You can have as much as you want alongside the usual accompaniment and it's absolutely delicious. Other starter options include the fantastic Arabic mezz which I would always choose when available and main courses are substantial which may not be needed given all the caviar and mez. And you can then follow up with a very tasty dessert. You'll not be going hungry here. Before the end of the flight, you'll receive a box of chocolates from the crew to either eat your own landing or to take away with you. But now we have to talk about some unique and special options available in business class and first class when you're on an A380. First up, we have the bar. Available at the back of the top deck to all business class and first class passengers. This is a social space where you can order cocktails from the bar, help yourself to snacks, and chat [music] with your fellow passengers. You can even stick around here during turbulence thanks to the seat belts that they have back here. And why not hop behind the bar yourself [music] for a quick photo op. It's a fun space and it really makes a difference to have a separate space or venue to be able to go to on a plane that's away from your seat. And if you are visiting from first class, the better quality drinks will be available to you. Next up, we have the incredible bathroom and shower that is available in first class on the A380. But first, a quick word about the toilet facilities in the other classes. In economy, it's a pretty standard economy l without too much to call out. In premium, you'll get a separate dedicated toilet for premium economy passengers. No sharing with economy like on some other airlines. Plus, you'll find these stocked with a fragrance and amenities such as dental kits and hand cream. You'll also get proper towels rather than paper towels for drying your hands. In business class, the toilet is set up the same as premium with the nice features like the fragrance and amenities. But things [music] really step up in a big way in first class, particularly on the A380 where you can take that shower. Yes, you can actually take a mid-flight shower here with 5 minutes of running hot water. Your shower slot can be booked with a dedicated shower attendant who will also make sure that the bathroom is cleaned between each use. The bathroom itself as well is huge and has heated floors and everything that you need for a bit of a freshen up and [music] some pampering before you land or perhaps before you go to sleep on an overnight flight. And on the subject of sleep, what is it like in each cabin? In economy, there's not much recline, not much space, and although the blanket's quite nice, the pillow [music] isn't. No chance I'm sleeping here. In premium, the recline is generous. There's a great amount of space, and you have a great footrest and leg rest to enhance the comfort. Many will be able to sleep well here, but I always personally struggle a lot unless I can go fully flat. In business, you're provided with good quality mattress pad and [music] some very comfy bedding. The foot space here can be a little restrictive in bed mode for taller [music] passengers. For context, I'm 6', but overall, it is comfortable, if not particularly protected [music] from the aisle in some seats. and the crew will offer to set up that bed for you. In first class, again, the crew will set up the bed for you. Although my flight was a shorter daytime one, I didn't want to bother them, so I just did it myself. It's a very wide, long, and comfy bed with a great mattress pad, pillow, and bedding. With so [music] much space and comfort, it shouldn't be a struggle for anyone to sleep here. And if you're not sleeping, how else can you pass the time? Well, Emirates's ICE inflight entertainment system is probably the best in the industry in terms of options available. A huge selection of films and TV shows, live TV and sports, plus onboard cameras. The higher the cabin you're in, the bigger the screen will be. [music] Wi-Fi is also available, and free Starlink is being rolled out to all. However, on those flights that don't have Starlink yet, there are charges that can apply. Free messaging is still available to all and business class and first class passengers do get completely free Wi-Fi, [music] but economy and premium will still have to pay for anything more than messaging on those ones that don't have Starlink. Overall, which one to book will a lot of the time come down to cost or on availability of reward flights if you're using points, although that's a bit more difficult to do on Emirates these days. It's difficult for me to say definitively if one is worth your money over the other because ultimately it depends on your personal financial circumstances and which of the elements discussed you value the most as well as what the specific price differences are on the route and dates that you're looking at. But hopefully this video at least gives you a clear understanding of the differences in each cabin to be able to make a decision on which one to go for based on the pricing that you're presented with. And if you'd like to see how this compares to each class of travel on UK airlines like British Airways and Virgin Atlantic, go ahead and watch one of these videos next. Thanks for watching.

reviews.transcript_full: In this video I'll share my experience flying from Amsterdam to New York JFK with KLM in premium comfort cabin.  It was a 7200 that took us over to New York and the flight time was around about 7.5 hours.  The seat plan was a 242 configuration and we were sat in row 15 seats F and G.  Big plus for the premium comfort cabin is the upgraded seat you get compared to economy.  Not only are the seats in premium comfort wider than economy you also get additional recline and you can see the legroom which is a significant improvement over economy.  You also have a fruit stand you can set in two different positions.  You also have an extendable lower leg rest as well. Because of the reduced number of seats the premium comfort cabin does feel more spacious just less congested than in economy.  The personal front has reclined our seat and I'm just trying to demonstrate here that even with the seat reclined in front of you you still have loads of space.  You don't have the seat getting close to your knees that you do in economy.  Talked away in your arm rest you'll find the noise canceling headphones. These are the same headphones the issue for the business class passengers.  How did they perform? My honest impression was these were some of the best airline issues and noise canceling headphones I've ever tried.  I thought they performed really well. And just to avoid anyone taking these headphones home they have this really weird three point connection.  Took about ten minutes to work out how it really attaches and it's just in here in your arm rest if you just look to cover and you'll see the small connection point here.  Also at the side of your seat you'll find a bottle of water.  You'll also find a couple of buttons one for the recline one for the extendable leg rest.  These are not electric functions you just push your button you still have to manually adjust these things.  And then you'll find a USB A and a USB C point.  On the right hand side of my seat the first thing I noticed was the top cover was actually broken.  This does protrude slightly and it's quite easy to catch it when you get in and out of your seat and I think that's what happened in the past.  Another passenger has broken this and it's not been repaired by the airline.  This is actually where you'll find your tray table just pull the small lever the table will pop up and then it can be in the half open position or the full open and it also slides back and forwards as well.  On the back of the seat in front you have a coat hook and you also have this small area for your phone and your glasses as well as the standard seat back pocket down below.  Also between the seats you have these multi plug outlets.  Over your shoulder you have an adjustable reading light.  The well padded headrest is adjustable up and down and the edge is also folded.  And finally above the seat you have individual reading lights.  Something else that differs from economy is the infotainment to screen on the seat back in front.  In economy it's 9 to 11 inches and premium comfort it's 13.3 inches.  The screen itself is fully adjustable so if the person does recline their seat in front that's not an issue.  The infotainment system itself I thought was quite responsive.  The offering they had a lot of different movies, box sets you could select their music, their games.  I thought it was quite comparable to other European airlines and there's a wide range something for everyone to show.  On the infotainment system you could also access the food and drink menu for your flight.  Another feature of the infotainment system they had a row of icons at the bottom of the screen.  And if you touch each of these give you information on your main meal, your light meal, the drinks.  And the planes sort of tracked along the bottom of the screen there so you gave an indication of when you might expect meals to be served.  Which I thought was quite useful.  I honestly didn't check to see if they stuck exactly to the schedule as the plane was moving below the icons.  But again just somewhere to quickly access information is quite important during the flight.  There were also a couple of screens in the cabin to show the safety briefing and the moving map during the flight.  Not on the KLA website you'll find the actual differences between the cabin types so just to quickly recap what you get in premium comfort versus economy.  Lightroom is 97 centimeters versus 79 centimeters and recline is 20 centimeters versus 12.5.  Get two check bags in premium comfort versus one in economy.  You also get an upgraded premium meal with a proper glass for your alcohol, metal cutlery versus a paper cup and wooden cutlery in economy.  And finally just a couple of extras at the airport you get sky priority throughout the airport.  So you can get sky priority for passport control for security and you also get priority boarding.  So you board with Group 2 which is just after the business class passenger board.  In terms of service on board not long after takeoff they came around with this refreshing towel, it wasn't warm.  And they actually didn't collect this after we'd used them as well just ended up in the seat pocket for the rest of the flight.  Around 30 minutes after takeoff they came around with a after takeoff drink and a small snack which was a bag of mixed nuts.  If you don't want to take out your tray table between the seats there's just a perfect location just replacing a drink.  And the crew also came around and handed out the amenity kits which were slightly different to what I've had before. ice cream. We get a perfect Movenpick box   and this gets me in a better mood. Once the 
desserts come, I cannot hold my smile again.   It's not a Sacher Torte or some fancy pastry. It's 
a KitKat bar. Well, actually two of them. I love   KitKat, but this is yet another piece in China 
Eastern puzzle. It's all about doing the least   effort while still ticking the box. I don't know 
if this is the intent or just how things work out,   but this is how my experience with them is shaping 
out. I am done with the meal. It might not be   award winning, but it was quite big after all. 
Full stomach makes me more relaxed and hopefully   less picky. So, let's explore further the seat, 
amenities, and of course, entertainment. What you   immediately see is that seat is quite spacious. 
You also get a lot of space for your belongings.   There is a big console by the window where you 
can place your stuff as well as a decent storage   compartment. Power outlets are right by your 
hand: Universal and USB type A, no type-C though,   which hints that this is a little older generation 
of seats. The remote has a built-in screen,   which I always like as it allows you to track the 
route while watching something on the main screen.   The controls are usual, so nothing to decipher. 
What's good is that they are mirrored on a lower   panel, which you can reach when the seat is in lie 
flat position. You can argue about materials and   finishes, but from the practicality perspective, 
the seat definitely gets the job done.   But what about in-flight entertainment? The seats 
are equipped with an 18" HD touchscreen monitors.   Very similar to what Delta and Quantas are using. 
Not award winning these days, but definitely   competitive hardware. But let's see what's 
inside it. And here I'm up to a surprise. The   media content is extremely basic. There are barely 
some 20 international movie titles, mostly old and   somehow heavily skewed to cartoons and superhero 
movies. It is even worse with the series.   There are just few in English and none that I 
even remotely heard about. Here I start feeling   annoyed. I could put up with the food, but this is 
10 hours dayflight. You're in business and there   is nothing to watch. I'm sorry, China Eastern, 
but this is not how it works in 2026. Checking   the headphones largely loses its meaning by now as 
there is not much use for them. On other airlines,   I could brag why don't they have a branded pair or 
if Bose is better than Harmon Kardon, but here we   are in a class of its own. This is the most basic 
headphone set I have seen so far in business.   It's generally what others give you in economy 
on long haul. But strangely here it makes sense.   Since there is not much to watch, why splurge for 
expensive headphones? I'm annoyed, but I cannot   argue with the logic. My last chance to entertain 
myself on this flight is to figure out Wi-Fi.   It's a bit complicated and there are many 
clicks to make, but ultimately I get there.   Wi-Fi connected. This is much further than I got 
in last couple of flights with Chinese carriers.   It's really surprising that country which 
literally lives online on the ground is still   struggling to figure out internet in the sky. But 
there is a surprise here too. We have Wi-Fi. But   it doesn't mean we have internet. The connection 
is so slow that after 15 minutes I totally give   up. The only thing it was actually good for was to 
fill in the lending card for Chinese immigration.   As if trying to compensate for the lack 
of proper entertainment, China Eastern is   providing newspapers. A nice touch, but probably 
too late for me to learn Chinese, at least for   this flight. So, it looks like that for a change, 
I will have a flight where my mind is not going   to be bothered by movies, surfing web, or doing 
emails. Well, peace of mind is a luxury, too.   And here at China Eastern delivered in full, even 
if not asked for. Meanwhile, I noticed something   interesting. There is a small round module below 
the screen which looks suspiciously like a camera.   Is this a hello from a Big Brother or is crew 
keeping an eye on annoying airline reviewers?   I doubt it is a surveillance camera, but honestly, 
I have no idea what else it could be. So,   if anyone knows, please let me know. And finally, 
amenities. Pillow and blanket were already on the   seat from the start. They are big and functional, 
but there is no way to mistake them for Armani   Caza bedding on Etihad . This is more of a summer 
camp vibe. There is also a pouch with slippers.   Check. Amenities come in a small fabric pouch 
which does look quite authentic. Unfortunately,   the contents tell a different story. It is the 
purest form of business class basics. An eye mask,   comb, toothbrush, and ear plugs. Everything is 
double and triple wrapped and boxed in plastic.   Many airlines now turn a mini kits into 
collaborations with artists and fashion houses.   Here it almost looks like China Eastern cooperated 
with an Association of Plastic Producers.   I'm done with almost everything and at 
the absence of any decent entertainment,   my best option is to get some sleep. This is 
a red-eye flight. Still a daytime for me, but   will arrive early in the morning. So catching some 
sleep is not the worst idea. I'm checking if there   are any mini mattresses, but no luck. Well, not 
having entertainment and internet might have been   a blessing in disguise. I managed to get a decent 
sleep instead. And now ready to check out the   second meal service. Time-wise, breakfast would 
probably make much more sense, but we get what   China Eastern calls "Light meal". By now, I know 
that menu is more of a guideline than a guarantee.   Tuna salad somehow turned into grilled salmon, 
but I did get sauteed shrimps with veggie and   steamed rice. Salmon tasted like it was cooked a 
week ago, but shrimps were actually pretty good.   And somehow this light meal turned out to be 
better than the main meal earlier on. Wonder   if China Eastern kept the best till the landing 
as it's often the last impression that stays with   you. Now it's the time to conclude and to make a 
verdict. I came with low expectations and with all   the baggage of stereotypes about China state-owned 
airlines. Some of them China Eastern proved wrong,   but others unfortunately were still there. The 
airport experience was very basic, but I wouldn't   give it too much weight as it wasn't their own 
ground. Then the plane was a nice surprise.   instead of beating up an old-fashioned 2-2-2 
product, China Eastern had a proper 1-2-1 business   cabin. And even if I could pick things here and 
there on lack of customization, it's still a very   competitive product. Where they failed to deliver 
for me though is the service and attention to   experience. After all these years, China Eastern 
still seems to be all about transportation   rather than passenger experience, even in business 
class. Interestingly, I expected them to score   higher than more rigid and formal Air China. But 
strangely, Air China still provided a more premium   and satisfying feeling. The way I understand China 
Easter now is that they try to tick all the boxes,   but in the most formal and minimalist way. It's

for international passengers, very weak internet,   bland food, and very little attention to all those 
small details here and there that ultimately give   you the experience. So, no surprise that I came 
up with 3+/5. China Eastern is clearly making an   effort to reinvent and to make themselves a global 
airline. And by its sheer size, it's as global   as it gets. But doing so, it prioritizes hardware 
over soft product. It invests billions into planes   but still fails to notice things that are beyond 
entertainment, service and passenger experience.   China Eastern got all the resources they need.

L3와 R3, 그니까 항공기 앞쪽 기준으로 3번째 왼쪽가 오른쪽 도와가 있는 구역인데요.  여기 화장실이 5개나 있습니다.  오른쪽에 두 개, 가운데 하나, 그리고 왼편에 두 개가 있어요.  사전 자석 지성하실 때 이 근처는 절대 지정하시면 안되는게  물레리는 소리 냄새에 이동하는 사람들, 또 가운데 서서 얘기하는 사람들.  이 근처는 편한 비행은 포기해야 된다고 보시면 될 것 같아요.  화장실에 치솔 치약이 준비되어 있는데요.  예전에 탓을 때는 즐겨게 치약이 콜게티였던 것 같은데  된티스트로 변경됐네요.  물연도 조제도 되니까요, 적당한 온도로 입을 헹궈주시면 좋아요.  그리고 기네에 선단는 부분들이 있잖아요.  폐쇄적인 공간에서 하루에도 수백 명의 손이 닿는 부위기 때문에  기네에 손소독제를 휴대하시면 좋습니다.  저는 특히 화장실 사용의 자리에 와서는 꼭 써주는 편입니다.  터빌런스가 좀 강해진다 싶으면 동남아에 거의 다 온거구요.  단ang쯤 지나갈 때 마지막 간식이 나옵니다.  타이밍크티 모찌 번인데요.  타이밍크티 약간 떨분 단마시 있는 모찌를 얹은 번인데요.  저는 잘 먹었는데 이렇게 호불호가 있는 것 같아요.  주변에서 안 드시고 그냥 버리시더라고요.  간식 먹고 나면 창유 준비 방송이 나오구요.  반곱수한 납품공항에 창유 갑니다.  아..  예동시간보다 43분 1찍 도착했구요.  개이트의 주기를 맞췄습니다.  하기 하면서 마무리하겠습니다.  사양공 인천에 뛰어는 세편을 모두 주력 기종인 에어 버스 3억웅을 뛰어고 있는데요.  이 친구들이 어느 더 기령이 평균 8년이 넘어가고 있습니다.  근데 이 친구들 관리 컨디션이 기령치고도 쏙 좋지 않은 편이에요.  나름 태국을 대표하는 공사인데 이런 부분은 좀 많이 아쉽습니다.  물론 코로나대 파산 직점까지 갔다가 회생이라는 과정에서 관리 공백이 생겼을 수는 있어요.  그래도 앞으로는 좀 나아줘야 되지 않을까 하는 생각이 들구요.  그리고 기네엔 더 한국어 미지원은 인천 방콩노선에 타는 승계 입장에서는 좀 많이 별로입니다.  그래도 대안한 공 아시아나보다 저렴한 포지션에 같은 국내의 시시들과 가격 차이가 많이 안 나서  여전히 가성비가 좋은 풀 서비스 한공사에게는 하구요.  승무원 서비스나 기네식도 태국 단계 훌륭합니다.  하얀공이 상원이 많이 좋아지면서 최근에 에어 버스 3일 레오도 새로 끓이고  고잉 7-8치도 5대나 주문하면서 새 비행기들도 많이 들을 것 같다고 하는데요.  기대를 좀 해볼게요.  요즘 방콩의 여행간은 한국 관광객이 많이 줄었다고 하는데요.  그래도 전 세계적으로 아직은 상위권의 위치한 여행지답게 다른 나라에서는 아직도 많이 오는 것 같습니다.  입구 심사줄이 어마어마해요.  1시간 반 정도 걸려서 입국 심사를 빠져나왔는데요.  아무래도 오전 비행기를 타고 와서 더 그랬던 것 같긴 해요.  너무 오랜만에 타고는 타이안공이었구요.  저는 방콩에서 귀향을 전하고 다음 주에는 16만원의 애매에 탄공을 탑승한 후기 들고 오겠습니다.  긴 영상 끝까지 봐주셔서 감사드리고요.  저는 다음 주에 뵙겠습니다.  감사합니다.

reviews.transcript_full: Good morning from Stockholm where after a two hour sleep, it's time for me to head back  to the airport for my first fifth freedom flight adventure.  Welcome to Gate F-62, the Gate of my flight on board Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 787-9,  taking me to Oslo, Norway for the day.  My flight today is operated by registration ET-AUP.  Delivered in November of 2017, this aircraft is just 8.5 years old.  This route by no means deserves such a large aircraft by itself, but to my surprise is  this flight ends up being nearly full.  I'll explain later.  Arriving at my seat for this short flight, covered in green is 22L, with 31 inches of  pitch, 17 inches of width, and 5 inches of recline, the seat itself is pretty standard.  The seat pocket features the usual safety card as well as another thing that surprised  me, not one, not two, but three different magazines.  The seat also comes with a standard sized IFE, which I will go more in detail with during  the flight.  I do find it a bit weird that Ethiopian would offer pillows with green covers, though it's  nothing new considering other airlines use colored cases as well. The reason I flew Swiss is because the evening departure time was much better time than the United flight which leaves early in the afternoon for my work travel purposes.

reviews.transcript_full: Good evening from San Francisco International Airport where we're about to get on a 10.5 hour flight on Swiss Air and fly across the US into the Atlantic and over to my favorite country in the world Switzerland.  Zurich Fun Fact is not the capital of Switzerland but it might be the global capital of hiding money.  But that's neither here nor there.  On a side note whenever you're in Indian traveling to India from the US your task would take baggage for your entire bloodline.  And so here we are but thankfully at least the journeys in business class where you can check in through the business class lane or the first class lane and drop your extra baggage off.  The first class lane applies if you have StarLines gold status. That's just how the Lufthansa group works.  Once you're done and through security turn right and head straight for the United Polaris lounge.  You can access the Polaris lounge as long as your business class ticket is either a business flex or a business basic fare.  If you have a business light fare you cannot access this lounge unfortunately.  If your business class ticket is a business light fare you can still use the United Club further down in the concourse but it's honestly not that great.  But while we're here at the Polaris lounge let's talk about it.  The Polaris lounge here at SFO is truly beautiful spanning two floors and clocking in at over 28,000 square feet. It's definitely the biggest one in the system.  The upper floor of this Polaris lounge is essentially a long rectangular room with a lot of seating options, a beautiful bar where you can get pretty much any drink that you'd like and a buffet area where you can get non-alcoholic beverages, cold food items and hot food items.  But the real star of this upper floor in my opinion is the dining room where you can order off an all-acart menu and have made to order dishes and drinks available to you.  But this is incredibly popular and the wait times can sometimes be north of an hour so I highly recommend joining the wait list as soon as you arrive into the lounge.  Whenever I'm in the dining room my routine is always a glass of champagne, a cheese plate of some kind, a protein with some fiber, although this rock cod really didn't have much fiber on the side and then of course the chocolate chip skillet cookie.  For this particular meal we're going to simply pretend that calories and macros do not exist.  Upper floor side the lower floor is much more quiet and separate and doesn't really have much except for additional seating but the main thing that it does have is the shower suites.  These shower suites are large, spacious, very nice and have all the amenities that you could possibly need to take a shower. However they also do get really popular so do check the wait list before you get in.  The main takeaway here is that the Polaris lounge has pretty much anything you'd need to get comfortable before your flight.  The one thing that I would always recommend is as soon as you enter the Polaris lounge check out the dining room wait list and check on the shower wait list first thing before you do anything else.  Coming to our aircraft we have my favorite aircraft of all time a triple 7300DR with the most powerful engines known to commercial aviation. The GE9115B which will hear all of its power during the engine start and take off.  By the time I got to the gate boarding had just kicked off for group 2 which is for business class and starlines, gold members and normally first and business class board through the first door of the plane but they reserved the first door just for first class which I kind of respect. It keeps that experience really exclusive for them.  So with Sarah's business class comes in a staggered configuration where the middle section always has two seats but on the windows side you either have one seat or two seats.  So for example this throne seat as they call it is a single seat and it's naturally more price here but free to loop thoncy elite members and then of course the other seat is your normal business class seat.  The throne seat was still available at check in and because of my starlines gold set as they gave it to me.  A short while after a crew member came round with pre-departure beverages between champagne and Swiss's famous elderberry drink and if you know anything about me you know the obvious choice.  Now coming back to our throne seat I'll say this about the seat. To say that Cathay Pacific had a few difficult years is quite an understatement.  First the Hong Kong protest and shortly after that COVID, enough to cripple any airline,  but Cathay is still around.  So what is like flying with them now, a strip down airline trying to save every penny  with bad service, or is it still one of the best airlines you can fly with?  Let me share you my experience in this review and I will figure out what's below missed.  Welcome to the frequent Business Traveler channel.  And we're starting the day in Amsterdam, sunny, shippled to be precise.  My fly today is from Amsterdam to Hong Kong with Cathay Pacific a 351,000.  Unfortunately the a 351,000 we're flying today doesn't have Cathay's newest Business  class product, the area suites, which apparently is an art form.  So you'll need to do it with the soft-front Business class seats.  The same you'll find in, for example, Air France and American Airlines.  Seats are in a 1-2-1 layout and have a width of 20.5 inch and they convert to a fully flat  bed of roughly 78 inch, 198 centimeters. I've got seat 23D.  Obviously, if you're traveling alone a window seat is the best, but this was simply the  last seat available.  As stated earlier, Air France is using the same kind of seat in their Business class.  So for me, it looks very familiar.  Having said that, there is some extra padding on the side of the seat.  That's actually a brilliant addition and is giving you a little bit more space when a seat  is in a live flat position.  The seat controls are next to the seat and there's already a bottle of water and an amenity  kit.  There are also slippers and there is a big bag which contains a mattress stopper and  a blanket and more on that one later.  Let's have a look at the amenity kit and I like the little look of the bag with very  subtle, the catholic logo on there.  Inside really everything you expect and more, because besides the lip balm and body gel  from the UK brand BEMFOOD, there's also a small bottle of mouthwater as well as pillow  mist.  Of course, I knew what pillow mist was and didn't have to look it up at all, but for sure  I will spray my whole pillow and bed linen with it later.  Let's look at the menu for lunch.  There are five main disoptions which is really good and it does include a veggie option.  Barbecue pork noodle soup that sounds excellent so that's my pick.  There's also a list of all day options which also includes a noodle soup but also a beef  burger.  For the pre-arrival meal you can choose out of four options and since I'm flying to  Hong Kong, the Chinese breakfast with chicken congee sounds excellent.  No short and eighties time but a glass of shabby would do very nice as well.  Oh, and you do need to fill in the breakfast card and hang it next to your seat.  Done!  And again, that huge bag contains the bed linen and mattress to be tested out later.  And if you curious to know what the flight will actually be like, then just hit that subscribe  button and follow the channel.  There's a lot more content coming including Lufthansa's new legory business class and  premium economy reviews.  Now let me already give you a spoiler alert on the bed linen.  There is blanket inside this bag, it's actually duvet or confortor and it was the most  comfortable luxurious bed linen I've ever had in business class.  This felt so comfortable and it actually came close to what you're getting with Air  Franz La Première.  The mattress stoper also helped with the experience.  I slept like a baby or maybe it because I sprinkled the pillow with mist everywhere.  Whatever it was, this bed linen gets a 10 out of 10.  Before the departure I also checked out the entertainment selection, the selection of  movies and TV series but also a live sports.  Since I was a world cup game going on during this flight, I was anxious to see if I could  actually watch again later.  Let's see.  After all that time for the departure and even if you don't have a window seat, you can  still enjoy the take off via the cameras.  Shortly after take off, crew comes by with drinks and a little snack.  Time to try out that chubby.  After that was time for the appetizer, I picked the octopus with potato salad and that  was accent and it came with garlic bread which seems a common thing lately with all Asian  airlines and that's not a bad thing.  And yes, that appetizer was really nice.  Time for the main which was the barbecue with pork noodle soup and like the appetizer,  I really enjoyed this noodle soup and the crew was also really friendly during this  whole flight which also helps with the overall experience.  So far so good and the only thing that could still ruin this experience would be a horrible  desire.  Talking about the desire after the main course, the desire truly makes its appearance.  I already could have a sneak peek and I'm seeing ice cream and fruit.  I decided to save the ice cream for later and for now settle for fruit and strawberry  mousse.  And this wasn't horrible on the contrary, a brilliant desire to finish off an equally  good main course and appetizer.  I had some really good meals in business class lately, Singapore Airlines stood out, but  also V-Number Airlines and Thai Airlines were pretty good, but I must say, Cathay Pacific  is up there with Singapore Airlines, this meal was brilliant.  Half a June flight I thought it would be a good idea to get a ice cream, get some caffeine  and check out the life sports.  And this was great, watching Norway against France live in a plane.  I'm telling it again, every airline should have a few channels with life sports.  Also here, Cathay didn't disappoint.  So after brilliant lunch, good sleep, it's time for the pre-arrival meal, the chicken  congee, while watching Norway against France with a brilliant ambale and ambapé.  And I'm sorry guys, it is getting boring, but also this dish was excellent.  I really enjoyed it, the only thing missing, a nice cappuccino.  Well, another 10 out of 10 would be a bit too much, wouldn't it?  And with the pre-arrival meal out of the way, it's time for a conclusion. Passengers can adjust the air conditioning in the car. I'm now heading to Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi. The free chauffeur service is available within the UAE, so transfers from Dubai to Zayed International Airport are also possible. We can see the futuristic airport building. reviews.transcript_full: Today we're back in Bangladesh to ride the most iconic form of transport in this fascinating country.  We will travel on this impressive river ferry and explore it all in detail from my luxurious suite to the cheapest tickets on board.  So come along with me and let's check out all the food options and a very special invite to meet the captain too.  It's going to be some adventure.  Oh yeah and we had a few crashes too.  We stayed in Kuln other previous night, 120 kilometres to the west of today's departure point in Barishal.  Our transfer included a few sightseeing stops along the way, including at the famous 60 domes mosque which was simply stunning.  I bet you'll never guess how it got that name.  Anyway it was well worth the extra time and super nice to see a bit more of off the beaten path Bangladesh.  Back on the road and before long we are arriving in Barishal.  This is Bangladesh's 10th largest city with a population of around half a million people.  We arrive at the river port around 4pm, some 5 hours before scheduled departure time, in the hope we can drop off our bags at the boat and have a look around.  Yes.  After paying the 10 taker port fee we were allowed in.  Thank you.  And here is our ferry for tonight, the MV Manami which has a top speed of 40 kilometres per hour.  This type of boat is referred to as a river launch in Bangladesh.  Bording is by way of this gang plank and as far as I'm aware there is no disabled access or facilities at all on board.  We had pre-booked and paid a 50% deposit in Dhaka about 6 days prior to secure our rooms and then paid the balance before departure.  I will go through all the prices once we get going.  The rooms were pretty much ready when we arrived so we were able to rest for a few hours before the fun starts.  I love the style of these river launches covered with all their flashy lights and all trying to outdo each other.  Let's now have a look at tonight's route.  We depart Barishal in a north-east-de-Led direction along the Curtain-Colar River before turning north on the Megna River direct to Dhaka.  We will be in one of the four VIP suites located on the top passenger deck towards the rear of the boat.  Here's mine which comes equipped with two double beds. Whenever I am travelling especially on longer trips like this 3 week one across Bangladesh and India, having reliable luggage makes all the difference to me. It's got a tough polycarbonate shell that's lightweight but incredibly durable, smooth 360 degree spinner wheels and a wide trolley handle that makes navigating busy airports and railway stations effortless. One feature I particularly like is the quick access front pocket which makes it easy to grab my laptop, new camera batteries, passport or other essentials quickly and easily.  However you're travelling all level 8 luggage is designed to cope with the demands of frequent usage while still looking sleek and elegant.  If you're wanting to upgrade your luggage you can grab 12% off anything on the level 8 website using my discount code non-stop12.  A huge thanks to level 8 for their ongoing support of the channel. Now let's get back to the boat and our overnight trip to Dacca.  River launches are a vital part of the Bangladeshy Transport Network connecting millions of people across the country's extensive rivers on a daily basis.  They provide essential access to remote communities, transport goods and passengers without which the country would not function.  Okay, time to have a proper look around the VIP area and my suite.  The lobby features four large sofas and a communal dining area down the far end. Orders will be brought up from the restaurant downstairs.  My room is one of the twin suites with a lockable door.  These feature full length blackout curtains on the windows.  There are a variety of main room lights which can be controlled by the switches near the TV or by the bed.  There are two double beds which have reasonably hard mattresses along with fluffy pillows and a soft duvet. All bedding was clean. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard Austrian Airlines' Boeing 777 Business Class Enjoy the full Austrian Airlines Business Class experience The video shows the Business Class seat, amenities, and food Expect some turbulence during the 9 hour flight ... This lounge is located in the non-Schengen departures area Most seating areas are arranged around coffee tables Red and green accents reflect Austrian Airlines’ colors A self-service buffet is located in the center of the lounge It's a short stroll from the lounge to the gate  This is the Boeing 777-200ER that will fly us to the Maldives Built in 2007, the plane has registration code OE-LPD Boarding begins on schedule Austrian Airlines' B777 Business Class cabin features 32 seats The lie-flat seats arranged in a staggered configuration The center seats are arranged in pairs, perfect for couples Window seats alternate between one and two per row 2K is my window seat for the 9 hour flight to the Maldives The best seats in the Business Class cabin are the throne seats These solo seats have two side tables and feel more private We have a full flight tonight to the Maldives The captain welcomes everyone onboard A welcome drink is offered (water, orange juice or Champagne) The welcome drink is served with some mixed nuts  Austrian's famous Flying Chef joins this flight The chef plates, garnishes and adds final touches to every meal The chef visits every Business Class seat to present the menu Austrian Airlines' safety video is shown prior to departure We're leaving the gate at 7 pm local time (on time departure) The cabin lights are dimmed prior to takeoff Austrian Airlines' Boeing 777 is powered by two GE90 engines Each GE90 engine produces over 90,000 pounds of thrust The GE90 is one of the world's most powerful jet engines Have you ever flown with Austrian Airlines?  Let's have a look at Austrian Airlines' Business Class seat A reading light and universal power outlets are built into the seat  A wired handset is located below a flap in the armrest A panel with the seat controls is easy to reach Storage space around the seat is rather limited In front of each seat is a HD entertainment screen  The seat's footwell is located beneath the screen The fold-out tray table is released at the push of a button A hot towel is distributed shortly after takeoff Austrian’s amenity kit is created by Vienna’s MAK Museum The bag & eyeshade features a Wiener Werkstätte design A warm, high-quality blanket and fluffy pillow are provided Noise-cancelling headphones are offered Let's have a look at the menu on tonight's flight Austrian Airlines collaborates with DO & CO for its catering Dinner service is delayed because of turbulence Are you afraid of flying through turbulence? Leave a comment Dinner service resumes shortly after the turbulence subsides The crew rolls a selection of starters through the cabin Starters: salad, roast beef, coleslaw & baked Emmental cheese Soup: clear beef broth with Tyrolian cheese dumplings Main course: braised beef with potato salad & tartar sauce  A selection of cheeses and desserts is offered Desserts: Demel's Esterhazy cake, vanilla crème fraîche & fruits There are three lavatories for the 32 Business Class passengers The seat reclines in a bed with a length of 2 m (6.5 ft) Unfortunately, the flat bed's foot compartment is quite narrow Each Business Class seat has its own 15-inch HD touchscreen The entertainment selection is decent, with many films & series Content is available in 20 languages and updated monthly Unfortunately, Austrian's B777s are not equipped with WiFi A few hours later: we're waking up above the Indian Ocean Breakfast service is postponed due to some more turbulence Look at the movement of the wing and engine A hot towel is provided before breakfast to freshen up Breakfast starts with an energy shot (apple, carrot, ginger, lime)  Main course: freshly prepared eggs sunny side up with toast The breakfast is served with muesli and strawberry yoghurt The First Officer is announcing our approach to Male We get some stunning views of the Maldives on approach Austrian Airlines was founded in 1957 Vienna has been the airline's home hub since the beginning Austrian Airlines joined the Lufthansa Group in 2009 Austrian operates a mixed Airbus and Boeing fleet Its long-haul fleet consists of Boeing 777s and 787 Dreamliners The Boeing 787 is gradually replacing the older 777 aircraft The airline also operates Airbus A320-family aircraft These modern jets serve shorter European routes The airline is famous for serving Viennese coffee onboard Austrian Airlines has been a Star Alliance member since 2000 Thx for watching my Austrian Airlines 777 Business Class video

reviews.transcript_full: For decades, the ultimate sign of a premium airline experience was staring right at you.  The hard-wired seat-back entertainment screen. But quietly, behind the scenes of airline  board meetings, a radical engineering shift is taking place.  Airlines are actively ripping them out. This mass extraction is being accelerated by a rapid  quiet takeover of the skies. Spanish carrier Iberia officially launched its very first  long-haul aircraft fully equipped with SpaceX's Starlink high-speed internet.  Simultaneously, the newly merged fleets of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines  hit a massive infrastructure milestone, with roughly 150 aircraft now actively operating on  the Starlink Wi-Fi network. To understand why this matters to an airline's survival,  we have to look at the brutal spreadsheet economics of InFlight hardware.  Outfitting a single wide-body aircraft with legacy seat-back systems from providers like Panasonic  or Thalas can cost up to $10 million. But the real financial bleeding happens in the fuel lines.  With the International Air Transport Association forecasting global airline fuel bills to hit a  staggering $350 billion, carriers can no longer afford to fly dead weight.  Dropping traditional seat-back monitors in favor of a Bring Your Own Device model  allows a standard narrow-body jet to shed up to 1,500 pounds of wiring, screens, and server boxes.  By letting passengers stream over low-latency satellite networks on their own phones or tablets,  airlines cut installation costs, reduce fuel burn, and protect bleeding profit margins from volatile  energy spikes. The reason this transformation is happening right now comes down to fundamental  orbital physics. Legacy InFlight Internet relies on geostationary or GEO satellites.  These massive spacecraft orbit at a fixed position over 35,000 kilometres above the earth.  Because the data has to travel 70,000 kilometres round trip,  passengers experience severe latency bottlenecks, frequently exceeding 600 milliseconds.  This makes simple tasks like video streaming or business video calls  completely impossible in the air. SpaceX's Starlink completely rewrote this math  by deploying a low-earth orbit or LEO constellation. Operating at an altitude of just  550 kilometres, Starlink cuts the physical distance data must travel by over 95%.  This drops InFlight latency down to roughly 30 milliseconds, delivering true ground-like broadband  speeds to an aircraft travelling at 500 miles per hour. This massive performance gap has triggered  an economic crisis for Legacy InFlight connectivity providers like Viassat and GoGo.  As major network airlines aggressively shift their fleets to Starlink's low-latency network,  traditional satellite operators are watching their market caps drop.  The infrastructure monopoly that Legacy providers held for two decades has evaporated,  forced out by the superior unit economics of reusable rocket-deployed constellations.  While removing screens saves millions in fuel weight, the business model behind free ultra-fast  InFlight Wi-Fi introduces a massive new ancillary revenue stream.  Airlines are no longer viewing internet access as a paid utility for passengers. Instead,  they are turning it into a high-value marketing platform.  By partnering with major digital brands, airlines can offer the Wi-Fi completely free to the  passenger, while a corporate sponsor subsidises the network operational costs.  This model creates a highly effective ecosystem for loyalty acquisition.  To unlock the free high-speed Starlink connection, passengers are typically required to log in  using their frequent flyer credentials or sign-up for the airline's loyalty program on the spot.  This allows carriers to capture valuable consumer data, drive co-branded credit card sign-ups,  and serve hyper-targeted advertising to a captive audience for hours at a time.  The internet isn't a cost center anymore. It's a customer acquisition machine.  However, the total elimination of seat-back screens isn't uniform across the entire aviation industry.  A distinct economic divide has formed between short-haul domestic fleets and long-haul intercontinental  networks. For domestic narrow-body aircraft operating two to four-hour flights, the data overwhelmingly  supports a complete shift to bring your own device cabins. But for ultra-long-haul wide-body aircraft,  the seat-back screen remains a critical competitive differentiator.  On international routes lasting 12 to 15 hours, battery depletion on passenger devices  becomes a major operational friction point. Furthermore, elite premium international carriers use  massive high-definition seat-back screens as a luxury status symbol to justify multi-thousand  dollar business and first-class ticket yields. While domestic low-cost carriers are aggressively  stripping hardware out to maximize short-haul margins, premium international airlines are doubling  down on ultra-thin, lightweight, OLD screens to preserve their top-tier branding.  The economic reality of the modern aircraft cabin is clear. The heavy, hard-wired,  $10 million seat-back entertainment box is a relic of an era before smartphones and low-earth  orbit satellite constellations. As Starlink continues to expand its footprint across global  mainline carriers, the traditional in-flight hardware model will continue its rapid decline.  By shifting the weight, maintenance, and upgrade costs of physical screens directly onto  the devices already sitting in the passenger's pocket, airlines are unlocking immense structural  fuel savings. The future of in-flight entertainment isn't built into the back of your seat.  It is beaming down from low-earth orbit directly to the palm of your hand.

After all, the 2026 Airbus A380 remains one of the finest passenger aircraft ever built.  Its combination of luxury, comfort, quiet operation, enormous capacity, and smooth flight  characteristics ensures it continues to deliver a world-class travel experience for passengers  across the globe.

reviews.transcript_full: Something significant happened at Accra International Airport this weekend. And while it may have looked like just another aircraft touching down on the runway, it actually represents a much bigger story about Ghana's growing role in global aviation, trade, tourism, and international business. For the very first time, Emirates flight EK 789 landed in Accra, introducing a new phase in the airline's operations in Ghana, and sending a powerful message that one of the world's most respected airlines sees increasing demand and enormous long-term potential in the Ghanaian market. Before we dive deeper into today's update, take a moment to like, share, and subscribe to the channel. Your support is key to helping us grow and reach more viewers like you. Don't forget to hit the notification bell so you never miss out on exciting update. This is not simply the addition of another flight to the schedule. It is a vote of confidence in Ghana's economy, its people, and its future as as one of West Africa's most important transportation hubs. For years, Emirates has connected Ghana to the rest of the world through its Dubai hub, but the decision to increase services from seven weekly flights to 11 represents a major milestone. Beginning immediately, travelers now have four additional flights every week operating every Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday. This means passengers have greater flexibility when planning international journeys, whether they are traveling for business meetings, family visits, education, medical care, or tourism. More importantly, the additional service introduces an early morning arrival into Accra, making international connections much smoother for passengers arriving from some of the world's busiest travel markets, including India, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Germany. Think about what this means in practical terms. A Ghanaian entrepreneur returning from a business conference in Dubai can now connect more easily from cities across Asia without spending unnecessary hours waiting at airports. Students studying abroad have more options during holiday seasons. Families separated across continents can choose flights that better fit their schedules. Tourists interested in exploring Ghana now have improved access from multiple international destinations, making the country more attractive than ever before. This expansion also tells us something about global travel trends. Airlines only increase frequencies when they are confident that passenger demand will continue to rise. Operating additional long-haul flights is expensive. It requires aircraft availability, highly trained crews, airport coordination, maintenance planning, and substantial operational investment. Emirates would not make such a commitment unless it believed Ghana's market had reached a level capable of sustaining continued growth. The airline's relationship with Ghana stretches back more than two decades. Since beginning operations in 2004, Emirates has steadily built connections between Accra and hundreds of destinations across its worldwide network through Dubai International Airport, one of the busiest aviation hubs on Earth. During that period, countless Ghanaian professionals, students, tourists, business executives, and investors have relied on Emirates to reach destinations across Asia, Europe, Australia, North America, and the Middle East. At the same time, thousands of international travelers have discovered Ghana through the airline's extensive network, contributing to tourism, investment, and cultural exchange. The introduction of flight EK789 strengthens this relationship even further. According to Emirates country manager for Ghana, Salem Al Mana, the additional service demonstrates the airline's long-term commitment to Ghana and reflects growing travel demand across the market. His comments highlight an important reality. Ghana is no longer viewed simply as another destination on the African network. Instead, it is increasingly recognized as a growing market deserving greater capacity, better scheduling, and enhanced connectivity. One of the most exciting aspects of this expansion is how it improves Ghana's position within the global transportation system. Dubai serves as one of the world's greatest connecting airports, linking passengers to hundreds of cities within a single network. From Accra, travelers can now enjoy even more convenient onward connections to major destinations throughout Asia, Australia, Saudi Arabia, Europe, and North America. Whether someone is flying to Tokyo for business, Sydney for education, New York for tourism, Mumbai for trade, or Jeddah for religious pilgrimage, these additional services significantly improve travel flexibility. Beyond passenger travel, stronger aviation links often generate broader economic benefits. Every additional international flight increases opportunities for business partnerships, foreign investment, conference tourism, international trade, and cargo transportation. Companies considering investments in Ghana value reliable international connectivity because executives, engineers, consultants, and specialists can travel more efficiently. Likewise, Ghanaian exporters benefit from stronger links to international markets, particularly for high-value products requiring fast transportation. The announcement has also been warmly welcomed by Ghana Airports Company Limited. Managing Director Yvonne Nana Afriyie Opare described the additional service as a strong endorsement of Ghana's growing aviation sector and the country's increasing demand for international connectivity. Her remarks underline another important point. Airports are no longer simply places where aircraft land and take off. Modern airports serve as economic engines that stimulate employment, tourism, logistics, retail development, hospitality, and international commerce. Every additional international service creates ripple effects throughout the economy, supporting businesses both inside and outside the airport. For Accra International Airport, attracting additional frequencies from a globally recognized airline like Emirates enhances its reputation as an important gateway into West Africa. As more airlines expand their operations, Accra becomes increasingly attractive as a regional transit point, encouraging even more international carriers to consider expanding their own services. This creates healthy competition that ultimately benefits passengers through improved connectivity, greater choice, and potentially more competitive fares over time. Passengers themselves will also experience the premium products for which Emirates has become internationally renowned. The additional services are operated using the Boeing 777-300ER, one of the airline's flagship long-haul aircraft. Travelers flying from Accra can choose between luxurious first class private suites, comfortable lie-flat business class seats, or spacious economy class cabins designed for long-distance comfort. Throughout the journey, passengers enjoy Emirates' award-winning hospitality, internationally inspired cuisine, and one of the world's most extensive in-flight entertainment systems. The airline's famous ICE entertainment platform offers more than 6,500 channels of movies, television programs, documentaries, music, games, and educational content in over 40 languages, including content specifically relevant to Ghanaian travelers. While premium onboard products certainly attract passengers, the real significance of these additional flights extends far beyond the aircraft cabin. Every extra connection strengthens relationships between nations. Students gain greater educational opportunities abroad. Entrepreneurs discover new markets. Investors explore business opportunities with increased confidence. Families separated by thousands of kilometers find it easier to reunite. Tourists contribute valuable foreign exchange to local businesses, hotels, restaurants, and transport providers. In many ways, aviation acts as the invisible bridge connecting economies, cultures, and people across continents. >> If today is your first time watching this channel or you are returning to this channel for the exciting content, please subscribe to our channel for more educated and developmental projects across Ghana and Africa as a whole.
