reviews.transcript_full: Hi, Mel here. In today's video, I'll be taking you with me as I fly with Luftwanzza in their new  Aliegris business class. It was my first time trying Aliegris, and based on the mixed reviews,  I really wasn't sure what to expect. The overnight flight from Chicago to Munich was scheduled to  take a little over eight hours. Plenty of time to get a real feel for this new product.  So how was my flight? Did the new Aliegris seating impress me as much as I expected?  And is it enough of an improvement to make Luftwanzza a serious competitor in the business class  market? I hope you'll come along with me to date to find out. Also, if you enjoy this type of content,  I hope you'll hit the like button and subscribe. And with that out of the way, let's get started.  Until recently, Luftwanzza's business class has had a pretty poor reputation. But things started  to look up when they finally introduced their new custom Aliegris business class product.  According to Luftwanzza, this travel experience has been thought through right down to the smallest  detail. And passengers will enjoy more flexibility, more comfort, and more privacy.  This past March, I finally had the opportunity to try Aliegris out for myself. A booked-in-award flight  through Air Canada for 70,000 points, plus almost 79 Canadian dollars in taxes and fees.  Right after booking, I went to select my seat, and it's definitely not as straightforward as it should be.  There are five different kinds of seats in business class, and each of the five has a different  price tag. Honestly, it's very confusing, and I can't understand why Luftwanzza would opt to do  it this way. Later in the video, I'll discuss this in greater detail and show you each category  with its corresponding price. But for now, I'll just let you know that I selected a privacy seat  for 210 Canadian dollars, or 150 US dollars. My flight wasn't departing until almost 11 pm,  but I headed to the airport early so I could enjoy dinner at the United Polaris lounge.  I was able to access the Polaris lounge because Luftwanzza is a star alliance carrier,  and so is United. And according to United's access rules, people flying business class on a  star alliance member airline can access the lounge at their departure airport. I had the Uber  drop me at Terminal 1, the terminal that handles United and almost all of the other star alliance flights.  Business class passengers received priority check-in and boarding. It's worth noting though that  Luftwanzza agents aren't there until a few hours before departure. Luckily, I already had my boarding  pass and was traveling carry-on only, so I was able to head straight to security. After security,  I made my way to the Polaris lounge. My flight was leaving from the same concourse as security,  concourse B, but the lounge is in concourse C, so I made my way from B to C with the underground  pedestrian tunnel. It's a quick and enjoyable trip due to the moving walkways and colorful neon lights.  At the end of the tunnel, take the escalator back up, and you'll see the Polaris lounge across  from the escalators on the left-hand side. I recently did a full review of the newly renovated and  expanded Polaris lounge, so if you're interested in that, I'll put a link in the description below.  But for now, here's a quick look.  My time in the lounge flew by, and before I knew it, it was time to head to my gate.  When I arrived at the gate, I was surprised to see a huge line of people extending a  surprisingly long distance from the gate. They had one agent at the front of the line doing an  extra security check of each person's boarding pass and passport. The line was moving very slowly,  and everybody seemed confused about whether they needed to be in the line or not. As people finally  made it through that line, they were being ushered into small boarding groups that seemed completely  random. My boarding pass said group two, but there were no signs or announcements about boarding  groups, and instead, I'm fairly certain that people were just being grouped together randomly.  And while there, boarding passes and passports were checked again. As I finally found myself  heading down the jet bridge, I was hoping that this chaotic start to the journey wasn't a sign of  things to come. Thankfully, as you'll see, things improved greatly once we were on board.  As we make our way onto the plane, let's check out the seat map. Our flight today is on one of  lift-hands's 835900s. The aircraft is equipped with an economy cabin of 201 Recaro CL 3710  slimline seats, arranged in a 3x3x3 configuration. Each seat has a width of 18 inches, a recline of  5 inches, and a rope hitch of 31 inches. The premium economy cabin offers 24 Zim privacy PCO2  recliner seats, arranged in a 2x3x2 configuration. Each seat features a winged four-way adjustable  headrest and an adjustable legrest, and has a back show with a slide-forward mechanism that  allows passengers to recline up to 7 inches. The seated self is 19.5 inches wide with a rope hitch  of 39 inches. The aircraft also offers a very small first-class cabin with a total of three  suites. The cabin can accommodate up to four passengers, though, because the middle suite can be  used for a single passenger or a couple. Each stalea suite is completely enclosed with sealing  height partitions and a privacy door, and features a personal wardrobe, large dining table,  and temperature control seats using a cooling system from Canova that enables passengers to  control the temperature in their suites. Finally, the aircraft is equipped with two business class  cabins offering a total of 38 stalea seats, and here's where the confusion begins. As I mentioned  before, there are five different seat types to choose from, and they all carry different price  tags. It's maybe the most confusing seat map and range of options that I've ever encountered,  so stick with me. First of the classic seats which you can book free of charge, these seats don't  offer much privacy, and most of the window options aren't aligned with the windows, so you'll have  little to no view. The lifelad length is 74.8 inches. There are 12 of these seats including 4C, 4D,  4H, 6C, 6G, 6H, 10C, 10D, 10H, 12C, 12G, and 12H. It's worth noting that seats 12C and 12H  offer a bit more counter space and better window alignment, but you will be over the wing.  Next are the privacy seats which had a booking fee of $150 on my flight. These are all windows seats  that offer more privacy than the classic seats, as well as better views. The length and the  lifelad position is a few inches more at 78.7 inches. The privacy seats include seats 3A, 3K, 5A, 5K, 7A, 7K,  9A, 9K, 11A, and 11K. The extra long bed seats are the third option, and on my flight they were  going for the same price as the privacy seats, $150. As the name suggests, these seats offer a  slightly deeper foot while with a lifelad length of 86 inches. But that's the only thing that  sets them apart. They are basically slightly longer classic seats. If you need the extra length,  though, you'll find this option with seats 4G, 60, 10G, and 12D. Four, they're the extra space  seats which are also referred to as throne seats, and on my flight they were going for $185.  While the privacy is great with these seats, it's worth noting that they actually have narrower  foot walls compared to the other seats, and are more pinched at the shoulders. Like the privacy  seats, the length and the lifelad position is 78.7 inches. If you want one of these seats, they're  located in the center of the cabin with excess alternating between the two aisles, seats 3E, 5F, 9E,  and 11F. Finally, the fifth and most expensive option is the business suite. A my flight you had  to pay a whopping $550 to reserve one. This option has a taller privacy enclosure and closing door,  and features a 24-inch 4K IFE screen. The lifelad seat length is once again 78.7 inches.  The business suites are in the front rows of both cabins, seats 2A, 2D, 2G, and 2K in the front cabin,  and 8A, 8D, 8G, and 8K in the rear cabin. The seat I had purchased was 5K, a private window seat  in the front cabin. With all that out of the way, let's head on.  We boarded the plane between the two business class cabins with the front cabin to my left and the  rear cabin to my right. Here we are, seat 5K. I was immediately impressed by how tucked away the seat  looked very private. This generous countertop and storage space provide a nice separation between  the seat and the aisle. There was a large pillow on my seat, as well as a pretty thick blanket,  and slippers were waiting on the footrest. I sat down to have a better look around,  as you can see there's plenty of legroom, and I have three windows. Gotta love that.  On my other side there's a handy storage locker. Inside headphones and a menadiquit in a bottle  of water were already waiting for me when I sat down, but there's extra room for a few personal  items too. If you like, there's a sliding door to better secure the items during flight.  On the lower front panel, you'll find a universal power outlet and a USB charging port.  Speaking of charging, there's also wireless charging on the side table. If you're looking for seat  controls, the basic options are right above the armrest. One of my favorite parts of the new seat  is the tray table, which is stored right under the IFE screen. It unfolds to create a very large,  very solid table. And it's so easily adjustable, you can just push it all the way forward if you  need to exit your seat during meal service. Speaking of foods, you may have noticed that when I  arrived, the small paper bag was already here. It's a small package of mixed nuts that says,  you're welcome moment. The flight attendant also came by to offer me a pre-departure drink.  She offered water, stillersbarkling, champagne, or Lufthansa's signature aperitif avionic,  which is what I selected. There's no detailed information on exactly what's in it,  but it is described as a refreshing, fruity, complex blend with peach notes, wild metal herbs,  and a bitter acidic finish typically mixed with tonic water. It was fruity and refreshing,  and I will say it's quite good. Continuing on with the seat tour, the armrests can be lowered  all the way down for sleeping, or raised up for sitting. One thing I was very happy about was  this individual air vent, which I could point at myself, especially given that there are no air vents  up above. I've already mentioned the basic seat controls, but there are many additional controls  that can be accessed through this 10-inch tablet. In addition to making fine adjustments to the seat  position, you can use the tablet to control both the temperature and the firmness of your seat.  I wish all airlines offered this. The tablet also allows you to control the lights.  You can use it well docked or take it out to operate.  It can also be used to control the iFe touchscreen, which I'll show you later.  And speaking of in-flight entertainment, the 8KG noise-canceling headphones can be plugged in right here.  If you're flying with Lufthansa, you should be able to view the menu online before your flight,  but if you don't have time, no worries, because they'll also pass out physical menus.  For my flight, everyone would be receiving the same appetizer, but there were three main courses  to choose from. Barbecue chicken thigh with mashed potatoes and corn, shrimp curry with jasmine  rice, or calenced wheat potato croquettes with a ferro salad and roasted vegetables.  They also offer champagne, white wine, rosé wine, red wine, spirits, lakurs, hot beverages,  beer, and non-alcoholic cold beverages. After I told the flight attendant that I wanted the  barbecue chicken for my main course, I decided to check out the amenity kit. The items are in a  zippered navy blue pouch. Inside I found a refreshing towel, ear plugs, and I mask,  a dental kit with a toothbrush and toothpaste, a pair of socks, a peppermint,  a headphone ear covers, and a little package of luxiton products,  with hand cream and lip balm inside. All in all, a pretty nice selection of amenities.  With boarding completed, the overhead bins were closed and we were told to prepare for departure.  The safety video began to play. In the ambient lights were turned off,  followed by all the cabin lights as we started making our way to the runway.  In case you're like me, you might be interested to know that Lufthansa's A3-5900 has five  external cameras that allow you to follow live, how the aircraft is moving, and what the surroundings  look like. This is especially nice for passengers not sitting at a window. Since I had a window  seat, I opted for a direct view, but it was raining, so the views were not ideal.  Nevertheless, I always enjoy watching the takeoff.  The  Once we reached a cruising elevation, I changed into my slippers and turned my attention to the  InFlight Entertainment. The IFE screen for my seat is a pretty average 18 inches,  but 4K resolution is nice to have. You can use the screen as a touch screen to  baruse all the options, which include movies, TV shows, music, audiobooks, podcasts, games,  e-journals, and editorial content. While navigating directly on the touch screen works,  most people find it more convenient to use the tablet. In terms of content, Lufthansa does  well here, especially in terms of movies. They offer over 300 movies and break things down into  12 subcategories, so it's easy to find something you're interested in. I'm glad the InFlight  Entertainment is good because the internet situation is not ideal. Lufthansa's on-board internet  services fly net, and while InFlight Entertainment in messaging our complimentary, normal internet usage  is not. On my flight, the price was 15 euro for two hours of Wi-Fi, or 25 euros for the full flight.  I skipped the internet and settled on an episode of Friends instead.  Dinner service began with a wet towel, followed quickly by a shrimp amuse bush, which was quite nice.  Next, my first course in main course arrived together. With this being such a late night flight,  I actually appreciated this because it helps speed things up and ensure more time for sleeping.  My first course was grilled artichoke with quinoa salad, goat cheese crumbles, and pomegranate seeds.  And honestly, it was delicious. The artichoke was tender and well seasoned, and the balance of  flavors was fantastic. The combination of goat cheese and pomegranate seeds is a winner in my book.  The main course, as I mentioned earlier, was barbecue chicken thigh with onion mashed potatoes and  roasted corn, pepper, and carrot. While not as delicious as my salad, the dish wasn't bad at all.  I think it qualifies as comfort food, which, on a flight, is a good thing in my book.  As I continued watching Friends, the flight attendant cleared my tray and delivered the dessert.  A souffle cheesecake with mixed berry sauce. And a milk chocolate candy bar as well.  I really enjoyed the cheesecake. It was much lighter than I expected. Fluffy with a light  airy consistency, perfect as a late night snack. With inner surface over, the flight  attendants prepared the cabin for sleeping. I was able to easily convert my seat into a  lifelap bed. While I would have liked a mattress pad, the pillow and blanket were both nice and  substantial. And once I climbed in, I could tell that the leg room was very generous.  I used the tablet to adjust the seat's firmness and temperature.  And then tried to get some much-needed rest.  When I woke up, the morning sun was shining brightly and the flight attendant stopped by with a  wet towel. I ordered a cup of coffee, put my seat back in the upright position,  and headed off to the lavatory. The lavatories for business class are located between the two  cabins. It's a little surprising that there are only two lavatories for 38 business class passengers.  But despite this, I was really impressed with what I saw. The lavatory was clean and had a premium  feel to it. The wooden leather accents are unique touches that add some warmth to the feel of the  space. The lighting is also nice and bright and I appreciate the inclusion of a small makeup  mirror. In addition to L'Occitane hand cream, I found individual bottles of mouthwash and refreshing  towels. And finally, I'm always happy to see a touch refosit and a pedal-operated garbage flap.  When I got back to my seat, I saw that my coffee had already arrived. Just a couple of minutes later,  breakfast was served. As with dinner, the meal arrived all at once rather than in courses,  and it was the same meal for all passengers. In addition to coffee, I received cold cuts,  double-in-er cheese, cream cheese, and grapes in a small bowl, Greek yogurt with mixed berry  compound, and a choice of bread roll along with butter. I selected a croissant. I was a little  surprised that there were no hot items like eggs, but everything was pretty good. I especially enjoyed  the yogurt with berry compound, and who doesn't love a croissant with butter? I actually wasn't very  hungry since I'd eaten dinner so late, so this light meal was actually just right.  After breakfast was cleared, the flight attendants passed out small boxes of chocolate.  A little memento of the flight, which I thought was a nice touch.  As we make our approach in landing in Munich, what did I think of my experience in  Lufthansa's Allegres Business Class? Did it meet my expectations? And with this new product,  does Lufthansa now a true competitor in the business class market? For the most part, I would say yes,  Lufthansa has really stepped up its game with their new Allegres Business Class. I actually think  Lufthansa is finally a real contender if you're selecting a European airline. The Allegres cabin is  attractive, and my particular seat was very private and comfortable. I also loved having a tablet  that controls so many things, including seat firmness and temperature. In terms of dining,  both meals were pretty good. While not exactly gourmet, meal service was efficient, and the food  itself was tasty. And finally, the service throughout my flight was friendly and proactive.  The crew definitely tried to make our time aboard as pleasant as possible.  But as nice as the flight experience itself was, there are a couple of big negatives that I really  wish Lufthansa would address. First and foremost, I really dislike the confusing seating chart with  five different options, each of which carries a different price tag. Why would they choose this  multi-seat selection model for their new business class? At best, it's incredibly confusing to  customers who are forced to research the options into a cost-benefit analysis for each seat type.  At worst, it feels like Lufthansa is trying to squeeze extra money from passengers who have  already paid a high price for a premium experience. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to the X-Pro Stay Channel.  Today, we are taking you along on Turkish Airlines flight 1888 Taka's from Vienna to Istanbul,  flying on the spacious Airbus A330.  If you're curious about the airport lounge experience in Vienna before we take off,  make sure to check out the dedicated lounge video right here on our channel.  Honestly, the flight was absolutely fantastic from start to finish.  Right after boarding, it was great to see that we received comfortable pillows, blankets,  and our own complimentary headphones for the flight.  As we cruised, I explored the Inflite Entertainment System.  The movie selection is massive, featuring everything from the latest blockbusters and  popular animations to a great mix of music and TV shows.  There is easily enough content to keep you entertained for hours.  Another huge highlight was the onboard catering.  For such a short flight, we actually had a choice between two different hot meals.  Turkish Airlines is truly amazing for this, because getting a proper, delicious meal in  economy class is a rare luxury these days. During the flight, I also visited the  lavatory and was really pleased to see how nicely clean and well maintained it was,  complete with good quality hand soap and lotion. It's always a big plus when an airline keeps  up with cleanliness mid-flight.  The only minor detail that didn't work was the connecting gate info screen,  which was supposed to display our transfer gates for Istanbul Airport.  Luckily, navigating the beautiful Istanbul terminal upon arrival was still very smooth.  To wrap things up, this Turkish Airlines flight from Vienna to Istanbul on the Airbus A330  was an absolute pleasure. From the great comfort pillows and headphones provided at the start,  to the spotless lavatory and the massive movie selection, they really know how to take care  of their passengers. Plus, getting a choice of two delicious hot meals on such a short economy flight  is something you rarely see these days. Despite the minor glitch with the connecting gate screen,  I highly recommend flying with them. Thank you for watching, and don't forget to subscribe to  XproStay for more travel reviews.

chapters.title: Check In and Upper Class Wing

reviews.transcript_full: Economy, Premium Economy, and three different versions of upper class.  What's the difference in all three cabins on version Atlantic, and is it worth paying for those more premium cabins?  After flying all five of those main seat types, day and breaking down what to expect in each class from the ground experience,  to the seats, the onboard dining, drinks and overall experience.  So let's start with the experience on the ground at Check-in.  Economy, Premium Economy, and upper class each have their own separate check-in areas, with typically shorter cues in those higher cabin categories.  luggage allowance is also differ with no check luggage for economy light, 23 kilos for economy classic or economy delight,  223 kilo bags for premium economy, and 232 kilo bags for upper class.  All upper class passengers and those with gold status can also make use of the upper class wing when departing from Heathrow,  which is a separate area that you can arrive in if travelling by car.  But also accessible by those using the main check-in area, via a lift that takes you to the private security area to skip the main terminal security.  Once you're all checked in and through security, economy and premium economy passengers will be killing time in the terminal,  whereas upper class passengers get access to the excellent clubhouse lounge.  The flagship clubhouse lounge at Heathrow is in lounge location H, just above the American Airlines lounge,  and can be accessed via the stairs or the lift if you fancy a sit-down for two seconds.  At the entrance you'll be warned and greeted and then it's on into the lounge.  The clubhouse has a variety of comfortable seating areas,  a dining area, a full bar, relaxation spaces, and my favourite feature, the outdoor terrace.  Over at the dining area, full alacart meals and snacks are ordered via the menus with the very friendly staff that work in here,  or you can order via the QR codes.  But you're not just limited to the dining area, you'll actually find these QR codes in all seating areas  to order food and drinks to wherever you're seated.  There's a good selection available and I've also always found the quality to be excellent.  You'll also find an extensive menu of high-quality cocktails, which is greatly appreciated alongside coffees,  soft drinks, and unique options like electrolyte drinks to stay hydrated.  The staff that work in this lounge are really great too, very attentive, friendly,  and provide great table service in all spaces at the lounge.  Overall, a really lovely place to spend a couple of hours before a flight.  Outside of Heathrow, you'll also find a couple of other clubhouses available in the US,  such as the one that I've visited in Washington,  dollars, and you can also make use of Skyteam partner lounges, such as those operated by Delta.  It is worth mentioning too that you can also access a lounge at the end of your trip,  arriving into Heathrow, you'll have access to the Revival's lounge.  This is accessed after clearing immigration and customs and comes complete with lots of  great showers, a dining area where you can order an alacart breakfast and coffee,  and it's a great place to just freshen up and refuel after an overnight flight.  But pack to the start of your journey and once it's time to board, this is done by a group number.  A per class all those with gold status were bored first, followed by premium economy and then economy.  So let's get on board and take a look at the different seat types and lawn boards service available.  One thing you'll notice in all cabins is that you'll almost certainly have very pink lighting  going on to hide what can be some quite ugly seats in some of the configurations.  But aside from the lighting, the cabins are each very different.  We'll start with the seats in economy, where there are actually a couple of different types.  In addition to the standard seats, you can pay to select an economy to light seats,  which offers about 3 inches of extra legroom.  Or alternatively, you can do what I would personally do and go for the exyro seats.  I would tend to struggle on a longer flight if I didn't at least have the legroom you get from  economy to light. The seats themselves are nice, nothing too revolutionary that would make them  stand out above economy seats on other airlines, but they are pretty much every feature you'd want  or expect in economy. There's a tray table that folds out, a seat pocket, an adjustable headrest,  a slight bit of recline, reading lights and air vents, and some good charging available.  We also get a pretty good infight entertainment system that will look at properly once in the air.  Up in premium economy, you'll find a wider and much more spacious seats with plenty of legroom  for all rows. The seat has a large and clear entertainment screen, a pretty rubbish in seat pocket,  an additional small storage space under the armrest, which unlike in economies and armrests that  you don't have to share with the passenger next to you, you've also got loads of great charging  options available in this one. And of course you have a tray table that folds out from one of the  armrests. As in economy you have an adjustable headrest, but the recline here is much more generous,  which can be a double edged sword when the first in front of you reclines and you lose a lot of your  space. The seat also has a fairly useless legrest and an okay fullrest. It's overall a decent  premium economy seat, significantly better than economy, but there are better premium economy seats  out there. Now at the front of the plane in upper class we have three very different seat types.  We'll go from oldest to newest. The oldest version known by summer's coffin class can be found  on Virgin 787s and their older A through 30s. It's a very dated business class product with a narrow  herring bone layout that faces inwards and away from the window. You're very close to your seat  neighbors here and if you don't select the A seats at the left of the cabin you'll be facing  towards potentially a stranger or staring at their feet for the half-light. The inflight entertainment  screening this one is small and dated and it's also in a bit of an awkward position to make  it difficult to leave it deployed at the same time as using the tray table, which comes out of  this side compartment. The tray table though is a good size, nice and sturdy and it can be slid  away from you to be able to gow with the seat whilst it's deployed. Storage in the seat is very  limited, just a small cubby under the IFE screen and a shell fob of your shoulder. For charging  you'll find one universal outlet and a USB port. This seat doesn't have the best recline and it  can't be reclined fully flat. For the bed mode the seat actually flips forward into a live flat  position, more on that later. The A350 seats is a big improvement on this and features a much more  modern reverse herring bone layout and a more modern overall design. Storage is still a bit limited  with a focus on shelves over enclosed storage spaces which is not the most practical decision.  The seat has good legroom though, an excellent inflight entertainment system and a slightly  unusual tray table design that deploys from the side wall.  See the sides will get into just a alarm rest and then rather than having a proper closing door  like you have on a lot of modern business class seats, you instead get a small privacy screen  which doesn't really do much. Good charging available including universal outlets and USB ports,  and the seat itself is comfortable enough and certainly an improvement on premium economy and  coffin class. But it's not the most comfortable overall when compared to other business class seats.  There's no headrest which is a shame and I found the reclined and seat adjustment buttons to  not work great and some of these seats are showing some serious wear in tear at this point.  The seats on the A313900 Nios has virgins most modern and it might be best business class seats.  You get a private suite with a closing door, a more comfortable seat, a nice size the modern  IFE screen, great charging options in the form of a wireless charging pad, universal outlet,  USB-A and USB-C ports. But again like the other seats storage is still pretty limited.  The tray table is deployed from the side console and in even row seats which sit closer to the  window you can't get out of your seat with the tray table deployed. So pick an order row seat which  is closer to the aisle if that's important to you. Another slight limitation here is the seat  controls and adjustability which like the seats on the A350, I struggled with a bit to get into  position that I wanted. Once settled into your seat the pre-departure service can begin.  So what kind of service can you expect pre-departure in each cabin? Well in economy you get nothing  apart from a safety video. In premium economy you will get a pre-departure sparkling wine or juice  or water and of course you'll also get this in upper class.  Virgin do also provide some additional service items that are root dependent. For example they  provided dates and Saudi coffee on their now cancelled rehab routes.  Orders from the menu might be taken pre-departure in upper class but this isn't always the case  and you can actually pre-order meals in all classes of travel. More on that will become  onto the food. Different levels and amenities will also be provided pre-departure in each cabin.  In economy you'll find a basic blanket, pillow and a pretty rubbish set of headphones.  In premium economy you'll find better versions of those items. Plus a basic  amenity kit with things like a toothbrush and toothpaste but those are only provided on overnight  flights. And as with economy you'll also get a pretty rubbish set of headphones.  In upper class you'll get a proper amenity kit or goody bag as they call it and what's the bag  itself is nothing exciting it does have some good contents including nice products and rent,  a moisturizer, hand cream and a lip balm. On overnight flights pajamas will also be provided  although I've found that you can sometimes ask for these on daytime flights too.  Headphones are provided here too and whilst these ones aren't amazing they are a significant  upgrade from what you get in economy and premium economy. But now let's get up in the sky  and see the differences in the on-board service, the food and drink and what each seat is like for sleep.  What's up in the air the drink service will shortly start in each cabin.  Back in economy you're offered drinks from the trolley including beer, wine and spirits served  in a plastic cup alongside a light snack. In premium you'll get a physical menu listing the beer,  wine, spirits and many soft drinks available and you'll also get the choice of one cocktail.  Drinks are served in a proper glass and are accompanied by the same nibbles that you get in  economy. You'll also get a hot towel but it's more like a wet wipe than a towel.  In upper class the on-board service starts with a proper hot towel before the drinks are served.  The drinks menu here is more extensive and includes cocktails,  lorant perier champagne, a good spirit selection including cognac,  plus plenty of non-acoholic mocktails, teas and coffees. Drinks are served alongside a pot of  crisps. It might not give as premium the feeling as the warm nuts that you might get in other  airlines but they are tasty and I've always found that the crew are really on the ball when it comes  to drink top-ups as well. I've never sat with an empty or even slightly low glass for long before  the crew are back around to ask if they can get me another. But once that drink service is complete  it's time to get started on the meals. Now as I mentioned earlier in all cabin classes meals can  be pre-ordered, yes even in economy. This means you don't need to worry about not getting what you  want if you sat further back in the cabin. Plus in upper class there are additional items available  for pre-order that you'll not find on the inflight menu. But what can you actually expect from  these meals in each class? Well in economy meals are all served on one small tray and portion  sizes are fairly light. Alongside the main course you can expect a couple of side dishes like a  small salad, some basic biscuits and cheese and a dessert pot. To accompany the meal you'll also  be offered water plus beer or wine which is served in a can. Now this meal might not look  like lunch but this was actually really tasty and impressive quality for economy just a bit of a  small portion size. In premium economy meals are also served on one tray but the presentation is  slightly elevated with the use of proper crockery and cutlery. Plus you'll get a silver version of  the iconic virgin Atlantic salt and pepper shakers. Food quality in premium is very good and the starter,  the cheese and dessert are all bigger and better than what you get in economy. Still quite a  light portion for the main course though. In upper class your table is set with either a proper  tablecloth or a small purple mat depending on the aircraft type. And you'll be served bread  and butter whilst waiting for the starter. The table will also include the gold version of those  iconic salt and pepper shakers. To start I've actually always come for the soup which has been  absolutely delicious and the main courses have also been really tasty for me. Virgin tend to  lead them more towards comfort food than anything fancy so although the meal options won't sound  particularly elevated compared to some of rail lines it has all at least been high quality in my  experience and I've always cleared my plate. For dessert you can expect quite a small and tasty  bite like a sticky tougher pudding and you'll also be able to get a cheese course.  Between meals I've not been offered additional snacks in economy but I believe they will have  some in the galley if you get hungry. In premium though you get access to the wander wall.  An airy in the galley that is well stocked with a greater salt amount of snacks and drinks to  help yourself to throughout the flight. Whereas in upper class you'll have access to a lounge or  bar space. These are great in theory as it is fantastic to have a separate place to go that's  away from your seat where you can socialise. And these are usually stopped with drinks and snacks  but I do find that pretty underutilised and I've never actually been on a flight where anyone  has sat in these and if you don't want to head over there for snacks the crew will also come  through the cabin with things on occasion. For example on one of my flights they did bring me some  sorbet. You will also get a second meal service on your flights but on daytime flights this will  almost always be virgin to mile high tea which is delivered slightly differently in each cabin.  In economy this has served in a box and ingredients are a little more limited and basic  but really excellent as far as the second meal service for economy goes. In premium the quality  items like the scones, the jam and the other treats were noticeably better than in economy.  And then further up in upper class things are definitely presented a bit better and I do like  the virgin Atlantic mucks but I will say the food wasn't significantly different from what they  serve in premium and I couldn't really tell much difference between the two. Not sure whether to  count that as a positive for the premium service or a negative for the upper service. Either way though  it was very nice and a good second meal and obviously no matter what cabin you're in you'll of  course go with the cream before the jam on your scope. A quick word about Inflite Entertainment.  Generally the better the cabin you're in the better the screen but there is some variation  across the aircraft types. Virgin generally have a really great selection of films and TV shows  and a very good Inflite Entertainment system overall. Wi-Fi is available but it's at a very  steep cost on some flights however virgin are rapidly rolling out Starlink Wi-Fi and at the time  of recording in June 2026 all of their A350s now offer free Starlink. As mentioned earlier headphones  are provided in all cabins but they're not the best quality however the A330 and Nio's will allow  you to use your own earphones via Bluetooth. What about sleep? In economy you do get the pillow  blanket and a slight recline but I'd be seriously struggling to sleep here. Premium economy definitely  gives more of a recline and a better blanket plus some over-night amenities like an i-mask but the  pillow isn't very good and it is a bit lumpy. For the best chance of a good sleep you're going to want  that life-flat seat in upper class. In upper class you can change into your provider pajamas which are  very comfortable and actually do wear them at home sometimes. The crew will proactively offer to set  up your bed and in the old coffin class seat the seat folds forward to create a life-flat bed  so if you can't quickly and easily transition from life-flat to recline door fights first.  The bed here is on the narrow and firm side but I've managed to sleep okay in it. It won't be a  comfortable choice for wide passengers and anyone told them six foot will likely struggle with this  bed length. In the A350 I found the bed comfortable and spacious but it is worth noting that I was in  the bulkhead which does have a bit of a wider foot could be so this will be a bit more restricted  further back. In the A313900neo seats I found the bed very comfortable to sleep on my side but  lying on my back it definitely felt a bit on the narrow side so no issues if you're  a side sleep like me but if you do like sleeping back again it might be a bit of a struggle if you  are a bit wide. Next up let's talk about the service from the crew. Throughout the flight you  can expect great and friendly service from the cabin crew. In each of my fights we're verging in  every class the crew have really impressed me but especially in premium and upper class.  On these flights they've always been very attentive checking in regularly to see  there's anything else they can get me whenever I've finished a drink or had something to eat.  And I'm yet to encounter a single member of Virgin cabin crew who hasn't been  incredible friendly. I'm sure they must exist out there but I'm just yet to personally experience  that and it's that service both on the ground and on board that makes me very happy to fly with  Virgin above some other airlines who might have better seats. If you're going to be flying with  Virgin overall which cabin to book will a lot of the time come down to cost or availability of  saver and walled seats if you're using Virgin points. It's difficult for me to say definitively  if one is worth your money over the other without knowing your personal financial circumstances  which of the elements is discussed you value the most and what the specific price differences are  on your routes and dates. Virgin's pricing is variable and demand-driven so there are times you'll  see premium economy fair for example be extortionally higher than economy and at other times it might  only be quite a small price difference. But hopefully this video at least gives you a clear  understanding of the differences in each cabin to make a decision on which one to go for based on  pricing you're presented with and if you'd like to see how this compares to each class of travel  on British Airways go ahead and watch this video next. Thanks for watching.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, in early February 2025! Heading toward Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Terminal 2, which opened in 2018. Today, we're flying on China Southern Airlines flight CZ 381 from Guangzhou to Brisbane, Australia. China Southern, Asia's largest airline, operates a massive fleet of 700 aircraft—with Guangzhou as its main hub. Checking out the China Southern Lounge in the international departures area. It scores a 6 out of 10 — a bit small and cramped. China Southern operates a fleet of 20 Airbus A350-900 aircraft on long-haul routes to Europe and Australia. Our aircraft for tonight's flight to Brisbane: an Airbus A350-900 (registration: B-32AV), delivered in October 2022. Boarding for flight CZ 381 begins at 20:07 at gate A147, 48 minutes ahead of our scheduled departure. Stepping into China Southern's Airbus A350-900 Business Class cabin, featuring a 1-2-1 zigzag seating configuration. The cabin offers a total of 28 lie-flat beds, giving everyone direct aisle access. Settling into seat 9A. It's a window seat featuring a great privacy divider between the galley and the lie-flat bed. Aircraft doors close right on time at 20:42 as the safety video begins to play. An in-flight security officer — known as a "Fangbao" — is seated right behind me, equipped with a bodycam. Fangbaos stay with the plane at outstations like Brisbane and fly right back to China, which is why they are seated in Business Class. Pushback begins at 20:49, 6 minutes ahead of our scheduled 20:55 departure. Taxiing out to Guangzhou's Runway 01R, which stretches 3,600 meters (11,811 feet). Taking off from Guangzhou at 21:12 China Standard Time. It's a surprisingly chilly night for the tropics, sitting at just 10°C. At 7,300 km, this is a short route for the A350 (15,750 km max range) — making for a very light, easy takeoff roll. Goodbye Guangzhou and Mainland China! Listen to the magnificent roar of the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines, each capable of producing 84,000 lbf of max thrust. China Southern selected the Recaro CL6710 model for its Business Class cabin. The seat extends into a fully lie-flat bed reaching up to 208 cm (approx. 6'10") in length. The great-circle distance between Guangzhou and Brisbane is 7,062 km, with a scheduled gate-to-gate block time of 9 hours and 20 minutes. Dinner service begins 40 minutes after takeoff at 21:52, starting with an amuse-bouche. The appetizer cart arrives at 22:10, offering pork pâté with mango salad or a prawn and chicken salad alternative. Cruising smoothly directly over Manila, Philippines. The main course — a Western option of beef with potatoes — is served at 22:16. The dessert cart comes around at 22:41 with a choice of fresh fruit, cheese, or ice cream. The entire four-course dinner concludes by 22:52 — just 1 hour and 40 minutes after takeoff. That is remarkably swift service. Economy Class features 307 seats in a standard 3-3-3 layout. Note that Premium Economy is not available on this configuration. Checking out the IFE. There is a decent selection of Western movies, but it doesn't quite match Emirates or Singapore Airlines. At 00:57 — 4 hours and 45 minutes into the flight — we are just about to cross the equator over the Maluku Islands in the Halmahera Sea. Watch the latitude value in the lower right corner of the flight tracking app flip from positive to negative! With La Niña in full swing in early 2025, this equatorial region around Indonesia is packed with remarkably powerful thunderstorms. Cruising through a turbulent Intertropical Convergence Zone tonight over the Arafura Sea, right between Western New Guinea and Australia. The pilots are constantly navigating around severe thunderstorm cells over the Gulf of Carpentaria. Anyone getting Air France flight AF447 vibes? First signs of daylight approaching at 03:30 China Standard Time. Flying over Northern Queensland, Australia. Time to set our clocks 2 hours forward, transitioning from China Standard Time to Australian Eastern Standard Time. The cabin crew begins serving breakfast at 05:50 — a full 1 hour and 45 minutes before landing. That feels a bit too early. Once again, opting for the hot Western option featuring an omelette, sausages, and baked beans. Total sleep time is just 5 hours between the end of dinner and the start of breakfast—a bit too short for a proper rest. The seatbelt signs switch back on at 07:00, 35 minutes before arrival. Chinese regulations mandate that all seats must be fully upright at the top of descent, significantly cutting down on flatbed relaxation time. That said, the 5-minute mood lighting show to wake up the cabin is a really nice feature by China Southern. Cloudy skies outside. February brings the rainy season here during the Southern Hemisphere's summer. Flying over Bribie Island with a view looking out toward the Sunshine Coast. Moreton Island stands in the background as the aircraft makes a turn over Moreton Bay. Lining up for Brisbane's Runway 19R, which is 3,300 meters (10,827 feet) long. Welcome to Brisbane Airport, Queensland, Australia! It's now 07:35 Australian Eastern Standard Time, marking a total flight time of 8 hours and 23 minutes. Taxiing toward Brisbane Airport's International Terminal. Despite the early wake-up call, this was definitely a dream flight in a modern, luxurious Business Class product between two amazing destinations. With ongoing terminal modernizations, the immigration, customs, and biosecurity checkpoints were a bit of an unpleasant zoo. Stepping out into the warm, tropical Australian air here at the Brisbane Airport station. Catching the Gold Coast Line train from the airport down to Helensvale, which takes around 90 minutes. Queensland Rail trains operate on a distinct narrow-gauge system (1,067 mm). Transferring at Helensvale to the G:link tram to reach our final destination: Surfers Paradise. Enjoy some beach impressions from the Gold Coast, stretching from Surfers Paradise down to Tweed Heads! What do you think about China Southern Airlines, especially their long-haul premium product? Let me know in the comments below. Thanks for watching! Please subscribe to my channel, doc7austin's DreamlinerCentral.

reviews.transcript_full: Greetings everyone from Kuala lumpur international airport. Thank you for joining us! Today we're experiencing Singapore Airlines business class on their shortest route, from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore. Singapore Airline deliver outstanding service—whether it's the cabin setup, the meals, or the overall service. So, can they still keep up the great service? Let's check it out together. This is the T1 Satellite Building. It's got this round design, and the gates are spread out in four different directions. There's no Singapore Airlines-operated lounge at Kuala Lumpur airport. Singapore Airlines runs at least 8 daily services,they are always full. Crazy busy! This 5.3‑year‑old Airbus A350‑900 will be taking me to Singapore. The crew's smiles gave me an instant sense of warmth as I boarded. This seat is pretty much the standard now for Singapore Airlines business class. You'll see it on most of their A350s and 787s. There are 40 seats in business class, from row 11 to row 21, with 4 seats per row. Only 40 minutes in the air, but they've still got a pillow and blanket set out for you, nice touch. Small sliding storage with USB and power， ideal for phone, earphones,or other little items. Touchscreen panel for all the controls. Lights, seat adjustment, IFE switch – everything's there. And the icons are so clear, you can't really mess it up." I've got to say, legroom is limited. When I lie flat and bend my knees, always touch the sides. For just rest, fine. But for a longer fligt, that would get uncomfortabl a little. Clever and thoughtful, love this design. Adjustable reading light. The headrest is soft and resilient. The pillow is so fluffy. The tray table is placed right below the screen, so it's really easy to use. And it fits in perfectly with the overall design of the seat. But the only downside is that it takes up a bit of legroom. Welcome drinks included orange juice, apple juice, and water. But since it was breakfast time, no champagne was offered. The crew brought another hot towel. Honestly, that woke me right up. Ambient lighting and reading light on and off. When you're sleeping or just don't want to be disturbed, you can press this button. The flight was so short that the seatbelt sign actually went off just five minutes after takeoff. Honestly, I thought it'd just be a bottle of water and a sandwich – but nope, they brought out a proper light meal and drinks too.  Option one is Japanese-style soba, a light noodle dish. Loved the texture of the noodles - nice and springy. So flavorful.  Option two is a Malaysian-style salad. Fresh ingredients, looks so healthy! Cheers, everyone! Now, let's see how this seat transforms into a bed. Fully flat, great privacy around the head. The only downside is the limited legroom. Full cabin view with Business class. So, do you think this 40‑minute business class flight is worth it? How would you rate the overall experience? Feel free to leave your comments! Looking forward to our next journey together, see you next time !

Shortly after takeoff drinks and snacks were offered and then the meal service began.  For lunch I went for the salmon and rice dish and I have to say it was actually very tasty.  The salmon was nicely cooked, the rice went well with it and overall it was a solid  business class meal for a regional flight.  Was it fine dining, no, was it enjoyable, definitely.  After lunch most of the passengers around me seemed to settle in and go to sleep, the  cabin became fairly quiet and the atmosphere on board was very calm.  With a two-two configuration it was very relaxed up front here.  However I decided to stay awake, partly because I wanted to enjoy the seat and the flight  and partly because I had somehow ended up watching a Russian movie.  Not exactly what I was expecting on a flight from Bangkok to Shanghai but sometimes that's  part of the fun when flying different airlines.  You never quite know what you're going to get.  It was a good film after all.  The entertainment system itself was not modern at all and the content selection was not  anything great apart from said Russian movie.  But for a short haul flight it was enough to pass the time.  There was only one toilet up front for business class passengers but for eight seats that's  a good ratio.  On a Boeing 737 it's pretty snug but it was kept nice and clean.  As we continue towards Shanghai the flight remained smooth and comfortable, the seat made  it easy to relax and the cabin was quiet and the crew continued to check in without  being intrusive.  The views outside became noticeably hazy and foggy.  Now when arriving in large cities in China especially around Shanghai it's easy to wonder  whether that hazes fog humidity, pollution or a mix of everything.  In reality it can be a combination.  Shanghai is a huge busy city and depending on the weather, the season and the air quality  on the day the approach can look quite grey and misty.  So I wouldn't immediately say it was pollution but the haze definitely gave the arrival a  very atmospheric look.  So final thoughts.  This was not the flight I originally booked but it turned out to be a much better experience  than expected.  I started the day with an economy ticket on China Eastern and ended up flying business  class on Shanghai Airlines.  That is what I call a successful check-in desk surprise.  On board Shanghai Airlines the business class cabin was older but still very comfortable.  The beige cabin may not be the most exciting visually but the seat itself was wide, soft  and relaxing.  Would I say this is the best business class product in Asia?  No.  Would I be happy to fly again?  Especially as a free upgrade?  Absolutely.  Sometimes the flight does not need to be flashy to be enjoyable.  Sometimes good service, a comfortable seat, decent food and a bit of luck at check-in  are enough to turn an ordinary journey into a memorable one and this flight from Bangkok  to Shanghai was exactly that.  As always thank you so much for watching please like and subscribe and remember to enjoy  the journey.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back. Today's a big day. We're finally welcoming American Airlines to the channel. Join me as I board Airbus A321neo in first class on a flight from Phoenix to Charlotte where we'll show you the seat and service on this flight. This is one of the newest aircraft in their fleet and it's equipped with their latest first class product, but it's missing a key feature you'll find on Delta and United. This will be a good test of American as we fly out from their hub in Phoenix to Charlotte. Plus, stick around and we'll tell you how much we paid for today's ticket and you can decide if it's worth the upgrade. >> [music] >> Welcome to Arizona. We're starting today at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. There are two main terminals and they're connected landside via the SkyTrain. Terminal 3 is newer and serves Alaska, Delta, JetBlue, and United. Phoenix Sky Harbor is a hub for American and Southwest. Terminal 4 is their home along with all the international flights. American's checking counters are located on level two of the terminal. First class passengers have access to priority check-in and bag drop. And our ticket includes two free checked bags of the 70 lb each. There was a bit of confusion here this morning as they tried to charge me for my bags. So, know what your ticket includes. Sometimes you have to be your own champion. With that out of the way, let's head up to security. All gates in Terminal 4 are connected so you can go through any of the four security checkpoints. The airport posts wait times so you can pick the best option. While the airport was busy, security was very quick today. As is pretty standard with US domestic first class, lounge access is not included. And today, this lounge is so full they won't take day passes either. So, while you can buy a day pass, don't always count on them working. There are several other lounges in Terminal 4 accessible with Priority Pass or American Express Platinum Card. We recently did a lounge showdown in Phoenix and we'll leave a link to that in the description if you'd like to see more. We didn't make it into the Escape Lounge last time we were here, so let's go check it out. American Express has both a Centurion and Escape Lounge located next to gate B21 in Terminal 4. You do need to choose wisely, though. Once you enter one, you cannot swap to the other on the same day. There was quite a line for the Centurion Lounge this morning, and based on our last visit, I'm not surprised. But, no one was in line for the Escape Lounge, and I walked right in. Access is granted to American Express Platinum, Centurion, and select Delta card holders. This is also Priority Pass Lounge. Alternatively, you can buy a day pass for $45 per person in advance or $60 at the door. This lounge is open from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. There's a large bar, most of the drinks are free. Premium spirits are available for purchase. The buffet had a good selection. We were visiting during the changeover from breakfast to lunch. The food comes from the same kitchen as the Centurion Lounge, and in our experience, it's largely the same. There's a self-service espresso machine and drip coffee available. This isn't a huge lounge, but there was plenty of open seating. I settled in a high-back chair with views of the final approach path. There are also some dining tables near the buffet. This lounge features two single occupancy restrooms, which are large. However, there are no showers in the Escape Lounge. The seating capitalized on the great views, and I had a bit too much fun watching the planes land. I even managed to catch our plane. I think the views are actually better here than they were in the Centurion Lounge. Wi-Fi is free, and speeds were decent. The password is posted throughout the lounge. When I first came in around 9:30 a.m., it was a little busy, but this lounge was not hard to find a seat. And actually, it emptied out around 10:00 a.m., being very quiet and pleasant the rest of the time. Overall, I was really impressed with the Escape Lounge. This was the first time I've been in one. When we did our lounge showdown in Phoenix, it was around the same time of the day and week. While the airport was busy, the lounge was calm and quiet. Overall, it was comfortable and dare I say I preferred it to the Centurion Lounge. It was less crowded, the food was pretty much the same and the staff were great. >> [music] >> That was a good lounge, is it? But now it's time to board. Sky Harbor is large, so make sure you plan plenty of time to get to your gate. Our 4-hour and 17-minute flight today takes us 1,771 miles from Phoenix, Arizona to Charlotte, North Carolina on board an Airbus A321 neo in first class. Boarding is done in zones with American's premium loyalty program members following after pre-boarding. First class boards in zone one. The first class cabin has 20 seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. There are also 176 main cabin seats in a 3-3 configuration. 18 of these are main extra. These first class seats are 20 inches wide, have 36.5 inches of pitch and a recline of 5 inches. Overall, the legroom is decent, but similar to other domestic first class products. The headrest is adjustable both up and down and the wings fold in. Each seat has overhead air vents and reading lights. The center armrest flips up to reveal a thin storage compartment. You'll find a universal power outlet in here. Between the seats is a small drink table and an extension table pops out of the front for even more space. There is a USB A port located on the seatback in front along with the device holder. The power output here is low, so if you want to fast charge, use the universal outlet instead. The tray table comes out of the outer armrest and is sturdy. It includes an integrated device holder, which can work in both the half open and fully open modes. >> [music] >> You may have noticed there are no seatback screens. Since there's no IFE, there's plenty of room under the seat in front of you. This is often where some Some the IFE equipment is installed. During the boarding, the flight attendant came by for a pre-departure beverage service. It's a hot one today, so I'm keeping it simple with water, but you can choose other beverages. Boarding wrapped up early and we pushed back. I will admit the red, white, and blue mood lighting was cool. >> [music] [music] >> As we get up to altitude, let's check out the onboard entertainment. As mentioned earlier, there's no IFE system on the plane. American has a BYOD approach and when connected to the onboard Wi-Fi, you can access a library of movies, series, live TV, and audio content. The selection is comparable with other carriers, although they only had partial seasons of TV shows. You do have to watch two long commercials before each video, but the playback was smooth. We had read that they had a moving map feature, but for the life of me, I couldn't find it. I ended up improvising with my phone. Internet is now free for Advantage program members. Download speeds were good, upload was serviceable. Once we leveled off, the flight attendant came by to take drink and meal orders front to back. Service then started with a hot towel, which is always a nice touch in a premium cabin. Drinks and warm nuts came out first, since our baseline drink is a G&T, that's what I got started with. 30 days before your flight, American lets you pre-order your meal online. There were six options to choose from and options for special meals. It's funny that the short rib was on here in two different ways. Options. I ordered the short rib with broccolini and grilled onions. I guess the problem with two similar dishes is I got the other one when I was on board. Not the end of the world, but a mix-up nonetheless. So, my actual meal was the short rib with a twice baked potato. This came with a warm roll, Mediterranean salad of artichoke and stuffed peppers, and a charred romaine salad. In another small mix-up, I did see my neighbor got dressing for the salad and it seems to miss my tray. The meal was a good size, the beef was nice and tender. I was surprised to find two side salads and a roll. The flavors were good, but the presentation wasn't going to win any awards. You may notice something was missing from the tray. Dessert. I was surprised to find out that American actually serves this separately and you get a choice, so that's nice. This is something you typically see in long-haul business class and not in domestic first class. The choices were a fruit and cheese plate or chocolate chip ice cream. I opted for the fruit and cheese plate just to try something different. It was nice to get a choice and for a not sweet option, though the grapes had seen better days. These seats are very similar to the WestJet flight that we reviewed a few weeks ago. We'll put a link in the description if you'd like to check that one out and see how it compares. We're only about halfway through, so let's check out the lavatory. There's one forward lav for the first class cabin. These are a bit small for tall folks like me. I'm 6'4" for reference, but this is a typical narrow-body lav and it was kept clean during our flight. The crew were quick to start service and efficient with the meal, but didn't come through much until we approached Charlotte. I ordered a coffee right after lunch and my empty cup kept me company until our descent. Enjoy the views and I'll see you on the ground to wrap things up. So, that's it. That was our first American Airlines first class flight on this channel on the proper mainline American Airlines. Uh I thought the service was pretty good. Food was better than I expected. The seat was comfortable for a flight of this length. There's plenty of storage and I found the seat was spacious. However, service in the second half of the flight was not proactive. We really didn't see much of the crew after the meal. So, was this premium flight worth the upgrade? Price-wise, American was not the cheapest for this route. My one-way first class ticket connected in Charlotte on my way to Washington, D.C. Delta and United were both about $150 less for this first class ticket from Phoenix to DCA, also with connections. Since Phoenix is an American hub, the other carriers are likely actively undercutting American here. The lack of seatback screens is a unique choice for American. The bring your own device approach is fine and the media selection was decent, but it's not competitive with Delta and United. What do you prefer? Using your own device or having a seatback screen? Let us know in the comments. So, back to our question. Is it worth it? Well, there wasn't anything that made American stand out enough to justify the higher price. Given the choice, we'd probably pick the lower fare on another carrier. The products are just that similar. Thanks for making it to the end. If you enjoyed today's flight, please give us a thumbs up and subscribe to keep up to date with our latest content. You can also check out our channel memberships here and on Patreon, where we post exclusive content that doesn't quite fit the main channel. Thank you for watching. On to the next adventure.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard Emirates’ new Boeing 777 Business Class The video starts with a tour of Emirates' Business Class Lounge  Emirates offers one of the world's best Business Class products  This video covers the full Emirates Business Class experience   This includes Business Class meals, amenities, IFE & flat bed The Emirates Boeing 777 takes us from Dubai to Brussels Keep watching till the end for some stunning drone footage Our journey starts at Atlantis The Royal Hotel in Dubai Emirates Business Class includes free airport transfers  The complimentary limousine service adds extra comfort Emirates operates from Terminal 3 at Dubai International Airport  T3 features a dedicated check-in area for premium passengers  Emirates Business Lounges are located throughout Terminal 3 The airlines' flagship lounge is housed in concourse B I've previously published a full video tour of this lounge The lounge is huge, but still quite crowded during peak hours Emirates’ lounges in Dubai are open 24 hours a day. Our flight to Brussels is departing from Concourse C Emirates also operates a Business Lounge at Concourse C   The lounge features Emirates’ signature Arabian design Large curved windows offer views of the airport apron Comfortable leather chairs fill the spacious seating area The lounge includes a dedicated dining area with buffet The buffet offers a wide selection of hot and cold dishes Guests can enjoy mezze, salads, cheeses, and desserts The Emirates Business Lounge at Concourse C features 2 levels   The upper level offers additional seating areas A second buffet area is also available upstairs We're taken by bus to the remote aircraft stand We pass one Emirates Airbus A380 after another along the way The A380's massive size is incredibly impressive up close Emirates operates the world's largest A380 fleet The A380's wingspan is nearly 80 meters (260 feet) wide The fuselage of the A380 is almost 73 meters (239 feet) long The A380 remains the largest passenger aircraft in service Some Emirates A380s carry more than 600 passengers Emirates also has the world's largest Boeing 777 fleet Emirates' 140 Boeing 777s form the backbone of its network This is the Boeing 777-300ER that will fly us to Brussels Built in 2017, this Boeing 777 has registration code A6-EQH The cabin has 38 Business Class seats in a 1-2-1 layout The cabin is split into two sections: a front cabin and rear cabin The rear cabin (shown here) features seven rows of seats The 1-2-1 layout is a significant upgrade over the previous cabin Some center seats are separated by wide consoles Some seat pairs sit close together without wide console These paired seats are ideal for couples traveling together  Window seats also alternate between two different layout Some window seats are closer to the window, others to the aisle  6A is my Business Class seat for the 7 hour flight to Brussels Each seat is 53 cm (21 in) wide with a 112 cm (44 in) pitch This is the smaller front Business Class cabin, with just 10 seats  A welcome drink is offered (water, juice or Champagne) A hot towel is provided as well to freshen up before the flight Let's have a look at the menu on today's flight Let's explore the amenities while the captain welcomes us Slippers and an eye mask are provided A large pillow and a warm blanket are offered as well Noise-cancelling headphones are available at each seat We're leaving the aircraft stand at 8:20 am (on time departure) Emirates' safety video is shown as we taxi to the runway Emirates Boeing 777's nose camera offers a pilot's-eye view We get more awesome A380 sightings while taxiing What's your favorite aircraft type? Leave a comment We're next in line for takeoff Dubai International Airport (DXB) has two parallel runways Emirates' B777-300ER is powered by two GE90-115B engines The GE90 is one of the world's most powerful jet engines We get some nice views of Dubai after takeoff Can you spot Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building? The Burj Khalifa towers 828 meters (2,717 feet) over the city The tower features a staggering 160 habitable floors Let's have a detailed look at the Emirates Business Class seat The windows feature electronically controlled window shades In front of the seat is a 23-inch (58 cm) HD touchscreen  A wide ottoman and some storage space sit beneath the screen  A multi-purpose console sits beside the seat The console features a reading light, a small shelf, and a minibar  The minibar is stocked with water and snacks A universal AC socket, USB-A and USB-C ports are available The side table has a tablet for the seat & entertainment controls  A panel offers quick-access buttons for seat recline & lighting The tray table folds neatly from the console An aperitif and breakfast is served shortly after takeoff Assorted deli selection: cold cuts, cheese, hard-boiled egg Breakfast is served with fresh cut fruits A self-service bar is located in the front Business Class cabin The bar is stocked with snacks, fruits, and light refreshments Emirates’ B777-300ER features two Business Class lavatories  We get some nice views while cruising over the Persian Gulf Can you recognize this well-known city? It is Kuwait City, the political and economic capital of Kuwait  The entertainment is controlled via touch or via the tablet  Let's explore Emirates' inflight entertainment system Emirates calls its inflight entertainment system ICE ICE stands for Information, Communication and Entertainment Thousands of movies, shows, podcasts and music are available Business passengers enjoy complimentary Wi-Fi access Onboard cameras offer stunning views during the flight The Dubai to Brussels flight covers 5,150 km (3,200 miles) The cabin is kept dark for most of the flight, allowing relaxation  The crew adds a mattress topper to each Business Class seat The topper adds softness and reduces firmness of the seat The seat converts into a spacious 78 inch (200 cm) lie-flat bed The lie-flat bed and its plush padding offer exceptional comfort The bed & footrest offer ample room even for taller passengers Emirates features a fiber-optic starlight ceiling on its Boeing 777  An aperitif starts the dinner service (2 hours prior to landing) Starter: traditional Arabic mezze Houmous, tabouleh, kisir, soslu patlican and lamb kibbeh Main course: salmon, hollandaise sauce, polenta, peas & carrots  Dessert: coffee and almond mousse Post-dessert treat: chocolates The pilot announces our descend towards Brussels Airport Emirates was founded in Dubai in 1985. The airline was created with support from Dubai’s government Emirates began operations with just two aircraft The carrier launched its first flight to Karachi in Pakitan The airline expanded rapidly across international markets Dubai’s location helped Emirates become a global hub Emirates built its network around long-haul connections Emirates is known for its premium onboard experience Have you ever flown with Emirates? Leave a comment I absolutely loved this flight in Emirates' new Business Class Upgrading to Emirates’ Business Class is worth every penny Thx for watching my Emirates 777 Business Class review

Boarding was taken very seriously by the ground staff, and they strictly arranged passengers into the correct lanes. Of course, in business class, we were placed at the priority area, and soon it's time for boarding. >> Get a flight to your right. >> Okay, thank you. Welcome on board Cathay Pacific flight CX 928. After being greeted by a few cabin crew, I was shown to my seat 14K. I was actually the first passenger to board and seats in business class have a pitch of 45 in and a width of 21 in. Pretty spacious, if you ask me. In total, there are 24 Recaro CL 5510 seats in business class arranged in a 2-2-2 configuration. Welcome drinks were offered and we both got orange juice. Power options are excellent with two USB-C and power points between the seats. Finally, a quality pair of headphones are provided. Next to me are two windows and looking outside, we are in front of the right-hand side engine. As the pilots make their introductions, I couldn't help but notice the distinctive Australian accent, which I found to be common on Cathay flights. Let me know in the comments below if that is your experience as well, but for now, it's time to depart for Chongqing. >> After takeoff, let's look at the flight map which provides a good amount of information including altitude, time to destination, and speed. The map is customizable. However, performance-wise though, you can tell the unit's age as it is pretty laggy. Moving on to other parts of the units, there are of course movies and TV shows available in many categories. Next, music is available in several languages and genres if you want to sit back and chill. If you're taking kids for this trip, there is a dedicated kids section for movies, TV shows, music, and games. The Gate A shop with many items is available to browse in addition to the paper booklets. For games, there are about 15 titles to choose from including puzzle, sports, and strategy. Lastly, there is an information page which provides extra details including arrival information and weather forecasts. That's it for the IFE, and now looking at the seat controls, there are buttons to adjust the seat recline and leg rest. The recline amount is 9.5 in backwards and when extended the leg rest provide excellent comforts. The tray table is pretty unique and is found in front of you. Simply pull it out and extend as required. You can leave it in the half open position which provides a slim surface with two cup holders or you can fully extend it which provides a very large area. An Airbus A330 safety card is also provided to all passengers along with the Cathay in flights magazine. Lunch service was soon conducted after reaching cruise and the cabin crew came around and took our meal selections. Today I chose the grilled lamb rack with thyme and rosemary sauce. Stepping through each of the items the main meal looks fantastic and includes vegetables and potato gratin. For sides we have tuna, egg and vegetables as well as fresh fruits. For drinks I got the signature Cathay delights and a glass of water was also provided. Finally bread was given as an optional extra and of course you will have a full set of metal cutlery. Doing some taste testing the lamb main meal was absolutely delicious and the tuna was equally impressive. All ingredients were fresh including the fruits which were crunchy and sweets. To finish premium Häagen-Dazs ice cream was served which was excellent. Moving into the laboratory there is a single one available for business class passengers at the front of the aircraft. Inside everything was fully stocked but otherwise nothing really special stands out and the space is still pretty small. So after a very relaxing hour it's time to make our approach into Chongqing. As we descend let's go through today's ratings. First up is the cabin crew who were fantastic on this flights. The cabin crew offered pre-eparture drinks and the captain welcomed everyone aboard. He announced a flight time of 1 hour and 45 minutes, [music] said that we would be cruising at 37,000 ft and mentioned that there may be a few bumps as we got closer to Atlanta. Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat. [music] Around 20 minutes after takeoff, the crew came through the cabin taking drink orders and addressed each first class passenger by their last name. I was actually pretty impressed. Similar to my third flight from Las Vegas to DFW, the cabin crew on this flight seemed more senior and really showcased their years of experience. After the drinks were served, the crew came around with a basket of snacks. I just grabbed one bag of Kettle brand potato chips. Even though we were told we could take as much as we wanted, the crew offered snacks twice during the flight and regularly checked to see if anyone wanted another drink. A little over an hour and a half later, we started our descent into Atlanta. This flight went by pretty quickly, maybe because I was ready for the trip to be over. Other than the sea cleanliness issue, which is still mind-boggling considering we were at their home base, this flight felt very similar to the one before it, except that there were no hot meals served on the shorter flight. Before landing, the lead crew member came around and thanked each first class passenger for flying with the airline. I was half expecting some acknowledgement or apology regarding the condition of my seat, but I didn't get one, which was fine. It was just a small blemish on what was otherwise amazing service. >> [music] [music] >> place. >> [music] >> So, what are my overall thoughts on American Airlines's domestic short and medium hall first class on the Boeing 737800 and Airbus A321? Before this whole trip, I had actually flown American Airlines first class many times before. And although my first impression was that the cabin lacked character and felt somewhat bland, I thought the light colored interior contrasted with the gray seats looked modern and premium, giving the cabin a clean, spacious, and airy feel. And that's still how I feel about it today, but more so on the A321 than the 737. The seats were fine for the most part, although I do wish they had seatback entertainment screens. [music] I'm not sure if every seat has the same amount of padding, but I definitely felt that some were more comfortable than others. The hot meals were hit or miss, although nothing was downright gross or inedible. The cabins weren't spotless, but they were about what you'd expect in terms of cleanliness on domestic flights these days. That filthy seat on my last flight was inexcusable though, but it also seemed to be the exception rather than the norm. [music] What really made flying with the airline more pleasurable though was the flight and cabin crew. I don't think I encountered a single disengaged or unprofessional crew member throughout the entire trip. Everyone was professional, friendly, and efficient. Overall, I would fly American Airlines domestic first class again if the fair or mileage redemption was reasonable, especially on longer flights. Otherwise, it's not a product I would go out of my way to book. I couldn't help but compare it to my most recent Alaska Airlines domestic first class flight on the 737 Max from Atlanta to Seattle where the first class cabin was more spacious, the seat [music] was wider, the aircraft was noticeably newer, the food was more refined, and the overall experience was simply better. I'll post a link to that review in the description below for those who are interested. Thank you for watching and safe travels. Please make sure to like and subscribe. [music]
