reviews.transcript_full: Today we're in Shiyan, one of China's most fascinating cities. To ride one of the country's  most popular sleeper trains on a 1,200km trip across to the capital Beijing.  We will deep dive into the different accommodations, check out the food options,  and walk through the whole train to see whether this 12 hour overnight rail journey is the best way  to cross China. So come along with me and let's check it all out together.  Welcome to the home of the Terrakosawarias, the afterlife army of Kin Shikuan,  the first emperor of China in 210 BC. There have been archaeological finds in this area,  suggesting it was first inhabited around half a million years ago by Homo erectus,  but it definitely became most prominent in the 11th century as the political and cultural center  of the Xiao Dynasty. Nowadays it is homesy around 13 million people and is capital of China's Shangxi  province. Okay, let's head to the station to get this trip started. We are departing from the  most central of the main railway terminal I hear, simply named Shiyan. It sits just outside the  14th century city walls, around 2km northeast of the city center. I'm a bit early, so I'm going  to pop and have some dinner, before returning around an hour before scheduled departure time.  Let's head inside and check it out. As with most Chinese train stations, there is an ID and  security check before you can access the concourse. Foreigners using their passport should head to the  manual lane where the staff member will check you in. Then you must have your bag exact  trade and pass through a body metal detector check. It's very quick and easy taking less than a minute,  liquids are permitted. Once through you need to head up one level to the departure concourse.  This can be accessed by these escalators but there are also lifts for a step-free route.  This station is fully accessible. All signages in both Chinese and English so you should have no  trouble way finding. One thing I do love about Chinese railway stations is that once you've used  a few they do all feel very familiar but they also all have their own quirks and design features  such as unique displays or local touches. The main departure lounge is large with a plethora  of seating options throughout. There is essentially located information kiosk and many shops and  food outlets spread around the edges including western brands. There were also free to use toilets  and water dispenses. It's a very impressive station. Our train tonight is the D-44 service  to Beijing West departing at 8.35pm. We will leave Xi'an in an easterly direction before turning  north and making just one intermediate stop overnight in the early hours before arriving in Beijing  tomorrow morning around 8.30am. Boarding starts 20 minutes before scheduled departure time and  everyone lines up for the ticket gate check about 15 minutes prior to this. Again you should head  to the manual lane if using your passport as ID as it rarely works on the automated gates and the  member of staff will need to process you. Then head one level down to the platforms. You can do  this by stairs or escalator. Again there is also a lift if required. And now we get the first glimpse  of the superb train which will convey us all the way to the Chinese capital tonight with comfort and ease.  It's a China Railway's Fuxing CR-200J Stemy High Speed Electric Multiple Unit or EMU.  These train sets have a power car on each end and 16 passenger coaches in between. There are  three classes of travel on board. They have a maximum in service speed of 160km per hour and a power  output of 5600kW. I think they look super smart in this green, white and red  livery. What's your favourite China Railways livery? Leave me a comment below.  Whenever I'm travelling especially on longer trips like this two week one across China,  having reliable luggage makes all the difference to me. For the past four years I've been using  level 8 cases and they have recently sent me their new adventure 20 inch carry-on and it's  quickly becoming one of my favourites. It's got a tough polycarbonate shell that's lightweight  but incredibly durable, smooth 360° spin-a-wheels and a wide trolley handle that makes navigating  busy airports and railway stations effortless. There's also really well thought out interior  with separate compartments that keep everything organised. One feature I particularly like is the quick  access front pocket which makes it easy to grab my laptop, new camera batteries, passport or other  essentials quickly and easily. However you're travelling all level 8 luggage is designed to  cope with the demands of frequent usage while still looking sleek and elegant. If you're wanting  to upgrade your luggage you can grab 12% off anything on the level 8 website using my discount  code non-stop 12. A huge thanks to level 8 for their ongoing support of the channel.  Now let's get on board the train and start our overnight trip to Beijing.  The platform is level with the train with just a small gap to cross.  We will be travelling in the highest class on board this train that being first class sleeper.  This is laid out in four birth private rooms similar to a kushet coach within Europe.  I will show you the other accommodation options later on in the video.  And here is my room for tonight. My first impressions are good, it looks very clean and comfortable.  Right, let's settle down and get ready for departure.  We leave exactly on time at 8.35pm. Chinese trains are very punctual and that really is the  magic of taking the night train in this part of the world. This trip from Xi'an to Beijing  covers a distance of 1,200 kilometers which is scheduled to take us 11 hours and 47 minutes of  travel time. I love that we only make one intermediate stop on route as that really helps with  a continuous sleep. The price of a single birth in this first class sleeper compartment is 458  Chinese yuan, which I think is very reasonable for this journey. You will be sharing with other  passengers of your gender unless there are four of you travelling and there is availability at the  time of booking. Children under six travel for free if sharing a bed and those aged 7 to 13 get  around a 25% discount on the overall ticket price. The cheapest way to travel on this train is in a  second class state which costs just 192 Chinese yuan. I will show you this in a bit but I wouldn't  want to spend 12 hours in one. Tickets go on sale 15 days before travel and I would recommend  booking through the China Railways 12306 Apple website or trip.com. The latter is more foreign  or friendly with a clear interface and more payment options but they do charge around a 15%  commission. You can also pre-book up to two months before travel and trip will then purchase the  tickets the moment they go on sale. Okay let's check out my first class sleeper compartment in more detail.  The door can be locked in two places but only from the inside.  On the wall here are controls for the rims air conditioning, main lights and announcement volume.  The window has a full closure blackout blind. The beds themselves come with all the bedding  pre-assembled at one end but not made up. The base is relatively soft but there is also a foam  topper for additional comfort. All the bedding was clean and of good quality and the pillow was very  fluffy. Fold down steps can be found by the door to make access easier for the top  bunks which are basically the same as the bottom ones. They all have little storage pockets,  clothing hooks, a small shelf, personal reading lights and two USB-A ports.  In between the bottom two bunks is a large sturdy fix table. Under this is where you'll find  the rims only proper power socket. There is also a bin down here.  Luggage storage can be found under both bottom bunks and also above the main door over the corridor.  Overall a pretty good sleeper room very clean and I love the ambience.  As there's not much to see outside let's go and check out some more of the train now.  The carpeted corridors have fold down stalls as well as some additional power sockets if required.  Each coach has hot water dispenses and cups so you can make up your own tea, coffee or pot noodles.  There is also a communal wash area along with two toilets in each vestibule.  They are both modern vacuum toilets with one being a Chinese squat-slire one.  But don't worry there is a regular western style sit-down jolly too.  They were both very clean and the water worked so it was only available at the sinks outside.  There was a bin along with plenty of toilet paper and toilet seat covers too.  Okay now let's go and have a look at the buffet counter.  There is no sit-down dining cart on board these trains and you just take your  purchases back to your room for consumption.  This mainly consisted of drinks and snacks but there were some microwave hot meals too.  As I'd already had dinner I just bought a drink that I could make up in the morning.  Now let's look at the other accommodation options on board.  These are the second class seats which are in a 3 plus 2 configuration.  As I said before it's cheap at about a third of the price of my birth so it's great for the  budget traveler. There are power sockets and tray tables. The seats are also quite comfy,  have a good legroom and do recline a long way but for a 12 hour overnight trip I'll take the bed please.  One wheelchairs space is available in the coach next to the buffet area and the accessible toilet  is in the adjacent vestibule.  The other bed adoption on the train is second class sleeper which is laid out in six bed open  compartments. This costs about 30% less than my first class bed. Bedding is still provided and all  the other amenities are pretty much the same.  Okay that sums up the train tour so let's head back to my room now and settle down for the night.  As soon as I crawl into my bed I know it's going to be a good night's sleep. See you in the morning.  And wow I was totally right. I got at least eight hours solid sleep. I didn't even wake up for  the stop around 6am. It makes all the difference on a sleeper train to not be constantly stopping  throughout the night with a large throughput of people making noise and the train has a very good  ride quality too on these super smooth tracks. Okay time to make up my strawberry milk tea that I  bought last night. As I mentioned you can just use the hot water dispenses in the corridors whenever  you want. If well ah it was very delicious. We are now passing through Baoding approximately  135 kilometers to the southwest of Beijing and the last major city we will transit before we arrive  in the Chinese capital in an hour or so. The train window views are unfortunately limited on this  route as most of it is in darkness however we do pass some nice temples and rivers in the final  part of the journey. And just like that we are now in the suburbs of Beijing so let me summarize  this trip from Xian on board this D44 sleeper train service in a first class compartment.  Overall I think it was excellent and I had a wonderful journey. The room was clean, comfortable  and very well appointed with everything you could need for this 12 hour overnight journey.  As for the toilets and other shared spaces the train really was in a very good condition.  Although there is not a full dining car the offerings that were available from the buffet  counter were sufficient seeing as most passengers including myself would have eaten dinner before  boarding last night. And the most important thing you can ask for from a sleeper train the quality  of sleep was superb a great bed and bedding and a train which doesn't stop during the night  and has an excellent ride quality. I would say that the 160 kilometer per hour maximum speed is the  perfect sweet spot for travel time versus a very comfortable experience.  We arrived into Beijing's West Station right on time at 8.22am. This was pretty much the perfect  sleeper train journey and I would highly recommend it to travel between Xian and Beijing.  The Chinese capital is home to 22 million people and is without doubt one of my favorite cities  in the country. There is so much history standing hand in hand alongside such modernity  and amazing value hotels too.  Have you been on any Chinese sleeper trains before? If so which ones and on which routes?  How did you find them? Let me know in the comments below.  I'm also open to new video ideas so if you have something you'd like to see on the channel  then drop me a DM on Instagram, BlueSky or Twitter.  Don't forget to subscribe thanks for watching till the end and I'll see you in the next video.

A Closer Look at the Aircraft

reviews.transcript_full: Cutting short a family holiday in Japan to fly a specific airline is a questionable  decision.  Are you serious?  But when this award seat popped up, that's exactly what I did.  This is Stalux, the Taiwanese airline that went from zero to five star rating faster than  any airline industry.  And with their first Australian route landing soon, I wanted to find out if the airline  delivers on its high price.  Today we're going to be flying on a new airline for us anyway.  Stalux heard lots of great things about it, but is it actually worth your help?  Let's find out together.  Osaka's Kansai International Airport sits on an artificial island in Osaka Bay, about  50 kilometers from the city.  The Harukure Express gets you there from Osaka in about 40 minutes.  Japan is a huge market for Stalux.  The airline flies to 12 destinations across the country.  Osaka gets two white body aircraft per day and via on the 135 pm departure.  The airport was pretty busy at the time, but the Stalux check-in was quite efficient.  Stalux has dedicated first and business task counters with carpeted lanes.  Two check bags up to 32 kg is interiorized part of the ticket.  And I'll get to how I redeem points for the ticket at the end of the video.  A fast-made ticket for security and immigration was also provided, which made those formalities  a breeze.  Soon via airside, walking past the array of duty free shops in pursuit of our lounge  for the day.  Now Stalux doesn't have its own lounge at Osaka, so eligible passengers are directed  to the shared KIX lounge instead.  The airport lounge can be a hit or miss, but this one has a little skip.  Three thousand square meters with 600 plus seats and two distinct sections.  The north side of the lounge is your go-to for food.  The selection was an alright buffet of hot dishes, but the real shore-stealer was this  giant cup noodle figurine, an old Dorsaka as the birthplace of cup noodles.  There was also a small self-service bar with a selection of drinks, as well as a paid  menu for cocktails.  The lounge had shower facilities and even a children's play area, which was really appreciated.  If you're after a quiet workspace, the south is more suited to that.  This area had its own snacking station and a mini bar.  On the downside, the views were pretty limited, so I headed to my gate instead to watch  our aircraft coming into land.  Here's a closer look at our aircraft taking us to Taipei today.  There was a slight delay in boarding due to the late arrival of our aircraft, but soon  we're on our way.  Starlux has 6 Airbus A330DO aircraft in its fleet.  These are run in a two-class configuration, with 28 seats in business class and 269 seats  in economy.  The business class seats are laid out in a staggered 1-2-1 configuration.  There are no bathrooms in this cabin, so to minimize disruption to others, we chose  the seats in row 8 right at the back of the cabin.  Today's aircraft was less than 3 weeks old and you could tell, not a scarf, not a mark,  that new plain smell.  Starlux uses the Safron Skylaunch Core Seat.  In fact, they are the lounge customer for this product.  BMW Designworks did the interior styling and it shows, with its charcoal shells, gold  trim and warm wooden tones.  This flight is just over 2 hours in length, so understandably, the amenities were limited  to a pillow, blanket and a bag with slippers.  Paper menus were provided, which you'll take a look at later.  On the specs front, the seat is 20 inches wide, with 44 inches of pitch, converting to  a fully flat bed.  This is been lined with other 830 Neo regional business class products out there.  However, the foot well does feel a bit narrow.  On a flight under 5 hours, which is the longest that this aircraft flies for, at least  right now, it is a non-issue.  Storage-wise, there is a big cabinet in the side console and this is where you would find  the Starnex branded headphones.  The seat comes with more amenities, including a large wireless charging pad and both USB  seat and USB A ports.  The crew set a positive impression right from the start of the flight.  They helped me put away my many items, which I'm thankful for, especially when travelling  with a baby.  They also confirmed my meal order and took my pre-departure drink order from the menu.  Usually, you're offered a tray with a couple of options, but the Starlex crew let me  pick anything from the extensive menu.  And I had to go for this rather mysterious looking blue drink.  Starlex has a comical but fun safety video and this was played as we pushed back from  a gate.  An extended taxi to runway 24 hour followed, after which we were on our way to Taipei.  As we climbed out, the entire runway appeared to be floating out there in the middle of  the seat, something genuinely strange but impressive at the same time.  Time to day, 2 hours and 15 minutes.  So let's get ourselves up to speed with the menu.  The thick booklet consists of two options, Asian or International.  Here's the full breakdown.  Starlex does let you view and please select your means online.  Following those two pages is a super extensive drinks list.  That includes a cocktail selection as well as a wide range of spurs, liquors and beers.  Then this continues to keep going with motels, juices, sake and a selection of coffee and  tea.  And oh, we're not finished yet with the drinks, because wines get their separate menu.  That list consists of a champagne, two white wines, three reds and a port.  This is the most extensive drinks list I've seen for a flight of this length.  But just as I had convinced myself of that, Starlex hit me with their trump card, their signature  boba tea latte.  Love Taiwan is home to Mabel tea, so it's only natural that a Taiwanese airline would  offer this.  I never thought bubble tea at 35,000 feet would make it to my bucket list, but here we are.  We took turns with our meals, so while I wait, here's a look at the baby menu that was  provided.  A couple of purée and some juice, which was thoroughly enjoyed.  He also got this Starlex A350 inflatable toy.  So it's time for my tray table to come out, and it's a pretty practical setup, which  can be pushed out of the way if you need to exit the seat.  As I mentioned before, Starlex lets you choose your meal online before your flight, and  I had pre-selected the Asian option for lunch.  Alongside the braised chicken and the mushrooms, there was a lack of bento with a few small  dishes.  There was a bowl for the soup with rice tucked away in its own lidded container.  Overall this was a genuine challenger to some of the best airline meals I've had, both  in terms of presentation as well as taste.  Sir came in its own tray, which in itself is unique for a shock flight like this.  It was a beautiful looking matcha pudding with fresh fruit, and a pressed butter stand  cookie with Starlex branding.  I didn't know this at the time, but this small piece of chocolate turns out to be one  of the most sought after chocolates in the world made from rare post-Sinana beans.  After the meal service, I took some time to check out the inflight entertainment unit.  The screen is a massive 17.3 inch 4K touch screen, and it's one of the best reviews.  It is sharp, responsive with a vast content library.  It can also be controlled by this rather funky looking remote.  I also like how you can view titles as list-style grids, which makes searching a lot easier.  The system also supports Bluetooth pairing if you'd rather use your own headphones.  WIFE is available, but unfortunately not the fast kind.  Starlex despite its closeness to the name doesn't use Starlink for its Wi-Fi.  The service is provided by YSAT and a clocked around 1.5Mbps.  It is totally fine for texting and browsing, but you're not going to be able to stream  anything.  I also took a quick look at one of the two lavatories in the cabin.  The new aircraft thing probably plays its part, but this was one of the cleanest lavatories  I've stepped in on an aircraft.  The amenities were all well stocked too.  And it was nice to see an anus in the loop.  It's next like these, the crew kept us treated for the rest of the flight.  As you began our dissenting to Taipei, it's time to wrap up this Starlex experience.  If I really had to critique something, here are two things.  The seat has a narrow footwell and the Wi-Fi won't be streaming anything for you.  But apart from that, this is about as close as it gets to a 5 star business class experience,  a stunning hot product on a brand new aircraft and a soft product that felt consider rather  than checklisted.  Special mention to the crew, who are attentive and warm throughout.  Checking in regularly, the thought ever feeling scripted.  Starlex knows exactly what it wants to be, and for an airline that's only 5 years old,  it executes at a level.  Many legacy carriers still haven't figured out.  This experience has made me want to fly Starlex again, hopefully out of Taipei, so that I  can check out their hub ground experience, and perhaps some of that long haul to Sydney  next year.  Before we go, here's a look at how we booked this Starlex ticket.  Starlex has a reciprocal partnership with the last car airlines at most program.  It costs 15,000 at most rewards points plus 65 US dollars in taxes for the seat.  For comparison, a cash prize on this road is usually 600 US dollars.  Was cutting short a family holiday to fly this the right call?  Objectively no.  To either credit, not even a little, and spending a few extra days in Taipei on the way  home wasn't bad either.

reviews.transcript_full: Planning a trip to Asia?  Korean Air is one of the leading airlines connecting North America with destinations across  South Korea, Japan, China, Southeast Asia, and beyond.  Korean Air offers non-stop service from several major cities in the United States and Canada,  making travel to Asia convenient and accessible.  Most journeys connect through Seoul, Incheon Airport, known for efficient transfers, clear  signage, and a traveler-friendly layout.  If your itinerary includes more than one destination in Asia, Korean Air's extensive regional  network can make planning easier.  Economy class is known for comfortable seating, adjustable headrest, and generosity legroom  on many long haul aircraft.  Meals and beverages are included, with both Korean and international menu options available  on many flights.  Long haul aircraft feature personal entertainment screens, with movies, TV shows, music, and  games.  USB charging is also available on many aircraft.  Blankets, pillows, and headphones are typically provided to help make long journeys more comfortable.  Korean Air is a strong option for travelers heading to Seoul, Tokyo, Osaka, Bangkok,  Manila, Ho Chi Minh City, and many other destinations throughout Asia.  For more airline reviews and helpful travel tips for economical international flights,  stay tuned with ASAP Tickets.

reviews.transcript_full: From the moment the wheels begin to roll on the runway, still damp from the morning [music] mist, the aircraft stands like a giant collecting its strength, preparing for a grand journey. Each rotation of the jet engines gradually accelerates. The deep majestic roar is not merely mechanical noise, but the rhythm of life awakening. Under the light of a new day, the metallic ship stretches its wings, gliding powerfully along the runway, ready to leave the ground behind and conquer the vast sky. >> [music] >> But the sky is never a path paved only with roses. When darkness suddenly descends, black clouds swirl as if to swallow the space whole. Lightning streaks across the heavens, illuminating heavy raindrops that hammer against the windows, creating a dramatic symphony of nature. Inside the cabin, the atmosphere hangs suspended in anxiety with expectant gazes fixed toward the windows. The intense turbulence challenges the nerves of those aboard, turning every passing second into a slow-motion sequence, a haunting testament to human endurance against the forces of nature. Amidst the heart of the chaos, the cockpit is another world, a place where composure reigns supreme. The glow from the control panel illuminates the faces of the pilots who remain in deep concentration, their hands steady [music] on the controls. Every button pressed and every parameter monitored is the result of tireless training, enabling them to comprehend and steer the ship through the harsh gusting winds. It is the perfect fusion of advanced technology [music] and the iron resolve of those who command the skies.

reviews.transcript_full: Hace casi 40 años la primera aerolínea española que cruzó el Atlántico con un avión de dos motores no fue Iberia, fue Ede Europa, sí, Ede Europa.  Y es que hizo lo que ninguna otra aerolínea española se había traído intentar, la ruta Madrid no mayor con un vi motor.  Fue la primera vez en la historia de este país.  Casi 40 años después esa misma ruta la disputan cuatro compañías y una de ellas acaba de cambiar por completo loco frecabordo, justo donde casi nadie mira.  En económicas. Hoy volamos ese producto recién estrenado al que la aerolínea ha llamado Ede Europa ON, de Madrid a Nueva York, para responder a una pregunta muy muy simple.  ¿Ha conseguido Europa que su económico juegue en la ligada de las grandes?  Nuestra ruta de hoy Madrid no mayor es lo que en aviación se conoce como una ruta de prestigio.  No es la más rentable, tampoco la más larga, pero es la que conecta la capital española con la capital Financiera del mundo,  y la que toda aerolínea de red quiere en su mapa.  Porque lo que dice de ti es tan importante como lo que genera.  El trayecto arranca en Madrid, librando en la península ibérica por las costas gallegas a la altura de la ciudad de Acoruña,  y entra en el alánico por ruta randon sobre el sector oceánico de Shangwick,  ascendiendo hasta los 52 grados de la Ditud Norte, posterior las provincias marítimas de Canadá, paralelos a la costa estadounidense,  iniciando el descenso sobre la vertical de Boston, rumbo nuestro destino, el aeropuerto internacional JFK en New York,  curiendo 7 horas y 30 minutos de tiempo de vuelo.  Desde Madrid, esta ruta la vuelan 4 aerolíneas inescalas,  Iberia, con hasta 2 frecuencias diarias, su feudo histórico, un cruce que domina desde hace décadas,  American ideal está empujando desde atrás con todo el tráfico de conexión del mercado doméstico estadounidense,  y por último la víctima de hoy, en Europa.  4 aerolíneas, mismas rutas, posiciones muy distintas,  la pregunta entonces es inevitable, que ofrece el Europa en el Atlántico que justifique elegir la frente a sus competidoras directas.  Si viste el vídeo donde analizábamos su business en el 787, ya conocerás la trayectoria de esta compañía,  su nacimiento, su transomación de chártera, aerolínea regular, los intentos de IAG por adquirirla o su situación actual.  ¿No nos vamos a repetir? ¿Todo dejo que arriba por si quieres echarlo un vistazo?  ¿Por qué hoy lo que nos interesa es otra cosa? ¿Qué construyó realmente Juan José Hidalgo para que los mayores grupos aéreos del mundo se pelearan por comprarla?  Y como es el producto que ofrece a Borde, en el trozo del pastel más codiciado por todas las compañías de este lado del mundo en Atlántico?  Y es que la coincidencia juega a nuestro favor, porque Eri Europa acaba de lanzar una iniciativa de transformación de la experiencia de Ecliente,  a la que ha llamado Eri Europa ON. Entre muchas otras cosas incluye un nuevo servicio en economía,  y este es uno de los primeros vuelos en estrenarlo.  Si alguna vez tomas un vuelo de largo radio desde la terminal uno de Madrid un consejo, ve a la aeropuerto con Margen,  especialmente si vuelas en economía y no tienes status, porque a estas horas alrededor del mediodía,  una punta de todas las salidas hacia América, este lugar es sencillamente un caos.  Justo de reconocer que este verano 2026 la climatización acompaña, algo que en un hole de techos bajos con esta multitud y el calor de Madrid, no siempre se puede dar por hecho.  Una cierta de aina, sobre todo para los pasajeros de mayor edad o comobilidad reducida.  Y el Europa dispone de mostradores de facturación internacional en esta zona de la T1,  y aunque el espacio de reducido la afluencia es la que ves, el personal gestiona el flujo como oficio y mantiene el orden dentro del desorden, la verdad.  Por suerte hoy, aunque vuelo en economía al tener status Sky-Chin el Eclash en el programa Sumadero Europea,  puede usar uno de los privilegios que otorga a partir de nivel gold, el uso del mostrador diferenciado de business,  además de equipaje facturado adicional.  Acomular punto en suma, abre ciertas puertas que queremos viendo lo largo del vídeo de hoy.  Como ya sabemos de vídeos anteriores, las terminales 1, 2 y 3 disponen de varias alas, según el destino.  Hoy volamos a un destino en Long Shengen, así que nos corresponde la terminal 1 y con ella la sala que utiliza Europa, las alas y veles,  operada por Plaza Premium y comercializada por aina, entorno a las puertas veles en la segunda planta.  Y aquí una sorpresa antes incluso de entrar, las alas y veles parece a ver reabierto su ubicación original tras una larga reforma,  y el espacio que la sustituyo durante las obras se ha convertido ahora en sala altitude, la propuesta de aina para el pasajero premium que busca un plus de privacidad y de servicio.  Se acceder viajando en business con ciertas aerolíneas con algún pase tipo trago un pas, y poco más, pero si a cual sea tu acceso,  importa te cobrarán una tarifa adicional que justifica esa exclusividad.  Me reje la pena, entrada al contraste habla por sí solo, altitude está prácticamente vacía mientras Cibeles registra esta cola interminable,  porque según los informan a la llegada al cansado su aforo máximo.  En un próximo vídeo la analizaremos a fondo y te dejaré a ti como pasajero y espectador,  juzgar si compensa pagar ese extra sobre el ya elevado precio de un billet en business.  Salas Cibeles ha sido siempre mi favorita en la T1 por su amplitud, por su cantidad de asientos, por su espacio de descanso,  o sin embargo no cabe un alma y ese ángulo premium se devalua de inmediato.  Aquí accede literalmente de todo, desde quien abona la tarifa en puerta o en la web de aina hasta pasajeros de business y en las aerolíneas asociadas,  titulares de ciertas tarjetas de crédito o como es mi caso hoy viajeros en economy con estatus en programas de filialización como el mío Skye Chimalit Plus.  La sala cuenta con zonas diferenciadas, mesas altas de trabajo, áreas de descanso, algunas aisladas y una zona de televisión con sillones.  Aunque la saturación de hoy convierte la zona de trabajo en un improvisado comedor con una imagen que dista mucho de lo premium.  Habrá que ver si la estrategia de aina al guiar la masificación cobrando un extra por altitude termina funcionando.  Algo parecido a lo que han diseñado en la T4 con sala de retiro, pero con un toque algo más exclusivo,  ya que altitud dispone de hasta el restaurante a la carta.  El buffet central despliga una selección más que correcta, comida caliente, saladas, snacks y toda clase de bebidas,  el línea con el estándar de plaza premio en estas salas, haulado un par de neveras con bebidas alcoholicas y la zona del café.  Pero lo que convierte a esta sala en mi verdadero refugio es esta tarraza con vistas a la plataforma.  Para los friquis como tu y como yo solo por acceder aquí, ya merece la pena la espera, la cola y cualquier otra pega.  Mira qué vistas, y lo mejor no hay casi nadie, cuatro affix, dos fumadores y tuyo.  Desde aquí se ve toda la terminal ejecutiva y buena parte de la flota del largo radio de Europa,  calentando motores para cruzar el Atlántico casi el unízono rumbo al continente americano.  Un mercado que conviene recordar esta compañía y no empezó a volar con el modelo TrinLiner, pero ojo, ni siquiera con el 767.  Para entender la operación tras Atlántica de Europa hay que retroceder casi 40 años.  En noviembre de 1988, Europa hizo historia, o pero entre Madrid y Nueva York,  el primer vuelo tras Atlántico e-tops de una aerolínea española y lo hizo con un bimotor, un Boeing 757200.  Hoy suena trivial, entonces era casi una heregía. Hasta ese momento cruzar el charco era territorio casi exclusivo de aviones de 3 y 4 motores.  Una norma estricta limitaba cuánto podía lejarse un bimotor de un aeropuerto alternativo.  La certificación e-tops cambió esa regla y el Europa quiso ser bionera,  trabajando con la autoridad española y la FAA Americana apenas 3 años después de que nacer la normativa.  Elejó precisamente la misma ruta que hoy volamos.  Y aquí conviene una precisión, porque aquí la historia tiene matriz, y es que como sabemos de vídeos anteriores,  aquella Europa pionera nació en 1986, dentro de un grupo británico, y operaba un modelo esencialmente charter,  pero habría una puerta que, hasta entonces solo ibería tenía el poder de abrir y cerrar.  Con los años llegaría el Boeing 767, que convirtió aquella superaciones puntuales en una reta satlántica real,  después en la arbusa 330 que consolido al crecimiento hacia América, y finalmente el Boeing 787,  más eficiente, más silencioso, y que pase hacer cada día con total normalidad, lo que 1988 parecía experimental.  Y sin embargo, esta historia estuvo punto de no existir, porque aquel grupo británico quebró en 1991,  dejando a la aerolínea al borde del cierre. ¿Qué hoy la estemos volando? ¿Qué exista siquiera?  Se la debemos a un elemento que lo cambió todo. ¿Cuál? Bueno, mejor te lo cuento en crucero. Ahora nos tenemos que ir.  La flota de Europa ya la revisamos en un vídeo anterior, pero desde entonces ha habido cambios que merecen la pena repasar.  Para largo radio la compañía sigue apoyándose en el Boeing 787, en su dos versiones, la 800 y la 900.  Un producto que los próximos años iremos viendo ceder terreno, frente a la nueva puesta de la casa,  el Airbus A350 900, cuya incorporación está prevista a partir de 2018, según fuentes oficiales.  Pero las novedades están en el corto y medio radio, junto al Boeing 787, auténtico pilar de la operación,  el Europe incorporó en mayo de 2025 el primer Boeing 787 Max 8 matriculado en España.  En la ranca de la renovación de su flota de pasillo único, tras más de dos décadas fiel al 787,  y recordemos que, además de la flota de la Matriz, la compañía opera a través de su filial con aoce propio aeronová,  bajo la marca comercial y Europa Express, con una flota integrada de Boeing 737 800.  No puedo contener ciertas satisfacción cada vez que en barco en un 787 de Europa,  no solo por el avión, sino por lo que representa, que un país de menos de 50 millones de habitantes  dispongate dos aerolíneas de arred como Europa e Iberia.  Este Boeing 787 900 está configurado en alta densidad, 32 asientos en business y 307 en economy,  sin cabina premium economy, las cabinas bravo y charle con forma en clase economy,  en disposición 333, la entrada se respira marca el Europa,  ese azul corporativo en un tono sereno que da la bienvenida con notable calidad.  Estos asientos del fabricante alemán recaro en su versión si el 3710,  visten un tapizado textile a diferencia del de piel de business en este mismo avión,  que aporta una sensación agradable y confortable.  El pitch ronda las 31 pulgadas unos 78 centímetros el estándar del segmento,  pero es suficiente para un economy de largo radio,  veamos pues donde está el benchmark en España,  Iberia ofrece exactamente el mismo espacio en su saerbusa 333,  y los A350 900,  de modo que Europa juega sin más en línea con el mercado.  El asiento nos recibe con una almohada y vuelta en una banda sin fundas de plástico,  enfrente la pantalla de LIFE a la que luego volveremos y esta mesa aplicable que también analizaremos.  Un repos abrazo con el botón reclinado, otro fijo a la derecha  y un repos acabezas regulable de diseño envolvente,  que por tacto y aspecto parece reciente y que en esta fulclaro resulta especialmente elegante.  La pantalla de LIFE es abatible para cuando el asiento de adelante se reclina a integra puertos  U S V A y U S V C.  Los compartimientos superiores de serie del RuiLina son excelentes,  permiten estivar el equipaje de canto y albergar más cultos en cabina.  Y de paso, mención al trabajo de la tripulación resolviendo un auténtico tetris de equipaje,  agirizando el embarque en una de las configuraciones de 787 900 más densas del mundo  entre las rolinias full-sovies, 339 pasajeros, un trabajo impecable.  Y como es habitual a la bordo de los TrunLiner, lamentablemente este avión no dispone de aereadores individuales.  En un vuelo que despega las 3 de la tarde, completo y en plena pixis un rumo a Estados Unidos,  la prioridad es clara, servir el almuerzo, cuanto antes para dejar después descansar al pasaje hasta un par de horas antes del descenso. Me llama la atención que Hire Europa haya recuperado la literatura en papel, además de todo el contenido digital en el IF,  en el bolsillo la revista de la casa en Europa, y sí, los aficionados vamos directos siempre a estas dos secciones,  la carta del CEO y el mapa de destinos y flota. Y aquí es donde Hire Europa quiere que pereste es atención, porque este menú no es el de siempre.  En mayo de 2026, la compañía puso en marcha Hire Europa ON,  el plan más ambicioso de renovación de su experiencia bordo en años,  y uno de sus cambios aterrizza justo aquí, el l'économie del largo radio,  una actualización del servicio principal y la recuperación de un segundo servicio antes del escenso.  Detrás de la cocina, sigue Gatecormet del grupo Gatecrup,  que abastecia a la aerolínea desde hace años,  y aunque lo juega en la liga de Joe Enco, lo que tenemos delante se defiende con sorvencia.  De entrada a dos opciones, pasta o pollo, nada extraordinario en el enunciado,  lo interesante está en la ejecución.  El pollo llega a la plancha con lo que parece un glaseado demostaza a la antigua,  sobre una base de orzo, esa pasta con formato de grano de arroz,  salteado con verduras Mediterráneas, acetunas y tomate,  ya que llega lo que no esperaba, y pollo estaba tierno. Y que en mi caso he decidido optar por un vino blanco,  que me han servido de forma generosa en un vaso de cartón. reviews.transcript_full: Economy class was never meant to be luxurious. It only needs to do one thing well, make a 10, 12, sometimes 14-hour flight variable.  A seat that lets you sleep, a cabin that doesn't crush you into the person beside you.  Most major airlines manage this, most of the time, but some don't, not consistently, not across their entire fleet.  This is a ranking of the 10 full service airlines with the worst long haul economy products in 2026,  judged on seat comfort, cabin density, sleepability, fleet consistency, and entertainment.  Not safety crew or business class. Not because they're bad airlines, because on the wrong aircraft on the wrong day,  economy stops being tolerable. Let's start at 10.  10. Air France  Air France's newer Airbus A35900 is, by most measures, a modern and comfortable long haul economy seat.  The airline has invested seriously in its recent fleet and it shows. The problem isn't simply age.  It sits with Air France's high-density Boeing 777-300ER aircraft, configured for leisure routes,  where the economy cabin is stretched to its limit.  Personal space narrows considerably, and the gap between this configuration and the A350 experience  is significant. Even these co-con configured 777s have received newer seats and updated entertainment  systems in places. But the underlying 343 layout hasn't changed. The issue was never the age of the  seat. It's the density around it. Air France avoids ranking higher because most of its newer fleet  is genuinely competitive. The problem is simply that its oldest high-density leisure configured  777s remain common enough to keep it on the list. Better Aircraft Airbus A35900  Worst Aircraft High-Density Boeing 777-300ER leisure configuration  Who should still consider it? Travelers booking routes confirmed to operate the A350,  or those prioritizing Air France's broader network and pricing.  Number 9 takes the fleet lottery problem and adds one more variable, a cabin that barely varies  at all. Number 9 Kuwait Airways  Kuwait Airways is not a poorly maintained airline. Its Boeing 777-300ER fleet is relatively young,  and the newer Airbus A3-3800neo brings a noticeably more spacious, better laid-out economy cabin.  But the 777, which carries the bulk of the airline's long haul network, is configured in a dense 343  layout with narrow seats and limited recline, a combination that makes sleep difficult on overnight  sectors. In-flight entertainment on these aircraft also lags behind regional and international  competitors. Unlike several airlines on this list, the issue isn't an aging cabin. It's  that a relatively modern aircraft is still configured in a way that leaves economy feeling unnecessarily  cramped. Better Aircraft Airbus A3-3800neo Worst Aircraft  Boeing 777-300ER Who should still consider it? reviews.transcript_full: Around nine years ago Sri Lankan Airlines took delivery of five brand new aircrafts into their fleet fresh from the Airbus factory.  They were the 320 NEOs and 320 one NEOs.  And to this day, this is the best economy class that they can offer with working entertainment systems that are responsive and comfortable seating.  I want to see if that is really the case as I fly them from Jakarta, Sokarno, Hata, International Airport here in Indonesia, all the way to Columbus.  I want to see if that is really the case as I fly them from the Airbus factory.  Welcome to Terminal 3, where my journey begins.  This is Jakarta's main international terminal, serving a wide range of airlines including Karuda Indonesia, Singapore Airlines, Oman Air and of course, Sri Lankan Airlines, which I'll be flying today.  Sri Lankan Airlines operates a multitude of seating products across its fleet, meaning you'd never quite know what onboard experience you'd get.  For example, when I checked the radar yesterday, this route was operated by an A320-200, featuring hard seats and no in flight entertainment.  In fact, I flew that very aircraft type from Bangalore to Columbus recently.  A review you can check out after this one.  My point is that, the experience on that aircraft is vastly different from what I'll be flying today.  This Singapore Airlines A350 certainly catches my eye, so stay tuned. You might see a review on this soon.  We've already seen quite a few interesting airlines, and Sokarno Hata is a fantastic place for plane spotting, with carriers from all over the world passing through.  There are plenty of airlines that I'd love to try in the future.  Our gate is located towards the find of the terminal, and interestingly, the air conditioning in this section feels noticeably weaker.  At times, it almost feels as though you're sitting in a semi-outdoor area, so that's something to keep in mind if you find yourself departing from here.  So if you're departing from gates 1-4, consider yourself warned.  Following an even further delay caused by the aircraft having to perform a go-around, our flight finally arrived to the gate.  For those unfamiliar with the term, a go-around is when an aircraft is unable to land on its initial approach, and must circle around to make another landing attempt.  Today's aircraft is 4 Romeo-Alpha-November-Fox Tron, an Airbus A321 Neo that was around 80 years old at the time of this video being published.  My seat for today is 15 Alfa. It comes equipped with an in-flight entertainment screen, an adjustable headrest, and even a footrest, making it a comfortable option for medium-haul flights such as this one.  Another nice feature is the foldable cocktail table, which comes in handy during the drink service, when you don't want to bring down the entire tray table just for a drink.  Please feel free to contact me if you know the graph on the internet.  I shall see you in the scope. For now, enjoy the taxi and take off.  Get me a groupie on the takeoff.  For those who don't know me, welcome to my channel, Tristan Trip Reviews. I'm Tristan.  As a passionate flight influencer, I'm dedicated to providing honest, transparent insights into various modes of travel, with a special focus on the flight travel industry.  Every review I share is 100% self-funded, ensuring that the opinions you hear are genuinely mine.  Join me as I uncover the heightened laws of travel to help you make better informed decisions for your next adventure, and now to the review.  Hey, you seem to be enjoying the video, so why not hit subscribe and turn on notifications.  It really helps the channel out and genuinely makes me happy.  Plus, it will be officially part of the Tristan Trip Reviews family, where we explore more flights, more cabins and more honest reviews together.  Come on, join the journey.  The thing I'd like to mention is as I boarded the aircraft, one of the cabin crew members asked me to stop filming.  I found this quite surprising, as I've reviewed Sri Lanka now there are more than 10 times on the channel.  And I've flown with them many more times beyond that, but yet I've never encountered anything like this.  I found it rather peculiar, but what could I do?  So I just respected the crew members' requests and continued filming once I got to my seat.  With that behind us, it's time to settle in and see what Sri Lanka Airlines has to offer.  Speaking of the on-board product, each passenger is provided with headphones to use with the IFE.  Browseing through the movie selection with Sri Lanka Airlines is always decent.  There were quite a few interesting titles, but eventually my options fell down to either Joker, Folle other or Wicked.  I've already seen Joker on a previous flight, and ironically I've also seen Wicked.  But well, I chose Wicked again.  Before long, the meal service arrived.  Today's main course consisted of chicken red curry, tempered potatoes and yellow rice.  On the side, a potato corn and carrot salad with mayonnaise, and the dessert was a passion fruit mousse, and of course, accompanied by an apple juice.  Honestly, I don't think I've ordered any other beverage on the flight in the past seven years, and the streak is going strong.  Let's all stay a moment to appreciate the metal cutlery.  Thank you Sri Lanka, L.A.S.  My thoughts on the meal. It tasted better than it looks, and that is a pleasant surprise.  Approximately 30 minutes before landing, headphones are taken from the passengers.  That's something to keep in mind in case you were planning to watch a movie until the aircraft taxis the gate.  With that, sit back, relax, and enjoy the descent into the capital city of Sri Lanka, Kalapur.  We are flying at one of the best times in the evening, so get ready for the golden hour.  Welcome to Bandar Nike International Airport, Kalambo, Sri Lanka. The local time is around 550 in the evening.  It's time to assess the flight using my calculated scoring system Tristan's SkyScope.  To evaluate each flight consistently, I use a set of key metrics that assess different aspects of the experience.  This allows me to reach a fair and balanced conclusion at the end of every review. Those categories are as follows.  The ground service, service onboard the aircraft, seat catering, and in flight entertainment.  Starting with the ground service, this category covers everything before boarding, including the booking process, online check-in, seat selection, and the overall airport experience with regard to the airline.  There wasn't anything particularly remarkable here. It was a straightforward process from start to finish.  One thing worth mentioning, however, is that Sri Lankan Airlines frequently swaps aircrafts.  You'll have to often wait until online check-in to choose your seat, and even then, the final product can still vary depending on the aircraft assigned.  Fortunately, I didn't encounter any inconsistencies on this flight. Overall, ground service earns a 7 out of 10.  Next up is the service, which covers everything that happens once you're on board, from the professionalism of the cabin crew to how they handle the flight overall.  Throughout the journey, the crew were responsive and respectful towards passengers. The only notable hiccup was my interaction during boarding, where one crew member asked me to stop filming.  Given my previous experiences on Sri Lankan Airlines where filming has never been an issue, I found this rather unusual.  That said, aside from this isolated incident, service was perfectly adequate, although it didn't particularly stand out.  Overall, the service receives a 6 out of 10. Next we have the seat. This particular A321 Neo seat is one of my personal favorites in the Sri Lankan Airlines fleet.  Not only does it look modern and inviting, but it's also comfortable for medium-all flight.  It comes equipped with a sturdy adjustable headdress, a footdress, and a responsive in-flight entertainment system, that works well throughout the journey.  Overall, this is one aspect of the flight that I was genuinely pleased with, so the seat earns an 8 out of 10.  Onto the catering. Overall, I thought it was good. The stand up for me was the passion for it most. Having quite a sweet tooth, I really enjoyed the dessert.  The main course also pleasantly surprised me. While it didn't look particularly appetizing at first glance, it tasted much better than it appeared.  Sri Lankan Airlines also earns extra points for serving the meal with metal cutlery, which not only elevates the dining experience, but it's also a more environmentally friendly option.  The portion size was generous enough to leave me satisfied as well, taking everything into account the catering receives a 7 out of 10. Lastly, we have in-flight entertainment.  Sri Lankan Airlines offers a decent selection of movies, TV shows, and music, certainly enough to keep most passengers entertained for a flight of this length.  While it doesn't quite match the extensive libraries offered by some world-leading carriers, it does the job well, and the content is refreshed regularly to keep the selection reasonably up to date.  I ended up browsing the library and listening to some music, and unsurprisingly watching Wicked once again. Overall, the in-flight entertainment earns a 6 out of 10.  Before we come to the final verdict, let's take a look at how today's flight scored across each category. And now, for the final score.  Sri Lankan Airlines Airbus A321 Neo from Jakarta to Colombo in Economy class earns an overall sky score of 6.8 out of 10.  So, the big question. Is it worth it flanks Sri Lankan Airlines on this route when alternatives such as Singapore Airlines, Malaysia Airlines or Thai Airways are available?  While those airlines require a layover and two flight sectors, they arguably offer a more refined and consistent product.  If my priority was to simply get from Jakarta to Colombo as quickly and as comfortably as possible, then based on today's experience, I choose the direct Sri Lankan Airlines flight in a heartbeat.  The convenience of a non-stop service is difficult to overlook. That's it. It's important to remember that Sri Lankan Airlines is particularly consistent with its on-world products.  As you've seen throughout this review and in many of my previous Sri Lankan Airlines reviews, the experience can vary significantly depending on the aircraft you are assigned.  On one flight, you could end up with an excellent A321 Neo product. While on another, you might find yourself on an older aircraft with a noticeably less impressive cabin.  In many ways, booking Sri Lankan Airlines can feel like a bit of a lottery.  If you're lucky enough to get an aircraft like this one, you're in for an enjoyable journey.  If not, you could end up paying a similar fare for a considerably less competitive product.  Airlines, like Singapore Airlines, on the other hand, offer a far more consistent experience across their fleet.  But that's a comparison for another video. Thank you very much for watching and welcome to Colombo, the capital city of Sri Lanka.  If there's any way you'd like to see me fly next, be sure to let me know in the comments below.  I always enjoy reading your suggestions and they generally help shape future reviews.  And until next time, bye for now.

But there is a problem here. The first of those A350s won't arrive until  2027 at the earliest. So if Indigo's first widebody of its own is still years away, what am I sitting  on right here? Well, Barty and Elbers made probably the most defining decision of this entire  transformation. They chose not to wait for those A350s and instead start borrowing now.  The first toe in the water came in February of 2023 with a couple of ridiculously dense  531s seat wet-least Turkish Airlines Boeing 777s that they used for flights from Delhi and Mumbai  to Istanbul. They weren't glamorous but this was the first time Indigo was selling widebody seats  on a longer haul service. But then they ramped things up. Just a little. In early 2025, Indigo struck  a deal with North Atlantic to damn police 787 Dreamliners. What's a damn police you may ask?  Well, North supplies the plane, the pilots and the maintenance and Indigo just brings the cabin  crew and then sells you the ticket. Anyway, this deal escalated quickly. One borrow Dreamliner in  February became four by the end of that month and then six were under contract by May.  For reference, that's half of North Atlantic's entire fleet. And the routes quickly followed.  There was Mumbai to Manchester on the 1st of July 2025. This route to Amsterdam, the very next day,  then Copenhagen, Heathrow and even Delhi to Heathrow by February of 2026. An airline whose entire  world was once little A320s hopping around India was now flying all over Europe. All before a  single long haul jet of their own had even arrived. And they've also, I guess, to use the same  analogy, borrowed themselves a network too. Indigo hasn't joined an alliance per se. Instead,  they've stitched together a dozen odd partnerships with some of the world's most notable airlines.  Peating together what is essentially a virtual alliance of their own, one the  construction Indigo ticket right across the globe. And if we zoom out from all of this,  we can start to see the shape of what they're actually building here. The partner network,  that business class seat and the loyalty program. They're all slices of the same cake. Indigo is  slowly baking in everything a proper global airline has. Maybe not a full service one,  but far more premium than they were just five years ago. But here's the thing about baking this  cake. It's not being baked in some quiet home kitchen. This is MasterChef, it's Hell's Kitchen.  The clock is running, the competition is right there, staring them down, and there's a lot of  steps where things can go very wrong. And, well, let's just say not everything has gone to plan.  So far, I organized clean, got space to myself, I popped the screen out, and yeah, they've got  like a bunch of movies and a few TV shows. I might try and watch a movie or something. We all  included all free. Or a whole 30 minutes in, but I would say I am so far pleasantly surprised.  So where did this start to go wrong? Well, through 2025 and into 2026, cracks have started showing up  basically everywhere. And the first one was just purely geopolitics. Remember those Turkish  Boeing 777s? Well, in May of 2025, India and Pakistan had a pretty serious military flare-up.  And Turkey came out and publicly backed Pakistan.  This meant that an indigo flight operated with Turkish planes and Turkish pilots instantly became  politically radioactive in India. This led the DGCA, the Indian Aviation Regulator, to eventually stop  extending the approvals for this service. And by early 2026, those 777s were gone. They were killed  by politics, not by a lack of sales. But that same conflict caused an even bigger problem.  In the aftermath, Pakistan shut its airspace to Indian Airlines completely. And if you look at  the map, that is a disaster for flying to Europe. Indigo's jets now have to fly these long,  looping detours, burning more fuel and adding hours to every trip. Now, to be fair, this wasn't  just an indigo problem. Air India, with its much bigger long haul network, arguably got hit even  harder by all of this. But this is the indigo story, air India can wait for their own video.  This Pakistan airspace problem was not the end of it either. In early 2026, the Iran situation  shut even more airspace in the Middle East. And on top of that, it sent fuel prices soaring.  At one point in March, it got so bad that the entire North Fleet flying for Indigo was temporarily  grounded. And all of this has led Indigo to quietly retreat. Flights to Copenhagen have been  suspended. Manchester, the very first long haul route they have launched, is being temporarily  discontinued. Their words, at the end of August 2026. The Heathrow schedule has been trimmed back,  a fuel surcharge has quietly started appearing on tickets, and one of those six borough dreamliners  is being handed straight back to North. Indigo's own framing here is worth mentioning. They say  demand is actually strong. It's the longer flying times and dramatically escalating costs that are  the problem. Which is probably all true. It just makes this whole glorious bridge to the promised  global airline land a little bit more ironic or curious. I guess there is going to be a real  window here where Indigo's long haul operations might actually shrink before its own planes even arrive.  But none of this really matters in the grand scheme of things, because the biggest crack of all  didn't appear over Pakistan, the Middle East, or Europe. It appeared back home in India.  Okay, so in early December 2025, over about a 72 hour period, the airline that built its name on  punctuality, Indigo, completely falls apart. Thousands of flights are cancelled and hundreds of  thousands of passengers are left stranded across the country. So what happened? Well, throughout  2025, new pilot rest rules came into place in India. Pilots now had to get 48 consecutive hours of  rest every week, up from 36, and night flying was tightened right up. That 48 hour requirement is  one of the strictest in the world. Stricted them both the US and Europe, but they didn't appear  out of thin air. They followed years of growing alarm about pilot fatigue in India, including pilots  literally dying on duty. And I guess more crucially and relevant, they were not a surprise. These rules  were announced back in early 2024. The airlines fought them, the airlines lost, and then they had  nearly two years to prepare. So how did Indigo prepare? Well, according to the pilot's federation,  they basically didn't. They kept running their famously lean staffing strategy right through  the warning period. And on the second of December, everything went wrong at once.  Fog delayed one evening flight, then that crew hit their legal duty limit, and then there's no  rested reserve crew to replace them. Why? Well, reserve crews are expensive slack, and Indigo doesn't  do expensive slack. So that flight gets cancelled, and now that plane and crew are stuck in the wrong  city, which means tomorrow's schedule starts breaking to 1 delay becomes 10, 10 becomes a nation-wide  meltdown. It got so bad that the government stepped in to cap airfares and Indian railways  started adding extra carriages to trains. Now, to be fair, the acute chaos didn't actually last  that long. Within about a week, Indigo had stabilized things, but this was a patch together recovery.  The government forced Indigo to shrink its schedule by around 10%, and things didn't properly  return to normal until well into 2026. reviews.transcript_full: What's EVA Air's long haul economy actually like? After recently flying their excellent premium economy to Taipei, let's take a look at their standard economy. >> [music] >> Hello and welcome back to K S Aviation. Today, we're at Taipei Taoyuan International Airport getting ready to fly home on board EVA Air's flagship Boeing 777-300ER in economy class. We've got a long flight ahead of us, so let's get checked in. Here at TPE, [music] EVA Air exclusively uses Terminal 2. The airline has plenty of check-in counters, and [music] since they open around 2 and 1/2 hours before departure, there weren't any major lines. The entire process was quick, efficient, and friendly. After a quick security check, we are now airside. There's still nearly 2 hours until boarding, so I spent some time exploring TPE's brand new Terminal 3 North Concourse. After a bit of exploring, I made my way over to gate C6 where BR8 was boarding. A quick look at our aircraft for today, Bravo 16716, and it was finally time to head on board. >> Bye-bye. 66 >> If you'd like to see what EVA Air's business class is like, be sure to check out this video. And if you're interested in their premium economy, I've got a review on that as well. But for today, let's check out their economy. Welcome to seat 46 Kilo, a window seat located in the second row of EVA Air's economy cabin. EVA Air's 777 has three configurations. While the premium cabins remain mostly the same across all aircraft, economy varies. Newer 777s feature a 3-4-3 layout, while older aircraft like today's have a more spacious 3-3-3 configuration. This version features 221 Collins Aerospace Pinnacle seats spread across two cabins. Starting at the top, [music] we have a nicely padded four-way adjustable headrest. Moving down, the seat back and cushion are both comfortable, while the seat itself [music] measures 18 in wide. Turning around, the adjustable 10-in IFE screen features both a headphone jack and USB A port. As for the content, we'll take a closer look once we're in the air. [music] Below that is a large and sturdy bi-fold tray table. Underneath sits a spacious literature pocket containing the safety card, inflight magazine, and a small trash bag. Legroom is also very generous, which means I'll be very comfortable throughout the flight. Each seat is also equipped with a universal power outlet, which I found the charging speeds pretty fast. Soon, we were ready for departure. And with EVA Air's new safety video playing, it was time to go. While we taxi, let's talk about today's aircraft. Bravo 16716 is a 16.5-year-old Boeing 777-300ER. It first flew in November 2009 and was delivered to EVA Air the following month. Interestingly, this aircraft was involved in an incident in July of 2024. While operating a flight from Los Angeles to Taipei, the crew encountered an issue with engine number two and returned back [music] to LAX. The aircraft landed safely and later returned to service. Hopefully, we won't be repeating that experience today. Although, we may find out pretty soon as we're now lined up on the runway. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Now that we're the air, let's take a look at the amenities. Waiting at each seat was a nice plush pillow along with a large soft blanket. I especially liked the texture of the blanket, which felt comfortable and cozy. Also provided were a pair of earbuds. While they're fairly standard, I appreciated the soft rubber tips, which made them fit very comfortably. While we wait for the meal service, let's check out the in-flight entertainment system. During takeoff, the glare from the sun actually revealed a fairly large scratch on the screen. Fortunately, it wasn't very noticeable once the display was turned on. The screen itself is actually quite responsive. When it comes to movies, EVA Air offers a large selection, including many new and popular titles. There's also a dedicated TV [music] and music section with many shows featuring full seasons and albums available to enjoy. One of my favorite features is the dedicated kids section, which is great for families traveling with children. Lastly, here's the flight map. It offers several different views and provides plenty of information throughout the flight. Unfortunately, there are no exterior cameras available. Overall, I quite like this in-flight entertainment system. It's responsive, easy to navigate, and does a great job of keeping me entertained throughout the flight. Around 25 minutes after takeoff, the cabin crew came around with a pre-meal snack consisting of mixed nuts, crackers, and a cup of [music] water. For some reason, it took another 30 minutes before the main meal service began. I'm not exactly sure why, but by that point, I was definitely starting to get a little hungry. Thankfully, the wait was worth it as the crew returned with many cards and [music] two meal options to choose from. The choices were Gambay barbecue karubi with steamed rice or spaghetti with seafood in a creamy mushroom sauce. If you don't know, Gambay is a well-known upscale restaurant here in Taiwan. [music] So, my choice was pretty obvious. The presentation of this meal honestly looks really nice. I especially like the individually packaged side dishes as they gave the meal [music] a more premium course-like feel. Along with that, the metal cutlery included [music] in the packet is a nice touch. And even the little tea mug feels surprisingly premium. I then got my drink of choice, an ice-cold Coke. Now, onto the food. Starting with the bread, it's nicely toasted and when paired with butter isn't dry at all. This small appetizer appears to be some noodles with slices of meat. Personally, I found it to be a little salty, but otherwise it was quite good. Next to that is a cup of fruit. For some [music] reason, EVA Air never fails to deliver when it comes to fruit. It's always sweet, juicy, and refreshing. Finally, it's time for the main dish. Starting from left to right, there are several layers of barbecue karubi served over steamed rice. On the right are some vegetables, including broccoli and bell pepper. Sitting on top is a piece of tamagoyaki, a Japanese-style folded omelet. This dish was actually really tasty. The beef was flavorful and remained surprisingly moist. In the corner were some kimchi along with a really [music] tasty green sauce, both of which added even more flavor to the meal. I then devoured the entire meal in no time, and it was finally time for dessert. Today's dessert appeared to be some sort of strawberry pudding topped with a small layer of jelly sauce. It's certainly an interesting choice, but at least EVA Air didn't skip dessert. Honestly, that was one of the best airplane meals I've had in a while. Everything was delicious, and I almost forgot I was eating an economy class meal. As the crew came around to collect my now completely empty tray, they also handed me a bottle of water. Hopefully, that'll keep me hydrated while I get some rest. After the meal, I decided to check out the restroom. Inside, you'll find a large changing table, two full-size mirrors, and a clean spacious layout. As for amenities, there was hand soap, lotion, and even a selection of scented sprays available for passengers to use. Moving over to the sink, it's decently sized and features adjustable water temperature. The water pressure was decent as well. Cups and napkins were also provided on the wall free for passengers to [music] use. The wooden floor was pretty clean, and any water visible on the floor was from me washing my hands, which I cleaned up afterwards. Overall, this is a nice lavatory with plenty of amenities and a surprisingly spacious feel. I then spent some time exploring the aircraft. Near the rear galley, I found an even larger lavatory, which offered noticeably more space than the one I just visited. Also located in the rear galley was a self-serve snack station, where passengers could help themselves to a selection of snacks throughout the flight. After a bit of exploring, I eventually headed back to my seat and noticed a couple of small issues. There was a minor crack near the tray table latch, along with some wear around it. Honestly, it didn't bother me too much, since it was purely [music] cosmetic and didn't affect the functionality of the seat at all. As the sun slowly began to set over the Pacific, [music] it seemed like the perfect time to see just how comfortable this seat would be for the [music] long flight ahead. Holding down the button on the armrest and leaning back, the seat reclines a fair amount. About half a window's worth. Combined with the generous legroom, I found it quite comfortable and had no trouble getting some rest. I actually ended up sleeping for around 4 hours. When I woke up, it was time for a mid-flight snack. Yes, EVA Air actually serves a snack between meals, which is always appreciated on a long-haul flight. Today's offering was a sandwich filled with tuna, lettuce, cheese, and tomato. It certainly looked appetizing and thankfully it tasted just as good. A cup of water was also handed out alongside it. After the snack, I decided to test out the Wi-Fi. During this flight, EVA Air was actually running a promotion that offered complimentary Wi-Fi to all passengers. After connecting, I ran a quick speed test. While the speeds were definitely on the slower side, I couldn't complain too much, considering it was completely free. At the end of the day, it's still better than having no Wi-Fi at all. By this point in the flight, there were only around 4 hours remaining. I spent some time getting a bit of work done, and before I knew it, the pre-arrival meal service was underway. Just like the first meal, there were two options to choose from. This time, the choices were a savory porridge with chicken and corn, or a vegetable frittata with bacon and roasted potatoes. Both sounded quite good, but I ultimately went with a porridge as I was in a mood for a lighter breakfast. A short while later, my tray arrived, and once again, the presentation looks quite nice. Included was the same bread roll as before, while the side containers held an appetizer and a serving of fresh fruit. The appetizer consisted of mushroom, seaweed, egg, and bell peppers. It was surprisingly flavorful and seasoned just right. Moving on to the main dish, it came with a packet of fish floss to mix into the porridge. Combined with the chicken and corn already in the porridge, it made for a very comforting breakfast. After a long flight, I especially appreciated having something warm and easy to eat. The flavors were excellent, and the corn added a nice burst of sweetness in every bite. Overall, I really enjoyed this breakfast. To finish things off, I dug into the fruit. Just like the first meal, it was sweet, juicy, and disappeared in no time. After the meal, I made another trip to the lavatory, and it was just as clean as before. I wish I could say this flight was any level of luxury for me, but being considered the budget long-haul carrier from Germany, they definitely slacked in some areas. This one is pretty typical, no surprises besides the slightly higher image quality because of the 4K screen. Still a very popular feature on any flight. Condor also has Wi-Fi on board this flight, charging a steep 7 euros for just text messaging and 20 euros for the full flight internet. Not my cup of tea. The IFE offered other things like Bluetooth and custom settings as well. The seat offers a mere 30 inches of pitch, 18 inches of width, and a nice 8 and 1/2 inches of recline. And, of course, some USB ports and a headphone jack for your wired desires. For the drink service, I stuck with apple juice. This was then followed by a meal. I did not film the meal, even though I've done these videos countless times. So, feel free to pause and read the label there if you'd like. All in all, the meal was a solid seven out of 10. Later on in the flight, the crew came around with some water, and I, being fairly reliant on the substance for life and hydration, went ahead and took a cup of my own. I don't know if I happen to get the handicap lav, or if all the lavatories were like this, but this place could fit at least two people. On top of that, it was clean and had an amazing striped accent wall, which is absolutely fantastic. The sink had some interesting signage on it, and the finishing touch was the trash pedal so that you don't feel like you have to wash your hands all over again. I'm sure there was a purpose to filming me do this, but I don't remember what that was. I thought I'd let you all watch anyway. Before the flight, we gave all members of the crew little goody bags. Inside the goody bag was some snacks, which we definitely cracked open after I stopped recording. I guess today I'm feeling the cup shots. There wasn't really a breakfast, but I did get a box pizza as a pre-arrival snack. This was not too greasy and pretty tasty for what it was. I've got to be honest, I got on this flight filled with anger and frustration of how both Lufthansa and Condor treated me and my reservation throughout this trip. A mix of passing the blame and lack of internal communication led to me having to take a flight that no longer worked with my schedule. But by the time this flight reached the point of landing, my hopes for Condor were definitely met and in some ways exceeded. This flight genuinely surprised me for an airline that's supposed to be a more low-cost option versus Lufthansa. It wasn't all perfect, but Condor definitely holds a certain quality to it that at some point will have me flying them again. With all that being said, let's see how it holds up against the legit score. In terms of the seat, it was a modern-day thin seat with some of the worst long-haul legroom I've seen, but good recline and well-maintained. There was no lack of amenities, either. This was super impressive. Entertainment-wise, the IFE was great, but the Wi-Fi options cost money and didn't seem all that worthwhile. For service, the ground staff failed to change my flights to something that worked better, even when I opted to take an extra day of travel in order to better align with my goals. I was forced into taking this flight for a delay that was not my fault. I will say from the agent's perspective, I don't think they could see all the previous cancellations and delays of this trip as I was rebooked to a shorter Condor flight the day prior, which inevitably caused this mess. From their end, I only had a short delay which caused a misconnection. The in-flight service was great. I have no complaints here. For value, I can't say it's a good value because it was not what I paid for and was not what I wanted. Value versus competition, the product was still pretty good and it definitely was not the worst way to fly home. And of course, the cleanliness. The cabin and lavatory were super clean other than the tray table. I ended up awarding the lavatory a bonus point for the sheer size of it. Easily the best lavatory I've seen in a while. Overall, the flight scored 37 out of 50, which amounts to a 74% a solid C tier flight. But had this flight been what I booked or at least what worked for me, the airline's handling of the situation dropped its score by several points. At the end of the day, I would still recommend flying Condor. Just preferably do it by choice and not by force. Welcome to the city where at least seven people call home. It's Seattle, Washington. My flight today was uneventful once on board and I've got to say the in-flight experience was more than what I expected. It's always difficult rebooking with an airline who has limited code share partners or at least partners that fly to the US in any way, shape, or form. Regardless, I walked off this flight with a smile, at least up until I had to deal with more Condor ground staff that didn't seem to have any power to do anything for my reservation.
