reviews.transcript_full: KLM once used to be our favorite airline, but recent experiences have not been great. We haven't tried our economy product in a while, so we are curious to find out if flying standard economy with them is still worth it and if they live up to their own slogan, travel well. So, let's have a look at our full flight experience including an emergency landing and one a very questionable food item. We're flying to Bangkok and our journey starts at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. We booked an economy standard ticket and that includes one piece of check-in luggage of maximum 23 kg and free seat selection upon check-in. Since we're flying economy, there are no further perks for us, which means we entertained ourselves by walking over this glass floor luggage belt. Last time we flew with KLM, we were in premium economy, which was fine, but not amazing. And especially the breakfast eggs were terrible. So, here's hoping we don't have to deal with those again. All right, let's go and experience economy standard. Time for our flight and here we are boarding the Boeing 777-200, which is set up in a 3-4-3 configuration. It's a full flight and we were seated apart because we wanted to get the full economy standard experience and did not pay for advanced seat selection. Also, because our ticket includes free seat selection during check-in, we figured if we were the first to check-in, we could still select two seats next to each other. We were wrong. Despite the seat map showing lots of availability mere minutes before check-in, the only option to be seated together the second check-in opened were paid seats. A little strange if you ask us, but okay. A very kind solo passenger offered to switch seats, which was a win-win situation since these seats are a lot less wide than we remember and are definitely not made for people with broad shoulders. Remember this solo passenger for later though. So, let's have a look at the seats. When you enter the plane, there's a blanket and basic pillow waiting for you. We have to say the pillow and the blanket feel a bit cheap and especially the pillow is not very comfortable. As for the legroom, it's pretty standard with 79 cm and when the person in front of you reclines, there's still luckily a bit of space left. The seat also comes with a split fold-out table and there's an adjustable headrest. For charging your device, you can either use the USB-A port integrated in the screen or the power outlet below the seat, but it seems that it doesn't get cleaned that often. Now, let's get ready for takeoff and continue our review in disguise. Shortly after takeoff, we received a wet towel and a headset. So, up until that point, you could not watch anything on your screen if you forgot to bring your own. We suspect it's because boarding started later than planned, but we're not sure. Let us know in the comments if you know if this is always the case with KLM. Speaking of the entertainment system, I have to say we were pretty impressed with it and dare I say it, it's one of the better ones we've experienced in economy recently. The home screen nicely shows a timeline of what you can expect during the flight. There's also a pretty good selection of entertainment. You can find the in-flight drinks menu and of course the most important part, a working in-flight map. Yay! To help us celebrate having a good in-flight map, make sure to like this video and subscribe to our channel. Aside from that, there's also free Wi-Fi on board that allows for messaging and emails. If you need more internet capabilities, you do have to pay for it. Before we move on to the food, let's quickly check out the toilets. There's only hand soap available though and no moisturizer creams that other airlines sometimes have. Time for our first meal, which was dinner. And we had the option to choose between the classic chicken or pasta. So, of course, we chose both. As for the sides, there were some peppers stuffed with cream cheese, a mystery dip that was definitely not mayo, some olives and sun-dried tomatoes, and finally, a bread roll. Taste-wise, I'm not sure what to say, except that we recommend the chicken over the pasta. And yeah, don't come to this flight hungry. Right after the meal service, something unexpected happened. Shortly after we were up in the air, a flight attendant noticed that a passenger was feeling unwell, and then someone yelled if there was a doctor on board. And remember that kind solo traveler offering to switch seats? Turns out that person is a doctor and rushed to help immediately. After some time, it was decided that we were going to have to make an emergency medical landing, and that's why we were now heading to Istanbul instead of Bangkok. To be able to do so, the plane started dumping fuel to get ready for landing. We never experienced an emergency landing before, and we really hope that the person in question has made a full recovery in the meantime. We have to say, it made for an impressive sight, though, and Istanbul by night looks very beautiful from above. Once the plane got a whole lot lighter, we made our descent, and once we made it, we awaited the medical staff to do their thing and take away the sick passenger. After refueling, we quickly left again for Bangkok, and the whole situation only took about 1 and 1/2 hours or so, which was very impressive. With the plane safely back in the air and most people trying to sleep, it was time for the dessert portion of the meal, and a brownie. The timing was very unfortunate, because everyone was trying to sleep and these things have the loudest wrappers imaginable. Then finally after some sleep and with only 2 and 1/2 hours of the flight left, it was time for breakfast. We were lucky to not have the dreaded eggs again, but we're not sure if what we got instead is any better. Dear viewer, behold the KLM breakfast. A cup of sour fruit, strawberry yogurt, and what's that? Oh yes, it's a Dutch pastry snack known as a cheese roll or kaasbroodje. Only eaten for breakfast by those who are either under 21 or hungover or both. With the Dutch travelers, you can count on some nostalgia and our love for greasy savory pastries, but to serve this for breakfast to an international audience even is definitely a choice and not a very good one if you ask us. Especially because the cheese roll wasn't executed that well. It was just very fatty and greasy and not something you want to start your morning with. So with a disappointing breakfast done and after 12 plus hours of flying, it was finally time to land >> [music] >> in Bangkok. With us safely arriving at Suvarnabhumi International Airport, it's time to have a look at what we paid for this eventful flight and if we think KLM is still worth it. For a direct flight from Amsterdam to Bangkok, we paid 950 euros per person for a return ticket including one piece of check-in luggage and so-called free seat selection during check-in. Although, I wouldn't attach too much value to that. As for the emergency landing, this was obviously not planned, but was handled very well by the cabin crew who were attentive overall. The in-flight entertainment system was good, too, but the food was honestly very sad, and especially the breakfast is a poor showing. The seats have also become very thin and narrow, and the overall cleanliness is debatable. It seems that KLM is dealing with some sort of identity crisis where its most recent campaign slogan "Travel Well" alludes to flying with a good experience, whilst their pricing and ancillary revenue strategies creams low-cost carrier, but without the fares to match it. So, while the flight was pretty okay and definitely not the worst we've experienced in economy, it's also not worth it to pay a whole lot extra for, since the experience as a whole is just mediocre at best. Oh, well, at least it was a direct flight. Well, sort of. If you want to see what flying premium economy with KLM is like, click here, and otherwise, thank you so much for watching. Bye.

Once the jet bridge was connected, it was our turn to leave the plane. And after thanking the crew for the lovely service, Thank you for the service. It was lovely. Thank you. Thank you. It was great. Thank you for the service. Thank you. We were off the plane and on the jet bridge. Once past the jet bridge, it came time to look for immigration to be allowed into the country. While it looked a little bit long, there were multiple immigration checkpoints and the lines kept moving. After immigration, we passed through the baggage claim area. Since we had no checked bags, we were able to continue straight forward to customs and the arrivals hall. There are public transportation options available from the airport, but for today, we will be taking a Grab. To get there, we took the famous stepless moving walkway, which I quickly learned is basically a rite of passage at this airport. Outside the airport are dedicated taxi, shuttle, and Grab pickup areas. Grab is Southeast Asia's main ride-hailing similar to Uber or Lyft, and it's one of the easiest ways to get from the airport into Bangkok. At the dedicated Grab pickup area, there are zones clearly marked by letter to help passengers and drivers find each other more easily. Once in the city, it was time to explore Bangkok. One of the city's most famous sites [music] is the Wat Pho. It is filled with beautiful decorated chedis rising in colorful intricate patterns across the temple grounds and home to the massive reclining Buddha. Wat Pho is so famous that Obama came here during a state visit as well. Nearby is the Grand Palace, one of Bangkok's most recognizable landmarks and one of the most important historical sites in Thailand. For more context on Thai history and culture, the National Museum of Bangkok offers a look at the country's art, artifacts, and royal heritage. But Bangkok is not just temples and museums. The city is also known for its street food, busy roads, tuk-tuks, and the kind of organized chaos that makes it feel alive at almost every hour. And few places capture that energy like Khao San Road, one of Bangkok's most famous streets [music] and a major gathering point for travelers. People were so friendly here and kept offering me massages. From historic temples to street-level energy, Bangkok offers a completely different kind of experience after arriving from Singapore. This flight was not the longest or the most expensive, but sometimes travel doesn't need to be extreme to be memorable. Singapore Airlines delivered a polished and comfortable experience, and Bangkok gave us the perfect reminder of why we travel in the first place. For the food, the history, the chaos, the beauty, and the feeling that somewhere completely different [music] can suddenly feel exciting and familiar all at once. Thank you very much for watching the Singapore to Bangkok trip report. If you enjoyed the video, consider subscribing so you don't miss the next flight. Let me know what you think in the comments below. I'd read and respond to every single one. You were incredible, Bangkok. Your temples, your food, your lights, your chaos, and all your beauty came together to make this city unforgettable. I can't wait to see you again. And until then, I'll see you in the next trip.

reviews.transcript_full: Hi there, my name is Earl and welcome back to Bahi Mennez. Hong Kong airport is an AV geek's paradise, and I could honestly spend an entire day here just walking around the terminal like I'm in Disneyland. So, I headed straight to the sky bridge near gate 24 to check it out for myself. Opened in late 2022, the Skybridge connects Terminal One with the Terminal One satellite concourse and is considered the world's longest airside bridge. The bridge measures 200 m long and 20 m wide and sits 28 m above the ground, allowing even the world's largest passenger aircraft, the Airbus A380, to pass beneath it. The glass flooring offers a unique perspective, giving passengers a bird's eyee view of aircraft moving below them. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to San Juan, Puerto Rico. Our time in the sun is over and now we have to head back home. Today, we're going to be flying in first class on United. We'll be checking out their service on board a Boeing 737 MAX 9. Join us as we put one of United's newest first class cabins to the test. We'll evaluate the seat comfort, in-flight service, and overall value of United's premium cabin experience. This is also a dinner flight, so we're going to evaluate United's catering and see if it's any good. Plus, stick around and we'll tell you how much we paid for this flight so you can determine if it's worth the upgrade. Welcome to the capital of Puerto Rico, San Juan. We're starting today at Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, airport code SJU. Puerto Rico is a US overseas territory located between the Dominican Republic and the US Virgin Islands. No passport is required if you're traveling from the mainland US. SJU is the busiest airport in the Caribbean with over 13 and 1/2 million passengers in 2025. The island is home to more than 3 million people. If you're flying out of San Juan, there's one thing you must do before you head to your airline check-in or TSA, and that is go to the USDA inspection. If you've ever flown out of Hawaii, you've probably seen this. Among other things, they're checking to make sure you're not taking any fresh fruits or vegetables or plants off the island. You'll see signs for this just inside the terminal. Make sure you complete this before heading to your airline to check in. With USDA inspection complete, let's head over to United. >> [music] >> Our first class ticket gets us access to the priority check-in line. Two 70-lb check bags are included with our ticket. The bag drop was a quick process and now it's off to security. If the lines are long, you can also walk over to the other terminal and use that checkpoint. All of the gates in San Juan are connected airside. After security, you're dropped into a duty-free store. Good to note, even if you're traveling back to the mainland, you can buy duty-free. Just like Delta and American, United does not provide lounge access on a domestic first class ticket. That wouldn't matter today because United does not have a lounge in San Juan. But there are a few Priority Pass and credit card lounge options at SJU. The Global Lounge Network operates two lounges, a small location near the JetBlue gates and a second location near the C gates. This is closer to American, United, Delta, and Southwest flights. Both of these accept Priority Pass. We reviewed one of those lounges in a previous video when we flew JetBlue Mint. We'll leave a link in the description if you want to check that out. Plus, now's a good time to click that like button and subscribe so you never miss one of our flight reviews. We missed the Escape Lounge last time we were here, so let's go check that out. This lounge is located near gate B2. >> [music] >> There are a few ways to access the Escape Lounge. You can access it with the American Express Platinum or Centurion card. Delta Reserve card members are also eligible if flying on a same-day Delta ticket. Amex card holders receive two complimentary guests. This lounge also sells day passes on a space-available basis for $55 per person. Upon arrival, there was a waitlist today, so I signed up. They text you when it's your turn to enter. Unfortunately, the wait today was only about 10 minutes. The Escape Lounge is open daily from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. The lounge is located one level below the gates. It's not a large space, but it's nicely broken up into a few different seating areas. There's a bar across from the elevator and main staircase. It features a limited selection of complimentary alcohol and non-alcoholic drinks. Oddly, they didn't have any beer, which was disappointing since they advertised their partnership with a San Juan brewery. In the center of the lounge is a food buffet. It featured a decent mix of hot and cold items. The shredded meat was actually quite good. You can definitely find enough food here for a meal before a flight. There were several friendly staff walking around taking drink orders. This included coffee, tea, and water. The main coffee machine by the buffet was out of order. Seating is broken into a few different areas. There are dining tables and chairs near the buffet and tucked behind the elevator and staircase. Near the bar area was a sofa. Many of the seats were perfect for solo travelers and featured high walls for privacy. There were also pairs of seats together. It was tough to film since this lounge was quite busy most of our visit. There are three single user restrooms in this lounge and they were kept clean. There are no showers in this lounge. The lounge is at ground level and does offer a pretty good view of the nearby Southwest Airlines gate. There is Wi-Fi. It was easy to connect and speeds were very fast. So, this Escape Lounge isn't bad. It's a little small and there was a short wait to get in today. Now, it's about half empty. The only big problem is it's really warm. The air conditioning's not working, so they have some temporary units and looks like they've been here for a while, so I'm guessing it's always like this. Having been to all of the lounges at SJU, the Escape Lounge definitely had the best food, but the other lounges aren't bad options either and I think they had a better selection of drinks. >> [music] >> Our 3-hour and 30-minute flight today takes us 1,570 miles from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Washington Dulles Airport on board of Boeing 737 Max 9 in first class. Time to board our flight. United uses the B gates in San Juan. Boarding here can get a bit hectic as the gate areas are a bit crowded. We've said it before about United, but one of our biggest complaints with United's boarding process is that they board the 1K members well before zone one, even if they're not in first class. So, even if you're in zone one, you're going to be competing for overhead bin space with the 1Ks who got on before you. This can also mean you may be putting your bag in economy, which on a paid first class ticket is not an ideal situation. Boarding started right on time. On this 737 Max 9, there are 20 first class seats in a standard 2-2 layout. The aircraft also features 45 extra legroom economy seats and 114 standard economy seats in a 3-3 layout. I'm in 1B today, the bulkhead. This flight was completely full. One of the reasons we tend to avoid the bulkhead is there's no under seat storage. All personal items and bags must go in the overhead bin for takeoff and landing. Fortunately, there was enough overhead bin space on today's flight. The advantage of the bulkhead is that no one's going to recline into your space. Today, we're on a 2-year-old 737 Max 9 featuring United's new signature interior. Depending on what version of this plane you get, [music] you may or may not get an IFE screen. The older Max 9s don't have screens. The first class seats are 20 in wide with a pitch of 37 in. The legroom is good and on par with other domestic first class seats. The crew had all of the window shades closed to keep the cabin cool and the lights were very dim, so it was difficult to film the cabin upon boarding. Here's a shot of these seats from a previous trip we had on United's Max 9. The legroom in the bulkhead is decent. However, there are no cutouts at the bottom of the partition for your feet, so keep that in mind. We like to see individual air vents above. This is also where you'll find the reading light. There's a wide center armrest. At the front is a small table. Tucked between the seats is a space to hold a water bottle and the universal power outlet and USB-C port. Unfortunately, my outlet didn't work, but the USB-C port did. In front of the seat is a small storage pocket. This was large enough to hold a tablet. And under the center armrest is a small storage cubby. The bifold tray table pops out of the armrest. It was sturdy and it featured an integrated device holder. Under the armrest closer to the aisle is another storage compartment, large enough for a laptop or something skinny. The seats feature an adjustable headrest that goes both up and down and the wings fold in. Blankets were also passed out by the flight crew, which is a nice touch. Overall, the seat is comfortable with decent padding for our 3 and 1/2 hour flight. Pre-departure drinks of water or sparkling wine were offered, both in plastic cups. I had some water. We do wish United offered a full selection of pre-departure beverages like some other carriers. Boarding wrapped up and we pushed back from the gate a few minutes early. Let's get up in the air and we'll take a look at the entertainment options on board. As we mentioned earlier, these newer Max 9s feature IFE screens. Each seat has a 13.3-in touchscreen. The screen is bright and fairly responsive. The system features a large selection of movies and TV series. The IFE supports Bluetooth as well. I was able to easily connect my AirPods. Wired earbuds are also available from the crew if you forget to bring your own. This plane features a fully interactive inflight map, and the flight tracker allows for a selection of views. I also like that I could access the onboard menu in the IFE. Since I'm not a frequent flyer on United, it was nice to see which drinks were available. Wi-Fi is available for a fee. $8 or 800 miles for MileagePlus members, or $10 for everyone else. Free messaging is available regardless, but you do need to activate it. T-Mobile customers are eligible for free Wi-Fi as well. I did connect to the free messaging, but I couldn't get it to work 100% today. This is a good time for me to mention I'm traveling with my good friend Mira on this flight, and she did get the messaging to work. We were in Puerto Rico on a volunteer trip to assist local animal welfare organizations. We helped out with a community vaccine clinic and rescued some street dogs. If you'd like to learn more about the organization's work and their mission, we'll leave a link in the description. Once connected to the Wi-Fi, you can use United's private screening library of onboard media on your own device. There was a good selection of movies and TV shows, but it was similar to what was available on the IFE. About 20 minutes after takeoff, the crew started the onboard service. United Airlines lets you pre-order on most flights that offer a meal service, including flights to and from United hubs. 5 days ahead of your flight, you'll get an email or push prompt to select your meal. Catering is limited out of San Juan, so there were only two options for our flight, chicken or a vegetarian pasta. Be aware, there is no option to order a special meal on this route. Working front to back, the purser came around to confirm our meal choices and take drink orders. Drinks arrived with a small ramekin of mixed nuts. I ordered a gin and tonic. It was served with a second round by default. The purser gave me the unopened can of tonic so I could decide how much to use. This was a thoughtful touch. Hot towels were then distributed, which is always nice. We've been missing this on Delta. Meal service comes out as a single tray. I pre-ordered the grilled chicken breast with almond rice pilaf, red pepper sauce, and grilled vegetables. This was accompanied by a side salad of fresh cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and red onions. Dinner also includes a roll with butter. My friend Mira had the cheese manicotti with marinara and alfredo sauce. Overall, I thought the quality of the food was good. The chicken wasn't dry, which was my fear. The salad was an interesting mix. It was a lot of raw red onions. The bread was fresh, but could have been warmed up. For dessert, the menu had listed a cheesecake, but we received a flan. This was a decent and nice local element for a flight from Puerto Rico. Following the meal, I ordered a cup of coffee. The purser checked in periodically offering drink refills, but no other food or snacks were offered on this flight. There's one lavatory at the front of the 737 for first class passengers. Unfortunately, on these Max 9s, they're a bit tight, but they get the job done. This one was kept clean during our flight. I spent the rest of the flight enjoying a movie on the onboard IFE. Trevor and I fly a lot of Delta in and out of DC. So, it was interesting to give United a shot. I think this crew in particular was outgoing, friendly, and worked hard the entire flight. The purser and a second flight attendant served the first class cabin and this meant service was fast and efficient. On many domestic flights, there's often one flight attendant up front. We were soon approaching northern Virginia. Enjoy the sunset approach and landing into Dulles and we'll be back to wrap things up. Welcome to Dulles Airport. We have made it. Uh that was a pretty good flight. The flight crew was super friendly. The flight attendant, especially during uh meal service, was very proactive with drink refills. They were very quick to start the meal service and clear the trays. We didn't see much of them after that, but we were in the bulkhead, so it was very easy to wave to them if we needed something. Overall, I was very happy with that flight. I'm going to get my bags and I'll finish the rest of this with voiceover. Not only was this a pleasant flight, we also arrived about 30 minutes early, which is always nice. So, how much did we pay for today's flight? For this one-way ticket in first class from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Washington Dulles, we paid $573. Keep in mind that that fare included my two checked bags. Overall, I thought that was good value for this flight. The flight crew, especially the purser, were friendly and I would definitely fly United again. Today I'm flying Sydney to Adelaide on a Boeing 737-800.  It's a short flight just under 2 hours, and in this video I'll show you the lounge  the seat and what this flight actually costs. Qantas started in 1920, not in Sydney, not in Melbourne, but in Outback Queensland.  Two pilots, one aircraft, mail routes across the runways.  Flying wasn't glamorous, it was survival, and that survival mindset shaped the airlines  DNA.  Later on it would also become the problem.  So this is the Qantas domestic lounge?  The lounge is wide and spacious and relatively empty.  People were mostly working with a handful being the exception to this.  And you can see why, with loads of places to charge your devices and bright open spaces,  it makes it feel like it was built for efficiency.  Pretty much like Qantas itself.  I just got an apple juice to drink, but they had a lot of food on offer.  There's quite a lot of space, they've got TVs round to tenement so you can basically  watch the news.  There was a lot of clanging of colour, which I noticed, but I mean, I'm not really too bothered  about it.  It's just because it's a huge space and there's a lot of effort, okay?  By the jet age Qantas had it all, it had global routes, a huge safety reputation, and the  famous kangaroo route to London.  It was iconic, prestigious, but prestige didn't guarantee a profit.  And when Anset collapsed, Qantas absorbed international routes extremely quickly.  They had a bigger network, bigger costs, and thinner margins.  From the outside, everything looks stable, but internally, it wasn't.  Okay, so it's time for boarding now, let's see how busy it is at the gate.  The crew was super friendly, highly rated.  It was a very short route to the plane.  So there's no interlite entertainment to my knowledge, you might go with that, but  what I can see is, you can have just a new bike.  Oh, they do have screens, they just come out of the ceiling.  So this is a Boeing 737800, it's a standard Qantas domestic setup, I'm 172 centimeters tall,  but between 2011 and 2014, Qantas was anything but quite financially.  Here's the table, quite spacious, I mean it's a standard table, I don't really what you'd  expect.  I guess in terms of measurement, it's about two hands, we got some food, but I  wasn't really sure what it was.  It was kind of okay, a lot of people were rejecting it, which was kind of surprising, but it  tasted all right, it didn't taste super salty or anything, it just tasted like a sandwich.  If you're wondering how loud it gets in the cabin, it's about 76 decimals on average,  and then we pretty much landed and that was it. reviews.transcript_full: ഹായ് ഗയ്സ് വെൽക്കം ബാക്ക് ടു കുട്ടി ട്രിപ്പ്സ്. അപ്പൊ ഇന്നത്തെ വ്ലോഗ് നമ്മൾ ഒരു എയർ ഇന്ത്യ റിവ്യൂ ആക്കാം എന്ന് വിചാരിച്ചു. ഞാനിപ്പോൾ കോപ്പൺ വേഗനിൽ നിന്ന് ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് ട്രാവൽ ചെയ്യുകയാണ് എയർ ഇന്ത്യയിൽ. ഫസ്റ്റ് ടൈം ആണ് ഞാൻ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ പോകുന്നത്. ഒരുപാട് കാര്യങ്ങൾ എയർ ഇന്ത്യയെ പറ്റി നമ്മൾ എല്ലാ ദിവസവും കേൾക്കുന്നുണ്ട്. അപ്പൊ എങ്ങനെയാണ് എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ട്രാവൽ [സംഗീതം] അതിന്റെ ഒരു റിവ്യൂ എക്സ്പീരിയൻസ് ആണ് ഞാൻ ഈ ഒരു വ്ലോഗിൽ ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നത്. സോ അപ്പം എന്റെ പെട്ടികളൊക്കെ ഇവിടെ റെഡിയാണ്. സോ നമുക്ക് അപ്പം എയർ ഇന്ത്യ എക്സ്പ്രസ്സിൽ നാട്ടിലോട്ട് പോകാം. സോ ലെറ്റ്സ് ഗെറ്റ് ഇന്റു ദ വീഡിയോ. ഈ രണ്ട് വലിയ പെട്ടികൾ ഞാൻ പൊക്കുന്നത് കണ്ടിട്ട് ഞാൻ ഒരു സംഭവമാണെന്ന് ആരും വിചാരിക്കണ്ട ആ പെട്ടിയിൽ ഒന്നുമില്ല എനിക്ക് ആക്ച്വലി ഇവിടുന്ന് അങ്ങോട്ടല്ല കൊണ്ടുപോകാനുള്ളത് വീട്ടിൽ നിന്ന് ഇങ്ങോട്ടാണ് സാധനങ്ങൾ വേണ്ടത് സോ കാലിപ്പെട്ടിയുമായിട്ട് അങ്ങനെ വീട്ടിൽ എത്തുന്നതും കാത്ത ഉള്ള ഒരു യാത്രയാണിത് അങ്ങനെ ബാഗ് എല്ലാം നമ്മൾ ചെക്കിൻ ചെയ്തിട്ട് ദാ ഇമിഗ്രേഷനിൽ സീലും വെച്ച് ദാ ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് പോവുയാണ് ഇപ്പോഴാണ് ഇത് [സംഗീതം] റിയൽ ഫീലിങ് വരുന്നത് ഞാൻ ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് പോവുയാണ് വീട്ടിൽ പോവുയാണ് എന്നുള്ള ഫീലിങ്് അപ്പൊ ദാ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ജേർണി സ്റ്റാർട്ട് ചെയ്തുഒപന് മറഞ്ഞിരുന്ന ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് ആണ് [സംഗീതം] ഡിലേ ആയിട്ട് ഇപ്പം 10:45നാണ് എടുക്കുന്നത് ഡിലേ ആവാത്തവർ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് ഇല്ലഎന്നാണ് എനിക്ക് തോന്നുന്നത് ഈ ഒരു കോപ്പൻ ഡൽഹി അറ്റ്ലീസ്റ്റ് എപ്പോഴും ഡിലേ ആയിക്കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും. സോ ഇതാണ് [സംഗീതം] ഡിലേ ആയതുകൊണ്ട് എന്റെ സെക്കൻഡ് ഫ്ലൈറ്റും ക്യാൻസൽ ചെയ്ത് റീബുക്ക് ചെയ്യേണ്ടി വന്നു. ഫ്രം ഡൽഹി ടു ബാംഗ്ലൂർ ആദ്യമായിട്ട് നമ്മുടെ എയർ ഇന്ത്യ ഫ്ലൈറ്റിൽ കയറിയ എന്റെ ഒരു ചെക്കിങ്ങും കാര്യങ്ങളും ഒക്കെ ഉണ്ട്. ഞാൻങ്ങനെ മൊത്തത്തിൽ എല്ലാ സീറ്റും [സംഗീതം] പരിസരവും ഒക്കെ ആകെ ഒന്ന് ചെക്ക് ചെയ്തുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുയായിരുന്നു. നമുക്ക് യൂഷ്വൽ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ്സിൽ കിട്ടുന്ന പോലെ ഇതിലും കുറച്ച് പുതപ്പും പില്ലോയും കാര്യങ്ങളഒക്കെ കിട്ടിയിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. [സംഗീതം] പക്ഷെ മറ്റുള്ള ഫ്ലൈറ്റിലൊക്കെ കിട്ടുന്ന അത്രയും ഐറ്റംസും എന്താ പറയുക ആ ഒരു പ്രീമിയം [സംഗീതം] സംഭവംില്ല. എങ്കിലും ഓക്കെ ഓക്കെ ആണ്. വലിയ ബുദ്ധിമുട്ടൊന്നുമില്ല. സീറ്റ് ഒക്കെ കുഴപ്പമില്ലായിരുന്നു. പിന്നെ ചില [സംഗീതം] സ്വിച്ചുകളും കാര്യങ്ങളും ഒക്കെ എന്താെന്ന് ശരിക്കും എനിക്ക് മനസ്സിലായില്ല. അതൊന്നും വലിയ യൂസ് ഒന്നുമില്ല. ചിലരുടെ ഒന്നും മോണിറ്റർ ഒന്നും വർക്ക് ആവാറില്ല എന്ന് കേട്ടിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. താങ്ക് ഗോഡ് എന്റെ മോണിറ്റർ വർക്കിങ് ആയിരുന്നു. അതുകൊണ്ട് വലിയ കുഴപ്പമില്ലായിരുന്നു. സ്റ്റിൽ ഞാൻ ഒരു ഫിലിം കണ്ടു ബാക്കി ഞാൻ എന്റെ ഫോണിലും ടാബിലും ഒക്കെയാണ് [സംഗീതം] ഫിലിം കണ്ടത്. അപ്പൊ ഈ ജേർണി എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് വെരി വെരി ലോങ്ങ് ജേർണി ആണ്. ഇവിടുന്ന് ഡെൻമാർക്കിൽ നിന്ന് ഇന്ത്യയിലോട്ട് ഓൾമോസ്റ്റ് 9 ആൻഡ് ഹാഫ് ഹവേഴ്സ് ഉണ്ട്. ഓൾറെഡി നമ്മുടെ ഫ്ലൈറ്റ് വൺ അവർ മേലെ ഡിലേ ആണ്. ഇത് കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് നമുക്ഒരു ലേഓവർ ഉണ്ട് ഡൽഹിയിൽ അവിടുന്ന് നമുക്ക് മൂന്ന് അവർ ഉണ്ട് തിരിച്ച് ബാംഗ്ലൂരിലോട്ട് സോ വെരി വെരി ലോങ്ങ് ജേർണി ആണ് ഇരുന്നിരുന്ന് ഉപ്പാട് വരാൻ പോകുന്ന ഒരു ട്രിപ്പ് ആണിത്. വാ സിറ്റുവേഷൻ ഇപ്പോഴും നിലനിൽക്കുന്നത് കൊണ്ട്തന്നെ റൂട്ട് കുറച്ച് വ്യത്യാസമായിട്ടാണ് എയർ പോകുന്നത് സ ഇപ്പോ കാണുന്നതാണ് ട്ടോ ഈ ഫ്ലൈറ്റിന്റെ റൂട്ട് അങ്ങനെ നമുക്ക് ഫ്ലൈറ്റിൽ നിന്ന് കിട്ടിയ ഈ ഒരു ഇയർഫോൺ ഒക്കെ ഞാൻ സെറ്റ് [സംഗീതം] ചെയ്തിട്ട് ദാ ഈ ഒരു പടം കാണാൻ വേണ്ടി സ്റ്റാർട്ട് ചെയ്തു വേറെ ഒരു പടം എനിക്ക് [സംഗീതം] ഞാൻ കണ്ട ഫിലിംസ് ആണ് പിന്നെ പിന്നെ ബാക്കിയൊന്നും അങ്ങനെ കാണാൻ നമുക്ക് ഇൻട്രസ്റ്റ് തോന്നാത്ത ഫിലിംസ് ആണ് വലിയ കളക്ഷൻസ് ഒന്നുമില്ല ഫിലിംസ് പിന്നെ മോണിറ്റർ ക്വാളിറ്റി ഒക്കെ ഒരു പിക്ചർ ക്വാളിറ്റി ഒക്കെ ഒരു കുറവായിരിക്കും അങ്ങനെ ഞാൻ ഒരു ഫിലിം ഒക്കെ കണ്ടട് ഇരുന്നപ്പോഴേക്കും നമ്മുടെ എയർ ഹോസ്റ്റസ് ഫുഡുമായിട്ട് എത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ട് അങ്ങനെയാണ് ഞാൻ മനപ്പൂർവം ഉറങ്ങാതെ ഫിലിം കണ്ടതാണ് എനിക്കും നല്ല ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ടായിരുന്നു കാരണം ഓൾമോസ്റ്റ് ടൈം 12ത എല്ലാം ആയിട്ടുണ്ടായിരുന്നു നുക്ക് നല്ല ഉറക്കം വരുന്ന സമയമാണ് ഉറങ്ങിയിട്ടും കാര്യമില്ല ഉറങ്ങി വരുമ്പോഴേക്കും ഒരു ഫുഡ് [സംഗീതം] കൊണ്ടുവരും അതുകൊണ്ട് ഞാൻ മനപ്പൂർവം ഉറങ്ങാതെ അപ്പ ഫുഡ് വന്നിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഞാൻ നോൺവെജ് ഫുഡ് ആണ് ട്ടോ. ചിക്കൻ കറിയും റൈസും ആണ് വന്നിക്കുന്നത്. അതിന്റെ കൂടെ നമുക്കൊരു ബണ്ണ് ഉണ്ട്. പിന്നെ ഒരു കറി ഉണ്ട് ചോക്ലേറ്റ് ഉണ്ട് ബട്ടർ വാട്ടർ ആൻഡ് ഹെരിക ടേസ്റ്റ് എങ്ങനെ ഉണ്ടാന്ന് നോക്കാം ഫുഡ് വലിയ തരക്കേട ഇല്ലായിരുന്നു വലിയ ഒരു പ്രീമിയം സംഭവം ഒന്നുമല്ല നമ്മൾ മറ്റുള്ള ഫ്ലൈറ്റ്സിലൊക്കെ എപ്പോഴും [സംഗീതം] നല്ല പ്രീമിയം ക്വാളിറ്റി ഫുഡ് ആയിരിക്കും ഇതങ്ങനെ വലിയ സംഭവംൊന്നുമില്ല കഴിക്കാം [സംഗീതം] വലിയ തെറ്റൊന്നുമില്ല അങ്ങനെ അത് കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് നമ്മൾ ഒരു വാഷ്റൂം ടൂർ ഒക്കെ [സംഗീതം] നടത്തിയിട്ട് ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ടോ എന്ന് ചോദിച്ചാൽ ഉറക്കം വരുന്നുണ്ട് എന്നാൽ ഉറക്കം വരുന്നില്ല അപ്പോ പിന്നെ വെറുതെ അങ്ങോട്ടും ഇങ്ങോട്ടും [സംഗീതം] ഒക്കെ നടക്കാം ഇരുന്നിരുന്നു അടുത്ത് അപ്പോ ഒന്ന് വാഷ്റൂമിൽ എല്ലാം പോയി അങ്ങനെ ഒന്ന് കറങ്ങി നടന്നു അങ്ങനെ കുറച്ച് ഉറക്കവും ഇരിപ്പും നടപ്പും ഒക്കെ കഴിഞ്ഞ് [സംഗീതം] രാവിലെയായി. രാവിലെ ആയപ്പോഴേക്കും അതാ നമുക്ക് അടുത്ത ഫുഡ് എത്തി. ഇതാണ് ബ്രേക്ക്ഫാസ്റ്റ്. reviews.transcript_full:
Sat Morning 9:30am @ Manchester Airport T2 
Not many pax at CI counters, finish bag drop within 10 min Completed security within 10 min and heading to 1903 Lounge There are quite a lot of food & beverage choices There are two lounges at T2 - 1903 & escape Cathay Pacific passengers use 1903 lounge Not a very big lounge, but it offers a great view through the glass window Wide variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks Free flow of Jacques BARDELOT Champagne and Langlois crémant de loire brut réserve Enjoy a nice light breakfast, champagne & glass coke I really appreciate the made-to-order egg & toast Plenty selection of pastries Here comes to what I love the most in this lounge Cheshire Farm Ice Cream!!! One more glass of Champhagne before going to gate Today's flight was operated by this Airbus A350-900 B-LRO Mentioned in last video, I tried extra legroom seat 60K this time My question is: Is this aisle-access seat? There is a missing seat in front but the flight exit door is in front I think I like this extra legroom seat more than the 2 in front,
as I don't have to bother where to look at during take off and landing and this seat got a window unlike the row in front. You can find the remote at the side of the seat The drawbacks are sacrificing a bit of seat width
for the folding table and the IFE screen and cannot use the screen during take off and landing The screen size is ok.  Given the aircraft is about 7 years old,
a little bit of wear and tear is understandable. Greetings in English and Chinese (Cantonese & Putonghua)
Flight time would be 11h47m The space in front looked barely enough to walk
and would probably bother the passenger. Not so aisle-access as I thought Printed menu was distributed by FA Baked chicken fried rice, Braised beef or vegeterian choice
Mushroom and spinach risotto. Shortly after safety demo, we were ready to depart Cloudy morning, very Manchester Here we go A bottled water was distributed shortly after take off Followed by nuts and drink service (12:05pm) I planned to watch three live Premier League games The live streaming is smooth and clear I really enjoyed it becaues the flight departed at 10:30am UK time,
I did not feel sleepy at all. Lunch was served from the front compartment to the back
I chose the baked chicken rice. (1:16pm) It tasted surprisingly good although the serving may be
a little bit small for lunch if I didn't have my breakfast Always love the view from the window Nice sunset near Georgia After the second game, walk to galley to stretch my legs
Snacks in the galley Hot noodle was my choice. I am quite sure it was customised, s
mell not as strong as those purchased from supermarkets. Another concern of these exit row seats are their
proximity to the toilets This seat is ok, but I think row 59 may feel it a bit bothersome. Cannot sleep at all, can only enjoy the night view from sky. 05:50am HKT, breakfast was served
Also from the front compartment to the back Congee with 2 prawns, not bad 06:23 HKT descending to Hong Kong International Airport
Here are some final thoughts CX Airbus A350 economy class is good
at least better than its 777-300er in 3-4-3 seating config The extra legroom seat 60A/K is ok
Can walk from the narrow space in front But if you wish to walk around quite often, aisle seats
or row 59 seats are better choices Because going in and out would inevitably 
bother the passenger in front In terms of the best seat in economy class on CX A350-900, 
I would prefer bulkhead seats in row 40A/C/H/K. I sat at seat 40C on my return flight, and the passengers at 40A/B
did not have to wake me in order to walk out from their seats Lounge 1903 at Manchester Airport T2 is good I like the made-to-order toast and Cheshire Farm ice cream so much There could be more snacks available in the galley
and it would be better if water and juice were ready to take In-flight entertainment system is superb! I enjoy the 3 premier league games on this flight  No free wifi in economy class unless you are CX Diamond member Hope free wifi will become norm in the future You always need some luck to have a cry-free flight, 
but this time, I didn't. Price. About GBP 800 for a MAN-HKG return ticket
Direct flight is more expensive than that with transfer. For comparison, my wife's PEY ticket with AF & KLM also costed her
around GBP 800, but only with 2 carry-on luggages. Find the best deal is better than stick to any specific airlines IMO. Thank you for watching and I will soon post another video
comparing this extra legroom seat and 40A/K bulkhead seats. Stay tuned!

actually a bit wider than the A350 Today I’m departing from Osaka Connecting in Tokyo Narita before Chicago And flying on Japan Airlines’ 777 I’ll also be testing what this economy seat is really like every seat comes with a screen But this flight was only about an hour So efficiency mattered the most Because after arriving at Narita I still had to clear security and immigration This time I only had a 60 minute connection Tokyo airports can get really crowded By the time I reached the gate Boarding had already started So if you transfer to an international flight in Japan You should leave at least 90 minutes To be on the safer side Now let’s get onboard And see what JAL’s 777-300ER economy class is like The 777 economy cabin uses a 3-3-3 layout Seat pitch is around 86 cm And the seat width is 47 cm That’s 1 cm wider than JAL’s A35k economy class So on paper the specs look pretty good But the armrests might be a bit thicker So it doesn’t feel too different from the A350 The seat already came with a pillow and blanket I also brought a pair of hotel slippers Which makes long haul flights feel more comfortable And the cabin lighting was dim With a sunset kind of vibe So I already felt relaxed right after sitting down I tried out the headrest It doesn’t adjust very high But it’s thick and soft So overall it feels good enough Whether it keeps its shape on a long haul flight We’ll have to find out after sleeping Legroom has always been one of JAL’s strengths And this aircraft is no exception There’s still some space in front of my knees So it’s not easy to hit the seat in front But the magazine pocket feels a bit loose And it does touch your legs This tray table can also slide forward And it feels quite large and stable Even though this 777 is already 21 years old The cabin still looks well maintained It doesn’t really feel extremely old And now we’re getting ready for Chicago After takeoff we’ll check out together What good food is available from Tokyo The aircraft has now reached cruising altitude And the crew started preparing dinner While everyone was waiting They first served drinks and snacks One special thing is that JAL has its own peach flavored juice A lot of people order this drink And it actually tastes pretty good There wasn’t a printed menu at my seat I only got the menu when the meal cart arrived Option A was braised pork chirashi sushi rice Option B was tomato chicken pilaf rice Both meals were baked rice dishes For airplane food The photos matched the real meal quite well And the presentation looked pretty nice The meal also came with a salad Japanese style chicken balls Salmon salad And broccoli salad One thing I found very thoughtful Was this paper listing all the ingredients So you don’t have to guess what you’re eating Taste wise it was actually pretty decent The tomato rice looked very rich in color But the sauce wasn’t too heavy And it even came with a soft boiled egg Which is quite rare for airplane food The pork rice portion was pretty generous Much better than flights from overseas stations I think JAL meals from Tokyo Are very different from overseas departures Even today’s ice cream Was a limited edition flavor And for drinks I noticed juice servings were only half full So I ordered beer instead They give you the whole can So it doesn’t finish in two sips One more thing during the meal service The crew asked everyone to sit upright And they started collecting trays very quickly It felt like there were only 10 to 15 minutes to eat This aircraft’s entertainment system Only supports Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English Inside there are 7 categories Including movies, news, music and games The interface looks a bit outdated But it’s still easy to use The movie selection feels pretty average Most of them are Japanese movies There’s also some Disney+ and Hulu content But if you want Hollywood movies There aren’t that many new releases The news channels had even fewer choices If you want to play games The older system and screen Can feel a bit slow to respond But some other features are very convenient For example below the USB port There’s a small storage space Which is useful for your phone or earphones This flight also has Wi Fi JAL economy passengers get one hour free But don’t expect the speed to be very good It’s just enough for messaging But streaming or uploading files Probably won’t work very well On long haul flights to North America JAL doesn’t blast the air conditioning like US airlines The cabin was actually kept quite warm So I barely used the blanket on this flight But if you get hot easily and can’t sleep And want to watch movies to pass the time It might be better to bring some snacks onboard Because on this 12 hour flight There were no sandwiches or cup noodles mid flight So if you get hungry halfway through There really aren’t many choices The whole flight only had two meals Breakfast on this flight was American style pancakes Served with sausage and hash browns Overall it was a bit dry with little sauce There was also yogurt and fruit Which are pretty standard side items I think it was filling enough But not something I’d want to eat again Before landing I also checked out The rear lavatory on the aircraft Even after more than 10 hours It was still kept pretty clean There were also paper cups for brushing teeth But the space was definitely very tight Still for a 20 year old 777 The condition was actually quite well maintained Before landing in Chicago Let’s talk about the overall experience Even though this Boeing 777 is already quite old I still think the Sky Wider seat is pretty good After more than 10 hours in the air My knees didn’t feel too uncomfortable And the lower back support was better than expected JAL’s inflight service isn’t especially extensive But small details like the ingredient list Show that they are quite thoughtful At least you know clearly what you’re eating Without needing to ask the crew If you’re flying from Asia to North America And don’t want to pay extra for premium economy But still want a more comfortable seat I think JAL’s long haul economy class Is a very solid option What do you guys think And which airline’s long haul economy class Do you think is worth trying? Feel free to leave your thoughts below That’s it for this JAL 777 video If you enjoyed it Don’t forget to like, comment and subscribe And I’ll see you in the next video

reviews.transcript_full: Flying from Cebu to Hong Kong, most people choose Cebu Pacific because it's usually the cheaper option. But this time we decided to fly with Cathay Pacific instead. The ticket cost more, so the question is simple. Is the extra money actually worth it? If you're flying from Cebu to Hong Kong, you'll usually end up comparing these two airlines. Cathay Pacific is often more expensive, although the price difference can vary quite a bit depending on when you book. But first, Cebu Airport. Still my favorite airport in the Philippines. It's modern, spacious, clean, and has plenty of food options. Waiting for your flight here is actually enjoyable. Boarding was right on time for us. The staff were professional, everything was [music] organized, and the whole process felt smooth from the start to finish. The aircraft isn't brand new, but it feels very well maintained, clean, comfortable, and in great condition. This is the Airbus A330, a wide-body aircraft commonly used on longer routes. Inside, you get a two-four-two seating layout, which immediately feels more spacious than the narrow-body aircraft used by many budget airlines. By the way, I have a video about the Cebu Pacific aircraft, linked down below in the description if you want to check it out. The seat was comfortable, and the legroom was more than enough for this 3-hour flight. [music] You also get a personal entertainment screen with movies, TV shows, games, and a flight tracker. Headphones are included as well. So already it feels like a different experience compared to most budget carriers. Then came the food. She went for the chicken and rice, while I chose the seafood pasta. I'll be honest, seafood on an airplane is always a risk, but surprisingly, it was delicious, cheesy, flavorful, and I finished every bite. No regrets here. And unlike most budget airlines, the meal is already included in your ticket. Drinks are included, too. Soft drinks, such as or or I asked the cabin crew for a recommendation and ended up trying a Hong Kong craft beer. Really good. Definitely didn't expect that. You also get a fresh fruits and a Haagen-Dazs ice cream for dessert. Simple, but a very nice touch. After the meal service, the crew came back offering coffee, tea, and hot chocolate. They also mentioned that drinks were free flow throughout [music] the flight. Service overall was excellent, friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the flight. The flight itself was smooth and comfortable with flight time of around 3 hours. There's enough time to relax, watch a movie, enjoy the meal, or simply sit back and enjoy the ride. So, is Cathay Pacific worth paying more compared to Cebu Pacific? In my opinion, yes. You get better comfort, better service, included meals and drinks, in-flight entertainment, and an overall more premium travel experience. Is it essential for a 3-hour flight? Not necessarily. But, if you value comfort and want to start your Hong Kong trip on a better note, I think it's worth considering, especially if the schedule is more convenient for you. And that's what it's like flying Cathay Pacific from Cebu to Hong Kong. If you found this review helpful, consider subscribing. reviews.transcript_full: The A380 on Singapore Airlines known to most for the streets on the upper deck, arguably  the most luxurious commercial aviation products have been built.  But today, I'm in economy, hosting 18.5 inches of seat width, one of the widest economy  seats owing to the sheer size of this aircraft.  Today's route is Singapore to Sydney on SQ-231, a red-eyed parting Singapore just passed  midnight with a total flight time of 7.5 hours.  Let's see what the A380 on Singapore Airlines actually feels like in the back of the bus.  Singapore Airlines operates out of Terminal 3 at Changi Airport.  In the world's best airport, 14 times by Skytrikes.  Checking counters are at Rho 3 and 4, with plenty of self-service kiosk if you want them.  I went to the desk as I wanted an actual boarding pass, not a floppy piece of paper from a  kiosk.  The entire process took about 10 minutes with the queue and if you're short on time,  the kiosk with automated backdrop make it even faster.  Not long after, I was ASI.  The transit area at Changi is its own thing entirely.  Food and beverage, luxury duty-free, liquor, versalaction is immense.  There are well-designed seating spaces everywhere you look from proper lounging areas to productivity  setups to dining.  It was passed 11pm and I wasn't feeling particularly hungry, so I found a quiet corner and said,  I love this airport.  It's the only one in the world where you genuinely don't feel like lounge access is necessary.  Today's departure gate is B7, roughly a 5-minute walk from the immigration area in Terminal  3.  If there's one thing that consistently gets brought up as a friction point at Changi,  it's the security screening that happens at the gate itself.  I got through security almost immediately only to be greeted by a packed seating area.  Fun fact, the aircraft taking me to Sydney tonight is on its first commercial flights of  the coming out of months of maintenance in Spain.  During an A380, an economy is a serious waiting game and the numbers explain why.  Business class alone is 78 passengers.  By the time you work through sweets, business, premium economy and however many economy zones  they have carved out, it makes you acutely aware of how far down the food chain you are.  The line moves slowly and I eventually made my way to 66h.  I selected this seat right before checking after spotting what looked like an empty row  on the seat map as it turns out the whole row was mine.  Having a whole row to yourself on a packed red-eye flight is like winning the lottery.  People call it the poor man's business class but I prefer the term make shift business  class.  After what seemed like a long-browling process I finally settled in and the first thing  waiting for me was the signature hot towel.  After 30 minutes of shuffling down an aisle with a couple hundred people, it's a huge  stress reliever.  The seat itself 32 inches of pitch and 18.5 inches of width.  Above average for economy and noticeably so at 178cm tall I had enough leg room.  The in-flight entertainment screen is 11 inches with an adjustable angle to touch response  is decent not laggy.  Load screen on the left you get a USB-A charging point, reading light controls, call button  and a two pin headphone jack.  On the subject of the provided headphones it's not the best.  If you can bring a blue-tooth transmitter that plugs into the two pin jack and pair it  straight to your airport.  The sound quality difference is significant and on a long flight it's worth it.  The new tray table has a vanity mirror built in, it's an odd placement but it's there  if you need it on the right there's a cup holder.  Useful between new service when you want somewhere to put a drink, standard blanket and  pillow provided, worth noting for window seat sleepers.  The A380 is so wide that the wall is too far to lean against.  Chris World is extremely well stocked.  Singapore Airlines updates their library regularly with the latest blockbusters.  You'd be hard pressed to fault it.  We push back slightly late.  The flight was intentionally delayed to allow some connecting passengers to make it.  Our estimate economy was around 85% full and we taxied out to it, run way zero to center  and took off into the moonlit skies.  Shortly after takeoff, refreshment service comments.  Two options were offered, mozzarella, mushroom pizza bar and margarita pizza bar, along with  coffee or tea, beer, soft drinks, wine and cocktails were available too.  I went with the margarita pizza bar and it delivered cheesy, good umami and the bread texture  was decent.  It's a great late night snack, just don't expect the quality of a naveli pizza.  After the crew made their rounds to clear the rubbish, I got comfortable in my makeshift  business class seat.  It was amazing.  And I wholeheartedly endorsed gaming the system to snack a whole row for free on empty flights.  Keep checking up to when checking closes.  Singapore Airlines offers complimentary wifi to every economy passenger, but only if you  tag your ticket to your Chris Flyer account during checking.  Speeds are solid for general browsing but don't expect to stream 4k videos on your phone.  On this front, airlines like Carter with Scarling have an edge.  Singapore Airlines is planning to upgrade their fleet with Starlink from 2027.  So this is only going to get better.  After the best economy sleep I've had, breakfast came around.  I went with the scrambled eggs with cheese and chicken sausage, accompanied by a fruit  platter, strawberry yogurt and a bread roll with butter.  Full beverage service was available with hot and cold options.  There are usually three options for mains on flight to Australia.  Western, Indian and an East Asian or Singaporean option.  The metal cutlery is a nice touch and its genius marketing on their part.  Research shows that the tactile experience of handling heavier items triggers a higher  perceived value.  For an economy meal, it was solid.  If they had offered the Singaporean fried carrot cake, I would have gone for that.  As new service wrapped up, we were fast approaching Sydney.  The crew prepped the cabin for landing and soon we were on approach.  Follow me on Singapore Airlines is one of the best in the industry.  It's not easy to differentiate an economy class, but there are some standout features  such as the hot towel service and above all, the crew.  I've flown an economy class on other five star carriers and while the hard product  is often comparable, the crew experience ends to fall short.  On Singapore Airlines, the crew is the difference maker.  It's what the brand has been built on and it's what keeps me coming back.  As I've mentioned in previous videos, the crew have the ability to straddle both eastern  formality and western casualness in a way that's unique to places like Singapore.  Beyond the product itself, what Singapore Airlines is really selling is trust.  You're buying the confidence that you'll be taken care of.  That if something goes wrong, it gets resolved quickly and competently.  That's why I would gladly pay a premium for Singapore Airlines economy.  If you would like to check out my return flight to Singapore in business class, that video  is up right now.  Drop a like and subscribe if this was off-value to you and I'll see you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: When you think of airlines known for being super connectors, you might immediately think of the Gulf carriers who specialize in funneling passengers through their Middle Eastern hubs on journeys from east to west or north to south. But here in the Americas, there's one airline that might not be as popular worldwide, but regardless plays an important role in connecting not just North and South America, but also Central America and the Caribbean. Of course, I'm talking about none other than La Compania Panamena de Aviacion, otherwise known as Copa Airlines. The Panamanian flag carrier is one of the most prominent international carriers in the Americas and it's an airline that I've always been curious to try. So in the next few videos, we'll be experiencing Copa Airlines on a trip not just to its home nation of Panama, but also onwards to Colombia. This video will cover the first leg of this trip from Chicago to Panama City on the 737-800 in economy class. Thanks so much for tuning in. Viva Panama City. Buenos dias from O'Hare Terminal 5, where since filming this video, Southwest no longer flies here. Typically, you should try to get to the airport about 3 hours before departure for international flights. I was here about 2 hours early, but I guess I hit the sweet spot because there was no line for check-in and within 5 minutes, I had my boarding passes and was off to security. I'm traveling on the economy classic fare and I'm allowed one free personal item, carry-on and checked bag, but be sure to check your specific fare class as allowances [music] vary. The early morning international departures at Terminal 5 are primarily to Mexico alongside this flight to Panama. All of these aircraft arrive between 11:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m. and remain overnight until returning to their home bases between 6:00 and 8:00 a.m. Apart from Copa, these include flights from Volaris, Viva, and Aeromexico. We're departing from M16 this morning, which unfortunately doesn't offer any view of the aircraft. So, just imagine you can see it. Copa starts boarding 1 hour before the scheduled departure time, which given its fleet is entirely 737s, may seem excessive, but it's a huge factor in ensuring everyone has enough time to board and is a prime reason behind Copa being ranked as the most punctual airline in the Americas and the second most punctual in the entire world, according to Cirium. The Copa 737-800s feature 166 seats with 16 in business and 150 in economy. Seat selection is free for economy classic tickets, and today I'll be in 22A. Overall, the seats are comfortable with adjustable headrests, and I love how the Copa name is embroidered into the seat. Now, I couldn't find any details about this online, but it seems that Copa is quietly removing seatback entertainment from its aircraft, at least in economy, and mainly shifting to streaming entertainment. Seatback screens were offered on the 737-800s at one point, but I'm not sure how many aircraft still have it. Anyway, the legroom on board is decent, and I was happy to find that all passengers have access to their own set of USB-A and C ports. So, now let's address the elephant in the room. Why on earth does Copa's livery look exactly like United's? Well, this is no coincidence, and no, it's not because one airline copied the other. reviews.transcript_full:
Hello everyone. Welcome back to another video. I 
apologize, it's been a while since I last posted,   but today I'm so excited to fly Etihad's business 
class on their A380 from Toronto to Abu Dhabi.   If you've looked at my other videos, you'd 
know that I rarely fly business class. So,   while I am stoked to fly today, I still want 
to make it a fair review. As always, I'm so   grateful for the opportunity to do things like 
this. So, don't mistake any criticism for a lack   of gratitude. Etihad departs from Terminal 1 at 
Toronto with business and first class passengers   using the Plaza Premium Lounge in the domestic 
area of Terminal 1. We arrived a little late,   so we didn't go inside. The lounge is sufficient, 
but it can get crowded during peak times. Now, for the seat map. On the Etihad A380, the 
entire main deck is filled with 405 economy seats   in a 3-4-3 layout. The best economy seat here is 
69D because there's a missing seat in front of it.   Similarly, both 76A and 76K have almost 
infinite legroom. Moving to the upper deck,   there are 70 business class seats in a staggered 
1-2-1 layout. Half of the seats are closer to the   aisles and face backward, while the arguably 
better other half are closer to the windows   and face forward, offering more privacy. In the 
center are the honeymoon seats, which are close   together in private for people traveling 
together. First class, on the other hand,   has nine seats in a staggered 1-1 layout with 
some seats being closer to the aisle or window   and some facing forwards and backward. And of 
course, seats 1A and 1C are the Residence. My   seat on today's flight is the more exposed 13C, 
but regardless, it's still a great product. At each seat, there is a plush blanket...
...a really nice mattress topper... ...and a large pillow... The noise cancelling headphones 
provided are very good. ...with the nicest slippers I've ever seen. The amenity kits are from Armani 
Kasa and have various Espa products. Now for a seat tour. In front there's an 18.5   bright touchscreen IFE. Below that is 
the footwell with storage beneath it. To the right is the standard 
Panasonic remote for the IFE   that extends. You can view the flight map 
on it independently from the main screen. Below are some seat controls. And next to the   seat is a storage cubby with 
headphones and a water bottle. Just above is a modern mood 
light and a reading light. Next to the if there's a large table. 
It can be pushed forward so that you   can leave the seat while eating with a 
table light above. Next to the remote,   there's a control panel 
for various seat functions. The seat has lumbar support, 
which while it sounds cool,   it basically feels like sitting on 
a balloon. If it fails and deflates,   it's basically like sitting on a metal 
bench. There is also a privacy partition   at all aisle seats. As this is an A380, there 
are large storage cubbies at every seat on the   upper deck as well. There aren't individual 
air vents, but the flight was cold enough. Now for the if It's called E-Box with the 
home screen laid out in a series of, well,   boxes. The touch screen isn't the most responsive, 
but that's why there's a remote. There's plenty of   movies and TV shows with a search menu 
at the bottom to easily find content. There's also live TV... ...a kids menu... ...seat to seat... ...chat and call... ...and outboard cameras and a movie map. Dinner service started with a bowl of 
warm nuts and a drink of your choice. I got the Arabic Mezze to start, the beef short 
rib as a main, and the cheese plate and ice cream   for dessert. The meal overall was very high 
quality and delicious, with no complaints. After that, I got a hot chocolate which came 
with...more chocolate. (It was really good,   though). The bar on board, referred 
to as the lobby, is a nice place to   hang out with the self-service bar, too. 
While it is dark and possibly uninviting,   it is a really cozy place to be in after 
sitting for hours in the same place. All the toilets on board are spacious and 
kept very clean throughout the flight. It   has more amenities from Espa and overall 
they just look super cool and modern. There is Wi-Fi on board, with Etihad guests 
receiving free messaging. I didn't purchase   Wi-Fi, but it's roughly $20 for the entire 12-hour 
flight. I made the most of the flight by trying as   many things as possible off the all-day menu, like 
these blueberry soufflé pancakes and the granola   yogurt bowl, which, for some reason, came with a 
cheese plate and cookies. Maybe I'm just easily   impressed because I don't fly business class 
often, but they both tasted really, really good. Listen, it's not often I'm able to fly business 
class like this. So, yes, I was easily impressed.   However, I want to evaluate the aspects of the 
product by talking about two distinct things:   the hard product and the soft product. The 
hard product is the seat itself and the cabin,   while the soft product is a service, food, and 
amenities. Let's start with the hard product.   The seat came out roughly 10 years ago, 
and while it looks modern and good, there's   definitely some wear and tear with some of the 
things like the windows wouldn't work properly. Also, backwards facing seats have slightly less 
pitch by a few inches, so if you're tall like me,   it may be a bit tight in the footwell. Besides 
that, the food was really good and high quality.   The amenity kit had sufficient amenities, and 
while the crew from Middle Eastern Airlines   can be hit or miss, the crew here were pretty 
friendly. I especially like the mood lighting   in the cabin with many elements featuring the 
Lights of Abu Dhabi theme with a lamp that   mimics sunlight under a palm tree, and triangles 
basically everywhere. A lot of thought and work   went into making this product and cabin, and it 
definitely still feels like this 10 years later.   I really enjoyed my time on Etihad today. And 
while I don't fly business class too often,   hopefully this gives you an insight into the 
experience on board. Now, time for landing. Thank you.

yt_comments.text: Not bad for a startup, but of course there are flaws: 1. No personal airvents 2. No universal power outlets in economy, I think only included in business class, which is a shame. 3. Weak Wi-Fi for a premium full service carrier that is digitally native (should have just stuck with StarLink) 4. Average lavatory, very ordinary, nothing special like Emirates Or Qatar Airways. 5. No onboard external cameras (forwards and downwards) QR and EK offer them on almost every aircraft and dreamliners are supposed to have them. 6. Safety Video seems to have used lots of AI and CGI (not necessarily a complaint but apparently some were bothered by it.) 7. Tray table cannot be extended, if seat in front reclines, can be difficult for the passenger. Some of the positives: 1. Very aesthetic mood lighting 2. Premium cabin with generous recline 3. Comfortable seats 4. Generous meal portions even for a short haul domestic flight 5. Massive screen (13.3inch for economy) with Wi-Fi (regardless of speed as some airlines don’t even offer it) and responsive. 6. Experienced staff, lots of former cabin crews from EK, QR, EY etc. 7. Metal cutlery provided, lavender scented hot towels, branded soaps and other little touches that make the experience much better 8. In-built headphones inside the headrests for passengers in premium economy and business class 9. Business elite is said to be even better than some airlines first class suites 10. Bluetooth pairing with personal headphones 11. One of the best in-flight map, interactive experience with the IfE, good content for a start-up, with games, music and much more. 12. Provided amenity kit for long haul travel Can still add much more Overall probably one of the best startups and there’s more postives than negatives. Thanks for the review and can’t wait for this airline to dominate the passenger experience in future travel.
