reviews.title: Flying on a WWII-Era DC-3! A Historic Day Trip from Melbourne to King Island
reviews.transcript_excerpt: The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience.…

captions.text: The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience.

chapters.title: Currie Boathouse (The Restaurant with No Food)

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Melbourne! Today, I'm taking a flight like no other, I'll be flying on an 81-year-old DC-3 to King Island. Built in 1945 during World War II, this aircraft is truly a piece of living history. I can't wait to get on board and learn about its story. Let's go! My DC-3 flight departs from Essendon Fields Airport. From 1921 to 1970, Essendon was Melbourne's main airport and played a key role during the 1956 Olympic Games. Suburban expansion prevented the airport from expanding, so Tullamarine was constructed and has since become Melbourne's main international gateway. Today, Sharp Airlines is the only airline that operates scheduled passenger flights from Essendon Airport. The DC-3 is owned by Shortstop Jet Charter, one of many charter operators based at Essendon. This flight isn't a scheduled commuter service but is sold as part of a day tour to King Island. Check-in took place at their hangar 30 minutes before departure. We received our seat assignments and were then invited to relax with a cup of tea in the lounge or enjoy a glass of champagne or orange juice in the hangar. Here, you can see the company's Falcon 900C business jet and, in the distance, our legendary DC-3. The Douglas DC-3 was developed in 1935, just 32 years after Orville Wright made the world's first powered flight. Before World War II, it revolutionised air travel by establishing longer routes previously unreachable by its predecessors and became one of the first airliners capable of operating profitably without mail subsidies. It was affectionately nicknamed the "Gooney Bird" due to its resemblance to the albatross, a large seabird known for its long wings and effortless gliding ability. This particular aircraft was among the last ones produced. Delivered as a C-47, the military version of the DC-3, to the Royal Australian Air Force in 1945, it was purchased by Shortstop Jet Charter in the late 1980s. While the airframe is quite old, the interior has been refurbished. There are 28 passenger seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. I was allocated a window seat in row 3. As the DC-3 has a small tail wheel at the back, boarding requires a short uphill walk to the front. The seats, sourced from a former Airbus A300, are quite comfortable and have plenty of legroom. This aircraft is powered by two Pratt & Whitney twin-row Wasp piston engines, each with fourteen cylinders and generating 1,200 horsepower. The DC-3 can take off and land on dirt runways and has a low stall speed of around 125 km/h. It felt like we lifted off the ground in just a few seconds. The flight to King Island takes about one hour. We will fly past the Westgate Bridge, over Port Phillip Bay, and across the Bass Strait. This flight operates on selected Sundays throughout the year, and as of January 2025, the cost is $697 per person. The price includes return flights on the DC-3, lunch, and a tour of King Island. For an additional $75, you can ride in the jump seat with the pilots during either takeoff or landing. Apart from trips to King Island, this aircraft is also used for day excursions to wine regions, 45-minute joy flights over Melbourne, and evening cocktail flights. The back section of the plane has been converted into a lounge area, where passengers can relax, chat, and take in the views through the large rectangular windows. I was pleasantly surprised to find a toilet onboard, and it's very spacious. Back at my seat, I was offered a snack pack and a drink. The DC-3 does not have a pressurised cabin or air-conditioning, it flies much lower than modern jets. As such, for passenger comfort, flights are often cancelled, typically when the temperature exceeds 25 degrees Celsius or the wind surpasses 25 km/h. In the event of a cancellation, you can request a refund or be rebooked for a future date. The one-hour flight passed quickly, this was certainly a unique, once-in-a-lifetime experience. About 20 minutes before landing, I was escorted to the cockpit for my pre-booked jump seat into King Island Airport. Watching the pilots land an aircraft from inside the cockpit had always been a dream of mine, and sitting in the legendary DC-3 made it even more special. I was given a headset, which allowed me to hear the pilots' communications with Air Traffic Control. King Island Airport is regularly served by Rex Airlines, King Island Airlines, and Sharp Airlines, connecting the island with Melbourne and a few other Tasmanian destinations. A bus was already waiting outside the terminal to take us to lunch and the attractions. During the ride, the driver provided a brief yet informative commentary about this Island and its largest settlement: Currie. For lunch, we were taken to the King Island Hotel. The meal was included in our tour, and we were given several options for entrées, mains, and desserts. The hotel had set aside a dedicated area for our group, with each family assigned their own table. Since I was travelling alone, I had a table to myself. To start, I ordered the chilli plum prawns served with steamed rice. The sweet and sour plum sauce complemented the rice beautifully, creating a delightful contrast of flavours. For the main course, I chose the steak with gravy. The portion was generous, and the steak, cooked to a perfect medium as requested, was exactly to my liking. To finish, I chose the panna cotta of the day, which had a rich and creamy texture with a refreshing strawberry flavour. Overall, I was thoroughly impressed with the quality of the meal. Each dish was prepared with care, and everything was absolutely delicious. The lunch took up half of our time on the island. Now, we are taking a scenic route to Currie Harbour, where we enjoyed a short walk along the beach and came across a beautifully decorated boathouse. This small building, overlooking the harbour, is dubbed 'the restaurant with no food.' The place is furnished with an assortment of colourful dining tables and chairs. The only thing missing is the food. You can bring your own, and enjoy the company of friends and family.  Furthermore, the paintings on the walls, books on the tables, and nearly every collectible in the house are for sale. Just leave the money in the honest box or pay ID the owner, and you can take an artwork or two as souvenirs. The harbour at Currie is small, but it holds significant importance as the only safe haven for boats on the storm-battered west coast. Currie Wharf was King Island's major port for over 100 years until Grassy Harbour was constructed in 1972. Before heading back to the airport, we made one final stop - the highlight of the day and a key reason for many people to book this tour: the King Island Dairy. Established in 1923, this dairy has earned an international reputation for producing exceptional specialty cheeses, including award-winning varieties of blue, cheddar, brie, and camembert. Upon arrival, we were welcomed into their tasting room, where a tasting plate featuring six of their most iconic cheeses awaited us. Each cheese was a masterpiece, and I can confidently say they were some of the finest I've ever tasted. Sadly, the future of this iconic dairy is uncertain. Saputo, a Canadian multinational company that acquired the diary in 2019, announced in September 2024 its decision to close it by mid-2025 after failing to find a buyer. The closure will mark the end of an era for King Island, taking with it over a century of cheese-making excellence. It would be a heartbreaking loss for the local community, the dairy industry, and cheese lovers around Australia. And just like that, our enjoyable time on King Island has come to an end. One of the greatest perks of a charter flight is the convenience—once everyone is onboard, we're ready for takeoff! An hour later, we're already over Melbourne. Essendon Airport's proximity to the city means passengers on the right side of the plane are treated to stunning views of the CBD during landing. To conclude, what an incredible day out!  I think $697 for two flights and a guided tour of King Island is excellent value. Everything was well-organised, the flights were smooth, and the staff were exceptionally friendly. Considering the cost of maintaining this historic aircraft and its age, it's hard to say how much longer the DC-3 will continue flying. If you're an aviation enthusiast, this experience should definitely be on your bucket list. Thank you so much for watching. If you find this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. See you all in my next video!

Finally, London to Dubai, you can fly Emirates premium economy for almost the exact same price as one of my favorite business classes in Europe, Finnair’s Air Lounge. I'll let you guess which I think is the better value there. With that, we're already approaching Dubai. As a Skywards member, I was able to stay connected with free wifi throughout the flight. Do I still think Emirates A350 Wi-Fi speed could use some boosting? Well, let's just say, unfortunately, I could barely send a WhatsApp message, but still it's free so I shouldn't complain. A wonderful flight on a wonderful aircraft in an especially comfortable seat. Welcome home A350. Four hours later, I'm back where I started, but now I get a real gate, which feels nice. That was a really fun day trip from Dubai. if you don't wanna go to the desert or to the mountains or to the beach, why not go to Bahrain. In all seriousness, though, I am glad to say I've now tried every cabin class on the Emirates A350. Business is beautiful, very comfortable in my opinion. Economy is where I feel like maybe I would all wanna experience that on a longer flight than I did today. The real question when it comes to economy class is, is this better than the A380 or the 777? Well, here's my answer. The A380, in my opinion, even if you get one of the older A380s, is still a superior option, just like I said about business class, this also applies to premium economy. The A380 is just such a pleasure to fly and Emirates has over 100 of them. The economy class on an A380 doesn't get more spacious, so even though this is a beautiful, modern new seat, the A380 is still the way to go. But what about compared to the Emirates 777, which I've never really been a huge fan of in economy class? Well, then, of course, the A350 wins. It's a much more modern, comfortable aircraft. The seat, I would say is about comparable in terms of leg room. That's not to say the leg room is great, but if you have a choice Emirates 777 or A350, the A350 is the way to go in economy and in premium economy. So, on that note, thank you for joining me in today's video, can I remind you again to check out Rocket Money to save a lot of money and until I see you in my next video, as always, fly safe.

yt_comments.text: We flew Chicago to Frankfort and back route in Jan 2024. Both legs were on the 747-800 and we were upstairs in business for both flights. I found both flights to be enjoyable. The planes were clean, the staff was some of the best I've encountered and every meal and drink onboard was great. With all that said, I'm really looking forward to trying out the new cabin on the 800's once it is in place. If these flights were daytime flights I'd give them 9 out of 10 but, because they were at night, both my wife and I tried to get a little sleep. I'm 6ft tall and have broad shoulders. My wife is 5'9. We both felt the shoulder area of the seats when in the bed configuration was too narrow. She is a side sleeper and she found it very difficult to get comfortable. I tried to get comfortable but eventually gave up and put the seat back in the upright but reclined position and was able to get an hour or so of sleep. I found the IFE to be pretty good but the screens were dim even when adjusted to their max brightness and showing their age. I still watched several good movies during my flights but did wish for a better screen. Can't wait until they update the 800's cabin.

DAVID: The Boeing 747, the Queen of the skies! Since it's introduction in the 1970s, the type has carried more
than 7.5 billion passengers on more than 23 million flights,
according to Airways Magazine. Over 1,200 Jumbo Jets were built
for passenger service, with the 747-400 being the most popular version, accounting for
over 500 of these frames. Of those 528 Boeing 747s able to carry passengers,
only a low two-digit number is still being used. You may find them on occasional
domestic flights on Air China and Rossiya, and there are a few
dubious airlines in countries like Iran, Nigeria and Moldova
still having some 747-400s registered. The only airline still relying on them for
a significant portion of their network is Germany's biggest airline, Lufthansa. A combination of factors led to them
being the type's last major operator, and with deliveries of new widebody
aircraft expected to pick up in 2025, it's days there are numbered too. Shortly before Asiana retired it's last
Boeing 747-400, we caught a flight on it from Osaka to Seoul, and captured the experience
of what the plane was like in service. And today we'll extend those same
 honours to Lufthansa's Boeing 747-400, but we one upping ourselves. Instead
of a single 2-hour short-haul flight, we'll cover 8-hour long-haul
flights across the Atlantic. And you heard right, flights!
As this video will be the first of two in-depth episodes covering the aircraft.
Today we're starting with a journey from Hannover via Frankfurt to
Chicago O'Hare in Economy Class, followed by a special video
to be released next month, taking a flight on, coincidentally,
the exact same 747, from Frankfurt to New York JFK in Business Class,
but not just any Business Class seat, the one in the first row,
in the nose of the plane! This video is already available to watch
right now to all of these amazing people who support our channel
with a paid sponsorship. Starting at as little as €2 per month,
which is just €24 per year, you too can support our mission to create
the most detailed flight reviews possible by signing up for a channel
membership right here on YouTube by simply clicking on the "Join"
button beneath this video. If you cannot wait or simply
share our passion for air travel, signing up for a channel membership helps us
put more time and energy into this channel, and I'm deeply grateful for
all of you who tirelessly support our work with your own hard-earned money. There's a lot to cover in these
two videos, and I'm excited to bring you along the journey
and share every last detail of it. So without further ado, let's get going! THEME MUSIC PLAYING Aviation geeks and frequent fliers,
welcome to this new episode of our flight review series Brutally Honest! My name is David and we're in
Hannover, Germany right now, about to catch the early morning
flight over to Frankfurt. Hannover is home to Germany's 8th busiest
airport, catering mainly to local vacationers, but is also very well-connected to
Europe's major hubs. Lufthansa offers up to eleven
daily flights to Frankfurt and Munich and airlines like Swiss, Austrian,
KLM, Air France, British Airways and Turkish Airlines also have
a sizeable presence here in Hannover. Check-in and security were super quick,
as the airport mainly sees seasoned business travelers
that early on a Monday Over there you can already see the plane
taking us to Frankfurt, a 1996-built Airbus A319, which touched down
just a minute after the A319 from Munich. Look at how both planes taxi into
their parking positions perfectly in sync! In general, these early morning domestic
flights to Lufthansa's hubs are very reliable, as virtually everyone on these flights is connecting to somewhere else, so even the tiniest delay would be
incredibly costly to the airline. Well, that includes us today too,
heading to beautiful Chicago, IL with a mere 70 minutes
to transit at Frankfurt Airport. Lufthansa's old short-haul planes are
all equipped with these Recaro 3520D seats, offering acceptable legroom, a standard
tray table and a high literature pocket. Adjustable reading lights and personal
air vents are located on the ceiling above. The gate is supposed to close at 8:25
and the doors have just been shut, perfectly on time for our
35-minute-long flight to Frankfurt. This, by the way, is one of my Holzkern
watches, which have been loyal companions on most of my trips and I'm very glad to have
Holzkern as a long time supporter of this channel, sponsoring today's video, which might be
handy to some of you because their products actually make fantastic
Valentine's Day presents! Holzkern is a company based in the same
town we're from, beautiful Vienna, Austria, so recently I made them show me
how they conduct their business. As you know we don't advertise much on
this channel because I want to truly believe in the company before I endorse them to you,
and Holzkern is definitely one of them, and their products make the perfect
gift for Valentine's Day, as the materials used mean no two
watches, rings or necklaces are the same! A unique piece of nature for that unique someone! And with every order Holzkern offers
free worldwide express shipping, meaning the products typically arrive within
less than a week, regardless of where you live and therefore are a great choice last-minute too. In their logistics center in Vienna I got to see just how much they offer and how many customers they're serving already. If you're interested too, for a limited
time only, using the dedicated link... ...and entering Coupon Code at checkout
gets you 15% off your entire order plus a free gift bag for your loved one's present.
Thank you to Holzkern for sponsoring this video. CAPTAIN SPEAKING IN GERMAN PLANE TAKING OFF Despite the flight being
only half an hour long, Lufthansa provided complementary
bottled water on this flight. Other beverages and snacks
had to be purchased, as is usual on Lufthansa's short-haul
flights in Economy these days. Considering how centrally located
Frankfurt and Munich are in Europe and how short most of Lufthansa's
intra-European flights are, that's something I have honestly
stopped being bothered by. Look at today's flight, for instance.
35 minutes wouldn't even be long enough for a complex beverage and snack service,
so a bottle of water and a little chocolate they hand out before landing are totally appropriate. ENGINE HUMS WHEELS TOUCH DOWN And after just 36 minutes in the air,
we've made it to Frankfurt. 9:14am, touchdown 26 minutes
ahead of schedule, as these early morning schedules have generous buffers. So, let's see how long it'll take us to get
from our plane to the connecting gate. Remember, we only have 70 minutes
until the departure of our connecting flight, which means more like 50 minutes
until the gate closes. I personally would not consider Frankfurt
a well-designed or easy to navigate airport, but it has, admittedly, improved a lot in terms
of efficiency and reliability in recent years. Still though, way too many flights use
remote stands and, what's noticeably annoying is that the airport doesn't use dedicated airport buses, but rather just uses regular
public transit buses, which due to their large number of seats offer
way too little space for all the carry-on luggage. BUS ENGINE NOISE, INDISTINCT CHATTER Now that we've arrived in the terminal,
let's see how long everything takes us. Three minutes in and we've
made it to passport control. Luckily, thanks to arriving from a Schengen
flight, we don't need to clear security again. And including the walk to our gate, we've made this connection within just slightly over 16 minutes. And for an airport the size of Frankfurt,
this is really good! The Lufthansa app has also
added quite a bit of functionality, assisting with real-time information
regarding our transit. Out there is the Jumbo Jet taking us to Chicago,
D-ABTK, a 2001-built Boeing 747-400. As of December 2024, Lufthansa still has
eight Boeing 747-400s in passenger service, in addition to 19 of newer 747-8s,
which are even slated to be fitted with new cabins in the coming years,
meaning they'll luckily stick around for now. TURNSTILE CHIMES
DOORS OPEN ENGINE HUMS Entering the plane through door two,
we're first passing through a sizable galley, followed by the plane's 2-4-2 configured
Premium Economy Class INDISTINCT CHATTER A small two and a half row Economy section
before door three and a regular 3-4-3 configured
Economy Class cabin behind that. I've chosen to sit in 40K for the wing view you'll
see in a minute, and just like all other seats, it comes with a headrest, adjustable vertically,
as well as on the sides. INDISTINCT CHATTER Waiting for us as well is a super soft
pillow with a reusable fabric cover, which are so much more comfortable than
a scratchy single-use covers many other airlines use. A blanket is provided too,
saving the plastic packaging thanks to only having a strip
of paper holding it together. Being 180cm tall, the legroom
is impressively good! Each seat comes with a cup holder,
which is on the back of the bi-fold tray table. Above that, a literature pocket with
a safety card and inflight shopping magazine, and each seat is also equipped
with an adjustable entertainment screen, which has USB-A and audio ports on the side,
right next to which you'll find a coat hook. Beneath the seats you'll find universal
power ports,with two per each three seats. Despite being amongst the older
types in Lufthansa's fleet, their Boeing 747-400s don't
actually have the oldest cabins. If you compare our seats today with the ones aboard the Boeing 747-8, you'll notice one distinct difference. While both feature Recaro CL3520
Economy Class seats, the Boeing 747-8 is fitted with a
Panasonic eX2 entertainment system, whereas our 747-400 has the slightly
more modern and higher quality Safran RAVE system you'll also find on
Lufthansa's A330s and A340s. That's because the 747-8s were
delivered in early-to-mid 2010s, while the 747-400s' cabins were
retrofitted only around the mid-2010s. Some more differences between
the 747-400 and the 747-8 cabins will become apparent in the
upcoming Business Class video. Lufthansa has also finally updated it's safety video
with one that, at last, has a modern feel to it. The 747-8 we're parked next to
is heading to Mexico City today. Before departure the crew handed out earbuds. In case you were wondering what it's like
to travel aboard Condor's new Airbus A330neos, we have two detailed narrated videos
available on our channel showcasing both their transatlantic Economy and Business Class products. BABY CRIES
ENGINE STARTS UP PLANE TAKES OFF After climbing out of Frankfurt, the crew
began the main meal service with a round of beverages
and a little salty snack. As for drinks, both hot and cold beverages, as well as options with
and without alcohol are offered at no extra charge. For the main meal service, Lufthansa
offers two choices in Economy Class, the classic chicken or pasta question. I went with the vegetarian pasta, which
today is penne with cheesy cauliflower. This is accompanied by a cold but crispy
bread roll with butter and cheese, some coleslaw and a piece of apple cake. And Lufthansa provides metal cutlery, which\ gives
the meal service a slightly more elegant feel. Overall, this is a good
Economy Class meal service! I particularly appreciate the availability
of a vegetarian meal option and the lack of single-use plastics. However it wasn't the tastiest, as the cheesy
cauliflower pasta was a bit dry and bland, and I would've appreciated
the bread roll being warmed up. But compared to what Lufthansa
used to offer in the past, this is a giant leap forward and,
generally, a totally fine lunch spread. Afterwards, tea and coffee were offered
in those slick reusable cups. Lufthansa has made notable efforts
to reduce waste, which is commendable. Half-litter bottles of water were handed out too. ENGINE HUMS The lavatories have a really cool retro feel
to them, but are still very well-kept. There's regular hand-wash, little cups for when you
brush your teeth, as well as hand- and face-towels. Some also have changing tables. In the rear galley, more bottle water, as well as
some other beverages were made available. I always emphasise: drinking enough water
is the key to not feeling fatigued after a long-haul flight, and Lufthansa
offering half-liter bottles of water, both handed out proactively as well as yours
to take in the galley, really helped with that. So kudos to Lufthansa for keeping me hydrated
and not just offering water sparsely in shot-glass sized plastic cups
like many other airlines do. As we're cruising towards Greenland,
let's have a view at what the In-Flight Entertainment System has to offer. Aboard the 747-400s Lufthansa
employs Safran's RAVE system, which you will also find
aboard their A330s and A340s, as well as on older twin-aisle airliners of their
subsidiaries Austrian, Brussels and Discover. Despite it's age, it offers a solid
selection of movies and TV shows, including multiple episodes of popular ones as well as games, the Kids section,
as well as music, audio books and podcasts. An in flight mapping application
is installed too. The headphones handed out in the beginning
are simple earbuds that get the job done. After a little nap, we're already
above North America, and before we start our descent into
Chicago, it's time for another snack. On this flight, Lufthansa offers
a vegetarian hot pocket, a simple yet tasty tomato-and-cheese calzone. Before landing they even handed out
hot towels, which is a nice gesture. And we've got another little piece of chocolate,
which shows a small change as well. This is still some of the old chocolate they've
been serving for a while, made by coppeneur, while the new ones, which are equal in weight, are made by Lindt and also come in a paper packaging. Over the years, Lufthansa was widely criticized
for an array of issues, and rightfully so. However, I personally believe it is time to
acknowledge just how much things have improved In the grand scheme of things, today's journey was superb! An on-time connecting flight, a fast
and efficient transit at Frankfurt, good legroom on the long haul flight,
high-quality amenities with a focus on reducing plastic waste, an overall good meal offering, a pleasant crew, and, considering how little I actually paid,
including a checked bag and a seat reservation for what essentially was a main season ticket,
a fantastic value for money! With the arrival of more modern aircraft, which will come with a new and improved in-flight entertainment system
and a bunch of new seat features, Lufthansa is slated to become one of
the better choices to cross the Atlantic with. And I'm here for it! WHEELS TOUCH DOWN With that, welcome to Chicago's
O'Hare International Airport! We're about to arrive at O'Hare's
Terminal 5, like all international flights, but it's important to note that
Lufthansa is one of three airlines whose international flights depart from Terminal 1, alongside United and ANA. Thank you again to Holzkern for sponsoring this video and check out their selection of watches, jewelery and accessories,
as Valentine's Day is coming up and Holzkern offers the perfect gifts,
plus free worldwide express shipping. Once again, also a very special thank you
to our channel members for supporting our work, through monthly financial contributions,
but whether you are a channel member, a subscriber or are simply stopping by for this
one video, thank you very much for watching! I'll see you again for a new video soon
and until then, safe travels!

reviews.transcript_full:
While other US legacy carriers have sought 
to ensure inflight entertainment is present   on ALL their mainline aircraft, American 
Airlines has moved forward with more of an   austerity approach. Indeed, we’ve seen 
a reduction of seatback entertainment   across much of the fleet operating 
domestic services. Most recently,   the carrier opted to remove seatback screens from 
its A319s in its latest retrofit program. These   jets were the carrier's final short-to-medium 
haul aircraft equipped with the systems. It should go without saying that this 
move has been implemented to save costs. As you can guess, when compared to NO 
screens at all, inflight entertainment   systems cost money to install and upkeep, and 
licensing for the films and TV is not free. Furthermore, screens add additional weight,   thus contributing to greater fuel 
burn. From an operational perspective,   there’s a lot to lose by having the systems, 
and a lot to gain from removing them. American has begun retrofitting the 
cabins of over 30 legacy Airbus A319s.   This move is important because the 
legacy A319s were the last of the   carrier's short-to-medium-haul aircraft that 
were fitted with seatback entertainment. Thus, it won’t be long before American Airlines 
short and medium-haul passengers will lose all   hope of seatback entertainment. Of course, 
a notable exception occurs when widebody,   intercontinental jets are deployed domestically as 
a way to reposition for another long haul flight. There were 32 A319s received from 
2013 to 2015, with the airline's   other A319s having been inherited from 
US Airways and America West Airlines. The group of 32 are noteworthy as 
the only Sharklet-equipped A319s   that operate in the US. These will 
be American Airlines' first batch   of aircraft to be overhauled as part 
of its fleet retrofitting efforts. When it comes to the passenger experience, it will 
set American Airlines back from the competition,   as it will become the only US legacy carrier that   has no seatback entertainment on its 
short-to-medium-haul mainline aircraft.   Carriers like Delta and United have opted to 
continue seatback entertainment. These carrier   retrofits have focused on improving 
and installing seatback screens. It won't be a case of bringing a 
book or getting bored, however. As is a trend with some airlines, 
seatback entertainment will be   replaced by seatback device holders and 
passengers are able to stream content. This is available on smartphones,   tablets and laptops, although it may not 
work until the aircraft reaches 10,000 ft. There is also free Wi-Fi for T-Mobile customers   on certain plans, while connectivity 
can be accessed by others for a fee. To bring things full circle, American has 
taken a bet that customers won’t mind the   lack of seatback entertainment because they’ll 
choose the airline for other reasons - such as   connectivity to certain airports, or comfortable 
flight scheduling. IF this bet pays off,   then American will save money on acquiring, 
installing, and maintaining those screens.   And again, as mentioned, it will 
save on fuel with lighter aircraft. But what do YOU think of this 
decision by American? Is it a   move that will pay off? Or backfire? 
Let us know by leaving a comment.

reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm taking you on one of the longest flights I've done recently, flying Qantas from Sydney to Dallas on the Airbus A380. This was a long haul economy flight, and a lot of people ask me about it, and I took notes the entire way, so I can give you guys an honest review. Okay, before we get started, this flight came right after a cruise around New Zealand. So, I boarded the flight well rested and really curious to see if Qantas actually lives up to its reputation. Qantas gets a lot of hype, at least that's what I'm seeing, especially when it comes to their A380. And by the end of this video, I'm going to share whether I think it is deserved, plus three important watch outs you're going to want to know before you book this exact flight. So, I want to know if you've ever flown Qantas before. Drop your experience down in the comments. I'd love to see if your Qantas flight lived up to the hype, too. This was a Qantas Airbus A380 800 flying nonstop from Sydney, Australia, to Dallas/Fort Worth. The flight time was 15 hours and 25 minutes, and we departed about 20 minutes late, around 2:30 in the afternoon. So, you guys, this aircraft is massive. It is a full two-level plane, and it was not at capacity, which definitely impacted the experience. So, before boarding, I stopped off quickly at the Qantas First Lounge. I have One World Emerald status through American Airlines Executive Platinum, and the lounge was outstanding. And I don't always get access to the first lounges, so this was a real treat for me. I had a lovely lunch there, and I even got a complimentary 20-minute foot massage, which felt like a total luxury before such a long flight. So, I want to know if you're kind of a lounge person. Do you hit the lounge before a long flight? Which one do you like to go to, or are you kind of a person that just goes straight to the gate? I'm curious which approach that you prefer. So, boarding took place at gate eight in Sydney and it was very organized and well staffed. So, Qantas boards by number and the lower level of the aircraft actually boarded first, which made the boarding process really smooth and efficient and I was in that first group cuz I was on the bottom floor of the aircraft. My seat was actually 52H. It's an aisle seat at the front of the economy cabin on the lower level one row behind the bulkhead and right behind first class and kind of the galley. So, I had this entire row to myself, which meant I could enjoy the window for takeoff and if I wanted to to stretch out to nap throughout the flight. You guys, so good. I thought about choosing the bulkhead, which is like the front row in economy, but ultimately I didn't do that because the armrest don't lift up and the seats feel kind of tight and if you get really lucky and there's nobody else there, you can't lay across at all. I'm going to come back to that later when we talk about some of the watch outs here, but I just wanted to mention that. So, what do you prefer on long haul flights? Are you front of economy? Are you bulkhead, back of the plane? Are you first class, business class? Let me know your go-to spot. I'm usually an economy girl, but I love to try to get as close to the front of that cabin if I can. So, I was seated just in front of the wing near the engines, but the takeoff and landing were so smooth. We had zero turbulence at all and you guys, honestly, the seat belt sign, I think, was off for almost the entire 15-hour flight and the cabin on this aircraft is extremely quiet, which I had read was the case. It was so nice not to hear that constant, really loud, reverberating engine noise. And like I mentioned, I had those two windows I could kind of see halfway out each one of them, which was really nice. The cabin temperature was a little bit warm while we were on the ground in Sydney, but about an hour into the flight it kind of cooled down a little bit and stayed more comfortable throughout. As I would walk back to the restrooms, I did know that the uh noticed that the cabin got a little bit cooler. So, as you were going towards the back of the temperature came down a little bit. Now, the cabin noise level was really low, like I said, exactly what you'd expect on an A380 out of the aircraft itself. And one of the biggest positives on this aircraft was the seat recline. You guys, look at this. I mean, this is excellent. It makes a huge difference on a long-haul flight. You can really get that seat back. Now, charging in the seats was a little bit tricky. My US plug actually worked to charge, and I was really glad I brought a long cable because the charger's kind of down low between the seats close to the floor. Now, I didn't even find the USB port in the armrest until the very end of the flight, but the USB charging did not work on my seat, and I heard a lot of people saying that it did not work in their seat. So, it is best to pack a traditional charging setup with like a cable and actual, you know, little hub thingy just in case. Let's talk about entertainment. The in-flight entertainment system was okay, but nothing really special. It's controlled with a remote and the touchscreen option is available, but it worked really inconsistently and with a noticeable delay. In fact, I noticed people banging on their touchscreens to get them to work, and that is really unpleasant for the person in front of you. It feels like a thumping banging sound. So, I think this aircraft needs a little bit of repair. And compared to my recent Japan Airlines flight, the screen quality felt really small and pretty poor. With that said, though, there was actually a good selection of content, including movies from HBO, Paramount. They had Australian films, music, and lots more. I watched a full two movies and appreciated the first-run selection. I saw a lot of people watching a lot of movies on this particular flight. There was also a moving map that showed airspeed, altitude, like time to destination, and even a sky cam view from above the aircraft, which was really, really cool. And the system also very clearly displayed meal and drink options with detailed choices, which was great. So, how do you entertain yourself when you're flying? Are you like a a movie person? Do you listen to music on your own device? Do you use the seatback, or do you just try to conk out? I'm kind of trying to see what's most popular here. Now, the restrooms were a little larger than average, especially compared to like American Airlines, but smaller, I'd say, than Japan Airlines, but they were not cleaned a single time during the 15-hour flight. Yeah, they replaced the toilet paper, but trash overflowed, the floor became literally sticky, like your feet would stick and unstick when you walked in there, and the overall cleanliness really declined throughout the flight. I just couldn't believe it. The service overall was professional, but it was kind of, I guess you could say, minimal. The crew did their jobs, but there was no explanation of like restroom locations if you're in this cabin or that. There was really no overview of how the self-serve snacks worked. The captain said something about it for like 1 second, and there just wasn't a lot of proactive communication. And if I'm being honest, some of the interactions came off as a little bit snobby. >> [gasps] >> But then some of the crew were warm and friendly, so it was kind of a mixed bag. People are people, it's just the way it is. Now, let's talk about the food. I had high expectations for this. On the way to New Zealand, I flew American Airlines from Dallas to Auckland, and the snack that they gave me at mid-flight, you guys, it was like a raw stromboli, like they'd forgot to bake it. It was like raw dough. So, my expectations for Qantas were kind of high because I thought, well, I mean, it's got to be better than this, right? So, here's how everything worked. About 30 minutes into the flight, we were handed a bottle of water, which was great. A lot of times you're thirsty and you don't want to wait forever, followed immediately by a snack and beverage service. A very early dinner was served around 3:45. I mean, that's early if you're thinking the flight just took off. The main options were pumpkin tortellini, a beef with mustard gravy, or cold chicken salad along with a selection of Australian wines. I chose the beef. It was served hot, but it was fatty, it was kind of bland, and the gravy tasted like cheap brown gravy, not like a mustard gravy. The meal came with bread and cheese and crackers, but there was no salad or fruit. They gave us a dessert of an ice cream bar, which was really delicious, but I don't know, I just wasn't in the mood for it. In hindsight, I probably would have selected the salad main cuz I saw it and it looked really nice and tasty and fresh. Had like edamame in there, looked really good. There were also some self-serve snacks and drinks toward the back of the plane, but it was really easy to miss that because they didn't talk much about it, and the drinks were like put away. If you didn't know, you wouldn't be able to grab them. Later in the flight, there was a snack walk-through around 8:00 p.m. It was a little chicken toasty. Oh, I'm sorry. The snack walk-through was just like little packaged snacks and some waters. And then around 10:00 p.m., we got a chicken toasty, which tasted great. It was served hot and not raw like my weird American Airlines strong bully. Then they had a full breakfast before landing at 3:30 in the morning with a choice of your main could be frittata or fruit. Everybody then also got a muffin, coffee, and a yogurt pod on the little plate. That was great. I'm sorry, the coffee would have been on request, but the the yogurt and the muffin were included. The breakfast was decent and hearty, and the yogurt was really, really good. I'd say the coffee, though, was really bad. It was watery, lukewarm, so I ended up having to grab a coffee when I landed in the airport to trick my body into thinking, "Okay, it's like morning time." So, for those of you out there who fly a lot, I want to know what is the best or worst economy meal that you have ever had on a flight. Share it below. I really love to read the flight food stories. Now, for those watch-outs about this flight specifically from Sydney to Dallas. First, I would not recommend boarding the flight super hungry. The food is fine, but it's not especially filling or exciting, and timing kind of matters on a flight this long, so I would bring some snacks. Second, be very, very cautious when you're booking bulkhead seats, the ones up at the very front of the economy cabin. The seats are narrower, remember those armrests don't lift, and there is a lot of foot traffic and galley noise cuz you're right by the galley a lot of times. Also, if you see baby icons on the seat map, book those nearby rows carefully. They have these pull-down bassinets and a lot of times toddlers, babies, families are traditionally seated here. And in my experience, because these families sometimes will congregate here and sit here, the extra space in front of them means the kids are going to roam about, run about, and that can happen. On the flip side, if you are traveling with kids or as a family, this can be a great place for you to sit as long as you understand the front row armrests don't move, and your little ones cannot nap. I saw a family with a baby moving from the bulkhead to an empty row behind them because they couldn't let their baby nap. So, just something for you to be aware of. And this again has happened multiple times on my flights where the little ones are up front. So, if you want to sleep, I would not recommend booking at the front of the aircraft. I'm going to change my strategy on this. Now, the back of the lower deck of this aircraft actually tends to be really quiet, and you're not really sacrificing space. So, move yourself back there if you're going for quiet. Third, Qantas does not allow power banks, you guys. They mention it several times in their overhead announcements. So, you're supposed to rely on that in-seat power. You need to bring long charging cables or charging your phones and your devices might be really frustrating due to the location of the charging spots close to the floor, and your USB charging in your armrest may not work. All right, my overall thoughts on this, you guys, on the flight. I got to tell you, that seat recline alone makes this a good aircraft for long-haul flights. The flight was quiet. It was smooth. It was comfortable. But, beyond that, nothing truly wowed me about Qantas in this case. It's a solid experience, but it's not one that completely lives up to the hype. Now, if you want a comparison, be sure to check out my Japan Airlines flight review. That one is from Dallas to Haneda Airport, which is Tokyo. And also, for my adventures before this flight, be sure to watch my New Zealand cruise content, which I'm going to link to down below. Now, I want to hear from you. Would you fly Qantas again based on what you've heard? Comment yes or no, and tell me why. I'll be reading all your thoughts. And until next time, we'll see you on the high seas or in the friendly skies. Bye-bye.

So, how was my Emirates economy class flight? Overall, I'm super impressed with the experience. The airport experience wasn't the best, but not much you can do if you fly from Heath Terminal 3. Emirates clearly has the best I in disguise. I have mixed feelings about the food. The main meal was delicious and the quality and quantity of the food were spoton. Breakfast was very underwhelming though. The cabin environment was perfect. The aircraft was very clean and the crew were extremely welcoming and attentive. What do you guys think? Please like, share, and subscribe the channel for more content. The meal included a salad, the main course, dessert and bread. The bread unfortunately didn't impress me much. It lacked flavor. [Music] My wife went with the vegan option again, and this time it came with tofu and some other ingredients that we honestly couldn't identify. reviews.transcript_full: Cathay Pacific is well regarded for its comfortable and high-quality economy class service, offering a solid experience for both short and long-haul flights. Seat comfort and legroom. Cathay Pacific offers a seat pitch of 31 to 32 inches and a seat width of 17.5 to 18 inches with seating arrangements in 3 to 4 to 3 or 2 to 4 to 2 configurations, depending on the aircraft. While legroom is adequate for most, taller passengers may feel a bit cramped. The seats feature moderate recline, adjustable headrests, and are equipped with pillows and blankets on long flights for added comfort. In-flight entertainment (IFE), the personalized screens, 10 to 12 inches, offer a wide selection of movies, TV shows, games, and music. Wi-Fi is available on many long-haul flights, though it's often pricey. Passengers also have access to USB charging ports and power outlets, ensuring devices stay charged throughout the flight. Food and beverage meals in economy class include a mix of Asian, Western, and vegetarian options with complimentary soft drinks, wine, and beer. Special meals, e.g., gluten-free, halal, can be requested 24 hours in advance. Overall, food quality is above average for economy class, and service is efficient. Service. Cathay Pacific's cabin crew is known for being friendly, attentive, and professional, making sure passengers are comfortable throughout the flight. Boarding is well organized with priority boarding for premium passengers. Cabin ambiance. The cabin is modern and clean with calming lighting and good air quality. Restrooms are regularly cleaned, and the overall atmosphere is conducive to relaxation, especially on long-haul flights. Baggage allowance. Economy class passengers are typically allowed one checked bag, up to 23 kg, and one carry-on bag, up to 7 kg. A small personal item is also permitted, offering enough space for most travelers' belongings. Final verdict. Cathay Pacific offers a comfortable and reliable economy class experience with solid service, ample entertainment, and good meal options. It's a great choice for travelers looking for a pleasant flight experience. Pros: comfortable seats with adequate legroom, extensive in-flight entertainment options, friendly and professional service. Cons: limited legroom for taller passengers, Wi-Fi can be expensive. Overall, Cathay Pacific is a strong contender for those seeking comfort and reliability in economy class.

price of this flight is From Islamabad to Istanbul business class ticket will cost you between 2000 to 2200 USD If you convert these charges into rupees, it will be around Rs.350,000 Inside the plane, the business-class cabin, from Islamabad was almost empty, and very few seats are occupied Before that, I give you a review of the cabin And how were the hospitality and food How were the inflight entertainment and utilities Before the review of these facilities, I want to tell you that I will tell you at the end The difference between, Business class flights from Islamabad and Business class flight from Istanbul What is the difference between both flight services But first, you can enjoy the take-off from Islamabad Airport And witness the beautiful scenes of Islamabad, during take-off The first thing you get when seated on the plane is this hygiene kit And this is a uniform kit for all classes Passengers of Business class and Economy class both get the same hygiene kit In these kits, they provide you masks and sanitizers And wet wipes too Now let's talk about cabin space Obviously, as this is business class, it is very much spacious Legroom is big and wide You can travel lying down comfortably There is a storage box given to you, just in front of the seat Which is very spacious You can keep your shoes or handy luggage in it Your passport or tickets anything you can keep inside The seats are reclinable completely This seat also doubles as a bed If you want to make it a bed, it becomes like a bed If you have a long flight, you can easily travel by lying down or sleep easily on these seats It is a very comfortable experience Apart from this, In the cabin, there are electric sockets near your seat To help you to charge your laptop or phone  Now let's talk about something to eat and drink First, we are talking about drinks You are initially provided with a menu It has three options, You can take 
 juices, soft drinks, or alcohol Due to the pandemic, there is an issue you cannot order Tea or Coffee Because as per international regulations, during the pandemic there is no concept of reheating So, you don't get Tea or Coffee here That is a big issue on the flight, because if you are feeling tired And you don't get Tea or Coffee, then it will be a problem Now let's talk about food, First of all The food tray in the cabin is of standard size like the one you get in economy class During the pandemic, the in-flight food is not very good, it was a bad experience Even if you are traveling in Business class, the food you get First of all, you do not have any other option Every passenger gets the same food In the meal tray, you can get a sandwich and salad Vegetables, Yogurt, and a brownie And as I told you earlier, the food is cold If the food is cold, it does not taste good But my return flight in Business class from Istanbul Food served there, I will tell you how this food is different from that one, will tell the experience, in the end Now let's talk about connectivity, there is a Wifi facility available in Business class flights, And it is a reasonable connection You can get 1GB of data in it When I take a speed test for Data, It is about 670 Kbps which is the half of the 1Mbps. I get this If you have to send e-mails, check Twitter, Whatsapp or  want to communicate, then this is enough In fact, I tried using Netflix, but it was a little bit slow Still, you can use it on mobile in standard definition Now let's talk about the inflight entertainment system Nothing fancy about entertainment Only one notable thing which differentiates  Business class from economy class is the bigger screen size, Big than the Tablet size It makes the experience better The other options you have related to content A lot of international movies and series All the famous blockbusters, you can see Besides that, the Turkish series are also available Ertugral and other famous series available There is only one Pakistani movie, Chalay Thay Saath Also, there were limited options in Indian movies Only 3 or 4 movies were available So, there is less content on Bollywood and Lollywood But If you are a Hollywood fan, then you have No issue If you want to see the trending series, they are available Live TV is also available, with 5 or 6 channels Among these 4 are news channels BBC, CNN, one Turkish channel, and CNBC Live are available These channels are also available in Economy class But as a sportsman, and a Football fan I have an issue during flights, as I mostly travel on weekends And most of the matches are on the weekends So this issue arises, how to watch the match on the flight But in past, I traveled on Etihad Air as well And now traveling in Turkish Airlines, in both they have options to watch Live sports Now let's talk about what I told you When you came back from Istanbul The services of Business class from Istanbul are quite different, in comparison with the same flight from Pakistan Let me tell you, As you board the flight, you will get a Versace pouch containing the essential toiletries, like perfume, facewash Tindle kit, shaving kit. This is a fancy pouch you get On your return, you get a royal treatment Besides that, the headphones you receive are fancy and comfortable for your ears So, you will get to know that the services are upgraded And my favorite is, these slippers are provided If you have a seven to eight-hour flight If you are wearing shoes all the time then it will be very uncomfortable On my return flight, slippers were provided to me It helps to make the journey comfortable In food, again due to the pandemic, the food was cold But there are more options, compared to my last flight. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Plane Stuff! Today’s flight review will take us aboard Delta Air Lines newest fleet member, the A321neo, from Los Angeles to Minneapolis. In the next video I'll cover the onward flight on an almost 31 year old A320. Make sure to subscribe so you don't miss it! This is my first narrated video, or even video of this type in general, so it will probably be a little rough. Please do let me know what you think in the comments below so I can improve! Flight details can be found in the description, and I hope you enjoy! Welcome to LAX. It's very early in the morning and I've just been dropped off in front of Delta’s Terminal 3. LAX has 9 terminals in total, Delta occupies Terminal 2 and 3, although all check-ins for Delta now go through 3. I’m not checking bags on today's flight and already have my boarding pass, so I’m able to head straight to TSA, which is really quick at this time in the morning. It looks like we'll be going out of Gate 37B, so time to get walking! LAX is in the middle of a massive overhaul and work on terminal 3 was just completed shortly before filming. It feels very clean and roomy, although it has no moving walkways and some pretty long distances, which may be annoying to some. The food options here are a little limited, however all LAX terminals are now interconnected thanks to the ongoing overhaul... ...so you can always make the hike to other terminals for plenty more options. I decided to grab some snacks at this Hudson Nonstop, which uses cameras to track what you pick up and automatically charge you without the need for a cash register. Here is our aircraft today! N512DE. This aircraft was delivered to Delta in December 2022, making it just 8 months old at the time of filming. The A321neo is the newest member of Delta's ongoing fleet renewal... ...alongside the A220, A330neo, A350, newer 737-900s, and the upcoming 737 MAX, which are replacing or already have replaced many of Delta's older fleet members. One thing I didn't mention earlier about Terminal 3 is the music. The music here is pretty overwhelming, especially near the windows where I tend to sit. I think I can safely say this music just doesn't work at 7am, and even less so at 5am as I’ve previously experienced. Well after about an hour of enduring the music, it’s time to board. Delta boards in 10 groups. As with most full service carriers, Delta starts by boarding premium cabins and elite status holders... ...and after that they’ll move into the Main Cabin, which is split between status holders in Main 1, this will be our group, then Main 2 and 3, and finally Basic Economy. Gate Agent: In the general boarding lane I'd like to continue the boarding process by inviting Main 1, Main 1 welcome aboard. It looks like this aircraft has Delta's new free WIFI! We’ll check that out after takeoff. Delta A321neos currently have one seat layout, with a total of 194 seats. The front of the cabin has 20 of Delta's newest first class product, these are hard-shell recliners that are supposed to be a step up above their traditional counterparts. These seats do look really cool and I'd love to review them one day, but for now I'll have to direct you to this great review by Jeb Brooks! Behind first class, there are 42 Comfort+ seats, Delta's premium economy offering with more legroom, extra snacks, and dedicated overhead bin space. Finally in the back is the main cabin, with 132 seats. And here is our seat 30F... without a window. Well it looks like I got unlucky, and booked a windowless window seat. I normally check third party seat maps while booking, and this is the one time I slipped. This is exactly why I recommend you check out websites like seatmaps.com while selecting your seats to help avoid reclineless seats or windowless seats like this. I really wish airlines would just warn you if a seat lacks a window, I'm sure plenty of people out there wouldn’t shy away from such a seat... ...given how many I never even see open their window shades anyway. If Ryanair can get this right, I'd expect Delta to. Anyway, time to check out the seat! Overhead you will find the standard personal air vent, reading light, and flight attendant call button. The seatback features one of Delta's wonderful screens, which we will explore in a few minutes. Just below the screen you will find your headphone jack as well as a USB port. The seat also comes with a single piece full sized tray table. The Legroom is perfectly fine, for reference I am 6ft/1.8m tall. In between the seats in front of you, you will find universal power outlets, meaning there are two for every row of three seats. The seat also has a moderate amount of recline and an adjusting headrest. The seatback pocket is pretty big, and another safety card pocket is hidden inside. Speaking of the safety card, here is a quick look! After getting complementary earbuds, which are alright, it's time to take a look through the in flight entertainment system. First off, Delta seatback screens have a very clean flight tracker installed, which offer tons of viewing options, including the heads up display, which is my personal favorite. Next up, the screen has this nice list of all the aircraft types in Delta’s fleet. As well as an airport directory featuring terminal maps of major Delta hubs and their partner hubs. You will also find a link to the menu for today's flight on a QR code, as well as a WFI guide. Now for the main feature of the in-flight entertainment, the entertainment. Delta offers a massive selection of movies and tv shows, too big to scroll through in reasonable time.  I doubt most people will have a problem finding something to watch here. You can also find live news, music, games, and a kids section. If you prefer to use your personal device instead of the seatback screen, inflight entertainment can also be streamed to your device for free. Safety Video: …make sure your seatbelt is fastened, to fasten, insert the metal tip into the buckle and adjust the strap so it's low and tight across your lap. Safety Video: To release the belt, just lift the top of the buckle. Please remain seated with your seatbelt securely fastened... Time to push back! Thankfully the person sitting behind me said they didn't mind me filming out of the window just behind my seat, so I still got some cool views for you. If you’d like to skip the takeoff and head straight to the narrated part of this video, chapters are available below. Now that we are in the air, it’s time to check out the WIFI. Delta is in the process of rolling out free WIFI for SkyMiles members on domestic flights. You can tell if your aircraft has their new WIFI system by looking for that blue sticker next to the door we saw earlier as we entered. Getting access to that free WIFI is as simple as just logging into your SkyMiles account, and watching a quick ad. I'd say that's a pretty good deal! About 40 minutes after takeoff, a snack and beverage service arrived.  For snacks you have the choice between a small bag of Sunchips, a bag of salted almonds, a white chocolate granola bar, and the famous Biscoff cookies. I always ask for two items, and have yet to be disappointed! And here is the bathroom, this one is the rear right. There isn't anything special about it, being a little tight, and a little dirty just an hour into the flight. Well, without a window there isn't really much else for me to show you, as I didn't want to disturb the passengers behind me mid flight... ...so I'll check back in as we get closer to Minneapolis. About an hour before landing, the crew did a second quick service! I decided to just get another cookie. I really hope this screen isn't correct! And thankfully it wasn't, so time to get ready for landing! Flight Attendant: It's been our pleasure to have you on board with us today. Flight Attendant: To prepare for landing please ensure your seatbelt is fastened, your seatback and tray table are in their upright and locked... Flight Attendant: It's our pleasure to welcome you to Minneapolis-Saint Paul where the local time is 11:34, there has been a two hour time change. Flight Attendant: Please stay seated with your seatbelts fastened...  I really enjoyed my first time on a Delta A321neo, despite the lack of a window, which is partly on me anyway. Overall Delta offers a great service, and they have equipped their A321neos with very nice and comfortable seats... …and good quality in-flight entertainment systems that should hold up for years to come. Anyway welcome to Minneapolis-Saint Paul! I hope I'll see you in the second part of our journey, where, instead of a brand new aircraft, we'll be taking a nearly 31 year old A320! Please let me know what you thought of my first flight review in the comments! I know I have a lot to learn, but I still hope you could enjoy it, and will stick around for the next one!

reviews.transcript_full:
Tonight it's American Airlines turn 
to show us what they got for one of   their transpacific flights! We'll be flying 
from Tokyo to Dallas in Main Cabin Extra,   American's step-up economy product. We'll 
also see how the largest airline in the   world stacks up to some of the other 
transpacific flights we've seen on this   channel. Is Main Cabin Extra worth the extra 
cost? Come along and let's find out together! Good afternoon and welcome back to another video and welcome back to Haneda Airport terminal 3. Well,   we're getting close to the end of the year but
we still have time for a few more flights and   to start us off we'll be flying with American 
Airlines on a flight from Tokyo to Dallas. And   this is actually going to be my first time 
flying American on an international flight   outside North America so we'll see how their 
trans-pacific product is and compare to some   of the other airlines which we've experienced on 
the channel. We'll be flying in economy class on   one of their Dreamliners and the flight is set 
to depart at 6 p.m. So come along let's enjoy   American Airlines as we go from A to to A!  All right well arriving to the airport I headed to   the kiosks at the I check-in area which was 
being used by American. Earlier I checked in   online through the AA app so by the time I arrived at the airport I just had to drop off my bags and   the bag drop off lane took no more than a few 
moments. I should point out that I was headed   to Toronto so at baggage drop off I received an 
'international to International' sticker on my   passport which signified that I didn't have to collect and recheck my bag after US Passport control. With   the formalities out of the way I figure it was 
a good idea to step outside for a few moments   before heading through passport control on a 
pleasant early winter day. We even catch a Finnair Dreamliner! They have quite the interesting 
route due to the closed Russian airspace and   I recently found out that they were the first 
European airline to fly non-stop between Europe   and Japan. Did their non-stop flight to Japan 
begin in 1979,  '81, or '83? Leave your guess in the comments. EE: Terminal 3 used to be called the "Intl Terminal"
until T2 started accepting intl flights! Today we'll be departing from gate 145.   It's one of these lower level gates 
which exist only on the east side of   the terminal. Already waiting for us is 
our Dreamliner which will take us to DFW! We still had some time to kill and the good 
news is that gate 145 is not too far from the   food court so I figured I might as well. I went 
to the noodle outlet at the end and picked up   a tsukemen dish - one of my favorite noodle 
dishes in Japan! It's very similar to Ramen   with the main difference being the noodles and 
soup are separate and you dip one in the other.   There's a healthy serving of cold noodles 
alongside a warm broth with pork, nori and   green onions. A solid call and I can't believe 
it took me all these years to try this place out! By the time I returned to the gate boarding 
was well underway and look who's beside US! Air   Canada has since returned to using the B777
for their Toronto - Haneda route. That plane will beat   me to my final destination by about 6 hours. So is a detour through America worth it? Stay tuned and   find out! The only upgrade I purchased for this 
trip was Main Cabin Extra which gave me group   five boarding. It appears that Americans value 
higher boarding zones a little bit more than we do   north of the border. I really don't know why nine 
boarding zones are necessary but I digress. today   Today we'll be in seat 20J, an aisle seat on the emergency row which is dedicated to Main Cabin Extra passengers.   Passengers in this row can take advantage 
of the dedicated overhead storage bins as well. EE: Winter is a good time for aisle seats. Easy access to the aisle, and there's not too many sights due do darkness. Tonight we're on an almost 4-year-old 787 7-8 Dreamliner. American   has one configuration of this aircraft with 
234 seats across three cabins. Main Cabin Extra   and main cabin seats are in the same cabin but 
marketed as different products. There are seven   lavatories on board and it's important to 
note that there are none at the rear of the aircraft. It'll take about 10 
and 1/2 hours to reach Dallas.   and we'll be staying well south 
of Alaska as we cross the Pacific. EE: Footage of cabin is combination of AA176 and AA169 (LAX-HND) The economy cabin is laid out in a 3-3-3 seating 
configuration. Bulkhead monitors provide flight   information and messages throughout the flight. 
The cabin had a healthy blue glow during the   start of the flight and warm orange and reds 
towards the end. Main Cabin Extra are rows 10,   11, and 20 along with the centre seats of rows 12 through 18 so if you are after a window seat and   Main Cabin Extra you are limited to six possible 
options on the dash eight Dreamliner. The seats were   quite comfortable with an adjustable headrest. 
A pillow and blanket were provided for guests   which was advantageous as I thought they kept 
the cabin on the very chilly (read: freezing!) side. Of course one   benefit of the emergency row is the unlimited leg room at your disposal and you don't have to worry   about others in your row passing you when they 
want to get out. On the other hand no luggage can   be stored on the floor during taxi takeoff and 
landing so the dedicated bins come in especially   handy for the emergency row passengers. With no lavatories at the rear of the plane this area   was highly trafficked perhaps more than other 
Dreamliners particularly after the meal service   so I wouldn't recommend the aisle seat of the 
emergency row. The seats are slightly different   than the rest of the cabin housing a control 
panel on the one side. The IFE system pulls out   from under the armrest and you have to to press 
the tab to release it which took a few moments to   spot in the dim cabin. On my return trip I was in 
17D which I think is a better illustration of what   you get with Main Cabin Extra. The seatback has 
a large adjustable display. The lit pocket which   contained the safety card was just below with 
a table and pocket under that. You'll find the   power outlet at the base and the seat pitch is 35 
to 36 inches, about 5 in more than main cabin seats and   the extra bit of space is quite welcomed on these Long Haul flights. With the table extended you can   really get a sense of the extra space. To compare you can see how the table meets the armrest in the   regular main cabin seats over there overall. I was 
pleased with this seat more than the emergency exit   row and I thought the extra space was worth the 
added cost for Main Cabin Extra on these Long Haul flight. Wi-Fi is offered on the Dreamliners and is 
available for purchase at $23, about $30 Canadian   for the full flight it's in line with what I've 
seen on other airlines. With the AA app you can   also stream videos to your device which is useful if you have your own Bluetooth headphones. The app   is pretty extensive and worth downloading for 
your trip. It even has a track your bag feature   which provides peace of mind especially if 
you have connections. And as always I take a   moment to welcome new viewers to subscribe 
for continued travel and aviation related content:) About an hour after takeoff the dinner 
service commenced. The service started with a warm   oshibori... nice touch! The options were pork 
and rice or a shrimp pasta and I went with   the pork and rice which was a solid call. It came 
with a salad, a spinach side, and a lemon cake and   bonus points for providing a warm bun!
Everything was delicious and it was no chore   finishing every last bite. To accompany the meal 
I enjoyed a Goose Island IPA so cheers to another flight! ooo fresh! The IFE system on American is 
smooth and easy to operate. They have a   very extensive library in which to choose 
something to watch. One difference compared   to domestic flights is that there is no live 
TV available even when the plane is over the   US. Also one thing I think missing from the I 
system is a menu tab for the onboard service   many other airlines have this feature and 
I think it greatly benefits the guest!  And here's a look inside the lavatory closest to 
my seat considering there are no laboratories in   the rear the plane they were kept quite clean 
throughout the flight despite being heavily used. Don't let the darkness fool you it's early 
afternoon outside and plenty bright perfect time   for breakfast which was served with the last hour to go. The options were French toast toast or udon.   The hot meal was accompanied by some fresh fruit I wasn't particularly fond of the French toast   I thought it was on the dry side and no amount 
of syrup was going to save it but I did manage   to have a coffee with my breakfast ...or lunch ...or whatever you want to call this early afternoon meal. Overall this was a pleasant way to cross 
the Pacific the staff were kind and friendly   there was good entertainment and an abundance of food, snacks, and drinks. The flight was one   of five on a roundtrip ticket from Tokyo to 
Toronto and the price came out to C$1,368 which   includes the C$230 upgrade to main cabin extra. I thought the added of cost of main cabin extra was   worth it considering it was spread out over five 
flights. We also offset 613 tons (kg) of carbon for this flight. Landing in Dallas the passport control 
was much faster and better organized than when   I flew through Chicago a year ago. There's a 
dedicated line for US and Canadian [and PR] passport   holders which sped things up a bit. The ITI 
sticker on my passport did its job and my   bag was checked onto my next flight without 
me having to collect it at the carousel. So   as a Canadian would I fly them again well it 
depends! There is added time to your trip when   transferring through the states and another set 
of passport control but the flight was about 400   bucks cheaper compared to Air Canada. American is the largest airline in the world and they   simply have the size to provide a competitive 
price and times so if the price is right I'd   fly them again though I'd Try to snag a codeshare
flight with JAL through the American   website like I did last year. Anyways thanks 
for watching let me know what you thought   about the American Airlines transpacific 
product and I'll catch you in the next episode :)

It was just like the flight um before the flight I had 2 years ago on Oman or the same pattern, the same stuff where I really questioned myself, don't they like train their crew? Um don't they spend any money on their training? And if they're not capable to serve passengers on a 6-hour flight because they even like abboarded the uh coffee and um tea service because they weren't simply capable to do that. And then I asked myself if they can't even serve passengers, which is their their duty they do every time, are they actually able to evacuate an airplane within 90 seconds in case something really happens? Are they up to their job? It's like is there are there any like safety flaws we need to know? It's like all those kind of questions where I think like this is a professional airline and their stuff is acting like that's their first day at the job, you know? I don't think that applies to everyone in the morning air, but I didn't see effort. I didn't see like the energy like they couldn't just simply be be bothered. So yeah, overall it was just a really disappointing experience and considering that I paid money for this, I felt ripped off throughout the flight. You could see the bells ringing all the time and the cabin managers spent most of the flight in economy cars trying to pade and look after very angry passengers. Oh my god. So the guy next to me, he's like so angry. So he just got up to talk to crew. He wasn't very impressed either. Literally the cabin manager is here in economy class trying to pade people and uh trying to fix the situation because half of the people are rather unimpressed and a bit angry because of the situation. As you can see, she just walked past here. She has a lot of fixing to do. But I guess what describes the airline the best is the fact that I sent an email. I told them how my experience was. my screen wasn't working, the food was a joke, um the upgrade experience was a bit of a scam. They never replied, you know, I think that stands testament for the philosophy of the management or they what they think or how much respect they have for their customer, their paying customers because they have none. So I personally think that we work really hard for our money and if we spend money on a flight ticket, we expect uh certain standards and especially airlines are very eager to advertise how beautiful their cabins are, how great the inflight entertainment is or their dining uh experience on board and they should deliver. You know, flying is not just taking you from A to B safely. Of course, it's part of it, but that's not what we pay for. We pay for the bigger experience. And this is where Oman airline totally failed. And in a time right now during Corona where airlines are begging us so hard and saying we are in this together to not insist on a refund because they need the cash flow and please keep the credit and take a flight later this year. I think this is when uh we actually or I have to send out this message and make this video and hope that Oman Air now when they really start flying that they overthink their uh relation they have with their customers and whether they want to keep on going and fooling people around and offering such nonsense and not even reply to customers inquiries. And I think hope that this video helps them to readjust and uh maybe perhaps have a little more respect for people who work very hard for their money and purchase a ticket with your airline. And yeah, interestingly, the saga continues. A few months ago, I purchased a pretty cool business class deal uh from Zurich to Oakuckland on Oman Air. So I thought like okay give them another chance next year try their premium product because a lot of people say actually their business class is not too bad. And interestingly I got an up I got an email this week by a guy called Joseph who is uh like uh works for Omania and said they mistakenly posted the wrong fair and they need to downgrade me to economy class which is like oh it's all repeating itself. the same pattern over and over again like taking me for a ride once more. I think that's really uh strange and I don't know what's happening within this airline. Um but yeah, weird things keep on happening with uh Oman Air. Well guys, this is it for today's video. I hope you enjoyed um me sharing my experience on Omani and I really hope it helps to improve our flight experience um and the airline takes the the feedback seriously and improves the way they handle things. Um let me know in the comment section below what you think uh of Oman and my flight in particular. If you want to see more videos, feel free to subscribe, leave a like uh and let me know what you think. Guys, where are you after? If you're after during these times, stay safe. Otherwise, uh I hope you get to fly very soon. Thanks for watching. [Music]

yt_comments.author: @marekadboy
yt_comments.text: To any cabin crew reading this, if a passengers request you to fix their in-flight entertainment system and you can’t fix it for whatever reason then GO BACK to the passenger and explain the situation rather than waiting for them to ask you or your colleagues over and over again. It’s just a common courtesy and not a hard thing to do!! Passenger may not be happy but you have done what you can and they’ll appreciate it. Simples!!!! I had this several times hence why I am posting it here.

yt_comments.author: @JohnF677
yt_comments.text: I flew Omam Air earlier this year and it was absolutely useless. My IFE did not work for the entire of my first flight. They turned the IFE of over 30 minutes before landing on the second flight. On both flights the service was very slow with disinterested crew. After my experience and watching your video I will definitely be avoiding Oman Air in the future.

yt_comments.author: @Shashwatibose
