reviews.transcript_full:
Hi there and welcome to a bit of a gloomy day 
in Taipei. This was actually filmed the day   before my Starlux flight. I was hungry and as one 
does in Taipei when you’re hungry during the day,   you goto 7-Eleven. Of course at 
night, you would goto a night market.  I could say that I’m here because my flight 
to Saigon is Starlux 711, which is true,   but that’s not trueeee. Why I really came 
to this side of town, is because of this.  How often do you get to see an airline and 
a convenience store collaboration? I sure as   hell never have. Now, you’ll forgive me, filming 
inside 7-Eleven’s is not quite my forte, but I did   think visiting this 7-Eleven would be a good way 
to really show you how ingrained the three major   airlines are in daily life in Taiwan. I’m going 
to buy my very cool seat belt key chain and then-  Ah here we are, it’s tomorrow. I 
suppose gloomy is going to be a theme.  Taipei has two airports, the much smaller 
Shongshan airport in the city center which   serves some regional and domestic flights and 
then the much larger Taoyuan airport to the   southwest of the city. Taoyuan is the primary hub 
for Starlux along with China Airlines and EVA Air.   Quite the trio of airlines, literally three of the 
best in the world, just casually chilling here in   Taipei. I guess that tips my hat on this review.
So, before we head inside and get checked in with   Spiderman, let me introduce myself to those of you 
that are new to the channel. My name is Kevin and   I am the Flip Flop Traveller. I’m here to give you 
two honest videos each week about unique flights,   hotels and trains. This flight today was 
self funded, the price I paid is in the   description and Starlux has no idea who I am. 
So without further ado, let’s get into episode   316 and see what Starlux is really all about.
Here we are at Terminal 1. The airport has a   bit of a unique setup in that terminal one is over 
here on the right side and everything on the left   is terminal two, but they are all connected 
in what is in theory a continuous loop. Plus,   there’s a new terminal three being built as well- 
the concourses of which should be open by mid next   year with the full terminal opening in 2027.
Today is a pretty easy day here but I’ve seen   this place packed before, so they certainly need 
the breathing room with Starlux now added to the   mix. Last year Taoyuan saw around 35 million 
passengers, putting it in the same league as   the like of Tokyo Narita and Hanoi Noi Bai.
Here in terminal 1, Starlux has a single row   of check in desks- and there’s spiderman. 
They seem to be very much into the branding   collaborations. On their LAX flights, 
they even have LA Clippers branding.  I should mention that Starlux has a 
split operation now between the two   terminals and since my flight, Saigon and 
Da Nang’s flights have moved to Terminal 2,   while Hanoi and Phu Quoc stays here.
Let’s get through security and immigration   and head to the lounge, on the way, I can tell you 
about the level 9 drama that morphed into Starlux.  The current CEO of Starlux- Chang Kuo-Wei- used to 
work at EVA Airlines. He was a mechanic and then a   pilot and eventually made his way to be chairman, 
since you know, his father was the founder of   Evergreen Group. Chang became chairman of EVA in 
2013. Three years later, his father died and named   Chang as his successor as Chairman of Evergreen 
Group. This is when things got spicy. Problem was,   Chang was the youngest of his father’s sons, from 
his second marriage to boot. There was more a less   a coup that ensued at Evergreen and Chang was 
booted from the company. Within a few months,   he had the idea to create Starlux.
The name Starlux comes from the Chinese   character for Star, in honor of his father 
who navigated via the stars before GPS and   the Character for Universe, framing Chang’s 
own ambitions. In English, it became Starlux.  Let me pause that for a moment as we take a look 
at the lounge here in Terminal 1. It is small and   this is probably the weakest link of the entire 
Starlux network. That said, all of the longer   or more premium routes are now operating 
from Terminal 2 which has a larger lounge.  There was a small buffet selection on offer 
as well as a few a la cart items, from which   I chose the scallion bun and soy milk which was 
actually quite a stand out, all things considered.  I also loved the attention to small 
details- such as the ice on offer.  The only other big negative for this lounge 
is that the restrooms are a solid 100 meters   down the corridor outside of the lounge.
I know this isn’t ideal, but if the lounge   is ever too crowded, there’s a public lounge of 
sorts named the Airport Experience Zone which   looked surprisingly calm and comfortable.
I can never leave this airport   without mango tarts in hand.
So, obviously, Starlux is competing with China   Airlines, but much more so, with EVA. Their first 
flights were in late 2020, delayed due to COVID,   with the first three destinations being Da Nang, 
Penang and Macau. They’ve quickly expanded to   their current 26 destinations with 2 more on the 
way by the end of the year, with an impressive   operation to Japan and a stated goal of being a 
major player connecting southeast asia to the US.  One unique thing is that on their A350s,   which they have five of at the moment to fly to 
the US, they actually have a true first class,   something you won’t find at their competitors, 
as Starlux says they, “promise to commit to   luxury that Taiwan’s dominant carriers have 
lost sight of in recent years.” Still ironic,   they're talking about two great airlines. Also 
kinda cool that Chang flew the first A350 from   Toulous himself for the delivery flight.
They currently have 23 aircraft on   hand with 30 on order.
I got to the gate on time   but our aircraft didn’t. While the signs were 
updated in time, I was surprised there were   no announcements for the flight’s delay.
Here’s our 2 year old bird pulling in now.  Around 30 minutes behind schedule, boarding 
began with Business Class passengers- they’re   not part of any alliance yet, so it was a very 
small group one. That said, there’s quite a bit   of speculation that Starlux may end up joining 
Oneworld alliance- especially since there’s also   speculation that Cathay may leave it. Then Taipei 
would be one of the only cities on earth serving   as a hub for all three alliances.
Ok, as we head down the jetbridge,   let’s take a look at today’s flight stats.
I stepped on board and there is one thing   that is like the finest crystal clear as soon 
as you step on board. This is an airline that   is here to impress- and I mean that both 
for the hard product and soft product.  The staff were enthusiastic, thoughtful and 
knowledgeable and that cabin was gorgeous.   The business class on these A321neos has just 
8 lie flat seats in a 2 x 2 configuration.  As I’ve said before, I’ve always liked 
these seats since in the seated position,   I think they’re pretty comfortable, even 
if they’re a bit narrow when lie flat.  But it’s all of the finishing details 
that make the difference here though.  From the leather trim, to the contrast stitching, 
and even things like the quality of the seatbelt-   it’s a very well designed product.
There’s a fully adjustable headrest   as well as a storage space over your 
shoulder with a universal outlet.  So we all know what happens if you click 
like on this video and subscribe to the   channel, but do you know what happens if you 
don’t? You may never see me again. So if you enjoy   this style of content, be sure to click all of 
the buttons. If you’re interested in a peak of the   inner workings of the channel or just need some 
travel advice- be sure to check out my Patreon.   Whatever you do, thanks for being here right now.  I was served a hot towel along with a 
really good cold pressed pineapple and   guava juice. I love creative- but not too 
creative- signature pre departure drinks.  Across, there’s a nice high resolution in 
flight monitor along with a good side foot   rest. The storage space under the foot rest 
is limited though. Also keep in mind the foot   rests for the bulkheads in this type of seat 
are around double the size of the other rows.  We pushed back and a very- shall 
we say different- safety video   began to play. Perhaps, not to Emirates taste.  We had an excruciatingly long taxi and wait in 
line for take off- at one point we were next in   line and it honestly felt like they just forgot 
about us. 72 minutes from push back to take off.  But it’s coming up now, 
along with the airport stats.  So before the meal begins, let’s take a look 
at the comforts and amenities on offer today.  The pillow is a decent size and 
quality- and freshly laundered.  Then there’s a fantastic blanket. At 
first glance it may look like a towel,   but it’s actually a super soft and fluffy blanket 
which thankfully doesn’t leave lint everywhere.  As for the headphones, they were noise canceling 
and quite good actually, but I think I actually   like the case even more than the headphones.
The tray table could be used fully   extended or folded in half.
Ok, let’s get into this really good   meal service. First, we will start off with an 
insanely comprehensive menu for a 3 hour flight.  Note that the prices in red are my addition 
to the graphic just to give you an idea of   the current retail price for each bottle.
As I said before, I love drinking wine   but my knowledge is limited, so I always 
appreciate wine lists that go into detail   about region, pairings and tasting notes.
Of course, I chose the Contemporary Asian   and Longtail Menu for my meal which 
honestly, even if I didn’t like it,   I would have loved it- and I’ll tell you why.
It’s clear, even for a single tray service,   they are trying to elevate the 
experience from the ground up.  For our meal today, we start with a Pineapple 
Pura Longtail and sparkling water. The starter is   Milkfish toast, Avocado, Daikon and Dill. Reading 
that, I had precisely zero idea what to expect,   but I think this is quite clever. 
It’s so elevated for in flight food,   but not at all fussy or difficult to serve.
For the main, we had USDA ANgus Beef Tenderloin,   Pineapple Rice, peanut and pickled kohlrabi.
So, when it comes to beef, let me tell you   how I know when a dish is really good. 
When I start taking little tiny bites.   I think I cut each of those slices into 2 or 
3 pieces. The pineapple rice was great too.  In East Asia, we are spoiled with the food 
offerings in business class on these regional   routes, but it’s worth pointing out that Starlux 
is the only airline in the region right now that   doesn’t follow the same exact format for 
meals. Small salad or cold meat appetizer,   plus hot preplated main and dessert. 
Cathay, ANA, JAL, EVA, China Airlines,   Korean Air, Asiana- it’s all the same 
format- and it’s generally all good,   but this is just another level. I’d be 
really curious to try Starlux’s catering   on long haul services- more on that in a bit.
Earlier I’d asked for a glass of the Reisling,   but the crew insisted that I allow them to chill 
it for a bit more time since it wasn’t properly   prepared- attention that I appreciated- so that 
came along with my dessert which was a Chocolate   Magao cake along with seasonal fresh fruit.
Entertainment on board- it’s just okay. I   have little doubt that it’ll improve 
overtime, but at the time there were   just around 150 movies on offer- along with 
a handful of TV shows with random episodes.  Loved the detailed map and in 
flight magazine though. There   was also in flight wifi which 
was free for Business Class.  And here we have the seat in full 
flat mode- definitely not needed on   this short day flight, but nice to have for sure.
So, how I ended up on this short Starlux flight.   Last year, Starlux announced a partnership with 
Alaska Airlines and then Alaska announced they’d   be selling Starlux tickets for points. Alaska 
communicated that there would be promotional   fares available for the first few months. The 
aviation world collectively freaked out and   everyone started trying to book. At that time, I 
had 43000 Alaska points. The had a promo to buy   more points and so I topped that up to 60000 
miles which would be enough for the Taipei   to LAX flight. I knew the points would take 2 
days to appear in my account, but it was fine,   Alaska advertised these fares would be 
available I believe from April until August.  Well wouldn’t you know they forgot to mention that 
each flight only had four seats available at that   price. By the time I went to book, everything 
was more than double the price. So in the end,   with my 60k alaska points, I got this 
flight, plus a longhaul LATAM flight,   decided to dump Alaska all together before 
they continued to devalue their program.  So yeah, I wanted a long 
haul flight- and I still do,   perhaps now even more so- and will 
keep my eyes open for them. That said,   this was a really nice first taste of what will 
clearly be a new major player in the market. Oh,   did I mention they even already began 
turning a profit last year? Yeah.  Ok, I’ll let you enjoy the rest of the approach 
into Saigon. The airport stats are coming up.  And so, that is that. We were late, the 
airport was mobbed but I was still on   cloud 9 so I didn’t even care. Starlux, 
I will be back- if you join Oneworld,   or any alliance frankly, I’ll be back often.
So I really hope you enjoyed this trip report   today. If you did, be sure to click the like 
button and subscribe with notifications on so   you don’t miss out on my twice weekly videos. 
I’ll see you next time from a surprise out of   order flight on an airline that needs to do a 
hell of a lot better protecting their passanger’s   data. You don’t want to miss that one. Oh and 
as always, thanks for watching until the end.

yt_comments.text: I took Oman Air from Kuwait to Muscat and onwards onto Frankfurt. On the KWI-MCT leg, the service was really fast because of the short duration of the flight. The b737 IFE and seats on this part was modern and amazing. But, I noticed the crew of the Frankfurt flight being very slow. The a330 on this route had old, unresponsive IFE and it felt really hot and uncomfortable. I believe the quality of a flight in Oman air depends on the route you take.

reviews.transcript_full:
Hello everyone, I’m Edin~ Today, I’m taking you from Taipei to Singapore~ This time, I’m flying on Starlux A330-900 in economy class I’m seated in 32K, near the No. 2 engine~ Engine View (Aviation enthusiasts’ favourite!!) A blanket and pillow are already prepared at the seat. The headrest has multi-angle adjustments. There’s a TV in front, with space below for small items. Under the TV, there’s a USB port and headphone jack. Meal tray~ Legroom when sitting upright (I’m 177cm tall)~ Underneath, there are headphones and a stack of documents (the black bag on the right is mine). In the middle, there’s a shared Type-C/international charging port with the adjacent seat. In-flight magazine, Wi-Fi access card, safety card, and airsickness bag. The in-flight entertainment system offers a variety of movies, TV shows, music, and games from different countries. There’s a decent selection, and most are fairly recent. You can also check the menu on the screen. There were two meal options that day (I chose beef pasta). Meals can be pre-selected online. Starlux offers signature drinks in collaboration with local bars (not available on the short Taipei-Hong Kong route).
This flight offered the Sci-Fi Cosmos signature drink. Of course, standard drinks are also available~ Now for the aviation enthusiast’s favorite section – the flight map!! It can be viewed from multiple angles! For convenience, you can connect wireless Bluetooth headphones to the TV. It’s meal time! This time, it’s beef in tomato sauce with long pasta~ Overall, I found the taste to be very high quality.
The beef had a great balance of fat and lean meat, with excellent texture! If I had to nitpick, I’d wish they offered ice cream. Sci-Fi Cosmos drink paired with a movie! Drinks in blue plus blue skies and white clouds outside ^^ Snapping a photo for the memories~ All Starlux flights offer free Wi-Fi for text messaging.
Just connect to the plane’s Wi-Fi, enter your email, and agree to the terms. Lavatory Visit There’s a green plant~ Moisturizing spray/lotion. Overall, it’s clean and tidy! About an hour before landing, they offered snacks and drinks (peach juice). In summary, I found this flight experience very comfortable and enjoyable. The hardware was nearly flawless.The only minor issue is that the window could be cleaner... On the software side, the meal exceeded expectations in taste.
The cabin crew worked very efficient too. The entire journey was very smooth, and I hope to try other international routes in the future~ Have you ever flown with Starlux Airlines?
What’s your opinion of them? Let me know in the comments! Thanks for watching, see you in the next video, bye bye!

reviews.transcript_full:
Today, we’re flying Singapore Airlines Business Class
aboard an Airbus A350 from Brussels to Singapore The video features the complete Singapore Airlines Business 
Class experience (cabin, seat, meals, amenities, entertainment)  The video also features the spectacular landing 
in a thunderstorm at Singapore Changi Airport Welcome to Brussels Airport in Belgium
for today’s Business Class flight on Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines has dedicated Business Class 
check-in counters at Brussels Airport Long lines snake through security and passport control Before the flight, it’s time to relax in 'The View' Lounge The lounge is located in Pier B,
just past security and passport control Seating areas are arranged for both comfort and privacy There are plenty of charging points and
work tables for business travelers The lounge's decor is simple yet stylish, 
with warm wood tones and soft lighting The natural light and design make it a pleasant place to wait A self-serve bar includes wine, beer, and a range of soft drinks The lounge's large windows overlook the tarmac A buffet area offers a selection
of snacks, salads, and hot dishes During the morning, you’ll find pastries, fruit, and yogurt Later in the day, sandwiches, soup, & Belgian waffles are served Showers are available for passengers
who want to freshen up before a long flight It’s time to head to the gate for boarding This is the Singapore Airlines A350 that will fly us to Singapore The aircraft has registration number 9V-SMO (built in 2017) Singapore Airlines has 65 Airbus A350s
(the world's largest fleet of 350s) Singapore Airlines operates several versions of the A350,
including the A350-900ULR ('ultra-long-range' model) Singapore Airlines was the A350-900ULR's launch customer
and remains the only airline to operate it Singapore Airlines’ A350-900ULR operates the world’s longest
scheduled commercial nonstop route (Singapore to New York) The A350 is one of the quietest jets in the sky The A350’s sleek carbon-fiber design also makes 
it lighter and more fuel-efficient The A350’s wings are elegantly curved
and flexible, improving aerodynamics It’s time to board the aircraft Singapore Airlines’ A350 features 42 Business Class seats The seats are spread over two cabins
and arranged in a 1-2-1 layout A larger cabin in the front of the plane
holds the bulk of the Business Class seats (26 in total) The remaining 16 seats are located in a smaller
and more intimate Business Class cabin over the wings The cabin design was created by James Parker Associated,
the company that also created the interiors of the Orient Express  Center seats include a partition screen
that can be raised for extra privacy All seats along the windows are single seats Singapore Airlines' Business Class seat 
is one of the widest seats in the sky Seat pitch is 153 cm (60 inches), and width is 71 cm (28 inches) The crew welcomes passengers with a drink and hot towel The pilot welcomes the passengers Singapore Airlines’ hospitality is
world-renowned, and it’s easy to see why Once boarding is complete, the safety video is shown It’s a beautifully produced film (not just a safety briefing) The video blends essential safety instructions
with Singapore’s cultural landmarks The famous Singapore Girl gracefully
guides passengers through each instruction Her presence symbolizes the airline’s
heritage of service and professionalism We’re leaving the gate (on time departure at 12 pm) Brussels Airport has three runways:
one north-south and two parallel east-west runways Singapore Airlines’ A350s are powered by
Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines Have you ever flown with Singapore Airlines?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Let’s explore Singapore Airlines’ A350 Business Class seat A reading light sits at eye level for easy use during night flights Seat adjustments are made through
a control panel in the armrest by the aisle In front of the seat is a large 18-inch HD screen A small compartment with vanity mirror sits beside the screen The entertainment screen can be tilted The seat features a large ottoman (foot rest) A console next to the seat holds another reading light,
the power outlets and some storage space Next to the console sits the handheld remote
for the inflight entertainment system A storage box in the armrest is perfect
for a bottle of water or small personal items The tray table is stored in the armrest
and can be adjusted in height and position The bulkhead seats in rows 11 & 19 feature full-width ottomans In the other seats, the footwell is tucked
diagonally into the side of the seat ahead When the seat converts into a bed,
your legs extend into this angled cubby In Singapore Airlines' Business Class, amenity kits 
are available upon request rather than automatically provided The amenity kit is designed in collaboration with
Le Labo, the boutique fragrance house from New York The kit holds a selection of
Le Labo Bergamote 22 skincare essentials Singapore Airlines sometimes gives Business Class 
passengers a collectible plush bear as a keepsake Slippers, socks and eye-masks are offered A large pillow and soft duvet are provided Noise-cancelling headphones are provided,
ensuring an immersive experience Flying through high clouds shows just how fast we’re moving Let’s explore the inflight menu Singapore Airlines partners with world-class chefs
to create its Business and First Class menus The airline’s “Book the Cook” service lets passengers
pre-select main courses before departure Canape : Singapore chicken satay,
with onion, cucumber, and spicy peanut sauce Cocktail: Singapore Sling Appetizer: Vitello Tonnato (thinly sliced veal), with creamy
tuna sauce, capers, tomato, caviars and snow pea tendril Main course: classic beef stew in beer sauce,
Brussels sprouts, carrots, shallot and roasted grenaille potatoes Dessert: Oreo ice cream, raspberry bavarois
and a selection of cheese and sliced fresh fruits Singapore Airlines' Airbus A350 features 
three lavatories for Business Class passengers Payot hand lotion and facial mist
are available in the lavatories during the flight We can enjoy some beautiful views along the way The IFE system is controlled using a handheld remote Called KrisWorld, Singapore Airlines' IFE system includes
hundreds of movies, TV shows, and curated playlists Singapore Airlines offers its Business Class passengers
complimentary onboard Wi-Fi during the entire flight The flight can be tracked
in real-time using an interactive 3D map The sun sets as we fly over Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan A light bite is served mid-flight: vegetarian rice noodles,
with lettuce, black mushrooms, and Chinese greens Snacks are also available in the galley throughout the flight It’s time for some rest:
the cabin crew assists in setting up the bed When fully flat, the bed measures 198 cm or 78 inches in length I am lucky during this flight: one seat can be used for sitting,
while the other is fully converted into my bed The full-width ottoman of the bulkhead seat allows
for a natural sleeping position and unrestricted legroom A few hours later: we're crossing the Bay of Bengal As dawn approaches, the cabin lighting
gradually brightens to mimic sunrise Breakfast starts with a selection of sliced fresh fruits,
Bircher muesli, flavored yoghurt, and assorted bread rolls Main breakfast course: Dutch mini fluffy pancakes
with pineapple compote, strawberry and butter We're encountering some moderate turbulence near Phuket Turbulence can feel unsettling, 
but the plane is designed to handle it safely How do you feel about turbulence — calm or anxious? I’m a nervous flyer, but it helps  
to be on a reputable airline like Singapore Airlines A crew member, curious about my blog, shared 
this lovely note before we landed We’re approaching the Singapore Airlines airspace Unfortunately, thunderstorms are building up
over Singapore, so we have to circle before landing The sky over Singapore is stormy as we approach the airport Thunder rumbles in the distance,
and lightning flashes across the clouds Singapore Airlines is one of the world’s most awarded airlines Singapore Airlines' story began in 1947
when Malayan Airways operated its very first flight The airline was founded with a twin-engined Airspeed Consul In 1966, it became Malaysia-Singapore Airlines, known as MSA When MSA split in 1972, two national carriers were born:
Malaysia Airlines and Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines quickly established
itself as a global carrier with high standards The airline built a reputation for reliability and premium comfort Singapore Airlines has often led the way in aviation innovation It was the first airline to offer free headsets,
choice of meals, and drinks in Economy Class In 2007, Singapore Airlines was the launch customer
for the Airbus A380, the world’s largest passenger aircraft The carrier is part of the Star Alliance network,
connecting passengers to over 1,000 destinations The company’s commitment to quality extends
beyond its cabins — to training, safety, and sustainability The Singapore Airlines brand stands for
precision, warmth, and world-class service Would you be scared to land in a thunderstorm? Despite the storm, the aircraft touches
down smoothly on the wet runway Thank you for watching this
Singapore Airlines A350 Business Class flight

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard Business Class in Finnair's Airbus A350 Finnair offers one of the world's best Business Class seats This video documents the full Finnair Business Class experience  This includes Business Class meals, amenities, IFE & flat bed Welcome to Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, Finland's main airport Last year, 17 million passengers passed through Helsinki Airport The airport offers relaxing virtual tours of Finnish forests The airport is the main hub for Finnair, the flag carrier of Finland Finnair's Lounge in the non-Schengen side is located at Gate 52 At the entrance is a small display of retro Finnair uniforms The lounge design is characterized by Nordic aesthetics Seating options include sofas, armchairs, and workstations The Finnair lounge is divided into two main sections A quieter zone is located near the entrance A larger space is found toward the back A buffet offers hot and cold dishes Next to the buffet station is a dining area A lounge area behind the buffet is centered around a circular bar The lounge is open to Finnair Business Class passengers Oneworld elite members can also access the lounge Finnair Plus Gold, Platinum and Platinum Lumo members can also access the lounge Private shower suites are available at the lounge This is the Finnair Airbus A350 that will fly us to Hong Kong Aircraft registration number: OH-LWA (built in 2015) Finnair has 18 A350s in its fleet, with an average age of 8 years The A350 forms the backbone of Finnair’s long-haul operations Finnair's fleet consists mainly of Airbus aircraft Finnair also operates 6 Airbus A330 aircraft on long-haul routes Finnair's short-haul fleet comprises A320s, Embraers & ATRs  I am the first passenger to board tonight's flight Business Class in Finnair's A350 features a 1-2-1 seat layout All Business Class seats offer direct aisle access The cabin's calm design reflects Scandinavian aesthetics The window seats are best suited for solo passengers The paired center seats are perfect for travel companions The 43 Business Class seats are spread across two cabins A smaller mini-cabin contains just 13 Business Class seats A larger forward Business Class cabin holds 30 seats 8A is my seat for the 12 hour flight to Hong Kong Finnair’s unique Business Class seat is called 'AirLounge seat' A welcome drink is served in the iconic Ultima Thule glass I'll take a detailed tour of Finnair's AirLounge seat after takeoff We're leaving the gate (local time: 5 am) Finnair's A350s are equipped with several cameras Finnair's safety video is played as we taxi to the runway The tail camera offers a great view during the takeoff roll The A350 is powered by Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-84 engines Have you ever flown with Finnair? Leave a comment Finnair is one of the world’s oldest and safest airlines The carrier was founded in 1923 in Finland Today, Finnair serves over 80 destinations worldwide Finnair's slogan is “The Nordic Way” Let's have a look at Finnair's AirLounge Business Class  seat An 18-inch TV and large ottoman are located in front of the seat The AirLounge seat features multiple storage spaces The wide side table offers wireless phone charging A tray table deploys at the push of a button The seat's side holds a reading light and a storage compartment Finnair's amenity kit comes in a stylish Marimekko pouch The kit includes earplugs, an eye mask, tootbrush & toothpaste Extra items are available on request, including lip balm & lotion Each Business Class seat includes two plush cushions A warm duvet - matching the pillow design - is also provided A mattress pad adds extra sleeping comfort Slippers are offered for convenience Noise-cancelling headphones are provided Let's have a look at the menu on today's flight A light supper is served after take off (starting with a hot towel) Main course: lemon and basil ravioli with red pesto and pine nuts Cold plates: green salad with quinoa and coleslaw + fresh fruits  Dessert: chocolate brownie with vanilla crème and blueberries A nice feature of Finnair’s A350 is the Business Class galley The galley is set up as a self-service area for snacks and drinks The Finnair A350 Business Class cabin features three lavatories The lavatories are stocked with eco-friendly SEES products Finnair’s AirLounge Business Class seat does not recline The seat converts into a flat bed by raising the legrest  The AirLounge seat feels more like a sofa than a seat You can sit cross-legged, lounge sideways, or sleep comfortably  It’s one of the most comfortable Business Class seats in the sky  Finnair's inflight entertainment is intuitive and user-friendly A wide range of movies, shows, music, and games are available The touchscreen is fast and responsive Navigation of the inflight entertainment is smooth and easy Wi-Fi onboard the A350 is accessed via the Nordic Sky portal Business Class passengers get one hour of free Wi-Fi The menus can be accessed through the IFE system Onboard amenities can be ordered through the IFE system An interactive map allows to track the flight in real time  Finnair’s inflight entertainment also includes a kids’ section The plane cameras are the highlight of the IFE system There’s a tail camera and a belly camera The sun rises as we fly over the Black Sea The flight detours around Russian and Ukrainian airspace My heart goes out to everyone affected by wars worldwide Mid-flight snacks are offered by Finnair's lovely cabin crew The flight path takes us over Xinjiang's vast Taklimakan Desert The Taklamakan Desert is China's largest desert  It is also the second-largest mobile desert in the world The Taklamakan Desert has dunes up to 300 m or 1000 ft high The desert is often called the “Sea of Death" Crossing the Taklamakan Desert was once very dangerous Traders on the Silk Road skirted the harsh interior of the desert The desert is one of the most remote places on Earth  The sun sets as we leave the Taklamakan Desert behind A three-course brunch is served two hours prior to landing A hot towel is provided prior to the brunch Main course: vegetable frittata with roasted chicken Cold plates: gluten-free blackcurrant oats and vitello tonnato Dessert: fresh fruits The co-pilot announces our approach to Hong Kong Airport. We fly over Macau as we prepare to land in Hong Kong Macau is famous for its casinos and nightlife Macau is often called the “Las Vegas of Asia” Macau was a Portuguese colony from 1557 to 1999  We're landing at Hong Kong Airport (local time: 10 pm) Thank you for watching my video about Finnair's Business Class

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Welcome back. In this video, we're stepping on board Delta Airlines in business class aboard an Airbus A330 flying from Madrid, Spain to Atlanta, Georgia in the USA. Is this old and dated Delta 1 cabin worth the hefty price tag? Stay tuned to find out why Delta's recent retrofit of this aircraft missed the mark. We'll also tell you what you need to look for if you're looking to book Delta's business class product in order to make sure you know what you're booking before you board. So, join us as we explore the seat, service, and experience on board this 9 and 1/2 hour daytime flight. And stick around to learn about Delta's plans for these aircraft. Welcome to Travel at Random. We're Trevor and Ryan. This channel started out of a love of travel. We're here to share unbiased and self-funded trip reports, hotel and flight reviews, and travel advice. We hope we inspire your next getaway. Check out our playlist in the description and browse the channel. If you enjoy this video, please hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Thank you for watching. Now, let's head to the airport. [Applause] [Music] Welcome to Madrid, the capital of Spain. We are just wrapping up a week of exploring several historic Spanish cities. Check out our playlist at the end of the video to see more from our trip. We'll have new videos in this series over the next few months, so make sure you subscribe to stay uptodate. Today we're flying Delta out of Adulo Suarez Madrid Barahas International Airport, Barahas or MAD for short. Last year over 66 million passengers made their way through this airport, making it one of the busiest in Europe. MAD is located about 7 mi or 11 km from the city center, about 15 minutes by train or 30 minutes by car or taxi. The airport is connected to Madrid's public transit. Metro line 8 has stops at all four terminals and the commuter train system has a train station at terminal 4. There are five terminals in total. Terminals 1, 2, and three are older and are connected. Terminal 4 and 4S are newer and about 5 km from the other terminals. You can take a shuttle to move between 4, 4S, and the older terminals. Delta operates out of terminal 1 along with most of the other major international carriers. Except for one world alliance members like Iberia and American Airlines which are out of terminal 4. We're traveling in Delta 1 today. So there's a dedicated baggage drop and check-in line just for business class passengers. If you're flying Delta, enter through door 1 at terminal 1 and head to the right. Just look for the Delta 1 sign. Check-in was rather quick and we were off to security and passport control. There is fasttrack security at this airport and it was included with the Delta 1 ticket. The passport control line was pretty quick at this time of the morning and we were through in a few minutes. As part of your Delta 1 ticket, you also have access to the Seless VIP lounge which is located near gate B29 up the escalators just past the duty-free shop. This is also a priority pass lounge and is the only lounge in terminal 1. There are no Delta or Sky Team specific lounges in this airport. The Seless Lounge is large and there was plenty of seating available the morning of our flight. Most seats are set up at tables. This club also features a large outdoor terrace that wraps around the building, offering 180° views of the runway, remote stands, and gates. [Music] There are a lot of seating options out here, including some elevated sections with sofas. In the center was the main food and drink buffet. For breakfast, it had pastries, fruits, cold cuts, and salad items available. [Music] On the back wall are pairs of grabandgo refrigerators with items like packaged sandwiches, fruit cups, and bottled drinks. [Music] In the middle are two self-service espresso style drink machines. On the far side of the lounge is a large bar with wine, cocktails, soda, and beer on offer, even at 8:00 a.m. The club had showers available, which you can request. Since we were leaving first thing in the morning and we came from our hotel, we skipped the showers. The lounge also has pretty nice and clean bathrooms. Near the entrance, there's a quiet room with some tables where you can get some work done. Reviews online of this lounge are mixed with some reporting long entry lines and picked over food offerings. As far as lines go, there's always a customer arguing about access at any club we go to these days. But there were multiple agents working it, so it was less than five minutes. The food on offer looked fine, but was pretty basic for breakfast with the only hot option being a toaster for the bread. Overall, the lounge was a nice space to spend a little bit of time and grab a drink. The terrace was unexpected, and we always appreciate being able to get some fresh air while traveling. Otherwise, it's a pretty standard international priority pass lounge. Our daytime flight today takes us 9 and a half hours from MAD to ATL, about 4,300 miles. Delta flies this route once daily. Boarding started on time and was orderly. There were clearly marked cues for each zone. After scanning our boarding passes, we were surprised to be heading down some stairs. [Music] We then found out that we were on a remote stand this morning. This caused the actual boarding to be a bit chaotic as they loaded several zones into the bus before sending it off and everyone rushed the single set of air stairs at the same time. This Airbus A330300 features 282 seats across four classes. 34 Delta 1 seats, 21 premium select seats, 24 comfort plus seats, and 208 economy seats. Delta 1 seats on this A330 are arranged in a one 121 reverse herring bone configuration. We're in seats 2A and 2J today. The bulkhead on opposite sides of the plane. Privacy was reasonable, but mainly due to having your back facing the aisle, not due to the walls of the seat. Be aware, these are not Delta's newer suites, and the seats do not feature closing doors. If a door is important to you, make sure you look for flights operated by Delta's A350s and A330900 Neos. When booking, look at the more details to see the aircraft type. Delta 767s have a variant of the Delta 1 suite, but don't feature closing doors due to the narrower cabin width. Delta will also eventually have closing door suites on their upcoming A321 Neos that feature Delta 1. These A330 Delta 1 cabin seats are 19.6 7 in wide and are fully lie flat. There was plenty of room to lay down, even for Trevor at 6'4. [Music] Each seat features a 15.4 in touchscreen if that swings out, as well as USBA and universal power outlets. The tray table extends from the side console and folds open. It's a good size for both dining and getting some work done. While in seat mode, the seat has great leg room. I'm 6 foot for reference. There's also an adjustable armrest on the aisle side. Delta's A33300's underwent interior refits in 2021. In 2022, a new premium select cabin with 21 seats in a 232 configuration were added. The Comfort Plus cabin was downsized from 40 to 24 seats in a 242 arrangement. They also refreshed the lavatories and even added an espresso machine. Delta 1 and economy cabins got new upholstery, but otherwise went unchanged. These current seats are rather dated and are not as private or modern as Delta's other widebody Delta 1 seats. Delta must agree because they've announced they're going to refit these aircraft in 2026. They plan to start taking the 42 aircraft back into refit to replace the business class cabin with the latest Delta 1 seats. Each seat had a Mason branded bedding pack that includes a pretty substantial pillow and a good quality duvet. This flight also featured Delta's brand new mattress toppers which are now available on all Delta 1 flights. At this seat were also noiseancelling headphones, a large bottle of water, and an amenity kit. Delta's current amenity kit is from a Sony. It has a dark blue soft leatherrett bag with a zipper and contains a small card for the brand, an eye mask, and some of the nicest airplane socks we've seen. Normally, these things are like tissue paper, but these were decidedly thick and even had a nice Delta logo on the back. Rounding out the kit are earplugs, Grown Alchemist brand hand cream and lip balm, a dental kit, and a cardboard pen. Prior to departure, we were served a welcome drink. The standard sparkling wine, orange juice, or a mimosa. We had a lengthy taxi this morning to get out to the runway, but once we were there, we were off. [Music] [Applause] There have been a number of wildfires in Spain this summer, so the skies are a little bit hazy. [Music] Now that we're up in the air, let's take a look at the onboard entertainment. One area where these seats really show their age is the if system. The screen swings out when you push a button to release it from the seat in front of you. My screen was not very bright, and the touch is not responsive. There is a remote, but in our experience, it takes a little getting used to, as the arrows work almost 90 degrees to what you would expect. The selection of movies and TV shows was similar to older Delta planes and was decent, but the more modern IF systems have more content. The flight tracker and moving map are almost completely useless and show just how much better the newer systems are on other aircraft. Just look at this graphic. As mentioned earlier, the seats also have a universal power outlet near your shoulder, and there's a USB port. These aircraft are also equipped with Wi-Fi, which is free for all Sky Miles members in all cabins. It worked fairly well and was relatively consistent across the flight. Shortly after takeoff, the flight attendants were up and hard at work. Service started with a hot towel, followed by a drink service, and nuts. Trevor and I both opted for a glass of the Bordeaux red wine. It was decent. However, in our experience, the red wines in Delta 1 aren't very premium. Delta does also offer real champagne in Delta 1. Delta allows you to pre-order your meal a week ahead of the flight. Here's a look at the menu for today's route. I opted for the seafood paella and Trevor ordered the duck.com fee. [Music] following drinks and nuts, the starters arrived. The starter was a Thai coconut curry soup, chilled shrimp with herb crimp fish, a garden salad with roasted tomatoes, and a warm roll. The salad was actually the best part. The shrimp were good and tender, but we think the version with the aioli on some other routes is better. The soup was pretty good, but would have benefited from a little bit more curry flavor. The crew then moved on to mains. Their service was friendly and efficient on this flight. One thing to keep in mind is that the galley for Delta 1 on these A330s is at the back of the cabin, so they served rear to front. The paella included fish and shrimp. The fish was moist and not overcooked. The shrimp were also well prepared. The dish was a good take on paella, but after a few days in Valencia on this trip, not terribly authentic. The duckcomb feet came with spiced poached pears, carrots, kale, and mashed potatoes. The dish overall was good, but a little bland. The sauce didn't have much flavor, but when all mixed together, it was decent. It was nice to have the fresh veggies, which were well cooked and still had some texture, which is nice, and it wasn't overly heavy. The duck was shredded and served as sort of a ball wrapped in the skin. The duck was a little dry, and there was a tiny bone fragment, so this was a miss, we'd say. For dessert, the options were fruit and cheese, ice cream sundaes, or a Sarrento lemon cake. I opted for the ice cream. Trevor had the lemon cake. The cake was a dome of whipped cream with a thin slice of cake with lemon filling and coated with a thin layer of chocolate. This was light, fresh, and enjoyable. The entire main meal service was completed about 2 hours after departure. During the flight, the crew made themselves available for drink refills. They set up snacks and bottled water in the forward galley, and passengers were welcome to help themselves. Mid-flight, the crew baked cookies. This is one of our favorite features of Delta 1, and the flight attendants often take pride in the fresh baked chocolate chip cookies at 36,000 ft. During the flight, we came down the East Coast and had some great views in New York. About 90 minutes before arrival, the crew came around with a hot snack. The options were a pizza or a cheeseburger. I opted for the burger and requested the cheese be removed before they heated it up, and the person was happy to oblige. I made this request earlier in the flight since I don't eat cheese. Trevor was offered a tomato and basil pizza. They had run out of the burger by the time they reached midc cabin. He reported that the pizza was actually really good. The crust was crisp and soft, not soggy at all. The pizza came with roasted vegetables and pesto and a very dense chocolate cake. After the snack, it was about time to descend into Atlanta. Enjoy the landing and we'll be back to wrap things up. [Music] We landed from the west and then taxied to gate F1. So that's the Delta 1 experience on the A330 from Madrid to Atlanta. While these seats are definitely not as private as some of Delta's newer seats, the flight was comfortable and the crew was great. While old, the seats are definitely spacious. Delta excels at the soft product with a friendly and responsive crew and decent food. The hard product is inconsistent. Delta has too many aircraft with different Delta 1 seats, but they are working to bring the fleet closer to alignment. These A330s are some of the oldest business class seats in Delta's lineup, but that should start to disappear next year. To recall a bit, if you want to fly Delta's latest product, look for the A330 900 Neo or A350 aircraft. You'll also find upgraded Delta 1 seats on the 767s. They just won't have closing doors. A few months ago, we flew Delta 1 to Lima, Peru on an Airbus A350. We'll link that review down in the description. That plane had a unique configuration that's about to disappear. Also, make sure you check out our entire Spain playlist. We'll be releasing new content over the next few months, including hotel reviews, city tours, and Spain by highspeed rail. If you enjoy this video, please give it a thumbs up and make sure you subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Both of these are a great way you can help out the channel. We really appreciate it. Thank you for watching. We'll see you on the next adventure.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to the TALA exhibition at the Dubai Show in 2011. Today we're here demonstrating  some equipment from the Inflight Entertainment and Connectivity Group, based in Erlinon,  California. We're showing examples of equipment which will be installed on various aircraft  times from 2012 onwards and forms part of our next generation Inflight Entertainment  platform which is known as top series avont. We're showing examples of the economy seat  screen which is a 12 inch capacitive touch screen interface and supports high definition  video, MPAC 4 and a very very wide range of applications delivered through the use of  the Android operating software and the Android market. As you can see it's a very  responsive interface. We have swipe capability which is very much in line with the latest  consumer electronics devices which are available in the marketplace. The viewing experience  for the passenger is a very rich and high quality video stream and again integrates the  latest in high definition close caption capabilities. All of the passenger interface functions  are integrated into the screen itself which means we can avoid the need for a control  handset which is particularly valuable in economy class configurations in terms of reducing  weight and minimizing maintenance. We're also integrating what we call smart passenger  interface modules and each of these modules is independently changeable so we can have  a combination of audio, Apple device connectivity USB and then we've also got an example here  of an early prototype of a webcam for barcode reader technology. reviews.transcript_full:
Hello! As you know, you take a plane
when you want to travel quickly. Yet, the trip can still be long
if you’re going half way around the world! On long-haul flights, especially,
it‘s important to travel in comfort and not just have to count
the passing clouds for entertainment. So airline companies have made
passenger satisfaction a priority. In particular, via two key
pieces of equipment: the seats and the entertainment systems. More than just something to sit on,
the aircraft seat blends design with safety, thanks to prototypes
developed in top secrecy. Made from light materials to guarantee
minimum weight and maximum solidity, it's designed to absorb shocks and to keep the passenger firmly in place,
even in case of turbulence. And because passengers spend most
of their journey sitting or lying down, aircraft seats have to be comfortable,
whatever class they happen to be in. So, on long haul flights,
you find 4 types of seats, a different seat
equipping each travel class: Economy Class... Premium Economy Class... Business Class... and First Class. For airlines, the choice of seat is a way
of differentiating their company. They choose its design, its covering and its color. But also the LOPA,
the Layout of Passenger Accommodations. Basically, how the seats
are positioned in the cabin. Other accessories possibly integrated
into the seat are up to the airlines. For example, the headrest, the provision of electrical power sockets, or even stowage. But airline companies also focus
their attention on another key element: the choice of screen. User-friendly interfaces, diversity
and quality of content, reliability... Indeed, airlines pay special attention
to their choice of IFE: In-Flight Entertainment systems. The most recent feature:
a touch-screen... that lets you watch movies, listen to music, play games, pull up a flight plan, check out the meal menus, or even order duty-free merchandise. Usually, all content is hosted
on one or several servers that then feeds all the screens. But Safran has developed a revolutionary
new IFE system called RAVE: a stand-alone system,
equipped with broadband connectivity, integrated into
a high-resolution 4K screen that hosts the content independently. The beauty of this system
is its ease of maintenance, because,
as opposed to other systems, here,
if one screen goes down, the other passenger screens
are not impacted. What’s more, RAVE is equipped
with a very high performance, interference-free
Bluetooth audio connection that provides the passenger
with superb listening comfort when synchronized with their own headset. And so... this system allows passengers
to personalize their content according to their areas of interest. In short, trips have never seemed shorter, even when you’re flying
half way around the world! There, now you know everything,
or nearly everything. But before we sign off, know that
with greater onboard connectivity, you can now hook up your smartphone
to the IFE system to use your very own Apps. And thanks to Wi-Fi, you can also use
your smartphone just like on the ground, or even enjoy a live program
comfortably seated with your head... in the clouds!

reviews.title: How Do Pilots Pass The Time On Long Flights?
reviews.transcript_excerpt:
additional forms of entertainment 
found on the flight deck.…

captions.text:
additional forms of entertainment 
found on the flight deck.

reviews.transcript_full:
For most passengers, long-haul flights are 
a matter of endurance aided by a few drinks,   inflight entertainment, and trying to get some 
sleep between meal services. It is an entirely   different matter for the people flying the plane 
as there are still plenty of things to do even   after takeoff. Let’s look at what’s happening 
on the flight deck during these longer flights… Even though flight paths are decided upon 
before departure, pilots have to monitor   weather conditions and decide whether 
or not to alter them during the flight.   On long-haul flights, weather conditions are 
more likely to change from initial forecasts,   with aircraft often encountering multiple 
weather systems. These systems can vary in   intensity from slight turbulence to dangerous 
thunderstorms. Traveling at high speeds,   pilots must be prepared at all times 
to alter the flight path if necessary. If, for example, they see a 
thunderstorm on the radar,   they must first get the OK from air traffic 
control (ATC) to change their route. Clear air turbulence is another worry, and 
because it cannot be seen on the radar,   pilots rely upon the information provided by 
pilots flying the same route ahead of them. When   flying across oceans such as the Atlantic, one 
pilot's job is to communicate with the ATC while   the other monitors a common air-to-air frequency 
that pilots use to communicate with each other. The entire time a flight is 
in the air, the pilots monitor   all kinds of gauges to ensure that the 
plane performs how it is supposed to. Making sure that the temperature of the fuel 
is not too cold is another thing pilots must   monitor. If the fuel cools down too much, 
its flow can be restricted due to waxing.   If this happens, pilots can rectify 
the situation by descending, or by   increasing the aircraft's speed (and, 
thus, its skin temperature). However,   this isn't a particularly frequent occurrence, 
as engine oil helps fuel to retain heat. While one of the pilots monitors all the 
gauges, the other will be busy taking care   of the paperwork. Before the flight, the 
pilots are given a written flight plan.   Anything that deviates from this 
must be written down as notes. Outside of these important activities, 
long-haul flying can be very boring for pilots.   During cruise phases, pilots will often pass 
the time by making small talk with one another,   or doing some reading. Smartphone games and 
good old fashioned crossword puzzles might be   additional forms of entertainment 
found on the flight deck. Finally, just like passengers, 
enjoying inflight meals   is another part of the long-haul pilot experience. The pilots typically wait until the passengers 
have been served and then eat separately.   They do this so that there is 
always one person at the controls. For long flights over twelve hours, there 
are one or two relief pilots onboard   so that the two pilots who performed the 
takeoff can take a break and get some rest. There are just two pilots on shorter 
long-haul flights of eight or nine   hours. The only opportunity they get to 
leave their seats and stretch their legs   is when they go to the bathroom. Did you know about these long-haul duties and 
activities? Let us know by leaving a comment.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Chicago Hair International Airport.  Today you'll join me on a business class journey to Munich aboard Lufthansa's A350.  This flight is part of my return trip between Vienna and Chicago, initially booked an economy  for 751 euros, then upgraded using e-vouchers from my mouse and more senator's status.  Unlike Austrian Airlines and Swiss, which operate out of Terminal 5, Lufthansa shares Terminal  1 with United Airlines.  We arrived at the airport just before 5pm, only to discover that the check-in desks wouldn't  open until 10 past 6.  Anticipating this, we queued up at 550 as the staff began to appear and the desks opened  slightly ahead of schedule.  Check-in and priority security were remarkably efficient and we found ourselves at the  sea gates in no time.  Traveling through O'Hare's iconic tunnel, a brief 3-minute walk brought us to the highlight  of our early arrival, the United Polaris Lounge.  Exclusively available to international, star alliance, business or first class passengers,  the Polaris Lounge offers the finest lounge experience in Chicago.  Even if your flight departs from a different terminal, you can switch terminals airside  to indulge in this unparalleled oasis of comfort and luxury.  Feeling hungry, we bypassed the drinks counter and the inviting seating pods and headed straight  for the dining room, the Allacard restaurant of the lounge.  While reservations are possible during busy times, we were fortunate to find the lounge  almost empty, securing a table immediately.  The menu, though small, was perfectly curated.  In a business class lounge, quality over quantity is key and a limited selection ensured each  dish was of top-notch quality.  We settled into a cozy booth with a view of the dining area and enjoyed a delightful meal.  I opted for the signature burger, customizable with a variety of toppings and it exceeded  my expectations.  For those in a hurry or seeking a quick snack, the expansive buffet offers a variety of options.  The lounge also features a manned bar for alcoholic beverages.  As a huge fan of cocktails, I eagerly ordered an old-fashioned but was disappointed by how  overly sweet it was.  I decided to switch to champagne for the rest of our stay, which proved to be a much better  choice.  It's worth noting that the bar expects you to tip, which I find a bit off-putting in  a lounge setting.  The lounge provides excellent apron views, though there wasn't much activity to observe  during our visit.  As our time in the lounge drew to the close, we learned that the showers and nap rooms  were already closed as well, which was a minor disappointment.  However, the all-gender restrooms were plentiful, spacious and impeccably clean, adding to  the overall comfort of our lounge experience.  After a delightful stay in the lounge, we made our way back through the tunnel and headed  to the B gates, where two Lufthansa flights, one to Frankfurt and our Sumeunik, were scheduled  to depart from neighboring gates in quick succession.  These convergence created a somewhat chaotic scene, with passengers crowding the area.  However, when priority boarding commenced, we swiftly left the crowd behind and joined  the queue to board our aircraft, an Airbus A350-900.  The A350 features eight rows in a 2-2-2 business class configuration.  The larger cabin spans rows 1-2-6, while a more intimate mini cabin occupies rows 7-8.  For this flight, we selected Seats 7 Hotel and 7 Kilo in the bulkhead row of the smaller  cabin, seeking a bit more privacy.  We were warmly greeted at the door, and again, as we made our way down the aisle, but unfortunately,  that was the extent of the warm hospitality we had anticipated.  Currently, the most common business class product in Lufthansa's fleet is starting to see  a change with the introduction of their new Aliegris business class, which debuted on  the Munich-Tubank Uber route on May 1, 2024.  While this older configuration is certainly outdated and lacks privacy, it does offer an  advantage for couples like us who enjoy sharing a window seat.  Here's a clear view of row 8, along with a look at the bulkhead footwell, which was  unfortunately smaller than I had hoped for.  However, this was not the biggest issue I encountered with the seat.  More on that later.  We had ample time to settle in, as the crew assigned to our cabin was noticeably absent.  It wasn't until long after the left side of our cabin had been served the welcome drinks  that we were finally offered a glass of champagne.  Let's take a closer look at the seat.  Unfortunately, there are no individual air vents.  The aisle seat offers a bit more storage space than the window seat, thanks to the litter  richer pocket positioned between the footwells.  The closed cubby initially housed the amenity kit and a water bottle.  Head folds outwards in the middle.  Between the seats there are two universal power outlets.  The whole next to them housed the AKG on ear headphones and the headphone jack.  On top of the consoles are the controls for the air cushioned seat and a flap opens up  to reveal the tray table and IFE remote.  Underneath the console is a USB-A port.  The tray table is released by pushing on it and folds out to double the surface area.  Although there was some flex, it felt sturdy overall.  The remote uses a D pad instead of the cursor found on other Loftanza planes.  My left armrest could be lowered to widen the bed or make it easier to leave the seat  with the table deployed.  The headrest which also houses a reading lamp is adjustable as well.  Here you can see the amenity kit, a pouch from Portia design containing the bar essentials  and a few lotions from Lotsitun.  Next to the IFE screen there is a coat hook and a holder for your glasses.  After take off the meal service began with a hot towel.  As is typical with overnight flights from the US, the selection was somewhat limited and  the meal was served on one tray to save time.  If you're eager to get to sleep you can opt for the Express service.  Nuts were handed out with the drink service.  For my main course I chose the surf and turf which was easily the best dish I enjoyed  on this flight.  The appetizer salad wasn't too my liking but the ice cream provided a satisfying conclusion  to the meal as I decided to skip the cheese course.  The restroom was a standard A350 bathroom featuring a full body mirror and a few amenities  stocked on the counter.  In addition to soap there was also lotion available.  As for the seats they are slightly angled towards the fuselage unlike the bulkhead.  The IFE screens fold out slightly but unfortunately cannot be angled downwards when you're in  bed mode which can't be inconvenient.  The entertainment selection was just okay.  I found a few movies that caught my interest but frequent flyers might quickly exhaust the  available content.  The user interface worked well with the remote but the limitations of the system became  apparent when trying to scroll with a finger.  The TV show selection was a significant letdown.  While waiting for the flight map to load I checked out the Wi-Fi prices.  25 euros gets you unlimited data with the highest speed for the entire flight.  The plane is equipped with three cameras providing different views during the journey.  Lufcans are offers unpackaged headphones for their business class customers with ear  pad covers available in the amenity kit.  As usual I opted to use my AirFlight Pro Bluetooth transmitter in conjunction with my AirPods  Max.  Before bed the crew handed out a small box of pre-leens a delightful touch to end the evening.  As I mentioned before the seat is air cushioned theoretically allowing you to adjust the firmness  of the mattress.  Unfortunately an hour after I managed to fall asleep I awoke with hip pain because the  bottom half of the seat had completely deflated leaving me lying on the metal frame.  The crew had to partially disassemble the seat to check all the hoses and restart it.  Luckily this fixed the issue but it still disrupted my sleep.  Unlike on other long haul flights to Asia for example no mattress pads slippers or sleeping  shirts were provided on this flight.  Breakfast was served on a single tray which was perfectly fine.  The Greek yogurt bowl was into my liking but the rest of the breakfast dish was okay.  I was left a bit underwhelmed by this flight.  The crew member attending to us throughout the journey neither greeted us nor smiled during  any interaction.  It is heartening to feel like a burden to the crew especially when you are being friendly  and not making any special requests.  The entertainment selection was lackluster which isn't a huge deal for a night flight  but it could be a let down on day flights or for frequent flyers who get the same limited  selection.  The food was okay though I can't be somewhat picky so I might not be the best benchmark  in that regard.  The issue with the seat in bed mode was unfortunate but thankfully could be fixed.  I had a similar issue on Swiss a few years ago and that persisted throughout the whole  flight.  Our flight to Chicago in Austrian Airlines business class was much more enjoyable.  If you have the option I would recommend choosing them over Loftanza.  You can see what that flight was like by clicking on this video.  Thank you so much for watching, please like and subscribe if you're new, happy travels  and see you soon.

article_text: Singapore Airlines (SIA) has made in-flight entertainment (IFE) a central passenger experience feature of its new Premium Economy cabin , through a combination of latest generation hardware, a user-friendly interface and a strong content platform.

The selected Panasonic eX3 system boasts the largest screen introduced into a premium economy cabin. It dominates the back of the modern, feature-rich seat , giving passengers an immersive, cinematic experience. To make that experience complete, SIA will offer premium economy passengers the same Phitek noise-canceling headphones given to passengers in the airline’s business class cabin.
The hardware upgrade also includes an overhaul of the airline’s KrisWorld IFE interface, capitalizing on new touchscreen and swipe capabilities to build an intuitive menu.

SIA’s vice president of Public Affairs, Nicholas Ionides, tells us that the selection of Panasonic’s eX3 system for the new cabin was based on a long-term vendor relationship with Panasonic that “began in 2006, when SIA was the first airline to launch Panasonic’s eX2 system.”

“SIA subsequently launched a next generation KrisWorld, based on Panasonic’s eX3 system, for the Boeing 777-300ERs that entered service from September 2013,” Ionides says. “Our premium economy class customers will enjoy the same next generation KrisWorld, and will experience an improved graphical user interface on our 13.3-inch HD-enabled touchscreen LCD monitor.”

The airline’s content mix includes early-window, popular and foreign films, as well as television programs, music channels, hosted radio programming, games and learning content. SIA has paid special attention to ensure that KrisWorld’s content will appeal to a diverse passenger mix.

“[IFE is] specially designed and continually adapted to suit the prevailing tastes and preferences of our customers who come from all over the world,” Ionides says, adding that airline monitors consumer trends and passenger response to content to inform its product decisions.
“Awards like the Passenger Choice Awards do affirm that we are on the right track.” – Nicholas Ionides, VP Public Affairs, Singapore Airlines

“We do track viewership numbers and we use these figures to constantly adapt our in-flight entertainment to what our customers want,” Ionides adds. “Awards like the Passenger Choice Awards do affirm that we are on the right track.” The airline offers films for all ages in a variety of genres, and includes a content warning screen which lets viewers make their own decisions on the film that follows.

“KrisWorld is an entertainment platform that caters to various groups of customers – both adults and children,” Ionides says. “We therefore need to ensure that besides providing entertainment value, our in-flight selection of films and movies needs to be evaluated for content such as crude or tasteless humor, excessive graphical violence and controversy relating to race, religion or politics. That said, the above are guidelines as we would still assess films on a case-by-case basis, whenever the need arises.”

The airline also offers a “Kid’s Mode,” which gives children access to cartoons, family-friendly movies and games, and allows parents to ensure the content their children enjoy on the KrisWorld dashboard is suitable.

Because many of its routes are long-haul flights, SIA lets passengers make the most of their time with educational content. “Passengers can choose to enrich themselves with Berlitz World Traveller, a fully interactive language-learning program,” Ionides tells us, which offers “a total of 23 of the world’s most popular languages.”

There are also courses to sharpen business and cultural skills. “Culture Quest is an information application that provides cross-cultural tips for doing business in more than 10 countries,” Ionides says. Also, DK Travel Guides give passengers destination information on major cities around the world.

Connectivity complements the airline’s IFE product, increasing the choice of activities onboard. “Singapore Airlines launched in-flight connectivity services in 2012 as part of a $50-million program,” Ionides says. “Passengers can surf the Internet, send and receive e-mails on smartphones and other electronic devices, and send and receive SMS text messages with GSM-compatible mobile phones.”

OnAir provides connectivity service to the airline, which also offers telephony, but SIA has elected not to allow telephone calls on its flights. On the airline’s six new 777-300ERs, connectivity is provided by Panasonic Avionics.

“Thirty-eight aircraft have been equipped to date and the service will be rolled out to the rest of the 777-300ER aircraft in the fleet by 2016,” says Ionides. “The A350s will also be fitted with connectivity services.”

article_text: There has been an explosion in the number of airlines offering fast WiFi and in-seat charging for mobile devices. The temptation, therefore, is to shift away from inflight entertainment (IFE) systems and expect passengers to create their own fun. However, some airlines are resisting this momentum to keep providing leading IFE that ensures passengers have an enjoyable inflight experience.

One such airline is Cathay Pacific. The carrier has recently been recognized for its efforts with a first-place in the Skytrax award for The World's Best In-Flight Entertainment 2025. Discover below more about the award and the systems and partnerships that have allowed Cathay Pacific to take the top spot.
Cathay Pacific Receives The Skytrax Award

The aviation industry group Skytrax has released results for its 2025 awards. Included in the host of categories is the Skytrax World's Best Inflight Entertainment 2025 award, which Cathay Pacific has won. In achieving this accolade, it has beaten the likes of Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Singapore Airlines, all of which are close behind.
The table below shows the full top-20 standings in Skytrax World's Best Inflight Entertainment 2025 award:

Unsurprisingly, Cathay Pacific has also performed well in the other Skytrax awards. This includes winning the World's Best Economy Class award and placing in the top three for the overall 2025 Skytrax World Airline Awards. Chief Executive Officer Ronald Lam said: ""Being voted among the top three best airlines in the world, up two places from last year, and the world’s best for Economy class and inflight entertainment again is extremely encouraging. These accolades underscore our unwavering commitment to delivering exceptional service and enhancing the customer experience across every part of their journey."
What IFE Does Cathay Pacific Offer?

Cathay Pacific's inflight entertainment is delivered on a touchscreen Panasonic Avionics screen. Newer aircraft, including the carrier's A321neo and select 777s, also have 4K HDR displays and Bluetooth audio. There is a focus on both Asian and Hollywood cinema and boxsets, alongside music.

A full HBO MAX rollout from January 2022 has further expanded the entertainment available onboard Cathay Pacific jets. It added over 200 hours of HBO MAX content within the first three months of this rollout, helping passengers catch up on their box sets. That meant a passenger would have to circumnavigate the globe 45 times onboard a Cathay Pacific aircraft before they ran out of shows. Cathay Pacific's General Manager Customer Experience and Design, Vivian Lo , said, "To be the first in Asia to launch the HBO Max brand, not just onboard flights but anywhere is exceptional. It’s a great example of an airline and streaming service working together to bring an unprecedented entertainment experience to passengers, and we hope our customers find their next new binge-worthy show on Cathay Pacific."

The host of children's films and television available through the inflight entertainment systems also contributed to Skytrax recognizing Cathay Pacific in its World's Most Family Friendly Airline 2025 rankings . Other airlines featured on this list include EVA Air, Lufthansa, and British Airways.
Cathay Pacific's IFE Is Getting Upgraded

2025 is set to bring more improvements to Cathay Pacific's IFE through the introduction of a new interface that allows passengers to personalize their environment, as reported by Apex. The carrier collaborated with Reaktor Aero to debut the new IFE system aboard the retrofitted Boeing 777-300ER within the Aria business class suites. Reaktor’s VP, Michael Holler, said that the system “is truly state-of-the-art, seamlessly incorporating the latest technology with a design that is elegant and intuitive to use.” Meanwhile, Cathay Pacific’s Head of Customer Experience – Connectivity & IFE Strategy, Guillaume Vivet, said that the system emerged from multiple rounds of customer interviews and testing.

The central concept is an interface that allows passengers to customize their cabin. One example is extensive seat controls so that passengers can easily find the most comfortable position and lighting for work, eating, using the IFE, or sleeping.

Cathay Pacific has also embedded features to enhance the overall experience. This includes incorporating the lavatory occupancy status into the system. The carrier also had plans to introduce a "My Journey" interface, so passengers can play around with flight paths and map layers. "My Journey" is developed in collaboration with FlightPath3D’s API toolkit and widgets. "My Journey" isn't just entertainment, but will also allow passengers to set their preferred times for working, eating, watching movies, and sleeping.
What Does Skytrax Think Of Cathay Pacific's Other Attributes?

Skytrax has named Cathay Pacific a "5-Star Airline" after combining its ratings for the carrier's airport, and onboard product, and staff service across all classes, reflecting that the industry group believes that the carrier is a strong performer overall. In long-haul aviation, business class is rated five stars, while first class, premium economy and economy classes all earn 4.5 stars. Meanwhile, both business class and economy class receive five star ratings for short-haul travel.

Within each class, Skytrax has a further breakdown, assigning stars to different characteristics. All of these characteristics have four stars or more across all classes. Examples of four-star attributes in economy class include the cabin temperature, washroom amenities, and WiFi service. Meanwhile, check-in and priority check-in staff and facilities receive four stars for Premium Economy. Finally, premium customers flying in first class will find four star quality in many aspects of the long-haul onboard product, including the provision of comfort items such as duvets.

Skytrax ratings are also useful to see the areas where Cathay Pacific excels by identifying the attributes that received five stars. In economy class, this includes the quality of meals, seat comfort, and, unsurprisingly, inflight entertainment. Jumping up to business class, Skytrax praises Cathay Pacific's onboard staff. Speed, language skills, and attention to cabin safety all receive five stars. Finally, Skytrax is complimentary of Cathay Pacific's first class lounge. It gives five stars to The Wing/The Pier's washrooms and showers, choice of beverages, comfort, and access to power and WiFi.
Business Class: Another Reason To Fly Cathay Pacific

Skytrax has also recognized Cathay Pacific for its excellent business class. The carrier uses a reverse herringbone arrangement to look beyond glitzy momentum in the business-class industry to offer a product with subtle comfort. Each passenger has plenty of space and direct access to the aisle. The business-class suites are also noteworthy for their openness, rather than the claustrophobic privacy. The simple comfort is also present in the carrier's customer lounges, where customers can enjoy a peaceful experience and delicate local cuisine. This includes specialty tea and dishes inspired by Hong Kong street food. The same sort of culinary options are available onboard.

Everything is rather muted onboard with minimalist bedding and amenities, all contained within eco-friendly packaging. Yet, there are some drawbacks to be aware of. Considering the cost of business-class and the desire for many onboard to get some work done, the pay-per-use WiFi will sting. The quality of the IFE does somewhat lessen the blow. The show or movie you want to stream is probably available on their system. Other passengers may be perturbed by the comparative lack of privacy.
What Are The Skytrax World Airline Awards?

Everybody has a different opinion on what makes a great IFE. There will be plenty of disagreement on which carrier has the best system. This article has based its position of Cathay Pacific at the top of the world's IFE on the results of the 2025 Skytrax World Airline Awards for the best IFE. Skytrax refers to these awards as "the Oscars of the aviation industry." They have been running since 1999.

A unique attribute of these awards is how open they are. Any airline can be nominated and there is no charge for entry fees or to attend the awards event. That is because the awards are fully funded by the other services that Skytrax offers. The final winners of each category are selected by customers, making these awards truly a passenger choice. There were 325 airlines included in the awards, with the survey running from September 2024 to May 2025. Over 100 nationalities participated in the survey. Skytrax also has strict security measures to ensure that the results are fair. This includes the fact that they host the survey themselves and take steps to ensure that individuals do not complete it multiple times.

Some nine years after Panasonic Avionics first introduced 4K inflight entertainment touchscreens via the Waterfront concept at CES , the hardware and content pipeline has finally brought 4K aboard an aircraft I’ve flown.

Your author recently experienced his first actual, real-world 4K video on board a Cathay Pacific A321neo this month, in conjunction with Cathay’s launch of 4K HDR content last month (for which, full disclosure, he was a guest of the airline), and the experience was an absolute joy.
