reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Istanbul! I have two flights coming up today. First, I’ll be flying with Turkish Airlines to Helsinki. After that, I’ll be flying in Finnair’s brand new A350 business class to Singapore. This is my entire itinerary: Istanbul - Helsinki - Singapore, then Hong Kong! The total duration comes close to 52 hours. This exciting journey gives me the chance to enjoy business class services with three different airlines, all at a low cost of AU$2200. I consider this an absolute bargain, so let the adventure begin! Istanbul has two major airports. The New Istanbul Airport, opened in 2018, handles most of the city’s international traffic. Being the hub for Turkish Airlines, there’s a dedicated entry for the airline’s business and elite-level frequent flyers. I booked all my flights on Finnair’s website, but as my first flight was with Turkish Airlines, I had to check in with them. This airport is one of my favourites in the world. The international departures area resembles a giant shopping mall! Sam Chui thinks the terminal is too big, but I find it to be of a good size, getting to the furthest gate takes no more than 20 minutes. The Turkish Airlines business lounge is quite exceptional. Each chef has a dedicated cooking station, and the food is prepared right in front of you. For eligible passengers with long layovers in Istanbul, Turkish Airlines provides free hotel rooms in the city, and the lounge also offers private rooms and showers. My flight to Helsinki this morning is on a Turkish Airlines A321neo. There are five rows in business class with seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. They have a sleek, modern design. The small divider adds a bit of privacy to the seat. There’s a universal power plug and USB port below the armrest. The 13-inch high-definition touchscreen is packed with entertainment options, including a collection of 659 movies for you to choose from! Turkish Airlines is known for its excellent in-flight catering. For this 3-hour flight, I was offered a watermelon and cheese appetiser, along with three main meal options. The plating is vibrant, and the food, as always, showcases the best of Turkish cuisine. The 3-hour flight went by quickly, and welcome to Helsinki! Helsinki is renowned for striking a harmonious balance between urban sophistication and serene landscapes. This Finnish capital is the perfect gateway for international visitors eager to chase the enchanting Northern Lights or the midnight sun in the nation’s Lapland region. Ladies and gentlemen, and dear children, we hope that you had a pleasant flight. As a Star Alliance member, thank you for flying with Turkish Airlines, Scandinavian Airlines, and Finnair's codeshare flight. We would like to say goodbye and hope to meet you again. Helsinki-Vantaa is the busiest airport in Finland. It’s the hub for Finnair, a member of the Oneworld alliance. Despite not being as busy as other major European hubs like Heathrow, Charles de Gaulle, or Frankfurt, its smaller size makes it one of Europe’s easiest and most pleasant transfer airports. Of course, there are duty-free shops, restaurants, and cafes for you to pass the time. My flight to Singapore is 13 hours away. While I could leave the airport and explore the city,  I decided remain airside and check out the two Finnair lounges in the non-Schengen zone. The Business Class Lounge is open to Oneworld Sapphire frequent flyers and business class passengers. Meanwhile, the Platinum Wing Lounge stands as an exclusive oasis for Oneworld Emerald frequent flyers. Upon entering, you’ll find luggage lockers, eliminating the need to drag your suitcase around the lounge. The lounge is divided into several separate spaces for working, relaxing, and dining, with distinctive Nordic design elements seamlessly integrated throughout. The upscale bar is really impressive, the shelves are stocked with vintage champagne, spirits, wines, and beers from local and international markets. The bartender is well-versed in creating signature cocktails as well as barista-style coffees. When I requested a fruity mocktail, the bartender prepared a delightful blueberry drink that tasted amazing. Since the Platinum Wing is only open to a handful of qualified passengers, it never gets crowded. Instead of exuding a business atmosphere, this lounge makes me feel as if I were at home. The couch-style chairs are incredibly comfortable, and nearly every seat is equipped with power plugs. For those who enjoy conversing with their travel partners, there are tables and stools behind the bar. And the working area provides seats fitted with small tables and lamps. Toward the far end of the lounge is the main dining area. The tables and chairs have a casual Ikea vibe, aligning with the overall homely atmosphere of the lounge. On every table, there’s an à la carte menu showcasing the month’s featured dishes. Additionally, there’s a dessert table with fruit, petit fours, cheeses, and a buffet station offering Nordic delicacies and Asian-inspired treats. I particularly appreciate the vibrant colours of the dishes, and the open kitchen at the back gives you a glimpse into the meal preparation process. I ordered the grilled salmon from the à la carte menu. It was delicious. And later decided to sample the reindeer burger from the menu! It was cooked nicely. The patty is a combination of smoked reindeer and beef, it tasted just like a classic hamburger, nothing special. Behind the dining room curtain hides a rather spacious, quiet area. This dark-blue-themed section emulates a living room, with numerous couches to cosy up in. For a flagship lounge, there has to be showers. There are three private shower rooms accessible on a first-come, first-use basis. You can reserve one for 30 minutes using the control pad. Once booked a vacant room, the door automatically unlocks. The shower room features a tasteful colour scheme of navy and grey, and you’ll find organic hand wash, creams, and various premium amenities at your disposal. The shower cubicle is generously sized and includes a rainfall and handheld showerhead. The most distinctive feature of the Platinum Wing is the sauna. In Finland, saunas are an integral part of the culture and hold deep significance. In the dressing room, there’s a vanity table, lockers, towels, and showers. The sauna can accommodate 4-5 people at a time. Since someone was already inside, I refrained from filming it. Here’s a picture I found on the internet. In general, the Platinum Wing is one of the most remarkable lounges I’ve ever visited. Unfortunately, it currently only opens from 10:30 am to 5:30 pm, which coincides with the departure time of most of Finnair’s long-haul flights. At 5:30 pm, I was asked to relocate to the business lounge next door. The business lounge is accessible to Oneworld business class passengers and Sapphire-level frequent flyers. There are luggage lockers at the entrance. Now, this place resembles more of an airport lounge than a cozy living room, it’s more ordinary, but the facilities remain largely similar. Upon entering, you’ll find a self-service beverage station stocked with beers, soft drinks, and tea bags. The seating looks a bit simpler but remains comfortable. The space is considerably larger, with a seating capacity of 450 people, compared to just 155 in the Platinum Wing. The buffet offers similar food, including salads, hot meals, side dishes, soup, snacks, and desserts, although there’s no à la carte menu. Behind the main dining area, there’s a circular bar. It’s not always staffed, therefore you can pour your own wines and mix drinks. I appreciate these wall-enclosed seats that provide both privacy and comfort. Once more, nearly all seats have power plugs nearby. While there’s no sauna, you can still take a shower before your flight. Can you guess the current time? Does this look like 6 pm to you? Well, surprise — it’s actually 10:21 pm. The sunset is expected at 10:46 pm, and sunrise at 3:53 am. This video was filmed in mid-June. Due to Helsinki’s geographical location, in June, the sun only briefly dips below the horizon before rising again. To me, this is quite phenomenal! Finnair’s long-haul fleet comprises 8 A330-300s and 17 A350-900s. They are undergoing gradual refurbishment, with plans to install the new business, premium economy, and economy class seats on all these aircraft by early 2024. The plane that will take me to Singapore is a refurbished 3-class 278-seat A350. It’s now 12:30 am, and the sun will rise again in just 3 hours. Yet remarkably, the sky remains anything but dark! Boarding commenced 35 minutes before departure. Welcome aboard! Finnair’s new business class is arranged in a 1-2-1 configuration, featuring Collin’s AirLounge seats. I love the dark blue colour, and it’s certainly one of the widest business seats I’ve seen. For optimal privacy and an excellent view of the engine during daytime, I picked seat 8A, located in the last row of the main cabin. The most unique design of the seat is that it’s not reclinable. The seat-back seamlessly blends with the sidewall, forming a semi-enclosed cocoon-like structure designed to resemble a piece of classic Nordic furniture rather than a simple airline seat. Once I settled in, the crew offered me a choice of still or sparkling water, champagne, or Finnair’s signature blueberry juice, which quickly became my favourite drink throughout the flight. Cabin crew arm the doors and cross check... We pushed back on time, and I couldn’t tell whether this is a sunset or sunrise! Helsinki-Vantaa Airport has three runways. This morning, we took off from runway 22R, then executed a left-hand turn over the city before continuing across the Gulf of Finland towards Tallinn, Estonia. As we headed south, the sky gradually darkened. Once the seatbelt sign was turned off, the crew handed me a wet towel to refresh myself. A meal will be served shortly. In the meantime, let’s take a closer look at the AirLounge seat! At the front, there’s a big high-definition entertainment screen. A mattress pad, a quilt, and a pair of slippers are neatly placed in the foot nook. I always appreciate having a small compartment like this so I can store small loose items here instead of having to always reach for my backpack. The left armrest doubles as a large table with a built-in wireless charging pad. There are buttons to control the leg rest, lights, and call the flight attendant. There’s another tray table that folds out to become a sizeable dining table or desk for work. Apart from the overhead reading light, there’s an adjustable lamp positioned near my shoulder to ensure ample lighting around my seat on a night flight like this. Beneath the lamp, there’s another concealed compartment where I found the remote control for the entertainment screen, a noise-cancelling headphone, and both USB type A and type C sockets. I also spotted a universal power plug near my feet, which I had missed earlier. The concept of the AirLounge is to offer both personal space and freedom to move, allowing me to relax in the most comfortable position. Furthermore, the two firm pillows on my seat make me feel like I’m lounging on a couch. Finnair does not have a dine-on-demand service in Business Class. Instead, long-haul flights typically include a main meal after takeoff and a lighter second meal a few hours before landing. A paper menu was given to us while we were on the ground, and you can find it on your entertainment screen too. To ensure your preferred choice is available, Finnair suggests that passengers pre-order their main meals online on long-haul flights from Helsinki. In terms of drinks, there’s a good selection of wines, beers, cocktails, and other non-alcoholic beverages. I must say, I love the presentation of the meal, each dish looks colourful and beautifully plated, and strikes a great balance between meat and vegetables. To begin, there are two cold plates. The thinly sliced beef is tender with a slightly caramelised exterior.  The citrusy ponzu sauce creates a delightful contrast that tantalises the taste buds. Instead of serving the typical green leaf salad found on many other airlines, the second cold plate is a creamy mustard potato salad. The green pea puree brings a burst of freshness and sweetness to my palate. Moving on to the main dish, the pork belly delivers a lavish and indulgent protein. The meat was well marinated in the sauce and was cooked thoroughly. It melted in my mouth instantaneously. Overall, all three dishes were incredibly delicious and maintained a high standard. I couldn’t fault anything. Aside from the cheese, there are two dessert options. Seeing that I was filming the flight, the crew warmly offered me both. I appreciate the petite portions they provide, as I assume most passengers, including myself, would prefer a lighter treat after a large and satisfying meal. The meal service concluded just 70 minutes after takeoff, which is remarkably swift. Shortly after that, the crew dimmed the lights to enable passengers to settle down for sleep. An amenity kit is provided in business class, featuring lip balms, facial cream, earplugs, and eye masks. The slippers in the foot nook come in two sizes, and the large size fits my feet perfectly. When it’s time to rest, you can press this button to elevate the leg rest, transforming the entire seat into a fully flat bed. The crew then kindly offered to make the bed for me. Now you can see how wide the seat is. The bed is long, I’m 6’1” or 186cm tall, and I couldn’t reach the end of the foot nook. Before I sleep, let me quickly show you Finnair’s redesigned inflight entertainment system. The touchscreen is 18 inches in size and offers eight languages. I love this timeline on the home screen, showing the time in both Helsinki and Singapore, the scheduled meal times, and the recommended sleep time. A quick glance would let passengers easily keep track of their flight progress. In terms of entertainment, there are movies, TV series, music, and games. There are 100 popular movies to choose from. The flight map proves that the Earth is not flat! If you select the explore mode, you can zoom in and out of the map. I find this to be a perfect way to enhance my geography knowledge. The aircraft is equipped with satellite Wi-Fi, which is free for the first hour for business and Finnair Gold frequent flyers and for the entire duration of the flight for Finnair’s platinum members. Other passengers can purchase internet access using a credit card or Finnair points. I connected with my free 1-hour pass, and the speed was fast enough to upload stories on my Instagram. It’s been 24 hours since I last slept. I had to get up at 3am for my flight from Istanbul to Helsinki yesterday morning. So, goodnight! I woke up after having a solid 3.5-hour nap. The quilt is fairly warm and soft, and my legs have plenty of space to move around. We are currently flying over the Caspian Sea and are still over 7.5 hours away from Singapore. There are three lavatories for the 43 business class passengers. I love this disinfectant spray so that I can wipe the toilet seat. As we are flying eastward, it’s now daytime outside. While there isn’t any eau de toilette or cologne,  the hand wash and body lotion are produced in Finland, and I love their scent. I then took a stroll to door 2. The crew has set up a small snack bar here where you can help yourself to water and a range of snacks. Feeling a bit peckish, I grabbed a pack of gummies and chips. In business class, Finnair provides noise-cancelling headphones, this pair effectively lowered the cabin noise, I was satisfied with them. After finishing my snack, I felt sleepy again, so I took another nap, only waking up 3 hours later. The time between the two meals is about 10 hours, which I find to be a really lengthy gap. Breakfast was still 2 hours away, and I began feeling quite hungry. I asked the crew if they had any more substantial snacks, such as a sandwich. Unfortunately, they didn’t have any, but they kindly offered me some fresh fruits. I decided to stay awake from this point on, as I was concerned that if I slept now, I might struggle to sleep tonight when the plane landed at 7:30 pm. We are finally only 2 hours away from landing. It’s 12 o’clock in Helsinki and 5 pm in Singapore. I find it amusing to have breakfast at nearly dinner time. Unless you have pre-ordered a dietary meal, there’s only one choice for everyone. It’s a typical Western breakfast consisting of bread, scrambled eggs, hash browns, baked beans, spinach, cold cuts of meat, fresh fruits, and yogurt. To complete the meal, I enjoyed a cup of cappuccino. As we begin our descent into Singapore, I’d like to share my thoughts on this flight. I genuinely admire Finnair’s innovative spirit: being the world’s first and only airline to offer non-reclining seats in business class is a bold move, and I must say I’m quite impressed. The contoured shell design provides exceptional privacy, creating a sense of being in a private suite. The spacious seat gives me ample room to sleep and stretch out. The dining experience, both in the lounge and onboard, was delightful. However, the absence of substantial snacks left me hungry between the meals. I believe, well, judging from their accents, the cabin crew were all based in Singapore. They were warm, polite, and professional, addressing me by my last name throughout the flight. Starting this October, Qantas Airways, the flag carrier of Australia, will be wet leasing two of Finnair's A330 aircraft for routes between Sydney and Bangkok, as well as Sydney and Singapore. I'm eagerly anticipating the opportunity to fly on this exceptional product again! Furthermore, I think getting three business class flights for AU$2200 was definitely a steal. A warm welcome to Singapore ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of all of us onboard Finnair, and the oneworld alliance, I hope you have enjoyed your stay with us. Thank you, goodbye, and we look forward to seeing you again soon onboard Finnair. Welcome to Singapore! Finnair uses Terminal 1 at Changi Airport, which provides convenient connections with its Oneworld partners. The arrival time is perfectly aligned for an onward Qantas flight to Australia. My next flight with Cathay Pacific to Hong Kong will depart in 17 hours. I decided to enter Singapore and stay at the Crowne Plaza, which offers fantastic views of Terminal 3 and the runway, as well as convenient access to Jewel Changi Airport Shopping Complex. I’ll tell you more about it in my next video! Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. See you again soon!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Jakarta! Today I’m going to travel on the Argo Bromo Anggrek, Indonesia’s most prestigious rail service to Surabaya. Introduced in 2018, the Exectuive Luxury Class on this train only has 18 lavishly designed lie-flat seats in each carriage. I’m excited to find out what this 8hr journey will look like! Let’s go! Jakarta is the capital city of Indonesia, situated on the northwest coast of the island of Java. The Greater Jakarta region has a population of over 33 million, making it one of the most densely populated metropolitan areas in the world. The city is investing heavily in public transport infrastructures to reduce road congestion. There are several rail terminuses in the city. Jakarta Kota is the historic terminus, the current building was constructed in 1929. It handled most of the intercity trains to and from the capital until 2014. At the moment, it is used mainly by commuter trains and two long-distance trains. Most executive and business class trains currently commence their journeys from Gambir station, and economy class trains use the Pesar Senen station. Expected to be fully operational in October this year, Halim station will be the terminal for Southeast Asia’s first high-speed rail line, linking Jakarta to Bandung. Trains on this line can reach speeds of up to 350 km/h. All these stations are easily accessible by commuter trains, except for Gambir Station. It’s on the Bogor line. However, due to limited platform space, the Bogor trains do not stop here. Therefore, passengers needing to catch a train at Gambir must find their own way to the station. I used the ride-sharing app Grab to get here. The Argo Bromo Anggrek is long regarded as Indonesia’s most prestigious train. The name “Argo Bromo” was derived from the famous Bromo volcano in East Java. "Anggrek" means orchid. There are four train services operating under this name, travelling between Jakarta and Surabaya each day: one daytime service and one overnight service, departing from both cities. Gambir Station has three floors, the rail tracks are located on the top floor. Mornings are the busiest period. There is hardly any seating space on the ground level. So, unless you’re here to film a review, it’s best not to arrive too early.  There are a few options to purchase a train ticket: go to the station, visit certain convenience stores, or buy online through the official Indonesian railways website. However, the website only accepts Indonesian bank cards. As such, I purchased mine through a third party, ticket.com. Currently, bookings open 45 days before departure. The website charges a small commission, around AU$2.5. I was able to select a seat, and the whole process was straightforward. After making the payment, they will send you a barcode. They have a mobile app where you can check your bookings. On the day of travel, you must head to one of these kiosks and scan the barcode to print out the ticket. To access the platforms, you can either present the staff with the ticket and a photo ID, or you can enter by scanning your face. The new technology doesn’t seem to be widely embraced by locals yet. Once you’re inside, you’ll find toilets and prayer rooms. And on the second floor, there are more convenience stores. The station has four platforms, and my train will depart from platform two this morning. Based on my observation, it appears that most long-distance trains departing from Gambir are hauled by this type of locomotive: The GE CM20EMP is a double-cabin, diesel-electric locomotive introduced in 2013. The engines and bodies are manufactured by General Electric in the United States, while the bogies were built locally in Indonesia. They are now the workhorses of the Indonesian Railways. Here comes the 8:20 am Argo Bromo Anggrek! It arrived just 15 minutes before departure. As expected, the locomotive is the GE CM20EMP, followed by a power van, a single executive luxury sleeper carriage and nine executive class carriages with a dining car in the middle. Notably, this stands as the most opulent non-tourist train in Indonesia, there’s no business or economy class onboard. The executive carriage looks like this. There are two toilets at the rear, one for males and one for females. The seats are arranged in a 2-2 configuration and are rotatable, allowing them to face the direction of travel. Under the windows, there are European-type power plugs, and the seats can recline by about 30 degrees. The legroom is quite generous. Welcome to the executive luxury class. There’s a dedicated train attendant who warmly greets everyone on board. The seats are in a 1-1 configuration, with nine on each side. They resemble the reverse herringbone business class seats found on planes. Since the seats are not rotatable, half of them do not face the direction of travel. I chose seat 4A, which does indeed face forward. While Indonesia used to have trains with proper sleepers, they were all retired in 1995. Therefore, this is the finest bed you can find on an Indonesian train today. No matter which class you travel in, the luggage allowance is strictly 20kg per person, and there’s a good reason for it. The carriage lacks luggage storage space, you can only place large bags either behind the last row of seats or on the overhead luggage racks. We departed Gambir Station right on the dot. The Argo Bromo Anggrek is the fastest train between Jakarta and Surabaya. It only makes four stops in between, covering a distance of 725 km in 8 hours and 5 minutes. Other trains typically take up to 10-15 hours for the same route. Our next stop is over 2 hours away. The dedicated executive luxury class attendant just served everyone a glass of apple juice. This is Manggarai Station. It currently serves as an interchange station between Jakarta’s two commuter lines and the Soekarno-Hatta Airport Rail Link. As you can see, part of the station is still under construction. Once completed in 2025, the fully expanded multi-level Manggarai Station will become Indonesia’s largest station, replacing Gambir as the terminus for long-distance trains. Around 35 minutes after our departure, we arrived at Cikarang, located on the outskirts of Greater Jakarta. It’s the terminus of the Cikarang Loop Line commuter trains and is the end of the electrified rail line. From this point onward, I will be able to enjoy the lush greenery of the Javanese countryside. Introduced in 2018, the Executive luxury class is a relatively new experience in Indonesia. Let’s take a closer look at the seat’s features. At the front, there’s a small Android-based entertainment screen. Beneath the foot nook, there’s a blanket. This space is large enough to store a small bag. Within easy reach, there’s a small rubbish bin. The left armrest is equipped with a built-in cup holder, and there’s an additional storage area that’s perfect for a laptop or magazines. The seat is upholstered in leather, and a movable headrest adds to the comfort. Adjacent to my seat, there’s a lockable small compartment featuring a mirror and a USB port inside. It’s designed for storing valuable personal items, unfortunately, keys were not provided to lock it. There’s another power plug and USB port below this compartment. Noise-cancelling headphones are supplied for use with the entertainment screen, and an eye-mask is available for those who wish to nap. A built-in control panel is situated on the right armrest, featuring buttons for adjusting the seat, a remote control for the TV screen, a crew call button, and a switch for the reading light. A tray table is stored inside the armrest. This video was filmed on 31 May 2023, when masks were still mandatory on all public transport across Indonesia. Thankfully the government has now relaxed the mask rules. Although there isn’t a blackout curtain to completely block out daylight, there’s a semi-transparent blind to help filter out the sun. The Wi-Fi sticker on the window frame is hard to miss. For the review, I decided to give the Wi-Fi a try. However, it didn’t work on my first attempt. The entertainment screen is also Wi-Fi enabled. But that didn’t work either. The screen is a touch screen and provides several language options. Let’s take a look at the movie collection. Surprisingly, there’s quite a diverse selection of movies available, far more than I expected. Aside from movies, there are games, music, live TV and radio. The map icon displays the train’s current location, but the screen seems to struggle to load it. The map likely requires an internet connection to load. Lastly, I came across a food menu. Given that the train has a dining car, I assume this menu displays what’s available for purchase on board. The tenderloin steak looks particularly delicious! About an hour after departing Gambir, a complimentary breakfast was served,  accompanied by a choice of tea or coffee. The meal was presented in a paper box and included bread, a bottle of water, a mango pudding, a pack prawn crackers, some fried rice, a piece of chicken, and a fried egg. The portion size was notably generous. Fried rice is called “Nasi Goreng” in Indonesia. The rice is flavoured with sweet soy sauce and mixed with sambal, giving it a spicy taste. I enjoyed it. The cutlery pack only contains a spoon and a fork, making cutting through the chicken with them impossible. Although the meat was cold and dry, it had been marinated with a blend of aromatic spices and seasonings, it tasted really good. Overall I enjoyed my breakfast. If it had been plated on fine bone china and provided with metal cutlery, I would say it is of the same quality as an airline business class meal. I decided to give the Wi-Fi another try. This time, the login page appeared, and after providing my email and signing in, I finally managed to connect to the internet. The Wi-Fi speed was pretty fast. My Facebook feed refreshed instantly, and I could watch YouTube videos without interruptions. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Cirebon Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Cirebon Station, Please prepare yourself, check you luggage and belongings, make sure that nothing is left behind. For your safety, it is forbidden to open the train door, before the train completely stops. Thank you for choosing train services from Indonesian Railway Company. See you on your next trip! We have arrived at our first stop, Cirebon. The train only stops here briefly. Therefore there’s no time to get out and stretch your legs. Cirebon is the sole coastal city in West Java, situated just 40 kilometres from the provincial border with Central Java. As a result, the city’s history has been shaped by the influences of both Javanese and Sundanese cultures, resulting in a diverse and vibrant cultural landscape. Let’s take a look at the toilet in the executive luxury class. Due to the fewer number of passengers, there’s only one unisex toilet in this carriage. It’s very spacious and remarkably clean. It’s fully equipped with essentials, including toilet paper, hand wash, and paper towels. I like the water plant decoration. Behind the mirrors, there’s a window that keeps the area ventilated. With not much else to do, I decided to lie down for a while. After playing around with the control buttons, I finally managed to adjust the seat to a 170-degree position, which is nearly fully flat. Even though Indonesia is located right on the equator and doesn’t experience winter, the provided blanket is a welcome addition as the air conditioning can get a bit chilly. Being 6’1” or 186 cm tall, the bed is just long enough for me to stretch out fully. While it would be even better if they provided a pillow, the bed is comfortable enough for an 8-hour journey, whether it’s during the daytime or nighttime. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Pekalongan Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Pekalongan Station, please prepare yourself... The train maintains a speed between 90 - 120 km/h for most of the journey, swiftly passing through numerous small towns. Around halfway through the trip, near Plabuan Station, the train briefly runs right next to the coastline, providing a stunning view of the ocean. Semarang, the largest city in Central Java, has an estimated population of over 1.6 million. It is an important regional centre, acting as the primary hub between Jakarta and Surabaya. Opened in 1868, Semarang Tawang Station is the oldest major railway station in Indonesia still in operation. Nearly all trains that go through the North Java line stop at this station. During our 5-minute stop, you can see workers using this valuable time to perform some work on my carriage’s roof. Since I received a delicious breakfast in the morning, I assumed that lunch would be included in my ticket as well. However, it’s now 1:40 pm, and I just saw the train staff coming through the aisles selling snacks and drinks. I guess I’ll have to arrange my own lunch then. Let’s visit the lounge car and see if I can get the steak. After walking through several executive class carriages, I reached the dining car located in the middle of the train. The kitchen takes up half of the space in this carriage, and the other half is a dining area with face-to-face seats. There are power plugs under the tables. Alright, the menu is different from what I saw, there’s no steak available. Instead, they offer a variety of hot Indonesian dishes. The pictures of the dishes look quite appetising. In addition to the meals, there are many snacks and drinks. Indonesia is largely a Muslim country. Alcohol is not served on board. I expected the hot meal to be of the same quality as my breakfast. I ordered a Nasi Rendang Padang for 40,000 Indonesian rupiahs and coconut water for 15,000 rupiahs. The prices are very affordable. Here it comes! The packaging isn’t the same as breakfast, but the picture on the lid still looks quite appealing. After opening it up, it turns out the meal is not freshly cooked. The meal weighs 346 grams, the rice is wrapped in paper, and all the other ingredients are prepackaged. There are spicy potatoes, a piece of beef, some chilli paste, and green vegetables. “Nasi” means rice in Indonesian, and “Rendang Padang” is an authentic style of slow-cooked beef stew that originates from the Padang region. The chilli paste is a nice addition to mix with the rice. Once again, cutting through the beef with just a spoon was quite challenging. Personally, I think this is a disgrace to Padang: the beef tastes like a piece of jerky, it’s really dry and hard to chew. Unfortunately, the dehydrated green vegetables are tasteless and inedible. Overall, I came to the dining car with high expectations but left feeling greatly disappointed. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Bojonegoro Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Bojonegoro Station, please prepare yourself... So that was the last stop we made before reaching Surabaya. Here are my thoughts about this trip. First, let’s talk about the things I liked: the train was punctual, it departed Jakarta on time and arrived in Surabaya a few minutes early. The seat is comfortable, and is equipped with all the amenities I needed. Furthermore, I was never tired of the scenery, no matter when I looked outside, it was always beautiful. Before arriving in Surabaya, the carriage attendant handed me a hot towel to freshen up. And the things I don’t like: the staff served an excellent breakfast in the first hour of the journey, but then there’s nothing else for the remaining 7 hours—no food, no snacks, and not even a drink. I paid 1,145,000 Indonesian rupiahs for this trip, that is almost 50% more than the price of a 90-minute economy-class flight between Jakarta and Surabaya. I wish they could offer a proper lunch meal to the luxury sleeper passengers. The tracks on this line are narrow gauge and old, making the ride very bumpy. Additionally, on the journey from Jakarta to Surabaya, the sleeper carriage is at the front, and the train driver frequently honks the horn. Overall, I would rate this trip 7/10. Surabaya is the capital of East Java and the second-largest city in Indonesia. While this city might not be widely recognised by international tourists, it holds a significant place in the hearts of Indonesians as the “City of Heroes.” The Heroes Monument in the city centre stands as a prominent landmark, commemorating the Battle of Surabaya and honouring the bravery, resilience, and sacrifice of the city’s inhabitants during Indonesia’s struggle for independence in the late 1940s. Surabaya has two major railway stations, both situated in the heart of the city. The Argo Bromo Anggrek terminates at Surabaya Pasarturi Station, which serves as the final stop for all trains arriving from the northern and western parts of Java. Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more train and flight reviews. See you all in my next video!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Bangkok. Today, I’ll be flying in Emirates A380 First Class to Hong Kong. That’s right, you didn’t hear me wrong.  Emirates does have fifth freedom rights between these two cities. And this is one of the most affordable ways to experience one of the world’s best first-class products. Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, is a city that blends ancient traditions with modern wonders. Nestled along the Chao Phraya River, it entices visitors with its bustling markets, ornate temples, and dynamic cityscape. Emirates provides a complimentary chauffeur service to eligible business and first-class passengers. Sadly, my ticket was not qualified. The most convenient public transport option to reach Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport is the Airport Rail Link. Starting from Phaya Thai station, the fare is 45 baht for an 8-stop journey, and it takes just 30 minutes to reach the airport. The train operates from approximately 6:00 am to midnight daily. Emirates uses check-in bay U at Suvarnabhumi. As of August 2023, the airline operates five daily flights to and from Dubai, one of which continues to Hong Kong. There are four separate check-in lanes, and the signs are fairly self-explanatory. Check-in for my Emirates flight opened precisely 3.5 hours before departure, not a minute early. First Class passengers receive absolute priority. Despite the long lines in other queues, I was the first to be checked in. After getting your boarding pass, eligible passengers can use the express path for immigration and security. I got through in no time. Upon clearing security, you’ll be welcomed by various duty-free shops. And there are many signs to help you find the boarding gates and lounges. Most shops are on level 4, while the lounges and boarding gates are on level 3. The Emirates lounge is located in Concourse G, opposite the Cathay Pacific lounge. Qantas is a partner with Emirates. Unfortunately, there’s no dedicated Emirates First Class lounge outside Dubai. As such, this lounge can be used by both Qantas and Emirates gold and platinum members and business and first-class passengers flying with either airline. Wow, the cleaning robot is so cool! It knows how to avoid my feet! The lounge has a long rectangular layout. As you enter, you’ll find the business centre on the left, equipped with workstations, a TV, and a self-service bar. On the right is the main dining area. Towards the end of the lounge, there are toilets. The overall colour tone and decoration resonate with the lounges across the Emirates network, with towels neatly rolled and stacked in a pyramid shape. And of course, showers are available as well. In front of the main buffet table is an eye-catching buffet dome, which serves pre-plated desserts, appetisers, salads, dips, cheeses, and juices. They are all beautifully presented to the fine-dining quality. I’m not a wine expert, here are all the alcohol options available. This lounge lacks a proper bar with a bartender, so you’ll have to pour your own wine and mix your own drink. As for the food, although there’s no a la carte dining, I believe that Emirates provides the best lounge buffet worldwide. They offer a diverse selection of Middle-eastern, western, and local dishes crafted with premium ingredients. The lounge chairs are all covered in leather, with most having universal power plugs and USB ports installed next to them. You will not see any planes outside the windows because the Cathay Pacific lounge, located opposite ours, has taken all the apron views. For the purpose of this review, I decided to sample a bit of every hot dish. In general, I am thoroughly impressed with the variety and quality of the food here. Premium proteins such as salmon, duck, and tuna are not always found in an airline’s business lounge. Boarding for the flight typically starts around 45 minutes before departure. Emirates encourages its first-class passengers to relax in the lounge until just 10 minutes before the gate closes. However, I prefer to unwind in my Private First Class suite, so I arrived at the gate early. The A380 aircraft flying me to Hong Kong today is in a special livery dedicated to Dubai’s newest architectural icon, Museum of the Future. The ring-shaped Arabic calligraphy-encapsulated building encircles both sides of the aircraft, featuring the message “Journey to the future” across the fuselage. There are 10 A380 aircraft painted in this livery. Following the retirement of most passenger B747s around the globe, the A380 has become one of the most easily recognisable aircraft to the general public. Wherever it goes, it always draws lots of attention. Emirates currently has 116 A380s in service, with seven different seating configurations. Most of these aircraft have three classes, while some have just economy and business, and the newer and refurbished ones offer four classes. The capacities range from 484 to 615 seats. This particular aircraft is the three-class mid-range version. The entire lower deck is fitted with economy class seats in a 3-4-3 configuration. Moving upstairs, the first-class section takes up the whole space before the upper deck door 1. The suites are in a 1-2-1 configuration, with four rows along the windows and three rows in the middle, totalling 14 seats. The privacy divider between the middle seats can be lowered if you’re travelling with a companion. There are no overhead storage bins, but you can store your suitcase or bags on the floor. I’ll show you later. Although I’ve seen numerous pictures and videos of this product online, experiencing it firsthand feels totally different, I’m incredibly excited about this flight. As soon as I settled in, I was warmly greeted by the crew, and I asked for a glass of champagne as my pre-departure drink. I noticed that they poured me a glass of Moët, which is typically served in business class. But don’t worry, the superior Dom Pérignon will be available after takeoff. Moments later, I was served some dates and Arabic coffee, followed by an onboard menu with a wine list, and a fresh towel. I am a huge fan of the A380 aircraft. I was lucky enough to visit the A380 assembly line in Toulouse in 2019. However, I don’t like how thick the wall is between the inner window and the outer window on the upper deck. This significantly limits my view outside the window. Suvarnabhumi Airport currently has two active runways, and this afternoon, we will be taking off from runway 19R. On the other hand, the thick windows have contributed to a quieter onboard environment, making it the quietest aircraft I’ve ever flown on. Now, let’s take a detailed look at my first-class suite. Each suite has sliding doors that can be closed after takeoff, ensuring great privacy. The suite has a luxurious feel with its walnut veneer and gold trim. There’s a mini wardrobe next to the doors. The front of the suite is fitted with a massive entertainment screen, a lamp, a light, and a built-in lighted makeup mirror that can be tilted open or closed. When open, you’ll find an amenity pack from Byredo. Since this is a short flight, no other amenity kits or pyjamas were provided. In the drawer, there’s a notebook and pen that you can take home with you if you wish. As there are no overhead bins in first class, you can place your bags on the floor, beneath the TV screen. The space is big enough to fit a carry-on suitcase. Underneath the table, there’s a magazine holder where the headphones are stored. There’s a universal power plug under the lamp, with two USB ports just below that. The coolest feature of this suite, aside from the sliding door, is this built-in mini-bar next to the armrest. With a simple push of a button, you have quick access to water and some soft drinks. However, as the mini-bar is not refrigerated, I still had to request ice from the crew. The other button here is for taking out the tray table. This is certainly the largest tray-table I’ve seen on a plane. Very stable too. Pretty much everything in this suite can be controlled via physical buttons or touch screens. The window blinds have two layers, and the buttons allow you to manage all three windows together or separately. Even the lamp has three brightness levels! Above those buttons is a tablet that can be used to adjust the seat, the lights, and the sliding doors. It also serves as a mini entertainment screen where you can check the flight path or browse the movie options. Furthermore, there’s another remote control inside the armrest. In terms of storage space, there’s a compartment here for small items. A blanket and mattress pad are stored here. The seat has a width of 23 inches, which is on the narrower side, but it was comfortable enough for me. I’m sitting on a large, firm pillow, and on the other side of the seat, there’s a reading light and an air vent. Both armrests can be opened up, and each has a small tray perfect for storing items such as glasses, rings and a watch. In addition to a private suite, first-class passengers have the privilege to use the “Shower in the Sky". Emirates was the first commercial airline in the world to have showers on board. The two spacious bathrooms are located at the front of the upper deck. Each bathroom has under-floor heating. It’s so spacious inside. There’s a TV screen showing the flight information. Fresh towels are prepared, along with various toiletries and a huge selection of products from VOYA. And there’s a full-sized sink with hand towels, VOYA hand wash, body lotion, and Bvlgari fragrances. And here is the shower! Each passenger gets up to five minutes of water. The indicator on the wall shows you how much water you have left. The water pressure is quite good! The shower is certainly a bonus to the Emirates A380 first-class experience, especially during long-haul flights. Behind the first-class section, the rest of the upper deck is fitted with business-class seats. They are in a staggered 1-2-1 configuration, each with a pitch of 48 inches and a width of 18.5 inches. All of them are lie-flat seats, and as you can see, there are overhead bins above each seat. No trip on the Emirates A380 is complete without visiting the iconic in-flight bar. It’s at the back of the upper deck and is reserved for business and first-class passengers. There’s a dedicated crew member serving as a bartender, ready to make any drink you desire. Additionally, you can find some sandwiches and other snacks for nibbling.  There’s also a large TV displaying the progress of the flight. Seeing that I was filming, the crew offered to take a photo of me standing inside the bar. Emirates is definitely one of the most camera-friendly airlines in the world, the crew goes above and beyond to maximise my in-flight experience. Returning to my seat, it’s time for lunch. The menu is put inside a leather binder. Emirates offers a dine-on-demand concept in first class, so you can eat whatever is on the menu whenever you want. As this is a short flight, the meal consists of only three courses, excluding canapés and the signature caviar service. This is reasonable, considering how little I paid compared to other Emirates First class flights. The drink list includes a wide selection of alcoholic beverages, teas, coffees, juices, and soft drinks. And there’s a separate wine list with some of the most expensive beverages on a commercial airline. For instance, the 2013 Dom Pérignon, served exclusively on Emirates, retails for AU$400 per bottle in Australia. To start, since Caviar is not available, I picked the other popular dish: Arabic Mezze. The presentation looks terrific, resembling a restaurant in the air. The mezze refers to a selection of small and flavourful dishes commonly served before a main meal in the middle east, shared among families and friends. The mezze on Emirates includes three cold spreads, some cold dishes, and some hot items. Overall, it was a sensational and filling appetiser that showcased the best of the local cuisine. I totally enjoyed it! Shortly after finishing, the crew cleared my plates and immediately served my main course. The beef tenderloin dish looks simple: steak, sauce, steamed asparagus, potato gratin, and some garnish. For safety reasons, there’s no steak knife on board. As the steak was prepared in the central kitchen on the ground, and the crew only had to reheat it, I couldn’t select how I wanted it to be cooked. However, they did it perfectly. They used an excellent cut of steak, it was cooked to medium,  and cutting it with a regular knife was effortless. It was still tender and juicy, and the sauce was lovely. Since I had already enjoyed two very filling dishes, I opted for some fresh-cut fruits for dessert. In general, Emirates’ first-class dining experience was sensational. I loved the large tray table, the private sliding doors, the convenience of watching a movie while eating, and the easy access to water in the mini-bar when thirsty. Time in first class flies by quickly. We are now only 60 minutes away from touching down. The TV screen is 29 inches in size. It’s huge. Emirates’ ICE entertainment system is one of the best in the world. Through the Information panel, you can view the flight path. There are three exterior cameras on the A380, which provide outside views from different angles. The Communication section mainly shows you how to connect to Wi-Fi. Sadly, due to a problem with the satellite, the Wi-Fi wasn’t available for the whole flight. As for entertainment, Emirates offers up to 6,500 channels of movies, TV shows, music, and games. The library is updated every month. Look at how many genres it has for its movie collection. Of course, leaning forward to touch the main screen is not always comfortable, especially when lying down. That’s why Emirates provides another 9-inch tablet and a remote to control the screen. You can select the movie you want to watch on the tablet, and the main screen will start the show right away.  The Emirates First Class headphones are manufactured by Bowers & Wilkins. They are very comfortable to wear.  And I must say, these are the best noise-cancelling headphones I’ve ever used. I decided to lie down for a bit, and the crew offered to make the bed for me. Very good afternoon ladies and gentlemen, this is the captain speaking. We are gonna commence our gradual descent toward Hong Kong International Airport in about 7 minutes from now, Estimated time of arrival will be after 35-45 minutes from now. This is pretty much a full-sized single bed, there’s no narrow foot nook at the front, and you don’t have to sleep sideways like on many business-class seats. Even when lying down, the tablet is still within easy reach.  The bed is 78 inches or 198 cm long. There’s plenty of space between my head and the wall. Unfortunately, there’s no time for a nap as it’s time to return to planet Earth. The plane has started its descent into Hong Kong. Just before the seatbelt sign was turned on, the crew handed out some fine luxury chocolates. This flight has been truly eye-opening for me, it’s my first time flying in first class, seeing a bar in the sky and a shower on the plane. Although it has been 15 years since this product was first revealed, and other airlines like Singapore and Etihad now have even bigger suites on their A380s, flying on the Emirates A380 first class is still a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Of course, flying first class usually comes with a very high price tag. The two most affordable routes you can take are between Bangkok and Hong Kong and Sydney and Christchurch. I paid just over AU$900 for this flight, and I believe this is the cheapest Emirates A380 first-class flight across its entire network, without using points. Welcome to Hong Kong! If you’re staying on Hong Kong Island, the quickest way to get there is by catching the Airport Express Train. It runs from roughly 5:50 am to 12:48 am daily, and it takes just 24 minutes to reach Central Station. The ticket is more expensive than the buses, costing HK$115 each way, but the journey is smoother, and the train is less crowded. There’s dedicated luggage space in each carriage. Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews! See you all in my next video!

captions.text: Tonight, I am going to travel on the newly launched overnight train from Riyadh to Qurayyat.
Once inside, there’s a small waiting room with beam seating, with UK-type power sockets and USB ports under each seat.
The seats are in a 1-2 configuration with a comfortable pitch of 47 inches.
Since I am travelling alone, the upper berths were not lowered.
These reclining seats are exceptionally comfortable and spacious, with a pitch of 47 inches.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has a relatively young history of passenger railways. Tonight, I am going to travel on the newly launched overnight train from Riyadh to Qurayyat. I expect the private sleeper cabins to be modern, clean, and comfortable. I’m excited to try them out. Let’s go! The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, situated on the Arabian Peninsula in the Middle East, is the birthplace of Islam. Riyadh is the country’s capital and largest city, with a population of over 7 million. Before 2018, Saudi Arabia only allowed foreign individuals visiting for specific purposes to visit the country, such as religious pilgrimages or business-related matters. With an E-Tourist visa being introduced for the first time in 2019, citizens of many nations can now visit this mysterious country purely for tourism purposes. I am very excited about this trip. Modern railways were first introduced in Saudi Arabia after World War II to mainly facilitate oil transport. Passenger rails only became popular in recent years. Currently, there are three passenger train lines in the kingdom. The Riyadh to Dammam line was opened in 1981, connecting the capital with the port city of Dammam. The Haramiah high-speed railway, opened in 2018, connects Jeddah with the holy cities of Medina and Mecca. And finally, tonight I’ll be travelling on the 1,242 km long North-South line, connecting the capital to the border with Jordan. The first service from Riyadh to Qurrayyat commenced in 2022. Riyadh has two railway stations. Trains to Dammam leave from Riyadh East Station, while the newly-built Riyadh North Station is the departure point for services heading to Qurayyat. Located approximately 30 kilometres from the city centre, this new station lacks public transport options. I had to catch an Uber to get here. The station resembles an airport terminal, with the entry for departures on the left and the exit for arrivals on the right. Once inside, you can easily navigate by following the bilingual signage. Train tickets can be booked at the station, over the phone, and online via Saudi Arabia Railways’ official website or mobile app. Sales typically commence 40 days in advance. On the train to Qurayyat, there are three travel classes available. Similar to catching a flight, passengers can check-in their suitcases. The allowance for Economy class passengers is one piece of 25kg luggage, while for business and private cabin passengers are 32kg. The counter closes 20 minutes before departure. If you happen to arrive at the station too early, you’ll find several cafes and restaurants. As the boarding time approaches, passengers can proceed to the waiting room through the ticket-checking counters. There is a priority lane for business and private cabin passengers. Once inside, there’s a small waiting room with beam seating, with UK-type power sockets and USB ports under each seat. Business and private cabin passengers can use this lounge while waiting for boarding. I’m not sure what time they open, but when I arrived here 90 minutes before my departure, I was able to enter. The lounge has some sofas, armchairs, and dining tables. Since I arrived early, I had the entire lounge to myself, but it filled up quickly. The lounge offers a range of complimentary treats, including pastries, fruits, dates, tea, Arabic coffee, and bottled water. In addition, you can make yourself a cup of cappuccino using the coffee machine. When it’s time for boarding, the staff will open the door that directly connects the lounge to the platform. Interestingly, rather than granting priority boarding, economy class passengers get to board first. I guess the concept behind this approach is to allow us to relax in the lounge until the boarding chaos outside subsides. It’s probably not a bad idea. Riyadh North Station has two side platforms, and to access platform 2, we need to pass through a tunnel. The trains operating on this line were manufactured by CAF. Each set consists of push-pull locomotives located at both ends of the train, with up to 20 carriages in between. Tonight’s train has 13 carriages, including three economy class, one lounge car, one business class, three sleeping cars, and the remaining carriages are designed for cargo and vehicle transport. Since all the economy passengers are already on the train, for privacy reasons, I did not film the interior of the carriage. This is a picture from the operator’s official website. The seats are arranged in a 2-2 configuration, with a generous pitch of 37 inches. There’s a power socket under each seat. Separating the economy and business class carriages is a lounge car. And you can purchase food from this counter. To access the menu, simply scan the QR code wth your phone, and a PDF will pop up on your browser. Once again, due to the same reason, I refrained from filming the business class section. The seats are in a 1-2 configuration with a comfortable pitch of 47 inches. They are all reclinable, and meals are included in the ticket. These windowless carriages are car wagons that can take up to 20 vehicles. You can book the car transport service online. As I attempted to walk towards the front of the train, I was stopped by a staff member. Despite my efforts to explain what I do, I was not permitted to pass through. Unfortunately, this means I didn’t get footage of the locomotive. "Can I just take a photo of the train?" "It is not permitted." Welcome to the private cabin carriage. Shortly after settling in, the train began its journey. These trains are specially designed for Saudi Arabia, allowing them to operate efficiently even in extreme weather conditions of up to 55ºC. They can reach a maximum speed of 200km/h, which is quite impressive for a diesel-powered train of this length. Now, let’s have a look at the facilities on board. The train doors and the two toilets are in the middle, with four private cabins on either side of the carriage. The common areas of the train are all equipped with CCTV cameras. The toilet door can slide open, and dedicated cleaners regularly clean the toilets. While the space may be compact, they are equipped with all the standard facilities, including a mirror, sink, hand wash, paper towels, and a baby change table. This is my private cabin, it offers a sense of security with its lockable door and a peephole to check the hallway. Each private cabin has four beds, and the cost to book the cabin is 1,515 Saudi Riyal. The room cannot be shared with a stranger, meaning that even when travelling alone, I still had to pay for the entire cabin. The high ceiling and the absence of a luggage rack above the door make the room feel spacious. There’s a coat hook for each person, and the light switch and the train attendant call button are located here. Prior to boarding, the staff had already prepared the beds in each cabin, taking into account the number of occupants. Since I am travelling alone, the upper berths were not lowered. Adjacent to the bed, you will find a light switch, a reading light, a USB port, a universal power plug, and a small space for small personal belongings. Before being transformed into a bed, each lower berth can be used as two lounge seats, providing a comfortable space to relax. I particularly like the leather cover, as it not only adds a touch of elegance but is also easy to clean. The window is long and massive, providing a panoramic view during the day. Above the window, there is a TV screen displaying the route map. The red dot on the map indicates the approximate location of the train between stops, which is a brilliant feature. There is a USB port here. And you have the option to mute the onboard announcements, which can get annoying after some time. There is a window blind to block the outside light completely. The table is fairly large, and on either side of it, you will find a power socket and a USB port. Lastly, there is ample space beneath each lower berth to store a carry-on bag. My impression of this cabin is that it is absolutely modern and clean. Charging ports are everywhere. Although the train has no shower, I didn’t find it to be an issue. After departing from Riyadh, there are only five stations along this entire 1200km line. The first station, Majmmah, approached quickly. This is train No. 39, which operates from Qassim to Riyadh. It’s in a standard 9-car configuration as it doesn’t have car wagons or private cabins. During the stop at Majmmah, the attendant came to each cabin and offered a meal for dinner. Despite having paid for the entire cabin, the number of meals served is based on the number of occupants. The three-course dinner consists of a salad, a hot meal, and dessert, all served in single-use plastic containers. This dish looks like butter chicken. It features a generous amount of succulent chicken pieces immersed in a flavourful and mildly spiced sauce, complemented by potatoes, carrots and green beans. For individuals with dietary requirements, it is possible to request a special meal when booking the train ticket. Although it may seem unusual to have such a substantial meal at 10:30 pm, I must admit that it was delicious. Before heading to bed, I decided to take a quick look at the lounge car. Surprisingly, there were no passengers present, only a few staff members relaxing on their phones. There are lots of bottled water on each table that are free for everyone to grab. And this is the menu of the cafe. It primarily caters to economy-class passengers. There is a good selection of snacks and drinks at reasonable prices. The train is scheduled to arrive at 8:25 in the morning. It’s time for me to get some rest. Each bed is provided with a thin blanket. The mattress is thick, and the pillow is made of memory foam. It feels quite comfortable. The bed is a bit narrow and only just fits my entire body. But it should be sufficient for a night of rest. Good night! I had a restful five-hour sleep, only to be awakened by a series of knocks on my cabin door at 4:25 am. To my surprise, it was time for breakfast. After doing some research online, I realised that this early timing can be attributed to the religious practice of Muslims, who are required to wake up before dawn for the morning prayer, which takes place around one to one and a half hours before sunrise. Inside the box, I found a bottle of water and apple juice, two bread rolls, and a hot meal. The staff also gave me a cup of Arabic coffee and some dates. The hot meal features a slice of green and red capsicum, scrambled eggs, and three boiled potato wedges seasoned with Arabic spices. Once again, the meal was very tasty, and I really appreciate the freshness of all the ingredients used both in this dish and my dinner. There are still three hours until Qurayyat, so I decided to go back to sleep. After another two hours, I am finally fully awake. This rail line is truly built through the desert. Everything looks so brown. As most passengers have disembarked at the last few stations, I now have the chance to show you the business class seats. The carriage is equipped with an accessible toilet. These reclining seats are exceptionally comfortable and spacious, with a pitch of 47 inches. Every seat has a universal power plug and a USB port. Each window has two blinds, allowing passengers to control the brightness of their own portion of the window. It’s a thoughtful design. The seats are not rotatable, so only half of them face the direction of travel. Overall, this was an enjoyable and unique journey. The train is modern, the private room is spacious, and the meals are delicious. However, it's worth noting that the temperature inside the cabin tends to be set quite low, possibly due to the cultural preference for wearing long sleeves in the Middle East. The provided blanket is thin. I'm glad that I brought a jacket with me. While the train does offer Wi-Fi, it didn't seem to work during my trip. The mobile coverage along the route can be inconsistent. As we travelled further north, I had to wait until the train arrived at a station to regain an internet connection. Qurayyat is currently only served by this train once a week. Hopefully, in the future, the Jordanian government could construct a direct rail link from here to Amman. Furthermore, I couldn't help but notice the striking similarity in the design of all the train stations on this line. From the interior to the exterior of the departures building, they all appear almost identical to Riyadh North Station. Qurayyat station is located 10 km from the city centre, and no public transport is available. Ride-share companies Uber and Careem both claim to operate in this area, but in reality, I couldn't find a driver using either of their apps. As a result, I had to negotiate a fare of 40 Saudi Riyals with a local driver to get me to the city. Qurayyat is a small city near the border with Jordan. The Al-Hadithah border crossing is just 30 km from the city centre. It is one of the largest and most important land crossings in Saudi Arabia, providing links to Jordan and indirectly to Syria, Lebanon and Türkiye. Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more train and flight reviews! See you all in my next video!

reviews.transcript_full: hello and welcome to Singapore today I'm going to fly in air India's Boeing 787 business class to Delhi also I've seen many mixed reviews about this airline online I believe some of them may have been exaggerated therefore I decided to book this flight and let's go and find out what Air India is really like poor is a vibrant and dynamic city state located in Southeast Asia renowned for its impressive Skyline adorned with futuristic skyscrapers this small island nation has emerged as a global economic Powerhouse so most economical way to get to Singapore Changi Airport from the city is to catch the MRT the MRT does not operate 24 7. it runs roughly between 5 30 a.m to midnight daily since my flight was scheduled for the early morning I decided to spend a night at the airport the Crown Plaza is definitely the top choice for an airport hotel it offers the convenience of being located within terminal 3. however it comes with a higher price tag with rooms typically costing around 350 Singapore dollars alternatively there is the option of your hotel air situated inside the Drew Changi Airport shopping complex this mall is famous for housing the world's tallest indoor waterfall and is directly connected to Terminal 1 with terminals 2 and 3 just a 10 minute walk away via a Footbridge check in for Utah air begins strictly at 3 pm if you happen to arrive earlier there is an additional fee of 10 Singapore dollars per hour for early check-in furthermore Utah Air does not offer luggage storage facilities you can store your bags at this place located on level 1 of the shopping center it opens 24 hours and the cost ranges from 10 to 15 Singapore dollars per piece despite the strict checking hours the hotel air offers a more budget-friendly option I paid 198 Singapore dollars for my stay this is what the premium Queen cabin looks like it spans 10 square meters in size and features a queen bed a TV a foldable work desk and a private shower behind the bed the room does not have any windows the bed known as the smart bed is adjustable and reclines to suit your preference overall the room provided everything I needed but I wouldn't recommend staying here for more than one night Air India operates from Terminal 2 at Changi Airport initially opened in 1991 this terminal underwent a complete shutdown and renovation of its departure Hall in May 2020 taking advantage of reduced passenger traffic during Covent in May 2022 Terminal 2 started reopening progressively India usually uses the counters in io-10 and check in should open three and a half hours before the departure time which in this case would be 450. however the staff didn't start accepting the bags until 520 therefore definitely don't come to the airport too early business class passengers and Star Alliance Gold members can use the priority line for checking the whole process proved to be rather slow the staff requested the PNR to locate my booking and along with document verification and tagging the luggage it took six minutes to finally receive my boarding pass being one of the best airports in the world once airside you'll find plenty of shops and restaurants to explore and there are plenty of signage throughout the terminal making it easy to navigate and locate your boarding gate the default Lounge for eligible Air India passengers is stats Premiere It's a Good Lounge but since Air India is a member of the Star Alliance passengers can access any of the Singapore Airlines lounges as well with a comfortable amount of time before boarding I decided to take the sky trying and head to terminal 3. inaugurated in 2008 Terminal 3 stands as Singapore's Aviation Jam this bustling terminal offers an impressive range of amenities featuring upscale boutiques tantalizing dining choices and captivating entertainment venues primarily utilized by Singapore Airlines terminal 3 is home to the flagship silvercrest Lounge in 2022 Singapore Airlines completed a 15 million Singapore dollars renovation project for its lounges at tableau 3. upon entering the shared Lounge entrance Star Alliance first class passengers and Singapore Airlines sweet passengers can access the first class lounge and private room on the left meanwhile All-Star Alliance business class passengers can use this business Lounge the business Lounge operates 24 hours a day and it is divided into two distinct sections to the right you'll find an eye-catching bar where you can indulge in a barista made coffee and alcoholic beverages are available throughout the day with the option to request custom cocktails from the skilled bartender or help yourself as a self-serve drink station the drink selection includes esteemed choices such as cognac ROMs vodka jeans and whiskey [Music] with continuing past the bar you'll discover a spacious open play area with different seating options [Music] alongside the upgraded amenities the renovated Lounge added a 30 increase in customer capacity despite the morning Rush the lounge managed the crowds efficiently if you turn left at the lounge entrance you'll find the well-appointed bathroom and shower facilities followed by the main dining area while the business class Lounge doesn't provide a la carte dining the buffet section showcases a wide selection of culinary Delights to cater to every taste within the Asian section there's an assortment of stained stumbles and stir-fried noodles as a dedicated Noodle Bar you can order a personalized laksa or me robust for those seeking Western Fair a selection of cereals yogurts fruits and sandwiches is available complemented by classic breakfast items like boiled and scrambled eggs sausages hash browns and crispy bacon one particular aspect that truly stands out is a self-born joint counter the beverages are meticulously maintained at their Optimum temperatures with champagne kept cool beneath a blanket of ice white wine chilled at a precise 6 degrees Celsius and red wine served as a comfortable 16 degrees even the beer glasses are stored in the fridge ensuring a refreshing and crisp drinking experience in addition to alcoholic options they are juices and soft drinks for tea lovers this is a dedicated station with tea bags and cups and they are numerous DIY coffee machines overall the dining experience at the lounge is undeniably delightful the staff exude warm hospitality and a dedicated team of attentive waiters ensures that tables are promptly cleaned without a doubt this ranks at the finest business class Lounge I have ever visited apologies for attending the India review into a Singapore Lounge review returning to Terminal 2 security screening and document checks are conducted at the boarding gate unfortunately there was only a single long line at my gate with no priority given to business class passengers it took some time to clear security however boarding commands punctually uh Air India currently operates two direct flights to Delhi daily the morning flight is operated by a Boeing 787-8 while the late night departure utilizes an A320 Neo [Music] welcome aboard air India's Boeing 787s are in a two class layout at the front are three rows of business class seats in the 222 configuration followed by 238 economy class seats in the 333 configuration these type of seats were introduced in 2012 and appear somewhat stated the good news is that hey India will start refurbishing them in 2024 promising a more modern travel experience the overhead beings are massive [Music] this morning's business class cabin is rather quiet with only six passengers luckily I have the entire last row to myself shortly after I settled into the seat the cabin crew offered me a bottle of water followed by a hot or cold Tower and a welcome drink with a tray of orange juice or champagne continuing their attentive service the crew kindly inquired if anyone desired Indian newspapers or magazines and to my surprise they were all published today the seat had an ample width of 22 inches and a generous pitch of 74 inches ensuring plenty of legroom the whole plane was pushed back on time Changi Airport is expanding the new Terminal 5 that's currently under construction is said to surpass the combined size of all four existing terminals as for our flight this morning we will depart from Runway zero to right the taxi to reach this Runway took a good 20 minutes [Music] after the seat belt sign was turned off the crew set all the electric dimmable Windows to a semi-dark mode however I was pleased to discover that they did not completely lock the windows allowing passengers to retain full control over the brightness level let's now take a closer look at the features of these seats adjacent to the entertainment screen there's a cold hook and a headphone holder just below the tv a large ottoman offers Ample Storage Space for small bags as well as housing the bedding a blanket and a pair of slippers the tray table is stored inside the central console and you can easily adjust the seats recline using this control panel additionally there's a button to raise the armrest creating a privacy barrier with a neighboring seat unfortunately on my side the button was broken [Music] beneath the armrest you'll find a small cup holder a remote control for the entertainment screen a USB port and a universal power socket all of which function properly each seat is equipped with an adjustable reading light and two pillows are provided to enhance overall comfort the tray table is large and rotatable allowing you to leave the seats and move around even during the mule service above each seat you'll find an additional reading light that can be turned on using the TV remote and an adjustable air vent [Music] before the plane took off the crew handed me a breakfast menu offering four main course options since I wasn't familiar with Indian cruising the cabin manager currently took the time to explain each choice to me in course I was offered a beverage of my choice and an assortment of pastries is this the most substantial meal we've ever witnessed in business class well it certainly is for me apart from the main course there is a croissant accompanied by a selection of spreads fresh fruits and a glass of berry smoothie for my beverage I opted for a cup of tea and the crew also offered me a cheese plate with it for my main dish I picked the Anda Masala porgi a popular Indian Street Food consisting of spicy scrambled eggs the eggs were cooked with a mixture of onions tomatoes green chilies and aromatic spices served alongside the dish were tomato chutney and spiced potato wedges the combination of flavors was absolutely delightful and I saved it every bite this massive breakfast on Air India left me thoroughly satisfied and it's safe to say that hunger is not something you'll ever experience on this Airline the entertainment screen in business class is 15.1 increasing size and it is controlled by the provided remote there is a modest range of Hollywood and Bollywood movies TV shows and games while this aircraft has no exterior camera you can still stay informed about the flight's progress by tracking the flight path through these interactive maps when it's time to get some rest each seat can be transformed into a fully flat bed measuring 74 inches or 188 centimeters in length [Music] the generous seat with and spacious ottoman made it very comfortable to relax and watch a movie while lying down the noise canceling headphones provided are basic but they do the job flight duration from Singapore to Delhi is just under 6 hours around halfway through the Journey while I was watching a movie The Crew approached me with a variety of movies next to enjoy with the cabin lights themed and the adjacent aisle seats are occupied the window seat provided a sense of complete privacy there are two lavatories dedicated to business class passengers and both are at the front of the cabin [Music] so one I visited was cling and stalked with essential amenities such as tissues paper cups and body lotion the time spent in business class always seems to fly by quickly as we Flew Over The Majestic Taj Mahal the plane commands this descent into Delhi Air India has exceeded my expectations perhaps the airline had undergone significant improvements since its privatization in 2022 the seeds and amenities provided were notably clean and well maintained the service throughout the flight was impeccable and as someone who values onboard dining I was thoroughly impressed by the quality and variety of food offered with nearly 500 new planes on order and ongoing Fleet refurbishments Air India is poised to become a strong competitor in the global Aviation Market after landing in Delhi I continued my journey to Muscat in Oman on air India's A320 Neo the service on that flight was once again excellent and the food was delicious the economy class fair for these two flights was 682 Singapore dollars while I paid 1038 Singapore dollars for the business class which I believe was a great deal welcome to Indira Gandhi International Airport the busiest airport in India in the 17th busiest in the world as of 2019. the airport has three active terminals with terminal 3 being used by all International and full-service domestic Airlines while serving as a hub for Air India the airline offers a relatively compact Lounge in Delhi the lounge caters to business class and Star Alliance Gold members with a separate section dedicated to first class passengers during peak hours finding an empty table can be challenging and the food selection is fairly average on a positive note I did not get daily belly after enjoying the in-flight and Lounge cuisine thank you so much for watching if you found this video interesting please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews see you all in my next video
