reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Istanbul, Turkey! We all know that Western Europe and East Asia are home to some of the fastest trains in the world! But did you know that Turkey is also building a high-speed rail network that will link up all its major cities? For my first train video filmed outside Australia, I decided to go somewhere that is less well-known, so today I’m going to travel on Turkey’s first high-speed train line from Istanbul to Ankara. Let’s go! Istanbul is Turkey’s financial centre. It has a population of over 15 million people, making it the most populous city in Europe. It’s also the world’s largest transcontinental city. The Bosphorus strait is considered the boundary between Europe and Asia, and Istanbul straddles both sides of it. Personally, what I love about this city are its history, the food and the friendly people. Being a city that connects Europe and Asia, Istanbul has been an important rail hub since the late 19th century. There were two major rail termini in the city. The one on the European side is Sirkeci Railway Station. You may not be familiar with this name, but I’m sure you’ve heard of a train called the Orient Express. The current terminal building was built in 1890 by the Oriental Railway, and Sirkeci was the train’s eastern terminus until 2009. Sirkeci Terminal had 4 platforms and 7 tracks, serving Istanbul commuter, Turkey regional and International trains to nearby European nations. Unfortunately, this famous station was closed to long-distance trains in 2013, and today, it is only used by Istanbul’s Marmaray commuter trains. The Turkish State Railways TCDD still has a ticket office at Sirkeci Terminal, but if you would like to catch the train from Istanbul to western Turkey and the rest of Europe, you now have to take the Marmaray to Halkalı station, which is over 27 km away. The rail terminus on the Asian side of Istanbul is Haydarpaşa station. It used to be the primary terminal for trains travelling to and from eastern Turkey and was the country’s busiest railway station. However, this historical station was closed in 2012, and its future remained unclear. Hopefully, it’ll be redeveloped as the terminus of the high-speed trains. At the moment, trains between Istanbul and the Anatolian region of Turkey, including my train to Ankara, depart from the nearby Söğütlüçeşme station. Söğütlüçeşme is located 1.46km east of Haydarpaşa. It has 4 platforms. Platforms 1 and 2 are used by the Marmaray, and platforms 3-4 are used as the temporary terminus of the long-distance trains. Purchasing a train ticket in Turkey is fairly straightforward. There are ticket counters at most major stations, or you can book online through the official Turkish State Railways website. Booking for most domestic trains opens 30 days before departure, and you can even select your seats. To catch the long-distance train at Söğütlüçeşme, you have to put your luggage through an X-ray machine. After that, the staff will check your ticket and your photo ID before you can take the escalators up to the platforms. My train is scheduled to depart at 9:15 am, and boarding commenced only 25 minutes before departure. If you arrive early, there’s a small waiting area with luggage lockers. The High-Speed Train in Turkey is called Yüksek Hızlı Tren, short for YHT. The trains currently come in two varieties. The first generation is TCDD HT65000. They were designed by CAF in Spain, based on the Renfe class 120 trains. They have a top operating speed of 250 km/h and typically run in a 6-car formation. The newer type of the YHT is TCDD HT80000, also known as Velaro TR. They were built by Siemens in Germany. Each set comes in an 8-car formation with a top speed of 300 km/h. Other than Turkey and Germany, the Velaro class can also be seen in Belgium, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Spain, China and Russia. My ride this morning is operated by an 8-car Velaro. Let’s hop onboard. Car 1 is the business class carriage. The seats are in a 1-2 configuration with a total of 15 rows. None of the seats is rotatable. Therefore, only half of them face the direction of travel. At the rear of each carriage, there is dedicated luggage space for large suitcases. The first half of car 2 has 3 business-class compartments.  Each has privacy screen doors, and each seat can rotate for around 45 degrees. These compartments are perfect for business travellers wishing to make phone calls and conduct a meeting or those travelling in a group of four. The second half of car 2 is fitted with standard economy class seats in a 2-2 configuration. Compared to only having 15 rows in business, a standard economy class carriage has 21 rows of economy seats. But the legroom still looks decent. Each seat is equipped with a large tray table, footrest, USB port, and there’s a power plug shared between two seats. Car 3 is a restaurant carriage, I must say this whole train looks modern and incredibly clean, I think I’m going to have a great time on this 4.5h journey to Ankara, and I’m looking forward to enjoying a hot meal in this restaurant car later. The rest of the train, from car 4 to car 8 are all fitted with economy-class seats. Car 4 has an office for the train guard and two accessible spaces. As most passengers were already onboard, I did not continue my filming in cars 5-8, but like I said, they all are just economy class seats. The first railway line from Istanbul to Ankara was opened in 1892. Trains can run on the existing tracks at a maximum speed of 160km/h. In order to allow the YHT to travel faster, the construction of a high-speed railway commenced in 2003. The line was opened in stages between 2009 and 2019. The tracks of the new line are primarily laid parallel to the existing railway, and they enabled the YHT to travel at 250km/h after passing Izmit. Let’s have a more detailed look at the business class seat. The 1-2 configuration made the carriage feel less crowded, and the train is quiet and smooth when in motion. The overhead TVs show the train’s speed and upcoming stations. The seat has a large foldable tray table,  a seat pocket, a footrest, a power plug under the seat in front, and two USB ports under your seat. In addition, the ergonomic cushion and the headrest have made the seat quite comfortable to sit in. There’s a personal entertainment screen hidden inside the armrest. Earphones are not provided so if you wish to watch a movie you’ll have to bring your own. The system is not the latest on the market, but it is a touchscreen with a lot to offer. There’s internet onboard, and I’ll get back to that later. If you tap the information section, you can find the train’s timetable, moving map and the live onboard camera. This is very cool. The news tab provides information on the weather forecast and headlines of the latest breaking news. In terms of entertainment, there are TV shows, music, e-books, and as you can see, there’s a great selection of movies to choose from. To access the internet, you have to put in the booking reference number on your train ticket and seat number. The internet is complimentary for business class passengers. I was expecting the screen to generate a password for me to connect my phone to the onboard wifi, turned out that the screen itself can become a web browser. The internet is fast enough for me to search things on Google, check out my Instagram feed and even watch a YouTube video. However, this also means that there’s no wifi on this train. The distance between Söğütlüçeşme and Ankara is 560km, if travelling at a speed of 250km/h, it shouldn’t have to take the YHT 4.5hrs to complete this journey right? The longer-than-expected journey time is because the 43 km line between Söğütlüçeşme and Gebze only has 3 tracks, two of them are used by the Marmaray and the YHT from both directions can only use a single track. And the reason for only having three tracks instead of four is that the areas around the line are heavily urbanised, building another track would require demolishing hundreds of properties. Furthermore, the speed limit is restricted to 120km/h. Approximately 40 minutes after our departure, the staff came over to offer business class passengers a complimentary snack box. There’s bread, a marble cake, a juice box and a small bottle of water. The portion is big enough for a morning snack but in my opinion, not enough for lunch. Well, again, I’m looking forward to checking out what food the restaurant car has to offer later. After passing Izmit, there are finally 4 tracks on the railway line, with the two northern tracks being mostly used by the YHT, After Köseköy, approximately 100 km from Istanbul, the remainder of the line to Ankara was newly built, and the train can finally run at 250 km/h. The Turkish state railways started modernising its entire fleet in the 1990s to stop losing market share to roads. Between 1993 and 2005, TCDD introduced over 300 brand-new TVS2000 railcars for its regional trains. Depending on the service you travel on, there are coach cars, dining cars, couchette cars, sleeping cars and generator cars. Although not as fast as the YHT, the TVS2000 are also very clean and comfortable to travel on. I'll show you more about them in my next video! Here’s a quick tour of the toilet, there’s one at the end of each carriage, it is clean and has plenty of space. Car 4 is equipped with an even bigger accessible toilet to accommodate passengers travelling in wheelchair. It’s almost lunchtime. Therefore I headed to the restaurant car, looking for a hot meal. Unfortunately, TCDD did not make good use of the kitchen. All they had were some cold snacks and drinks. The price seems reasonable but I think this is quite disappointing. I always love having a meal on the train while enjoying the ever-changing scenery outside. In the end, I only purchased a can of coke. We are now in Eskişehir. This junction station is one of the largest and busiest stations in Turkey. It is served by many intercity and regional trains as well as the YHT to Istanbul, Ankara and Karaman. Inaugurated in 2009, the 246 km line from here to Ankara was the first section of the Ankara - Istanbul high-speed railway to be constructed, and it’s the first high-speed rail line in the Middle East. Travelling at 250 km/h, Ankara is not too far away. Overall I enjoyed this trip. The YHT have reduced travel time between Istanbul and Ankara from 7.5-11hrs to 4.5hrs. The tickets are affordable, and the service is popular among locals. I love how comfortable and smooth the Velaro train is, and the scenery outside is beautiful. My only disappointment is being unable to enjoy a hot meal in the dining car. In addition, the train staff don’t speak much English, but they’re friendly. I find it helpful to have google translate opened on my phone when communicating with them. Welcome to Ankara, the capital and the second-largest city in Turkey. Since opening the first high-speed railway in 2009, Ankara has become the main hub for the YHT. This building built above the YHT platforms was opened in 2016, containing an information desk, ticket offices, waiting rooms and a VIP lounge. You'll learn more about this station in my next video. Thank you so much for watching! If you find this video interesting or helpful, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more train and flight reviews. See you all in my next video!

reviews.transcript_full: Hey all, here OS reviews. During the holiday season, I did a little bit of traveling. For the first time, I tried a carrier called Iceland Air connecting over to Europe. And that's because Iceland Air offered some discounts that made it one of the more cost effective options to get from the US to Europe. oftent times with roundtrip tickets, that is getting there and then getting back costing around $300 to $400 USD, which is considered quite good for international travel on a flight that takes around 7 hours give and take. And so I was actually quite surprised because this was an economy ticket. But I found myself staring at a pretty recently renovated screen in front of me when sitting down. And that's because later on I discovered that Iceland Air actually partnered with Panasonic to kind of refurbish their planes which are based on the Airbus A321 Neo long flight with the newer Panasonic Estroa in-flight entertainment system. They now have 13in 4K OLED displays for accessing videos that you can watch, playing back some mini games, listening to music to help the time pass by a little bit more quickly. It actually felt very modern because of the inky vibrant contrast of the OLED panels as well as having a matte layer on top of the display to further reduce glare and reflections coupled with relatively slim bezels on the side of the screen just made the entire experience. The content seemed to fill up even more space. And all of this was flanked by an LED light strip beneath the display itself, which can be further tilted up and down to give you some more adjustability depending on how far back you want to recline the seat. So, these large 4K HDR certified OLED panels are not only extremely sharp, but furthermore, if you are in business class, it comes with an even larger 16-in panel, but again, across the board, they are all 4K resolution OLED displays. Now, I have a couple of thoughts around this. I wanted to briefly point out and that is of course OLED and AMOLED displays have a potential or higher likelihood of burn-in over time. That is if it's sitting on a static image like this for example hours and hours on a higher brightness level there can be some ghosting or residue image left on there which is typically not found on LCD screens despite those having inferior contrast. reviews.transcript_full: There are often a few things we can enjoy to pass the time while crossing the world at subsonic speeds over 30,000 ft above sea level on a commercial airliner. On the long flights, after enjoying a meal and drinks, we then decide what we want to do for the rest of the time. Some will take a short nap or just go to sleep or start to read a book or magazine. Those sitting in the window seats can enjoy the window views. Then there's the option to watch a movie or listen to music on the seatback screen or our own device. Since the first commercial flights, keeping passengers occupied while infight has been a question airline operators have asked themselves. One answer has been to provide audio and video systems referred to as infight entertainment or if to provide content such as movies and music to enjoy while on board. Today, these systems have been advanced to allow passengers to go beyond movies and music to play video games, see outside views of the aircraft, or get the flight status and connecting flight information on their own seat. if systems have come a long way from the early projection screens to show the very first inflight movies to the vast content libraries available on HD seatback screens today. So in this video, we'll take a look at the history of inflight entertainment systems and how airlines have made improvements to these systems that not only we enjoy inflight but have empowered passengers and enhanced the overall travel experience. Far from the modern IF systems we enjoy today, the very first infight video was shown on a short fight over the skies of Chicago in the early 1920s. In the August 22, 1921 issue of Aerial Age magazine, history's first aerial movie show took place aboard an 11 seat Felixto F5 flying boat named the Santa Maria as part of Chicago's Pageant of Progress trade show. The short film shown was named Howdy Chicago, which was a local production to promote the city. According to the account on aerial age, the film was shown on a plane while flying 90 mph 2,000 ft above the city of Chicago. A dey suitcase projection machine was fastened in a position and connected with an electrical flight socket. The film was viewed on a projection screen towards the front of the cabin and it was switched on by a projectionist who pressed the button to start it. This was the first known experiment in showing a flight on board an aircraft. Though the technology at the time was limited, it was described as a success. An account from the article said, quote, "Before the flight, it was feared that the vibration of the giant hydroplane as it shot through at 90 mph would seriously interfere with the screening, but it did not." This historic flight demonstrated the practicability of movie entertainment for transatlantic aerial commuters in the days to come. The success of the film screening on the promotional flights around Chicago opened up the ideas for those in aviation and how to show films on board. This would lead to the very first featurelength movie film being shown a few years later aboard a Imperial Airways flight. On April 6th, 1925, the very first movie shown on an airplane, The Lost World, was promoted by Imperial Airways with its flights as being quote the world's first aircraft cinema. Following the first movie showings aboard the Imperial Airways flights, airlines would experiment using radio signals from the ground for live broadcasts and performances from singers. Fast forward to the 1960s and jet aircraft then started to fly faster, higher, and for longer distances than the previous generation of planes. The aviation industry had to adjust some challenges to show movies on planes, such as getting the reels on board. The other challenge was to find a projector that could withstand turbulence yet be light enough not to add extra weight onto the aircraft. These challenges would be solved by cinema owner named Dave Flexer. Flexer would start a company named Infight Motion Pictures, a company that would lead to the rise of regular film showings on flights, but also served as the foundation for systems that the aviation industry would improve on later. After an investment of $1 million, Flexer and his company would develop a 16mm film system with a 25-in reel mounted horizontally to maximize space. Passengers would view the film on a projector at the front of the cabin. Using the new system, Transorld Airways showed the movie by Love Possessed to firstclass passengers on board a Boeing 707 in 1961. TWWA's main rival Pan-American would then follow and a year later Pakistan International Airways became the first international airline to introduce inflight movies with the same new system. The ability to show films on board aircraft presented an opportunity for airlines to show another type of film before a flight inflight safety videos. Provided the aircraft had the required video and sound systems, the US FAA from 1984 allowed for these pre-recorded videos to be shown replacing the standard live demonstrations performed by flight attendants. Airlines such as TWWA, Panama, and Northwest began showing their own inflight safety videos to passengers using the onboard screens. The aviation industry would continue to experiment with new media technologies that were introduced in the 1970s and 1980s such as videotapes, closed circuit television, and overhead screens. The one airline, Northwest Airlines, would make infight entertainment become more personal with the introduction of individual seatback screens in the late 1980s. During this time, Arn Stevenson, a businessman involved in aviation components, wanted to put a small liquid crystal display LCD TV screen for each airplane seat. This would lead to the founding of a new company, Airvision, and the company would partner with Philips for the screens. Warner Brothers would provide the content for this new IF system. And in June 1988, Northwest Airlines began trials using the new IF system on its flights between Detroit and Tokyo. Airvision's if was the world's first with personal if screens. The Boeing 747 on Northwest Detroit Tokyo flights had 116 of the 6.9 cm seatback screens installed on which passengers could watch video content on six channels. These six channels showed movies, news, documentaries, music videos, and cartoons on a fixed schedule. Both Northwest and Warner Brothers surveyed the passengers, and the result was 70% preferred the personal screens to the overhead screens. Following Northwest, British Airways and Quantis would launch their own trials of Airvision's IP system on board their aircraft. From six channels offered on the Northwest Airlines 747s, these IP systems would expand with far bigger libraries and CPC screens going beyond movies and music to offer passengers the ability to play video games, listen to podcasts, watch live TV, see the inflight map, and even communicate with their fellow passengers. Among the biggest libraries of content that airline passengers can enjoy today comes from Emirates ICE system. Widely regarded as the world's largest with 6,500 channels of audio video on demand content. It is one of the well- reggarded IF systems along with Qatar Airways Orics, Singapore Airlines Chrisworld and Cafe Pacific's own system. Of the audio video on demand IF systems today, Singapore Airlines Chris World is widely regarded as the first to allow passengers to pause, rewind, and fast forward movies or music. After launching Chrisworld in 1995 with 32 audio and video channels and 10 video games, it launched the new system called Wisemen 3000 in September of 1997. First introduced to first and business class passengers, it was then rolled out to economy class passengers in 2001. In addition to the media control options, it also featured news text displays and destination information. While Chris World is the longest active prior to the Singapore's Wisemen 3000, Swiss Air had launched its own audio video on demand system earlier in the year 1997 with its own system powered by interactive flight technologies. Similar to Wisemen 3000, it also let passengers watch pay-per-view movies and take gaming on an airplane to another level with infight gambling. However, that system was cited as a factor in the crash of Swiss Air Flight 111. Prior to the crash, Swiss Air complained that the electric boxes under the seat would get too warm and hard drives installed failed regularly. Following the crash, Swiss Air removed the IFT system from aircraft with them and it was never used again. Well into the 2000s and the rise of the internet, airlines, including the budget airlines, have expanded the streaming the very same content on their IF systems beyond the seatback screen, but rather onto the passenger's very own device. This has led to the rise of the bring your own device model, providing inflight entertainment. Airlines now make decisions on whether to install seatback entertainment screens or skip it in favor of providing Wi-Fi and content through passengers own devices. To install modern seatback screens, the cost can vary depending on aircraft. Whether it's a small narrow body jet or a wide body such as the 8380, a typical individual seatback installation can cost between $10,000 to $15,000 per seat. Along with the installation of wirings, servers, power systems, insec controls, airlines also have to invest heavily in both the hardware and software along with the maintenance after installation. Combined those costs can be far higher than offering a Wi-Fi system minus the seatback screens. Adopting the bring your own device model, airlines, especially budget airlines, can focus on modifying the seats to offer maybe a device holder and charging ports. With these choices, airlines may have fleets with mixed entertainment systems. Their narrow body jets used on short hall flights may have just bring your own device systems, while widebody jets used on medium and long haul flights featuring both Wi-Fi and seatback screens. Whether aircraft are equipped with seatback screens or not, more aircraft are now featuring seatback charging ports as passengers increasingly bring their own devices on board. Passengers can also use their own audio devices such as Bluetooth enabled earphones to enjoy the content. Compared to the IF systems of the past, modern seatback and wireless systems also provide passengers more flight information. Passengers can view the current flight status information and the exact location of the aircraft on interactive maps. External cameras installed on select aircraft such as the Airbus A380, A350, and 7 intended for pilots to navigate on the ground. allows for passengers to view things that they would normally not get during takeoff and landing. In addition to getting the estimated arrival time, passengers can also access connecting flight information and airport terminal maps at key airline hubs through the same if systems. While some aircraft lets passengers enjoy external views to the IF, one airline has allowed passengers to actually listen into the conversations between the pilots and air traffic controllers United. There is no official history of Channel 9 and it's not really mentioned by the airline, though it history goes back to the 1980s. There are videos on YouTube that do feature passengers listening in onto the pilot ATC conversations on channel line, but on board the pilot in the command has the final decision on whether the passengers can listen into it. Today, it can be found on United Seatback screens listed as from the flight deck. In recent years, there has been an increased interest from airlines and the traveling public for infight Wi-Fi access. On a casual poll on the Fights in Asia X page, when asked which is more important on a flight, having infight Wi-Fi or an in-flight entertainment screen, over 70% of the over 180 people voted for the Wi-Fi. In a larger poll of over 11,000 passengers by Viasat, 81% of those surveys said that being able to connect is more important for them. Among the headline internet providers has been SpaceX's Starlink, which has seen a growing list of major airlines selecting Starlink to provide free high-speed internet access on board. Starlink is one company that addresses an interest from passengers and airlines for great internet access on board flights, which the 2023 VISAT survey also reported 48% of passengers want the reassurance of free and reliable internet on board an aircraft. Having this feature is an important and will influence booking decisions as 83% of respondents in the VISAT survey said that they would select an airline if they offered quality Wi-Fi experience. With more surveys showing similar sentiments and a growing number of airlines introducing free onboard internet, it is becoming clear having free high-speed internet access is becoming an important factor when selecting which airline to fly with. Going forward, the basic amenities most airlines will offer to each passengers will be free internet access and charging ports. Budget airlines and those with aircraft operating shorter flights will likely take the route of bring your own device, while bigger full service carriers may choose the hybrid model that allows connections between passengers devices and the seatback screen. Regardless, there are opportunities for budget and full service carriers to incorporate personal greetings and allow passengers to enhance their infight experience by using it for meal orders, showing food and beverage options, reading materials, or communicating with the flight attendants. Airlines could further experiment with technologies such as virtual reality and augmented reality, but the successes of those technologies will depend heavily on the ability for passengers to enjoy these activities in the limited space on the plane. even in the premium seats and the needed equipment can safely be installed on the aircraft. That said, modern IF have come a long way from the simple projector showing how Chicago. We now have more options when it comes to the types of content and games to keep us occupied as airlines push the boundaries of flight. We are no longer just limited to the personal screen, but can enjoy and control the same content and connect to the internet on our own devices. With the internet, if systems expanded what can be enjoyed in a flight beyond the seatback screen. That's all for now, though I do want to hear your thoughts. Which airline has your favorite inflight entertainment system? As inflight Wi-Fi becomes more common, which is more important, the internet access or having an I screen? And how do you see the future of inflight entertainment? I definitely would love to hear your thoughts again, but in the meantime, this has been another edition of Flights in Asia, highlighting the news and updates from the aviation and travel scene in the Asia Pacific. Thank you for watching and have a great day.

reviews.transcript_full: In my previous video, I briefly reviewed the Business Class of An India's Airbus A319  aircraft, which you can see by clicking on the video now or clicking the link in the description  box.  In this video, I will show you the details of the in-flight entertainment system available  on their Airbus fleet for domestic sectors.  The Business Class VTV is 10.6 inches in size and is touchscreen.  The IFE starts in the map mode wherein it toggles between the flight details screen,  the airline logo screen and the map screen in three different zoom levels.  Touching the mode button on the screen brings you to the video mode where 6 movie channels  are displayed.  This unfortunately is a non-Award system which I believe is a norm for short-haul flights  these days.  The on-screen touch controls give you an option of changing channels, volume and brightness  of the screen.  Touching the mode button again will switch off the video and take you to the audio mode  with the wide variety of audio channels choose from.  Press mode again and the map screen appears along with the music playing in the background.  There is also an option to change the aspect ratio of the screen if you are not a big fan  of 16s to 9.  All this can also be controlled by the hard button controls on your armrest.  The IFE kept me busy on a 3 hour flight from day to day and the movie is that being played  with a tradition.  Overall I would rate the IFE 4 out of 5 for short-haul flights.  It would have been a perfect 5, 100 been an Award system just how they have on their long  haul-buying aircraft. article_text: A lot of airlines carry the same inflight entertainment system on board their aircraft for as long as ten or 15 years. But IFE screens and associated technology typically evolve at a much faster pace than aircraft seats and other interiors.

That’s why, when Panasonic Avionics Corporation (PAC) set about to design its next generation inflight entertainment system, it listened closely to customers about the long-term pain points they’ve experienced, such as their need to update IFE hardware without going through the costly and time-consuming engineering certification phase, including head injury criterion (HIC) testing.

“We really took a thoughtful approach to how to improve both the passenger experience, and then how to make something that the airlines can keep up-to-date and then swap out as required and deliver a terrific experience. And so, the hardware architecture fundamentally changed. The software architecture is fundamentally changing,” says Panasonic Avionics CEO Ken Sain.

The fruits of PAC’s labor, known as Astrova — and featuring inherent modularity, sharp 4K OLED screens, and USB-C charging connections that provide a guaranteed 67 watts of charging output and the ability to flex up to 100 watts of power — is now the fastest growing product ever to hit its portfolio.

Launch customer Qatar Airways will bring Astrova to its Boeing 777X fleet. SAUDIA is retrofitting 30 widebodies , a mixture of A330s and 777s, with Astrova and with it will provide up to 100 W of direct current power, via USB-C, at every seat. And United Airlines recently revealed at the Aircraft Interiors Expo (AIX) in Hamburg that it will install Astrova on select new Boeing 787 and Airbus A321XLR aircraft beginning in 2025 .

United’s passengers will also enjoy up to 100 W of DC power via USB-C at their seat, providing the ability to quickly charge the latest phones, tablets, and laptops through all phases of flight. Image: Panasonic Avionics
PAC says it’s winning the majority of IFE business — as much as nearly 70% — on the strength of Astrova. But just how has PAC accomplished this feat?

Sain explains: “Our monitors used to be smart monitors, and the processor was in the monitor. Problem is that the processor in the monitor is in the HIC path. So, if you want to run a bigger software package because you want to do something amazing around personalization, you’d have to change the monitor. The minute you change the monitor, you’re in a normal seat retrofit, so most airlines won’t do that — because it’s so expensive — for seven to 10 years. In this case, we took the GPU [graphics processing unit] and the CPU [central processing unit] and put it in the seat box. And we took Bluetooth and USB-C ports and put them in the peripheral bar. So those can be swapped.”

As USB-C goes to USB-D or USB-E, as Bluetooth goes 5.0 to 6.0 to 7.0, the customers will be able to change just the peripheral bar and have an upgraded system right then and there and do it on an overnight without having to do HIC tests.

To be clear, this is not the clunky IFE seat box of old, consuming your legroom. “It’s a third smaller, it’s lighter. It’s more powerful. It fits inside the seat rails, and it provides like three inches more footwell space,” says Sain.

“We even changed the harnesses between them, you know, moving from what the industry’s been using forever, 1950s technology, to the latest technology. It looks like a USB cord, almost. But it’s high power, high throughput and it’s future-proofed for anything that we can see going forward.”
The brains of the Astrova system. Image: Jason Rabinowitz

Regarding the choice of 4K OLED screens for Astrova, PAC is also “absolutely convinced” that this is a long-term solution for airlines, says Sain. The company recently attended a trade show in Los Angeles where all the big screen manufacturers come together. “Not one of them had anything but OLED screens. And so, this is the right technology that lasts for a long time,” suggests the Panasonic Avionics CEO.
One complaint about going 4K for IFE screens is that there is still not enough 4K content being delivered to the airline market. But PAC’s Astrova engine can upscale 480p content to 4K.

Certain studios are very particular about how their content is shown so if you’re going to show 4K content, they want to make sure it meets the expectations of the original creators. That’s why PAC has ensured that its Astrova monitors are compliant with HDR10+, the high dynamic range video technology that adds dynamic metadata to HDR10 files, with the dynamic metadata used to adjust and optimize each frame of the HDR video to the display’s capabilities in a way based on the content creator’s intentions.

In keeping with the big new IFE screen trend in commercial aviation, Panasonic took the opportunity at AIX to unveil five new larger Astrova screens for first and business class, with a 19” screen targeted at high-density business class; 22” for standard business class; 27” for front row ‘super business’ and for airlines that want to differentiate standard business class; 32” for front row business or first class; and 42” for first class.
Astrova also features programmable LED accent lighting to enhance the passenger experience. Image: Panasonic Avionics
Notably, every new size monitor introduced at AIX 2023 has already been selected by an airline.

reviews.transcript_full: Ladies and gentlemen, aviation geeks and frequent flyers.  My name is David and today we're flying out of Dubai, a city which hasn't been featured  too much in our recent episodes of Pro-Telionist, at all.  Don't know what you're talking about.  Anyway, we will be flying aboard Emirates Boeing 777-300ER.  Having a fleet of more than 120 of them, they are by far the largest operator of this  type on the planet, with Kata Airways coming in second at only 52, and Air France and  Kathy Pacific tied for third at 43.  All three will have been featured on our channel with four of course.  After all, our mission at SimpliViation is to provide first-hand reports of as many  different planes as possible, so make sure you are subscribed to join our journey.  And today's trip is special to me personally, because Emirates 777 was the plane featured  in my first ever trip report all the way back in 2012.  So 10 years later, let's see how their economy product holds up and how our video quality  has evolved as well.  Our trip begins in the lively Banias neighborhood of Dubai.  I always like to stay in Dubai's old town because it has the most authentic and affordable  restaurants and it's well connected with public transit.  After all, I'm a big believer in public transport, which I used to get to airports as often  as I can.  Luckily in Dubai, the red metro line connects all major parts of the city directly with  terminals 1 and 3 of DXB.  However, if you're departing from terminal 2, which is the case with many leisure and  low-cost airlines, or from Dubai's world central airport, those are not connected to  the metro network.  The building which houses Emirates main check in area looks different than most other  airports departure halls.  You might have noticed all the columns.  That's because we're right beneath this taxiway at the moment.  So there might be an Abbas A380 above our heads as we speak.  This means that airplanes can taxi all the way around the terminal, making airport  operations more reliable and Emirates has repeatedly been listed amongst the most punctual  airlines in the Middle East.  And our flight to Hamburg is no exception to that, being perfectly on time today, and  operated by A6ENX, a 2014 build Boeing 737-300ER.  Emirates 777 is a bit of an outlier amongst major network, carrier Seastays, in that it  still doesn't offer all its business class passengers direct aisle access, and 2 to  its 2-3-2 configuration even has some middle seats in business class.  Emirates Boeing 777 fleet also doesn't have a premium economy section, so right behind  business class you'll find 5 rows of economy, then another galley, and then the cabin section  will be in today.  I chose a window seat right before the second last door, which is 36A.  Waiting on the seat already is a pillow, but notably absent as a blanket.  They were available upon request, but I'm still surprised they're not provided on  every seat as they were on my flight to Vienna just a couple months prior.  The leg room is okay, being 180cm tall, I don't have any issues with that, and there  is a standard seat back pocket.  Emirates is known for their fantastic inflight entertainment system, which also means large  state-of-the-art touch screens.  A few planes in their fleet still feature smaller older screens, but they too come with  Emirates' enormous library of movies and TV shows which can be watched on demand.  Beneath the screen you will find a remote control with a little touch screen, as well as  a USB port, any personal universal power outlet.  Beneath that, a coat hook, and then the back of the tray table, a cup holder.  The tray tables can be used half opened or fully opened.  Before take off, the crew also handed out headphones, fresh face masks.  Today's flight to Hamburg is surprisingly empty, with just over 70 passengers aboard.  This video was recorded right before Christmas, which is why you might have faintly heard  Feliz Navidad in the background during boarding.  The Christmas spirit also touches Emirates in flight catering every year.  A little more than an hour into the flight, the crew started the main meal service.  Of course I went with a holiday meal option, which was roasted turkey with sweet pumpkin  mash, potato dumplings and peas, served alongside an orzo salad, chocolate mousse with  mandarin compote, to drink a cup of water and I also went with a can of beer, as well as  a warm bread roll with butter, and some crackers and cheese.  An elegant meal service, also because Emirates still offers metal cutlery in economy class.  This was in all honesty one of the best economy class meals I have tried so far, but unfortunately  you can only enjoy it in the month of December.  During that time you can also enjoy hot cocoa and traditional mold wine in the days leading  up to Christmas on select routes.  Emirates offers such themed meals and service elements quite often, including on Valentine's  day, during Thanksgiving on flights to the US, October Fest on flights to Germany, the  Rio Carnival on flights to Brazil, Cherry Plus some season on flights to Japan, and of  course the many different religious holidays in the Islamic world and in South Asia.  After the meal it was time to simply enjoy the flight.  Watching the sunset, the fake stars sparkling in the ceiling, and the views over the snow-covered  mountains of Turkey.  You will find a self-service snack bar with savory biscuits or kit-cats, as well as a small  selection of beverages and galley.  Emirates Triple 7s also come with Inflite Wi-Fi, though you have to pay even for the  messaging options, which is provided for free on some of their competitors.  Before landing another beverage and snack service was provided, where I went with a can  of ginger ale and a bag of salted popcorn.  Ladies and gentlemen, the right kind of popcorn.  Hashtag Team Salted Popcorn.  Then it was time to start our descent into Hamburg.  And I once again have to admit Emirates is worth its price.  Now rarely the cheapest option, and the product doesn't justify paying considerably more,  but a bit more than the cheapest competitor might actually get you some additional quality  and professionalism that might well be worth your buck.  So with that, thank you very much for watching and coming along today, and special thank you  to all of those who support us by being channel members and help us keeping our videos free  from all that VPN BS.  I'll see you again next week for another episode of our review series, Brutally Honest,  which will continue until we have all airlines covered, so make sure you're subscribed  to come along that journey.  Thanks again and have a great day!

time to try North America's favorite Airline according to the rankings but seemingly every Canadian's least favorite airline in the history of humanity this is Air Canada's Flagship triple seven business class on a transatlantic flight and oh boy am I excited to share all my thoughts with you let's Dive Right In I'm non-stop Dan a half sweet and half American who's been obsessed with airplanes for as long as I can remember over the past seven years I've been lucky to call reviewing flights my job and in that time I've flown 150 different airlines virtually all self-funded because I'm really into this honesty thing non-stop Dan is all about trying to get as much value as possible with my miles or when those are running low my money and then spreading the word so you guys get optimal value and can enjoy your travels to the Max and hopefully enjoy my geeky videos along the way where on earth have I been the past month and a half taking a much needed break but now I'm back and ready to rumble it's a miracle finding business class award seats on Air Canada between Europe and North America somehow I found one little lonely seat from Montreal to Athens for 70 000 Aeroplan miles so I quickly transfer those over from Capital One to book you can currently earn more than enough points for this one-way ticket as a sign opponent on the Capital One Venture Card at the link in the description I had just spent four lovely days visiting my family in New York after flying in on air France's a350 that review will be up soon but I needed to get up to Montreal somehow luckily it isn't very expensive or far so I booked a one-way basic economy ticket on Delta from LaGuardia for just a hundred dollars the flight was on one of the snazziest little birds in the sky the crj-900 it almost looks like a cartoon to me the flight time was less than an hour and we eventually touched down in a cloudy Montreal [Music] from there the connection process was a lot more seamless than you'd find in the U.S before checking out the Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounge I saw on flight radar that my aircraft was just pulling into the gate so I ran over and got some great views of its arrival well guess where there were also great views from the Air Canada Lounge Air Canada takes a love for dark a little too far in some aspects of their branding for my taste the lounge is thankfully a lot brighter than the entrance and features a variety of seating I know it looks big but wow did this Lounge fill up to the brim most of the seating is arranged in fours meaning that if one person is sitting there the quad already feels occupied making things unnecessarily awkward I was so excited to see Air Canada's food offering and it wasn't bad I say it was on par with a Delta Sky Club but certainly not a premium business class Lounge like the one they offer on paid tickets in Toronto there was also what appeared to be a chef making fresh meals it turned out he was just there to serve the pre-made meals and this was merely a display overall the food was fine and relatively healthy but not a standout what is a standout is always a lounge with showers which are so appreciated after a long trip speaking of a long trip should we head over and get on this nine hour overnight flight to Athens boarding was scheduled to start an hour before departure which sort of makes sense given that this bad boy is Air Canada's highest capacity aircraft a special Triple 7 300 ER configuration with around 400 seats wowza there are only 28 business class seats spread across seven rows in a one two one configuration taking up the entire space between the first two doors this is clearly a Leisure focused configuration but the seat is the same as you'll find on all Air Canada's triple sevens and 787s I had selected the only window seat that was left when I booked the flight one month prior 5K I was the very first person on board since I sneakily weasled my way past a few people in the jetway these empty cabin shots are not going to take themselves you know I really like the look of Air Canada's business class cabin not to mention their fantastic reverse herringbone seats as you can see the center seats face each other but they're still far apart so it almost doesn't make a difference if you sit here or in the window when traveling with a companion the seats are extremely private considering that they don't have a door you'll have to bend forward to even see the person next to you and the only head you'll see is the top of the passenger in front other than that there might as well be no one else on board now let me guide you around the seat even though I'm sure you've seen the reverse herringbone before Air Canada chose a beautiful setup but it's actually quite Bare Bones as far as the c-type goes there is one storage compartment on the side which contains all your electronic stuff so charging ports and your remote Etc this is already more than enough storage but most Airlines choose to also have a drawer under the surface which Air Canada did not your other storage area is to your left under the armrest which makes it quite an awkward place to put things I ended up using this as sort of a disposal for all my plastic wrappings the armrest can also be raised or lowered now when it comes to raising and lowering things in business class nothing is more important than the almighty recline to say I was blown away by the advanced seat control system on Air Canada is an understatement it allows a level of C customization that few other airlines offer in business or even first class you can really adjust every little part of your seat down to the centimeter I also appreciate the equally adjustable tray table allowing ample room to get out and use the bathroom even when the tray table has food or a laptop on it speaking of the lavatory's sorry for letting my inner Americans say Hello by saying bathroom they are fine but far from impressive amenities wise for a business class bathroom lavatory I guess that's because most of what you need like moisturizer or toothbrushes can be found in a far more hygienic and less smelly place your personal amenity kit I must say guys this kit impressed me North American Airlines really know how to do amenity kits the contents were useful and yeah this freaking cloth tell me this isn't the best design ever if you want your own amenity kit from a number of different airlines you can now buy one on my website the link for that is also below during boarding each of the 28 passengers received a personal welcome by our last names from the quebecois cabin Services director Julie one of the youngest persons I've ever seen she was so lovely and great at small talk as someone who values good service over almost all else this was such a nice and unexpected touch she spoke for a good minute or two to almost everyone chef's kiss I have to say the man who took care of me during the flight was also fantastic I was consistently addressed by name throughout the flight that's impressive and sadly I can't imagine that's a guarantee on Air Canada but I'd love to hear if this is a norm rather than an exception he also perfectly balanced professionalism with humor telling the occasional joke like a few years ago I said to this man are you finished sir he goes no I'm not finished I'm Swedish perfectly appropriate joke for me besides the lovely crew I was sad to discover there was no pre-departure service whatsoever no drinks or hot towels still with kovid as an excuse they did come by handing out menus though which were pretty nice I like the variety not only in options but of Cuisines the vegan dish sounded really cool with lentil pasta something I'd only expect to get on an airline with a hub in LA but there you go [Music] good [Music] I rarely had time to study the menu because the ground crew in Montreal had about the same sense of urgency to get our plane out of there as Lufthansa has to install an acceptable business class seat too soon sorry a full hour behind schedule we pushed back despite boarding being completed on time at 6 30. we then had a short taxi out to the runway and we're off to Athens this is a great time to congratulate this subscriber on being the latest to win a 100 gift card with an airline of their choice if you subscribe right now if you're not already you'll be entered to win for my next video [Music] looking at the triple seven Wing is almost the best type of entertainment but I didn't want to break my neck staring backwards for nine hours so I checked out the entertainment system the menu looked like something out of the 90s which cracked me up but the contents were fine not very good but also not bad like which airline should I pick on now why not Lufthansa also SAS whose entertainment system is inspired by the extravagance of 1970 Swedish socialist TV channel offerings now if you want to use the onboard entertainment you might as well hear the audio and if you don't have a Bluetooth connector these provided headphones are not bad at all sadly they were collected a full 30 minutes before landing which is always a bummer since it interrupts people's morning movies speaking of entertainment there Comes A Time in life where whatever you have at home simply isn't enough well thank goodness for today's video sponsor nordvpn who unlock a world of new content by opening up streaming services and sites that aren't available where you live due to Geo restrictions with the fastest connections of any VPN by the way that's besides the main benefit of a VPN of course which is to hide your information and keep you safe so the bad people can't steal it best of all nordvpn now includes threat protection an additional layer of of the description you can always try it see how much awesome stuff you can do with it and if for any reason you don't like it as much as I do you can always use their 30-day money-back guarantee Air Canada has a wide array of Wi-Fi offerings with many different speeds to choose from which I think is super cool several of these plans supposedly offer speeds fast enough to stream video which is an ambitious promise at 35 000 feet nonetheless super impressive that they offer such speeds and the price isn't too bad especially when you combine it with a great deal on nordvpn to stream really whatever you want and stay safe on the network the one thing I forgot to mention that really cracked me up before takeoff is that Canadians seem to have an unspoken rule that as soon as you board a red eye it's time to make your bed I felt awkward recording but at one point I swear half the cabin was standing up putting on their little mattress pads before they even settled in listen guys Air Canada has among the comfiest business class beds in the world I think it comes down to the ability to adjust the seat's firmness because I managed to make it super soft and cozy which made for my best night of airplane sleep since 2019. yes the space is quite restricted since almost half your body is under the entertainment screen but it didn't bother me too much and I'm six foot two there are also individual air vents so you can get that perfect sleeping temperature now for the most surprising part of the flight the food even I have to admit that this is not a good representation of the regular meals on board as always I ordered a vegan meal and what is this presentation who would Air Canada thought this was a good idea I mean the food wasn't bad it was actually very tasty but why is it in a big paper box and apparently this isn't even due to covid the main course was literally an economy class meal but again it tasted delicious I had to sneak a video to show that the others food looked different I even went so far to order the vegan pasta off the menu to compare and although the concept is nicer lentil pasta is pretty dry to start with put it on a plane and you're basically eating pasta shaped cardboard and tomato sauce at least I got a lot of protein when the meal was served I asked for tea to drink with it and the crew said they couldn't serve hot drinks while the seat belt sign was on the problem was that the seatbelt sign was on a good seven hours of our nine hour flight including when there was no turbulence the crew gave me all these tea bags to keep as compensation which I thought was hilarious two hours later I didn't tell them that I'm not really a big tea drinker at this point I was so ready to enjoy the comfy bed so I reclined and woke up five hours later it's such a Heavenly feeling to get such a good night's sleep on a plane I was starting to worry I'd lost my airplane sleeping skills before this [Music] once I opened my eyes I immediately opened my window blinds because we were flying over the Balkans and you know what that means what a view [Music] as I was looking out our breakfast was served it came in the same box of Doom as the previous meal but again the contents weren't bad I didn't really feel like eating salad at 3am eastern time but I enjoyed the fruit and a recent breakthrough as an oatmeal slash porridge hater I love overnight oats with that the Purser Julie Came to Say Goodbye To Us Thanking us for flying with them which was again a lovely touch I can't say enough good things about the service on this flight it could have almost been Qatar Airways given how dedicated the staff was besides that my thoughts on Air Canada are as with most Airlines quite mixed but generally positive I love the seat I loved the service I thought the food was tasty despite the bad presentation I enjoyed the amenities and thoroughly enjoyed the bed so overall an above average transatlantic flight I guess I would seek out Air Canada again over for much of the competition across the Atlantic and a really wouldn't hesitate to play them again based on this flight now to all my Canadian viewers who are excited to see me trash your National Airline I have one thing to say sorry see you all on the next one my friends until then fly safe

reviews.transcript_full: would you ever fly the worst airline in the entire world because according to google ryanair has been voted the world's worst short haul airline for six years in a row and they're so bad that they have literally become a meme so today i'm gonna be flying ryanair to see if they're really as bad as what everyone says but the reviews are honestly terrifying apparently messy planes delays hidden fees and the worst landings imaginable are all normal for ryanair and honestly i'll be lucky if the plane doesn't crash after reading this but there's also another problem ryanair only operates in europe so being a canadian that means i need to fly all the way there just to see how bad they actually were so obviously i booked the cheapest flight i could and after appreciating my final time on a decent airline nine hours later i found myself in rome italy now over the next few days i traveled to the smallest country in the world because i had to kill some time before my ryanair flight but now it was finally time to see if it was actually as bad as the reviews say all right so today i'm taking a one hour ryan airplay from rome to a city called palermo and already things are off to a terrible start last night i had to do the check-in process for my flight and literally the worst case scenario ended up happening so i was going through the normal check-in process where you have to avoid all of the hidden fees that ryanair tries to hit you with and by accident i ended up buying a bag that i didn't actually need and when i finally got to the end of the check-in process it wouldn't even work so i'm trying to contact customer service at ryanair and every time i try and sign in it says my ip isn't permitted so that means i can't change the bag that i bought by accident and i can't even check into my flight all because ryanair's customer service and website was absolutely useless so at this point i'm literally praying that they're going to be able to fix it at the gate and on top of that i don't even know if they're going to be able to let me on my flight and that's thanks to our good old friend coven because in europe the travel restrictions are completely different from in canada because in italy and in all of europe you apparently need three doses to be considered fully vaccinated for travel and in canada you only need two i am beyond stressed out right now but you know what let's see what happens so now it was time to see if everything was gonna work out or if i would end up being stranded in rome after not being allowed on my flight so i left my airbnb and after a 30 minute trip to the airport i finally ended up making it just in time before checking closed alright time to see if ryanair is actually the worst airline in the world hello hello um i had a question yes so i paid for this to be checked is there any way i could switch it to like an overhead or is that not possible you're at the boarding pass yeah yeah but even though i paid for that to be checked i can't switch it if you want to you can pay for priority and you can take with you on board now some of you guys may be confused here so let me explain this a little bit better unlike other airlines where you're allowed to bring a carry-on for absolutely free on ryanair you have to pay extra and by accident i ended up buying a checked piece of baggage for 30 euros instead of the cheaper option which is the carry-on so oh yeah you want to send or you want to take and instead of switching it to the cheaper option he instead tried to sell me on buying another carry-on on top of what i already bought so obviously i was angry and i ended up googling why i wasn't allowed to change and apparently it is ryanair policy to not allow customers to do this so thankfully i'm going to be allowed on the plane but that whole bag process was a pain in the ass so ryanair really does just want to scan people out here now after going through security and getting yelled at for filming i ended up finding my gate only to realize that i went to the wrong one and my actual gate was on the other side of the airport and at this point my flight was supposed to be boarding so i had to run as fast as i could but when i got there i realized that my fight was delayed with zero reason given by ryanair but the real test here is gonna be the flight because that is what we came here for so hopefully it goes better than the reviews set now after about 30 minutes ryanair finally began boarding but for some reason they still never acknowledged the delay but all that matters is i was finally gonna be able to experience what a ryanair flight was actually like and i was totally caught off guard the first thing that happened was we ended up taking off an hour late which is a bad look but what was even weirder was the flight was pretty much a store in the sky unlike other airlines there was no complimentary drink or food and halfway through the flight they were trying to sell perfume which was super weird and on top of that the ac wasn't really working the floors were still messy from the flight before but the most surprising thing of all was that the landing was actually smooth now even though the flight wasn't as bad as i thought it was gonna be there are some things that we should probably talk about the whole point of this video is to see if reviews.transcript_full: If you want to fly on the A380, the easiest way is going to be Emirates.  With over 100 of these super-jumbo's in their fleet, they are by far the world's biggest  A380 operator.  It's known for its first class shower rooms and for the legendary bar in the rear of the  upper deck.  We won't be able to take a shower on the A380 tonight, but we will be able to visit the  bar as it is accessible not just for first, but also for business class travelers.  And thanks to a special offer during check-in, on today's flight we have the honor to  fly to Dubai in business class.  And with that, welcome to tonight's video.  My name is David and as always, if you want to follow our flights along life as they  happen, do follow me on Instagram if you want to hear me rant about airlines, do follow  me on Twitter.  And a big disclaimer before we start this video, this is not like the real business class.  I mean, it's the real business class on the flight, but it's not the real business class  ticket because I actually expected flight economy class today and I booked an economy class  flight.  As you've probably seen already a couple of weeks ago, I have a brutally honest episode  about Emirates A380 economy class already, so I wasn't actually playing on making any  video tonight.  But yesterday when I wanted to check in online, Emirates made me an offer that I just couldn't  refuse because they offer business class upgrades on this flight to Vienna yesterday, at least  they offered it for just a little bit over 500 euros, which isn't actually that much  if you know what Emirates usually charges for their fully paid business class tickets.  So I now have the real business class seat on the upper deck on the A380, but the important  thing to note here is that everything around the flight is not actually part of those upgraded  fares, meaning that you don't get any extra miles, you don't get any extra checked luggage,  you also don't get lounge access.  So I'm just here in the lounge today because I have a priority plus card, but otherwise  I wouldn't have been able to access this lounge even though my ticket says business class  on it.  And you also don't get the chauffeur service that Emirates office in Dubai, which is a really  cool thing they offer with paid business class tickets.  So basically a chauffeur in an Emirates branded car comes to your apartment or your hotel  and they pick you up and bring you to the airport before the flight or if you arrive in  Dubai they bring you home or back to the hotel.  So that is a really cool feature, but it's not included in these business class saver tickets.  So without further ado, let's have to the gate and let's fly to Dubai.  The night's flight to Dubai will be operated by A6 EOT, a 2015 built Abbas A380 and one  of the A380s carrying the special delivery promoting Expo 2020.  By the way, every Emirates tickets regardless of class came with a free ticket to Expo 2020  which I made good use of.  Yena Airport is one of the few airports served by the A380 which was too stingy to build  a proper A380 gate, so we're boarding on the lower deck and then head upstairs to get  to our seat.  Weirdly enough, I almost prefer it this way as it makes you realize again that this airplane  has two decks which is something we won't get to experience forever.  Because sadly the days of the A380s and the 747s are numbered and a decade or two from  now the A380 will be extinct and will be remembered as a unique part of aviation history  just like the Concordes today.  After passing by the first class suites which I had the honor to be invited to try back  in 2018 on Emirates first ever A380 flight to Columbus, Rilanka, we reached the business  class section which consists of 76 lifelad seats in a staggered 1-2-1 configuration, meaning  every seat has direct eye-laccess.  My seat for this red eye flight to the Middle East will be 28, which has a pair of noise  canceling headphones, a blanket and a comfy pillow waiting for me already.  As expected for business class, the legroom is very good and right above the footwell  you'll find a small literature compartment.  Right next to the window you have these enormous storage boxes which is a feature unique to  the upper deck of the A380 and can be found on every airplane.  Even on airlines which have economy class seats on the upper deck you also get access to  these storage boxes as I showed in our Brutaliana's episode about Singapore Airlines upper  deck economy class back in 2019.  Emirates also installed automatic window shades up here.  Before take off the crew handed out some hand sanitizer, a fresh face mask, as well  as a welcome drink and the menu cards.  To start off I went with a classic business class option, a glass of champagne.  Hot Towels were handed out as well.  Emirates offers a truly exceptional selection of beverages for business class, which is  likely aided by the existence of a staffed bar in the rear of the cabin.  You can choose between a wide range of cocktails both with or without alcohol, as well as four  different beers, various wines, spirits and liquors, and a lot of sodas, juices, teas  and coffees.  On this 5 hour overnight flight, Emirates offers one main meal service with three choices  each for the appetizer, the main meal and dessert.  All snacks like sandwiches, fruit and cakes are available upon request or in the bar.  Emirates A380s feature one of my all time favorite kind of business class seat.  Back here you'll find a remote control for the entertainment system, which features  a little touchscreen.  Above that you will find a reading light and the button to control the mini bar light.  Yes there is a mini bar.  Over here is a universal power outlet and a USB port, as well as the audio port and  another USB port and an HDMI port.  A pack of socks and eye shades was also waiting for me already in this upper compartment.  And down here is the unique selling point of this seat, your own mini bar, which comes  with a glass, two bottles of avion water, a small can of Pepsi, and a can of 7 up as well  as a bottle of periase sparkling water.  This metal guard protects everything should turbulence arise.  Next to the app you have this control panel, which is still locked, but after takeoff they  get unlocked automatically and you can use it like a wireless tablet computer to control  the seat and the entertainment system.  The staggered configuration means that some seats are closer to the aisle than others.  I would recommend to reserve a seat closer to the window while booking your flight.  And in the center this means that every two rows you have seats together right next  to each other, which is perfect if you're traveling as a couple.  And now it's time to start off our journey and head to Dubai.  The business class cabin has its own lavatories, some of which even come with a window.  And in it you'll find various amenities such as toothbrushes and toothpaste or moisturizer.  However, amenity kits were also handed out and Emirates and amenity kits are amongst  the best I have experienced in business class so far.  They include some moisturizer, shaving cream, a comb, a razor, some aftershave balm,  odotolette, lip balm, a deodorant, a toothbrush and toothpaste, as well as a pack of tissues.  And this is in addition to the socks and eye shades I showed earlier.  Now it's time to relax and enjoy the flight, starting off with a warm mix of nuts and  a virgin mojito.  For the appetizer I chose the traditional Arabic mezzet, which came with hummus, muhammara,  laba ganoush and a stuffed wine leaf, served alongside some pita bread and a fresh salad.  Additional bread was provided as well, all of it warmed up including garlic bread, sourdough  and whole grain bread rolls.  For the main course I went with a seared salmon with prawns, which was served alongside  some pilaf rice, asparagus and creamy cherville sauce.  The salmon was a bit dry but that's because of the limitations of warming up certain dishes  on an airplane.  Taste wise both the mezzah and the main dish were delicious.  For dessert I went for the apricot tart with vanilla muskipone.  The crew also gave me some pralines with that.  As you have probably seen in my economy class review already, Emirates' inflight entertainment  system is fantastic and offers one of the widest selections of any airline in the world.  The only downside is that they show ads before each movie and TV show and quite a lot of  it, which is especially annoying when trying to watch multiple episodes of a TV show and  have to skip through 3 minutes of the same ads every time.  But that's a very high level of complaining when overall the rest of the flight is highly  enjoyable.  Wi-Fi is also available for purchase.  If you want to get some rest, each seed can be converted into a fully fled bad.  A topper is provided which means you don't have to sleep right on top of the seed itself.  And of course you also have a comfy blanket and a pillow.  And Emirates' planes also have these little lights in the ceiling to create the illusion  of little stars, which is just amazing.  But in contrast to some other flight reviewers, I don't fly business in first class all the  time.  So I don't want waste my precious time on this flight with sleeping, so let's head to the  bar.  A flight attendant is there at all times to prepare drinks just the way you like them.  A wide variety of snacks is available as well, such as sandwiches, fruit, crisps and chocolate,  as well as little cakes and pastries.  You can enjoy the bar standing up as well as sitting down.  And newer A380s have a slightly updated interior which also features tables.  I wanted to refrain from drinking alcohol on this flight, but the flight attendant told  me about the special cocktails they currently offer which were designed for Expo 2020,  which I couldn't say no to.  This one is called Mobility.  Another unique aspect of flying Emirates is that the cabin crew has a Polaroid camera  available to them.  So when it seems right, the crew can take pictures of passengers who are traveling for a special  location to remember their flight.  They even have little cards to put the picture into.  That's a very creative thing, which I am sure is appreciated, for example by couples  on the way to their honeymoon or a crazy aviation geek like me who gets to hang out around  a bar at 2.30 in the morning 30,000 feet up in the air.  Where I forget about it, this is the tablet you have at your disposal.  You can use it to browse the entertainment system without having to interrupt what you  are watching right now, and you can control your seat or even display the flight map on  it so you know where you are even while watching a movie.  But with all that we experienced already, the time literally flew by as we are already  back in primary, it's where we stopped in car airplane机.  While I would never pay thousands of euros to sit in business class and upgrade like this  for around 500 euros, I can really see being worth it.  I certainly enjoyed my time here and I'm leaving the aircraft well fed, a bit tipsy and  very tired, just like a night out in a fancy restaurant. article_text: We all like to be entertained at 35,000ft in the air – and Finnair has selected Panasonic Avionics to upgrade the in-flight entertainment (IFE) systems across the airline’s widebody long-haul fleet. Panasonic ex3 in Business Class The IFE upgrade is a part of the Nordic cabin enhancements being introduced by Finnair across its long-haul fleet. In terms of hardware, Panasonic Avionics is installing its latest eX3 system in all cabins on Finnair’s eight Airbus A330-300 aircraft – upgrading them from its eX2 system. When installed with the Premium Economy cabin, new seatback systems will be installed. Premium Economy IFE featuring the Panasonic ex3 – Image Finnair/Panasonic Avionics Finnair’s 19 A350-900 aircraft, which already carry eX3, will also see their premium cabins upgraded to the latest version of the system. Once deployed, the Panasonic ex3 system will be installed in all cabins of Finnair’s long haul fleet. These feature HD screens at each seat, complete with capacitive touch displays and handsets, and USB and laptop charging facilities. In Quotes Ken Sain, Chief Executive Officer of Panasonic Avionics Corporation, said, “Finnair’s innovative and eye-catching widebody cabin enhancements take their passenger experience to a new level. Panasonic Avionics is honored to be contributing to this upgrade with our latest in-flight entertainment solutions, marking the latest chapter in our relationship with this industry-leading carrier.” Harri Valkama, Digital Channel Lead at Finnair, says: “This upgrade for Finnair reflects our commitment to deliver a premium experience in every cabin on our aircraft. Having the latest technology on board will allow our customers to stay entertained as they travel long-haul. We chose Panasonic Avionics for its innovative solutions and ability to support Finnair developed digital inflight eco-system. We can rest assured that our customers will experience high-quality, state-of-the-art systems.” Upgraded aircraft now flying Economy Cabin with ex3 systems deployed – Image Finnair/Panasonic Avionics The first aircraft was completed in February 2022. As well as providing the IFE system, Panasonic Avionics provide the in-flight connectivity system (which is offered under the Nordic Sky brand). The airline also became the launch partner of the Arc map platform too. For passengers, updated hardware is a wonderful thing to have, with responsive touch screen interfaces. However, this has to be matched with content to drive those screens. It’ll be interesting to see how these systems are loaded out.
