That’s all part of the sculpted precise design that we put together, and we did that because it then strips weight out.” Astrova was unveiled at the Aircraft Interiors Expo, sized here for premium seat implementations.
Image: Jason Rabinowitz The plastic front end is polycarbonate, bonded optically to the screen behind, which is 4K OLED HDR.
Most airlines still have just a handful of 4K movies on board.
And there’s an impressive amount of power to go round: Astrova can provide 67W of juice over USB-C, enabling fast-charging of devices — even the larger, power-hungry ones like tablets and laptops.

article_text: Behind Panasonic Avionics’ new Astrova inflight entertainment system — with its consumer-grade thin screen, ultra-fast charging and substantially lighter weight — are key technology, trend and development drivers. Runway Girl Network sat down with company vice president of product development Andy Masson at the Aircraft Interiors Expo to discuss them.

During Astrova’s development, Masson tells RGN, “we went and did a whole bunch of research during COVID: we weren’t standing still. We wanted to know what’s changed: what’s changed for the public? What are the things that are changing for the customers and the customer base? One was sustainability, and this huge drive towards sustainability, specifically in terms of reduction of weight, is how we looked at that. Customers want to reduce their carbon footprint.”
To that end, Panasonic claims “significant” weight savings in the seat-end portion of the system, while remaining backwards compatible with its previous IFE platforms including eX1, eX3 and NEXT .

RGN quizzed Masson on details, for a notional Boeing 787 Dreamliner updating from a baseline eX3 system at just the seat end — in other words, without the head-end system upgrades beyond the seat itself. “This system is 30% lighter than eX3, per seat,” Masson says, and that “includes the seat box, the harness to the monitor itself, and then the monitor itself.”
That cable, harness and seat box redesign makes up a significant part of the weight savings, particularly when replicated 200–300 times across a widebody aircraft.

In terms of choices for airlines watching interior upgrade budgets at present , “you could just do the seat-end. You could leave the network in place. And we’ve designed it specifically with that in mind,” Masson explains. “You’re probably taking the cabin out, you’re probably changing the seats out anyway — you don’t have to … but you probably are — in that particular case, seat-ends only. If you wanted to upgrade the head-end, you can but you don’t have to.”

The screen itself impresses in its styling, size, clarity and performance, with Masson citing a “6.5 millimetre bezel around the outside, that’s three millimetres less than an iPad Pro. It’s seven millimetres thin: it’s extremely thin. That’s all part of the sculpted precise design that we put together, and we did that because it then strips weight out.”
Astrova was unveiled at the Aircraft Interiors Expo, sized here for premium seat implementations. Image: Jason Rabinowitz
The plastic front end is polycarbonate, bonded optically to the screen behind, which is 4K OLED HDR. Let’s unpack that.

The 4K part arguably remains something of an overkill, and has done for more than half a decade because content creators continue to charge high rates for 4K content. Most airlines still have just a handful of 4K movies on board. Upscaling from 1080 is all very well and good — but the current paradigm means that airlines aren’t yet making full use of the 4K technology.

On the OLED side, much like the home consumer market the difference between LED, OLED and QLED is one of those technical questions that largely will make little difference for anyone with average onboard requirements. In theory there is a benefit to the deeper blacks of OLEDs, but in the real world if you’re trying to watch a movie formatted to fit the aviation screen, upscaled from 720p, in a sunny airplane cabin with all the window shades open, will the difference be relevant?
HDR, or high dynamic range, is a video and image technology that improves the way light is represented. And in some ways, it is the new studio-thrown hurdle to surmount for IFE providers.

“You have to have HDR if you want to put content on from specific studios,” Masson tells us. “Some studios demand HDR before they will allow you to have 4K content, because they want to protect the creativity of their content, and they’re getting very restrictive about that.”

Speaking of brightness, Astrova also includes programmable LED lighting in the screen surround, enabling airlines to subtly signal passengers about phases of flight: transitioning to a sunset peach in the evening, or to a dawn blue in the morning, say.
And there’s an impressive amount of power to go round: Astrova can provide 67W of juice over USB-C, enabling fast-charging of devices — even the larger, power-hungry ones like tablets and laptops.
“Our research showed that more people are now bringing tablets on an airplane than laptops, for the first time,” Masson tells RGN. “14% of people bring on tablets, 12% of people bring on laptops.”

Astrova delivers this via its peripheral bar underneath the screen, both making it very clear where the sockets are and enabling changes and upgrades to the passenger device power supply without having to remove the entire screen assembly.
Astrova delivers 67W of power to laptops, tablets and other hungry devices. Image: John Walton

Overall, Astrova is impressive, and contains some of the most innovative developments out of Panasonic Avionics for years. And it already boasts a customer in the form of Qatar Airways’ 777X fleet . With the launch of Astrova, and several very interesting new hires, we’ll be watching closely for the next clues to how Panasonic is repositioning itself.

article_text: 2 November 2022 By Seth Miller 2 Comments

The inflight entertainment industry has evolved massively since the days of overhead screens and pneumatic headsets. On-demand content and live television on individual high definition screens are a far cry from a projector mounted to the cabin ceiling. But suppliers and airlines alike are not sitting still.

The next generation of IFE is coming, and it will feature at-home entertainment concepts, including pairing and casting from personal devices, as well as streaming content from online providers. And, quite likely, a new generation of suppliers will also participate in the developments.
Bluetooth Pairing goes mainstream

For several years in the middle of the last decade the idea of Bluetooth pairing for headphones on in-seat IFE systems was considered impossible. Too much complexity and interference in the radio spectrum would mean poor quality and lost signals. Turns out those challenges could be solved .

Today, new IFE installations include Bluetooth more and more. United Airlines is doing it on its single-aisle fleet refresh . Delta Air Lines has it on the A321neo fleet, and it will fly on the A330neo and 767-400 as well . Saudia , Cathay Pacific , Qatar Airways and many other airlines are also rolling it out. Bluetooth pairing is, at this point, table stakes for a modern embedded IFE solution.
Streaming on the big screen

Going back to 2015 and JetBlue ‘s partnership with Amazon to support streaming content speeds on board, Viasat ‘s Don Buchman leaned in hard to the idea of “Bring Your Own Rights.” Rather than airlines paying content fees to load movies on board, they would invest in better inflight connectivity, delivering the internet pipe as an inflight entertainment solution on board. That content, however, is typically viewed on a personal device, not the screens installed on board.

Air Canada believes that model can change. Speaking at the World Aviation Festival in Amsterdam last month Director of IFEC Product and Analytics Norman Haughton explained a vision of streaming content fully integrated into the carrier’s fleet-wide IFE deployment.

Haughton is clear that the airline very much plays a role in this new inflight entertainment paradigm, but it is a passive position. He wants to be the middle-man, coordinating the blend of content rights and connectivity. He describes it as “providing the fuel” for the experience (including JET-A). And partnerships with streaming content providers will play an outsized role:

Air Canada invested heavily in seat-back entertainment, even on our single-aisle fleet. And now we’ve gone down the road of high speed Wi-Fi. Imagine what happens when those two roads intersect. People want to consume content the way they do on the ground. We can bring in partners that add extra value. Imagine where internet and seat-back merge, and then bringing partners on board to be the gateway of that intersection, to be traffic managers and to ensure that the experience we are delivering at that intersection meets or exceeds what our customers would expect on the ground.

The Android operating system also plays a major role in the process. It powers most modern inflight entertainment screens today, offering a known framework for application development and Digital Rights Management (DRM) services to satisfy the studios’ licensing concerns.

Streaming services already have an Android app available; extending that to be a module on an IFE system is more of an interface tweak than a ground-up build. That makes deployments far easier for airlines and IFE vendors alike.
Haughton declined to give a timeline for this new IFE concept to take flight. But he implied the shift will be on a timeline measured in weeks and months, not years.

Also worth noting that this approach is different from what Delta did with Hulu back in 2019 . That effort included a subset of content, cached on the planes. The new version of on-board streaming will take advantage of the aircraft’s connection to the internet, and enable the full product catalog.
Casting content to the screen

Air Canada is not alone in pursuing this concept, though it may be the furthest along from an airline perspective. Or at least the most willing to talk openly about it. Other vendors, however, are also looking at options, including casting content from a personal device to the IFE screens on board.
Upstart Apios is not just talking about developing a casting solution. The company now has a proof of concept developed, able to cast content at scale.
It is super simple. It is easy. It works. It delivers what the passenger wants. It delivers what the airline wants. – David Thomas, Apios Chief Product Officer
It is super simple. It is easy. It works. It delivers what the passenger wants. It delivers what the airline wants.

Similar to a ChromeCast or AppleTV, passengers will be able to connect to the screen on the seatback to display their own content. The connection is driven via a QR code on the screen and a unique Wi-Fi SSID for that seat, making it easy for the passenger at that seat while simultaneously reducing the opportunities to abuse the system.

Please ignore the part where I mildly curse the system for not being perfect in a demo, and enjoy this new IFE system from Apios, which enables streaming content from a PED on to a seatback IFE screen. #paxex #APEXEXPO2022 pic.twitter.com/X9ePkQuckd — Seth Miller (@WandrMe) October 26, 2022

Please ignore the part where I mildly curse the system for not being perfect in a demo, and enjoy this new IFE system from Apios, which enables streaming content from a PED on to a seatback IFE screen. #paxex #APEXEXPO2022 pic.twitter.com/X9ePkQuckd

It is casting, not mirroring, so it depends on integration with the mobile application. It also allows for offline casting (e.g. a plane with no inflight connectivity link), assuming the app supports it. At the APEX EXPO 2022 in Long Beach last month the company demonstrated a stream from cached Amazon Prime content on an iPad to the system.

Apios also can support online streaming, assuming the plane has an internet pipe and sufficient bandwidth. The flexibility built in to the platform allows for airlines and passengers alike to have options in terms of the content.

One notable holdout when it comes to casting is Netflix. But Apios addresses that as well. The company built a Netflix web client into the screen. Passengers will have to log in to their account while on board and navigate using the touch screen rather than their mobile device. But all their content rights can now fly with them.
As part of the launch of its Astrova platform earlier this summer, Panasonic Avionics executives also suggested that a casting solution was part of the architecture, though details were limited.

Getting from concept to deployed inflight solution is no easy task. It took years for Bluetooth pairing to evolve into a viable product. Haughton argues that Air Canada is only able to deliver on its streaming plan now because of decisions made more than five years ago, along with a commitment to continue those investments even when funds were tight. Apios and others also face challenges in making streaming and casting of IFE ubiquitous on board. Not to mention that the idea of pushing content from a PED to the screen goes back to at least 2009 and Panasonic’s eXport connector .
But it’ll be mighty cool when they pull it off with the updated technology stack.

reviews.transcript_full: Emirates is known for being one of the world's best airlines and after the COVID pandemic,  it will be one of the last operators of the A380. So it's probably a good idea that we revisit  this massive aircraft on our channel and see what it's like to fly with them in economy class  now in 2021. So thanks for joining me on this flight back to my hometown of Vienna on Emirates  Abyss A380.  Of course Emirates has its own terminal here at Dubai Airport. All passengers departing  Dubai do their check-in procedure here in Terminal 3 and this is no ordinary free standing terminal  as you can see there is a massive amount of columns in here and the reason for that is that  right above us is an active taxiway so we might just be a few meters away from an Abyss A380 right now.  The downside of having their own terminal is that during rush hour massive amounts of passengers  need to check in at the same time and due to increased travel requirements because of the pandemic  wait times can be quite long. Dropping off my bags and getting my boarding pass took me around  half an hour today. At least passing through security and passport control was quick and easy  today so let's head to the lounge and get a quick breakfast before departure. Unfortunately not  the Emirates lounge though just a priority pass lounge.  Our flight to Vienna will be operated by a 2016 delivered Abyss A380 which features Emirates  standard cabin which means no premium economy and also not the high density version.  Hours had first in business class on the Aburdeck both of which we have covered in previous  trip reports on our channel if you're interested and here on the lower deck I'll be in one of  427 economy class seats which are installed in a 343 configuration. There is my seat for today's  flight 75A a window seat as always. Right on your seat you'll find a pair of headphones  pre-high quality headphones for economy class actually as well as a regular airplane blanket and  a regular airplane pillow. Emirates economy class seats are one of the favorite kind of seats  of any airline for me even though the legroom isn't the best one I mean don't get me wrong it's  an absolutely fantastic legroom and I have no problem doing a 12 or 16 hour flight in this it's  just not the best in the world but that's a very high standard. The great thing about this seat  though is the entertainment system. It has a huge touch control screen and in addition to that  also a touch screen controlled remote control so you can browse mute movies and TV shows and even  view the inflight map while you're watching a movie. You also have a USB port here to charge devices  as well as the audio port for your headphones and over there you have a universal power outlet and  another USB port to charge devices as well as a coat hook. You have a cup holder in addition to having  a tray table which can be used half opened or fully opened so basically this seats has all features  that I could ever imagine in an economy class seat. I mean look at the size of this screen even  compared to my hand it's enormous it's like a large laptop screen. The seats themselves are  very comfortable too and they have an adjustable headrest which is an important thing especially  on the A380 because compared to other types of aircraft you can't really lean against the wall  and sleep like this because of the curvature of the aircraft but that's a very A380 specific problem  and not something that's Emirates fault. During boarding every passenger got one of these  little sanitizing kits which contained a fresh face mask as well as a bottle of hand sanitizer which  is definitely a nice thing to have now during the COVID pandemic.  And it's not just the hardware that's amazing the software in other words the content that  Emirates offers and its inflight entertainment is fantastic as well. Emirates is known actually for  being one of the best airlines to fly on if you want to watch a lot of movies and TV shows. I mean  the selection is just incredible and you even local movies from all around the world are available  on the system and even on a 20 hour journey if you do you know Australia to Dubai and then Dubai  onto somewhere else you're going to have a lot of things to watch and you'll definitely not get  bored on an Emirates flight.  One little annoying thing that I've seen more and more airlines do is Emirates puts two minutes of  ads in front of every single episode of a TV show. I mean even on a long haul flight I don't have  time for two minutes of ads every time a new episode starts.  The crew just handed out these sweet pastries and I got mine with a coffee and a cup of water  and what that means probably is that the hot meal is going to be served later into the flight  and we're just starting off with a small snack right now. So I mean if you're still exhausted  because it's an 830 AM departure and you had to get up at 6 AM to go to the airport  you'll still have a lot of time to sleep and then get the big meal before landing.  All right lunch is served and I mean just look at this this is one of the best presented meals  I've had on any flight. I mean I've had some really good looking meals over the years  A&A's economy class meal on the Vienna to Tokyo flight comes to mind Air France's economy  class meal on the Atlanta to Paris flight comes to mind but this might actually be the best  looking economy class meal I've ever had. So let's hope it also tastes good. So what we have here  is meatballs with a creamy sauce served with pasta and steamed vegetables. Then we have a little  pasta salad with vegetables and some chocolate mousse which I never say no to a chocolate  mousse and down here we also have some butter as well as some crackers and cheese which is always  a nice combination to have in addition to the meal and some high quality cheese at that  and we also got a cup of water and I also got another cup of water with that because  stay hydrated folks it's the best way to fight a jet lag and we got a bread roll here as well  and Emirates even still provides metal cutlery which always gives the meal a little bit of a more  fancy feeling. All in all that's a fantastic meal I mean I really can't complain and the taste  was also superb so 10 out of 10 fantastic economy class meal.  After around five hours we've made it back to Vienna and to conclude this video let me just say  Emirates still got it. Fantastic cabin with a great inflite entertainment system because of  both the screen size and the content variety as well as a top notch hot meal like really top  10 of all time kind of economy meal and then all around amazing crew. It's certainly an expensive  airline to fly with but one where you're almost guaranteed to have a great flight with. group consists of passenger facing components including the display unit audio jacks the passenger electronic device charging ports remote controls and any device that the passenger can see and touch reviews.title: United’s latest jets will offer Bluetooth for in-flight entertainment
reviews.transcript_excerpt: with these screens will finally make it a reality.…

captions.text: with these screens will finally make it a reality.

reviews.transcript_full: reported today in the verge. United's latest jets will offer Bluetooth for inflight entertainment.  United Airlines is adding a long awaited feature to the inflight entertainment seatback  screens of its new Boeing 737 MAX-8 jets, support for Bluetooth headphones. The company is  making the upgrade as part of United Next, a new plan to expand and modernize its fleet  with what it says are larger, fuel-efficient jets and a more comfortable inflight experience.  I haven't flown in the last two years, for reasons that are hopefully obvious, but the  thing that grinds most of my past flying experience to a halt is dealing with the bizarre  Tuporong Daudi OJax airplanes used for inflight audio. Having headphones with a 3.5mm  Zordio jack isn't hard, but it doesn't reflect the Bluetooth audio lifestyle, Apple,  and plenty of other tech companies have slowly forced me to adopt. I don't like the wireless  audio freak I've become, but it happened, which makes United's upgrades so exciting,  as demoed in the tweets below from aviation writer Jason Rabinovitz. The main attraction  of it United's new interior is the new at Panasonic Caroseat Back-Eye System. It finally offers  one of the overall most requested passenger items, Bluetooth audio. Narrow-body aircraft  with these screens will finally make it a reality.  Hashtagpacsexpick.twitter.com slash TDO04G4 by 7C. Adding seatback screens made a huge  difference in how tolerable flying is, but it's been held up by lagging audio support  that the Verge has even written a guide to getting around. And this isn't a problem  unique to United. Other airlines like Delta or JetBlue have been offering seatback screens  for years, but have also saddled flyers with analog audio. United just might be one of the  first airlines to start the next wave of in-flight entertainment improvements, hopefully.  However, there's room for things to go a bit sideways. As part of its upgrades, United's  new 737 Max8 jets offer 10 or 13-inch in-flight entertainment screens on the backs of all seats,  which might mean a lot of people trying to connect to Bluetooth at once. That could cause  interference, and might also make the process of connecting your headphones more of a chore if  you're having to hunt through multiple devices trying to pair in the same menu. United currently  only offers Bluetooth on its Max8 jets which it says should start flying this summer.  The company didn't share how it plans to address issues with Bluetooth, but said it's still  studying the technology. I can't rightfully claim that Bluetooth is as meaningful a change  as more a grimoire safer flights, but for an airline industry hoarding cash to make it through  the pandemic and looking to entice frequent flyers to earn their miles again, any snazzy new feature  can't hurt.For more on this story, visit the news article link.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome, thanks for joining us for a unique FG experience. Leaving Paris, Charles de Gould  Airport on the upper deck of the massive Airbus A380 Super Gembo, we're getting to watch  it all from my camera high in the plane's tail.  It was a pretty quick taxi to the runway. Before we left, we got to see a Vietnam Air  Alliance Airbus A350 take off in front of us.  Next it was our turn. We taxied on to the runway 26 right, which is 13 and a half  thousand feet long in Charles de Gould. There's a parallel runway out to the left  and if you look up ahead you can see a smaller plane landing on it.  This is the four massive engines of our Airbus A380 ramp up. You can actually see them start  to kick up moisture off the runway at the very bottom of the screen.  We ended up using 7,500 feet of the runway, a little more than half of it before we left it off.  We took a break from the tail cams to look out the window and get a view over the huge wing  and the outskirts of Paris flying by underneath. We kept climbing out directly to the west and  we were soon above the clouds and on our way to New York.  Check out our website for the full report from this flight plus plenty more videos, photos and  stories about aviation. Thanks for watching and consider subscribing if you enjoyed this video.

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] hi I'm back at the airport I'm in Milan at malpensa rec what I'm about to fly through to Egypt - to Cairo I'm flying that the newly rebranded air Italy it's now a part owned by cata and I'm looking forward to it in business cards it's on a 737 but hopefully it'll be quite nice so go and check in go and have a drink in the lounge and then they jump on board and fly to Cairo err Italy uses one of the generic lounges that Malpensa Airport it was pretty nondescript but the sweet treats and coffee were pretty good [Music] [Applause] [Music] [Applause] as soon as I'd consumed these I went to the gate for some plane spotting [Music] I also got to see my ride coming sadly today I would be flying one of err Italy's oldest aircraft this one was 19 years old and other than a name change is still carried the old Meridiana livery [Music] welcome aboard seeing on the under passenger in business class I think this is going to be a pretty comfortable fly cheese it's cloudy so that's what I felt like [Music] [Applause] [Music] the Air Italy business class cabin is laid out pretty much the same as all other European narrow-body business class cabins so it was pretty poor it was two by two basically you get an economy class seat a little bit of extra legroom and the middle seat is blocked off obviously on this flight I had the added comfort of being the only passenger in business class [Music] this aircraft was so old that the armrest still had ashtrays this did mean though that the seats were comfortable and well padded but dirty one advantage of old seats is that they have more recline than the modern ones and the legroom wasn't too bad either a blanket and pillow were provided and if I needed any more there was a massive stash of them on the row behind me before takeoff a drink was offered together with some snacks I just went with water after takeoff I asked for a gin and tonic but they didn't have any onboard I therefore opted for a whisky on the rocks I had no idea what it was but it went down well then it was time for dinner this was interesting the serves are huge but I reckon if you add all of this stuff you'd be clogged up for a week what I did eat wasn't that great so sadly most of it went to waste the only entertainment on board was the in-flight magazine as this was a nighttime flight there wasn't much to see out the window until we got to Cairo overall this was a pretty uneventful flight and I was pretty much left to myself as I hardly saw the crew based on this flight I would only choose to fly Air Italy again if the routing and the timing meant that it was the best option one other thing to note is that air Italy is a low-cost carrier it therefore uses the very very old terminal at Cairo Airport which is only used for pilgrimage and low-cost flights thanks for watching if you enjoyed this video give it a thumbs up leave a comment and check out my channel for lots more reviews in the meantime as always happy travels you

fancy premium check-in area at Auckland Airport this is available for both business and premium economy class passengers [Music] after check-in it was straight to the Air New Zealand business class lounge which this morning was packed there was some good food on offer and I eventually managed to get a coffee from from seriously overworked baristas [Music] the best bit about this lounge though was the great views of the airport it was a beautiful morning and there was plenty of aircraft activity [Music] welcome [Music] the business class cabin is laid out the one-one-one configuration I know this designers been around for quite some time and a couple of other airlines user however this was the first time I've ever flown it and I don't like it the cabin is really open and you all face each other so it feels more like a school dorm than a class in private business faster also one earth you would have seats facing away from the window is beyond me the a seats are certainly the ones to go for as the middle row is facing away from you the cabin is seat design made it really difficult to film as I don't like filming other passengers there forth much of this part of the video was filmed after landing in terms of seat selections my tips are as follows if you like being seen but don't like looking at other passengers then choose the seats towards the front of the cabin if you don't like being seen but I'm happy to look at everybody else then choose one of the seats towards the back of the aircraft couples are best choosing seats behind each other rather than across the aisle I know this sounds counterintuitive when looking at the seat map but in this configuration they're actually much closer to the person in front or behind you than you are to the person across the aisle this configuration is also no good if you're freaked out by people's feet it is everybody has their feet pointing out into the middle of the art for the entire flight the good news is that a New Zealand is currently designing a brand-new seat in a secret hangar in Auckland I'll definitely be giving that a go once it's released the seats themselves are pretty good they were well padded and comfortable and they're not as narrow as they appear on the video when in the upright position you sit up very high and everybody's head sticks up over the seat dividers as you recline the seat lowers and your level of privacy does increase ever so slightly power USB ports are provided and there are a couple of storage areas [Music] for some reason little fold-out table for your drink is located just behind you which is a bit awkward however the main trade table is a good design it's large sturdy and can slide forward so you can easily get in and out of your seat while it's in use when it comes time for sleeping the seat converts into a fully flat bed this is done by pushing this magic button which causes the seat back to fold down the resulting bed is fully flat and very well padded as a result it is very comfortable including lots of whips for your shoulders the only negative is that the footie area is quite narrow so when lying on your back the natural position is to have one foot hanging in midair sleeping on your side is therefore best there were no amenities kits provided as this was a short daytime flight on long-haul flats they are provided however sadly in New Zealand does not do PJ's in business bus I love the air new zealand crew then will relaxed fun and engaging which made the whole flight so much more enjoyable breakfast for the service shortly after takeoff I started with it mixed berry smoothie moved on to the fruit toast and finished it all off with eggs and sausage which is pretty tasty [Music] normally on 787 flight reviews I rave on about how good the windows are with their electronic shading system sadly there's not much point of having fancy windows when your seats have pointed away from them also for some strange reason the windows on this particular aircraft were really dirty I tried to wipe them but this made it worse it seems that some sort of Solon had been used that wasn't compatible with the plastic [Music] one thing that did work really well was the in-flight entertainment system here in New Zealand are right on the money their system is easy to use as plenty of choices and also provides lots of information I particularly like the fact that they feature lots of TED Talks one in particular really interested me it was a talk by Davey say about his story Corps program and app this allows ordinary people to record interviews with family members which are then saved forever I really wish this had been around 40 years ago because I'd give anything to hear my grandfather or OPA being interviewed I'm now planning to interview my parents so that my great-great grandchildren can hear them speak and learn about their lives I've put a link to the talk below I also spent a big chunk of time listening to New Zealand's greatest ever musical export kravid house this aircraft was not Wi-Fi enabled [Music] and if you've got about a five it marking wants to avoid a New Zealand business possible if you're fascinated by them you'd come into the bathroom and stuff suppose Evangeline's about an hour before we landed in adelaide the crew came around with the morning tea trolley service this was a nice touch and I can confirm that both the sweet and savory options were very tasty it was also very good cup of tea the final element of the service was just as we started our descent New Zealand lollies and chocolates for the landing I moved to an empty seat on the other side of the aircraft so that I could film the city centre on the way in it's always a nice view flying into Adelaide over the city even on a cloudy winter's day this footage obviously was only possible due to me attaching my smaller camera to the window at the time I was facing inwards looking at my fellow passengers that said other than the cabin design this was an excellent flight I love the air New Zealand in the flight crew their service and the entertainment system and I'm really looking forward to seeing what they new business class seats will be like thanks for watching if you've enjoyed this video please give it a thumbs up and leave a comment also please check out my channel where you'll find lots more reviews and more on the way in the meantime as always happy travels you

reviews.transcript_full: Hi there and this is OneWaltfly speaking. Just a quick and sharp video today regarding  the new YouTube partnership program that will come into effect on Lakefabury 2018. Just  last week, YouTube announced new eligibility requirements for the YouTube partnership  program. One channel needs to reach 4,000 watch hours in the previous 12 months and 1,000  subscribers in order to join or rejoin the program. If you don't understand yet, all of your  videos will be demonetised and you will no longer be able to earn money from YouTube if  you're out of the program. In my own opinion, YouTube is a video platform and its video quality  should keep improving with fewer commentations. I don't see this will happen. I reached 6k  yesterday so thank you and without many of you, my channel won't be here at all. Furthermore,  without listening to tons of feedback and suggestions coming from you, I might be kicked out  from the program as well. I think now is really the time for me to contribute back to the community.  In the past few days, I received messages from several YouTubers asking for help. I was like,  how can I help you? I subscribed to your channel last year so it's not that all I can do.  Now I was wrong and the answer is no. I'll try my very best to help you if you're desperate  to stay in the program. If you own a aviation channel and you don't have 4,000 watch hours in the  previous 12 months and all 1,000 subscribers, let me know in the comments. I will subscribe  to your aviation channel using both of my channels 1WattFly and ExpressFly.  After a while, I hope I will be able to give as many of these channels as I can. Then I'll  post a shout out video for these channels so they can subscribe to each other and watch each  other's videos. It will be great if anyone else can help out as well. Here what I'm trying to achieve  is being a hub of small YouTubers so we can together fight against the new unfair YouTube  partnership program before it comes into effect. Thanks guys, should you have any question regarding  this, just drop your comment down below. Thank you.

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] now this one I have been looking forward to for quite some time I'm in DOA and I'm about to fly with K in their brand new a350 through to Adela it's about a 12 13 hour flight so plenty of time to relax and indulge in the katar business class service in my mind they've uh they've always delivered in business class in this wide bodied aircraft so I'm really looking forward to it before then just going to quickly relax and have a shower in the uh in the lounge and then we'll we'll jump on board and uh see what katar's [Music] like Alan is katar's Flagship business class Lounge in Doha it is a lovely Lounge but for me it appears a bit spar with not much offered in the way of food and drink outside the designated dining areas that said this Lounge does Bast the best shower facilities I've seen and used in any airport lounge anywhere in the world [Music] [Music] the business class cabin on the catar a 350 is laid out in a 121 configuration the best seats for couples are the two seats in the middle which even have a handy privacy screen between them so if you really don't want to talk to your partner you don't have to the cabin has two sections the front larger section has six rows and the smaller back section has three rows separating these sections is an open space where the main doors are this gives a cabin a very open and roomy feel the space is created between these two cabins is used as a sort of meeting place for business class passengers with champagne and chocolates available on this flight I didn't see anybody using this area other than to go and grab some chocolates [Music] the katar business class seat on the A380 is my new favorite business class seat it's private comfortable and practical there are various storage options including a handy shoe drawer you can use even in full recline mode the armrest has a storage compartment which houses a water bottle and your headphones and there's also another compartment next to you where you can keep your valuables close by while you're sleeping as expected the seat is fully wide with a power outlet and one USB port the trade table is sturdy and a good size for working the clever design of the trade table and the tractable armrest means you can easily get in and out of your seat during meal service seat adjustments are endless and easy to use however these seats do not have a massage function and one other minor point is that the seat does not move forward so unless you're super tall you can't rest your feet on the ottoman that said there is a separate foot rest I'm a great fan of katar's inflight service their crews are very switched on and eager to please service starts with champagne and hot towel on boarding once you're in the air the service is up to you cuz Kata provides total freestyle dining this means that you can order whatever you like off the menu whenever you like there are no set meal times this may not sound important but it is when you are flying Long Haul for business and you're in different time zones all the time and it shows that katar really understands Long Haul business class travel I started this flight with a drink from the bar as usual a single malt served with warm nuts I followed this with dinner which started with a a salmon pallet pleaser and was followed by a traditional Arabic Messa both were delicious accompanying this was an excellent glass of the twoand shz from South Australia's McLaren V highly highly [Music] recommended for Mains I went with the spiced chicken breast again it was very good after all of this there was no room for dessert the catar amenities kit is functional but basic however where cat does shine is that it provides both PJs and slippers in business class I'm a very strong advocate for always wearing pajamas on uh on board when they're provided and I love uh airlines that provide pajamas and business class it keeps your clothes clean and crease free and it means that you're far more comfortable during the flight as well and how good do they look it was then time to try out the lay flat bed the crew make it up for you with a thin mattress cover the bed was so comfortable that I slept for a solid 7 hours straight and it was probably the deepest sleep I've had on any flight anywhere what made the bed so comfortable is that there was plenty of room for my legs and my feet and you could lie comfortably on it on your back your side or your front I woke up to some lovely views of the Australian Outback and the iconic wing tips of the a350 then just as I was looking out of the window along flew our aircraft's bigger brother the catar A380 on its way to Sydney this is why I love window seats I love the external cameras on the a350 and the really cool interactive root map in terms of the rest of the entertainment system it's okay without being fantastic it's not quite as easy to use as the emirat system and doesn't quite have the range of selections that said there does appear to be heaps of international content this aircraft was Wi-Fi enabled catata offers 15 minutes or 10 MB of data free and this worked well after this various packages are available to purchase but they were quite [Music] expensive I started breakfast with an Energizer this was followed by yogurt and musley and then an again I wasn't disappointed before landing I indulged in an espresso before turning on the tail camera to watch our approach into Adelaide overall this would have to be one of the best business class flights I've [Music] had katar sets The Benchmark with their Flagship business class product and this flight did not disappoint the a350 is an excellent aircraft and both the seat and the onboard service were brilliant [Music] thanks for watching if you like this review give it a thumbs up leave a comment and please don't forget to subscribe to my channel where you'll find a whole load of other flight reviews and some travel reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Now, we know that Katar is fantastic in business class. They set the standard in that category. However, I've always said that the mark of a truly great airline is how well they perform in economy because economy class is where the bulk of the people fly. So, tonight I'm giving them the ultimate test. I'm flying from Adelaide to DOA. It's an overnight flight, 14 hours. I'm actually looking forward to it because it's in their brand new A350 aircraft. So, let's go and see how Katar performs in economy. [Music] [Applause] [Music] [Applause] [Music] The Katar A350 economycl class cabin is laid out in a 333 configuration. There are two main economycl class cabins with 247 seats in total. For this flight, I was sitting in row 40 towards the back of the second cabin. I really like the A350. The ceilings are high which gives a much roomier feel than older aircraft and whilst the windows are not quite as big as a 787 Dreamliner, they are still bigger than normal which is great. The cabin lighting is all LED and it changes color depending of the time of day or night. This apparently helps with jet lag as does the lower overall air pressure of the A350 cabin. [Music] [Applause] [Music] Now, let's have a look at the seat. Overall, I really like this economycl class seat. It was very comfortable, and it provided a great level of comfort and support. The headrest was adjustable and supportive, and unlike many other airline seats, it actually stayed in position, which was nice. The leg room was pretty good, too. And I was able to cross my legs when the seat in front was not reclined. Even with that seat reclined, the leg room was still pretty reasonable. There was no footrest. There's not a massive amount of recline on these seats. However, it feels more than it is because the base of the seat also moves slightly forward when you recline. Like a lot of other airlines, Kata uses a clever design for the tray table that allows you to only use half of it when you've just got a drink. Another little clever design feature on this is that there is a slot for uh holding up a tablet or an iPad. Power is provided via a USB port in the seat in front of you. And this is also where you find the headphone socket. Overall, the seat comfort meant that I was able to get several hours of pretty good semi-olid sleep for this flight. The crew on this flight were excellent, friendly and engaging, just as you'd expect from Kata. We had a 10 p.m. departure and dinner was served shortly after takeoff. I went for the pasta. It was pretty good. Kata is a full service airline, so alcoholic drinks are included. I tried the red wine, and that was also very good. During the night, the crew would come around regularly with drinks. Snacks were also available. I didn't film any of this because it was too dark. Before arrival in DOA, breakfast was served. I had the chicken, sausage, and frittata. Again, it was pretty good. All passengers were provided with a comfortable pillow and blanket, as well as a basic amenities kit, which included socks, eye shade, earplugs, and a toothbrush. Each seat has a personal entertainment screen, which is located on the back of the seat in front of you. The screen is clear and bright and is adjustable as that seat recines. It has a full touchscreen functionality, but there is also a remote control device provided. I found the system relatively easy to use, and there appeared to be plenty of viewing and listening options. It certainly helped pass the time. The interactive route map was also really cool. And the A350 has three external cameras. It's a pity that this was a nighttime flight. This aircraft was Wi-Fi enabled. Kata offers 15 minutes or 10 megabytes of data free and this worked well. After this, various packages are available to purchase, but they were quite expensive, coming in at around about $1 per megabyte. It was still dark when we landed in DOA, so no spectacular views out the window. However, the excellent external cameras on the A350 meant that I got a great landing gear view as we came into land. This also gave me a chance to reflect on the flight. Overall, it was much better than I expected for a 14-hour overnight flight. The seats were comfortable. I got some good sleep. The crew were excellent. The meals were pretty good. And the entertainment system made the time fly by. And I'd certainly have no hesitation in flying Kata economy on the A350 again. And this is Medina, one of the fantastic crew that would look after you on board Kata. Thank you so much. Great flight. Thanks very much, guys. Thank you so much for flying with us. Byebye. [Music] Thanks for watching. If you like this review, give it a thumbs up, leave a comment, and please don't forget to subscribe to my channel where you'll find a whole load of other flight reviews and some travel videos around the world. In the meantime, happy travels. [Music]

reviews.transcript_excerpt: I'm going to make a bold claim here and say that the Turkish Airlines Business Class…
reviews.transcript_full: I'm going to make a bold claim here and say that the Turkish Airlines Business Class  Landage Istanbul's Ataturk Interaction Airport is the best business class  lounge I've seen anywhere in the world. It's a huge lounge spread over two  floors. How it's not the size that makes it a good lounge, it's a thought that's  gone into it, it's the small touches that make all the difference. The first of  these is the handy lockable luggage lockers which means that you don't have to  worry about your baggage as you enjoy the lounge. Other facilities include a  pool table, theatre, showers, golf simulator, racetrack and video game  conference.  What this lounge does better than any other is that it is a genuine showcase of  the food and culture of the country that you're in rather than being just another  bland international lounge. I had an early morning flight so breakfast was being  served. In addition to omla and panini stations it was the traditional Turkish  food that was being prepared and served which I enjoyed most. Everywhere there was  Turkish culinary delights on offer.  Colleagues flying out later that day enjoying freshly made pide and backloat.  This lounge was the perfect end to a great tripping turkey.  Thanks for watching. If you enjoyed this video please subscribe. There are more  of yous coming soon.

reviews.transcript_full: Normally my flight reviews are of larger aircraft on flying longer routes, but this was  cool so I thought I'd share it.  I flew from Kiev to Riga as part of a longer trip.  This section was on the dash 8.  I wasn't expecting business class in this sector as I didn't think that anybody did business  class on the dash 8, but it turns out that air bolt it does and it doesn't very well  indeed.  The business class cabin is small but functional and is laid out in a 2x2 configuration similar  to economy class, which is hidden behind this curtain.  There is a good amount of leg room and you can even cross your legs if the seat next to  you is empty.  The crew are fantastic, friendly, engaging and offering continuous drinks and a delicious  breakfast.  The analogue in-flight entertainment system works like this and this.  There is a wide variety of content to suit all tastes including destination information  and staff profiles.  Good day Chris.  You can even follow your flight using the interactive route map like this.  Before long we were coming into land in Riga.  That's a nice view of glad being forest on the way here.  All in all I thought air bolting was excellent and I would certainly recommend them and  fly with them again.  Thanks for watching.  If you enjoyed this video please subscribe. reviews.transcript_full: The Emirates Business Class Lounge at Dubai's Concourse A is huge. Just like the first class  lounge, it runs the entire length of the terminal and business class passengers port their  flights directly from the lounge.  Due to its size, the lounge is like a mini airport itself. According to this map, it would  take you 12 minutes to walk the entire length of the lounge. Running would be quicker,  but that's not encouraged.  My first stop between connecting flights is always the showers. My tip is to do this first  because during busy times, there can be a weight of up to 20 to 30 minutes. After shower,  it's time to sit down for a coffee, check the emails and have a bite to eat.  There are various facilities available, including charging stations, computer work stations,  prayer rooms and a smoking room. You can even get your shoes polished.  And for the best shoes shown, you're going to come and see Chris. And his Mayhood.  The main areas of the lounge can get busy during the early morning rush hour. However, the  size of the lounge means that there are plenty of quiet corners where you can relax in peace.  One stairs at the very end of the lounge is a special quiet zone. This area also has  the best views of the aircraft activities outside.  And then, when it's time to depart, it's straight on to your flight from the lounge.  Thanks for watching. For more reviews, please click on my channel and, of course, don't  forget to subscribe.

reviews.transcript_full: Alright, I'm on one of the thorns's Airbus A380s for the first time and let's go ahead and take a look at what we got here in the first class cabin.  One of the things you're going to notice in the first class cabin are there no overhead bins and that's because people in the first class get something a little bit of an overhead bins.  You get your own personal locker where you can put your hang your coat, hang your shirts and put your roll away bag in the bottom.  They go first class here or even have leather in the inside of your storage locker and you're able to do your own combination so no one's going to end up getting your stuff in there.  And then moving up to the first class you have a lot of room, a lot of high-end amenities and a couple toys.  If you're going to be sitting down here of course you got the Inflight Entertainment Center which you expect in most high-end seating arrangements.  But you also kind of have feels like something almost set of like the Batmobile here or there you have automatic settings for your seat.  You can also lift this up and you have easy adjustable settings.  And one of the best things here that if you got your neighbor over there and you really don't want to talk to them, you can push a button and the security screen will be coming up here to block them.  And coming over to the windows here if you're deciding you want to watch a movie or you don't want to have the light, you can just push one button here.  Push one button here, push one button here, there we go, there's the right button.  And the sunscreen will actually come down for you here and pretty high-end stuff going on.  And of course you have what you expect also, you have your remote control in here to build a handed your Inflight Entertainment System.

reviews.transcript_full: This is one of the most chaotic flights of my life. Today I'm flying [music] the new Etihad A3501000 to Amsterdam. And boy was the entire thing a crazy journey. From vomit on the seats to a snowstorm, this is something you'll not want to miss. So strap in and let's get going. Welcome to the third video of my Etihat series. So far, I've tried Etihad's 77 and 77. Now, time for one of the newest members of Etiad's fleet, the A350. reviews.transcript_full:
The A350, Airbus's flagship long haul aircraft, 
is well known for its excellent passenger comfort, with a low cabin altitude, a very quiet cabin, 
and perhaps most importantly, fairly wide seats. Normally this aircraft uses a 9 abreast seat 
layout in economy, offering 18 inches of width! Before I started making reviews on this channel 
I gave Delta’s a try and it has to be one of the comfiest aircraft I've flown on. The A350 
is also the only type of aircraft used by our airline today, French Bee! They are a Paris based 
long-haul low-cost carrier, offering some of the cheapest transatlantic fares available. Since I'm 
headed to Los Angeles, and I've already given Air France a try on the same route in a previous 
video on this channel, I figured I could save some money and give them a try! What's the catch? 
Well besides being a low-cost airline and all the things that come with that, their A350s are pretty 
unique. They have added an extra seat per row, meaning 10 abreast seating on an aircraft that 
was intended for 9, leaving economy seats with just 16.7 inches of width. So in today's video 
we'll see if French Bee’s seats are as bad as I am expecting them to be, or if the airline 
manages to make up for it with great service and cheap prices, flying from Paris-Orly 
to Los Angeles on French Bee’s A350-900! Welcome to Paris-Orly! Right now I'm flying in 
from Berlin aboard a Transavia 737. Thankfully for me we are about to land on time, since this 
ticket and our upcoming French Bee flight were booked separately. I had to do this because, at 
least when this flight was originally booked, French Bee had absolutely zero connecting 
options from Berlin. Today though, they partner with a third-party service, Dohop, which 
allows you to make self-transfer connections, basically what I'm doing now, but with the 
added benefit of coverage in case you miss the connection, although I've never tried 
Dohop myself so I can't vouch for them. Since I don't have any coverage, out of 
caution I booked a 7-hour connection here, so with our on-time arrival getting to 
our French Bee flight won’t be a problem. The connection is made especially easy thanks 
to French Bee using the relatively small Paris-Orly airport, instead of my personal 
worst nightmare, Paris Charles-de-Gaul. Here, the walk between Transavia and 
French Bee is short and simple since the two airlines are neighbors, with Transavia 
using Terminal 3, and French Bee Terminal 4. French Bee operates from Paris-Orly as their 
sole base. From here they focus mainly on North American destinations, with flights 
to Monteral, New York, Miami, San Francisco, and Los Angeles, our destination today. 
Alongside that they also operate to two French overseas territories, Reunion, currently 
the world's longest domestic route, and Tahiti, which would beat Reunion if they didn't 
make a stopover in San Francisco. French Bee offers online check-in, although 
like most people flying internationally, I have a bag, so we’ll still 
need to check-in in person. Thankfully French Bee makes that super easy 
with plenty of automatic check-in terminals, where we can print out our tickets and bag 
tags, before heading to a large check-in area that French Bee shares with fellow long-haul 
budget carrier, Air Caraïbes, where we can quickly give our bags to the airline with 
a self drop belt. By the way, checked bags, if one doesn't come included with your fare 
type, cost $70, which is unfortunately pretty normal for a transatlantic flight. Carry-ons 
however, are at least free for all passengers. And after about a 30-minute 
wait to get through security, we are airside. There is still a few hours 
to go before our plane even gets here though, so I'm gonna grab some food, and meet 
back up with you once it arrives. Well this is sadly the best view I could get of 
our aircraft, but here we are! This is F-HREV, a 2018 built A350-900, one of just 6 
aircraft in French Bee’s fleet today, 4 A350-900s and 2 A350-1000s, all of which 
share the same 10 abreast seating in economy. French Bee was founded in 2016 by Groupe Dubreuil, 
a family holding company, as a way to expand their aviation business. They already owned this airline 
next to us, Air Caraïbes, another long-haul low-cost carrier that unsurprisingly for the 
name, Caraïbes simply being French for Caribbean, operates flights between the Caribbean and Paris. 
Expanding flights from Paris to other destinations with the "Caribbean" branding would be a bit 
strange though, which is where French Bee came in. French Bee was actually founded as French 
Blue, but while applying for permission to fly to the US, Jetblue protested their 
being two airlines with “blue” in the name, so they switched to French Bee. Anyway, 
despite being two separate companies, with distinct networks, French Bee being the US 
focused brand, and Air Caraïbes being the, well, Caribbean focused brand, as sister airlines 
they have a lot in common. Like French Bee, Air Caraïbes uses a mix of A350-900s and 1000s, 
also with the same 10 abreast seating in economy, although they also fly a pair of A330-300s 
with a very dense 9 abreast seating. They also share facilities here in Paris-Orly, 
like the check-in area earlier. And they have a full codeshare agreement, allowing you to 
seamlessly connect between their flights here. [Announcement] Ladies and gentlemen, attention 
please, we start the boarding flight 72 for Los Angeles [Announcement] I invite passengers traveling in uh, 
[Gate Agent] 5 to 9 please! 5 to 9 premium! [Announcement] Premium Blue with the seat
5 to 9, 5 to 9 at the gate F21. [Announcement] For passengers travelling in Eco 
Blue with the seat 26 to 51, please proceed to [Announcement] the gate F20. For the other passenger,
please uh, please do wait and uh, [Announcement] and uh, wait for the next
announcement please. Thank you. As you may have been able to hear, French Bee 
boards by row, unlike most airlines that board by fare type. At the same time as premium passengers 
start boarding with their own jet bridge, the economy cabin is split in two, with the 
back half boarding first, followed by the front. I don't really know if this system is any 
faster than normal, and it wouldn't bother me, except for one issue… French Bee sells priority 
boarding! I paid the €15 so I could board early and get better footage of the cabin, but it 
seems they are just completely skipping over it! Thankfully we are in the back half of the aircraft 
which boards first, and I was already being a pest standing around the gate to film, so it 
looks like we will still get in pretty early. To be clear I'm not bothered by the 
lack of priority boarding in general, I normally wouldn't even get it if 
I weren't filming, but I really just don't understand why French Bee sells it as 
an option if they aren't going to use it, especially at their hub airport, where things 
should be running exactly as they want. All of French Bee’s aircraft are split simply 
between economy and premium economy. For the -900 like ours, the premium economy is a rather 
small section of just 35 recliner seats in a 2-3-2 configuration. We won't get to see it since 
we are boarding through door 2, but for premium economy French Bee chose Safran Z353 recliners.
Behind premium, the rest of the aircraft is filled with 376 economy seats, although the 
little section in between premium and door 2 is sold for a little extra as a quiet area.
And here is the economy cabin, with the infamous 3-4-3 layout, something that only French 
Bee and Air Caraïbes, as well as Philippine Airlines have dared to try on their A350. And 
I can immediately see just how thin these seats are! Back here in economy by the way, French Bee 
uses the Safran Z300, although I can only assume these are an extra thin version! Aside from the 
width though, the seats at least seem to be well padded, and have plenty of legroom.
You can actually find a wider version of this same seat on most of Air France’s 
widebodies you might fly on this same route. And here is our seat for the next 12 hours, 41A, 
located in the middle of the rear cabin section. Despite the obvious discomfort that comes from 
such a thin seat, French Bee tries to make up for it with some pretty alright legroom! I'm 
6-ft tall and this is good enough for me. More importantly, the shape of the seat 
allows me to comfortably stretch out my legs without hitting my shin on the seat!
Inside the seatback pocket you will find your standard safety card, sick bag, and magazine. 
The seatpack pocket itself is pretty tight, and lacks fully enclosed sides, making 
it hard to actually place anything in it. At the top of the seat you will find your 
10-inch seatback screen that, immediately to me, looks pretty nice. It is adjustable, and 
comes with a USB-A socket and headphone jack. And just below that, you’ll find your 
single piece adjusting tray table. The side of the seatback also 
comes with a little coathook. Above you, you will find some adjustable 
reading lights, although sadly no air vents. And finally underneath your seat, you 
will find a universal power outlet, with 2 for every row of 3 seats.
Overall not bad for a budget carrier. At least I can stretch my legs 
out while I'm being squeezed by the seat! [Pilot] Thank you from the flight deck, ladies 
and gentlemen, your Captain speaking. My name [Pilot] is uh, David Bernard and I’m very glad 
to welcome you aboard this Airbus A350 [Pilot] French Bee flight to Los Angeles. I share 
the cockpit today with Pierre and Clément. [Flight Attendant] In preparation for takeoff 
your seatback must be in the upright position, [Flight Attendant] your tray table stowed away, 
your armrest down, all window blinds fully opened, [Flight Attendant] and your seatbelt securely fastened 
and visible to the cabin crew. [Flight Attendant] Thank you for your attention
and I wish you all a very pleasant flight. Right now we’re passing by 
a Norse Atlantic Dreamliner, another one of Europe's long-haul budget 
carriers, who I actually reviewed in my last video on this channel! If you enjoy 
reviews like this and wanna see more like it, I already have a ton up on the channel for you 
to check out, as well as plenty more on the way, so make sure to like, subscribe, and 
hit the bell so you don't miss that! And just like that, I'll see you in the air! Even though I haven't messed with my screen 
at all yet, just after we passed through the clouds, my screen came on with an 
advertisement for the in-flight WIFI. Well since I was gonna give their WIFI a 
try at some point, might as well do it now! The network doesn't have any stream-to-device 
entertainment, or even really any flight info, instead connecting takes you 
straight to the WIFI page. You have 4 options for WIFI, ranging from the 
“Hello” fare offering slow speeds just good enough for messaging with a 25 MB maximum, to the 
“Addicted” fare, which feels a little personal, offering speeds quote “ideal for watching short 
videos or your favorite series with a faster connection” and a 250 MB maximum. For the purposes of 
this review I went for the addicted fare and well… Yeah it sucks. I did still try to load up 
a video and I couldn't even get past the thumbnail. Maybe we are just in a bad spot 
though, so I'll check in with that later. [Flight Attendant] Ladies and gentlemen 
please remain seated with your [Flight Attendant] seatbelt securely fastened until 
the seatbelt sign has been switched off. Just as we finished messing with the WIFI, and 
our aircraft finished climbing up to cruise, the crew handed out our amenity kit! I 
know for economy, on a budget airline, this may seem impressive, but don't get too 
excited, It only contains a few simple items. First off we get an eye mask, 
sadly with the wrong destination, not that that actually matters much.
Earbuds, which are as awful as any. Disinfectant wipes, which I 
actually really do appreciate, I wish more airlines handed these out especially 
before meals so credit to French Bee here! And finally the main point of the kit, our meal 
voucher! We’ll need it to actually get the main course coming soon. This is because the meal, 
and this kit, isn't free. Only passengers who paid the €25, or those who have an upgraded 
fare type receive it, although I'm honestly still not certain what the point of the voucher 
is since anyone getting the kit gets the meal, and it shouldn't be any harder to distribute 
the meal than the kit was. The only thing I could think of is they are worried about 
people switching seats in between I guess. While we wait, we can take a quick look 
through the duty-free magazine. It has all you could ever wanna buy on a transatlantic 
flight, perfume, bracelets, new headphones, and something actually a bit more to my 
taste, a 1:200 model of their A350-1000, as well as some pretty cute bag tags. 
Finally in the back you will find a limited version of their menu, which we 
will see more of once we dive into the IFE, and of course we are on a European airline so the 
last page is entirely dedicated to cigarettes. And about 45 minutes after receiving our amenity 
kit, I turned in our voucher for our meal! This was actually our only option, unlike most 
airlines French Bee won't give you the choice between say “chicken or pasta” on the spot.
You can choose other specialty meals beforehand while booking or in your itinerary, but the 
main course is simply described as “basic meal” which can mean a lot of things. Say you 
eat meat but don't like chicken, based on this information should you go for one of the others 
in case the only option is chicken or risk it? Anyway, our main course today is in fact 
chicken, which I don't mind! Specifically we have a quote “Chicken Stew with Philadelphia 
Sauce and Tri-Coloured Pasta”. I'll be honest I have no idea what Philadelphia 
Sauce is, I've looked it up, maybe it's a sauce literally based on Philadelphia 
Cream Cheese, but I don't know, that doesn't seem very french. Tasting it didn't help clear that up 
much either because unfortunately the flavour of the sauce is incredibly muted. That also means 
the noodles combined with the sauce doesn't add up to much. To make up for it though the chicken 
itself is actually pretty good, so I'll take that! Alongside that the meal comes with 
one small complementary drink, I just went for some water this time. Your side 
salad is a plate of mildly spicy tabbouleh, which actually tastes pretty good initially 
but left me with a bit of a weird aftertaste. No problem though since I can quickly cover that 
up with a great sourdough roll that comes with either some cream cheese spread or butter. For 
dessert you have a very small chocolate brownie and carrot cake which I would have loved some more 
of, and finally a little lemon and ginger cookie. So overall, I'm surprised to say the meal is 
actually, okay. The main course is definitely not the highlight but the quality of the chicken saves 
it from being necessarily bad, and all the sides are pretty enjoyable, if not a little small.
Would I have spent €25 for this meal, plus the kit? Probably not, but 
I'm also not disappointed by it. A little after the meal I 
noticed us approaching Iceland, you know I've flown over this country 
quite a few times now but I've never actually had the opportunity to visit 
it. Hopefully one day I can change that. Now that things have settled down a bit, 
let's take a look through our seatback screen! French Bee uses the Thales Avant 
system with a fair 10-inch screen. First off, the selection of movies is shockingly 
small, just 55, and this is on a system that is at most 6 years old, so storage space 
shouldn't be a problem. I think they just cheaped out on licensing. At least there are 
still a few movies here that I can… rewatch. The TV section is somehow even worse, 
with 7 shows, 3 episodes each, and of course some of them aren't even the first 3.
If you can't find anything worth watching between the TV and movies, there is also a music 
section with 21 albums, and a games section. Aside from that French Bee has a digitized version 
of their duty-free menu we looked at earlier, as well as a cafe menu with a 
daily special, some noodles, and a set of pre-prepared sandwiches and wraps 
straight from your average grocery store, along with a set of snacks, and drinks, that 
actually go for pretty reasonable prices. French Bee also provides a full menu for their 
in-flight meals, which I'm a bit impressed by, especially in a world where most mainlines 
can't be bothered to do this anymore. I just wish you could see this menu at least 
a little in advance to know if you should order a specialty meal or not.
The inflight map is pretty archaic, it's non-interactive, with no extra views except 
a full screen version of basic flight info. Luckly I paid for WIFI so I should just be able to use 
Flightradar on my phone as an in-flight map, if the WIFI actually works, which it still doesn't.
And finally, since we are on an A350, we have access to exterior cameras! It 
turns out now is the perfect time to check it out too with this really cool view 
of the ice sheets approaching Greenland! I would love to get some sleep on this 
flight, but honestly I think the seat width makes that impossible for me, there 
is just no getting comfortable here, even though I can fully stretch out my legs. At least 
staying awake will let me catch more of Greenland. I'm still going to put my camera away for a bit 
though, try to relax, maybe rewatch some movies, I think I'll start with rewatching Bullet 
Train, and I'll see you in a few hours! And welcome back, over the Great Salt 
Lake! I tried my best to get some sleep, but the thinness of this seat forces 
me to constantly turn side to side to try and get comfortable, which makes 
that impossible. Thankfully though there is only about an hour and a half left in the 
flight so we’ll be free of these seats soon! While I wait for the breakfast to arrive, the 
lavatories are about as bland as they could be, but even after 10 hours this one is at least 
still well kept. This plane has 7 in total, weirdly enough all in the economy cabin, forcing those in premium economy to walk 
back into economy to use the lavatory, something I don't think I’ve ever seen before. And here is our breakfast! French Bee sells 
these pre-arrival meals as bundles. You can either buy a snack or breakfast item along with 
a cold or hot drink for €5, or with a cold and hot drink for 7. I went for the €7 bundle, but 
remember you can always buy any of the snacks or drinks from the cafe menu separately.
For my cold drink I got an orange juice which I'll probably save since it's sealed, my 
hot drink is a hot chocolate, nothing special, just your standard powdered stuff, and the 
breakfast item is of course a croissant. While it doesn't quite match the expectations 
I'd have for a french airline, it still tastes alright and at least manages to hold its shape. 
This actually beats the croissant I got last time I flew on Air France, although I don't know if 
that says more about Air France or French Bee. You know overall I think for €7 this 
little breakfast bundle is fair enough. [Pilot] Good afternoon from the 
flight deck, ladies and gentlemen, [Pilot] your Captain speaking. It is currently 
4:10 uh Pacific and uh, we should start [Pilot] the descent in a short while. We expect 
the landing in more or less 40 minutes [Pilot] from now. I hope you have enjoyed the flight 
with us, I wish you a safe return back home [Pilot] or a very pleasant stay in the US and I 
thank you for choosing French Bee today. So is French Bee worth it? Well in the end it's 
a budget airline, so what really matters is how much your comfort, or discomfort, is worth to you, 
and while I try to stay positive on this channel, I’ve gotta be honest, French Bee excels at the 
discomfort. The one thing they are ok at is the food, but it's still certainly nothing noteworthy, 
especially since paying the extra price for the food just tightens the price gap more. Aside 
from that, the WIFI was non-functional and a complete waste of money. The seatback screen could 
have been good if they had more than a handful of movies, most of which I've seen before! They 
sold me priority boarding that they then skipped over. I know that's a bit of a niche issue but 
that doesn't make it ok. And most importantly, these seats are way too thin! For a person 
of my size, and I think for most people, there is just no way to get comfortable, which 
means there is no way to sleep, and on a flight this long that means you are going to deal 
with some pretty bad jetlag. But I know for some people that might all still be worth it if it 
means saving some money, and on this Paris to LAX route for example, French Bee can absolutely 
be cheaper than its non-stop competition, but is actually often more expensive than airlines 
with one stop. The same is true for San Francisco, and New York, and even at Miami where they are 
the cheapest overall, it's not by much. So for me, I doubt I'll be giving French Bee another try 
anytime soon, I'd much rather just deal with a connection, or pay up a bit more, if it means 
seats that can actually fit me, and unless you are really small and think you can actually fit 
in these seats, I’d recommend you do the same. [Flight Attendant] You can now use your mobile phone.
On behalf of our Captain, [Flight Attendant] David Bernard and the entire crew, 
we would like to thank you [Flight Attendant] for flying with French Bee and hope
to see you again on board soon thank you. With that, welcome to Los Angeles! What do 
you think of French Bee, are you brave enough, or small enough, to try and survive 
these seats, and if you have already flown with them before, how did it go for you?
And finally with a proper view of our plane, I hope you enjoyed the review. I’m 
always looking to improve these reviews, so if you have any suggestions please don't 
hesitate to tell me in the comments below! If you would like to see more reviews like this 
don't forget to check out the channel page, and subscribe so you don't miss new releases!
With my bags collected, it's time for me to leave you here so I can catch my next 
flight home, thank you for watching and especially sticking around till the 
end, and I hope to see you again soon!
