reviews.transcript_full: [music] [music] >> Hello everyone and welcome back to another flight review. I am Savi and today we'll be continuing our journey with Singapore Airlines as we make our way from Singapore to Barcelona on board their Airbus A350 aircraft in economy class. But before we begin today's journey though, we first have to arrive here at Singapore Changi Airport after our 3-hour flight from Manila. And once we're on the ground, we'll have some time to explore the airport [music] before it's time to board our flight to Barcelona. So, without further ado, let's continue our journey. Our flight from Manila arrived into Terminal 2, where we had around 4 hours before our connecting flight to Barcelona. Terminal 2 serves as one of Singapore Airlines key operating terminals, handling many of the airlines regional flights across Asia, while a large portion of its long-haul services depart from the neighboring Terminal 3, and some at Terminal 1. Since we were connecting onto another SQ flight, there was no need to clear immigration or to collect our checked baggage. Instead, we could simply remain within Changi Airport's transit area before making our way to our next departure gate. And with that, let's see what Changi Airport has to offer during our layover. One of the things that makes the airport so convenient for connecting passengers is that the transit areas of Terminals 1, 2, and 3 are all seamlessly connected airside. This means you can freely move between terminals without clearing customs or immigration, making even shorter layovers surprisingly easy to enjoy. And Terminal 2 itself recently just underwent a major renovation, giving it a much brighter and more modern feel inspired by nature. Throughout the terminal, clear transfer signs also make navigating between terminals incredibly straightforward, even if it's your first time connecting to Changi. And with plenty more to see, it was time to hop on the Sky Train over to Terminal 3 and continue exploring. Before long, we arrived at Terminal 3, one of Singapore Airlines' main hubs and arguably the airport's most recognizable terminal. With its spacious layout, modern design, and huge selection of shops and restaurants, it's easy to see why so many travelers enjoy spending time here between flights. One attraction I was hoping to visit was the butterfly garden, the world's first butterfly garden inside an airport. Unfortunately, with only a few hours between flights, I just didn't have enough time to check it out this time around. And with boarding time slowly approaching, it was time to head over to Terminal 1, where our flight to Barcelona would be departing. One thing I'm personally not the biggest fan of at Changi Airport is the security screening at each departure gate. And while it does allow passengers to freely explore the terminals beforehand, it also means you'll need to allow a little extra time before boarding, especially if the queues start to build up. But, once everyone had made their way to security, it wasn't long before boarding began. Waiting for us this evening is this 6-year-old Airbus A350-900, registered as 9 Victor Sierra Mike Yankee, one of 65 A350s currently flying in Singapore Airlines' fleet. Unlike the original A350 we flew from Manila, this aircraft features the airline's dedicated long-haul configuration, accommodating 253 passengers across three classes, 42 in business class, 24 in premium economy, and 187 in economy. Now then, let's head on board. Before anything, a pair of complimentary earphones were handed out to all economy class passengers, ready to be used in KrisFlyer during this flight. Upon boarding, we were warmly welcomed by the lovely cabin crew before making our way through the cabin. Even after flying with the airline just a few hours earlier, it's always nice to be back on board one of their aircraft. The atmosphere on board has a calm and premium feel, which is something I really appreciate, especially on a long-haul flight. Tonight's flight features Singapore Airlines long-haul economy class cabin arranged in a 3-3-3 configuration. The seats come from JPA Design and were manufactured by Recaro, offering a respectable amount of personal space for a flight of this length. [music] For today's journey, we'll be seated in 52 alpha, a window seat on the left-hand side of the aircraft. Waiting at each seat was a blanket and a pillow, both of which would certainly come in handy on today's nearly 13-hour journey. The seat itself felt comfortable thanks to the decent amount of padding and the six-way adjustable headrests. Directly in front of us is the 11.6-in full HD touchscreen running the airline's KrisFlyer entertainment system. Legroom was also quite generous with enough space to stretch out for tonight's flight. Starting with the storage, there are a couple mini pockets built into the seat back, perfect for keeping smaller personal items. Then, there is the main literature pocket housing the air sickness bag, a safety card, the Wi-Fi information card, and a copy of the Silver Kris magazine. The tray table folds out from the seat back, which provides plenty of space for meals during the flight. And tucked underneath is also a small mirror, a thoughtful little feature that's handy on a long journey. >> [music] >> Beside the tray table is a dedicated cup holder, allowing you to keep your drink within easy reach, even when the tray table is folded away. And just beneath the entertainment screen is another small storage compartment. And located on the lower left of the seat back are the USB A charging port, the headphone jack, the reading light button, and the cabin crew call button, all within easy reach while seated. Meanwhile, a universal power outlet is located beneath the seat. Then, overhead you'll find the individual reading lights, but one feature that's absent, however, is the individual air vents. With boarding still under way, let's take this opportunity to have a closer look at Singapore Airlines' KrisWorld entertainment system. The system offers an extensive [music] selection movies, TV shows, live TV channels, music, and a detailed in-flight map giving passengers plenty of ways to stay entertained throughout the journey. Before long, boarding was complete and the cabin crew began making their final preparations ahead of our departure. >> On behalf of my crew, I'd welcome you on board our flight SQ 388 from Singapore to Barcelona. The flight time for this flight is 13 hours and 30 minutes, 1330. We meet in the flight deck with our Captain Maxwell, Senior First Officer Rahman Hassan, Senior First Officer Lee Yong Ming, and in the cabin you have your in-flight managers, Mr. Lim Hock Chai, and the rest of the cabin crew will make sure that all of you are well looked after and certain you are enjoying your flight with us. For your safety, I do recommend that you always keep your seat belt fastened while seated just in case of some bumpy weather along the route. We'll be departing shortly. The progress of the flight is available to you on your in-flight entertainment system, KrisWorld. In the meantime, please sit back, relax, and enjoy the flight. Thank you for choosing Singapore Airlines. >> Welcome on board Singapore Airlines. As the safety equipment on this aircraft may differ from that on other aircraft, please give us your attention as we bring you through this important safety briefing and on a journey across our island. >> There are details you would not want to miss. >> [music] >> During takeoff and landing, ensure that your tray table is stowed away. Put the back of your seat upright >> [music] >> and keep your shoes on. Before we take off, stow your luggage under the seat in front [music] of you or in the overhead compartments. >> Life vests are located under or between your seats. Before using an evacuation slide, remove high-heeled [music] shoes and leave all belongings behind. Slide down sitting upright with your arms in front and focus on the landing area. Thank you for your attention and we hope you enjoy discovering the rich details that make Singapore home. Please refer to the safety card located in the seat pocket in front of you for more information. [music] >> And on behalf of Singapore Airlines, we wish you a great time on board as well as anywhere in the world we take you. >> Cabin crew take off stations, please. Ladies and gentlemen, please fasten your seat belts and draw up your window shades. Thank you. >> The seatbelt sign is now off. For your safety, always keep your seatbelt fastened while seated. When the seatbelt sign is on, toilets should not be used and hot beverage service will be suspended. Infants must be carried out from the bassinets and secured with an infant seatbelt. >> Shortly after takeoff, the cabin crew came through the cabin offering hot towels to every passenger. A thoughtful touch before the first meal service. And before long, it was time for dinner to be served. Well, technically, our second dinner of the day after the one on our previous flight. But, who's complaining? This evening, passengers had a choice between the chicken meatball marinara pasta or the sweet and sour fish served with egg fried rice. For this meal, I went with the chicken meatball marinara pasta. As for my drink, I went with Singapore Sling, one of Singapore's signature cocktails. It's made with gin, pineapple juice, cherry liqueur, and a dash of citrus. I found it to be light, fruity, and refreshing. A bottle of water was provided alongside the meal. The meal was served alongside a smoked salmon with honey mustard coleslaw as the appetizer. A warm bread roll with some unsalted butter, cheese and crackers, and a peach and strawberry crumble with vanilla sauce for dessert. Overall, it was a well-presented meal with generous portions. The pasta was cooked well, the meatballs were tender, and the rich marinara sauce brought everything together nicely. The smoked salmon appetizer was also a refreshing way to start the meal, while the peach and strawberry crumble was a fitting dessert to round everything off. With dinner finished, I thought it'd be a good opportunity to take a look at one of the economy class lavatories. As expected, it was clean, modern, and well-maintained. The toilet itself was spotless even a few hours into the flight, and there's also a fold-down baby changing table for those traveling with young children. And beside the sink, you'll find a stack of disposable cups for passengers to use if needed. And inside the storage drawers were a few extra essentials including dental kits, additional air sickness bags, and the sanitary napkins. >> With dinner finished, the cabin lights were dimmed as many passengers settled in for the night. After a restful night's sleep, the cabin came alive as the lights were brightened ahead of our arrival into Barcelona. At 1:00 after wrist, the cabin crew began serving breakfast. This morning, passengers had a choice between scrambled eggs with cheese and chicken sausage or international dim sum selection. For breakfast, I went with the dim sum selection consisting of lo mai fan, steamed glutinous rice with Chinese sausage and black mushrooms served alongside pork siu mai. As for my drink, I went with orange juice. While a bottle of water was also provided alongside the meal. The meal was served with yogurt, a selection of seasonal fresh fruit, and a warm bread roll with salted butter. >> All in all, it was another enjoyable meal. The lor mai fun was flavorful and satisfying, but the pork siu mai complemented it nicely. And combined with the fresh fruit, yogurt, and the bread roll, it made for a well-balanced breakfast before landing. Shortly after breakfast, something outside the window immediately caught my attention. At first, I thought it was a comet, but the longer I looked at it, the more it resembled what could have been rocket debris. Whatever it was, it was an incredible sight. If you know what it might have been, let me know in the comments below. As fascinating as that sight was, it wasn't long before the captain came over the PA to announce our initial descent into Barcelona. >> to Barcelona, and uh we'll commence in descent in approximately 15 minutes. Weather for Barcelona is reported to be partly cloudy, drizzling at this moment over the airfield with a ground temperature of 11° C, 11° C. Our new arrival time into Barcelona will be at 7:15 local time, 7:15. There is a 6-hour time difference between Singapore and Barcelona. Local time now is 6:28, 6:28. I trust you enjoyed the flight, and thank you for choosing Singapore Airlines. Cabin crew, prepare aircraft for arrival. >> [music] >> Singapore Airlines once again delivered an excellent long haul experience. The comfortable seat, extensive legroom, entertainment system, enjoyable meal services, and consistently attentive cabin crew made the flight pass by much quicker than I expected. >> [music] >> Looking back, it's hard to believe we were already preparing for landing. Whether it's aboard their flagship Airbus A380 or the state-of-the-art Airbus A350, one thing that has remained consistent throughout my flights with the airline is the high standard of comfort and service. If you're considering flying Singapore Airlines on one of their long haul flights, this is definitely a product I'd have no hesitation recommending. And as our journey came to an end, all that was left to do was sit back, relax, and enjoy the arrival into Barcelona. >> [music] >> Welcome to Barcelona, ladies and gentlemen. Please remain seated with your seatbelt fastened until the seatbelt sign is off. Please take care when opening the overhead compartment and remember to take all your belongings with you. It's been our pleasure serving you on this flight. Thank you for flying Singapore Airlines, a member of Star Alliance. >> [music] >> It's on this day that And we've arrived here in Barcelona, bringing our journey from Singapore to an end. It was certainly a memorable way to begin our European adventure. If you enjoyed this review or found it helpful, I'd really appreciate it if you could leave a like and consider subscribing to the channel for more aviation and travel content. I've got plenty more flights from this trip coming up, so be sure to stay tuned. And as always, thank you so much for watching and I'll see you all in the next one. Take care.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello everyone and welcome back to NMB Global where you join us here from Doha in Qatar. You have to excuse the fact that I've got no makeup on today. It's 40° and if I even attempted to put any on, it would melt straight off. Even just being out here for 5 minutes, I'm already sweating. So you might be wondering how do we get here? So we flew from Amsterdam Schiphol to Doha in Qatar and in this video you're going to see what the journey was like. So we did book the Qsuite but whether we got to travel in them is a different story. So follow along, watch the video and see what we get up to. So the video starts here at Schiedam train station in Holland. So we actually got a ferry crossing over from England to Holland and then got the train from the port to Schiphol Airport. The train journey took around an hour and a half and we had to change here at the train station in Schiedam. It was a relatively easy task and as you can see our double-decker train there, it was very full because we traveled in rush hour. So we did have to stand for most of the time but here we are, we've arrived at the train station at Schiphol and it's time to go and check in. Now the reason that we're flying from Schiphol instead of a London airport which is obviously closer to home for us is because we booked this flight using Avios and obviously when you do that you still have to pay the taxes and flying from a European airport is always so much cheaper than flying from London. So that is the reason we've done this and Holland is easy enough to get to for us. So it's a win-win situation. Welcome to another Travel Expertos flight review. Today, I’m flying Turkish Airlines Business Class from Geneva, Switzerland, to Istanbul, Türkiye, onboard the Airbus A321neo. We’ll be traveling on flight TK1920, connecting Geneva with Turkish Airlines’ enormous global hub at Istanbul Airport. And although this is only a narrow-body Airbus A321neo, the Business Class experience is quite different from what you normally find on flights within Europe. Instead of standard Economy Class seats with the middle seat blocked, this aircraft features a dedicated Business Class cabin in a 2-2 configuration, with significantly wider seats, generous legroom, individual entertainment screens and considerably more recline. Our aircraft for today’s journey is TC-LTL, a Turkish Airlines Airbus A321neo. The journey starts at Geneva Airport, where we’ll check in and make our way through security and passport control before heading to the non-Schengen C gates. We’ll then visit the Aspire Lounge, do some plane spotting and watch our A321neo arrive in Geneva before heading to gate C51. Once onboard, I’ll show you the Business Class cabin and my window seat, 5A. We’ll also take a detailed look at the seat itself, the inflight entertainment system, complimentary Business Class Wi-Fi, onboard menu and the full dinner service. Later in the flight, I’ll show you the lavatory, bedding and pre-arrival service before we descend over the lights of Istanbul for a spectacular nighttime arrival. So sit back, relax, and welcome onboard this Turkish Airlines Airbus A321neo Business Class journey from Geneva to Istanbul. Let’s get started. And our journey begins here at Geneva Airport. Let’s head inside Terminal 1 and check in for flight TK1920. Our first stop is the Turkish Airlines check-in area. One of the ground benefits of traveling in Business Class is access to dedicated priority check-in After presenting the required travel documents and checking in for the flight, our boarding passes are ready. With check-in completed, it’s time to continue toward security. Business Class passengers can benefit from priority facilities at Geneva Airport, helping to reduce the amount of time spent waiting in line. In no time the security is done, once again fast track security always saves a lot of time when flying. With the security control finished it is time to head to the non-schengen area with C gates in the other part of the airport.  But before we need to complete passport control. And welcome to Geneva Airport’s C-gate terminal. This part of the airport handles non-Schengen international flights and feels noticeably quieter and more separated from the main Schengen departure areas. Our Turkish Airlines flight to Istanbul will depart later from gate C51. Looking outside today, the weather in Geneva isn’t exactly perfect. This new terminal was officially opened on 14th of December 2021. With huge windows and modern structure it is a huge improvement. We still have plenty of time until boarding. And since we’re traveling in Business Class, our next stop is the lounge. For today’s flight, we have access to the Aspire Lounge in Geneva’s non-Schengen area. The lounge provides a comfortable place to spend the time before departure, away from the main gate area. Inside, there are different seating areas with sofas, armchairs and tables. One of the nicest parts of the lounge is the large amount of natural light coming through the floor-to-ceiling windows. Inside the lounge you will find a full Coffee machine to make any type of coffee you can think of. The lounge is located above the terminal on the second floor overseeing the waiting area.  Personally I like this lounge because it is modern and has plenty of seating options : sofas, single seats and much more. Lounge also features the departure and arrival table with updated information of arrival, departure and gate. And for aviation enthusiasts, those windows offer something even better: direct views across the airport apron. There is also a self-service food and beverage selection. With both hot and cold options. Overall it is a well stocked buffet and beverage area and a great lounge. I decided to have something relatively light before the flight, consisting of a mixed salad with tomatoes, some cold cuts and cheese, together with several pieces of bread and a drink. One advantage of these large windows is the excellent view over Geneva Airport. Geneva sees an interesting combination of traffic. Alongside the large number of European short-haul flights, the airport also receives long-haul aircraft and significant private aviation traffic. The runway is visible beyond the apron, while the mountains surrounding Geneva provide the backdrop. The weather today is still grey and rainy, but that isn’t stopping operations. As you can see I am really enjoying my time so far on this trip and particularly in this lounge. And while we’re watching the traffic outside, there is one aircraft in particular that we’re waiting for. Our Turkish Airlines A321neo from Istanbul. So let's head to the gate and see our plane arrive. But firstly a British Airways is landing in Geneva. Despite the grey weather outside, you can still watch aircraft movements from the Terminal. And now please enjoy this Turkish A321Neo touching down in Geneva. Let me properly introduce Turkish Airlines. Turkish Airlines is the national flag carrier of Türkiye and one of the world’s largest international airlines. The airline was founded on 20 May 1933 and is headquartered in Istanbul, Türkiye. Turkish Airlines operates under the IATA code TK and uses Istanbul Airport as its main global hub. The airline began operations with just five aircraft and has since developed into one of the world’s most extensive international carriers. Turkish Airlines currently serves destinations across more countries than any other airline in the world, connecting Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and the Americas through Istanbul. The airline has been a member of Star Alliance since 2008 and operates its Miles&Smiles frequent-flyer program. Its fleet includes aircraft from the Airbus A320 family, Airbus A330, Airbus A350, Boeing 737, Boeing 777 and Boeing 787 families. Turkish Airlines is particularly well known for its Business Class service, extensive international network and premium onboard catering. At the 2025 Skytrax World Airline Awards, Turkish Airlines was named Europe’s Best Airline and also received awards for Europe’s Best Business Class and the World’s Best Business Class Onboard Catering. Boarding time is approaching, so it’s time to head back take our belongings and leave the Aspire Lounge. From here, we make the short walk through the C-gate terminal toward our departure gate. Our flight today is leaving from gate C51. Before boarding, here’s one final look at our aircraft. Today’s flight is operated by a 3 year old Turkish Airlines Airbus A321neo TC-LTL. The aircraft is wearing Turkish Airlines’ familiar white fuselage and red tail, and despite the rainy conditions, we have a very good view of it from inside the terminal. Boarding area is well separated into 3lines one for Business and two for Economy. Boarding is now underway. Business Class passengers receive priority boarding, allowing us to make our way onto the aircraft ahead of most Economy Class passengers. We walk down the jet bridge closer and closer to our today's aircraft. Turkish Airlines has installed dedicated premium recliner seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration so I am looking forward to it. This plane has a 2-2 configuration in Business Class and 3-3 configuration in Economy Class. Welcome onboard Turkish Airlines A321Neo in Business Class. My seat on today's flight is 5A. There are two seats on either side of the aisle, with significantly wider seating than in Economy Class. Each passenger has a large individual entertainment screen installed in the seat in front and the legroom is excellent. Later on the cabin crew passed by with menus and the selection of pre departure drinks. I went with Turkish signature strawberry juice and it was delicious. The IFE alone is in countless languages such as Turkish, French, English, Spanish, German and much more. With boarding completed the safety video began play. Once the doors are closed, the cabin crew begins preparing the aircraft for departure. The cabin is checked, bags are secured, seats are returned to the required position and everything is prepared for pushback. While we wait, this is also a good opportunity to appreciate the cabin itself. Because the seats are arranged 2-2 rather than the 3-3 layout found behind us in Economy Class, the front of the A321neo feels much more spacious. The high seat backs and dividers around the headrest also provide some additional separation between passengers. Obviously, this isn't the level of privacy you would get from a modern Business Class suite with a door. But that's not really the purpose of this product. For a narrow-body aircraft operating flights of a few hours, the combination of a wide recliner seat substantial legroom, entertainment and full Business Class service is very competitive. As you can see I am really looking forward to this flight, and this is just the first leg of our journey to Miami. So stick around the channel because a Turkish Airlines B787 from Istanbul to Miami is coming up later. As we are ready to pushback the seat must return to its original position together with the drink holder between the two seats. We begin pushing back from the gate.  The jet bridge is disconnected, ground equipment is moved away, and the engines are started. After spending the last few hours watching this aircraft arrive and being prepared from inside the terminal, we’re finally onboard and moving. With pushback completed, the ground crew clears the aircraft and we begin our taxi. The inflight map is a great feature on every flight because you can see exactly where you are and how much until your arrival. We’re now taxiing across Geneva Airport toward runway 04. The apron is still wet from the rain, and the grey skies have remained with us throughout the afternoon. From seat 5A, we have an excellent view outside as we make our way toward the runway. Geneva operates with a single main concrete runway for commercial aircraft, so virtually all of the airport's airline traffic uses the same runway. Geneva Airport is the main international airport serving Geneva and western Switzerland and is located approximately four kilometres northwest of Geneva city centre. The airport opened in 1920 and has developed into one of Switzerland’s busiest and most important international gateways. It operates under the IATA code GVA and serves as an important base for airlines including easyJet Switzerland, while SWISS also maintains a significant presence at the airport. Geneva Airport is unusual for having a single main runway, which at approximately 3,900 metres is one of the longest in Switzerland. The airport handles flights across Europe as well as services to destinations in North America, the Middle East and Africa Today, we’ll be departing from runway 04. After a short taxi, we approach the holding point. The cabin is secured. And we’re ready for takeoff. Enjoy the rainy take off out of Geneva Switzerland. And we are in the air. We climb away from the runway and leave Geneva behind as we begin our journey east toward Istanbul. From the window, the airport quickly disappears beneath us as the aircraft continues climbing through the cloud layer. The A321neo's engines settle into their climb power as we gain altitude. Our journey from Switzerland to Türkiye is now properly underway. For the next few minutes, I’ll let you enjoy the departure from seat 5A. Now that we’re safely in the air, let’s properly explore what Turkish Airlines offers in Business Class on the Airbus A321neo. The IFE screen is movable according to passengers needs. A large and fluffy pillow is provided to every passenger in Business Class. There is a coat hanger located next to the IFE screen, together with extra storage pocket and endless legroom. The tray table is located in the armrest of your seat and comes up by a touch of a button. The tray table folds out and is well balanced and steady. Let's take a look of today's Business Class Menu. Between the two seats there is a small divider located at eye view for extra privacy. Cabin crew comes by to take orders for dinner. Seat 5A features a wide leather seat with an adjustable headrest and plenty of padding. We are on our way to Istanbul when the sun begins to set.  The seat controls are conveniently positioned beside the passenger  and allow the seat to be moved into a more relaxed reclined position. The leg rest comes up by a touch of a button. Cabin crew comes by and hands out hot towel prior to dinner. The Row pitch is 45", seat width
21" and seat recline 5". Between the two seats is a substantial fixed center console with power socket and extra storage space. Headphones are also located inside it. IFE remote control sits inside and is easy usable and adaptable.  Turkish Airlines also provides individually packaged wired over-ear headphones to every passanger. They're relatively simple headphones rather than a particularly high-end noise-cancelling set,  but having proper over-ear headphones is still useful for watching entertainment during the flight. One of the strongest features of this A321neo is the inflight entertainment system. Every Business Class passenger has a large individual touchscreen installed directly in front of them. Turkish Airlines' entertainment system provides several different categories. There are movies, TV programs, music, children's entertainment and games, as well as additional destination and airline content. It is really one of the best IFE out there with countless of options, but easy to navigate and organized. Turkish Airlines Planet IFE has previously offered nearly 400 movies, more than 750 TV series, documentaries and other programs, around 1,500 music albums with more than 20,000 tracks, as well as games and other entertainment. The selection includes Turkish and international movies, recent releases, TV series, documentaries, music and games. And the entertainment screen isn't the only connectivity option. This aircraft is also equipped with onboard Wi-Fi. For this flight, my Business Class internet package included 1,024 megabytes of complimentary data together with unlimited messaging. There is also an interactive flight information section. The moving map allows you to follow the aircraft's progress between Geneva and Istanbul and explore the route from different perspectives. At this point, the system is showing an estimated arrival into Istanbul at 22:52. As the time flies by we are approaching dinner time, together with a beautiful view of the outside.  For the starter, I had the chicken, fried eggplant and tomato salad, served with süzme yoghurt. The chicken is presented in slices together with pieces of roasted eggplant and tomato, with some fresh greens underneath. Alongside the starter, Turkish Airlines also serves marinated artichokes in olive oil. So far the starter and the whole dining experience is delicious and I am looking forward to the main course. And then came my main course.
I chose the homemade mantı with braised lamb shank. Mantı is a traditional Turkish dumpling dish, and here it is served with a large piece of braised lamb shank in the center,  together with slow-roasted tomato sauce, yoghurt and red pepper oil. There is also a small cheese selection, fresh bread with butter, and the strawberry and cream roll for dessert, all already arranged around the main plate. We’re flying on a narrow-body A321neo from Geneva to Istanbul,  yet this feels much closer to a proper long-haul Business Class meal than the basic catering you often receive on European flights. Let's head to the front and explore the business class lavatory. There is a dark sink and countertop area, a brightly illuminated mirror, hot and cold water controls and several pump-bottle toiletries around the sink. There is also a tissue dispenser together with branded amenities. Everything is reasonably clean and well presented during our visit. There isn't a dramatically different or larger dedicated Business Class bathroom, but the additional toiletries are a welcome touch. The lavatory was also kept spotless through out the flight. And now let's head back to our seat. The seat can be moved into a substantially reclined position, it makes the seat really comfortable for relaxing and even sleeping. And there is a large blanket, which makes the seat significantly more comfortable once you're settled in. With the  blanket over me and entertainment playing on the screen, this becomes a very comfortable place to spend the remainder of the flight. And because of the generous pitch, even in the reclined position you don't feel particularly cramped. In the meantime let's dive inside the IFE entertainment and play a movie. As we get closer to Istanbul, the crew begins another small service before arrival. We are given packages of Turkish Airlines roasted Turkish hazelnuts. Water is served alongside the snack in proper glassware. Once again, a hot towel is distributed through the cabin. It's a simple service, but a nice final touch before landing. As we slowly approaching Istanbul the cabin lights are dimmed for last relaxation before our arrival. Turkish airlines have a stunning and beautiful lighting in their planes which makes the flight feel even more comfortable. As we are approaching our destination it is already pitched dark outside with only few lights visible. The atmosphere inside the cabin begins to change as we are on or final approach to Istanbul. Blankets are put away, seats are returned to their upright positions and the cabin crew completes the final checks. Cabin lights are dimmed and we prepare for a stunning night landing into Istanbul. And before we begin the final approach, it’s time for my conclusion on Turkish Airlines Business Class onboard the Airbus A321neo. For a narrow-body aircraft, this is a genuinely strong Business Class product. The biggest advantage is obviously the seat. Instead of receiving a normal Economy seat with the middle seat blocked, you get a proper wide Business Class recliner in a 2-2 configuration. The seat provides excellent legroom, significantly more width and enough recline to properly relax. Every passenger receives an individual entertainment screen, a large selection of content, an interactive moving map and onboard Wi-Fi. On this flight, Business Class included 1,024 MB of complimentary internet plus unlimited messaging. From the pre-departure welcome drink to the hot towel, full dinner service, several main-course options, proper tableware and the pre-arrival snack. And a complete Business Class service from boarding until arrival. Overall, Turkish Airlines offers one of the more substantial narrow-body Business Class experiences you can find on routes of this length. And with that, our flight from Geneva is almost over. Thank you very much for watching this Travel Expertos flight review. If you enjoyed the video, make sure to leave a like and subscribe to the channel for more Business Class, First Class and full flight reviews from around the world. Now, there’s only one thing left to do. Enjoy the nighttime approach and landing into Istanbul. Welcome to Istanbul. Our Airbus A321neo slows down and exits the runway. We’ve successfully completed flight TK1920 from Geneva. But the journey isn't completely finished yet. Istanbul Airport is one of the largest aviation hubs in the world, and after leaving the runway, we still have to taxi across the enormous airport complex toward our gate. Turkish Airlines operates its main global hub here, with flights connecting Istanbul to countless of destinations, throughout Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and the Americas. Istanbul Airport is the main international airport serving Istanbul and one of the largest aviation hubs in the world. The airport officially opened in 2018 and took over the majority of commercial passenger operations from Istanbul Atatürk Airport in 2019. Located on the European side of Istanbul near the Black Sea, it operates under the IATA code IST and serves as the main global hub of Turkish Airlines. The airport was designed to handle the rapid expansion of Turkish Airlines and Istanbul’s growing role as a major connecting point between Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Istanbul Airport features one of the world’s largest airport terminal buildings under a single roof and has multiple runways capable of handling simultaneous operations. The terminal offers extensive shopping, restaurants, lounges and passenger facilities, while Turkish Airlines operates its flagship Business and Miles&Smiles lounges here. Thanks to Turkish Airlines’ enormous international network, Istanbul Airport has developed into one of the most important connecting hubs for passengers travelling between different regions of the world. Turkish Airlines offers Business Class across much of its international network, although the product varies significantly depending on the aircraft type. On long-haul flights, the airline operates Business Class on aircraft including the Airbus A350-900, Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, Boeing 777-300ER and Airbus A330 family, while narrow-body aircraft such as the Airbus A321neo and selected Boeing 737s are commonly used on European, Middle Eastern and regional services. The newest long-haul products can be found on aircraft such as the Boeing 787-9 and Airbus A350-900, with lie-flat seating, personal storage, large entertainment screens and enhanced privacy. The Boeing 787-9, for example, features a 1-2-1 Business Class configuration providing direct aisle access for every passenger and an 18-inch entertainment screen. Older wide-body aircraft such as the Boeing 777-300ER also feature seats that convert into fully flat beds, although some configurations do not provide direct aisle access to every passenger. On shorter routes, Turkish Airlines differs from many European airlines by offering dedicated Business Class seats on aircraft such as the Airbus A321neo  rather than simply blocking the middle Economy Class seat. The A321neo Business Class features larger reclining seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration, together with personal entertainment screens, with Turkish Airlines specifying a 13-inch high-resolution screen in Business Class and onboard Wi-Fi on the aircraft. Across its Business Class operation, Turkish Airlines places a particularly strong emphasis on catering and service, while its seat features can include lie-flat beds of up to 193 centimetres, power outlets, USB charging, privacy screens, storage and large entertainment displays, although the exact features depend on the aircraft. At this time of the day Istanbul airport is particularly busy with many planes arriving and leaving. Similar to Emirates and Qatar, Turkish Airlines build their hub and airline on connectivity. Eventually, we approach our parking position. After complete Business Class journey from Geneva, we’ve arrived. The seatbelt sign is switched off and passengers begin collecting their belongings. It’s time to leave seat 5A. Before stepping off, we get one final look at the Turkish Airlines A321neo Business Class cabin. Thank you to the Turkish Airlines crew for today’s exceptional flight and experience. And goodbye to TC-LTL. After leaving the aircraft, we enter Istanbul Airport. For us, the journey isn't ending here, so we follow the signs for international transfers. Istanbul is Turkish Airlines' primary hub and is specifically designed around large numbers of connecting passengers. We walk towards specific Turkish Airlines Business security control line and pass to the international terminal. This is not the end of our journey as we will be continuing to Miami, onboard their B787 in Business Class. So if you want to find more about that experience definitely stay put because the video will be coming out soon. In the meantime let's head to Turkish Airlines Business class lounge and rest until our flight to Miami starts. And I’ll see you onboard the next flight. Thanks for watching and fly safe.

reviews.transcript_full: [music] [music] [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Hey there, and welcome to Tokyo Haneda Airport for another trip report. Today, I'm checking out All Nippon Airways international economy class product on board their Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, where we'll put the whole experience to the test [music] on a 12-hour flight from Tokyo to Houston. Haneda Airport is the smaller of Tokyo's two major international airports, serving as [music] the primary domestic base for both ANA and JAL, and also handling a large number of international flights from both Japanese and foreign carriers. It is significantly closer to the city of Tokyo than the alternative Narita Airport, with Haneda located just 15 km south of Tokyo Station. Haneda Airport consists of three terminals named 1, 2, and 3, with terminal [music] 1 used exclusively for domestic flights, terminal 2 handling both domestic and international flights, and terminal 3 handling only international flights. I just arrived at Haneda off an ANA flight from Osaka, which parked at the terminal 2 south gates, and my flight to Houston departs from terminal 3. [music] To transfer to terminal 3, there's a shuttle bus that runs every 15 minutes or less between 7:00 a.m. and midnight. >> [music] >> The bus goes first to the terminal 2 north gates, which takes 5 minutes, and then it's another 20 minutes to terminal 3. >> [music] [snorts] >> After stepping off the bus at terminal 3, you head up to the main departures check-in hall where you have to re-clear security screening and then clear Japanese exit passport control. On domestic to international itineraries here at Haneda, check luggage is transferred to automatically, so I didn't need to claim it and re-check it here in Tokyo. Overall, this isn't the quickest or simplest transfer process, taking 40 minutes from when I got off my first flight to reaching the gate area of Terminal 3. Coming out of security, we have some helpful flight information boards and terminal maps indicating distances to each gate. My flight to Houston is using gate 109 today, about 250 m down the terminal to the right. There's plenty of high-end shopping throughout the terminal, including duty-free, as well as restaurants and several airline and contract lounges. Reaching gate 109, let's take a look at our aircraft. Taking me across the Pacific today is an 8 and 1/2-year-old Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner that was delivered new to ANA in November 2015 and is one of the aircraft painted in the special Star Alliance paint colors. As of August 2024, ANA had a fleet of 44 Boeing 787-9s with an additional four on order. They have three different seating configurations for these aircraft with two international seating plans and one seating plan solely for high-density domestic flights. Each of the international cabin configurations features business class, premium economy, and economy class with the key difference between the two configurations being the number of seats in each cabin. Our aircraft for today is the lower-density version with only 215 seats on board in total, split between 48 business class, 21 premium economy, and 146 economy class. ANA starts their boarding process with pre-boarding for those who need extra time to get on board and then proceeds with boarding by assigned group numbers 1 through 5, with group 1 for Diamond Service Members, group 2 for business class, Platinum Service Members, Super Flyers Members, and Star Alliance Gold members and groups three, four, and five for premium economy and economy class passengers. Stepping on board, we pass through the rear section of the business class cabin first with flatbed seats in a 1-2-1 layout and then into the premium economy cabin with three rows of recliner seats in a 2-3-2 configuration. The economy class cabin at the rear is split into two sections with a small three-row section first followed by a larger cabin with 14 [music] rows. The 146 seats in economy are in a 3-3-3 layout and I'm booked in seat 28A for this flight, which is a window seat on the left side of the aircraft in the larger cabin. Every seat is equipped with a 9-in personal touchscreen entertainment system with a built-in remote control, power outlets, and USB charging. >> [music] [music] >> The seats have a plush fabric back and base and are immaculately clean with height-adjustable headrests at the top that have folding sides to provide extra support. In terms of recline, these seats only have a couple inches of recline available, but on the plus side, they have absolutely phenomenal legroom. Economy class seats on this aircraft have a pitch of 34 in, whereas most international carriers have economy configurations with a standard pitch of 31 in. The The seats have a width of 17.3 in, which is fairly standard when compared to other airlines. Every seat also has a footrest which flips down from the seat in front and is actually comfortable to use as opposed to feeling cramped as I find in most cases. Looking at storage space in the seat, there's tons of space under the seat in front for my large backpack and no chair legs between my window seat and the middle seat to block that storage access. There's also plenty of overhead bin space down both sides of each aisle. Power outlets are located under the seat row with an AC power outlet available per seat. >> [music] >> Taking a closer look at the seatback in front, at the top we have our entertainment screen with a headphone port and USB charging port on the bottom edge. To the right of the screen, we have a small hook for hanging your jacket or headphones, and below the screen there's the remote control which pops out for use to control the screen instead of using the touchscreen function. Below the remote, there's a bifold tray table which flips out for use with a built-in cup holder, and the whole table's mounted on rails to adjust its position. Below the tray table near the bottom of the seatback, we have a pocket for storing the provided materials and a mesh pouch on the outside for your own items. Taking a look at the provided materials, we have an air sickness bag and the safety information card for the Boeing 787. A set of over-ear headphones were also provided at the seat when we boarded to use with the entertainment system, along with a soft, comfortable pillow and blanket. Taking a look at the overhead panel up above the seat, here we have personal reading lights but no adjustable air vents on this aircraft. On the whole, it's a modern, spacious, and comfortable cabin ticking just about all my boxes for a long-haul international flight. >> Please place your baggage in the overhead compartments or under the seat in front, and do not stack items on top of each other. Electronic devices is prohibited in the cabin, including the aisle and lavatory. >> [music] >> Prepare now ladies for takeoff. Please make sure that your seat belt is securely fastened. Please hold it tight on your lap. >> Climbing away from Haneda Airport and turning east to head out over the Pacific, these eastbound Asia to North America flights are neat because with the time difference and crossing the international date line, we'll actually arrive in Houston earlier on the same day than when we had left Tokyo. Our departure time from Tokyo was 10:30 a.m. and we'll land in Houston at 8:30 a.m. on the same day. Because this is a morning departure, I don't expect to get much sleep. My goal is to stay awake for the first portion of the flight and then uh hopefully somewhere near the end to get a couple hours of sleep to help me make it through that next day. >> [music] >> Before the first service of the flight, let's check out the entertainment system. [music] Getting into the system, a mini safety video plays first talking about in-flight turbulence and highlighting ANA's commitment to a super high level of safety. [music] After that, a slide noting that you can request in-flight magazines from the cabin crew at any time. Then we reach [music] the main content page, which is divided into on-demand content under the sky channel section and live TV content under the sky live section, as well [music] as sections for shopping, kids, info, maps, and ebooks. Checking out the on-demand content, there's a guide here for how to use the remote to control the screen, [music] which allows you to navigate, select content, and adjust the volume, and control the overhead reading light and attendant call button. In terms of the content available, there's a good range of on-demand movies with titles grouped by different categories, [music] from new releases to Japanese movies. We have on-demand TV shows with content grouped by ANA original titles, [music] content from HBO Max, and other genres. There's a new section with audio tracks from either NHK or BBC. >> [music] >> In the audio section, we have music playlists and audiobooks. And under the live TV section, we have CNN, Sport 24, and NHK News. The onboard shopping guide has all the duty-free items available on board, [music] and the ability to build a cart in the screen. There's a seat-to-seat messaging service through these screens as well, and the keyboard on the back of the remote control allows you to type messages for this service. There's a kid section with movies, TV shows, and music targeted to kids. [music] There's an info section with information about ANA, their products and services, including how to connect to the onboard Wi-Fi, and airport guides, and customs and immigration information. The last content section is [music] ebooks with the selection mostly focused on ANA and Japan tourism content. >> [music] >> Overall, the screen feels a little bit dated, but is fairly straightforward to navigate and responds quickly to commands. One of the cool features of the 787 Dreamliner is the dimmable window shades, as opposed to having standard pull-down shades. These dimmers have five different levels of light permeation, from fully black out to no dimming. The cabin crew handed out cleansing towelettes, and about 40 minutes after takeoff, they commenced the first service of the flight. On this 12-hour flight, there are two full meal services and two snack services, with water served periodically throughout the flight. The first service is a snack, consisting of a snack mix and a beverage service which included complimentary beer and wine. About 40 minutes after the snack, lunch was served. The flight attendants had menu placards showing the different options available with the choice for this meal between either beef sukiyaki with rice or seafood rice gratin. I opted for the sukiyaki which came with five different tray items. We have a starter mix salad with a packet of Italian dressing followed by an appetizer tray of smoked duck and potato salad. Then we have a kobachi dish of simmered daikon radish served with minced chicken sauce and a dish of soft cheese with crackers. And finally, the main course which looks pretty tasty. The tray was provided with a standard cutlery packet and serviette in addition to a set of chopsticks. A water bottle was also provided with the tray and a beverage service was offered as well and I opted for the green tea served chilled. The appetizer and kobachi dishes didn't really do it for me but the sukiyaki was really good. As I was wrapping up making my way through the tray, the cabin crew passed through with the sixth and final food course, mini Häagen-Dazs vanilla ice creams for dessert. When the cabin crew cleared the meal trays, they offered black or green tea as well as coffee. With 9 and 1/2 hours to go, let's hop up to explore the cabin. Standing at the back of the aircraft where the main economy galley is located, there are four lavatories available to economy class passengers with three in the mid section between the two economy cabins and one at the rear. Stepping into the lavatory at the rear of the aircraft, it's reasonably sized, clean, and modern. And true to Japanese style, the toilet is of course equipped with a bidet. Back at my seat, I'm planning to get some work done to pass the time. It's easy to use a 13-in laptop in these seats with plenty of extra room thanks to the fantastic seat pitch. There is Wi-Fi available on board, but it doesn't seem to be working on today's flight. >> [music] >> The crew passed through with water services every hour or so, and after about 3 hours of working, I decided it was time to get some rest. The amount of space in these seats made it easy to get comfortable with the provided pillow and blanket. >> [music] >> After an hour of shut-eye, the cabin lights came back on for the mid-flight snack. The snack was a corn and cheese bread along with a beverage service of apple juice or green tea. After that super quick service, the cabin lights were dimmed again until the next service. So, for me, it was back to sleep. I woke up after about an hour and a half more shut-eye and grabbed a water from the flight attendant who was passing through. [music] Taking a walk up to the midsection galley, the crew had set up a snack station with snack mixes, Kit Kats, and bananas for passengers to take. Back to doing a bit of work, we have just under 3 hours to go before arrival in Houston. With the sun rising, it's time for breakfast 2 hours prior to arrival. Refreshing towels were handed out first, and then the crew came through with the same helpful placards displaying the meal options for this service with options of red rock fish teriyaki with rice or tomato gratin with eggplant and broccoli. I opted for the tomato gratin, and the tray was served with a dish of fresh fruit and a pot of yogurt. The gratin had a base of penne pasta and was a really tasty dish. I'm not totally sure I'd classify it as breakfast, but it was good nonetheless. A beverage was offered with the meal and another one as the trays were cleared away. In the last hour and a half of the flight, the crew passed through with the onboard duty-free service as the last offering of the flight. Overall, ANA's cabin crew have been stellar with a super friendly and attentive service mindset while also being hyper professional. >> Touching down in Houston after 12 hours in the air, we're taxiing over to park at Terminal D, which is the terminal used for international flights from foreign carriers [music] here at Houston. Flying ANA into North America, as a Star Alliance member airline, you're able to [music] connect seamlessly across the continent through the networks of both United and Air Canada on a single [music] ticket. Thanks for joining me for this journey, and I really hope you enjoyed it. Now for some comments on the experience overall, ANA offers an impressive long-haul economy class product [music] with good food, comfortable seats, and Japanese hospitality that makes for an enjoyable experience. These seats have everything you could hope for with more legroom than the competitors, AC [music] and USB power outlets, personal entertainment screens, and typically Wi-Fi, though it wasn't working on today's flight. [music] If I had the option of ANA versus the likes of Air Canada and United on a trans-Pacific flight in [music] economy class again, I'd be choosing ANA in a heartbeat. >> [music]

The airport's free Wi-Fi came in very handy.

reviews.transcript_full: I was sitting there one evening, bored, and decided to look at my recent flight history. Then I caught myself wondering: am I flying the national carrier too much lately? Uzbekistan Airways is a full-fledged airline with meals, baggage allowance, in-flight entertainment, and a fairly high level of service. I'd gotten so used to it that I wanted to explore a different side of aviation. Especially since I already had one experience with a low-cost carrier. Last year, I flew with AJet. But this time, I decided to go further and try a low-cost airline from Uzbekistan. That's how the idea came about to start a small series of flights exclusively on low-cost airlines on the channel. I'd like to see how different such flights are from my usual full-service carrier and whether the low ticket price really means compromising on everything else. I decided to start this series with Centrum Air, Uzbekistan's largest private airline. Today, we're departing from Tashkent to Frankfurt on a completely new aircraft for me—an Airbus A320neo. Let's look at how much such a ticket costs, what's included, what extras you'll have to pay for, what the cabin and service are like, and, most importantly, how comfortable a few hours on a low-cost airline are. So, let's see what this budget flight option has in store for us. This story begins, of course, in Tashkent. That evening, the airport was noticeably more crowded than I expected. Even though it was almost midnight, the terminal was still quite busy. Overall, everything here is familiar to me. I've flown from Tashkent many times before and know this airport well. But this time, I decided to see it from a slightly different perspective. Recently, a special balcony with a view of the airport and the city became available. During the day, it probably offers some pretty interesting panoramic views of Tashkent. But today, it's already late at night, so photographing the city was practically pointless. However, I'll show you the terminal itself and tell you how everything is set up. Perhaps this will be a useful reference point for someone before their next flight from Tashkent. Meanwhile, ahead of me, I was checking in for a Centrum Air flight to Frankfurt. I noticed the first difference between Centrum Air and many other low-cost airlines even before boarding. They don't yet have the usual online check-in, so all passengers must check in at the airport. Flights to the European Union have another feature—the so-called Visa Check. Before boarding, the airline must verify that the passenger has a visa or other document entitling them to the destination country. And this isn't just a formality. If a passenger is brought to Europe without the necessary documents and denied entry, the airline will be responsible for returning them, and the carrier may also be fined. Therefore, documents are checked especially thoroughly before such flights. As a result, check-in lines are practically inevitable. However, there is a way to avoid them—you can purchase Fast Track and check in much faster. I decided not to spend the extra money and went the usual route. In the end, I stood in line for about an hour. For a low-cost airline, this is probably one of those things you should be prepared for in advance. If you're flying Centrum Air from Tashkent to Europe, I'd definitely allow extra time for check-in and document verification. The airport's clean area has also seen some minor changes compared to my previous visit. For example, a model of Tashkent Airport has been installed here. It's certainly not the most detailed, but you can clearly see the main elements, including familiar aircraft on stands. They're also almost finished building a plane-watching terrace directly above the apron . I think you could get some really interesting photos from here during the day. But my flight was late at night, so I wasn't able to fully appreciate it—I could barely see anything. I did try to take a few shots, but the quality wasn't the best, to say the least. So, I'll show you what I got and leave a full review of this area for another time. In the meantime, I needed something to occupy myself with before boarding. The airport's free Wi-Fi came in very handy. To connect, just enter the code sent via SMS. The SMS is not limited to Uzbek numbers. I specifically tested this on my German SIM card - the code arrived without any problems. So, if you have a long wait at Tashkent airport, internet access is quite convenient. If you're flying with a low-cost airline, be prepared for one minor inconvenience: you'll likely be taken to the plane by bus, and the plane itself will be parked at a distant parking area. And this is perfectly logical. Low-cost airlines try to cut corners on everything to keep ticket prices as low as possible. Airbridges, for example, cost money, so it's much cheaper to take passengers directly to the plane by bus. Centrum Air is no exception. Our plane was also waiting for us at a distant parking area, where we were transferred by bus. But this young airline has an interesting feature: it has its own ramps and tow trucks. This means Centrum Air can handle some of its ground handling itself, without relying entirely on third-party airport services. Another classic feature of budget airlines is the extremely dense seating arrangement. The more passengers fit on the plane, the lower the cost per seat, and the cheaper the tickets can be sold. This is usually achieved through thinner seats and reduced pitch between rows. On our Airbus A320neo, the seat pitch is only 28 inches—approximately 72 centimeters. The seats themselves, by the way, are modern—made by the renowned German company RECARO. So, the cabin looks quite pleasant and modern. But then comes the fun part. In this regard, I would call Centrum Air a true "healthy person's low-cost airline." Despite the tightly packed seating, the seats recline. Each passenger has individual air conditioning and a reading lamp, as well as a power outlet for charging a phone. There's even a dedicated smartphone holder. Entertainment is provided via a dedicated multimedia system, which can be accessed via Wi-Fi. And the surprises don't end there. On our flight, passengers will also receive meals. And the free carry-on baggage allowance is currently 8 kilograms. So, while we may be looking at a low-cost airline, it also offers a whole host of amenities you wouldn't expect from a budget airline. And now I'm wondering: if all this is included in the base price, how is Centrum Air actually saving money? Our departure was scheduled for 3 a.m. , so unfortunately, don't expect any beautiful shots out the window today. I tried to capture something during the climb, but at night, the plastic window insert becomes a real enemy for a videographer. The light sources from outside are blurred, glare appears, and instead of a beautiful view of Tashkent at night, you get a series of glowing spots. But almost immediately after takeoff, service began. First, the flight attendants offered drinks and juices. And then, quite quickly, the hot meal arrived. The main course was a chicken cutlet with rice and corn. It came with a white flour bun, samsa, sliced ​​cheese and vegetables. Sauces included ketchup. And for dessert, they gave me a cupcake. Frankly, for a budget airline, I expected a much more modest selection. But here, it turned out to be a full, hot meal. And now it gets especially interesting: we're buying a ticket from a low-cost carrier, but we get meals, baggage, and a pretty decent set of amenities right out of the box. So let's see if Centrum Air can really maintain this impression all the way to Frankfurt.   As we continue our flight toward Frankfurt, let's explore what a low-cost carrier is and how it differs from a regular airline. The word "low-cost" literally means "low cost." The main idea behind this model is to offer passengers the cheapest possible ticket by stripping out all unnecessary features and focusing solely on the flight itself. The first and most obvious is dense seating. The more passengers a plane can accommodate, the cheaper the cost per passenger. Therefore, low-cost airlines often have less space between seats. Secondly, additional services are paid for separately. Baggage, seat selection, priority boarding, and sometimes even meals and drinks can cost extra. You're not buying an all-inclusive package, but a basic flight, and then you decide what you're willing to pay extra for. The third key feature is rapid turnaround. For a low-cost airline, the aircraft should spend as little time on the ground as possible. The faster it arrives, disembarks passengers, loads, and takes off again, the more efficiently the entire system operates. This also leads to other cost-saving strategies: aircraft often use remote stands instead of jet bridges, strive to standardize their fleet as much as possible, and reduce ground handling costs. But the most interesting thing is that a modern low-cost carrier doesn't necessarily mean a bad aircraft or bad service. Some budget airlines offer quite a few amenities, simply making money elsewhere. Centrum Air is particularly interesting because it offers some of the usual low-cost compromises, while surprisingly omitting others. Incidentally, Centrum Air isn't the only low-cost carrier in our region. Uzbekistan has another low-cost carrier, FlyOne. And if you look a little wider, at Central Asia, many of you have probably heard of Kazakhstan's SCAT and FlyArystan. Incidentally, I already have a detailed review of SCAT on my channel—if you're interested, you can watch it after this video. In Russia, Pobeda remains one of the most well-known low-cost carriers. I'm sure many have encountered their rather strict baggage and carry-on rules at least once. And if we talk about Europe, the list of well-known low-cost carriers is even longer. First and foremost, there are Ryanair, Wizz Air, easyJet, and Transavia. Each of these airlines has its own budget travel philosophy. But they all have one thing in common: the ability to buy a ticket significantly cheaper than traditional airlines if the passenger is willing to give up some of the usual service or pay for additional services. And so, after 7 hours and 12 minutes, we finally landed in Frankfurt. Moreover, we arrived directly at the airport's new terminal—Terminal 3. And here another pleasant surprise awaited me. Despite Centrum Air being a low-cost airline, we were escorted directly to the jet bridge. For low-cost carriers, this is more the exception than the rule. Moreover, from touchdown to a complete stop at the terminal, only about five minutes passed. For such a huge airport, that's truly very fast. Now it's time to sum up our experiment. I bought a ticket for this flight for 240 euros, plus an extra 10 euros for seat selection. That's a total of 250 euros. I also got quite a bit of what you wouldn't expect from a low-cost airline: 8 kilograms of carry-on baggage, a reclining seat, a power outlet, individual air conditioning, a phone holder, an entertainment system, and, most importantly, a full hot meal. Yes, the seating is quite tight, there's no online check-in, and we were taken to the plane by bus. But for me, these shortcomings were quite tolerable. This is my longest flight with a budget airline. And, frankly, after seven hours on board, I expected to be much more tired. Frankfurt Airport, where we just landed, is Germany's largest airport and one of Europe's largest aviation hubs. Now I suggest we forget about planes for a while and just stroll around Frankfurt. That was my first full-fledged flight with Centrum Air. Would you choose this low-cost carrier for €250, or would you rather pay extra for a traditional airline? Let me know in the comments. See you in the next video .

reviews.transcript_full: How many aircraft types can you think of that today still have their earliest examples in operation? Chances are very few, if any at all. And yet, the second, third, and fourth Boeing 77s ever built are still in active service today with United Airlines. Since its first flight in 1994, the trip 7 family has logged almost 2,500 orders, becoming the most produced and most successful widebody aircraft of all time. Today we're going to be flying on an aircraft that has been part of the success story since the very beginning. November 774 Uniform Alpha, which was not only the second Boing 7 ever built, but also the oldest trip 7 in operation today. We'll be on board for 5 hours this afternoon over the Pacific today from San Francisco to Honolulu. I'm very excited to present this video to you all and I really hope you enjoy it. Good afternoon from San Francisco where I've just arrived 3 hours late from Chicago. That delay ate up most of my connection, but thankfully I only need to walk a couple of steps to reach my next flight. I arrived at F-14 and depart from F-15 with United 300 being my flight this afternoon to Honolulu operated on a Boeing 77200. But today it's not just any trip 77200. This is the world's oldest active Boeing 77 which just one day earlier celebrated 32 years since taking its first flight on July 15th, 1994. Despite 774 being the second trip 7 ever built, it was actually the ninth trip 7 delivered to United. And that's because it spent the first few months of its career as a test aircraft that helped certify the trip 7 before eventually joining United in 1996. There was only one trip 7 older than this plane, and that was Bravo Hotel November Lima, which flew for Cath Pacific until its retirement in 2018 and is now preserved at the Puma Air and Space Museum in Arizona. The trip 7 has been a revolutionary aircraft ever since its launch. It was Boeing's first commercial airliner designed entirely on a computer. Its first aircraft to use flybywire controls and the first twin engine aircraft to really push the boundaries of non-stop long haul flying. Until now, 1,791 trip 7s have been delivered to customers all over the world. A success story that 774 has continued to witness in its 32 years of flight. This afternoon, I'm seated in 32L and these leather seats are decently comfortable and as usual with flights to Hawaii, blankets are provided and no pillows. I guess that's just a thing. This is the most common domestic trip 7 cabin you'll find with seatback personal device holders for streaming entertainment through the Wi-Fi, decent leg room, and universal outlets between seats. Now, let's address the elephant in the room. 32 years is a long time. And of course, most airlines don't tend to keep their widebody aircraft for this long, especially with so many newer options on the market. Yet, the main reason United has kept most of its oldest trip 7s flying for three decades, is capacity. This aircraft is part of United's domestic trip 7 subfleet, which at its peak consisted of 1972 2000s and four trip 77200 ERS. These are the most densely configured aircraft in United's fleet with up to 364 seats. Those are a lot of seats to be filled and as a result lots of money to be made and thus these aircraft primarily operate flights between hubs, flights to Hawaii, and also flights to other high demand leisure destinations. Until recently, United has not been able to find a proper replacement for these highdensity planes.
